title: Luna, Phoenix, Queen
author: Julie Orringer
description: A novel about varieties of infidelity, the provenance of a literary masterpiece, and the power of storytelling to shape identity and destiny.

title: Music Against the Night
author: Yiyun Li
description: Figures of the past find new life in Yiyun Li’s saga following two musicians as they mature, study, travel, love, grieve, and, above all, chase their ambitions.

title: Peck & Peck
author: Bonnie Garmus
description: A literary novel set in the publishing world of 1980s New York City about a young man whose life turns upside down when he is hired by the most prestigious, secretive, and dysfunctional poetry journal in the world: the renowned Peck & Peck.

title: Did You Ever Have A Family
author: Bill Clegg
description: A novel about a circle of people who find solace in the least likely of places as they cope with a horrific tragedy.

title: Paradise of the Pacific
author: Susanna Moore
description: The dramatic history of Hawaii: America's tropical paradise.

title: Above the Waterfall
author: Ron Rash
description: A poetic and haunting tale set in contemporary Appalachia, which plays a park ranger’s past traumas against a sheriff’s present crises.

title: Strangers Drowning
author: Larissa MacFarquhar
description: What does it mean to devote yourself wholly to helping others? In Strangers Drowning , Larissa MacFarquhar seeks out people living lives of extreme ethical commitment and tells their deeply intimate stories.

title: Under the Udala Trees
author: Chinelo Okparanta
description: In 1968, during the second year of the war between Biafra and Nigeria, 11-year-old Ijeoma is sent away from her home in Ojoto for safety by her mother, Adaora.

title: Mothers, Tell Your Daughters
author: Bonnie Jo Campbell
description: Tales about strong but flawed working-class women and those they love.

title: Dietrich & Riefenstahl: Hollywood, Berlin, and a Century in Two Lives
author: Karin Wieland
description: The story of two icons and the turbulent times they lived through.

title: City on Fire
author: Garth Risk Hallberg
description: Gritty mid-1970s New York provides the backdrop for an epic story of musicians, writers, and power brokers and the surprising ways they connect.

title: The Gap of Time
author: Jeanette Winterson
description: In The Gap of Time , Jeanette Winterson’s cover version of The Winter’s Tale , we move from London, a city reeling after the 2008 financial crisis, to a storm-ravaged American city called New Bohemia. Her story is one of childhood friendship, money, status, technology and the elliptical nature of time.

title: The Longest Night
author: Andria Williams
description: A debut novel about a young couple whose marriage is tested when they move to an army base rife with love triangles, life-or-death conflicts, and a dramatic cover-up.

title: Bind Us Apart: How Enlightened Americans Invented Racial Segregation
author: Nicholas Guyatt
publisher: Bind Us Apart: How Enlightened Americans Invented Racial Segregation
description: Guyatt argues that, from the Revolution through the Civil War, most white liberals believed in the unity of all human beings. But their philosophy faltered when it came to the practical work of forging a color-blind society.

title: The Namesake
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
description: A first novel that follows Gogol Ganguli as he stumbles along the first-generation-American path, strewn with conflicting loyalties, comic detours, and wrenching love affairs.

title: Two Nights
author: Kathy Reichs
description: A search for a missing girl resurrects traumatic memories for a woman already struggling with life.

title: Sight
author: Jessie Greengrass
description: This debut novel considers the intrinsic intimacy and distance between mother and daughter, from the perspective of a narrator who is both, as well as the struggle to clearly see one another and oneself.

title: Well-Read Black Girl: Finding Our Stories, Discovering Ourselves
author: Glory Edim
description: A collection of essays by black women writers, curated by the founder of the popular book club Well-Read Black Girl, on the importance of recognizing ourselves in literature.

title: Down to Earth, Politics in the New Climatic Regime
author: Bruno LaTour
description: According To Bruno LaTour, belonging to a territory is the phenomenon most in need of rethinking and careful redescription; learning new ways to inhabit the Earth is our biggest challenge. Bringing us down to earth is the task of politics today.

title: Bedfellow
author: Jeremy C Shipp
description: From Jeremy C. Shipp, the Bram Stoker Award-nominated author of The Atrocities , comes a tense dark fantasy novel of psychological horror.

title: How Long 'til Black Future Month?: Stories
author: N K Jemisin
description: Three-time Hugo Award winner N. K. Jemisin's first collection of short fiction challenges with stories of destruction, rebirth, and redemption.

title: The Grandmaster: Magnus Carlsen and the Match That Made Chess Great Again
author: Brin-Jonathan Butler
description: A firsthand account of the dramatic 2016 World Chess Championship between Norway's Magnus Carlsen and Russia's Sergey Karjakin, which mirrored the world's geopolitical unrest and rekindled a global fascination with the sport.

title: To Keep the Sun Alive
author: Rabeah Ghaffari
description: A cinematic novel about an Iranian family and their fruit orchard, caught up in the Revolution of 1979.

title: Lord of the Butterflies
author: Andrea Gibson
description: A collection of poems exploring gender, romance, loss, and family.

title: We Were Mothers
author: Katie Sise
description: A group of women are bound by dark secrets in Sise’s adult debut.

title: Husk
author: Dave Zeltserman
description: Classic contemporary horror from the Shamus and Derringer-winning author of Small Crimes .

title: Which Side Are You On?: 20th Century American History in 100 Protest Songs
author: James Sullivan
description: Journalist and author James Sullivan delivers an anecdotal history of the progressive movements that have shaped the growth of the United States through the lens of the songs that have accompanied and defined them.

title: In a House of Lies
author: Ian Rankin
description: A cold case involving a missing private investigator threatens to unearth skeletons from Rebus's past in this series mystery.

title: Talent
author: Juliet Lapidos
description: A young graduate student writing about-and desperately searching for inspiration stumbles upon it in the unlikeliest of places.

title: Collected Poems of Bob Kaufman
author: Bob Kaufman, Ed. by Neeli Cherkovski, Raymond Foye, and Tate Swindell
description: Bob Kaufman (1925–1986) was one of the most important—and original—poets of the twentieth century. He is among the inaugurators of what today is characterized as the Afro-Surreal, uniting the surrealist practice of automatic writing with the jazz concept of spontaneous composition. Collected Poems brings together all of Kaufman’s known surviving poems, including an extensive section of previously uncollected work.

title: The Burglar in Short Order
author: Lawrence Block
description: Four decades ago, Mystery Writers of America Grand Master Lawrence Block introduced the world to one of his most beloved characters: the bookseller and burglar Bernie Rhodenbarr. This volume collects every published story, article, and standalone excerpt Bernie has ever appeared in plus two new, unpublished pieces.

title: Yellow Bird: Oil, Murder, and a Woman's Search for Justice in Indian Country
author: Sierra Crane Murdoch
description: When Lissa Yellow Bird was released from prison in 2009, she found her home, the Fort Berthold Indian Reservation in North Dakota, transformed by the Bakken oil boom. Three years later, when Lissa learned that a young white oil worker, Kristopher “KC” Clarke, had disappeared from his reservation worksite, she became obsessed with his case and went to great lengths to find him.

title: How the South Won the Civil War: Oligarchy, Democracy, and the Continuing Fight for the Soul of America
author: Heather Cox Richardson
description: A Boston College history professor debunks the myth that the U.S. Civil War released the nation from the grip of oligarchy, expunging the sins of the Founding, and instead spread the corrupt values of the Old South throughout the land—a phenomenon with present-day consequences.

title: First Principles: What America's Founders Learned from the Greeks and Romans and How That Shaped Our Country
author: Thomas E. Ricks
description: Ricks discusses the founding fathers, examining their educations and, in particular, their devotion to the ancient Greek and Roman classics—and how that influence would shape their ideals and the new American nation.

title: Chicago's Great Fire: The Destruction and Resurrection of an Iconic American City
author: Carl Smith
description: The full story of one of the most iconic disasters in American history, The Great Chicago Fire, told through the vivid memories of those who experienced it.

title: His Dark Materials: Serpentine
author: Philip Pullman
description: The world-changing events of The Amber Spyglass are behind them, and Lyra and Pan find themselves utterly changed as well. In Serpentine , they journey to the far North once more, hoping to ask the Consul of Witches a most urgent question.

title: Make Me Rain: Poems & Prose
author: Nikki Giovanni
description: One of America's most celebrated poets and authors challenges us with this deeply personal collection of verse that speaks to the injustices of society while illuminating the depths of her own heart.

title: Prefecture D
author: Hideo Yokoyama
description: A collection of tense thrilllers, each centered on a mystery and the unfortunate officer tasked with solving it, set in the world of Hideo Yokoyama's bestselling Six Four .

title: We Need to Talk: A Memoir about Wealth
author: Jennifer Risher
description: We Need to Talk: A Memoir About Wealth examines the hidden impact of wealth on identity, relationships, and sense of place in the world. At a time when income inequality is a huge problem and money is a taboo subject even among those closest to us, We Need to Talk aims to start a conversation that demystifies wealth.

title: Right Place, Right Time: The Life of a Rock & Roll Photographer
author: Bob Gruen
description: An action-packed memoir that takes readers on the road with rock and roll's hardest-working photographer.

title: Blood Runs Coal: The Yablonski Murders and the Battle for the United Mine Workers of America
author: Mark A Bradley
description: The most infamous crimes in the history of American labor unions, the Yablonski murders triggered one of the most intensive and successful manhunts in FBI history — and also led to the first successful rank-and-file takeover of a major labor union in modern U.S. history, one that inspired workers in other labor unions to rise up and challenge their own entrenched, out-of-touch leaders.

title: The Book Collectors: A Band of Syrian Rebels and the Stories That Carried Them Through a War
author: Delphine Minoui, tr. Laura Vergnaud
description: Award-winning French-Iranian journalist Delphine Minoui recounts the true story of a band of young rebels, a besieged Syrian town, and an underground library built from the rubble of war.

title: Apollo's Arrow
author: Nicholas A Christakis
description: An account of the impact of the coronavirus pandemic as it swept through American society in 2020, and of how the recovery will unfold in the coming years. Drawing on cutting-edge research from a range of scientific disciplines, bestselling author, physician, sociologist, and public health expert Nicholas A. Christakis explores what it means to live in a time of plague.

title: Sicily '43: The First Assault on Fortress Europe
author: James Holland
description: A new history of one of World War II's most crucial campaigns, the first Allied attack on European soil, by the acclaimed author of Normandy '44 and a rising star in military history.

title: Particulate Matter
author: Felicia Luna Lemus
description: In concise and distilled prose, Lemus presents a collection of still lifes, landscapes, and portraits of a challenging year that threatened all she loved most. Particulate Matter is the story of a year in Felicia Luna Lemus's marriage when the world turned upside down. It's set in Los Angeles, and it's about love and crisis, loss and grief, the city and the ocean, ancestral ghosts and history haunting.

title: A Galway Epiphany: A Jack Taylor Novel
author: Ken Bruen
description: In the newest novel in Bruen's series, ex-cop turned private eye Jack Taylor is pulled out of his quiet new life on a farm by three mysteries that soon prove dangerously linked.

title: Rave
author: Rainald Goetz, tr. Nathan Adrian West
description: 'Meet girls. Take drugs. Listen to music.' In Rave , cult German novelist Rainald Goetz takes a headlong dive into nineties techno culture.

title: Aphasia
author: Mauro Javier Cárdenas
description: A novel about coming to terms with a dysfunctional Columbian family, written in fragmented prose.

title: The Archer
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A fable from award-winning Brazilian author Paul Coelho about the importance of taking risks and overcoming difficulty ... told from the perspective of Tetsuya, a famous former archer, and his apprentice.

title: South to Freedom: Runaway Slaves to Mexico and the Road to the Civil War
author: Alice L. Baumgartner
description: Historian Alice L. Baumgartner tells the story of why Mexico abolished slavery and how its increasingly radical antislavery policies fueled the sectional crisis in the United States. This is an account of the coming of the American Civil War, showing the crucial role of slaves who escaped to Mexico.

title: Murder by Milk Bottle
author: Lynne Truss
description: A new crime novel set in Brighton, summer of 1957, from New York Times bestselling author Lynne Truss .

title: Piece of My Heart
author: Mary Higgins Clark
description: In the latest collaboration from #1 New York Times bestselling author and 'Queen of Suspense' Mary Higgins Clark and Alafair Burke, television producer Laurie Moran must solve the kidnapping of her fiancée's nephew — just days before her wedding.

title: The Fabric of Civilization: How Textiles Made the World
author: Virginia Postrel
description: Virginia Postrel synthesizes groundbreaking research from archaeology, economics, and science to reveal a surprising history of textiles and fabrics. From Minoans exporting wool colored with precious purple dye to Egypt, to Romans arrayed in costly Chinese silk, the cloth trade paved the crossroads of the ancient world

title: Sometimes You Have to Lie: The Life and Times of Louise Fitzhugh, Renegade Author of Harriet the Spy
author: Leslie Brody
description: In this biography, discover the true story of Harriet the Spy author Louise Fitzhugh—and learn about the woman behind one of literature's most beloved heroines. Harriet the Spy , first published in 1964, has mesmerized generations of readers and launched a million diarists.

title: Admission
author: Julie Buxbaum
description: From the New York Times bestselling author of Tell Me Three Things comes an of-the-moment novel that peeks inside the private lives of the hypercompetitive and the hyperprivileged and takes on the college admissions bribery scandal that rocked the country.

title: The Wicked Hour: A Natalie Lockhart Novel
author: Alice Blanchard
description: In the second book of the Traces of Evil series, a detective dealing with the scars of her past must solve a seemingly unconnected string of murders and face the impossible question of what to do when the killer may be hiding amongst the ones you know.

title: The New Long Life: A Framework for Flourishing in a Changing World
author: Andrew J Scott
description: Drawing from the fields of economics and psychology, Andrew J. Scott and Lynda Gratton offer a simple framework based on three fundamental principles to give you the tools to navigate the challenges ahead. Both a personal road-map and a primer for governments, corporations and colleges, The New Long Life is the essential guide to a longer, smarter, happier life.

title: Dark, Salt, Clear: The Life of a Fishing Town
author: Lamorna Ash
description: Before arriving in Newlyn, a Cornish fishing village at the end of the railway line, Lamorna Ash was told that no fisherman would want a girl joining an expedition. Weeks later, the only female on board a trawler called the Filadelfia, she is heading out to sea with the dome of the sky above and the black waves below.

title: Black Hole Survival Guide
author: Janna Levin
description: Levin takes us on an evocative exploration of black holes, provoking us to imagine the visceral experience of a black hole encounter. She reveals the influence of black holes as they populate the universe, sculpt galaxies, and even infuse the whole expanse of reality that we inhabit.

title: The Opium Prince
author: Jasmine Aimaq
description: "Born to an American mother and a late Afghan war hero-turned-magnate, Daniel Sajadi has spent his life navigating a complex identity. After years in Los Angeles, he is returning home to Kabul for the first time as the head of a US foreign aid agency dedicated to staunching the growth of the poppy fields in Fever Valley that feed the world's opiate epidemic. But on the drive back to Kabul from an anniversary trip with his wife, Rebecca, Daniel hits and kills a young Kochi girl named Telaya. Nomad tribes are ignored in the eyes of the law, and Daniel is let off with a nominal fine due to a mysterious witness at the scene-a man named Taj Maleki, who turns out to be a prominent opium khan. Wracked with guilt and visions of Telaya, Daniel begins to unravel, running from his rapidly crumbling marriage and threats of blackmail and murder from the man who would do anything to save his poppy fields from eradication. In a powerful literary thriller debut that captures the tumultuous, sometimes violent trajectory of revolution, Jasmine Aimaq draws the often invisible lines between criminal empires and shifting political regimes"--

title: The Pattern Seekers: How Autism Drives Human Invention
author: Simon Baron-Cohen
description: Cambridge University psychologist Simon Baron-Cohen makes a case that autism is as crucial to our creative and cultural history as the mastery of fire.

title: XX
author: Rian Hughes
description: Deconstructing layout and language in order to explore how idea propagate, acclaimed designer and artist Rian Hughes's debut novel presents a compelling vision of humanity's unique place in the universe, and a realistic depiction of what might happen in the wake of the biggest scientific discovery in human history.

title: Burning the Books: A History of the Deliberate Destruction of Knowledge
author: Richard Ovenden
description: Libraries preserve the knowledge and ideas on which rights depend; no wonder they are so often attacked. Richard Ovenden tells the history of this deliberate destruction of knowledge — from library burnings to digital attacks and contemporary underfunding — and makes a passionate plea for the importance of these threatened institutions.

title: Stories I Forgot to Tell You
author: Dorothy Gallagher
description: Gallagher moves freely and intuitively between the present and the past to evoke the life she and editor Ben Gallagher made together, and her life after his death, alone and yet at the same time never without thoughts of him, in a present that is haunted but also comforted by the recollection of their common past.

title: Together in a Sudden Strangeness: America's Poets Respond to the Pandemic
author: Alice Quinn

title: Revolutions of All Colors
author: Dewaine Farria
description: This is a novel about the uniquely American dilemma of chiseling out an identity in a country still struggling to define itself.

title: The River Within
author: Karen Powell
description: In the weeks that follow a tragic drowning, the river begins to give up its secrets. As the circumstances surrounding Danny's death emerge, other stories surface that threaten to disrupt everybody's plans and to destroy an entire way of life.

title: Owed
author: Joshua Bennett
description: Owed, is a book with celebration at its center. Its primary concern is how we might mend the relationship between ourselves and the people, spaces, and objects we have been taught to think of as insignificant, as fundamentally unworthy of study, reflection, attention, or care.

title: Older
author: Pamela Redmond
description: Sequel to Younger , the book behind the hit TV Land series.

title: The Distance
author: Ivan Vladislavic
description: In this formally inventive, fragmented novel, Vladislaviâc evokes the beauty, and the strangeness, of remembering and forgetting, and explores what it means to be at odds with one's surroundings in a portrait of two brothers and Muhammad Ali.

title: The Last Druid
author: Terry Brooks
description: Hope blooms anew for the Four Lands in this riveting conclusion, not only to the Fall of Shannara series but to the entire Shannara saga — a truly landmark event over forty years in the making.

title: African American Poetry: 250 Years of Struggle
author: Kevin Young
description: A literary landmark: the biggest, most ambitious anthology of Black poetry ever published, gathering 250 poets from the colonial period to the present

title: The Last Libertines
author: Benedetta Craveri
description: The story of a group of seven aristocrats whose youth coincided with the French monarchy's final moment of grace.

title: Stories from Suffragette City
author: M J Rose
description: A collection of short stories that all take place on a single day: October 23, 1915. It's the day when tens of thousands of women marched up Fifth Avenue, demanding the right to vote in New York City.

title: Our Last Season: A Writer, a Fan, a Friendship
author: Harvey Araton
description: The story of a bond between sportswriter and fan that was forged in a shared love of basketball and grew over several decades into a friendship that sees both through the trials of their later years.

title: Ravenna: Capital of Empire, Crucible of Europe
author: Judith Herrin
description: A history of the city that led the West out of the ruins of the Roman Empire.

title: Funeral Diva
author: Pamela Sneed
description: A poetic memoir about coming-of-age in the AIDS era, and its effects on life and art.

title: Dead Lies Dreaming
author: Charles Stross
description: In a tale of corruption, assassination, thievery, and magic, Wendy Deere must navigate rotting mansions that lead to distant pasts, evil tycoons, corrupt government officials, lethal curses, and her own moral qualms in order to make it out of this chase alive.

title: Saving Justice: Truth, Transparency, and Trust
author: James Comey
description: The former FBI Director and New York Times -bestselling author of A Higher Loyalty uses his long career in federal law enforcement to explore issues of justice and fairness in the U.S. justice system.

title: Marshlands
author: Andre Gide
description: The protagonist of Marshlands is a writer who is writing Marshlands, which is about a reclusive character who lives all alone in a stone tower. The narrator, by contrast, is anything but a recluse: He is an indefatigable social butterfly, flitting about the Paris literary world and always talking about, what else, the wonderful book he is writing— Marshlands .

title: A Red Line in the Sand: Diplomacy, Strategy, and the History of Wars That Might Still Happen
author: David A Andelman
description: Andelman uses original documentary research, previously classified material, interviews with key players, and reportage from more than 80 countries across five decades to help us understand the growth, the successes and frequent failures that have shaped our world today.

title: The Fortunate Ones
author: Ed Tarkington
description: When young Charlie Boykin gains entry into the wealthy society of the most exclusive part of Nashville, he falls under its spell. But he soon learns what he'd have to give up in return in this novel that asks why people envy and worship a class of people that so often exhibits the worst excesses.

title: Reel Bay: A Cinematic Essay
author: Jana Larson
description: Equal parts memoir, mystery, reclaimed screenplay, and travelogue, Reel Bay charts Jana Larson's unusual journey toward understanding another woman's life.

title: The Eagles of Heart Mountain: A True Story of Football, Incarceration, and Resistance in World War II America
author: Bradford Pearson
description: The impeccably researched, deeply moving, never-before-told tale about a World War II incarceration camp in Wyoming and its extraordinary high-school football team--for fans of The Boys in the Boat and The Storm on Our Shores .s .

title: Find Me in Havana
author: Serena Burdick
description: Blindsided by her mother's mysterious death, Nina Rodriguez navigates the troubling, opulent memories of their life together and discovers how much Estelita sacrificed to live the American dream on her own terms. Based on true events.

title: So-Called Normal: A Memoir of Family, Depression and Resilience
author: Mark Henick
description: A story of perseverance and recovery by one of Canada's foremost advocates for mental health.

title: Boomers: The Men and Women Who Promised Freedom and Delivered Disaster
author: Helen Andrews
description: Helen Andrews calls the Boomers to account, [presenting] profiles of luminaries who promised much, ... including Camille Paglia, Aaron Sorkin, Steve Jobs, and Sonia Sotomayor. In covering the mighty works of these titans, Andrews [posits that] their lives and their generational idiosyncrasies have secretly deformed — in plain sight — our society and our successive generations.

title: Breath Taking: The Power, Fragility, and Future of Our Extraordinary Lungs
author: Michael J Stephen
description: From an expert in pulmonary medicine, the story of our extraordinary lungs, the organ that both explains our origins and holds the keys to our future as a species.

title: Bad Medicine: Catching New York's Deadliest Pill Pusher
author: Charlotte Bismuth
description: The shocking story of New York's most infamous pill-pushing doctor, written by the prosecutor who brought him down in a landmark and precedent-setting case in the fight against opioid addiction.

title: The Effort
author: Claire Holroyde
description: When dark comet UD3 was spotted near Jupiter's orbit, its existence was largely ignored. But to individuals who knew better, the threat this eight-kilometer comet posed to the survival of the human race was unthinkable.

title: The Mission: A True Story
author: David W Brown
description: A masterful, genre-defying narrative of the most ambitious science project ever conceived: NASA's deep-space mission to Europa — the Jovian moon where might swim the first known alien life in the solar system-powered by a motley team of obsessives and eccentrics.

title: This Is the Voice
author: John Colapinto
description: Beginning with the novel argument that the ability to speak is what made man the planet's dominant species, the award-winning New Yorker writer and best-selling author shows why the voice is the most efficient, effective means of communication ever devised.

title: You Are Not American: Citizenship Stripping from Dred Scott to the Dreamers
author: Amanda Frost
description: Amanda Frost explores how the United States' concept of citizenship and the rights of citizens has evolved, and especially how it has been challenged.

title: In Search of the Color Purple: The Story of an American Masterpiece
author: Salamishah Tillet
description: Mixing cultural criticism, literary history, biography, and memoir, an exploration of Alice Walker's critically acclaimed and controversial novel, The Color Purple .

title: Finlay Donovan Is Killing It: A Mystery
author: Elle Cosimano
description: Edgar-Award nominee Elle Cosimano's adult debut Finlay Donovan Is Killing It is the first in a witty, fast-paced mystery series, following struggling suspense novelist and single mom Finlay Donovan, whose fiction treads dangerously close to the truth as she becomes tangled in real-life murder investigations.

title: On Corruption in America: And What Is at Stake
author: Sarah Chayes
description: Now, bringing to bear all of her knowledge, grasp, sense of history and observation, Sarah Chayes writes in her new book, that the United States is showing signs similar to some of the most corrupt countries in the world.

title: We Need to Hang Out: A Memoir of Making Friends
author: Billy Baker
description: A middle-aged everyman who realizes that he doesn't have any close friends is inspired to set out on a humorous and ultimately moving quest to revive old tribes and build new ones, all with the goal of having someone to hang out with on Wednesday nights.

title: The Historians
author: Saskia Maarleveld
description: Before the war they were the best of friends. Five brilliant young historians debated origins, ideas and the place of history in modern times under the guidance of the charismatic Professor Lindahl. When war broke out the five disbanded, ending up on different sides. Now one of them has been found tortured and killed . .

title: The Rope: A True Story of Murder, Heroism, and the Dawn of the NAACP
author: Alex Tresniowski
description: A true-crime thriller recounting the 1910 murder of ten-year-old Marie Smith, the dawn of modern criminal detection, and the launch of the NAACP.

title: The Paris Library
author: Janet Skeslien Charles
description: Lily is a lonely teenager looking for adventure in small-town Montana. Her interest is piqued by her solitary, elderly neighbor. As Lily uncovers more about her neighbor's mysterious past, she finds that they share a love of language, the same longings, and the same intense jealousy, never suspecting that a dark secret from the past connects them.

title: Rabbit Island
author: Elvira Navarro
description: Combining the gritty surrealism of David Lynch with the explosive interior meditations of Clarice Lispector, the stories in Elvira Navarro's Rabbit Island traverse the fickle, often terrifying terrain between madness and freedom

title: Homo Irrealis: Essays
author: André Aciman
description: A new collection of essays on literary and cinematic themes.

title: The (Other) You: Stories
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: A collection of stories that explores the musings of a writer, a prisoner, a student, and others who consider how their lives might have unfolded differently had they made different choices.

title: The Black Panther Party: A Graphic Novel History
author: David F Walker
description: A graphic novel history of the Black Panther Party.

title: Ida B. the Queen: The Extraordinary Life and Legacy of Ida B. Wells
author: Michelle Duster
description: American pioneer Ida B. Wells' great-granddaughter offers an inspiring biography of a leader called 'a dangerous negro agitator' by the FBI, and a 'brave woman' by Frederick Douglass.

title: Love Is an Ex-Country
author: Randa Jarrar
description: Queer. Muslim. Arab American. A proudly Fat woman. Randa Jarrar is all of these things. In this memoir of a cross-country road trip, she explores how to claim joy in an unraveling and hostile America.

title: Popular Longing
author: Natalie Shapero
description: Poet Natalie Shapero's Popular Longing explores sadnesses and subordinations in their myriad forms.

title: Let's Get Back to the Party
author: Zak Salih
description: Estranged childhood friends Oscar and Sebastian-both too young to have a personal relationship with the AIDS crisis but too old to have enjoyed the freedom of an out adolescence-spend a year grappling with cultural identity, generational change, and what they see in, and owe to, each other.

title: Thinking Again: A Diary
author: Jan Morris
description: The irrepressible Morris--author of such classics as Venice and Trieste --is at it again offering a vibrant set of reminiscences that wax on the ironies of modern life in all their resonant glories and inevitable stupidities.

title: The Next Apocalypse: The Art and Science of Survival
author: Chris Begley
description: Pandemic, climate change, or war: our era is ripe with the odor of doomsday. In movies, books, and more, our imaginations run wild with visions of dreadful, abandoned cities and returning to the land in a desperate attempt at survival. In The Next Apocalypse , archaeologist Chris Begley argues that we completely misunderstand how disaster works. Examining past collapses of civilizations, such as the Maya and Rome, he argues that these breakdowns are actually less about cataclysmic destruction than they are about long processes of change. In short: it's what happens after the initial uproar that matters. Some people abandon their homes and neighbors; others band together to start anew. As we anticipate our own fate, Begley tells us that it was communities, not lone heroes, who survived past apocalypses--and who will survive the next.

title: Reclamation: Sally Hemings, Thomas Jefferson, and a Descendant's Search for Her Family's Lasting Legacy
author: Gayle Jessup White
description: Gayle Jessup White had long heard the stories passed down from her father's family that they were direct descendants of Thomas Jefferson—lore she firmly believed. For four decades the journalist and genealogy enthusiast researched her connection to Thomas Jefferson. After she was named a Jefferson Studies Fellow, Jessup White discovered her family lore was correct. Poring through photos and documents and pursuing DNA evidence, she learned that not only was she a descendant of Jefferson on his father's side, she was also the great-great-great-granddaughter of Peter Hemings, Sally Hemings's brother. In Reclamation she chronicles her journey to definitively understand her heritage and reclaim it and offers a portrait of what it means to be a Black woman in America, to pursue the American dream, to reconcile the legacy of racism, and to ensure the nation lives up to the ideals advocated by her legendary ancestor.

title: The Crocodile Bride
author: Ashleigh Bell Pedersen
description: Set during the swampy summer in 1982, this debut novel follows eleven-year-old Sunshine Turner and her troubled father Billy as the secrets of their family’s past swirl around them in the one-road town of Fingertip, Louisiana.

title: Self-Portrait with Ghost: Short Stories
author: Meng Jin
description: From the author of Little Gods , comes a story collection that explores self-construction, female resilience, and migrations both literal and transformative.

title: The Boy and the Dog
author: Seishu Hase, trans. by Alison Watts
description: One dog changes the life of everyone who takes him in on his journey to reunite with his first owner in this inspiring tribute to the bond between humans and dogs and the life-affirming power of connection.

title: The Birthday Party
author: Laurent Mauvignier, trans. by Daniel Levin Becker
description: Buried deep in rural France, little remains of the isolated hamlet of the Three Lone Girls, save a few houses and a curiously assembled quartet: Patrice Bergogne, inheritor of his family's farm; his wife, Marion; their daughter, Ida; and their neighbor, Christine, an artist. While Patrice plans a surprise for his wife's fortieth birthday, inexplicable events start to disrupt the hamlet's quiet existence: anonymous, menacing letters, an unfamiliar car rolling up the driveway. And as night falls, strangers stalk the houses, unleashing a nightmarish chain of events.

title: The Happy Couple
author: Naoise Dolan
description: Meet Celine and Luke. For all intents and purposes, the happy couple. Luke (a serial cheater) and Celine (more interested in piano than domestic life) plan to marry in a year. Archie (the best man) should be moving on from his love for Luke and up the corporate ladder, but he finds himself utterly stuck. Phoebe (the bridesmaid and Celine's sister) just wants to get to the bottom of Luke's frequent unexplained disappearances. And Vivian (a wedding guest) is the only one with any emotional distance and observes her friends like ants in a colony. As the wedding approaches and their five lives intersect, these characters will each look for a path to the happily ever after—but does it lie at the end of an aisle?

title: Question 7
author: Richard Flanagan
description: By way of H.G. Wells and Rebecca West's affair through 1930s nuclear physics to Flanagan's father working as a slave labourer near Hiroshima when the atom bomb is dropped, this daisy chain of events reaches fission when Flanagan as a young man finds himself trapped in a rapid on a wild river not knowing if he is to live or to die. At once a love song to his island home and to his parents, this hypnotic melding of dream, history, place, and memory is about how our lives so often arise out of the stories of others and the stories we invent about ourselves.

title: Save Our Souls: The True Story of a Castaway Family, Treachery, and Murder
author: Matthew Pearl
description: The true story of a real-life Swiss Family Robinson (and their dog) who faced sharks, shipwreck, and betrayal.

title: Partita
author: Barbara Kingsolver
description: A story of a brief, passionate, life-changing love affair, wrapped up in what might be the greatest romance of all: our eternal human longing for art and beauty.

title: The Occidental Book of the Dead
author: T Geronimo Johnson
description: George Washington Jonson is determined to forge a new life. After growing up in one of Atlanta’s poorest housing projects, he enlists in the U.S. Army and finds some relief serving abroad. When events lead him back home, he joins the police force. After a decade on the job, Jonson has fashioned a new life in an affluent suburb with his white wife and stepson, though he’s still policing his old neighborhood, and now tasked with training hot-headed rookie recruits. One night on patrol a split-second confrontation with a white teenager takes a violent turn. That single gunshot sets into motion a series of escalating lies.

title: Blockers: Rebels in the Deep State
author: Michael Lewis
description: An inside look at the early days of Trump's Department of Government Efficiency, as told by the public servants it targeted.

title: The Rush: California Gold, the Civil War, and the Making of the Modern World
author: Nathaniel Philbrick
description: In January 1848, a carpenter spotted flecks of gold in a shallow stream at Sutter’s Mill in California, triggering the greatest voluntary migration in U.S. history, as hundreds of thousands raced west in pursuit of sudden wealth, reinvention, and power. In The Rush , Nathaniel Philbrick transforms the Gold Rush from a tale of sudden riches into the origin story of America’s modern contradictions—capital consolidated at dizzying speed, democracy in thrall to private power, xenophobia weaponized in the name of liberty—and a stubborn belief in the American experiment that refuses to die.

title: Cormac McCarthy: A Legacy Revisited
author: Tracy Daugherty
description: A biography of the late Pulitzer Prize-winning American author Cormac McCarthy, from Tracy Daugherty.

title: Death of an Ordinary Man
author: Sarah Perry
description: A memoir that’s at once an elegy for a beloved family member and a deeply moving meditation on what it means to be a mortal creature.

title: The Savage Mind: An American Legacy
author: David Treuer
description: An exploration of American violence, interweaving memoir, history, and reportage to reveal the wound at the heart of our nation—and to offer hope that the country, and we, might be healed.

title: Every Story Is a Love Story
author: Imbolo Mbue
description: Three years ago, Wolo’s wife was killed in a tragic car accident. In an instant, the great love of his life was gone, and so was their beautiful future. In the face of a loss that seemed insurmountable, Wolo has slowly rebuilt a semblance of a life: he goes to work, hangs out with a small circle of friends, and fends off the matchmaking efforts of the older women in his family. The grief that dogged him has, with time, become a little gentler. Until a letter arrives one day, unbidden, threatening to upend his life once again. It is from Victoria, the woman who was behind the wheel that terrible day. What do we owe to those who have hurt us? Are we defined by our worst moments and our deepest regrets? And, more than anything, can forgiveness ease our suffering? Every Story Is a Love Story charts the uneven path from heartbreak to healing.

title: Fair Ones: A Double Novel
author: Lydia Millet
description: Follows two Brooklyn women in their forties reeling from the sudden and baffling death of their friend Claire. Fair , Mara's account, opens in the wake of initial shock as she and Jen come to grips with the enigma of Claire's killing. Ones , told from Jen's point of view, picks up a year later as she and Mara wrestle with new relationships and old secrets.

title: The New Dark Ages: The Death of Reading and the Dawn of the Post-Literate Society
author: James Marriott
description: It’s not by chance that the rise of new printing technologies coincided with the age of revolutions and the decline of the aristocratic order. At the beginning of the modern era in Europe, a critical mass of people could share and debate ideas about individual rights, the purpose of government and scientific truth. With growing literacy came the world we recognize today. Now, around the world, the number of peo­ple who read is in free fall. In this critique, Marriott assails the culture of modern life and singles out the written word as the best defense we have for a more en­lightened world.

title: Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up
author: David Byrne
description: From David Byrne of the band Talking Heads, a reckoning with how breakthroughs across the arts and sciences get forgotten, and how they get rediscovered

title: Will and Attention: A Memoir
author: Meghan O'Gieblyn
description: In this memoir of secret drinking, fragile recovery, and the deep pull of religion, award-winning essayist Meghan O’Gieblyn seeks to understand why it is so hard to sustain the difficult work of personal change.

title: The AGI Chronicles: The Inside Story of the Race to Create an Artificial Superintelligence
author: Kevin Roose
description: This is the story of the twenty-first century’s Manhattan Project: the race to create artificial general intelligence.

title: Other Worlds Than These: A Talisman Novel
author: Stephen King and Peter Straub
description: Jack Sawyer, an enduring King protagonist, returns in the final book in the Talisman Trilogy.

title: The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford
author: Nafissa Thompson-Spires
description: A novel set in 1920s Oklahoma about the murder of an infamous moonshiner and the cacophony of true stories a small town can tell about itself.

title: The Names of the New World
author: Kawai Strong Washburn
description: A saga of resilience and ambition in the face of a chaotic world.

title: Ply
author: Hernan Diaz
description: A novel that examines the place of technology in the American imagination

title: American Hagwon
author: Min Jin Lee
description: In schools and churches, hotel rooms and nail salons, law firms and fried-fish shops; in cramped, dingy apartments and luxury, gated communities, the men, women, and children in American Hagwon struggle to find satisfaction and meaning in a world that seems to grow less forgiving with each passing year. Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children, Bo, DH, and Mido, find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John's oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis.

title: The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman
author: Deesha Philyaw
description: The wife of a popular and powerful megachurch pastor upends her charmed “rags-to-Rolex” life when her secret past comes roaring into the spotlight.

title: The Vanishing Family: Love, Fate, and the Quest to End Dementia
author: Robert Kolker
description: From the author of Hidden Valley Road comes the journey of a family facing an unthinkable destiny, whose flawed genetic code might hold the long-sought key to a cure for dementia.

title: Man in the Mirror: Hope, Struggle, and Belonging in an American City
author: Anand Giridharadas
description: In 2023, the lives of two men—Jordan Neely, a homeless man known in better days for his Michael Jackson impersonations, and Daniel Penny, an ex-Marine who had moved to the big city seeking more than Long Island could offer—collided tragically in a New York subway car. In Man in the Mirror , award-winning reporter and bestselling author Anand Giridharadas renders this deadly encounter and its aftermath as a propulsive crime story that opens onto a larger human drama: the search for belonging in an age of estrangement.

title: The Radiance
author: Ayad Akhtar
description: When a hit-and-run shatters more than his body, a writer is plunged into a spiritual awakening he can’t tell from madness. In its grip, he’s drawn to a brilliant campus colleague by an uncanny pull, and into a scandal that threatens to destroy them both. What begins as a provocative portrait of academic and cultural warfare deepens into erotic entanglement, the exposure of a family secret, and the mystery surrounding the narrator’s accident—both the violence and its aftermath.

title: May We Feed the King
author: Rebecca Perry
description: A curator spends her days reconstructing the past—selecting and carefully arranging furniture, fabrics, and replica food to bring medieval rooms back to life. After accepting a commission to work on the private quarters of a medieval palace, the curator becomes absorbed in the story of a king almost forgotten by history. As she studies the traces he left behind, the boundary between her own life and his begins to blur.

title: No Land to Stand on: Notes from Detention
author: Mahmoud Khalil
description: Drawing on his prison diary and writing, Mahmoud Khalil conjures the despair and cruelty of ICE detention, where prisoners can vanish overnight and visiting families risk their own deportation. There is humanity, too, in the men’s acts of care—their mutual help with documents, the prison cake they make after Mahmoud can only follow the birth of his son on the public payphone. In tandem, he tells the multi-generational story of a family expelled from Palestine to a Syrian refugee camp, of flight from Assad’s regime to Lebanon, of arrival in an America that promised permanence and protection, and of the enduring struggle for Palestine.

title: Sophie, Standing There
author: Meg Mason
description: Sophie Pattison loves books. And as well as a dream job at a local book festival, she has a husband she adores; a lifelong best friend, Emma; and a brother she’s always been close to. Which makes you wonder why since Christmas Sophie has been living alone, estranged from Emma, avoiding her brother, and about to be fired. Now it feels like the only thing she has left is reading. When Sophie rediscovers an author she first read in her twenties, the words on the page reach her in a new way—becoming both solace and company. Sophie devours every one of the author's novels and begins to dream of meeting her, but knows they never will. But what if they did? What if, by then, the author feels like a friend? What if, for Sophie, it feels almost like love?

title: Dodge City
author: Patrick DeWitt
description: A novel about a young man on an amphetamine-fueled cross-country road trip, fleeing the Vietnam War draft for the safe haven of Canada.

title: John Berger: From Life
author: Tom Overton
description: A biography of novelist and critic John Berger, whose work—including Ways of Seeing and the Booker-prize winning G. —revolutionized the critical tradition in the twentieth century

title: The City Without Jews: Life and Death in Nazi Vienna
author: Douglas Smith
description: The City Without Jews tells the story of the destruction of Jewish Vienna. Even more than a work of history, it is a reminder and a warning—of the consequences of forgetting a past whose legacy refuses to die.

title: Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History
author: Benjamin Moser
description: In Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History , Benjamin Moser uncovers a suppressed tradition that has shaped Jewish thought for generations. Through a cast of artists, rabbis, poets, lawyers, activists, journalists, and politicians—from Europe and Africa and Asia and Latin America—Moser traces a lineage of Jewish dissenters who confronted Zionism’s moral and political stakes—often at devastating personal cost, including censorship, exile, and death.

title: The Strangers
author: Naomi Alderman
description: A writer wrestles with grief even as a new species is discovered, forcing humans to reconsider what it means to share our planet.

title: Avalon, Rise
author: Madeline Ffitch
description: A novel of an Appalachian town, the diverse locals who make it home, an influx of white nationalists trying to take over, and the ways in which the battle brings out our light.

title: Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel: The New Miss Marple Mystery
author: Lucy Foley
description: The brand-new Miss Marple mystery from Lucy Foley.

title: True North: On the Road in Canada
author: Paul Theroux
description: Travel writer Paul Theroux turns his gaze to Canada in a sweeping, personal journey.

title: Hollywood, Ending
author: John Green
description: John Green makes his first foray into adult fiction with a behind-the-scenes Hollywood love story about finding someone to trust in an untrustworthy world.

title: Shadow Before the Flame: The Hindenburg Disaster and the Prelude to War
author: Catherine Grace Katz
description: The definitive history of the Hindenburg disaster, the rise of the Nazis, and the road to World War II as never before told.

title: An Unexpected Life: A Memoir
author: Gloria Steinem
description: In her final memoir, Gloria Steinem offers a candid, inspiring portrait of her early life and journey as an activist, while looking ahead to the next chapters of the fight for equality—a rare opportunity to learn directly from one of feminism’s most enduring voices.

title: Rock*: A Mainstream Alternative History of Alternative Mainstream Music
author: Chuck Klosterman
description: Kaleidoscopic culture critic Chuck Klosterman rewrites the history of reality in a work of speculative nonfiction based on a question that has never been considered or (in all likelihood) even asked: What if The Beatles had only developed a cult following while the Velvet Underground emerged as the most popular band in the world?

title: Said the Dead
author: Doireann Ní Ghríofa
description: From the author of A Ghost in the Throat , a time-traversing, form-defying, genre-morphing story of a reader unraveling the legacies of a fabled Irish asylum and the women who haunt its halls.

title: Swan Song: Diana, My Sister
author: Charles Spencer
description: The life and death of Diana, as told by her brother, Charles.

title: Cloud Six
author: Amy Fusselman
description: Following a catastrophic plane crash, married couple Mam and Bunko have found themselves in Cloud Six. It's the newest, and lowest, tier of heaven, run by a slumlord demon named Widdershins who takes the form of an underwear model. With a rabbit skeleton as their guide, the pair do their best to remain hopeful and together in their quest: to navigate the strangest of places, to find help, and to catch even one glimpse of the teen daughter they left behind.

title: Valley of Death: How Big Tech Is Fueling the Future of War
author: Sharon Weinberger
description: A national security correspondent reveals how a new military-industrial complex is arising from the cradle of Silicon Valley, with vast implications for American democracy and the global balance of power.

title: Birth of a Culture
author: Grandmaster Flash
description:
Step into the vibrant streets of the 1970s Bronx and witness the exact moment a global movement began. Birth of a Culture Embed our reviews widget for this book
What is this?

title: Exit Party
author: Emily St. John Mandel
description: A novel of doubles, shadow worlds, and fractured timelines as a man disappears from a glittering Los Angeles party, and a woman—a gunrunner, an art collector, an operative of the State—searches for answers.

title: Fallow
author: Sarah Anderson
description: The story of a young woman who signs up to be the world’s first in-house corporate surrogate, then finds herself caught up in a social experiment of another kind.

title: Our Noble Selves
author: Kate Atkinson
description: From the author of Life After Life . When crime correspondent turned war reporter Harry Flynn returns to Britain from Singapore in 1945, he takes a quiet job with the Festival of Britain, a government-funded endeavor aimed at celebrating the nation’s creativity, grit, and ingenuity. There, he joins a team of misfits and eccentrics as they help to ready the Festival for launch.

title: Redwood: The Untold Story of the Cold War's Most Extraordinary Spy
author: Ben MacIntyre
description: A true-life Cold War thriller: the untold story of a Russian double agent with a desperate secret—and the key to stopping a nuclear apocalypse.

title: The Newer World
author: Sebastian Barry
description: From the author of The Secret Scripture , a novel about one man’s life the in the aftermath of the Civil War.

title: End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World
author: Naomi Klein & Astra Taylor
description: An investigation into the apocalyptic thinking of the Christian nationalists, tech-bro reactionaries, and populist survivalists who increasingly define the contemporary right—and a recipe for how to fight them.

title: Call It Evil: Understanding the Trump Era
author: Susan Neiman
description: Call It Evil is a reckoning with one of the most fraught words in our vocabulary. Far from being a religious or outdated concept, evil is a vital lens, Susan Neiman argues, through which to understand the threats we face today.

title: Live Laugh Love: The Secret History of White Christian Women and the World They Made
author: Kristin Kobes Du Mez
description: Live Laugh Love explores a world intimately familiar to millions of American women: Christian bookstores and radio, Hallmark movies, multilevel marketing companies, and contemporary lifestyle brands. Du Mez explains how theological exclusion led women to build their own brand of Christianity, rich in cultural influence if thin in formal doctrine.

title: The Queen of Bad Influences: Stories
author: Jim Shepard

title: Soldiers & Sailors
author: Terrence Holt
description: An elegiac novel of war and peace, of fathers and sons, of fading memory and the terror of what cannot be forgotten, Soldiers & Sailors follows the tortured career of Dr. Hal Adams.

title: The Rouse
author: China Miéville
description: Maur’s life has been shaped by loss: an apparently ordinary tragedy. But in its aftermath arise deeper, stranger questions. Their answers may lie within the dark heart and darker history of an old soldier who shares Maur’s obsessions and who is violently pursued by the same unknown, unquiet forces. So begins a book unlike any other: at once an encyclopaedic and multitudinous saga of a bloody century and the intimate story of two lives, their loves, regrets, and secrets—and a terrifying journey into infinite mystery.

title: When America Roared: How the 1980s Saved, Then Broke, the Country--And Led Us to Today
author: Jonathan Kaufman
description: The panoramic story of the 1980s, exploring the triumphs and failures of the decade that shaped the 21st century more than any other, from a Pulitzer Prize winning reporter who witnessed the transformations firsthand.

title: The Everywhere Millionaire: Who Is Really Rich in America and How They Got There
author: Owen Zidar
description: From two leading economists comes a portrait of the hidden fortunes of Main Street business owners―ordinary Americans who built extraordinary wealth and are quietly rewriting the rules of money and power.

title: Hollow Bones
author: Jodi Picoult
description: On September 11, 2001, when Molly Fitzgerald was only two months old, her mother went to an appointment at the World Trade Center and never came home. Her father and the stepmother who raised her couldn’t have loved her more, but she still grew up with a healthy dread of disasters. Now an adult, she runs the Rhode Island Department for Emergency Preparedness, mapping out ways to save lives during storms, epidemics, and airplane crashes. Moving between past and present, Hollow Bones is a story of the lies we tell ourselves as we write the narratives of our lives, the plans we design to protect ourselves at the worst moments, and the ties that bind mothers and daughters.

title: American Nightmare
author: Kelly McWilliams
description: In this historical novel, a light-skinned Black man goes undercover to investigate lynchings in the South, only to be confronted by the very evil that has pursued him since childhood.

title: Switzy
author: Emma Cline
description: From the author The Girls and The Guest , a portrait of an aging man’s last pilgrimage.

title: Taipei Story
author: R. F. Kuang
description: A coming-of-age novel that grapples with grief, language, and culture shock—all set against the backdrop of an unforgettable summer in Taipei.

title: Money to Burn: The Unvarnished Truth about Leon Black, Apollo, and the Rise of a New Wall Street
author: William D. Cohan
description: The sweeping tale of a powerful and controversial financial empire, set against the turbulent backdrop of a rapidly changing Wall Street.

title: Ambivalence: An Education
author: Brian Dillon
description: A coming-of-age memoir set in late-twentieth-century Dublin, recounting writer and critic Brian Dillon's first encounters with pivotal writers in his life—Virginia Woolf, Samuel Beckett, Walter Benjamin, and others—and in the process arguing for the transformative power of art, literature, and learning.

title: The Pirate Queen
author: Ariel Lawhon
description: A historical adventure inspired by the life of Grace O’Malley, the legendary Irish folk heroine who risked everything to defend her people.

title: The Living Realm
author: Jordan Tannahill
description: While cruising one evening by Teufelssee, a small glacial lake in the Grunewald forest on the edge of Berlin, a man spots a handsome stranger who bears an uncanny resemblance to his former lover. Only, Lukas died nearly thirty years ago. Yet the man cannot shake the feeling that it was really Lukas he saw. As the man spends a long, hot summer by the lake, he continues to encounter Lukas, and then other lost lovers as well. As he attempts to make sense of the strange occurrences and learns more of Teufelssee, he finds himself venturing deeper into the mystery of the forest, leading him to question not just his sanity but the nature of time itself.

title: Living with Freddie: How a Dog Taught Me to Be Human
author: Anna Heyward
description: A memoir about learning to see the world through a dog’s eyes.

title: Frenchman Flat: The Rise and Fall of Atomic Bombs
author: Jon Else
description: Jon Else combines history, science, politics, popular culture, and personal testimony into a narrative of the American nuclear enterprise, from Los Alamos to the 1990s, tracing the production of ever more powerful nuclear weapons, the consequences of fallout from them, and the efforts to ban testing entirely.

title: In the Realm of the Last Man: A Memoir
author: Francis Fukuyama
description: Francis Fukuyama, a leading public intellectual, is well-known for his landmark, bestselling works of political philosophy and history. Here, for the first time, he charts his political and intellectual evolution across five transformative decades.

title: Is This It: The Never-Ending Rise and Fall of the Strokes (and Rock 'n' Roll)
author: Steven Hyden
description: An analysis of the rise and fall of rock n' roll through the lens of one of the best albums of the 21st century, The Strokes' Is This It .

title: Love Machines: How Artificial Intelligence Is Transforming Our Relationships
author: James Muldoon
description: An uncanny journey to the frontier of human-computer interaction, exploring what happens to our relationships with each other as artificial intelligence enters our personal lives.

title: The Passing of the Dragon and Other Stories
author: Ken Liu
description: A new anthology of stories from Ken Liu, author of the Nebula and Hugo Award–winning The Paper Menagerie and Other Stories .

title: Tower Hill: A Plantation on the Edge of Rebellion
author: Alan Taylor
description: The Nat Turner rebellion of August 1831, the iconic uprising of enslaved people in the United States, was much more extensive than we have understood. This exploration of a Tidewater Virginia plantation reveals how the daily resistance of the enslaved was heightened by spiritual beliefs to seek the divine overthrow of a wicked world.

title: Songs My Mother Taught Me: Why the Artist Must Take Sides
author: Saul Williams
description: Songs My Mother Taught Me is Williams' exploration of the role of the artist in these times by answering the question: what radicalized you? He answers by examining how his role models--writers and artists, from Amiri Baraka to local musicians in Brazilian bars to Palestinian hip-hop heads--have responded to imperialist violence, oppression, and genocide.

title: Acid Green Velvet
author: Grace Krilanovich
description: Californian freakiness meets Victorian preoccupations with the domestic, pollution and filth, haunted houses, fringe societies, living death, spiritualism, vampiric women, and class parasites. Acid Green Velvet is a blend of nihilism, fathers and their failures, manifest destiny, and American identity.

title: Monumental: A Stonemason's Tale
author: Simon Warrack
description: Discover ancient stone wonders and the secrets of architectural preservation through the eyes and hands of one of the world's greatest stonemasons.

title: The Art of Fighting: The Transformative Power of Conflict
author: Priya Parker
description: We say we want community. Successful teams. High-performing colleagues and workplaces. Dynamic friend groups. Yet many of us don’t understand the crucial element we need to forge long-lasting communities in our lives: healthy conflict. In The Art of Fighting , Priya Parker explains that we can’t form and grow effective relationships without a fight. She rejects the idea that conflict is abnormal or that good groups don’t fight. All groups change and evolve; indeed, it’s because people disagree that good groups flourish.

title: The Disappearers
author: Marlon James
description: From the Booker Prize-winning author of A Brief History of Seven Killings , the story of the murder of a gay man in 1980s Jamaica and its far-reaching consequences.

title: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea: Journeys Through Ancient Literature
author: Emily Wilson
description: From a celebrated translator of our time comes an exploration of how translation reshapes and enriches our understanding of the ancient world.

title: The Castle: Adventures in a World of Unraveling Men
author: Jon Ronson
description: From the author of The Psychopath Test and So You’ve Been Publicly Shamed , a darkly comic trip to the furthest reaches of the masculinity crisis.

title: Agrippa
author: Robert Harris
description: A tale of ancient Rome’s descent into dictatorship.

title: Under Story
author: Chloe Benjamin
description: At the edge of the world, biologist Laurel Salter is hiding from everything she’s ever known. For ten hours a day, six days per week, she works as a dishwasher at McMurdo Station, an isolated research base in Antarctica. She tells no one that before she arrived, she was a renowned young scientist with a promising career and a family. But even in this remote outpost, Laurel can’t escape her past. When a strange light appears across the ice—and draws a group of physicists to McMurdo—her former husband, Eli, won't be far behind. Laurel is captivated by the Arc: its surreal glow; the way it seems almost alive. And though Eli is reluctant to test her wildest theory, Laurel is convinced that the Arc leads down a rabbit hole and into a world they can barely imagine. Can she persuade him to risk everything to fix the burden that hangs between them—to turn back the clock and live their story a second time?

title: American Scoundrel: Roy Cohn's Dark Journey from Joe McCarthy to Donald Trump
author: Kai Bird
description: A biography of super-lawyer and political fixer Roy Cohn, whose shocking exploits over four decades have shaped the modern political era, most prominently the ascent of Donald Trump.

title: The Bed Trick: Sex and Deception on Trial
author: Izabella Scott
description: An account of a court case in which a woman accused her best friend of impersonating a man during sex, and won—a study of desire, performance, truth, and the stories we tell about ourselves in public, online, in love, and in law.

title: I Liked Rex
author: Diane Williams
description: From “the godmother of flash fiction," a new collection of thirty-six short stories about the mysteries of life and the human heart.

title: Asmodeus
author: Rita Indiana
description: A hallucinatory thriller about a failing demon's search for a new host in post-dictatorship Santo Domingo.

title: Profits, Prophets, Coaches, and Kings: (When) Do Leaders Matter?
author: Jared Diamond
description: Can one person change the world? What qualities determine effective leadership? How do individual talent and historical circumstances combine to shape great leaders? From Jared Diamond, a study of leadership across politics, religion, business, and sports—seeking to decode how and why leaders matter.

title: Huna: A Memoir of Revolution, Prison, and Becoming
author: Abdelrahman Elgendy
description: A memoir of survival, education, and resistance by a student protestor–turned–political prisoner in post-revolution Egypt.

title: The Rise and Fall of American Europe
author: Glyn Morgan
description: At the dawn of the Cold War, the US administration pushed reluctant Europeans to create a federation of democratic states. In doing so, they gave birth to an American Europe – a new political order protected by the US military and buoyed by transatlantic trade. Europe now faces a stark reality. The Trump Administration dislikes NATO, considers the EU's trade policies "worse than China['s]," and attacks the banning of nationalist parties. Many in the MAGA movement are similarly hostile to Europe, which they see as an overregulated museum, a US dependency, powerless on the world-stage. This book explains why American Europe fell from favor.

title: The Birthing Tree
author: Amanda Peters
description: From the author of The Berry Pickers , a novel about a woman who must confront her family’s buried truths and memories of passionate young love when her grandmother’s death leaves her as the only guide to her community’s future.

title: 53 Days: How Hitler Dismantled a Democracy
author: Timothy W Ryback
description: A chronicle of how Adolf Hitler overturned a constitutional democracy in less than eight weeks.

title: Life of M
author: Rachel Cusk
description: The movie star M is one of the most recognizable faces of our time. Her image is everywhere. It has been like that since she was a child. With such fame, her life has the appearance of freedom: people are instantly obliging, spaces are altered to accommodate her, time can be rearranged. M may live in the same places as real people. She may meet her friends or collect her children from school or walk her dogs as they do. But it seems the rules of reality have melted away. Now, a writer has decided to pay close attention to M’s life in the hope of understanding who she really is. It is hard not to feel ugly next to M, hard not to feel insignificant. But what truths—about the very experience of living—might this proximity allow the writer to briefly capture?

title: Dèy
author: Edwidge Danticat
description: A story, moving from Haiti to Brooklyn to Miami, of a woman whose sense of self and family are called into question when she gets caught in a random act of violence one sunny Florida day.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State
author: Jill Lepore
description: An account of how rule by machine has ravaged the world.

title: The Anniversary
author: Andrea Bajani, trans. by Geoffrey Brock
description: A portrait of an abusive marriage in patriarchal Italy and a son’s liberating decision to cut contact with his parents.

title: Big Little Truths
author: Liane Moriarty
description: The last time we saw the women of Big Little Lies —Madeline, Celeste, Jane, Renata, and Bonnie—their children were five years old. If someone wasn’t invited to a birthday party, feelings were hurt. But ten years have passed and the kids are in high school, navigating all of the drama that accompanies teendom (goodbye playdates, hello drugs, sex, and alcohol). When a stranger begins lurking around the school asking supposedly innocent questions, this tightly connected group of women must finally face the full repercussions of the big little truths they have and haven’t shared with their kids. Because the stakes are now much higher than not being invited to an ice-skating party—and the ice has never been thinner for any of them.

title: The Jackal: The Rise and Fall of Carlos, the World's First Super-Terrorist
author: Joby Warrick
description: The rise and fall of super-assassin Carlos the Jackal—one of history’s most infamous terrorist masterminds and the inspiration for numerous celebrated works of pop culture.

title: Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis's Trans Pioneer
author: Julie Kliegman
description: The definitive biography of professional tennis’s first openly transgender player, Renée Richards, featuring archival photos and untold stories.

title: Range
author: Dorthe Nors, trans. by Caroline Waight
description: An astrophysicist searches for her place among her neighbors and in the universe.

title: The Book of Chuck
author: Latoya Watkins
description: Set across Texas and spanning four generations, The Book of Chuck is an investigation into birthright and belonging through the story of one family in which certain members have clairvoyant powers.

title: The Maltese Version
author: Katy Simpson Smith
description: A novel of four women forging their way across time, place, and language in search of desire, power, and connection.

title: The Song of Stork and Dromedary
author: Anjet Daanje, trans. by David McKay
description: Who was Eliza May Drayden? Is she just the quiet, intensely private person she seems to all the world in her little village of Bridge Fowling in the shadow of the West Yorkshire hills—or is there more to her than meets the eye? It is only after her death that Haeger Mass, her one book—a dark and cryptic novel—assumes a life of its own. In each new chapter of this literary treasure hunt that spans almost three hundred years, we see the conundrum through the eyes of a new generation of characters, each providing competing and interlocking versions of the life—and cursed vision—of this Emily Brontë–like figure. Scholars immerse themselves in the mystery of her life and are led to ruin; the curse that hangs over her comes to visit a young couple; a mysterious diary emerges with her strange and indecipherable poetry and sketches. Elements and symbols repeat in relentless and varying combinations from one story to the next as the years pass: as if the truth at the center of her work is fighting to break free.

title: The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy
author: Gil Durán
description: A chronicle of the tech-authoritarian movement from its early days in San Francisco politics to its current moment on the international stage, exploring the dystopian ambition of the technocrats at its center, and offering a road map to resistance.

title: Nearshore
author: Steve Hawk
description: A mix of literary suspense and coastal noir—where the clash between land and sea unearths Silicon Valley’s darkest secret, and three people must reckon with all that is at stake in an age shadowed by greed, totalitarianism, and nuclear terror.

title: The Next Journalism: How the Press Must Change to Serve Democracy
author: Tom Rosenstiel
description: A case that the survival of democracy depends on reinventing the press, with ten pioneering reforms to help journalism better serve the public.

title: Unprecedented Times
author: Malavika Kannan
description: Which comes first: experience or narrative? Rishi thinks she knows the answer as she arrives on campus for her first year at Stanford. A burnt-out youth climate activist, she used to want to save the world, but now she just wants to have gay sex. Her plan is set—she’s going to leave behind the strict trappings of her Indian American childhood in Florida, study literature, experiment with love, and write all about it. Within a few months, she makes her first best friend, falls in love with her situationship, and promptly gets her heart broken. What is not a part of Rishi’s plan is the onset of the COVID pandemic. As the outside world becomes a terrifying place, she increasingly finds solace in the friendships she’s made. Instead of virtual college, however, Rishi and her classmates join a farm collective, where their political discussions and growing disillusionment collide with sexual tension and responsibility. It’s only when those relationships start fracturing under the stress of careless decisions, unrequited crushes, jealousies, and, yes, unprecedented times, that Rishi begins to question her own story.

title: Togetherness: Symbiosis and the Hidden Story of Life's Greatest Collaborations
author: Rowan Hooper
description: An exploration of the surprising ways life is interconnected—and why it matters.

title: The Breakup
author: Kurt Andersen
description: Natalie and Asher’s marriage has long been marked by fault lines, quiet rifts in how they view their fellow Americans and navigate AI-suffused life in 2045. After twenty-three years together, and after surviving the two years of civil war in the 2030s, Natalie in rural Tennessee (part of the new Free American Republic) and Asher in San Francisco (in the now smaller United States). Natalie and Asher’s relationship mirrors America’s own unraveling—confused, messy, painful, ambivalent, and impossibly intimate. When Natalie and Asher are brought back into proximity while touring far-flung colleges with their seventeen-year-old, they find themselves on a road trip through a strange, uncertain new American landscape, transformed by both the terrorist uprising and technology, all while dealing with the flux—and resilience—within their own family. They face the questions the nation has reckoned with for a generation: what differences are irreconcilable, and when is something broken worth saving?

title: Sunrise
author: Téa Obreht
description: From the author of The Tiger's Wife and Inland . Three lives, one hundred years, one ghost town: a novel about a mysterious place called Sunrise, where the secrets of the past refuse to stay buried.

title: A Tender Age
author: Chang-Rae Lee
description: From the author of Native Speaker and The Surrendered , a novel about guilt, innocence, and a boy on the cusp of adolescence.

title: Under the Falls
author: Richard Russo
description: A novel about a crime in a small town that exposes long-held secrets and betrayals among a group of lifelong friends.

title: The Responsible Party
author: Claire Carusillo
description: Claire grew up with the legend of the Unsinkable Mounsey Women. Her great-great-grandmother Fanny made headlines in 1915 for washing ashore in England nearly a year after her ship sank. Fanny’s daughter Sarah went to collect her mother on the equally ill-fated Lusitania—whose sinking she, too, survived. Their improbable endurance led to regional stardom on the Midwestern vaudeville circuit. But Claire never knew the full story—until now.

title: Depraved: The Story of Dangerous Art
author: Daisy Dixon
description: Philosopher and artist Daisy Dixon explores works of art that society has condemned as depraved, obscene, or dangerous, from prehistoric sculpture to extreme metal music, videogames to classical paintings. Interrogating our sense of morality, past and present, Depraved asks readers to engage with essential questions about art, censorship, social progress, and the eternal debate over right and wrong.

title: A Guide to Open Water Lifesaving: Lessons on Love, Care, and Survival: A Memoir
author: Virginia Eubanks
description: Someone you love, maybe the person you love most in the world, is drowning. Should you jump in the water? Will you be able to bring both of you back to shore?

title: Fed Up: What Evolution Reveals about Food, Diet, Health, and Eating Well
author: Daniel E Lieberman

title: Days of Miracle and Wonder: Paul Simon and the Trials and Triumphs of Graceland
author: Ashley Kahn
description: The story of the making and legacy of Graceland, Paul Simon’s still-beloved, career-topping 1986 album, drawn from extensive research and exclusive interviews with nearly 100 participants and witnesses: musicians, producers, engineers, record executives and journalists from Africa, the US, and Europe.

title: Hannah Arendt: A Life of the Mind
author: Thomas Meyer
description: An intellectual biography of Hannah Arendt, one of the greatest philosophers of the twentieth century.

title: Hocus Pocus
author: Brinda Charry
description: A young magician travels across the world seeking fame and fortune all the while hiding a secret, in a novel based on the renowned, real-life Indian stage magicians performing in the United States in the 1800s.

title: Are They Dead Yet?: The Art of the Obit
author: Sam Roberts
description: From New York Times obituarist Sam Roberts, the art of the obit: Who we remember, how we forget, and where we find the true meaning in a life.

title: Awake Awake
author: Fiona Mozley
description: Mary has started remembering things that she knows aren't real—but the events feel exactly like her actual memories. Who is she, if she can't be sure she knows her own past?

title: Etna
author: Paul Yoon
description: The story of a working dog, Etna, who, after a devastating war, embarks on an odyssey in the hopes of returning home.

title: Triage
author: Claudia Rankine
description: Follows the turbulent friendship between two composite characters, the narrator and the theorist, self-identified sisters struggling to define their wounded histories and their shared but separate lives. During college, they invent a game of collapse: Every time they see each other, they have to stop and fall to the ground. As their kinship continues off and on for decades, “collapse” takes on new meanings that are seen and felt in the violence of their pasts, artworks depicting couches where someone might ease their exhaustion, the ongoing devastation in Gaza, and the antagonism of their conversation and their love for each other.

title: The Amateur
author: Chris Bohjalian
