description: The Longe siblings are really botching their parents' American Dream. In the wreckage of their fateful reunion, each Longe is forced to reckon with the past, take stock of what really matters, and find a way back to each other.

title: A Terrible Intimacy: Interracial Life in the Slaveholding South
author: Melvin Patrick Ely
description: A new account of slavery, uncovering a surprising web of relationships between Black and white people.

title: The Future Is Peace: A Shared Journey Across the Holy Land
author: Aziz Abu Sarah
description: Two lifelong peace activists and guides to Israel/Palestine, both of whom have lost family in the conflict, take readers on a journey across this holy, bloodstained land and discover the mythic, political, and personal history that divides but also binds them and their peoples.

title: Rasputin: The Downfall of the Romanovs
author: Antony Beevor
description: A new biography of one of history’s most disturbing, dubious masterminds, showing how a Siberian peasant, through his seduction of the imperial household, contributed to the collapse of the greatest autocracy in the world.

title: Famesick: A Memoir
author: Lena Dunham
description: In this frank reflection on illness, fame, sex, and everything in between, the mind behind the hit series Girls asks whether fulfilling her creative ambitions has been worth the pain.

title: Where the Music Had to Go: How Bob Dylan and the Beatles Changed Each Other--And the World
author: Jim Windolf
description: This dual biography dives into the surprisingly supportive, occasionally rivalrous, and always fertile relationship between Bob Dylan and the Beatles, uncovering how they inspired and transformed each other as songwriters, recording artists, and cultural icons.

title: The Violence: My Family's Colombian War
author: Adriana E. Ramírez
description: A chronicle of Colombia’s descent into decades of civil war through the lens of a multi-generational tale of upheaval and betrayal.

title: A Private Man
author: Stephanie Sy-Quia
description: A debut novel inspired by the true story of the author's grandparents, tracing the slow-burn love story between a Catholic priest and a progressive theology teacher across Rome and England during the twentieth century.

title: Korean Messiah: Kim Il Sung and the Christian Roots of North Korea's Personality Cult
author: Jonathan Cheng
description: A history of North Korea and the Hermit Kingdom, told through the rise of the Kim dynasty and its surprising ties to American Christianity.

title: Empire of Skulls: Phrenology, the Fowler Family, and a New Nation's Quest to Unlock the Secrets of the Mind
author: Paul Stob
description: A tale of science and showmanship, ideology and enterprise, that provides not just a history of our country, but also insight into the deep currents that continue to propel modern life.

title: Jan Morris: A Life
author: Sara Wheeler
description: A literary biography of the immortal travel writer, journalist and twentieth-century trans pioneer, Jan Morris.

title: Transcription
author: Ben Lerner
description: An emotional drama and an examination of the devices, digital and literary, we use to store—or to erase—our memories.

title: The Witch
author: Marie Ndiaye, trans. by Jordan Stump
description: In a small, sleepy town, a mediocre witch, in a mediocre marriage, tries to pass on her gifts to her twin daughters, who, it becomes immediately apparent, have skills far beyond her own.

title: This Land Is Your Land: A Road Trip Through U.S. History
author: Beverly Gage
description: Historian Beverly Gage takes the ultimate road trip into the American past.

title: Mutiny: The Rise and Revolt of the College-Educated Working Class
author: Noam Scheiber
description: The story of a disillusioned generation that set out to reclaim its dignity and take on corporate America.

title: My Dear You: Stories
author: Rachel Khong
description: A short story collection about love, life, and the anguish of becoming oneself in a time when it’s so easy to be someone else.

title: London Falling: A Mysterious Death in a Gilded City and a Family's Search for Truth
author: Patrick Radden Keefe
description: An account of a family devastated by the sudden death of their nineteen-year-old son, only to discover that he had created a secret life which drew him into the dangerous criminal underworld that lies beneath London’s glittering surface.

title: What We Are Seeking
author: Cameron Reed
description: On the planet Scythia, plants give birth to insects and trees can drag you to your death. Artificial monsters stalk the desert, and alien basket-men have wandered into town. John Maraintha has been abandoned here, light-years from the peaceful forests that he loves. The desert is harsh and the people in thrall to a barbaric custom called marriage. He must find some way to make a life here. But on Scythia, survival means transformation—and not everyone is willing to change

title: The Confessions of Samuel Pepys: Private Revelations from Britain's Most Famed Diarist
author: Guy de la Bédoyère
description: A collection of the most personal aspects of Samuel Pepys’ diaries, in celebration of the two hundredth anniversary of their publication.

title: Attention: Writing on Life, Art, and the World
author: Anne Enright
description: Attention explores the intersection between the personal and political, the subtleties of bodily autonomy, complex family dynamics, and the challenges of intimacy. Here we see Enright grappling with and answering these questions in nonfiction.

title: The Oyster Diaries
author: Nancy Lemann
description: A diaristic novel of middle-aged reckoning that roves from Washington, D.C. to New Orleans, from court records to Don Giovanni .

title: Yesteryear
author: Caro Claire Burke
description: A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister.

title: American Fantasy
author: Emma Straub
description: A story about what happens when your teenage fantasy comes true after you’re already an adult.

title: Here Where We Live Is Our Country: The Story of the Jewish Bund
author: Molly Crabapple
description: The story of the Jewish Bund—a revolutionary movement from a vanished world—and its radical vision of solidarity in an age of division.

title: Hexes of the Deadwood Forest
author: Agnieszka Szpila, trans. by Scotia Gilroy
description: A debut novel about a woman who loses her job as an oil company CEO after she’s filmed having sex with a tree in her sleep, a calamity that unravels her mind, spiraling her through history until she’s united with a centuries-old coven of ecstatically revolutionary women.

title: The Ending Writes Itself
author: Evelyn Clarke
description: Arthur Fletch, one of the world’s bestselling novelists, is a reclusive genius known for his iconic protagonists and fiendish twists. When six struggling authors are invited to spend a weekend on his private Scottish island, they arrive to discover a shocking secret: Arthur Fletch is dead ... and his last book is unfinished.

title: The Oracle's Daughter: The Rise and Fall of an American Cult
author: Harrison Hill
description: A chronicle of the rise and fall of a woman-led cult—and the enduring allure of extremism across America’s turbulent religious history.

title: Day Care: Stories
author: Nora Lange
description: A ransacking of the house of motherhood and matrimony. With stories of lust, estrangement, and self-preservation, Day Care is a reflection on economic precarity, love, and peeing your pants.

title: Vermeer: A Life Lost and Found
author: Andrew Graham-Dixon
description: This biography addresses the two great unresolved questions about Vermeer: why did he paint his pictures, and what do they mean?

title: Like This, But Funnier
author: Hallie Cantor
description: When TV writer Caroline accidentally stumbles on her therapist husband Harry’s patient session notes and offhandedly mentions what she finds in a meeting with a producer, the momentum of Hollywood takes over. Before she knows it—and unbeknownst to Harry—Caroline finds herself pitching a TV show about the deepest, darkest secrets of her husband’s favorite patient, a woman known to Caroline only as the Teacher.

title: Like, Follow, Subscribe: Influencer Kids and the Cost of a Childhood Online
author: Fortesa Latifi
description: An investigation into the child influencer industry, the perils of childhood internet fame, and the ethics of online content.

title: The Keeper
author: Tana French
description: The third and final book in Tana French's Cal Hooper trilogy.

title: The Life You Want
author: Adam Phillips
description: Adam Phillips uses psychoanalytic and literary approaches to show that we are obsessed by the idea of our lives being ones we want and enjoy rather than merely endure, tolerate, or make the most of.

title: The News from Dublin: Stories
author: Colm Tóibín
description: A collection of nine short stories, many never-before-published, set across Ireland, Spain, and America—about the complexities of family, longing, loss, and love.

title: Kutchinsky's Egg: A Family's Story of Obsession, Love, and Loss
author: Serena Kutchinsky
description: A family memoir that blends art, obsession, and love as the author searches for the spectacular jeweled egg that consumed her father’s dreams—and spelled her family’s downfall.

title: Metropolitans: New York Baseball, Class Struggle, and the People's Team
author: A. M. Gittlitz
description: A love letter to a franchise and a study of New York City, Metropolitans traces the calamitous history of the New York Mets.

title: All Carry
author: Gene Wojciechowski
description: Joe is a golf reporter. Max 'Hard Way' Mitchell used to be one of the best caddies on the PGA Tour. When Joe is laid-off, and Hardway realizes that with a magical set of golf clubs he is better than anyone on the tour, he convinces Joe to do the seemingly impossible—win the Masters as an amateur.

title: Son of Nobody
author: Yann Martel
description: A retelling of the Trojan War from the perspective of two commoners: an ancient soldier and a modern scholar.

title: No New York: A Memoir of No Wave and the Women Who Shaped the Scene
author: Adele Bertei
description: An insider's account of New York's No Wave cultural revolution and the women who obliterated every barrier in their path.

title: American Han
author: Lisa Lee
description: Growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area in the 1980s, Jane Kim and her brother, Kevin, dutifully embodied the model minority myth as their parents demanded: Jane went on to law school. Kevin came close to becoming a professional tennis player. But where they started is nowhere near where they have ended up: Jane has stopped going to her law school classes, and Kevin, now a policeman, has become increasingly distant. Their parents, each on their own path toward the elusive American Dream, don't want to see the family unraveling. When Kevin goes missing, no one recognizes his absence as the warning sign it is until it erupts, forcing them all to come to terms with their past and present selves in a country that isn't all it promised it would be.

title: A Good Person
author: Kirsten King
description: A woman seeks revenge on her ex-situationship with a hex, only for him to actually, literally die.

title: The Adjunct
author: Maria Adelmann
description: A take on the campus novel that follows an adjunct professor gigging her way through academia’s poor job market when she crosses paths with her old PhD adviser, whose new novel might be about her.

title: Upward Bound
author: Woody Brown
description: Upward Bound is not a place anyone dreams of spending their days. The dreary adult daycare center for Los Angeles's disabled community is, for many of its clients and staff, a place of last resort. This includes Carlos, a young aide who lost his mother as a boy and now works there alongside his beloved sister Delia; Jorge, the gentle nonverbal giant whom Carlos seeks to befriend (and prevent from escaping); Tom, a beautiful young man with cerebral palsy, who pines for Ann, the summer lifeguard at the center's pool who feels out of her depth; then there's Mike, Upward Bound's director who came to L.A. to pursue an acting career but now channels his passion into staging an impressive holiday show starring the center's sorely underestimated clients.

title: True Color: The Strange and Spectacular Quest to Define Color--From Azure to Zinc Pink
author: Kory Stamper
description: A journey through the secret history of hues—and the story of the obsessive genius behind the definitions of colors we use today.

title: When the Forest Breathes: Renewal and Resilience in the Natural World
author: Suzanne Simard
description: The scientist who pioneered the concept of sophisticated communication between trees now offers a vision for saving our forests, based on nature’s deep-rooted cycles of renewal.

title: Python's Kiss: Stories
author: Louise Erdrich
description: Written over the past two decades, Louise Erdrich’s story collection features a range of characters—a tribal newsletter editor whose son tells her a story that nothing in her experience can encompass, immigrant farmers whose tenuous hold on the earth, and sanity, is challenged, and ordinary people, bird lovers, artists, grade-school teachers, and romantics. A girl decides to spend her life with a stone. A man is confronted with a folk-singing thief. A woman enters a corporately owned afterlife to seek revenge on her father.

title: Darkology: Blackface and the American Way of Entertainment
author: Rhae Lynn Barnes
description: A history that chronicles how blackface dominated American society culturally, financially, and racially for nearly two centuries.

title: Almost Life
author: Kiran Millwood Hargrave
description: Two young women meet in Paris one sultry summer in a decades-spanning story about the enduring power of young love and the heartbreak of missed chances.

title: Who Needs Friends: An Unscientific Examination of Male Friendship Across America
author: Andrew McCarthy
description: An exploration of male friendship and loneliness, from actor Andrew McCarthy as he crisscrosses the country to reconnect with his friends.

title: Open Space: From Earth to Eternity—The Global Race to Explore and Conquer the Cosmos
author: David Ariosto
description: The next space race has arrived—driven by rival nations, billionaire-funded ventures, and breakthrough technologies all vying to alter the balance of power on Earth and beyond.

title: Western Star: The Life and Legends of Larry McMurtry
author: David Streitfeld
description: The definitive biography of Larry McMurtry, the author and screenwriter of Lonesome Dove .

title: A Beautiful Loan
author: Mary Costello
description: A young woman finds herself in and out of love in this intimate novel.

title: How Flowers Made Our World: The Story of Nature's Revolutionaries
author: David George Haskell
description: An exploration of the power of flowers, placing them at the center of the story of how evolution created the world we know today.

title: Returning: A Search for Home Across Three Centuries
author: Nicholas Lemann
description: A family saga that follows the narrator as he rejects this assimilated world and embraces the rites of Judaism through a combination of biography and philosophy.

title: The Power of Life: The Invention of Biology and the Revolutionary Science of Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
author: Jessica Riskin
description: In the early nineteenth century, the French naturalist Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed the first evolutionary theory of life and, with it, a new science: biology. In this melding of biography, history, politics, and science, Jessica Riskin tells the story of Lamarck’s life and work as an intense struggle between rival forces to answer questions that remain foundational to our modern worldview: What is a living being, and what is science?

title: A Treacherous Secret Agent: How Literature Spoke Truth to Power During the Red Scare
author: Marjorie Garber
description: An account of the subversive acts of literary revenge performed during the Red Scare hearings of the 1950s, and the voices that rose in opposition to the House Un-American Activities Committee.

title: Celestial Lights
author: Cecile Pin
description: January 28, 1986: Soon after launch, the Challenger shuttle falls out of the sky and into the sea. At the same time, Oliver Ines is born. Celestial Lights is his story. A portrait of a complicated man and a tale of memory, personal choices, and the relationships that define us.

title: The Information State: Politics in the Age of Total Control
author: Jacob Siegel
description: We’re often told that disinformation is everywhere and that it’s endangering our democracy. But what if the war on disinformation itself is really just a weapon to squash any and all legitimate dissent? The Information State is an examination of how we reached the point where anything that contradicts the dominant narrative can be labeled dangerous disinformation.

title: The Insatiable Machine: How Capitalism Conquered the World
author: Trevor Jackson
description: Today, a vast majority of us live under the economic system called capitalism--it touches almost every aspect of our lives, and most people alive have never known another. Yet, a cursory look at the world around us reveals that things can't stay this way forever: an economy built on infinite amassing and consumption of resources is at odds with a finite planet. How did this happen? Economic historian Trevor Jackson provides an account of capitalism's rise to global dominance.

title: The Beheading Game
author: Rebecca Lehmann
description: We all know what happened to Henry VIII’s second wife, Anne Boleyn. But what if she woke up the day after her execution and took it upon herself to seek justice?

title: Sisters in Yellow
author: Mieko Kawakami, trans. by Hitomi Yoshio and Laurel Taylor
description: A novel of sacrifice and the tumultuous bonds of sisterhood, set in the gritty Tokyo of the 1990s.

title: Hooked: A Novel of Obsession
author: Asako Yuzuki, trans. by Polly Barton
description: A novel about obsession, female friendship, and the slow unraveling of two lives.

title: Stay Alive: Berlin, 1939-1945
author: Ian Buruma
description: An account of life under a murderous regime amid Berlin’s descent into utter annihilation during World War Two.

title: Lucien
author: J R Thornton
description: A gifted yet financially disadvantaged artist falls victim to the manipulative control of his wealthy, enigmatic Harvard roommate in this exploration of class, ambition, identity, and the perilous cost of reinvention.

title: The Feather Wars: And the Great Crusade to Save America's Birds
author: James H McCommons
description: A work of American history about how disparate characters came together to save hundreds of species of birds.

title: Under Water
author: Tara Menon
description: A novel about the devastating power of friendship, set against the backdrop of two cataclysmic events.

title: A Woman's Work: Reclaiming the Radical History of Mothering
author: Elinor Cleghorn
description: A narrative showcasing the mothers, othermothers, midwives, activists, community leaders, and more who have shaped the course of history.

title: Paradiso 17
author: Hannah Lillith Assadi
description: The tale of one Palestinian man’s restless search for home the world over, as the pendulum of fate swings between loss and life, grief and euphoria, regret and hope.

title: The Fountain
author: Casey Scieszka
description: Vera Van Valkenburgh hasn’t been home in one hundred and eighty-eight years. But now Vera, forever twenty-six and able to heal from any wound, has returned to the Catskills. Whatever made her family immortal happened here, and if she can uncover it, maybe she can reverse it. After nearly two centuries—an endless sequence of unnoticed, meaningless lives and a soul-shaking incident in the desert—she longs to be released.

title: The Secret History of French Cooking: The Outlaw Chefs Who Made Food Modern
author: Luke Barr
description: A cultural and culinary history of a group of French chefs in the late 1960s and 70s who revolutionized food culture, first at home and then, quickly, abroad.

title: I Am Agatha
author: Nancy Foley
description: A debut novel about Agatha, whose devotion to a widow with dementia (and an inconvenient attachment to her daughter’s grave) sparks a radical reckoning with life, loss, and love’s aftermath.

title: The Plans I Have for You
author: Lai Sanders
description: After a viral video costs her a spot at Columbia Law, her prestigious Manhattan law firm internship, and her hopes to build a better life for herself and her mother, Shelley Hu returns home to Florida, where new friend Sophia proposes a plan to rebuild her identity and exact revenge on those who brought her down.

title: In Search of Now: The Science of the Present Moment
author: Jo Marchant
description: A tour of the latest thinking in cosmology, quantum mechanics, psychology, and neuroscience to tackle the question of how we perceive time, events, and sensations.

title: Stephen Sondheim: Art Isn't Easy
author: Daniel Okrent
description: Drawing on Sondheim's intimate correspondence with such notable figures as Hal Prince, Leonard Bernstein, and Arthur Laurents, Daniel Okrent offers a look at the complex inner world of one of the twentieth century's most beloved theatrical composers.

title: Chain of Ideas: The Origins of Our Authoritarian Age
author: Ibram X Kendi
description: Ibram X. Kendi offers a global history of how great replacement theory brought humanity into this authoritarian age—and how we can free ourselves from it.

title: Black Bag
author: Luke Kennard
description: An out-of-work actor accepts the role of a lifetime—sitting soundlessly in a lecture theater, zipped into a large leather bag—to aid a professor’s psychological experiment. What could possibly go wrong?

title: My Lover, the Rabbi
author: Wayne Koestenbaum
description: A psychosexual relationship between a rabbi and the man devoted to him goes off the rails in the first novel from Wayne Koestenbaum in nearly twenty years.

title: Still Talking: Stories
author: Lore Segal
description: The final collection of stories from the late Lore Segal, with an introduction from Vivian Gornick.

title: I Love You Don't Die
author: Jade Song
description: A novel about the meaning of love, friendship, debt, depression, and death in New York City—a coming-of-age story for a new generation.

title: All the World Can Hold
author: Jung Yun
description: A novel set aboard an aging cruise ship bound for Bermuda, where growing tensions lead three strangers to confront their past regrets and imagine different futures.

title: In the Days of My Youth I Was Told What It Means to Be a Man: A Memoir
author: Tom Junod
description: A memoir about a charismatic, philandering father who tried to mold his son in his image, the many secrets he hid, the son’s obsessive quest to uncover them, and ultimately, the true meaning of manhood.

title: Nonesuch
author: Francis Spufford
description: A tale about an ambitious young woman who must thwart an occult plot by time-traveling fascists during the chaos of the London Blitz.

title: Whidbey
author: T Kira Madden
description: A portrait of three women connected through one man in the aftermath of his murder.

title: Kids, Wait Till You Hear This!
author: Liza Minnelli
description: Global icon Liza Minnelli shares her story: stepping out from the long shadow of a mega-star mother and legendary film director father, fighting a lifetime battle with addiction, and emerging from it all to become an artist.

title: Haven
author: Ani Katz
description: A summer retreat to an elite island enclave tied to a Big Tech company becomes a mother’s worst nightmare.

title: A Scandal in Königsberg
author: Christopher Clark
description: A true story from the aftermath of the Enlightenment period. Christopher Clark retells the cult scandal that sent shockwaves across nineteenth-century Prussia and sparked a movement for sexual freedom and liberation.

title: Down Time
author: Andrew Martin
description: A comic social novel of settling down, selling out, growing up, and getting out that turns a hyper-literate eye on our most desperately guarded ambitions: to love and be loved, to know and be known, to stay sane, if only just.

title: The Complex
author: Karan Mahajan
description: A novel moving between the US and modern India, following the illicit liaisons, real estate dramas, political ambitions, and mortal betrayals of one prominent Delhi family.

title: The Quantity Theory of Morality
author: Will Self
description: Self's middle-English characters appear trapped in a timeless go-round of polite chitchat in dinner parties that refract like a hall of mirrors, until one day someone says something to the effect of, "This way to the gas chamber, please, ladies and gentlemen."

title: Big Nobody
author: Alex Kadis
description: A coming-of-age novel about a misfit teenager in London determined to eliminate the one thing standing between her and a good life: her father.

title: Partially Devoured: How Night of the Living Dead Saved My Life and Changed the World
author: Daniel Kraus
description: Partially Devoured uses a frame-by-frame deep dive into Night of the Living Dead to produce a cultural investigation of the film’s importance and to examine the author’s early life of rural isolation and local violence.

title: Safe Passage: The Untold Story of Diplomatic Intrigue, Betrayal​, and the Exchange of American and Japanese Civilians by Sea During W​WII
author: Evelyn Iritani
description: An untold story of idealism, betrayal, and behind-the-scenes American–Japanese contacts in World War II.

title: Everybody's Fly: A Life of Art, Music, and Changing the Culture
author: Fab 5 Freddy with Mark Rozzo
description: Everybody’s Fly is at once a memoir and cultural history. It is a love letter to the art of seeing, an account of a creative life, and a celebration of what it means to shape culture.

title: The Golden Boy
author: Patricia Finn
description: After an involuntary retirement from his high-flying Hollywood career, Stafford Hopkins has retreated to a luxury estate on Maui, along with his wife Agnes, both grimly resigned to life in a paradise where neither feels fully at home. Returning to both the hardscrabble farming town and the dark secret he'd tried to forget for decades, Stafford is forced to confront his past in order to rebuild his future--and to redirect the fates of his family and the four young people suddenly in his care.

title: Spoiled Milk
author: Avery Curran
description: The untimely death of a student at a girls’ boarding school marks the first in a series of escalating supernatural events, and uncovers buried truths of teenage repression, queer desire, and the everyday horror of coming of age.

title: Judy Blume: A Life
author: Mark Oppenheimer
description: In Judy Blume , journalist and historian Mark Oppenheimer pens a portrait of the author through extensive interviews with Blume herself, access to her papers and correspondence, and analysis of Blume’s novels.

title: The Natural Way of Things
author: Charlotte Wood
description: When a group of women awaken from a drugged sleep to find themselves imprisoned in a broken-down property in the middle of a desert, they have no idea where they are or how they came to be there. Doing hard labor under a sweltering sun, guarded by two inept yet vicious jailers, the prisoners soon learn what links them: in each woman's past is a sexual scandal with a powerful man. They pray for rescue but as the hours turn into days and the days into weeks and months, it becomes clear that the women must rescue themselves.

title: Fatherland
author: Victoria Shorr
description: A tale of the American dream on the rocks. A legacy of broken promises, deceit, and perseverance against the backdrop of family commitment.

title: Apple: The First 50 Years
author: David Pogue
description: David Pogue tells Apple's entire life story: how it was born, nearly died, was born again under Steve Jobs, and became, under CEO Tim Cook, the most valuable company in the world.

title: Killers of Roe: My Investigation Into the Mysterious Death of Abortion Rights
author: Amy Littlefield
description: A reporter and abortion access correspondent investigates the secret killers and hidden motives behind the death of abortion rights.

title: The Beginning Comes After the End: Notes on a World of Change
author: Rebecca Solnit
description: Rebecca Solnit offers an account of the breadth and scale of social, political, scientific, and cultural change over the past three quarters of a century.

title: Repetition
author: Vigdis Hjorth
description: As winter approaches in Norway and the daylight dwindles, a chance encounter prompts a novelist to reexamine her past. The seismic events following her sixteenth birthday return, exposing a story both familiar and strange.

title: Now I Surrender
author: Álvaro Enrigue, trans. by Natasha Wimmer
description: A woman’s desperate flight from an Apache raid unfolds into a tale of the Mexico–US border wars.

title: The Violet Hour
author: James Cahill
description: Thomas Haller has achieved the kind of fame that most artists only dream of: shows in London and New York, paintings sold for a fortune. The vision he presents to the world is one of an untouchable genius at the top of his game. It is also a lie.

title: A Far-Flung Life
author: M. L. Stedman
description: A Far-flung Life is a tale about family and belonging, fate and time. It is about people trying to do their best, and each, for private reasons, seeking shelter from the storm of life.

title: Night Night Fawn
author: Jordy Rosenberg
description: A novel in which a yenta on her deathbed gives an unrepentant account of all her failures—including her child.

title: Field Notes from an Extinction
author: Eoghan Walls
description: Written in the form of a 19th-century notebook of ornithological observations, Field Notes from an Extinction follows the life and work of one Ignatius Green, a fictitious English scientist dispatched by the Royal Society to the remote island of Tor Mor off the northern Irish coast.

title: El Paso: Five Families and One Hundred Years of Blood, Migration, Race, and Memory
author: Jazmine Ulloa
description: A history of El Paso, revealing violence, power, and privilege at play in America's most famous border town.

title: Gunk
author: Saba Sams
description: The story of two women circling one another—working side-by-side, sleeping with the same man, inching toward friendship—until an unplanned pregnancy reveals the true nature of their connection.

title: Muv: The Story of the Mitford Girls' Mother
author: Rachel Trethewey
description: The story of the "seventh Mitford woman," a long-overlooked figure in the Mitford canon—told in full for the first time.

title: The Valley of Vengeful Ghosts
author: Kim Fu
description: In the aftermath of her mother's death, Eleanor is unmoored. For years, her mother orchestrated every detail of her life—from meals, to laundry, to finances—so that Eleanor could focus on her career as a therapist. Left to navigate the world on her own, Eleanor clings to her mother’s final directive: use her inheritance to buy a house.

title: The Glorians: Visitations from the Holy Ordinary
author: Terry Tempest Williams
description: A work of narrative nonfiction exploring beauty in the desert, climate change, and transformative moments of power in a world beset by uncertainty.

title: Reproductive Wrongs: A Short History of Bad Ideas about Women
author: Sarah Ruden
description: A feminist chronicle of the history of the West told through seven texts, exposing where our most virulent ideas about women came from.

title: The Body Builders
author: Albertine Clarke
description: A speculative debut novel about the frayed borders between our bodies and minds.

title: Every Time We Say Goodbye
author: Ivana Sajko, trans. by Mima Simic
description: A soliloquy of self-examination, upheaval, loss, hope, disillusionment, ambition and failure--Ivana Sajko paints a portrait of an intellectual at a crossroads.

title: The Disappointment
author: Scott Broker
description: Set during a doom-fated vacation to the Oregon coast, The Disappointment follows a couple trying to hold close to one another while a bent reality—warped by personal losses and an ever-increasing drift toward the surreal—threatens to unravel them.

title: Konfidenz
author: Ariel Dorfman
description: A woman travels to Paris to meet her lover. When she arrives at her hotel, however, she receives a call from a mysterious stranger claiming to be his friend, who somehow possesses intimate knowledge of their lives and why she fled her homeland. Over the course of nine hours, this man will draw her in, revealing details about her lover’s work, which could put him in grave danger, and the growing conflict that has ensnared them all.

title: 200 Monas
author: Jan Saenz
description: A novel about a college senior who has 48 hours to sell her recently deceased mother's surprise stash of rare pills, or suffer the consequences.

title: Stories: The Collected Short Fiction
author: Helen Garner, Foreword by Jonathan Escoffery
description: The collected short fiction of Helen Garner, best known for her portraits of Australian life. These stories delve into the complexities of love and longing, of the pain, darkness, and joy of being human.

title: Chosen Land: How Christianity Made America and Americans Remade Christianity
author: Matthew Avery Sutton
description: A history of Christianity in America, from the arrival of the first Europeans to the political triumphs of evangelicalism, showing the powerful role the faith has always played in American public life.

title: Cave Mountain: A Disappearance and a Reckoning in the Ozarks
author: Benjamin Hale
description: A true crime story about two young girls who went missing in the same Arkansas woods twenty-three years apart, and the strange circumstances connecting them.

title: Brawler: Stories
author: Lauren Groff
description: Ranging from the 1950s to the present day and moving across age, class, and region—from New England to Florida to California—these nine stories reflect and expand upon a shared theme: the ceaseless battle between humans' dark and light angels.

title: Kin
author: Tayari Jones
description: Vernice and Annie, two motherless daughters raised in Honeysuckle, Louisiana, have been best friends and neighbors since earliest childhood but are fated to live starkly different lives. Raised by a fierce aunt determined to give her a stable home in the wake of her mother’s death, Vernice leaves Honeysuckle at eighteen for Spelman College, where she joins a sisterhood of powerfully connected Black women and discovers a world of affluence, manners, aspiration, and inequality. Annie, abandoned by her mother as a child and fixated on the idea of finding her and filling the bottomless hole left by her absence, sets off on a journey that will take her into a world of peril and adversity, as well as love and adventure, culminating in a battle for her life.

title: A World Appears: A Journey Into Consciousness
author: Michael Pollan
description: A panoptic exploration of consciousness—what it is, who has it, and why—and a meditation on the essence of our humanity.

title: Starry and Restless: Three Women Who Changed Work, Writing, and the World
author: Julia Cooke
description: The story of three women reporters and the way they changed the world, work, and journalism.

title: White River Crossing
author: Ian McGuire
description: A novel about the lust for gold and its bloody consequences, set in the unforgiving landscape of the sub-Arctic Canadian wilderness.

title: The Optimists
author: Brian Platzer
description: A beloved schoolteacher chronicles the meteoric rise of his most dazzling student in this story of learning and legacy.

title: Defiance: A Memoir of Awakening, Rebellion, and Survival in Syria
author: Loubna Mrie
description: A memoir of personal rebellion and political awakening from a young woman raised to be loyal to a brutal regime—and the unimaginable cost of choosing freedom.

title: Red Dawn Over China: How Communism Conquered a Quarter of Humanity
author: Frank Dikötter
description: A new history of China's path to Communism.

title: I Give You My Silence
author: Mario Vargas Llosa, trans. by Adrian Nathan West
description: Toño Azpilcueta, writer of sundry articles, aspirant to the now defunct professorship of Peruvian studies, is an expert in the vals, a genre of music descended from the European waltz but rooted in New World Creole culture. When he hears a performance by the solitary and elusive guitarist Lalo Molfino, he is convinced not only that he is in the presence of the country’s finest musician, but that his own love for Peruvian music, as he has long suspected, has a profound social function. If he could just write the biography of the man before him and tell the story of both the vals and its attendant inspiring ethos, huachafería (Peru’s most important contribution to world culture, according to Toño), he might capture his country’s soul and inspire his fellow citizens remember the ties that bind them. Through music, the populace might unite and lay down their arms and embrace a harmonious and unified Peruvian culture.

title: A Fate Worse Than Hell: American Prisoners of the Civil War
author: W Fitzhugh Brundage
description: From the Pulitzer Prize finalist, a new history of the Civil War's prisoner of war camps, North and South.

title: The Science of Second Chances: A Revolution in Criminal Justice
author: Jennifer Doleac
description: Freakonomics for criminal justice, The Science of Second Chances presents a novel approach to criminal justice reform, revealing how small-scale interventions can reduce people’s chances of reoffending and break the incarceration cycle.

title: The Reservation
author: Rebecca Kauffman
description: The Reservation explores the loves and labors of an ensemble of more than a dozen restaurant workers as they strive to get a perfect meal to the table.

title: More Than Enough
author: Anna Quindlen
description: A woman confronts the surprising results of an ancestry test and begins to question the meaning of family and friendship.

title: One of Us
author: Elizabeth Day
description: A mash-up of The Wedding People and Succession —this ensemble drama about old friends and dazzling wealth captures the uneasy balance between personal ambition and collective responsibility.

title: Mule Boy
author: Andrew Krivak
description: An elegiac novel of men lost in a coal mining disaster and the boy who survives to tell the story.

title: Young Man in a Hurry: A Memoir of Discovery
author: Gavin Newsom
description: From California Governor Gavin Newsom, a memoir laying bare the defining moments of his childhood splintered by his parents' divorce that shaped Newsom's commitment to the state and nation.

title: Crown City
author: Naomi Hirahara
description: Two Japanese American men hired to investigate an art theft discover something much more sinister in turn-of-the-century California.

title: On Morrison
author: Namwali Serpell
description: A primer not only on how to read one of the most significant American authors of all time but also on how to read great works of literature in general.

title: Leaving Home: A Memoir in Full Colour
author: Mark Haddon
description: A memoir by the author of The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time : A testament about how one artist sees the world, and how his experiences have shaped his vision.

title: So Old, So Young
author: Grant Ginder
description: Five parties over the course of twenty years bring six college friends together, exploring the ways we run from and cling to our friends in love, life, and death.

title: Last Seen
author: Christopher Castellani
description: Caleb was driving home for Christmas. Steven was pounding beers at a local bar. Matthew was out looking for his ex-girlfriend. Leo was walking in the woods on a winter night. Then they disappeared. Days, weeks, years later, their bodies turn up in icy rivers hundreds of miles apart. How did they get there?

title: Railsong
author: Rahul Bhattacharya
description: A novel about a woman forging a life for herself on the railways, Railsong is the story of an individual coming of age amid the social and political upheavals of twentieth-century India.

title: The Blood Countess: Murder, Betrayal, and the Making of a Monster
author: Shelley Puhak
description: From the author of the national bestseller The Dark Queens , a work of true crime and feminist history about Elizabeth Bathory, the woman alleged to be the world's most prolific female serial killer.

title: Playmakers: The Jewish Entrepreneurs Who Created the Toy Industry in America
author: Michael Kimmel
description: The untold story of the first-generation Jewish American toymakers who literally manufactured "the century of the child."

title: Daughter of Mother-Of-Pearl
author: Mandy-Suzanne Wong
description: Seventeen essays devoted to snails' and aquatic invertebrates' uncanny ways of living.

title: Cleaner
author: Jess Shannon
description: A disaffected young woman’s work as a cleaner takes her on an increasingly surreal search for a creative fulfillment, gainful employment, and the meaning of life in this debut novel.

title: Kennedy's Coup: A White House Plot, a Saigon Murder, and America's Descent Into Vietnam
author: Jack Cheevers
description: Kennedy’s Coup recreates the Kennedy Administration’s secret encouragement of the fatal 1963 military coup against South Vietnam’s defiant president.

title: Rebel English Academy
author: Mohammed Hanif
description: In Rebel English Academy , Pakistan is struggling under martial law after the execution of its former leader. Mohammed Hanif has constructed a vibrant cast of interconnected characters who face this changing landscape with violence, passion, and humor.

title: A Hymn to Life: Shame Has to Change Sides
author: Gisèle Pelicot
description: Gisèle Pelicot tells her story for the very first time, not as victim, but as witness. Beginning in 2020, when she received the first phone call from a local police station, Gisèle recounts the fateful investigation that turned her life inside out.

title: Evil Genius
author: Claire Oshetsky
description: A young woman becomes increasingly obsessed with tales of love and death, and begins subconsciously plotting to murder her abusive husband.

title: The Powerful Primate: How Controlling Energy Enabled Us to Build Civilization
author: Roland Ennos
description: A journey through humanity’s relentless quest to harness and control physical power, fueling groundbreaking innovations while leaving a profound impact on our planet.

title: The Disappearing Act
author: Maria Stepanova
description: An exiled writer suffers from loneliness, shame, and despair, but then is invited to give a reading at a literary festival in a nearby country. The Disappearing Act oscillates between reality and dream, between an oppressive present and a lost past, between life and literature.

title: How Africa Works: Success and Failure on the World's Last Developmental Frontier
author: Joe Studwell
description: Highlighting the achievements of local leaders, Studwell argues that prosperity is well within reach and that the rapidly rising population will be foundational to Africa's flourishing.

title: This Is Not About Us
author: Allegra Goodman
description: A story of growing up and growing old, the weight of parental expectations, and the complex connection between sisters—a book about the love that binds a family across generations.

title: Eradication: A Fable
author: Jonathan Miles
description: A broken man confronts a broken world on an uninhabited Pacific island.

title: The Boundless Deep: Young Tennyson, Science and the Crisis of Belief
author: Richard Holmes
description: In this new biography, Richard Holmes discovers in Young Tennyson a magnetic and mercurial personality, a secretly expressive and highly emotional man haunted by the great intellectual and scientific issues of his time.

title: The Last Kings of Hollywood: Coppola, Lucas, Spielberg—And the Battle for the Soul of American Cinema
author: Paul Fischer
description: The story of how three young visionaries—Francis Ford Coppola, George Lucas, and Steven Spielberg—revolutionized American cinema, creating the most iconic films in history while risking everything, redefining friendship, and shaping Hollywood as we know it.

title: End of Days: Ruby Ridge, the Apocalypse, and the Unmaking of America
author: Chris Jennings
description: The story of the Ruby Ridge siege, showing how the historic standoff between federal agents and a white-separatist family set the stage for the conspiracy-laced politics of the Trump era.

title: A Better Life
author: Lionel Shriver
description: A New York family takes in a Honduran migrant who may or may not be the innocent paragon she claims to be.

title: The War Within a War: The Black Struggle in Vietnam and at Home
author: Wil Haygood
description: Explores how the Vietnam War became a mirror for the struggle of Black Americans—fighting for freedom abroad while demanding equality at home—and a lens through which to understand the racial and political divides that continue to shape American life.

title: They
author: Helle Helle, trans. by Martin Aitken
description: A portrait about the fragile, yet irrevocable bond between a young girl and her dying mother.

title: The Midnight Taxi
author: Yosha Gunasekera
description: When the last fare of the night turns up dead in her backseat, a Sri Lankan American taxi driver works off the clock to clear her name in this mystery novel by debut author Yosha Gunasekera.

title: The Real Ones: How to Disrupt the Hidden Ways Racism Makes Us Less Authentic
author: Maya Rupert
description: An exploration of how, for people of color, being real comes at a cost and authenticity is a privilege the marginalized cannot afford

title: White Nights
author: Urszula Honek
description: Thirteen interconnected stories tell of families, scarred by tragedy but also by each other.

title: Murder Bimbo
author: Rebecca Novack
description: A thirty-two-year-old sex worker is shocked when she’s approached by undercover government agents to aid them in a top-secret plot to assassinate a politician. But once the deed is done, she realizes what made her the perfect recruit: She’s 100% disposable.

title: One Bad Mother: In Praise of Psycho Housewives, Stage Parents, Momfluencers, and Other Women We Love to Hate
author: Ej Dickson
description: An exploration of what it means to be a “bad mom” by delving into the world of momfluencers, stage moms, trad wives, and more.

title: The Renovation
author: Kenan Orhan
description: A woman discovers that her bathroom has been remodeled into a prison cell—where she is an unlikely inmate—in this surreal novel of exile, grief, memory, and migration.

title: Warning Signs
author: Tracy Sierra
description: When a relaxing ski weekend goes horribly wrong, the snowy wilderness becomes deadly in the latest thriller from the author of Nightwatching .

title: Frog: And Other Essays
author: Anne Fadiman
description: Anne Fadiman returns to her favorite genre with essays ranging in subject matter from her deceased frog, to archaic printer technology, to the fraught relationship between Samuel Taylor Coleridge and his son Hartley.

title: I Hope You Find What You're Looking for
author: Bsrat Mezghebe
description: An ode to an immigrant community on the cusp of a new age, I Hope You Find What You're Looking For asks: How does our past define our present? And what stories must we let go of to be truly free?

title: Emilio Pucci: The Astonishing Odyssey of a Fashion Icon
author: Terence Ward
description: The drama of war and postwar Italy through the life of one of its most celebrated fashion icons.

title: She Made Herself a Monster
author: Anna Kovatcheva
description: In nineteenth-century Bulgaria, a self-proclaimed vampire slayer—in truth, a traveling con artist—joins forces with a teenage girl to create a monster deadly enough to vanquish their own demons.

title: Moses and the Doctor: Two Men, One Championship, and the Birth of Modern Basketball
author: Luke Epplin
description: The story of two trailblazing superstars--Julius "Dr. J" Erving and Moses Malone--whose improbable alliance and unsung legacies shaped the wildest and most innovative era of basketball history.

title: The Mixed Marriage Project: A Memoir of Love, Race, and Family
author: Dorothy Roberts
description: A memoir of growing up in an interracial family in 1960s Chicago and a daughter’s journey to understand her parents’ marriage—and her own identity.

title: Mass Mothering
author: Sarah Bruni
description: A novel of collective grief, resistance, and the radical, life-affirming virtue of testimony.

title: Autobiography of Cotton
author: Cristina Rivera Garza, trans. by Christina MacSweeney
description: In 1934, a young José Revueltas traveled to Tamaulipas to support the cotton workers’ strike in Estación Camarón. Cristina Rivera Garza recounts her grandparents’ journey from mining towns to those same cotton fields as it intersects with Revueltas’s life in a vivid and evocative history of cotton cultivation along the Mexico-US border.

title: Good People
author: Patmeena Sabit
description: A novel about an immigrant family living the American dream-and the daughter whose death raises questions about just how American they really want to become.

title: Empire of Madness: Reimagining Western Mental Health Care for Everyone
author: Khameer Kidia
description: A rethinking of the Western approach to mental health, which treats the symptoms rather than the exploitative systems causing our distress, offering lessons from the rest of the world.

title: Bernie for Burlington: The Rise of the People's Politician
author: Dan Chiasson
description: The early days and inexorable rise of the young Bernie Sanders, the one-of-a-kind visionary who changed American politics forever, told by a son of the People’s Republic of Burlington, Vermont.

title: The End of Romance
author: Lily Meyer
description: A novel about a woman who, after escaping a bruising marriage, theorizes that happiness is possible solely with the eradication of all romance—only to find a love that could change her life forever.

title: The Copywriter
author: Daniel Poppick
description: A portrait of the poet as an office worker, plumbing the depths of the spiritual gulf between art and work.

title: Superfan
author: Jenny Tinghui Zhang
description: A novel about a pop idol and his superfan, whose stories shockingly collide.

title: Clutch
author: Emily Nemens
description: As undergrads, Gregg, Reba, Hillary, Bella, and Carson formed the kind of rare bond that college brochures promise—friendship that lasts a lifetime. Two decades later, the women are spread across the country but remain firmly tethered through their ever-unfurling group chat. They’ve made it through COVID and childbirth and midcareer challenges, but no one can anticipate what’s coming down the pike. The five women converge on Palm Springs for a long overdue reunion.

title: Bonfire of the Murdochs: How the Epic Fight to Control the Last Great Media Dynasty Broke a Family — And the World
author: Gabriel Sherman
description: Sherman tells the inside story of an epic family war, one whose seeds were planted a half-century ago in Australia when the complicated patriarch left his homeland to conquer the world and please the ghost of his judgmental father. That quest culminated in a media empire that controlled Fox News, The Wall Street Journal, and tabloids on three continents, which wielded more political and cultural power than any single company in modern times.

title: Super Nintendo: The Game-Changing Company That Unlocked the Power of Play
author: Keza MacDonald
description: An ode to play and the story of the company that has redefined it—Nintendo’s quirky beginnings in 1889, its singular ethos, its endlessly innovative leaders and developers, its massive cultural impact, and, most of all, the video games themselves, which have inspired joy and creativity in millions.

title: The Wall Dancers: Searching for Freedom and Connection on the Chinese Internet
author: Yi-Ling Liu
description: An exploration of the Chinese internet that reveals the intricate dance between freedom and control in contemporary China.

title: Every Exit Brings You Home
author: Naeem Murr
description: A portrait of a Gazan immigrant's heroic efforts to heal his community and birth love from tragedy.

title: In Her Defense
author: Philippa Malicka
description: As a sensational celebrity libel trial unfolds, a young woman at the periphery secretly wields the power to make or break the case. But with her own hidden past, will she dare to speak up?

title: Second Skin: Inside the Worlds of Fetish, Kink, and Deviant Desire
author: Anastasiia Fedorova
description: A personal and cultural tour through different sexual fetishes that asks: Do we have the courage to look at our desires directly, and express them unapologetically?

title: The Family Snitch: A Daughter's Memoir of Truth and Lies
author: Francesca Fontana
description: A Wall Street Journal reporter confronts her father's criminal past and interrogates her own relationship to the truth.

title: Saraswati
author: Gurnaik Johal
description: As a holy river miraculously returns, seven lives change course, from an ambitious writer with her eye on legacy to a Kenyan archaeologist to a Bollywood stunt double, all of whom are brought together in a rapidly changing India.

title: Wolf Hour
author: Jo Nesbo
description: A serial killer, a suspended police officer and a self-proclaimed crime writer collide in an exploration of the murderer’s mind. A twisty thriller in classic Jo Nesbø style.

title: Language as Liberation: Reflections on the American Canon
author: Toni Morrison
description: An investigation of Black characters in the American literary canon and the way they shaped the nation’s collective unconscious.

title: Heap Earth Upon It
author: Chloe Michelle Howarth
description: The O’Leary siblings arrive in their new village under suspicious circumstances. Desperate to make a new start and leave their troubled life behind, the O'Learys offer few, contradicting details about their past. A tangled web that leaves you wondering who to trust.

title: Bookish: How Reading Shapes Our Lives
author: Lucy Mangan
description: A celebration of books and a love story to the written word that reveals how books help us connect with other readers through shared stories.

title: Family Drama
author: Rebecca Fallon
description: In New England, Susan Bliss is a young mother married to a professor. In LA, Susan Byrne stars in a soap opera beloved coast to coast. Decades after she’s gone, her twins have no idea of their mother’s fame. But the past can’t stay hidden forever.

title: Wolf Moon
author: Julio Llamazares, trans. by Simon Deefholts and Kathryn Phillips-Miles
description: 1937. Having lost the Civil War in Spain, four republican soldiers lead a fugitive existence deep in the Cantabrian mountains. They are on the run, skirmishing with Franco's soldiers, knowing that surrender means execution. They risk not only their lives but also the lives of anyone caught helping them.

title: Vigil
author: George Saunders
description: A novel that takes place at the bedside of an oil company CEO in the twilight hours of his life as he is ferried from this world into the next.

title: Fear and Fury: The Reagan Eighties, the Bernie Goetz Shootings, and the Rebirth of White Rage
author: Heather Ann Thompson
description: Heather Ann Thompson shines new light on an infamous 1984 New York subway shooting that would unveil simmering racial resentments and would lead, in unexpected ways, to a fractured future and a new era of rage and violence.

title: Black Dahlia: Murder, Monsters, and Madness in Midcentury Hollywood
author: William J .Mann
description: The first definitive account of the Black Dahlia murder, which humanizes the victim and situates the notorious case within an anxious, postwar country grappling with new ideas, demographics, and technologies.

title: Hated by All the Right People: Tucker Carlson and the Unraveling of the Conservative Mind
author: Jason Zengerle
description: An examination of Tucker Carlson’s rise through conservative media and politics, and his ideological transformation over the past thirty years, tracking the concurrent shifts in the political and media landscapes which have both influenced and succumbed to the hyperpartisan politics of today.

title: Neptune's Fortune: The Billion-Dollar Shipwreck and the Ghosts of the Spanish Empire
author: Julian Sancton
description: The true story of a legendary Spanish galleon that sunk off the coast of Colombia with over $1 billion in gold and silver—and one man’s obsessive quest to find it.

title: Island at the Edge of the World: The Forgotten History of Easter Island
author: Mike Pitts
description: The forgotten history of Easter Island.

title: Until the Last Gun Is Silent: A Story of Patriotism, the Vietnam War, and the Fight to Save America's Soul
author: Matthew F Delmont
description: A work of African-American history shedding light on a fractured civil rights movement, a generation of veterans failed by the country they served, and the valor of Black servicemen and peace advocates in the midst of it all.

title: A Great Act of Love
author: Heather Rose
description: A young woman with a mysterious past searches for her father—who has committed an unspeakable crime—among the champagne vines of 19th-century Australia.

title: One Sun Only: Stories
author: Camille Bordas
description: A collection of stories exploring love and art, luck and loss.

title: Escape!
author: Stephen Fishbach
description: A debut novel following a has-been reality TV star and a disgraced producer who get one last shot at redemption on a show set on a remote island, only to discover that the plot twists are beyond what they ever imagined.

title: Beckomberga
author: Sara Stridsberg
description: A portrait of a family and the ways in which our flaws, yearnings, and the unreachable parts of ourselves shape those we love as a woman bears lifelong witness to her father's illness, and Stockholm’s mythic mental hospital.

title: When the Museum Is Closed
author: Emi Yagi
description: A love story about a lonely museum worker who falls in love with a statue of Venus.

title: The Great Shadow: A History of How Sickness Shapes What We Do, Think, Believe, and Buy
author: Susan Wise Bauer
description: A story about sickness and our responses to it, from very ancient times until the last decade.

title: After the Flood: Inside Bob Dylan's Memory Palace
author: Robert Polito
description: Blending biography and archival history, After the Flood asks of Bob Dylan, "If your dreams are fulfilled at twenty, what do you do with the rest of your life?"

title: Everything Is Photograph: A Life of André Kertész
author: Patricia Albers
description: The first full biography of André Kertész, the “father of modern photography,” depicts his life and works, from Hungary to France and America, across the 20th century.

title: The Hour of the Wolf: A Memoir
author: Fatima Bhutto
description: A memoir of grief, heartbreak, and what we owe the natural world—all learned from the dog who saved the author's life.

title: The Infamous Gilberts
author: Angela Tomaski
description: A novel about a wealthy, eccentric family in decline and the secrets held within the walls of their crumbling country manor.

title: Everybody Loses: The Tumultuous Rise of American Sports Gambling
author: Danny Funt
description: This book pulls back the curtain on the alluring yet perilous world of American sports gambling. Built around interviews with the power players of the betting boom at FanDuel, DraftKings, and beyond, it reveals the troubling methods that are being used to bleed gamblers dry.

title: Departure(s)
author: Julian Barnes
description: On the occasion of his eightieth birthday, one of our great novelists delivers a playful and profound work about memory, love, and the writer's endgame.

title: Crux
author: Gabriel Tallent
description: In this story of intense friendship and grit, two down-and-out teens escape the hopelessness of their lives and chase a different future through rock climbing.

title: Half His Age
author: Jennette McCurdy
description: A novel about sex, consumerism, class, desire, loneliness, the internet, rage, intimacy, power, and the lengths we’ll go to in order to get what we want.

title: The Elements of Power: A Story of War, Technology, and the Dirtiest Supply Chain on Earth
author: Nicolas Niarchos
description: Epic, shocking, and deeply reported, The Elements of Power tells the story of the war for the global supply of battery metals—essential for the decarbonization of our economies—and the terrible, bloody human cost of this badly misunderstood industry.

title: One Aladdin Two Lamps
author: Jeanette Winterson
description: A memoir, manifesto, and a feminist reimagining of One Thousand and One Nights .

title: Five Bullets: The Story of Bernie Goetz, New York's Explosive '80s, and the Subway Vigilante Trial That Divided the Nation
author: Elliot Williams
description: An account of how one man, four teenagers, and a struggling city collided over race, vigilantism, and public safety.

title: The Flower Bearers
author: Rachel Eliza Griffiths
description: On September 24, 2021, Rachel Eliza Griffiths married her husband, the novelist Salman Rushdie. On the same day, hundreds of miles of away, Griffiths' closest friend and chosen sister, the poet Kamilah Aisha Moon, who was expected to speak at the wedding, died suddenly. Eleven months later, as Griffiths attempted to piece together her life as a newlywed with heartbreak in one hand and immense love in the other, a brutal attack nearly killed her husband. As trauma compounded trauma, Griffiths realized that in order to survive her grief, she would need to mourn not only her friend, but the woman she had been on her wedding day, a woman who had also died that day.

title: Two Women Living Together
author: Kim Hana and Hwang Sunwoo, trans. by Gene Png
description: A South Korean memoir co-written by two best friends flouting gender norms and societal expectations with their decision to grow old together under one roof.

title: Tangerinn
author: Emanuela Anechoum
description: A novel of memory about the search for belonging, the tension between departure and return, and the legacy of migration.

title: Eating Ashes
author: Brenda Navarro
description: Alone and adrift in Barcelona, an unnamed narrator is haunted by the death of her teenage brother, Diego. Now, his ashes in hand, she must return to Mexico.

title: Football
author: Chuck Klosterman
description: An examination of football's outsized role in American life, and what its future might look like.

title: Every One Still Here: Stories
author: Liadan Ní Chuinn
description: Stories set in Ireland under British occupation, a place where the past, grief, and guilt thrum behind every surface and refuse to stay buried.

title: How to Commit a Postcolonial Murder
author: Nina McConigley
description: Two Indian sisters living in the American west conspire to murder their uncle and then blame it on the British.

title: Not Your Founding Father: How a Nonbinary Minister Became America's Most Radical Revolutionary
author: Nina Sankovitch
description: The untold history of an early American renegade, and what the country might have become under their influence.

title: Once There Was a Town: The Memory Books of a Lost Jewish World
author: Jane Ziegelman
description: An exploration of the books created by Jewish Holocaust survivors to honor their lost world.

title: When Trees Testify: Science, Wisdom, History, and America's Black Botanical Legacy
author: Beronda L Montgomery
description: Combining science with stories from her own path to botany, Montgomery explores the connection between trees and black history.

title: Hemlock
author: Melissa Faliveno
description: A woman haunted by a dark inheritance returns to the woods where her mother vanished.

title: The Typewriter and the Guillotine: An American Journalist, a German Serial Killer, and Paris on the Eve of WWII
author: Mark Braude
description: The untold story of a Paris correspondent for The New Yorker who sounded the alarm about the rise of fascism in Europe while becoming enmeshed in the case of a German serial killer on the eve of WWII.

title: Discipline
author: Larissa Pham
description: The story of a woman forced to confront unsettling truths about herself, her past, and the life she rebuilt following a ruinous affair with her former mentor.

title: The Game Changer: How Harry Reid Remade the Rules and Showed Democrats How to Fight
author: Jon Ralston
description: The first full biography of Harry Reid, the five-time Senator from Nevada who produced some of the most groundbreaking legislation of the late 20th century.

title: The Einstein Vendetta: Hitler, Mussolini, and a True Story of Murder
author: Thomas Harding
description: A true crime investigation into the murder of the relatives of Albert Einstein, set against the backdrop of Nazi-occupied Florence during WWII.

title: Crucible
author: John Sayles
description: A sweeping historical novel about Henry Ford and his attempt to rule not only an automotive empire but the city of Detroit.

title: The Future Saints
author: Ashley Winstead
description: A novel about a music executive desperately trying to bring a rock band back from the brink.

title: The Oak and the Larch: A Forest History of Russia and Its Empires
author: Sophie Pinkham
description: A sweeping cultural and environmental history that reveals how forests have made--and resisted--Russia's many empires.

title: This Is Where the Serpent Lives
author: Daniyal Mueenuddin
description: Orphaned as a little boy and fending for himself in the city streets, Yazid rises to a place of responsibility and respect in the Lahore household of Colonel Atar, a powerful industrialist and politician, only to find that position threatened by conflicting loyalties and misplaced trust. Born on Colonel Atar’s country estate to a poor gardener, Saqib is entrusted with the management of a pioneering business, but he overreaches and finds himself an outlaw, confronting the violence of the corrupt Punjab Police. The colonel’s son competes with his cherished brother for the love of a woman and discovers that her choice colors his life with unexpected darkness as well as light.

title: Scavengers
author: Kathleen Boland
description: A novel about a cautious daughter and her eccentric, estranged mother venturing west in search of buried treasure—and a way back to each other—before they run out of patience, money, and options.

title: Lost Lambs
author: Madeline Cash
description: Follows a suburban family of five unspooling at the seams, navigating a disastrous open marriage, teenage rebellion, and an unexpected human trafficking/body-hacking crime conspiracy.

title: Winter: The Story of a Season
author: Val McDermid
description: Val McDermid delivers an ode to a lost world, ruminating on a single winter in her life as she journeys into the heart of the season's ever-evolving community-based traditions.

title: The School of Night
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard
description: Kristian Hadeland, young and ambitious, has moved to London to study photography; he knows that he and his art are destined for more. His family never understood him, and his fellow photography students bore him. But when he meets Hans, an eccentric Dutch artist, the future he yearns for becomes possible—as long as he is willing to sacrifice everything and stop at nothing. Twenty-four years later, Kristian sees his dreams come to fruition when a major retrospective of his work is held in New York City. As his past catches up to him, Kristian’s world begins to crumble. Success comes at a price, but is he prepared to pay it?

title: The Score: How to Stop Playing Somebody Else's Game
author: C. Thi Nguyen
description: The philosopher C. Thi Nguyen—an expert on the philosophy of games and the philosophy of data—takes us deep into the heart of games, and into the depths of bureaucracy, to see how scoring systems shape our desires.

title: The Old Fire
author: Elisa Shua Dusapin, trans. by Aneesa Abbas Higgins
description: A portrayal of family, secrets, and silence set against the backdrop of a crumbling house in the French countryside.

title: Strangers: A Memoir of Marriage
author: Belle Burden
description: A memoir about the sudden end to a seemingly happy marriage.

title: The Mattering Instinct: How Our Deepest Longing Drives Us and Divides Us
author: Rebecca Newberger Goldstein
description: A book about the primal drive that in our species alone has been transformed into one of our most persistent and universal motivations: the longing to matter.

title: Nothing Random: Bennett Cerf and the Publishing House He Built
author: Gayle Feldman
description: The story of the legendary Random House founder, whose seemingly charmed life at the apogee of the American Century afforded him a front-row seat to literary and cultural history in the making.

title: The Hitch
author: Sara Levine
description: A comedy following a woman as she attempts to exorcise the spirit of a dead corgi from her nephew and renegotiate the borders of her previously rational world.

title: Fly, Wild Swans: My Mother, Myself and China
author: Jung Chang
description: The follow-up to Wild Swans , the book that traces the history of modern China through the true stories of three generations of courageous women in one family.

title: The Revolutionists: The Story of the Extremists Who Hijacked the 1970s
author: Jason Burke
description: An epic, authoritative, gripping account of the years when a new wave of revolutionaries seized the skies and the streets to hold the world for ransom.

title: Miracle Children: Race, Education, and a True Story of False Promises
author: Katie Benner
description: A riveting investigation into a school, a scam, and a notorious college admissions scandal that exposes the inequalities and racial segregation of American education, from two award-winning New York Times journalists.

title: Woman Down
author: Colleen Hoover
description: In this twisty thriller from New York Times bestselling author Colleen Hoover, a frustrated author looks for her muse in a remote hideaway, but what she finds defies all expectations...and reality.

title: We Would Have Told Each Other Everything
author: Judith Hermann
description: A wise and subtle work from one of Germany's greatest living authors on the refractive power of memory, art, and how we live in the lives of others.

title: Sheer
author: Vanessa Lawrence
description: Told over nine charged days, Sheer is the gripping tale of a controversial beauty mogul’s insatiable ambition and the slippery ground between empowerment and abuse of power.

title: 99 Ways to Die: And How to Avoid Them
author: Ashely Alker
description: An illuminating, hilarious, and practical guide to 99 of the most terrifying ways to die and how to avoid them from an emergency medicine doctor.

title: The Age of Calamities: Stories
author: Senaa Ahmad
description: A collection of stories that uses absurdist humor and speculation to reexamine and reimagine historical figures and moments.

title: The Snakes That Ate Florida: Reporting, Essays, and Criticism
author: Ian Frazier
description: Selected pieces on nature, history, politics, and urban culture from Ian Frazier.

title: The Cradle of Citizenship: How Schools Can Help Save Our Democracy
author: James Traub
description: James Traub chronicles his year of observing public schools across the country, talking to teachers, scholars, and curriculum designers.

title: On Fire for God: Fear, Shame, Poverty, and the Making of the Christian Right - A Personal History
author: Josiah Hesse
description: An exploration of how evangelical Christianity has preyed upon its followers while galvanizing them into the political force known today as the Christian right.

title: Being Thomas Jefferson: An Intimate History
author: Andrew Burstein
description: A deep dive into the heart and soul, secret affairs, unexplored alliances, and bitter feuds of a generally worshipped, intermittently reviled American icon.

title: The Undead: A Novel of Modern Russia
author: Svetlana Satchkova
description: In this tale of contemporary Russia, a young filmmaker and her friends run afoul of a government that ruthlessly oppresses artists who dare to satirize the regime.

title: Jean
author: Madeleine Dunnigan
description: Seventeen–year–old Jean, a troubled Jewish boy caught in the countercultural swirl of 1970s London, arrives at Compton Manor, a rural alternative boarding school for boys with 'problems.' Though he is an outcast among these outcasts, he is befriended by Tom, a much wealthier, more popular classmate, and it seems as if Jean’s world might change.

title: Call Me Ishmaelle
author: Xiaolu Guo
description: A feminist reimagining of Herman Melville's classic Moby-Dick through the eyes of one inimitable woman and a diverse, swashbuckling crew.

title: Homeschooled: A Memoir
author: Stefan Merrill Block
description: A memoir about a mother's all-consuming love, a son's perilous quest to discover the world beyond the front door and the unregulated homeschool system that impacts millions like him.

title: The Spy in the Archive: How One Man Tried to Kill the KGB
author: Gordon Corera
description: The story of how one man—a librarian for the KGB—became a traitor to the intelligence agency, stealing the most prized Soviet-era archives and smuggling them to the West.

title: Watching Over Her
author: Jean-Baptiste Andrea, trans. by Frank Wynne
description: Follows a dwarf and skilled sculptor as he recounts the moments in his life that inspired his mysteriously powerful masterpiece.

title: American Reich: A Murder in Orange County, Neo-Nazis, and a New Age of Hate
author: Eric Lichtblau
description: An exploration of the violent resurgence of hatred and white supremacy through the lens of Orange County, California and the story of one brutal murder there that revealed the deep roots of violent bigotry as a bellwether for the country.

title: Black Bear: A Story of Siblinghood and Survival
author: Trina Moyles
description: A dazzling memoir about one woman's coexistence with bears in the boreal forest and a singular meditation on sibling loss.

title: The Architect of New York
author: Javier Moro
description: "A transportive work of historical fiction chronicling the life, loves, and iconic successes of Rafael Guastavino, the influential yet largely forgotten Spanish architect of New York’s Gilded Era."

title: Humor Me: How Laughing More Can Make You Present, Creative, Connected, and Happy
author: Chris Duffy
description: From a comedian and host of hit TED podcast, How to Be a Better Human, a hilarious and enlightening guide to laughing your way into a fuller life

title: Advance Britannia: The Epic Story of the Second World War, 1942-1945
author: Alan Allport
description: In this sequel to his prizewinning Britain at Bay, Alan Allport completes his superlative history of Britain’s role in World War II, once again weaving together the political, military, social, and cultural to tell a multifaceted story of a country forced to endure the profound stresses of total war.

title: The Matchbox Girl
author: Alice Jolly
description: From the multi-award-winning author - a beautiful, stunningly ambitious novel telling the story of a young girl’s battle for survival and search for the truth in occupied Vienna.

title: Meet the Newmans
author: Jennifer Niven
description: Funny, big-hearted, and deeply moving, Meet the Newmans is a rich family story about the dual lives we lead. Because even when our lives aren’t televised weekly, we all have a behind-the-scenes.

title: Converts: From Oscar Wilde to Muriel Spark, Why So Many Became Catholic in the 20th Century
author: Melanie McDonagh
description: Why did Catholicism attract so many unlikely converts in Britain during the twentieth century?

title: Battle of the Arctic: The Maritime Epic of World War II
author: Hugh Sebag-Montefiore
description: From the bestselling author of Dunkirk: Fight to the Last Man and Enigma: The Battle for the Code, the story of unsung American heroism in World War II's maritime epic in the Arctic.

title: Why We Drink Too Much: The Impact of Alcohol on Our Bodies and Culture
author: Knowles Charles
description: An exploration of our relationship with alcohol regardless of the severity of the problem or prior knowledge or experience.

title: Skylark: A Novel
author: Paula McLain
description: A woman’s quest for artistic freedom in 1664 intertwines with a doctor’s dangerous mission during the German occupation in the 1940s.

title: The Great Resistance: The 400-Year Fight to End Slavery in the Americas
author: Carrie Gibson
description: A comprehensive history of four centuries of slavery in the Americas, and those who never stopped fighting for freedom.

title: Life After Ambition: A Good Enough Memoir
author: Amil Niazi
description: An interrogation of the aspirations of young adulthood, early middle age, motherhood, and what life might look like "post-ambition."

title: The Rest of Our Lives
author: Ben Markovits
description: A road trip novel about marriage, middle-age, and a man at a crossroads in his life.

title: The Sea Captain's Wife: A True Story of Mutiny, Love, and Adventure at the Bottom of the World
author: Tilar J Mazzeo
description: The true story of the first female captain of a merchant ship and her treacherous navigation of Antarctica's deadly waters.

title: Cape Fever
author: Nadia Davids
description: A gothic psychological thriller set in the 1920s, where a young maid finds herself entangled with the spirits of a decaying manor and the secrets of its enigmatic owner.

title: A Danger to the Minds of Young Girls: Margaret C. Anderson, Book Bans, and the Fight to Modernize Literature
author: Adam Morgan
description: The life and times of literary pioneer and queer icon Margaret C. Anderson, who risked everything to be the first to publish James Joyce’s Ulysses in America.

title: House of Day, House of Night
author: Olga Tokarczuk, trans. by Antonia Lloyd-Jones
description: Nowa Ruda is a small town in Silesia, an area that has been a part of Poland, Germany, and the former Czechoslovakia in the past. When the narrator moves into the area, she discovers everyone and everythhing has its own story.
