description: Borrowed Time explores where science is taking us and what issues are being raised from a psychological, philosophical and ethical perspective, through interviews with, and profiles of, key scientists in the field and the people who represent interesting and important aspects of aging.

title: Don't Label Me: An Incredible Conversation for Divided Times
author: Irshad Manji
description: A unique conversation about diversity, bigotry, and our common humanity, by the New York Times bestselling author, Oprah Chutzpah award-winner, and founder of the Moral Courage Project.

title: Fay Wray and Robert Riskin: A Hollywood Memoir
author: Victoria Riskin
description: A dual biography of two of Hollywood’s most famous figures, whose golden lives were lived at the center of Hollywood’s golden age, written by their daughter, an acclaimed writer and producer.

title: Open Carry
author: Marc Cameron
description: A new crime series introduces readers to U.S. Marshal Arliss Cutter. On assignment in southeast Alaska, the shocking murder of a Tlingit Indian girl sets off a series of disappearances on Prince of Wales Island, including the crew of a reality-TV show set there, and it's Cutter's job to investigate.

title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
author: Samantha Shannon
description: From the internationally bestselling author of The Bone Season , an epic fantasy about a world on the brink of war with dragons and the women who must lead the fight to save it.

title: Savage Feast: Three Generations, Two Continents, and a Dinner Table (a Memoir with Recipes)
author: Boris Fishman
description: Boris Fishman shares the story of his family, their immigration, and the challenges of navigating two cultures—through the lens of food.

title: We Set the Dark on Fire
author: Tehlor Kay Mejia
description: In this debut novel and the first in a two-part series, Dani is a society-wife-in-training who has a great awakening after being recruited by rebel spies and falling for her rival and one-time bully Carmen.

title: Hunting Game
author: Helene Tursten Trans. by Paul Norlen
description: The first installment in Helene Tursten's brand new series featuring the Detective Inspector Embla Nyström.

title: That Time I Loved You: Stories
author: Carrianne Leung
description: In this American debut, Carrianne Leung evokes the legacies of Cheever and Munro with a depiction of 1970s suburbia.

title: The Enlightened Capitalists: Cautionary Tales of Business Pioneers Who Tried to Do Well by Doing Good
author: James O'Toole
description: An expert on ethical leadership analyzes the complicated history of business people who tried to marry the pursuit of profits with virtuous organizational practices—from British industrialist Robert Owen to American retailer John Cash Penney and jeans maker Levi Strauss to such modern-day entrepreneurs as Anita Roddick and Tom Chappell.

title: Widows-In-Law
author: Michele W. Miller
description: After the sudden death of her ex-husband Brian, Lauren helps Brian's much-younger widow, Jessica, arrange the funeral and settle his affairs. But Lauren gets much more than she bargained for when information comes to light about Brian's shady business deals with his old college friend Jordan Connors and the crime lord Jorge Arena, jeopardizing Brian's estate and throwing the women into the world of high-stakes illegal gambling.

title: Chocolate Cream Pie Murder
author: Joanne Fluke
description: In this 24th novel featuring baker Hannah Swensen, Hannah goes from idealistic newlywed to betrayed wife in a matter of weeks. And as a deadly mystery unfolds in town, Hannah must serve a hefty helping of justice to an unnamed killer prowling around Lake Eden, Minnesota.

title: An Unconditional Freedom
author: Alyssa Cole
description: In this third installment of a Civil War-era series, Daniel—a born-free Black man who was kidnapped, sold into slavery, and later escaped to join a Black spy organization—is intrigued by Janeta, the pampered mixed-race daughter of a plantation owner whom he doesn't know is acting as a double agent.

title: The Third Pillar: How Markets and the State Leave the Community Behind
author: Raghuram Rajan
description: From one of the most important economic thinkers of our time, an analysis of the current populist backlash against globalization.

title: Goulash
author: Brian Kimberling
description: A novel that stirs together the humor, history, romance, and myth to bring life a people, a time, and a city.

title: The Lost Night
author: Andrea Bartz
description: What really happened the night Edie died? Years later, her best friend Lindsay will learn how unprepared she is for the truth.

title: Darwin Devolves: The New Science about DNA That Challenges Evolution
author: Michael J Behe
description: The scientist who has been dubbed the 'Father of Intelligent Design' and author of the groundbreaking book Darwin’s Black Box contends that recent scientific discoveries further disprove Darwinism and strengthen the case for an intelligent creator.

title: Kid Gloves: Nine Months of Careful Chaos
author: Lucy Knisley
description: In this New York Times bestseller, Lucy Knisley explores fertility, pregnancy, and motherhood.

title: Last Night
author: Karen Ellis
description: NYPD detective Lex Cole tracks a missing Brooklyn teen whose bright future is endangered by the ghosts of his unknown father's past, in this highly anticipated sequel to A Map of the Dark .

title: Devices and Desires: Bess of Hardwick and the Building of Elizabethan England
author: Kate Hubbard
description: The critically acclaimed author of Serving Victoria illuminates the life of the little-known Bess of Hardwick—next to Queen Elizabeth I, the richest and most powerful woman in sixteenth-century England.

title: Birthday
author: César Aira, Trans. by Chris Andrews
description: In this first English translation of an auto-fictional memoir by Argentina's most prolific and respected authors, a writer resembling Aira contemplates his career and life's achievements and failures.

title: Louisa on the Front Lines: Louisa May Alcott in the Civil War
author: Samantha Seiple
description: A look at Little Women author Louisa May Alcott's time as a Civil War nurse, and the far-reaching implications her service had on her writing and her activism.

title: The Lessons of Tragedy: Statecraft and World Order
author: Hal Brands and Charles Edsel
description: Two historians and former State Department officials argue that the United States has imperiled itself by forgetting the tragic view of history that informed the cooperative world order it helped fashion after World War II.

title: Putin's World: Russia Against the West and with the Rest
author: Angela Stent
description: A former national intelligence officer charts Russia's emergence as a growing world power as President Vladimir Putin took advantage of a vacuum created by the West's distraction with its own domestic problems and U.S. foreign policy blunders.

title: We Must Be Brave
author: Frances Liardet
description: As World War II rages, newly married Englishwoman Ellen Parr finds a small child asleep on the backseat of an empty bus and takes her in. After three years together, the girl is taken away, leaving Ellen to wonder: In a world changed by war, is it fair to wish for an unchanged heart?

title: Magic Is Dead: My Journey Into the World's Most Secretive Society of Magicians
author: Ian Frisch
description: A freelance journalist threads together a personal story of the sudden death of his father, his mother's escape to the poker tables, and how his fascination with the modern magicians and their swift resurgence in popular culture led him to discover The 52, magic's most brilliant young minds who are gathering in secret and revolutionizing the art form.

title: On Freedom
author: Cass R. Sunstein
description: In this slim treatise, Cass Sunstein asks us to rethink freedom. He shows that freedom of choice isn’t nearly enough. To be free, we must also be able to navigate life, in order to get where we want to go.

title: The Trouble with Men: Reflections on Sex, Love, Marriage, Porn, and Power
author: David Shields
description: From the author of Reality Hunger comes an honest, explicit look at one man's marriage and the view it affords for examining relationships between men and women across our culture.

title: War Doctor: Surgery on the Front Line
author: David Nott
description: For more than twenty-five years, David Nott has taken unpaid leave from his job as a general and vascular surgeon with the NHS to volunteer in some of the world’s most dangerous war zones. In this memoir, he shares stories from 25 years on the front lines.

title: The Care and Feeding of Ravenously Hungry Girls
author: Anissa Gray
description: A debut novel about mothers and daughters, identity and family, and how the relationships that sustain you can also be the ones that consume you.

title: The White Book
author: Han Kang, Trans. by Deborah Smith
description: From Booker Prize-winner and literary phenomenon Han Kang, a lyrical exploration of personal grief, written through the prism of the color white.

title: Bangkok Wakes to Rain
author: Pitchaya Sudbanthad
description: Time collapses as these stories collide and converge, linked by the forces making and remaking the amphibious, ever-morphing capital itself.

title: Earth-Shattering: Violent Supernovas, Galactic Explosions, Biological Mayhem, Nuclear Meltdowns, and Other Hazards to Life in Our Universe
author: Bob Berman
description: An exploration of the biggest explosions in history, from the Big Bang to mysterious activity on Earth and everything in between.

title: Landfall
author: Thomas Mallon
description: Set during the tumultuous middle of the George W. Bush years—amid the twin catastrophes of the Iraq insurgency and Hurricane Katrina— Landfall brings Thomas Mallon's cavalcade of contemporary American politics, which began with Watergate and continue with Finale , to a final climax.

title: Trump Sky Alpha
author: Mark Doten
description: A novel on the political madness of our time and the Internet’s deep workings, by the author of The Infernal .

title: Arturo's Island
author: Elsa Morante, Trans. by Ann Goldstein
description: Follows the adolescent Arturo through his days on the isolated Neapolitan island of Procida, where―his mother long deceased, his father often absent, and a dog as his sole companion―he roams the countryside and the beaches or reads in his family’s lonely, dilapidated mansion. This quiet, meandering existence is upended when his father brings home a beautiful sixteen-year-old bride, Nunziatella.

title: Never Enough: The Neuroscience and Experience of Addiction
author: Judith Grisel
description: A behavioral neuroscientist explores the science of addiction through the lens of her own substance abuse during her teenage years and early 20s.

title: Negrophobia: An Urban Parable
author: Darius James
description: A provocative, raucous dark comedy about race and racism in America, now back in print after twenty-five years and with a new preface by the author.

title: The Vanishing Man: A Prequel to the Charles Lenox Series
author: Charles Finch
description: From the critically acclaimed and USA Today bestselling author Charles Finch comes a prequel to his Charles Lenox Victorian series, in which the theft of an antique painting sends Detective Lenox on a hunt for a criminal mastermind.

title: How to Hide an Empire: A History of the Greater United States
author: Daniel Immerwahr
description: A Northwestern University history professor argues that the United States represents an empire invisible to most of its inhabitants, one that consists of vast overseas possessions and a troubling history of interventionism abroad.

title: Nobody's Looking at You: Essays
author: Janet Malcolm
description: A collection of previously published essays and profiles by the legendary critic Janet Malcolm.

title: In the Dark
author: Cara Hunter
description: From internationally bestselling author Cara Hunter, a suspense novel about the secrets revealed when a woman is discovered held captive behind a basement wall—and no one is who they appear to be.

title: Blood Orange
author: Harriet Tyce
description: A young lawyer's outwardly perfect life spirals out of control as she takes on her first murder case in this dark and twisty debut thriller for readers of Paula Hawkins, A.J. Finn, or Shari Lapena.

title: The Polar Bear Expedition: The Heroes of America's Forgotten Invasion of Russia, 1918-1919
author: James Carl Nelson
description: In the brutally cold winter of 1919, 5,000 Americans battled the Red Army 600 miles north of Moscow. We have forgotten. Russia has not.

title: Spearhead: An American Tank Gunner, His Enemy, and a Collision of Lives in World War II
author: Adam Makos
description: From the New York Times bestselling author of A Higher Call comes the riveting World War II story of an American tank gunner’s journey into the heart of the Third Reich, where he will meet destiny in an iconic armor duel—and forge an enduring bond with his enemy.

title: The Darkest Year: The American Home Front 1941-1942
author: William K Klingaman
description: A look at America during the twelve months after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, during which an already strained social fabric became even more so and a heated debate swirled around the now-infamous internment of Japanese Americans authorized by Franklin D. Roosevelt in February 1942.

title: Nature's Mutiny: How the Little Ice Age of the Long Seventeenth Century Transformed the West and Shaped the Present
author: Philipp Blom
description: A work of environmental history that chronicles the great climate crisis of the 1600s, which transformed the social and political fabric of Europe.

title: The Threat: How the FBI Protects America in the Age of Terror and Trump
author: Andrew G McCabe
description: The former deputy director of the FBI recounts his career; discusses how law enforcement battles terror threats, Russian crime, and attacks by the White House itself on the U.S. Constitution; and offers details of the events leading up to his firing by Donald Trump.

title: Cherokee America
author: Margaret Verble
description: From the author of the Pulitzer Prize finalist Maud's Line , an epic novel that follows a web of complex family alliances and culture clashes in the Cherokee Nation during the aftermath of the Civil War, and the woman at its center.

title: The Next to Die
author: Sophie Hannah
description: The New York Times bestselling author returns with a disturbing tale of psychological suspense and obsession.

title: Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments: Intimate Histories of Social Upheaval
author: Saidiya Hartman
description: An exploration of the lives of young black women in the early twentieth century.

title: The Study of Animal Languages
author: Lindsay Stern
description: Meet Ivan and Prue: a married couple - both experts in language and communication - who nevertheless cannot seem to communicate with each other.

title: In Putin's Footsteps: Searching for the Soul of an Empire Across Russia's Eleven Time Zones
author: Nina Khrushcheva
description: Nina Khrushcheva and Jeffrey Tayler’s unique combination of travelogue, current affairs, and history, showing how Russia’s dimensions have shaped its identity and culture through the decades.

title: The Art of Leaving: A Memoir
author: Ayelet Tsabari
description: A memoir in essays by an award-winning Israeli writer who travels the world, from New York to India, searching for love, belonging, and an escape from grief following the death of her father when she was a young girl.

title: The Uninhabitable Earth: Life After Warming
author: David Wallace-Wells
description: In his travelogue of our near future, David Wallace-Wells brings into stark relief the climate troubles that await—food shortages, refugee emergencies, and other crises that will reshape the globe.

title: Aerialists: Stories
author: Mark Mayer
description: Nine stories in which classic carnival characters become ordinary misfits seeking grandeur in a lonely world.

title: The Good Immigrant: 26 Writers Reflect on America
author: Ed. by Nikesh Shukla and Chimene Suleyman
description: A collection of essays by first and second-generation immigrants—including Chigozie Obioma, Jenny Zhang, and Alexander Chee—each exploring what it's like to be othered in an increasingly divided America.

title: Alienated America: Why Some Places Thrive While Others Collapse
author: Timothy P. Carney
description: Conservative journalist and commentator Timothy P. Carney continues the conversation begun with Hillbilly Elegy and the classic Bowling Alone in this hard-hitting analysis that identifies the true factor behind the decline of the American dream: the collapse of the institutions that made us successful, including marriage, church, and civic life.

title: Gates of Stone
author: Angus Macallan
description: Just before her sixteenth birthday, Princess Katerina is refused her rightful place as heir to the Empire of the Ice-Bear—solely because of her sex. Determined to regain her inheritance, she murders the foreign lord she’s been ordered to marry and embarks on a perilous voyage in search of the vast wealth and power she needs to claim the Empire for herself.

title: Blood Echo
author: Christopher Rice
description: A conspiracy that promises bloodshed and the only woman who can stop it collide in the second thrilling installment of the Burning Girl series.

title: Rain: And Other Stories
author: Mia Couto
description: Published in the aftermath of Mozambique’s bloody civil war, Mia Couto’s third collection seeks out the places violence could not reach. These stories grapple with questions of what’s been lost and what can be reclaimed, what future exists for a country that broke the yoke of colonialism only to descend into internecine war, what is Mozambican and what is Mozambique.

title: The Haunting of Tram Car 015
author: P Djeli Clark
description: P. Djèlí Clark returns to the historical fantasy universe of A Dead Djinn in Cairo , with the otherworldly adventure novella The Haunting of Tram Car 015 .

title: Never Tell
author: Lisa Gardner
description: In the ninth novel featuring Boston PD Sgt. Det. D.D. Warren, a man is shot dead in his home office, and his pregnant wife—who was found holding the gun—has a connection to an old case from Warren's past. Police informant and one-time hostage Flora Dane steps in to share what she knows about the dead man.

title: Mission Critical
author: Mark Greaney
description: In this eighth novel in the bestselling Gray Man series, Court Gentry must find the men who kidnapped a CIA asset and murdered his compatriots while another attack targets his former lover, Zoya Zakharova, who narrowly escapes.

title: Devil's Daughter: The Ravenels Meet the Wallflowers
author: Lisa Kleypas
description: Phoebe, Lady Clare, finds herself attracted against her better judgement to West Ravenel, a self-reformed rake and the man who made her late husband's life a misery back in boarding school. Will their overwhelming passion be enough to overcome the obstacles of the past?

title: They Were Her Property: White Women as Slave Owners in the American South
author: Stephanie E. Jones-Rogers
description: Bridging women’s history, the history of the South, and African American history, this book makes an argument about the role white women played in American slavery.

title: Letter to Survivors
author: Gebe Trans. by Edward Gauvin
description: A post-apocalyptic graphic novel that follows an unusual postal worker on his very bizarre mail route.

title: The Secret of Clouds
author: Alyson Richman
description: An English teacher with haunting childhood memories gains perspective and inspiration while tutoring a young Ukrainian immigrant whose serious health issues prevent him from taking any day for granted.

title: For the Killing of Kings
author: Howard Andrew Jones
description: Their peace was a fragile thing, but it had endured for seven years, mostly because the people of Darassus and the king of the Naor hordes believed his doom was foretold upon the edge of the great sword hung in the hall of champions in the first book of this new adventure-filled trilogy.

title: Liquid Rules: The Delightful and Dangerous Substances That Flow Through Our Lives
author: Mark Miodownik
description: The bestselling author of Stuff Matters takes a transatlantic flight on British Airways during which he contemplates the various liquids that make the flight possible and more bearable.

title: Hunting LeRoux: The Inside Story of the Dea Takedown of a Criminal Genius and His Empire
author: Elaine Shannon
description: The story of Paul LeRoux, the twisted-genius entrepreneur and cold-blooded killer who brought revolutionary innovation to international crime, and the exclusive inside story of how the DEA’s elite, secretive 960 Group brought him down.

title: The Nocilla Trilogy: Nocilla Dream, Nocilla Experience, Nocilla Lab
author: Agustín Fernández Mallo, Trans. by Thomas Bunstead
description: First published in Spain beginning in the early aughts, these genre-bending books—hybrids of fiction, poetry, and meditation—are credited with shifting Spanish literature away from tradition and toward new forms of writing that grapple with the age of mass media

title: The Art of Dying Well: A Practical Guide to a Good End of Life
author: Katy Butler
description: The journalist and author of Knocking on Heaven’s Door , a mix of memoir and medical reportage, offers a handbook for navigating the practical and emotional complexities of aging, illness, and death.

title: The Stranger from the Sea
author: Paul Binding
description: A re-imagination of the characters from Ibsen’s The Lady from the Sea , set against the backdrop of a late-nineteenth-century English Channel town that harbors many secrets.

title: Broken Stars: Contemporary Chinese Science Fiction in Translation
author: TransKen Liu
description: Broken Stars , edited by multi award-winning writer Ken Liu, is his second thought-provoking anthology of Chinese short speculative fiction. Some of the included authors are already familiar to readers in the West, and some are publishing in English for the first time. Besides stories firmly entrenched in subgenres familiar to Western SFF readers such as hard SF, cyberpunk, science fantasy, and space opera, the anthology also includes stories that showcase deeper ties to Chinese culture: alternate Chinese history, chuanyue time travel, satire with historical and contemporary allusions that are likely unknown to the average Western reader.

title: Catherine & Diderot: The Empress, the Philosopher, and the Fate of the Enlightenment
author: Robert Zaretsky
description: In a dual biography crafted around the famous encounter between the French philosopher who wrote about power and the Russian empress who wielded it, Robert Zaretsky invites us to reflect on the fraught relationship between politics and philosophy, and between a man of thought and a woman of action.

title: Dancing With Merce Cunningham
author: Marianne Preger-Simon
description: Dancing with Merce Cunningham is the account of a talented dancer’s close collaboration and lifelong friendship with one of the choreographic geniuses of our time.

title: American Cosmic: Ufos, Religion, Technology
author: D. W. Pasulka
description: An examination of the mechanisms at work behind the thriving belief system in extraterrestrial life, a system that is changing and even supplanting traditional religions.

title: Appalachian Reckoning: A Region Responds to Hillbilly Elegy
author: Ed. by Anthony Harkins and Meredith McCarroll
description: In these essays responding to J.D. Vance's popular memoir, Hillbilly Elegy , writers and artists offer personal narratives and perspectives that challenge the stereotypes about Appalachian people and culture they feel Vance unfairly represented in his book.

title: Death Is Hard Work
author: Khaled Khalifa Trans. by Leri Price
description: A finalist for the 2019 National Book Award, this new novel from a chronicler of Syria’s ongoing and catastrophic civil war: a tale of three ordinary people facing down the stuff of nightmares armed with little more than simple determination.

title: Early Riser
author: Jasper Fforde
description: A madcap adventure through the Welsh winter, which has grown so deadly most humans literally sleep through it. Charlie Worthing has decided to join the Winter Consul Service, the select group of people who don’t hibernate through winter in order to keep the sleepers safe until they wake up in the spring.

title: The Cassandra
author: Sharma Shields
description: The Cassandra follows a woman who goes to work in a top-secret research facility during WWII, only to be tormented by visions of what the mission will mean for humankind.

title: Leading Men
author: Christopher Castellani
description: The author explores the real-life relationship between Tennessee Williams and his romantic partner of 15 years, Frank Merlo, through the lens of the couple's imaginary encounter with a beautiful young Swedish woman named Anja, whom they take under their wing and turn into a star.

title: The Source of Self-Regard: Selected Essays, Speeches, and Meditations
author: Toni Morrison
description: A gathering of Toni Morrison's essays, speeches, and meditations on society, culture, and art, spanning four decades.

title: The Night Tiger
author: Yangsze Choo
description: From New York Times bestselling author Yangsze Choo, a transporting novel set in 1930s colonial Malaysia, perfect for fans of Isabel Allende and Min Jin Lee.

title: 'Broadsword Calling Danny Boy': Watching Where Eagles Dare
author: Geoff Dyer
description: Geoff Dyer's tribute to a film he has loved since childhood: it's a scene-by-scene analysis—or should that be send-up?—taking us from it's snowy, Teutonic opening credits to its vertigo-inducing climax.

title: Mother Winter: A Memoir
author: Sophia Shalmiyev
description: A memoir equal parts refugee-coming-of-age story, feminist manifesto, and meditation on motherhood, displacement, gender politics, and art that follows award-winning writer Sophia Shalmiyev’s flight from the Soviet Union, where she was forced to abandon her estranged mother, and her subsequent quest to find her.

title: Midnight in Chernobyl: The Untold Story of the World's Greatest Nuclear Disaster
author: Adam Higginbotham
description: Journalist Adam Higginbotham’s years-in-the-making account of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant disaster—and an investigation into how propaganda, secrecy, and myth have obscured the true story of one of the twentieth century’s greatest disasters.

title: Lost Children Archive
author: Valeria Luiselli
description: From the two-time National Book Critics Circle finalist, a new novel about a family whose road trip across America collides with an immigration crisis at the southwestern border.

title: American Spy
author: Lauren Wilkinson
description: Inspired by true events, American Spy knits together a spy thriller, a family drama, and romance.

title: Say You're Sorry
author: Karen Rose
description: Introducing the first book in the new Sacramento series from New York Times bestselling author Karen Rose.

title: Shortest Way Home: One Mayor's Challenge and a Model for America's Future
author: Pete Buttigieg
description: The 37-year-old mayor of South Bend offers up a narrative about his life as a gay Rhodes scholar and a Navy man and his strategy for overseeing the economic rejuvenation of the Indiana city.

title: Long Shot
author: Azad
description: An Iran-born Kurdish journalist who joined the ranks of the Kurdish army as a sniper in the fight against ISIS tells his story under his nom de guerre, Azad, which means "freedom" in Kurdish.

title: American Heroin
author: Melissa Scrivner Love
description: In this sequel to Lola , the title character has become the head of her gang in South Central Los Angeles, where she has bought her family a better life but also become the target of a rival gang.

title: The Heavens
author: Sandra Newman
description: A novel of love and dreams that moves between a reimagined New York City and Elizabethan England to ask how our world comes to be.

title: Territory of Light
author: Yuko Tsushima Trans. by Geraldine Harcourt
description: From one of the most significant contemporary Japanese writers, a novel of loss and rebirth.

title: The City in the Middle of the Night
author: Charlie Jane Anders
description: Charlie Jane Anders, the nationally bestselling author of All the Birds in the Sky delivers a new novel set in a hauntingly strange future.

title: The Gilded Auction Block: Poems
author: Shane McCrae
description: In The Gilded Auction Block , Shane McCrae considers the present moment in America on its own terms as well as for what it says about the American project and Americans themselves.

title: The Wild Bunch: Sam Peckinpah, a Revolution in Hollywood, and the Making of a Legendary Film
author: W. K. Stratton
description: A look back at the dramatic filming and offset debauchery that occurred during the making of the groundbreaking Western.

title: Northern Lights
author: Raymond Strom
description: In this debut novel, a queer teenager named Shane Stephenson goes looking for his estranged mother in rural Minnesota in the late 1990s where he navigates homophobia and bigotry as well as falls in with a crowd of troubled friends.

title: Separate: The Story of Plessy V. Ferguson, and America's Journey from Slavery to Segregation
author: Steve Luxenberg
description: A myth-shattering narrative of how a nation embraced 'separation' and its pernicious consequences.

title: The Moroccan Girl
author: Charles Cumming
description: A successful spy novelist is drawn into a real-life espionage plot when he’s ordered to find a mysterious fugitive on the alluring but deadly streets of Morocco.

title: The Book of Delights: Essays
author: Ross Gay
description: The winner of the NBCC Award for Poetry offers up a collection of short lyric essays, written daily over a tumultuous year, reminding us of the purpose and pleasure of praising, extolling, and celebrating ordinary wonders.

title: How to Disappear: Notes on Invisibility in a Time of Transparency
author: Akiko Busch
description: Explores the idea of invisibility in nature, art, and science, in search of a more joyful and peaceful way of living in today's increasingly surveilled and publicity-obsessed world.

title: Parkland: Birth of a Movement
author: Dave Cullen
description: Offers an account of the extraordinary teenage survivors of Parkland who became activists and pushed back against the NRA and Congressional leaders, inspiring millions of Americans to join their grassroots #neveragain movement.

title: Good Kids, Bad City: A Story of Race and Wrongful Conviction in America
author: Kyle Swenson
description: The true story of the longest wrongful imprisonment in the United States to end in exoneration, and a critical social and political history of Cleveland, the city that convicted them.

title: Sounds Like Titanic: A Memoir
author: Jessica Chiccehitto Hindman
description: A young woman leaves Appalachia for life as a classical musician--or so she thinks.

title: Finding Dorothy
author: Elizabeth Letts
description: The author of The Perfect Horse returns with a novel inspired by the historical meeting between Judy Garland and Maud Gage Baum—the wife of L. Frank Baum, author of The Wonderful Wizard of Oz —on the set of the beloved 1939 musical film. In Letts's imagination, Maud becomes a mentor to the teenaged Garland, protecting her from abuse by her mother and Hollywood studio executives.

title: The Pianist from Syria: A Memoir
author: Aeham Ahmad, Trans. by Emanuel Bergmann
description: The man who gained attention on YouTube for playing piano amid the ravaged neighborhoods of war-torn Syria tells his life story—from his coming of age as the son of Palestinian refugees, to his training as a pianist and family music business, to his eventual flight form the country that is still in the midst of civil war.

title: Grateful American: A Journey from Self to Service
author: Gary Sinise
description: The man who played Lt. Dan in the beloved film Forrest Gump shares his journey from trouble-making Chicago kid to cofounder of the legendary Steppenwolf Theater Company, world-famous actor, and advocate for America's active duty defenders, veterans, and first responders.

title: Off the Rails: A Train Trip Through Life
author: Beppe Severgnini
description: An acclaimed journalist explores his obsession with trains--and what his rail journeys have taught him about culture and identity.

title: Eugene V. Debs: A Graphic Biography
author: Paul Buhle, Steve Max, Noah Van Sciver, and Dave Nance
description: A graphic biography of socialist labor legend Eugene V. Debs.

title: Ben Hecht: Fighting Words, Moving Pictures
author: Adina Hoffman
description: A vibrant portrait of one of the most accomplished and prolific American screenwriters, by an award-winning biographer and essayist.

title: The Empire and the Five Kings: America's Abdication and the Fate of the World
author: Bernard-Henri Levy
description: One of the West’s leading intellectuals offers a provocative look at America’s withdrawal from world leadership and the rising powers who seek to fill the vacuum left behind.

title: On Drinking
author: Charles Bukowski
description: The definitive collection of works on a subject that inspired and haunted Charles Bukowski for his entire life: alcohol.

title: Careless Love: A DCI Banks Novel
author: Peter Robinson
description: Two suspicious deaths challenge DS Alan Banks and his crack investigative team.

title: Rag: Stories
author: Maryse Meijer
description: From the author of Heartbreaker , a collection tracing the destructive consequences of the desire for connection.

title: The Reckoning: A Thriller
author: Yrsa Sigurdardottir, Trans. by Victoria Cribb
description: In this follow-up to The Legacy , Reykjavík detective Huldar investigates the case of a missing girl with child psychologist Freyja.

title: Any Means Necessary: A Leona Lindberg Thriller
author: Jenny Rogneby, Trans. by Agnes Broomé
description: In this follow-up to Leona: The Die Is Cast , corrupt detective Leona Lindberg deals with the emotional fallout of her actions while investigating a terrorist attack in the heart of Stockholm. With one foot on each side of the law, she mounts a special operation of grand proportions.

title: Felicity Carrol and the Perilous Pursuit: A Felicity Carrol Mystery
author: Patricia Marcantonio
description: Amidst the heraldry of Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee celebrations, a string of brutal murders rocks Britain's upper crust--and could threaten the realm itself in the debut of Patricia Marcantonio's Felicity Carrol mysteries.

title: Test
author: Sylvain Neuvel
description: Award-winning author of Sleeping Giants , Sylvain Neuvel, explores an immigration dystopia.

title: The Beast's Heart: A Novel of Beauty and the Beast
author: Leife Shallcross
description: A retelling of Beauty and the Beast set in seventeenth-century France and told from the point of view of the Beast himself.

title: Honey in the Carcase: Stories
author: Josip Novakovich
description: The newest collection of 14 short stories from award-winning Josip Novakovich, which moves from scenes as familiar as a dinner party to the brutal landscapes of war-torn Southeast Europe.

title: Nothing But the Night
author: John Williams
description: Stoner author John Williams's first novel is a searing look at a man's relationship with his absent father, and how early trauma manifests throughout one's life.

title: Trigger
author: David Swinson
description: In the latest novel from David Swinson, Frank Marr, a good cop with a bad habit, must choose between justice and loyalty to an old friend.

title: Elsewhere, Home
author: Leila Aboulela
description: Shuttling between the dusty, sunbaked streets of Khartoum and the university halls and cramped apartments of Aberdeen and London, Elsewhere, Home offers us a tableau of life as an immigrant abroad, and the challenges of navigating assimilation and difference.

title: The Nine Cloud Dream
author: Kim Man-jung Trans. by Heinz Insu Fenkl
description: Korea’s most prized literary masterpiece: a Buddhist journey questioning the illusions of human life—presented in a new translation by PEN/Hemingway finalist Heinz Insu Fenkl.

title: All Roads End Here
author: David Moody
description: Set in the world of David Moody's Hater trilogy, All Roads End Here is the sequel to the One of Us Will Be Dead by Morning about humanity’s fight for survival in the face of the impending apocalypse.

title: Lord
author: Joao Gilberto Noll Trans. by Edgar Garbelotto
description: From renowned Brazilian author João Gilberto Noll, a novel about the unsettling space between identities, and a disturbing portrait of dementia from the inside out.

title: The Victory Garden
author: Rhys Bowen
description: A novel about a woman’s love and sacrifice during the First World War.

title: Casting Deep Shade: An Amble
author: C.D. Wright
description: This final work by the National Book Critics Circle Award-winning poet meditates on humanity’s shared history with the beech tree, alongside color photographs of beech trees by artist Denny Moers.

author: Guillermo Saccomanno, Trans. by Andrea G. Labinger
genres: ["Award Winners", "Fiction", "Historical", "LGBTQ Stories", "Literary", "Literature in Translation", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: Winner of the 2008 Hammett Award, this newly translated Argentine thriller follows the precarious existence of Gómez, a gay high school literature teacher forced to make very uncomfortable choices to stay alive in Buenos Aires in 1977, during the throes of Argentina's military dictatorship and "Dirty War."

title: Good Reasons for Bad Feelings
author: Randolph M. Nesse
description: Why do I feel bad? There is real power in understanding our bad feelings. Nesse's book transforms our understanding of mental disorders by exploring a fundamentally new question. Instead of asking why certain people suffer from mental illness, Nesse asks why natural selection has left us all with fragile minds.

title: Reckonings: Poems
author: Ryan Walsh
description: Reckonings attempts to account for the slow violence of Appalachia's industrialization, while also positioning us in meaningful relation to this violence. It's impossible work, making meaning out of the willful destruction of the working class and of the earth, but Ryan Walsh mounts a passionate defense of the too-often overlooked and devalued lives and landscapes of West Virginia.

title: A Deadly Divide
author: Ausma Zehanat Khan
description: In the aftermath of a mass shooting at a mosque in Quebec, the local police apprehend Amadou Duchon―a young Muslim man at the scene helping the wounded―but release Etienne Roy, the local priest who was found with a weapon in his hands. The shooting looks like a hate crime, but detectives Esa Khattak and Rachel Getty sense there is more to the story.

title: Gilded Youth: : Privilege, Rebellion and the British Public School
author: James Brook-Smith
description: The British public school is an iconic institution, a training ground for the ruling elite and a symbol of national identity and tradition. But beyond the elegant architecture and evergreen playing fields is a turbulent history of teenage rebellion, sexual dissidence, and political radicalism. Drawing on personal experience, extensive research, and public school representations in poetry, school slang, spy films, popular novels, and rock music, Brooke-Smith offers a fresh account of upper-class adolescence in Britain and the role of elite private education in shaping youth culture.

title: Europe: A Natural History
author: Tim Flannery
description: World-renowned scientist, explorer, and conservationist Tim Flannery, traces Europe’s land, flora, and fauna over 100 million years, and looks to the future.

title: Black Leopard, Red Wolf
author: Marlon James
description: In the first novel of Booker Prize-winner Marlon James's Dark Star trilogy, myth, fantasy, and history come together to explore what happens when a mercenary is hired to find a missing child. (It's also a 2019 National Book Award finalist.)

title: The Last Romantics
author: Tara Conklin
description: The New York Times bestselling author of The House Girl explores the lives of four siblings in this novel in the vein of Commonwealth and The Interestings .

title: Bowlaway
author: Elizabeth McCracken
description: In this new novel from the award-winning author of Niagra Falls All Over Again , three generations of an unconventional New England family own and operate a candlepin bowling alley.

title: I Owe You One
author: Sophie Kinsella
description: From #1 New York Times bestselling author Sophie Kinsella comes a story of love and empowerment about a young woman with a complicated family, a handsome man who might be 'the one,' and an IOU that changes everything.

title: When You Read This
author: Mary Adkins
description: A comedy-drama for the digital age: an epistolary debut novel about the ties that bind and break our hearts, for fans of Maria Semple and Rainbow Rowell.

title: The Spirit of Science Fiction
author: Roberto Bolano, Trans. by Natasha Wimmer
description: A tale of bohemian youth on the make in Mexico City from Roberto Bolaño.

title: The Girls at 17 Swann Street
author: Yara Zgheib
description: Yara Zgheib’s debut novel is a portrait of a young woman’s struggle with anorexia on an intimate journey to reclaim her life.

title: The Unwinding of the Miracle: A Memoir of Life, Death, and Everything That Comes After
author: Julie Yip-Williams
description: As a young mother facing a terminal diagnosis, Julie Yip-Williams began to write her story. What began as the chronicle of an imminent and early death became something much more—a powerful exhortation to the living.

title: Merchants of Truth: The Business of News and the Fight for Facts
author: Jill Abramson
description: From former Executive Editor of The New York Times Jill Abramson, an examination of two legacy ( The New York Times and The Washington Post ) and two upstart ( BuzzFeed and VICE ) companies as they plow through a revolution in technology, economics, standards, commitment, and endurance that pits old vs. new media.

title: This Is Not a Love Song
author: Brendan Mathews
description: When marriages, friendships, and families come undone, to what lengths do we go to keep it all together? That question lies at the heart of Brendan Mathews's debut story collection.

title: I Am God
author: Giacomo Sartori
description: The diary of the Almighty’s existential crisis that ensues when he falls in love with a human.

title: Brothers Keepers
author: Donald E Westlake
description: What will a group of monks do when their century-old monastery in New York City is threatened with demolition to make room for a new high-rise?

title: No Beast So Fierce: The Terrifying True Story of the Champawat Tiger, the Deadliest Animal in History
author: Dane Huckelbridge
description: A multifaceted true account of the deadliest animal of all time, equally comparable to Jaws as to Matthiessen's The Snow Leopard.

title: The Collected Schizophrenias: Essays
author: Esme Weijun Wang
description: In essays that range from using fashion to present as high-functioning to the depths of a rare form of psychosis, and from the failures of the higher education system and the dangers of institutionalization to the complexity of compounding factors such as PTSD and Lyme disease, Wang’s analytical eye, honed as a former lab researcher at Stanford, allows her to balance research with personal narrative.

title: The Man in the Willows: The Life of Kenneth Grahame
author: Matthew Dennison
description: A biography of Kenneth Grahame, author of the children's classic The Wind in the Willows , and of the vision of English pastoral life that inspired it.

title: Zucked: Waking Up to the Facebook Catastrophe
author: Roger McNamee
description: The story of how a noted tech venture capitalist, an early mentor to Mark Zuckerberg and investor in his company, woke up to the serious damage Facebook was doing to our society and set out to try to stop it.

title: The Master Plan: My Journey from Life in Prison to a Life of Purpose
author: Chris Wilson
description: The memoir of a man who used hard work and a Master Plan to turn a life sentence into a second chance.

title: The Winter Sister
author: Megan Collins
description: A young woman haunted by the past returns home to care for her ailing mother and begins to dig deeper into her sister’s unsolved murder.

title: Watcher in the Woods: A Rockton Novel
author: Kelley Armstrong
description: The next installment of #1 bestselling Kelley Armstrong's riveting Casey Duncan series.

title: How to Be Loved: A Memoir of Lifesaving Friendship
author: Eva Hagberg Fisher
description: A memoir about how friendship saved one woman's life, for anyone who has loved a friend who was sick, grieving, or lost--and for anyone who has struggled to seek or accept help.

title: Where Reasons End
author: Yiyun Li
description: Yiyun Li meets life’s deepest sorrows as she imagines a conversation between a mother and dead child named Nikolai in a timeless world. Composed in the months after Li lost a child to suicide.

title: If We Can Keep It: How the Republic Collapsed and How It Might Be Saved
author: Michael Tomasky
description: An account of the deep roots of political polarization in America, including a fourteen-point agenda for how to fix it.

title: The Age of Light
author: Whitney Scharer
description: A novel inspired by the life of the Vogue model-turned-renowned photographer finds Lee Miller relocating to 1929 Paris, where she becomes the muse and colleague of the mercurial surrealist, Man Ray.

title: Milk of Paradise: A History of Opium
author: Lucy Inglis
description: A British writer unravels the history of the drug that has both healed and harmed since the beginning of civilization, tracing its emergence and evolution through to present-day addictions to derivatives such as OxyContin and heroin.

title: On the Come Up
author: Angie Thomas
description: This second novel from the bestselling author of The Hate U Give returns to the world of Garden Heights in a story about an aspiring teen rapper named Brianna.

title: Stalin's Scribe: Literature, Ambition, and Survival: The Life of Mikhail Sholokhov
author: Brian Boeck
description: A Russian historian complicates readers' understanding of the Nobel Prize-winning Russian author of And Quiet Flows the Don (1934), whom figures ranging from Alexander Solzhenitsyn to Salman Rushdie have maligned as a plagiarist and "patsy" of one of the 20th century's most brutal dictators.

title: I Am Yours: A Shared Memoir
author: Reema Zaman
description: A woman born in Bangladesh and raised in Thailand describes the difficulty of navigating life while female in a culture that silences and disbelieves women.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: A psychological thriller of a woman’s act of violence against her husband―and of the therapist obsessed with uncovering her motive.

title: The Lost Man
author: Jane Harper
description: Two brothers meet in the remote Australian outback when the third brother is found dead, in this new novel from New York Times bestseller Jane Harper.

title: Lady First: The World of First Lady Sarah Polk
author: Amy S Greenberg
description: The little-known story of remarkable First Lady Sarah Polk--a brilliant master of the art of high politics and a crucial but unrecognized figure in the history of American feminism.

title: What We Did
author: Christobel Kent
description: Bridget has a secret―one she keeps from everyone, even her husband. One that threatens to explode when her childhood music teacher, Carmichael, walks into her dress shop.

title: The Dead Ex
author: Jane Corry
description: One man's disappearance throws four women's lives into chaos--who will survive?

title: American Pop
author: Snowden Wright
description: Moving from Mississippi to Paris to New York and back again, a saga of family, ambition, passion, and tragedy that brings to life one unforgettable Southern dynasty—the Forsters, founders of the world’s first major soft-drink company—against the backdrop of more than a century of American cultural history.

title: Polaris Rising
author: Jessie Mihalik
description: A space princess on the run and a notorious outlaw soldier become unlikely allies—the first in an exciting science fiction trilogy.

title: Jimmy Neurosis: A Memoir
author: James Oseland
description: From a celebrated figure of the food world comes a memoir about being young and gay during the 1970s punk revolution in America.

title: Forget You Know Me
author: Jessica Strawser
description: Molly and Liza have always been enviably close. Even after Molly married Daniel, the couple considered Liza an honorary family member. But after Liza moved away, things grew more strained than anyone wanted to admit―in the friendship and the marriage.

title: The Stranger Inside
author: Laura Benedict
description: What if you came home to find a stranger living inside your house?

title: Such Good Work
author: Johannes Lichtman
description: Prompted by his drug addiction and latest dismissal to relocate to 2015 Sweden, creative-writing instructor Jonas Anderson volunteers to teach Swedish to Middle Eastern refugees, including one who challenges his views about making a difference.

title: Sea Monsters
author: Chloe Aridjis
description: One autumn afternoon in Mexico City, seventeen-year-old Luisa does not return home from school. Instead, she boards a bus to the Pacific coast with Tomás, a boy she barely knows.

title: The Made-Up Man
author: Joseph Scapellato
description: Existential noir meets absurd comedy when a young man reluctantly enlists as source material for an art project.

title: Same Same
author: Peter Mendelsund
description: In the shifting sands of the desert, near an unnamed metropolis, there is an institute where various fellows come to undertake projects of great significance. But when our sort-of-hero, Percy Frobisher, arrives, his mind goes completely blank.

title: Hard to Love: Essays and Confessions
author: Briallen Hopper
description: An essay collection about the importance of multiple forms of love and friendship in a world designed for couples, from a laser-precise new voice.

title: Walk This Way: Run-DMC, Aerosmith, and the Song That Changed American Music Forever
author: Geoff Edgers
description: A Washington Post staff writer offers a cultural history and play-by-play of the unlikely 1986 recording session that he argues catapulted hip-hop into the mainstream and revived Aerosmith's fading career.

title: Empty Planet: The Shock of Global Population Decline
author: Darrell Bricker and John Ibbitson
description: A social researcher and a journalist critique diagnoses of a coming overpopulation of Earth and counter it with the opposite conclusion—that birth rates are declining and will lead to a significant dip in the human population over the next century.

title: The Atlas of Reds and Blues
author: Devi S Laskar
description: Set in 2017 near Atlanta, the novel centers on Mother, an Indian-American woman in her 40s with three daughters and a husband who travels internationally more than he’s at home. One morning, after taking her children to school, Mother is gunned down in her driveway in an unexplained robbery; the narrative is told in discursive segments that jump around in time to present flashes of Mother’s life, all while she lies dying.

title: The Coronation: A Fandorin Mystery
author: Boris Akunin, Trans. by Andrew Bromfield
description: After five years spent abroad building up a business as something of a private investigator, the handsome, stuttering Fandorin is back in Moscow―and in for a case that entangles him with the highest echelons of Romanov royalty.

title: A Spy in Exile: A Thriller
author: Jonathan De Shalit
description: In this sequel to Traitor , former Israeli intelligence agent Ya'ara Stein is called upon by the prime minister to form a secret unit that must face a lethal terrorist cell with ties to old European factions.

title: A People's Future of the United States: Speculative Fiction from 25 Extraordinary Writers
author: Victor Lavalle
description: A collection of twenty-five tales explores the possible futures of the United States from such writers as G. Willow Wilson, Justina Ireland, Seanan McGuire, and Gabby Rivera.

title: Tonic and Balm
author: Stephanie Allen
description: Set against a backdrop of rural poverty and a wave of anti-black violence, Tonic and Balm examines the tenuous solidarity and shifting alliances of people on the fringes of society.

title: Notes from a Black Woman's Diary: Selected Works of Kathleen Collins
author: Kathleen Collins
description: Kathleen Collins’s writing brings to life characters whose quotidian concerns powerfully illuminate the particular joys, challenges, and heartbreaks rendered by the African-American experience.

title: Magical Negro
author: Morgan Parker
description: An archive of black everydayness, a catalog of contemporary folk heroes, an ethnography of ancestral grief, and an inventory of figureheads, idioms, and customs. These American poems are both elegy and jive, joke and declaration, songs of congregation and self-conception.

title: The Girl in the Glass Box: A Jack Swyteck Novel
author: James Grippando
description: Miami attorney Jack Swyteck lands in the heart of the contentious immigration debate when he takes on the heart-wrenching case of an undocumented immigrant who fled to America to protect her daughter and save herself, in this thriller that explores the stories behind the headlines from New York Times bestselling author James Grippando, winner of the Harper Lee Prize for Legal Fiction.

title: Stalker
author: Lars Kepler
description: The Swedish National Crime Unit receives a video of a young woman in her home, clearly unaware that she's being watched. Soon after the tape is received, the woman's body is found horrifically mutilated.

title: Wild Bill: The True Story of the American Frontier's First Gunfighter
author: Tom Clavin
description: The definitive true story of Wild Bill, the first lawman of the Wild West, by the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Dodge City .

title: The Hiding Place
author: C J Tudor
description: The second novel from the author of The Chalk Man , about a teacher with a hidden agenda who returns to settle scores at a school he once attended, only to uncover a darker secret than he could have imagined.

title: Figuring
author: Maria Popova
description: An exploration of the complexities of love and the human search for truth and meaning told through the interconnected lives of several historical figures across four centuries.

title: Good Riddance
author: Elinor Lipman
description: A new romantic comedy from Elinor Lipman, in which one woman's trash becomes another woman's treasure.

title: Enchantée
author: Gita Trelease
description: Paris is a labyrinth of twisted streets filled with beggars and thieves, revolutionaries and magicians. Camille Durbonne is one of them. She wishes she weren’t.

title: Off Season
author: James Sturm
description: Set against the backdrop of the disorienting 2016 presidential election, this graphic novel—first published in installments at Slate —offers a meditation on love, family, and masculinity in the Trump era.

title: The Peacock Feast
author: Lisa Gornick
description: In this imagined history, an aged Prudence looks back on her troubling life under the gilded roof of Louis C. Tiffany—the son of the founder of Tiffany & Co. and the company's design director—prompted by a visit from her grandniece nearly a century later.

title: The Glovemaker
author: Ann Weisgarber
description: In the latest from the author of The Personal History of Rachel DuPree , a Mormon woman living in a tiny community in the Utah Territory of 1888 faces tough decisions when a fellow Mormon shows up at her door looking for shelter from the federal government that he says is pursuing him as a practitioner of polygamy, a crime.

title: The Overnight Kidnapper
author: Andrea Camilleri, Trans. by Stephen Sartarelli
description: In this 25th mystery featuring Sicilian Inspector Salvo Montalbano, the titular hero investigates a series of abductions of young women and an arson case involving a store whose owner is missing.

title: The Ruin of Kings
author: Jenn Lyons
description: In this first in a planned five-book epic fantasy, Kihrin grew up in the slums of Quur, a thief and a minstrel's son raised on tales of long-lost princes and magnificent quests. When he is claimed against his will as the missing son of a treasonous prince, Kihrin finds himself at the mercy of his new family's ruthless power plays and political ambitions.

title: Snow White Learns Witchcraft: Stories and Poems
author: Theodora Goss
description: The World Fantasy Award winning author retells and recasts fairy tales by Charles Perrault, the Brothers Grimm, Hans Christian Andersen, and Oscar Wilde in stories and poems that re-center and empower the women at the heart of these timeless narratives.

title: Willa & Hesper
author: Amy Feltman
description: In this debut novel, two young women in an MFA writing program fall into an intense romance while exploring their families' traumatic histories during the Jewish holocaust during World War II.

title: Savage Conversations
author: Leanne Howe
description: In this genre-bending book of poetic drama that draws on the record of Mary Todd Lincoln's psychiatric problems and her institutionalization, the First Lady is haunted by the ghost of a "Savage Indian" who confronts her about her complicity in the 1862 hanging of 38 Dakota Indians ordered by President Lincoln.

title: Wild Life
author: Molly Gloss
description: Winner of the James Tiptree Jr. Award after its first release in 2000, this reissued novel tells the story—both real and imagined—of the free-thinking, cigar-smoking, trouser-wearing Charlotte Bridger Drummond, who pens dime-store women’s adventure stories. On a search in the woods for a lost little girl, Charlotte encounters a mysterious band of mountain giants, also known as Sasquatch.

title: Brown White Black: An American Family at the Intersection of Race, Gender, Sexuality, and Religion
author: Nishta J. Mehra
description: Essays describe how the author's experiences as an Indian American, the wife of a white Christian woman, and the mother of an adopted black son have been challenged by rigid cultural family norms.

title: El Norte: The Epic and Forgotten Story of Hispanic North America
author: Carrie Gibson
description: A sweeping saga of the Spanish history and influence in North America over five centuries, from the author of Empire’s Crossroads: A History of the Caribbean From Columbus to the Present Day and a contributor to The Guardian and BBC.

title: On Being 40(ish)
author: Lindsey Mead
description: Fifteen powerful women and writers—from the pages of the New Yorker , New York Times , Vogue , Glamour , and The Atlantic —offer candid explorations about what it’s really like turning forty—and that the best is yet to come.

title: Good to Go: What the Athlete in All of Us Can Learn from the Strange Science of Recovery
author: Christie Aschwanden
description: An eye-opening exploration of how the human body can best recover and adapt to sports and fitness training.

title: Iran Rising: The Survival and Future of the Islamic Republic
author: Amin Saikal
description: On the fortieth anniversary of the 1978–79 Iranian revolution, a political picture of the Islamic Republic

title: One Fatal Mistake
author: Tom Hunt
description: A thriller about a hit-and-run and a lie that goes horribly wrong.

title: The Future Is Asian: Commerce, Conflict, and Culture in the 21st Century
author: Parag Khanna
description: In the 19th century, the world was Europeanized. In the 20th century, it was Americanized. Now, in the 21st century, the world is being Asianized.

title: The Story of Britain: A History of the Great Ages: From the Romans to the Present
author: Roy Strong
description: An authoritative and sweeping history of Britain from the Romans to the present day--in a newly revised edition for the next generation of readers.

title: Whiteshift: Populism, Immigration, and the Future of White Majorities
author: Eric Kaufmann
description: A University of London political scientist examines ethnic change in Western Europe and North America and proposes political solutions for dealing with the anxiety surrounding that shift among whites.

title: The Story of Silver: How the White Metal Shaped America and the Modern World
author: William L Silber
description: How silver influenced two hundred years of world history, and why it matters today.

title: The Wedding Guest: An Alex Delaware Novel
author: Jonathan Kellerman
description: Psychologist Alex Delaware and detective Milo Sturgis unravel a shocking crime at a wedding reception in this psychological thriller from the New York Times bestselling author.

title: Empires of the Weak: The Real Story of European Expansion and the Creation of the New World Order
author: J.C. Sharman
description: A University of Cambridge international relations professor argues that European expansion from the late 15th to the late 18th centuries has less to do with Western military might than deference to strong Asian and African polities, disease in the Americas, and maritime supremacy earned by default.

title: All My Goodbyes
author: Mariana Dimópulos, Trans. by Alice Whitmore
description: Diffident, self-critical, wary of commitment, a young Argentinian woman feels her identity is in pieces and condemns herself to repeated acts of departure—from places, parents, and lovers. Then, arriving in the southernmost region of Patagonia, she convinces herself she has found happiness, until she’s caught up in the horrific murders that haunt her story.

title: When You Read This
author: Mary Adkins
description: When Iris dies of terminal cancer, aged 33, her friend and colleague Smith is left adrift without her. Smith is surprised to discover that in her last six months, Iris created a blog filled with sharp and often funny musings on the end of a life not quite fulfilled. She also made one final request: for Smith to get her posts published as a book. With the help of his new intern Carl, Smith tackles the task of fulfilling Iris’s last wish. Before he can do so, though, he must get the approval of Iris’ sister Jade. Each carrying their own baggage, Smith and Jade end up on a collision course with their own unresolved pasts and with each other.

title: The Killer Collective
author: Barry Eisler
description: A fast-paced, page-turning novel of betrayal, vengeance, and depraved secrets in high places from the New York Times bestselling author of the John Rain and Livia Lone series.

title: Go Ahead in the Rain: Notes to A Tribe Called Quest
author: Hanif Abdurraqib
description: Poet and essayist Hanif Abdurraqib digs into A Tribe Called Quest's history and draws from his own experience to reflect on how its distinctive sound resonated among fans like himself.

title: The Forgotten Hours
author: Katrin Schumann
description: In her debut novel, Katrin Schumann weaves a story of past and present—and how love can lead us astray.

title: Rock Needs River: A Memoir about a Very Open Adoption
author: Vanessa McGrady
description: The author's decision to enter into an open adoption takes an unexpected twist when her daughter's biological parents become homeless and she invites them to stay with her—an unusual living arrangement that becomes a well of conflicting emotions and increasingly difficult decisions chronicled here.

title: The Shaker Murders
author: Eleanor Kuhns
description: Shortly after Will Rees and his family arrive at a peaceful Shaker community, a series of unfortunate accidents occur killing several people. The community wants to believe nothing sinister is happening, but Rees thinks otherwise.

title: In Search of Isaiah Berlin: A Literary Adventure
author: Henry Hardy
description: The story of the decades-long collaboration between one of the great thinkers of the 20th century and his editor, Henry Hardy, who made it his vocation to bring Berlin's huge body of work into print.

title: Tombland
author: C. J. Sansom
description: This historical detective series continues with this mystery for fans of Hilary Mantel, set in a time of great political upheaval in Tudor-era England.

title: Deep Creek: Finding Hope in the High Country
author: Pam Houston
description: On her 120-acre homestead high in the Colorado Rockies, Pam Houston—the author of Cowboys Are My Weakness — learns what it means to care for a piece of land and the creatures on it.

title: The Plotters
author: Un-Su Kim, Trans. by Sora Kim-Russell
description: A fantastical crime novel set in an alternate Seoul where assassination guilds compete for market dominance.

title: We Cast a Shadow
author: Maurice Carlos Ruffin
description: In this near-future Southern city plagued by fenced-in ghettos and police violence, more and more residents are turning to this experimental medical procedure. Like any father, our narrator just wants the best for his son, Nigel, a biracial boy whose black birthmark is getting bigger by the day. How far will he go to protect his son?

title: House of Stone
author: Novuyo Rosa Tshuma
description: A sweeping epic that spans the fall of Rhodesia through Zimbabwe’s turbulent beginnings, exploring the persistence of the oppressed in a young nation seeking an identity, but built on forgetting.

title: Sleeping with Strangers: How the Movies Shaped Desire
author: David Thomson
description: An account of sexuality in the movies and of how actors and actresses on screen have fed our desire.

title: The Twenty-Ninth Year
author: Hala Alyan
description: Poems that examine the connections between physical and interior migration, from award-winning Palestinian American poet, novelist, and clinical psychologist Hala Alyan, author of Salt Houses .

title: Dreyer's English: An Utterly Correct Guide to Clarity and Style
author: Benjamin Dreyer
description: We all write, all the time: books, blogs, emails. Lots and lots of emails. And we all want to write better. Benjamin Dreyer is here to help.

title: All the Lives We Ever Lived: Seeking Solace in Virginia Woolf
author: Katharine Smyth
description: A lyrical memoir about the power of literature to help us read our own lives—and see clearly the people we love most.

title: The World According to Fannie Davis: My Mother's Life in the Detroit Numbers
author: Bridgett M, Davis
description: A singular memoir highlighting 'the outstanding humanity of black America' that tells the story of one unforgettable mother, her devoted daughter, and the life they lead in the Detroit numbers of the 1960s and 1970s.

title: The Goodness Paradox: The Strange Relationship Between Virtue and Violence in Human Evolution
author: Richard Wrangham
description: A Harvard biological anthropology professor offers a theory of how, in the last 250 million years, humankind became an increasingly peaceful species in daily interactions even as its capacity for coolly planned and devastating violence remains undiminished.

title: The Falconer
author: Dana Czapnik
description: A snapshot of the New York City and America through the eyes of the children of the baby boomers grappling with privilege and the fading of radical hopes.

title: Crazy Cupid Love
author: Amanda Heger
description: Eliza Herman (a.k.a. The World's Worst Cupid) has spent her entire life carefully avoiding her calling. But when a family crisis requires her to fill in at the local Cupid-for-hire shop, Eliza finds herself enchanting couples under the watchful eye of her assigned mentor and crush, Jake Sanders. Before long, Eliza is rethinking her stance on romance

title: Let Me Finish: Trump, the Kushners, Bannon, New Jersey, and the Power of In-Your-Face Politics
author: Chris Christie
description: From the former governor, a no-holds-barred account of Chris Christie's rise to power through the bare-knuckle politics of New Jersey and his insights about Donald Trump from inside the president's inner circle.

title: Golden Child
author: Claire Adam
description: A debut novel set in Trinidad, following the lives of a family as they navigate impossible choices about scarcity, loyalty, and love.

title: Judgment
author: Joseph Finder
description: New York Times bestselling author Joseph Finder returns with a new thriller about a female judge and the one personal misstep that could lead to her—and her family's—downfall.

title: Black Is the Body: Stories from My Grandmother's Time, My Mother's Time, and Mine
author: Emily Bernard
description: A memoir that looks at race in twelve telltale, connected essays that explore the complexities and memories and ambushing realities of growing up black in the South with a family name inherited from a white man, of getting a PhD from Yale, of marrying a white man from the North, of adopting two babies from Ethiopia, of teaching at a white college and living in America's New England today.

title: Team of Vipers: My 500 Extraordinary Days in the Trump White House
author: Cliff Sims
description: An insider's account of the Trump White House told by former Special Assistant to the President and Director of White House Message Strategy Cliff Sims.

title: Underground: A Human History of the Worlds Beneath Our Feet
author: Will Hunt

title: Downhill from Here: Retirement Insecurity in the Age of Inequality
author: Katherine S. Newman
description: The author of No Shame in My Game: the Working Poor in the Inner City turns her critical eye toward retirement, the struggles many Baby Boomers are encountering as they enter their golden years, and the not-so-bright future of Social Security and other protections for the aged.

title: Here and Now and Then (Original)
author: Mike Chen
description: Stranded for eighteen years since the 1990s, time-traveling agent Kin Stewart, suffering from memory loss, has started a new life, but when rescuers from the year 2142 finally arrive, he must choose between his current family and the one he left behind in the future.

title: The Bold World: A Memoir of Family and Transformation
author: Jodie Patterson
description: Inspired by her transgender son, activist Jodie Patterson explores identity, gender, race, and authenticity to tell the real-life story of a family’s history and transformation.

title: Antisemitism: Here and Now
author: Deborah E Lipstadt
description: The award-winning author of The Eichmann Trial and Denial: Holocaust History on Trial gives us a penetrating and provocative analysis of the hate that will not die, focusing on its current, virulent incarnations on both the political right and left.

title: The Temp
author: Michelle Frances
description: Emma would do anything to work for the woman who has the job she wants. Carrie is at the top of her game, with a dream career, a baby on the way, and a handsome screenwriter husband. For Emma, with parents who don’t understand her ambition and a serious misstep behind her, this temp position might be her last chance.

title: Vigilance
author: Robert Jackson Bennett
description: A dark science fiction action parable from an America that has permanently surrendered to gun violence.

title: The Lost Girls of Paris (Original)
author: Pam Jenoff
description: One morning while passing through Grand Central Terminal on her way to work, Grace Healey finds an abandoned suitcase tucked beneath a bench. Unable to resist her own curiosity, Grace opens the suitcase, where she discovers a dozen photographs—each of a different woman.

title: The Pope: Francis, Benedict, and the Decision That Shook the World
author: Anthony McCarten
description: From an Academy Award-nominated screenwriter comes the revealing tale of an unprecedented transfer of power, and of two very different men - who both happen to live in the Vatican.

title: Try Common Sense: Replacing the Failed Ideologies of Right and Left
author: Philip K Howard
description: Award-winning author Philip K. Howard lays out the blueprint for a new American society.

title: The Orchid and the Dandelion: Why Some Children Struggle and How All Can Thrive
author: W. Thomas Boyce
description: A developmental pediatrician reveals how genetic make-up and environment shape behavior and explains how to understand troubled children for their unique sensibilities, their considerable challenges, and their remarkable gifts.

title: The End of Loneliness
author: Benedict Wells
description: Jules Moreau’s childhood is shattered after the sudden death of his parents. Enrolled in boarding school where he and his siblings are forced to live apart, the once vivacious and fearless Jules retreats inward, preferring to live within his memories.

title: The Mastermind: Drugs. Empire. Murder. Betrayal.
author: Evan Ratliff
description: The true story of the decade-long quest to bring down Paul Le Roux—the creator of a frighteningly powerful Internet-enabled cartel who merged the ruthlessness of a drug lord with the technological savvy of a Silicon Valley entrepreneur.

title: That Churchill Woman
author: Stephanie Barron
description: Wealthy, privileged, and fiercely independent New Yorker Jennie Jerome took Victorian England by storm when she landed on its shores. As Lady Randolph Churchill, she gave birth to a man who defined the twentieth century: her son Winston. But Jennie—reared in the luxury of Gilded Age Newport and the Paris of the Second Empire—lived an outrageously modern life all her own, filled with controversy, passion, tragedy, and triumph.

title: From the Ground Up: A Journey to Reimagine the Promise of America
author: Howard Schultz
description: From the longtime CEO and chairman of Starbucks, a work about the new responsibilities that leaders, businesses, and citizens share in American society today—as viewed through the intimate lens of one man’s life and work.

title: Slow Motion Ghosts
author: Jeff Noon
description: It is 1981 and Detective Inspector Henry Hobbes is still reeling in the aftermath of the fire and fury of the Brixton riots. The battle lines of society - and the police force - are being redrawn on a daily basis.

title: What Hell Is Not
author: Alessandro D'Avenia, trans. by Jeremy Parzen
description: Sicily, 1993. Fear rules the streets of Palermo. Teenage boys patrol the narrow streets armed with AK-47’s, marking out the territory of their mafia bosses. This is what hell is.

title: The Wartime Sisters
author: Lynda Cohen Loigman
description: Two estranged sisters, raised in Brooklyn and each burdened with her own shocking secret, are reunited at the Springfield Armory in the early days of WWII.

title: Unmarriageable
author: Soniah Kamal
description: In this one-of-a-kind retelling of Pride and Prejudice set in modern-day Pakistan, Alys Binat has sworn never to marry—until an encounter with one Mr. Darsee at a wedding makes her reconsider.

title: The Eulogist
author: Terry Gamble
description: From the author of The Water Dancers and Good Family , a novel set in Ohio in the decades leading to the Civil War, that illuminates the immigrant experience, the injustice of slavery, and the debts human beings owe to one another, witnessed through the endeavors of one Irish-American family.

title: Golden State
author: Ben Winters
description: From award-winning, New York Times bestselling novelist Ben H. Winters comes a mind-bending novel set in a world governed by absolute truth, where lies are as dangerous as murder.

title: 99 Nights in Logar
author: Jamil Jan Kochai
description: A coming-of-age story about one boy's journey across contemporary Afghanistan to find and bring home the family dog.

title: Camelot's End: Kennedy vs. Carter and the Fight That Broke the Democratic Party
author: Jon Ward
description: From a strange, dark chapter in American political history comes the captivating story of Ted Kennedy's 1980 campaign for president against the incumbent Jimmy Carter, told in full for the first time.

title: Miraculum
author: Steph Post
description: When one tragedy after another strikes the carnival―and it becomes clear that Daniel is somehow at the center of calamity―Ruby takes it upon herself to discover the mystery of the shadowy man pulling all the strings.

title: Maid: Hard Work, Low Pay, and a Mother's Will to Survive
author: Stephanie Land
description: A journalist describes the years she worked in low-paying domestic work under wealthy employers, contrasting the privileges of the upper-middle class to the realities of the overworked laborers supporting them.

title: The Inner Level: How More Equal Societies Reduce Stress, Restore Sanity and Improve Everyone's Well-Being
author: Kate Pickett and Richard Wilkinson
description: The authors of The Spirit Level return with a new volume exploring how social and financial inequality affects us individually, altering how we think, feel and behave.

title: Mary Ventura and the Ninth Kingdom: A Story
author: Sylvia Plath
description: In this previously unpublished story penned more than a decade before the author published The Bell Jar , a young woman is coerced into taking a strange train ride toward a sinister destination.

title: A German Officer in Occupied Paris: The War Journals, 1941-1945
author: Ernst Jünger, Trans. by Thomas S. Hansen and Abby J. Hansen
description: Ernst Jünger, one of 20th century Germany's most important and controversial writers, faithfully kept a journal during the Second World War in occupied Paris, on the eastern front, and in Germany until its defeat. These wartime journals appear here in English for the first time.

title: Restoration Heights
author: Wil Medearis
description: In this debut novel, a young, white artist named Reddick is the last person to see the daughter of a wealthy Manhattan family before she disappears. When the family refuses to call the police, Reddick sets out to discover what happened to her where he saw her last—Bedford-Stuyvesant, the historically black Brooklyn neighborhood besieged by gentrification, where he lives.

title: Prisoner: My 544 Days in an Iranian Prison—Solitary Confinement, a Sham Trial, High-Stakes Diplomacy, and the Extraordinary Efforts It Took to Get Me Out
author: Jason Rezaian
description: In July 2014, Washington Post Tehran bureau chief Jason Rezaian was arrested by Iranian police on fabricated charges that he was spying for America. Here he narrates the story of his arrest and the 18 months he spent in an Iranian prison.

title: The Alarming Palsy of James Orr
author: Tom Lee
description: James Orr—husband, father, reliable employee and all-around model citizen—awakes one morning to find half his face paralyzed. Waiting for the affliction to pass, he stops going to work and wanders his idyllic estate, with its woodland, uniform streets and perfectly manicured lawns. But there are cracks in the veneer. And as his orderly existence begins to unravel, it appears that James himself may not be the man he thought he was.

title: Last Boat Out of Shanghai: The Epic Story of the Chinese Who Fled Mao's Revolution
author: Helen Zia
