description: The real life stories of four young people caught up in the mass exodus from Shanghai in the wake of China’s 1949 Communist revolution.

title: The Heartbeat of Wounded Knee: Native America from 1890 to the Present
author: David Treuer
description: A finalist for the 2019 National Book Award, The Heartbeat of Wounded Knee is a sweeping history—and counter-narrative—of Native American life from the Wounded Knee massacre to the present.

title: The Current
author: Tim Johnston
description: When two young women leave their college campus in the dead of winter for a 700-mile drive north to Minnesota, they suddenly find themselves fighting for their lives in the icy waters of the Black Root River, just miles from home. One girl's survival, and the other's death—murder, actually—stun the citizens of a small Minnesota town, thawing memories of another young woman who lost her life in the same river ten years earlier, and whose killer may yet live among them.

title: The Kingdom of Copper
author: S. A. Chakraborty
description: Nahri’s life changed forever the moment she accidentally summoned Dara, a formidable, mysterious djinn, during one of her schemes. Whisked from her home in Cairo, she was thrust into the dazzling royal court of Daevabad—and quickly discovered she would need all her grifter instincts to survive there.

title: Cuba Libre!: Che, Fidel, and the Improbable Revolution That Changed World History
author: Tony Perrottet
description: The surprising story of Che Guevara, Fidel Castro, and the scrappy band of rebel men and women who followed them.

title: The Suspect
author: Fiona Barton
description: The New York Times bestselling author of The Widow returns with a new novel of psychological suspense about every parent’s worst nightmare.

title: The Weight of a Piano
author: Chris Cander
description: The story of two women and the piano that inexorably ties their lives together through time and across continents, for better and for worse.

title: The Snow Leopard Project: And Other Adventures in Warzone Conservation
author: Alex Dehgan
description: The story of the heroic effort to save and preserve Afghanistan's wildlife-and a culture that derives immense pride and a sense of national identity from its natural landscape.

title: Holy Lands
author: Amanda Sthers
description: A dysfunctional family--led by a Jewish pig farmer in Israel--struggles to love and accept each other. Soon to be a major motion picture.

title: Team Human
author: Douglas Rushkoff
description: The host of the popular Team Human podcast offers a manifesto in which he argues that humans are essentially social creatures and achieve their greatest aspirations when they work together―not as individuals.

title: We Want to Negotiate: The Secret World of Kidnapping, Hostages and Ransom
author: Joel Simon
description: The executive director of the Committee to Protect Journalists offers an argument for the United States and United Kingdom to be less rigid in its policy of refusing to pay militants who have taken journalists hostage, arguing journalists taken hostage have a better chance of survival if they are from nations that do negotiate.

title: The Golden Tresses of the Dead: A Flavia de Luce Novel
author: Alan Bradley
description: In this 10th installment of Bradley's novels about 12-year-old sleuth Flavia de Luce, the gifted young scientist tackles a mystery close to home: an unwelcome discovery in her sister's wedding cake—a human finger.

title: All Systems Red
author: Martha Wells
description: On a distant planet, a team of scientists are conducting surface tests, shadowed by their Company-supplied ‘droid―a self-aware SecUnit that has hacked its own governor module, and refers to itself as 'Murderbot.' Scornful of humans, all it really wants is to be left alone long enough to figure out who it is.

title: Unexampled Courage: The Blinding of Sgt. Isaac Woodard and the Awakening of President Harry S. Truman and Judge J. Waties Waring
author: Richard Gergel
description: A United States district judge reviews the legacy of the case of Isaac Woodard, a black World War II veteran who in 1946 was beaten and permanently blinded by police officers in South Carolina, setting off a national controversy that led to important legal and political shifts that would influence the coming civil rights movement.

title: Bookends: Collected Intros and Outros
author: Michael Chabon
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning author Michael Chabon offers a compilation of pieces about literature—age-old classics as well as his own—that presents a unique look into his literary origins and influences, the books that shaped his taste and formed his ideas about writing and reading.

title: The Nowhere Child
author: Christian White
description: Winner of the Victorian Premier’s Literary Award, The Nowhere Child is screenwriter Christian White’s internationally bestselling debut thriller of psychological suspense about a woman uncovering devastating secrets about her family―and her very identity.

title: The Rule of Law
author: John Lescroart
description: In this 21st novel featuring attorney Dismas Hardy, Hardy's secretary Phyllis is arrested for allegedly abetting the murder of a coyote who’d been smuggling women from El Salvador and Mexico—and Hardy takes on Phyllis's case.

title: Rupture: An Ari Thor Thriller
author: Ragnar Jonasson
description: Young policeman Ari Thór tries to solve a 50-year-old murder when new evidence surfaces. But the case proves difficult in a town where no one wants to know the truth, where secrets are a way of life.

title: Hark
author: Sam Lipsyte
description: A send-up of our contemporary culture from Sam Lipsyte, the critically acclaimed author of Home Land , centered around an unwitting mindfulness guru named Hark Morner and the phenomenon he initiates.

title: The Dreamers
author: Karen Thompson Walker
description: An ordinary town is transformed by a mysterious illness that triggers perpetual sleep in this novel from the New York Times bestselling author of The Age of Miracles.

title: Late in the Day
author: Tessa Hadley
description: The author of The Past and other novels narrates here the story of two married couples—Alexandr and Christine and Zachary and Lydia—who get thrown for a loop when Zachary suddenly dies, stirring up old feelings between Lydia and Alexandr they'd thought long since snuffed.

title: Inheritance: A Memoir of Genealogy, Paternity, and Love
author: Dani Shapiro
description: The author of Hourglass now gives us a new memoir about identity, paternity, and family secrets—a real-time exploration of the staggering discovery she recently made about her father, and her struggle to piece together the hidden story of her own life.

title: You Know You Want This: "Cat Person" and Other Stories
author: Kristen Roupenian
description: The highly anticipated debut from the author of 'Cat Person.' A collection of short stories that explore the complex—and often darkly funny—connections between gender, sex, and power across genres.

title: Still in Love
author: Michael Downing
description: Replete with engaging writing exercises, harsh criticism, and contrarian advice, Still in Love is the story of one semester in a college classroom. And it is an urgent reminder that we desperately need classrooms, that those singular, sealed-off-from-the-world sanctuaries are where we learn to love our lives.

title: Mothers: Stories
author: Chris Power
description: Chris Power’s stories are peopled by men and women who find themselves at crossroads or dead ends―characters who search without knowing what they seek. Their paths lead them to thresholds, bridges, rivers, and sites of mysterious, irresistible connection to the past.

title: The Accidental Further Adventures of the Hundred-Year-Old Man
author: Jonas Jonasson, Trans. by Rachel Willson-Broyles
description: The sequel to Jonas Jonasson’s international bestseller The Hundred-Year-Old Man Who Climbed Out of the Window and Disappeared .

title: The End of Ice: Bearing Witness and Finding Meaning in the Path of Climate Disruption
author: Dahr Jamail
description: The author who Jeremy Scahill calls the 'quintessential unembedded reporter' visits 'hot spots' around the world in a global quest to discover how we will cope with our planet’s changing ecosystems.

title: Elsey Come Home
author: Susan Conley
description: From the widely praised author of Paris Was the Place --a new novel that bravely delves into the darkest corners of addiction, marriage, and motherhood.

title: Silence: A Social History of One of the Least Understood Elements of Our Lives
author: Jane Brox
description: A history of silence as a powerful shaper of the human mind—in prisons, in places of contemplation, and in our own lives.

title: Last Woman Standing
author: Amy Gentry
description: Dana Diaz is an aspiring stand‑up comedian—a woman in a man’s world. When she meets a tough computer programmer named Amanda Dorn, the two bond over their struggles in boys’ club professions.

title: As Long as We Both Shall Live
author: Joann Chaney
description: Detectives Loren and Spengler want to know if Matt is a grieving, twice-unlucky husband or a cold-blooded murderer. They dig into the couple’s lives to see what they can unearth. And they find that love’s got teeth, it’s got claws, and once it hitches you to a person, it’s tough to rip yourself free.

title: The Far Field
author: Madhuri Vijay
description: Pushcart Prize-winner Madhuri Vijay’s novel follows a complicated flaneuse across the Indian subcontinent as she reckons with her past, her desires, and the tumultuous present.

title: Joy Enough: A Memoir
author: Sarah McColl
description: A life-affirming memoir of a daughter making and remaking her life in her mother's image.

title: Night School: A Reader for Grownups
author: Zsofia Ban Trans. by Jim Tucker
description: A tongue-in-cheek textbook for how to live in our modern age.

title: No Sunscreen for the Dead
author: Tim Dorsey
description: The Sunshine State’s most lovable psychopath, Serge A. Storms, kills it in this zany adventure from the New York Times bestselling author Tim Dorsey.

title: Adèle
author: Leila Slimani Trans. by Sam Taylor
description: Adèle appears to have the perfect life: She is a successful journalist in Paris who lives in a beautiful apartment with her surgeon husband and their young son. But underneath the surface, she is bored--and consumed by an insatiable need for sex.

title: The Birth of Loud: Leo Fender, Les Paul, and the Guitar-Pioneering Rivalry That Shaped Rock 'n' Roll
author: Ian S Port
description: A saga in the history of rock ‘n’ roll: the decades-long rivalry between the two men who innovated the electric guitar’s amplified sound—Leo Fender and Les Paul—and their intense competition to convince rock stars like the Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, and Eric Clapton to play the instruments they built.

title: The Banished Immortal: A Life of Li Bai (Li Po)
author: Ha Jin
description: From the National Book Award-winning author of Waiting : a narratively driven biography of the Tang dynasty poet Li Bai—also known as Li Po.

title: Why We Fight: One Man's Search for Meaning Inside the Ring
author: Josh Rosenblatt
description: Using his own training as an opportunity to understand how the sport illuminates basic human impulses, Rosenblatt weaves together cultural history, criticism, biology, and anthropology to understand what happens to the human body and mind when under attack, and to explore why he, a self-described 'cowardly boy from the suburbs,' discovered so much meaning in putting his body, and others’, at risk.

title: Duped: Double Lives, False Identities, and the Con Man I Almost Married
author: Abby Ellin
description: Abby Ellin was shocked to learn that her fiancé was leading a secret life. But as she soon discovered, the world is full of people who aren't what they seem.

title: No Exit
author: Taylor Adams
description: On her way to Utah to see her dying mother, college student Darby Thorne gets caught in a fierce blizzard in the mountains of Colorado. With the roads impassable, she’s forced to wait out the storm at a remote highway rest stop. Desperate to find a signal to call home, Darby goes back out into the storm and makes a horrifying discovery: a little girl is locked in an animal crate.

title: Free All Along: The Robert Penn Warren Civil Rights Interviews
author: Stephen Drury Smith
description: A collection of previously unpublished interviews with key figures of the black freedom struggle by the Pulitzer Prize–winning author.

title: Code Name: Lise: The True Story of the Woman Who Became Wwii's Most Highly Decorated Spy
author: Larry Loftis
description: The true story of Odette Sansom, the British spy who operated in occupied France and fell in love with her commanding officer during World War II.

title: Last Night in Nuuk
author: Niviaq Korneliussen Trans. by Anna Halager
description: The highly acclaimed debut from an author profiled by the New Yorker as her country's 'unlikely literary star,' Last Night in Nuuk follows the lives of five young Greenlanders exploring their identities at the cusp of adulthood.

title: The Restless Kings: Henry II, His Sons and the Wars for the Plantagenet Crown
author: Nick Barratt
description: In The Restless Kings Nick Barratt presents the tumultuous struggle for supremacy between the first Plantagenet king, Henry II, and his four sons - a drama that tore apart the most powerful family in western Europe and shaped the future of two nations.

title: Unquiet
author: Linn Ullmann Trans. by Thilo Reinhold
description: A genre-bending book about time, memory, and the author's extraordinary childhood as the daughter of a genius filmmaker and his muse.

title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism: The Fight for a Human Future at the New Frontier of Power
author: Shoshana Zuboff
description: A retired Harvard Business School professor explores the challenges to humanity posed by the unprecedented form of power created in the digital age by corporations eager to predict and control our behavior.

title: Muhammad: Forty Introductions
author: Michael Muhammad Knight
description: Prophet, statesman, jurist, mystic, shaman, husband, father: there are infinite ways to remember and imagine Muhammad. This book provides forty different windows into his life, his teachings, and his legacy.

title: Only as the Day Is Long: New and Selected Poems
author: Dorianne Laux
description: A collection of new and selected works from prize-winning poet, Dorianne Laux.

title: Oculus: Poems
author: Sally Wen Mao
description: A second collection by Sally Wen Mao on the violence of the spectacle—starring the film legend Anna May Wong

title: Big Bang
author: David Bowman
description: This posthumous novel by the author of Let the Dog Drive , considers the events leading up to the assassination of President John F. Kennedy through the lens of many of the cultural figures of the mid-20th century, from Lucille Ball to Arthur Miller, engaged in various antics that skirt the line between fact and fiction.

title: Something Like Breathing
author: Angela Readman
description: In this debut novel, a girl named Lorrie strikes up a friendship with her strange new neighbor Sylvie in a remote Scottish town. The two young women are drawn into a series of events that leave the small town wondering who exactly Sylvie is and what strange gift she is hiding.

title: When Death Becomes Life: Notes from a Transplant Surgeon
author: Joshua D. Mezrich
description: A transplant surgeon discusses the pioneers, science, and ethical challenges of organ transplantation as well as the ways that organ transplants have revolutionized medical care, offering the stories of his own patients.

title: Confessions of a Rogue Nuclear Regulator
author: Gregory B. Jaczkzo
description: The story of the Birkenstocks-wearing physics Ph.D. and his controversial tenure as chairman of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, where he says he was pushed out after arguing for reforms of the nuclear-power industry after the disaster at Fukushima in Japan.

title: Bluff City: The Secret Life of Photographer Ernest Withers
author: Preston Lauterbach
description: The little-known story of an iconic photographer—and an FBI informant—whose work captured and influenced the U.S. Civil Rights Movement.

title: Tentacle
author: Rita Indiana, Trans. by Achy Obejas
description: One of the Dominican Republic's most prominent fiction writers narrates the story of Acilde Figueroa, a former sex worker and maid in post-apocalyptic Santo Domingo who finds herself at the heart of a voodoo prophecy: only she can travel back in time and save the ocean—and humanity—from disaster.

title: The Elephant in the Room: One Fat Man's Quest to Get Smaller in a Growing America
author: Tommy Tomlinson
description: Journalism Tommy Tomlinson chronicles his lifelong battle with weight in a voice that combines the urgency of Roxane Gay’s Hunger with the intimacy of Rick Bragg’s All Over but the Shoutin’.

title: Mala Vida
author: Marc Fernandez
description: Almodóvar meets Orwell in this acclaimed, fast-paced contemporary noir novel exposing the most shameful secrets of the Franco era.

title: No Mercy: A Mystery
author: Joanna Schaffhausen
description: Police officer Ellery Hathaway and FBI profiler Reed Markham take on two difficult new cases in this follow-up to The Vanishing Season.

title: Aristotle's Way: How Ancient Wisdom Can Change Your Life
author: Edith Hall
description: From renowned classicist Edith Hall, an examination of one of history's greatest philosophers, showing us how to lead happy, fulfilled, and meaningful lives.

title: Help Me!
author: Marianne Power
description: Marianne Power plumbs the trials and tests of being a modern woman in a 'have it all' culture, and what it really means to be our very best selves.

title: The Gilded Wolves
author: Roshani Chokshi
description: From the New York Times -bestselling author of The Star-Touched Queen comes a novel full of mystery, decadence, and adventure, set in a darkly glamorous world within 1889 Paris.

title: The Orphan of Salt Winds
author: Elizabeth Brooks
description: An old woman named Virginia returns to Salt Winds, a secluded house on the edge of an English marsh where she lived with adopted parents during World War II. Weaving between past and present, the novel follows Virginia's experience of a crime—and its haunting aftermath—that occurred when a German fighter plane crashed near Salt Winds.

title: The Liar's Room
author: Simon Lelic
description: Two liars. One room. No way out.

title: A Bound Woman Is a Dangerous Thing: The Incarceration of African American Women from Harriet Tubman to Sandra Bland
author: Damaris Hill
description: Contains biographical information about black women freedom fighters throughout the history of the United States, as well as poems inspired by the women discussed in the text.

title: The Time Has Come: Why Men Must Join the Gender Equality Revolution
author: Michael Kaufman
description: From the author of The Guy's Guide to Feminism comes this frank and forthright look at how men can fight for gender equality.

title: The Patricide of George Benjamin Hill
author: James Charlesworth
description: While their father takes his place at the center of a national scandal, these estranged siblings find themselves drawn from their four corners of the country, compelled along crowded interstates by resentment and confusion, converging on a 300-acre horse ranch outside Omaha for a final confrontation with the father they never had.

title: Creative Construction: The DNA of Sustained Innovation
author: Gary P. Pisano
description: A Harvard Business School professor offers his wisdom about growing companies based on research conducted over three decades and his on-the-ground experience with big companies and fast-growing ones that have moved beyond the start-up stage.

title: Women Rowing North: Navigating Life's Currents and Flourishing as We Age
author: Mary Pipher
description: The bestselling author who offered a psychological exploration of teenage girls in Reviving Ophelia returns with an examination of women and the challenges they face transitioning from middle to old age.

title: The Night Agent
author: Matthew Quirk
description: To find a Russian mole in the White House, an FBI agent must question everything. . . and trust no one.

title: The Post
author: Kevin A Munoz
description: Zone One meets Station Eleven in this chilling, post-apocalyptic debut, perfect for fans of The Walking Dead and The Handmaid's Tale .

title: Diderot and the Art of Thinking Freely
author: Andrew S. Curran
description: A biography of the prophetic and sympathetic philosopher who helped build the foundations of the modern world.

title: The Magnolia Inn
author: Carolyn Brown
description: Carolyn Brown brings together two wounded hearts in a Texas romance of second chances and twice-in-a-lifetime true love. Will they be able to let go of the past?

title: Horse Latitudes
author: Morris Collins
description: Haunted by guilt and reeling from his shattered marriage, New York photographer Ethan flees south to a Central American country on the brink of revolution.

title: Take-Out: And Other Tales of Culinary Crime
author: Rob Hart
description: Rob Hart explores the enticing and dangerous intersection where food and hospitality cross paths with crime and noir.

title: The Prosperity Paradox: How Innovation Can Lift Nations Out of Poverty
author: Clayton M Christensen
description: The ideas in this book will help companies desperate for real, long-term growth see actual, sustainable progress where they’ve failed before.

title: Rewrite: Loops in the Timescape
author: Gregory Benford
description: A history professor finds that he is able to travel back to 1968, the year he was sixteen—here, he finds a slew of mentors with the same ability, including Robert Heinlein, Albert Einstein, and Philip K. Dick and becomes a successful Hollywood screenwriter until some wicked time travelers try to subvert him.

title: The Perfect Liar
author: Thomas Christopher Greene
description: A seemingly perfect marriage is threatened by the deadly secrets husband and wife keep from each other.

title: Hitler's Pawn: The Boy Assassin and the Holocaust
author: Stephen Koch
description: A remarkable story of a forgotten seventeen-year-old Jew who was blamed by the Nazis for the anti-Semitic violence and terror known as the Kristallnacht , the pogrom still seen as an initiating event of the Holocaust.

title: Sacred Ground: The Chicago Streets of Timuel Black
author: Timuel D. Black
description: Sacred Ground is the personal memoir of famed Chicago historian Timuel Black, whose life and times from 1919 to the present capture pivotal moments in Chicago history as well as the civil rights movement in Chicago and nationally.

title: Mr Five Percent
author: Jonathan Conlin
description: When Calouste Gulbenkian died in 1955 at the age of 86, he was the richest man in the world, known as 'Mr Five Per Cent' for his personal share of Middle East oil. Written with full access to the Gulbenkian Foundation's archives, this is the story of the man who more than anyone else helped shape the modern oil industry.

title: An Anonymous Girl
author: Greer Hendricks
description: The next novel of psychological suspense and obsession from the authors of the blockbuster bestseller The Wife Between Us .

title: Old Newgate Road
author: Keith Scribner
description: The story of a father's return to his childhood home, the site of unspeakable tragedy, and of the often warring obligations we have to our family, our friends, and our past.

title: Ghost Wall
author: Sarah Moss
description: A teenager and her working-class family join a group of experimental archaeologists and must face the sinister connections between their own circumstances and the brutal lives of the Iron Age inhabitants of Britain.

title: An Orchestra of Minorities
author: Chigozie Obioma
description: A story about a Nigerian poultry farmer—and his guiding spirit, or chi —who sacrifices everything to win the woman he loves by the Man Booker finalist and author of The Fishermen .

title: Looker
author: Laura Sims
description: An unraveling woman, unhappily childless and recently separated, becomes fixated on her neighbor—the beautiful, famous actress. The unnamed narrator can't help noticing with wry irony that, though she and the actress live just a few doors apart, they are separated by a chasm of professional success and personal fulfillment. When an interaction with the actress at the annual block party takes a disastrous turn, what began as an innocent preoccupation spirals quickly—and lethally—into madness.

title: The Water Cure
author: Sophie Mackintosh
description: The Handmaid's Tale meets The Virgin Suicides in this dystopian feminist revenge fantasy about three sisters on an isolated island raised to fear men.

title: Sugar Run
author: Mesha Maren
description: In 1989, Jodi McCarty is seventeen years old when she’s sentenced to life in prison. When she’s released eighteen years later, not yet able to return to her lost home in the Appalachian Mountains, she heads south in search of someone she left behind, as a way of finally making amends.

title: Trish Trash: Rollergirl of Mars Omnibus
author: Jessica Abel
description: A collection of all three volumes about Trish "Trash" Nupindju, a girl and settler living under harsh and ruthless conditions on Mars, which she dreams of escaping by becoming a "hoverderby" star.

title: The Au Pair
author: Emma Rous
description: Seraphine Mayes and her twin brother, Danny, were born in the middle of summer at their family's estate on the Norfolk coast. Within hours of their birth, their mother threw herself from the cliffs, the au pair fled, and the village thrilled with whispers of dark cloaks, changelings, and the aloof couple who drew a young nanny into their inner circle.

title: The Widows
author: Jess Montgomery
description: Inspired by the true story of Ohio’s first female sheriff, this is a debut about two women’s search for justice as they take on the corruption at the heart of their community.

title: Mouthful of Birds: Stories
author: Samanta Schweblin, Trans. by Megan McDowell
description: Schweblin's stories have the feel of a sleepless night, where every shadow and bump in the dark take on huge implications, leaving your pulse racing, and the line between the real and the strange blur.

title: Henry VIII: And the Men Who Made Him
author: Tracy Borman
description: From acclaimed historian Tracy Borman, a new portrait of Henry VIII and the men who greatly impacted his life and historic reign.

title: The Perilous Adventures of the Cowboy King: A Novel of Teddy Roosevelt and His Times
author: Jerome Charyn
description: Jerome Charyn re-creates the voice of Theodore Roosevelt, the New York City police commissioner, Rough Rider, and soon-to-be twenty-sixth president through his derring-do adventures.

title: The Last Whalers: Three Years in the Far Pacific with a Courageous Tribe and a Vanishing Way of Life
author: Doug Bock Clark
description: On a volcanic island in the Savu Sea live the Lamalerans: a tribe of 1,500 hunter-gatherers who are the world's last subsistence whalers. They have survived for half a millennium by hunting whales with bamboo harpoons and handmade wooden boats powered by sails of woven palm fronds. But now, under assault from the rapacious forces of the modern era and a global economy, their way of life teeters on the brink of collapse.

title: The Paragon Hotel
author: Lyndsay Faye
description: The new historical thriller by Lyndsay Faye, author of Edgar-nominated Jane Steele and Gods of Gotham , which follows Alice 'Nobody' from Prohibition-era Harlem to Portland's the Paragon Hotel.

title: The New Iberia Blues: A Dave Robicheaux Novel
author: James Lee Burke
description: The shocking death of a young woman leads Detective Dave Robicheaux into the dark corners of Hollywood, the mafia, and the backwoods of Louisiana in this mystery.

title: How to Date Men When You Hate Men
author: Blythe Roberson
description: From New Yorker and Onion writer and comedian Blythe Roberson, How to Date Men When You Hate Men is a comedy philosophy book aimed at interrogating what it means to date men within the trappings of modern society.

title: Act Natural: A Cultural History of Misadventures in Parenting
author: Jennifer Traig
description: From the author of Devil in the Details and Well Enough Alone , a tour through the strange, and often contradictory, history of Western parenting.

title: Wanderer
author: Sarah Léon, Trans. by John Cullen
description: In this ode to Schubert and German Romanticism, a debut French novelist explores the relationship between Hermin, a composer and instructor, and his former pupil, Lenny, a piano prodigy who has returned to Hermin's life after a long time away.

title: All the Wild Hungers: A Season of Cooking and Cancer
author: Karen Babine
description: The award-winning author of Water and What We Know: Following the Roots of a Northern Life returns with a linked essay collection that explores her mother's fight with cancer and the role that cooking and food plays in health—both physical and emotional.

title: Burned: A Story of Murder and the Crime That Wasn't
author: Edward Humes
description: Jo Ann Parks has spent nearly three decades in prison for the murder-by-fire of her three children. But the writer of this book argues that she was unjustly condemned for a crime she didn't commit.

title: The Wicked King
author: Holly Black
publisher: Little, Brown Books for Young Readers
description: The sequel to Black's The Cruel Prince and second in the Folk of the Air series. As seneschal to High King Cardan, Jude must fight to keep control of the Faerie throne while her younger brother, Oak, enjoys the childhood she never knew.

title: The Sopranos Sessions
author: Matt Zoller Seitz
description: To celebrate the 20th anniversary of The Sopranos debut, Sepinwall and Seitz have reunited to produce a collection of recaps, conversations, and critical essays covering every episode.

title: Fault Lines: A History of the United States Since 1974
author: Kevin M Kruse
description: Two award-winning historians explore the origins of a divided America.

title: Receptor
author: Alan Glynn
description: More than 60 years after a man dies under suspicious circumstances, his grandson tries to uncover the truth about his life and death.

title: Queen Victoria: Twenty-Four Days That Changed Her Life
author: Lucy Worsley
description: The chief curator of England's Historic Royal Palaces offers a look at key moments in the life of one of Great Britain's most iconic monarchs, one who defined an era of social conservatism in the 19th century.

title: It Was All a Dream: A New Generation Confronts the Broken Promise to Black America
author: Reniqua Allen
description: Young Black Americans have been trying to realize the promise of the American Dream for centuries and coping with the reality of its limitations for just as long. Now, a new generation is pursuing success, happiness, and freedom -- on their own terms.

title: The Winter of the Witch
author: Katherine Arden
description: Following their adventures in The Bear and the Nightingale and The Girl in the Tower , Vasya and Morozko return in the conclusion to the Winternight Trilogy, battling enemies mortal and magical to save both Russias, the seen and the unseen.

title: Scrublands
author: Chris Hammer
description: In the vein of The Dry and Before the Fall , a town’s dark secrets come to light in the aftermath of a young priest’s unthinkable last act in this arresting and searing debut thriller.

title: The Red Address Book
author: Sofia Lundberg
description: A 96-year-old woman named Doris lives alone in her Stockholm apartment, where she looks forward to weekly calls from her American grandniece Jenny and reminisces about her colorful past—an impoverished childhood transformed by a series of accidents that take her to Paris to model during the 1930s and to Manhattan during the Second World War.

title: The First Conspiracy: The Secret Plot to Kill George Washington
author: Brad Meltzer and Josh Mensch
description: A thriller writer and TV documentary producer team up to unravel the little-known Hickey Plot of 1776, in which the governor and mayor of New York launched a deadly plot against the most important member of the military: George Washington himself.

title: She Lies in Wait
author: Gytha Lodge
description: A teen girl is missing after a night of partying; thirty years later, the discovery of her body reopens a cold case in a novel featuring a small-town cop determined to finally get to the truth—for fans of Tana French and Kate Atkinson.

title: The Truths We Hold: An American Journey
author: Kamala Harris
description: A politcal memoir from the current U.S. Senator from California and former California Attorney General.

title: The Misinformation Age: How False Beliefs Spread
author: Cailin O'Connor and James Owen Weatherall
description: Two philosophers of science argue that social factors, rather than individual psychology, are what’s essential to understanding the spread and persistence of false beliefs—a phenomenon that has irked truth seekers for centuries.

title: Lake City
author: Thomas Kohnstamm
description: From the author of the memoir Do Travel Writers Go to Hell? , this debut novel follows 27-year-old Lane after his marriage to a rich Manhattanite goes bust and he moves back to his parents' depressed neighborhood on the outskirts of Seattle, where he participates in a depraved scheme to make enough money to return to New York.

title: The Longest Line on the Map: The United States, the Pan-American Highway, and the Quest to Link the Americas
author: Eric Rutkow
description: From the award-winning author of American Canopy , an account of the world’s longest road, the Pan-American Highway, and the epic quest to link North and South America, a story of commerce, technology, politics, and the divergent fates of the Americas in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

title: The Edge of Anarchy: The Railroad Barons, the Gilded Age, and the Greatest Labor Uprising in America
author: Jack Kelly
description: The story of the explosive 1894 clash of industry, labor, and government that shook the nation and marked a turning point for America.

title: The Burglar
author: Thomas Perry
description: From the bestselling author of the Jane Whitefield series, this new thriller's titular thief is a small young woman in her 20s who must contend with a string of murders she discovers while on the prowl.

title: Trailblazer: A Pioneering Journalist's Fight to Make the Media Look More Like America
author: Dorothy Butler Gilliam
description: Dorothy Butler Gilliam, whose 50-year-career as a journalist put her in the forefront of the fight for social justice, offers a comprehensive view of racial relations and the media in the U.S. in her new memoir.

title: Welfare
author: Steve Anwyll
description: In this debut novel, a high school boy leaves his unloving father's home to squat on couches of friends while smoking, drinking, and avoiding all responsibility—until freedom appears.

title: Her One Mistake
author: Heidi Perks
description: What should have been a fun-filled, carefree day takes a tragic turn for the worse for one mother when her best friend’s child goes missing in this suspenseful and darkly twisted psychological thriller.

title: Freefall
author: Jessica Barry
description: Told from the perspectives of a mother and daughter separated by distance but united by an unbreakable bond. A debut novel about two tenacious women overcoming unimaginable obstacles to protect themselves and those they love.

title: Thick: And Other Essays
author: Tressie McMillan Cottom
description: A finalist for the 2019 National Book Award, these eight piercing explorations on beauty, media, money, and more, Tressie McMillan Cottom—award-winning professor and acclaimed author of Lower Ed—writes about all that is right and much that is wrong with this thing we call society.

title: Invasive species
author: Marwa Helal
description: In Invasive species , Marwa Helal’s politically charged poems touch on our collective humanity. This work centers on urgent themes in our cultural landscape, focusing on the victims of discriminatory foreign (read: immigration) policy: migrants, refugees―the displaced.

title: Mothers Over Nangarhar
author: Pamela Hart
description: Winner of the Kathryn A. Morton Prize from Sarabande Books, this debut collection considers war from the lens of the psychological battles suffered by parents, lovers, and friends on the home front.

title: Untouchable
author: Jayne Ann Krentz
description: In this third installment of the Cutler, Sutter, and Salinas romantic thriller series, a meditation instructor named Winter Meadows begins dating her client, FBI consultant Jack Lancaster, whose involvement with a cold case creates mayhem in their relationship.

title: Breaking and Entering: The Extraordinary Story of a Hacker Called "Alien"
author: Jeremy N. Smith
description: The true story of the brilliant, breakneck career of an extraordinary hacker—a woman known as Alien.

title: The Only Woman in the Room
author: Marie Benedict
description: She possessed a stunning beauty. She also possessed a stunning mind. Could the world handle both?

title: Ganges: The Many Pasts of an Indian River
author: Sudipta Sen
description: An interdisciplinary history of the world's third-largest river, a potent symbol across South Asia and the Hindu diaspora.

title: Fiber: The Coming Tech Revolution--And Why America Might Miss It
author: Susan Crawford
description: A vision of the next information revolution centered on a fiber-optic infrastructure.

title: Invisible
author: Andrew Grant
description: An Army veteran and intelligence agent goes undercover as a janitor at a federal courthouse to pursue his own brand of justice in a thriller that’s part John Grisham, part Robert Crais.

title: Showtime at the Apollo: The Epic Tale of Harlem's Legendary Theater
author: Ted Fox and James Otis Smith
description: The author of Showtime at the Apollo: The Story of Harlem’s World Famous Theater teams up with a comics artist to put a visual spin on the history of Manhattan's iconic theater, which since 1934 has nurtured many of the nation's most celebrated African American performance artists.

title: The Coming Storm: A Thriller
author: Mark Alpert
description: America is on the brink of collapse, devastated by a brutal government trying to silence its citizens.

title: Lives Laid Away
author: Stephen Mack Jones
description: Detroit ex-cop August Snow takes up vigilante justice when his beloved neighborhood of Mexicantown is caught in the crosshairs of a human trafficking scheme.

title: Twilight of the Elites: Prosperity, the Periphery, and the Future of France
author: Christophe Guilluy, Trans. by Malcolm DeBevoise
description: A passionate account of how the gulf between France's metropolitan elites and its working classes are tearing the country apart.

title: An Indefinite Sentence: A Personal History of Outlawed Love and Sex
author: Siddharth Dube
description: An Indian public health scholar describes the difficult experience of growing up gay in India, coming of age during the AIDS crisis, and his journey to the United States to study at the intersection of healthcare, sexuality, gender expression, and human rights.

title: A Bright Future: How Some Countries Have Solved Climate Change and the Rest Can Follow
author: Joshua S Goldstein
description: The first book to offer a proven, fast, inexpensive, practical way to cut greenhouse gas emissions and prevent catastrophic climate change.

title: First, Kill the Lawyers: A Holland Taylor Mystery
author: David Housewright

title: The Martin Chronicles
author: John Fried
description: The Martin Chronicles follows Martin Kelso as he grows up in 1980s New York and faces the magic of first experiences, as well as the heartbreak of hard-won life lessons.

title: Tell Your Children: The Truth about Marijuana, Mental Illness, and Violence
author: Alex Berenson
description: An exploration of the link between teenage marijuana use and mental illness, and a hidden epidemic of violence caused by the drug—facts that the author believes have been ignored as the U.S. rushes to legalize cannabis.

title: Too Close
author: Natalie Daniels
description: Constance Mortenson, a successful writer and happy wife and mother, meets and befriends Vanessa Jones, who has moved into her London neighborhood. Connie and Ness become fast friends and nearly inseparable, until things go horribly wrong between them. Flash forward six years. A bruised, burned, and unrecognizable Connie, who has been diagnosed with dissociative amnesia, is awaiting trial for heinous crimes that she seemingly doesn’t know she’s committed. Emma Robinson, a forensic psychiatrist, must gain Connie’s trust to determine whether the amnesia is feigned or real.

title: The One You Fight for
author: Roni Loren
description: The third novel in the Ones Who Got Away series. Taryn Landry was there that awful night 14 years ago when she lost her younger sister. Since then, psychology professor Taryn has dedicated her life's work to preventing something like that from ever happening again. Falling in love was never part of the plan.

title: The Last of the Stanfields
author: Marc Levy, Trans. by Daniel Wasserman
description: A popular French novelist narrates the strange tale of London journalist Eleanor-Rigby Donovan, who receives an anonymous letter alluding to a crime committed by her deceased mother. It points her to a bar on the Baltimore Harbor, where she meets a stranger who has received the same mysterious letter about his own mother, and the two embark on a quest through the shadowy past of the Stanfield family.

title: A Rope from the Sky: The Making and Unmaking of the World's Newest State
author: Zach Vertin
description: A senior adviser to the U.S. Special Envoy to Sudan and Sudan South offers a window into the process to negotiate the independence of South Sudan and the unraveling of peace in the new nation, shattering the promise of liberation and exposing the hubris of American backers of the freedom fighters there.

title: In My Mind's Eye: A Thought Diary
author: Jan Morris
description: In her first-ever diary collection, Jan Morris riffs on cats and Brexit, the Royals and the annoyances of aging.

title: How to Hold a Grudge: From Resentment to Contentment--The Power of Grudges to Transform Your Life
author: Sophie Hannah
description: The first and only comprehensive examination of the universal but widely misunderstood practice of grudge-holding that will show you how to use grudges to be your happiest, most optimistic, and most forgiving self.

title: Soviet Milk
author: Nora Ikstena, Trans. by Margita Gailitis
description: An act of resistance in Soviet-occupied Latvia leads to a form of banishment for a doctor and her daughter, who are sent to live to a remote area where they struggle to keep up their spirits in the face of an oppressive regime.

title: The Gown: A Novel of the Royal Wedding
author: Jennifer Robson
description: Jennifer Robson takes us inside the workrooms where one of the most famous wedding gowns in history was created.

title: The Boy
author: Tami Hoag
description: An unfathomable loss or an unthinkable crime? #1 New York Times bestselling author Tami Hoag keeps you guessing.

title: A Delicate Touch
author: Stuart Woods
description: Stone Barrington uncovers a societal minefield in the new adventure from #1 New York Times -bestselling author Stuart Woods.

title: The New Childhood: Raising Kids to Thrive in a Connected World
author: Jordan Shapiro
description: A provocative look at the new, digital landscape of childhood and how to navigate it.

title: On the Same Page
author: N D Galland
description: From the critically acclaimed author of Stepdog and The Fool’s Tale comes a romantic comedy that tells the story of one journalist secretly juggling two bylines for competing newspapers on a small island.

title: The Inflamed Mind: A Radical New Approach to Depression
author: Edward Bullmore
description: Goes far beyond the clinic and the lab, representing a whole new way of looking at how mind, brain, and body all work together in a sometimes misguided effort to help us survive in a hostile world. It offers insights into how we could start getting to grips with depression and other mental disorders much more effectively in the future.

title: Watching You
author: Lisa Jewell
description: Melville Heights is one of the nicest neighborhoods in Bristol, England; home to doctors and lawyers and old-money academics. It’s not the sort of place where people are brutally murdered in their own kitchens. But it is the sort of place where everyone has a secret. And everyone is watching you.

title: Turned on: Science, Sex and Robots
author: Kate Devlin
description: Sex robots are here, and here to stay--and more are coming. This book explores how the emerging and future development of sexual companion robots might affect us, and our society.

title: The Barefoot Woman
author: Scholastique Mukasonga, Trans. by Jordan Stump
description: In this finalist for the 2019 National Book Award, a survivor of the Rwandan genocide pays tribute to her mother, narrating the story of her life with the fierce and loving Tutsi woman who did everything to protect her children from the violence encroaching upon them in pre-genocide Rwanda.

title: Liars' Paradox
author: Taylor Stevens
description: New York Times bestselling author Taylor Stevens introduces a pair of wild cards into the global spy game—a brother and sister who were raised to deceive—and trained to kill.

title: Collected Poems
author: Robert Bly
description: Gathering more than sixty years of poetry, Collected Poems showcases the career of 'a great American transcendentalist' ( New York Times ).

title: Influenza: The Hundred Year Hunt to Cure the Deadliest Disease in History
author: Jeremy Brown
description: A veteran emergency room doctor explores the troubling, terrifying, and complex history of the flu virus, from the origins of the 1918 Great Flu that killed millions to vexing questions about whether we are prepared for the next epidemic.

title: Making Music American: 1917 and the Transformation of Culture
author: E. Douglas Bomberger
description: The year 1917 was unlike any other in American history, or in the history of American music. The United States entered World War I, jazz burst onto the national scene, and the German musicians who dominated classical music were forced from the stage.

title: Hunting Annabelle
author: Wendy Heard
description: In this debut thriller set in Austin in the 1980s, a former killer named Sean Suh has vowed to put his violent past behind him. But when Annabelle goes missing, Sean becomes a suspect and sets out to find her and clear his name.

title: Suitcase Charlie
author: John Guzlowski
description: Chicago, May 30, 1956: On a quiet corner in a working-class immigrant neighborhood, a heavy suitcase is discovered on the sidewalk late at night. Inside is the body of a young boy, naked and hacked into pieces.

title: Soldier, Priest, and God: A Life of Alexander the Great
author: F S Naiden
description: Whatever we may think of Alexander--whether Great or only lucky, a civilizer or a sociopath--most people do not regard him as a religious leader. And yet religion permeated all aspects of his career. When he used religion astutely, he and his army prospered.

title: Daniel Morgan: A Revolutionary Life
author: Albert Louis Zambone
description: A new biography of a man of humble origins who became one of the great military leaders of the American Revolution.

title: Milkman
author: Anna Burns
description: Winner of the 2018 Man Booker Prize and the 2019 National Book Critics Circle Award for Fiction, Milkman is about an unnamed girl in an unnamed town. When a local paramilitary known as "the milkman" begins pursuing her, she suddenly becomes “interesting,” the last thing she ever wanted to be.

title: The Day the Sun Died
author: Yan Lianke, Trans. by Carlos Rojas
description: In this winner of the Dream of the Red Chamber Award, one of the most prestigious honors for Chinese-language novels, hundreds of inhabitants of a town begin dream-walking, a state that causes them to act out the desires they’ve suppressed during waking hours. Before long, the community devolves into chaos, and it’s up to Li Niannian and his parents to save the town before sunrise.

title: This Is Cuba: An American Journalist Under Castro's Shadow
author: David Ariosto
description: Fidel Castro is dead. Donald Trump was elected president. And to most outsiders, the fate of Cuba has never seemed more uncertain. Yet those who look close enough may recognize that signs of the next revolution are etched in plain view.

title: A Matter of Taste: A Farmers' Market Devotee's Semi-Reluctant Argument for Inviting Scientific Innovation to the Dinner Table
author: Rebecca Tucker
description: A Toronto-based writer, editor, and journalist offers a critique of the farmer's markets and organic produce that have become synonymous with "good food"—to the problematic exclusion of other kinds of food movements.

title: In Our Mad and Furious City
author: Guy Gunaratne
description: Inspired by the real-life murder of a British army soldier by religious fanatics, Guy Gunaratne’s Man Booker-long-listed debut offers a snapshot of the diverse, frenzied edges of modern-day London.

title: For Better and Worse (Original)
author: Margot Hunt
description: On their first date back in law school, Natalie and Will Clarke bonded over drinks, dinner and whether they could get away with murder. Now married, they’ll put the latter to the test when an unchecked danger in their community places their son in jeopardy. Working as a criminal defense attorney, Nat refuses to rely on the broken legal system to keep her family safe. She knows that if you want justice, you have to get it yourself.

title: A Bad Deal for the Whole Galaxy
author: Alex White
description: The greatest dangers hide the brightest treasures in this bold, planet-hopping science fiction adventure series.

title: Unruly Waters: How Rains, Rivers, Coasts, and Seas Have Shaped Asia's History
author: Sunil Amrith
description: A Harvard history professor and MacArthur Fellow reimagines Asia's history through the stories of its rains, rivers, coasts, and seas—and of the weather-watchers and engineers, mapmakers and farmers who have sought to control them.

title: Fascination: Memoirs
author: Kevin Killian
description: From one of the founders of the New Narrative movement in San Francisco, this three-part memoir explores gay life in 1970s Long Island.

title: The Enemy of My Enemy
author: W.E.B. Griffin and William E. Butterworth IV
description: Special agent James Cronley Jr. finds that fighting both ex-Nazis and the Soviet NKGB can lead to strange bedfellows, in the dramatic new Clandestine Operations novel about the birth of the CIA and the Cold War.

title: The Meaning of Life: The Case for Abolishing Life Sentences
author: Marc Mauer and Ashley Nellis
description: The executive director and policy analyst of The Sentencing Project, which advocates for criminal justice reform, make an argument for eliminating life sentences, profiling six people directly affected by life sentences.

title: Broken Ground
author: Val McDermid
description: The accidental discovery of a body is the starting point for the latest mystery featuring the Scottish cold-case detective Karen Pirie.

title: North of Dawn
author: Nuruddin Farah
description: A couple's tranquil life abroad is irrevocably transformed by the arrival of their son's widow and children, in the latest from Somalia's most celebrated novelist.

title: All That Heaven Allows: A Biography of Rock Hudson
author: Mark Griffin
description: The definitive biography of the deeply complex and widely misunderstood matinee idol of Hollywood’s Golden Age.

title: Seasonal Associate
author: Heike Geissler, Trans. by Katy Derbyshire
description: A writer's account of her experience working in an Amazon fulfillment center and how the robotic monotony of the job is transformed into exhaustion, shame, and self-doubt.

title: The Storm
author: Tomas Gonzalez Trans. by Andrea Rosenberg
description: Twins Mario and Jose do not know how to cope with the hatred they feel for their father, an arrogant man whose pride seems to taint everything he touches. Over the course of a fateful fishing trip straight into the heart of a storm, father and sons are confronted with the unspoken secrets and resentments that are destroying them.

title: Once Upon a River
author: Diane Setterfield
description: From the instant #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Thirteenth Tale comes a new novel about how we explain the world to ourselves, ourselves to others, and the meaning of our lives in a universe that remains impenetrably mysterious.

title: Dear Los Angeles: The City in Diaries and Letters, 1542 to 2018
author: David Kipen
description: A mosaic of diary entries and letters from Marilyn Monroe, Cesar Chavez, Susan Sontag, Albert Einstein, and many more, this is the story of Los Angeles as told by locals, transplants, and some just passing through.

title: Radiant Shimmering Light
author: Sarah Selecky
description: Lilian Quick is 40, single, and childless, working as a pet portrait artist. She paints the colored light only she can see, but animal aura portraits are a niche market at best. She's working hard to build her brand on social media and struggling to pay the rent. This satire asks us: How do we recognize authenticity when storytelling and magic have been co-opted by marketing?

title: Kitchen Yarns: Notes on Life, Love, and Food
author: Ann Hood
description: The bestselling author looks back on her life, loves, and losses through the lens of food, with each chapter offering a recipe and a story to go with it.

title: The Dakota Winters
author: Tom Barbash
description: A novel about the Winters, a family living in New York City’s famed Dakota apartment building in the year leading up to John Lennon’s assassination.

title: Revolution Sunday
author: Wendy Guerra Trans. by Achy Obejas
description: A novel about glamour, surveillance, and corruption in contemporary Cuba, from an internationally bestselling author, translated into English for the first time.

title: Victory City: A History of New York and New Yorkers During World War II
author: John Strausbaugh
description: From John Strausbaugh, author of City of Sedition and The Village , comes the definitive history of Gotham during the World War II era.

title: The Future of Capitalism: Facing the New Anxieties
author: Paul Collier
description: From world-renowned economist Paul Collier, a candid diagnosis of the failures of capitalism and a pragmatic and realistic vision for how we can repair it.

title: Babel: Around the World in Twenty Languages
author: Gaston Dorren
description: A whistle-stop tour of the world's twenty most-spoken languages, exploring history, geography, linguistics, and culture—showing how the language we speak reflects our view of the world.

title: The Last True Cowboy
author: Laura Drake
description: This cowboy's got one last chance to prove himself.

title: My Favorite Half-Night Stand
author: Christina Lauren
description: By a New York Times bestselling author, My Favorite Half-Night Stand is a romp through online dating and its many, many fails.

title: Parallel Lives
author: Olivier Schrauwen
description: The revered Belgian comics artist imagines future lives for himself and his offspring that involve alien abduction, dialogue with future agents, and coded messages in envelopes at breakfast.

title: Bryant & May: Hall of Mirrors
author: Christopher Fowler
description: The year is 1969, and 10 guests are about to enjoy a weekend at Tavistock Hall. The guests also include detectives Arthur Bryant and John May - undercover, in disguise and tasked with protecting Monty Hatton-Jones, a whistle-blower turning Queen's evidence in a massive bribery trial.

title: At the End of the Century: The Stories of Ruth Prawer Jhabvala
author: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala
description: Collected short stories from the Booker Prize–winning author, with an introduction by Anita Desai.

title: The Mansion
author: Ezekiel Boone
description: In this thriller from Ezekiel Boone, author of The Hatching series, a family moves into a home equipped with the world's most intelligent, most cutting-edge, and most intuitive computer ever--with terrifying and catastrophic results.

title: Ike's Mystery Man: The Secret Lives of Robert Cutler
author: Peter Shinkle
description: The Cold War, The Lavender Scare and the Untold Story of Eisenhower's First National Security Advisor.

title: The Collected Poems of Bertolt Brecht
author: Bertolt Brecht
description: Widely celebrated as the greatest German playwright of the twentieth century, The Collected Poems of Bertolt Brecht is the most extensive English translation of Brecht’s poetry to date.

title: The Three Secret Cities
author: Matthew Reilly
description: In the latest novel featuring Jack West, Jr., dark forces are targeting Jack after he won the Great Games and threw the four legendary kingdoms into turmoil. With the end of the world fast approaching, Jack must find the titular three lost cities of legend if he wants to avoid catastrophe.

title: Deep War: The War with China—The Nuclear Precipice
author: David Poyer
description: In the latest installment of this military thriller featuring Navy commander Dan Lenson, war against China turns dire as the United States struggles to survive.

title: For the Sake of the Game: Stories Inspired by the Sherlock Holmes Canon
author: Ed. by Laurie R. King and Leslie S. Klinger
description: Bestselling editors Laurie R. King and Leslie S. Klinger collect stories here inspired by Arthur Conan Doyle's classic mysteries, written by the world's top writers—Peter S. Beagle, Rhys Bowen, Reed Farrel Coleman, Jamie Freveletti, Alan Gordon, Gregg Hurwitz, Toni L. P. Kelner, William Kotzwinkle and Joe Servello, Harley Jane Kozak, D. P. Lyle, Weston Ochse, Zoe Sharp, Duane Swierczynski, and F. Paul Wilson.

title: The Annotated Memoirs of Ulysses S. Grant
author: Ulysses S Grant
description: One hundred and thirty-three years after its 1885 publication by Mark Twain, Elizabeth Samet has annotated Grant’s landmark memoir and expands the Civil War backdrop against which this monumental American life is typically read.

title: Handel in London: The Making of a Genius
author: Jane Glover
description: An artistic director of The London Mozart Players explores the early 18th century arrival of the German composer George Freidrich Handel to London and his ensuing four decades in that city, where he crafted many orchestral masterpieces while engaging in the city's social and civic life.

title: Into the Night
author: Sarah Bailey
description: After the shocking murder of a high-profile celebrity, Gemma Woodstock must pull back the layers of a gilded cage to discover who among the victim's friends and family can be trusted--and who may be the killer.

title: The Great War in America: World War I and Its Aftermath
author: Garrett Peck
description: A chronicle of the American experience during World War I and the unexpected changes that rocked the country in its immediate aftermath--the Red Scare, race riots, women's suffrage, and Prohibition.

title: Never Grow Up
author: Jackie Chan with Zhu Mo
description: The beloved martial artist and stuntman of films such as Rush Hour reflects on his rags-to-riches life story, from childhood poverty in Hong Kong to a decade enrolled in the harsh China Drama Academy to his rise to stardom in Hong Kong and Hollywood cinema.

title: The Point of It All: A Lifetime of Great Loves and Endeavors
author: Charles Krauthammer
description: This posthumous volume collects columns and essays by the revered conservative commentator on subjects ranging from fatherhood to the Cold War to the decline of liberal democracy.

title: Violence: Humans in Dark Times
author: Ed. by Brad Evans and Natasha Lennard
description: This volume collects conversations originally published in The New York Times and Los Angeles Review of Books between the editors and leading intellectuals—including Oliver Stone, Gayatri Spivak, and Elaine Scarry—to explore the problem of violence in politics, culture, media, language, memory, and the environment.

title: Hong Kong Noir
author: Jason Y. Ng and Susan Blumberg-Kason
description: The history of Hong Kong, once a fishing village, encompasses piracy, the opium trade, prostitution, corruption, espionage and revolutionary plots; grist for the 14 dark tales in Hong Kong Noir .

title: Bleak Harbor
author: Bryan Gruley
description: The kidnapping of Danny Peters—the youngest member of the family that founded Bleak Harbor five generations ago, who is autistic—sets off a desperate search that has his parents worried their own secret dealings may have played a role their son's disappearance.

title: The Warner Boys: Our Family's Story of Autism and Hope
author: Curt Warner
description: A memoir of one family’s life in seclusion—and the love, strength, and faith it took to save it.

title: Winter Loon
author: Susan Bernhard
description: A debut novel about family and sacrifice, Winter Loon reminds us of how great a burden the past can be, the toll it exacts, and the freedom that comes from letting it go.

title: Long Road to Mercy
author: David Baldacci
description: Atlee Pine, an FBI agent with special skills assigned to the remote wilds of the southwestern United States who must confront a new threat . . . and an old nightmare.

title: Hazards of Time Travel
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: From the National Book Award-winning author, a novel about a defiant young woman in near-future dystopian America who is sentenced to hard time in the 1950s Midwest.

title: Kingdom of the Blind: A Chief Inspector Gamache Novel
author: Louise Penny
description: The new Chief Inspector Gamache novel from the #1 New York Times bestselling author.

title: The Adults
author: Caroline Hulse
description: A couple (now separated), plus their daughter, plus their new partners, all on an epic Christmas vacation. What could go wrong?

title: Come with Me
author: Helen Schulman
description: Amy Reed works part-time as a PR person for a tech start-up, run by her college roommate’s nineteen-year-old son, in Palo Alto, California. Donny wants Amy to be his guinea pig. And even as she questions Donny’s theories and motives, Amy finds herself unable to resist the lure of the road(s) not taken. Who would she be if she had made different choices, loved different people? Where would she be now?

title: Tell Them of Battles, Kings, and Elephants
author: Mathias Enard, Trans. by Charlotte Mandell
description: This imagined account of Michelangelo's 1506 journey to Constantinople to design a bridge over the Golden Horn is constructed from real historical fragments, meditating on why stories are told, why bridges are built, and how seemingly unmatched pieces, seen from the opposite sides of civilization, can mirror one another.

title: Tom Clancy Oath of Office
author: Marc Cameron
description: Marine officer. CIA analyst. President. Jack Ryan has devoted his life to protecting the United States. What if this time, he can't? President Ryan and the Campus return in the latest entry in Tom Clancy's #1 New York Times -bestselling series.

title: Robert B. Parker's Blood Feud
author: Mike Lupica
description: Robert B. Parker's iconic PI Sunny Randall is back, and the stakes are higher than ever as she races to protect her ex-husband—and his Mafia family—from the vengeful plan of a mysterious rival.

title: The Houseguest: And Other Stories
author: Amparo Dávila Trans. by Audrey Harris and Matthew Gleeson
description: The first collection in English from Amparo Dávila, who follows her characters to the limits of desire, paranoia, insomnia, and fear.

title: The Museum of Modern Love
author: Heather Rose
description: Based on a real piece of performance art that took place in 2010, the installation that the fictional Arky Levin discovers is inexplicably powerful. Visitors to the Museum of Modern Art sit across a table from the performance artist Marina Abramovic, for as short or long a period of time as they choose. As the performance unfolds over the course of 75 days, so too does Arky. As he bonds with other people drawn to the exhibit, he slowly starts to understand what might be missing in his life and what he must do.

title: Iron Curtain Journals: January-May 1965
author: Allen Ginsberg
description: A travel guide through one of the best minds of the Beat Generation—distinctly not destroyed by madness—Allen Ginsberg’s journals are more tour de force than simple diaries, charting his poetry, political antics, and high-profile encounters behind the Iron Curtain at the height of the Cold War.

title: The Frolic of the Beasts
author: Yukio Mishima Trans. by Andrew Clare
description: Translated into English for the first time, a short novel about an affair gone wrong, from the acclaimed Japanese author, Yukio Mishima.

title: Seapower States: Maritime Culture, Continental Empires and the Conflict That Made the Modern World
author: Andrew Lambert
description: Andrew Lambert investigates the extraordinary success of five small maritime states.

title: Breaking News: The Remaking of Journalism and Why It Matters Now
author: Alan Rusbridger
description: An account of the revolution that has upended the news business, written by one of the former Editor of The Guardian .

title: Where We Go from Here: Two Years in the Resistance
author: Bernie Sanders
description: The Democratic presidential candidate, senator, and economist traces the first year of the Trump administration and what he and his colleagues are doing to reinforce the progressive movement.

title: Someone to Trust
author: Mary Balogh
description: During a rare white Christmas at Brambledean Court, the widow Elizabeth, Lady Overfield, defies convention by falling in love with a younger man in this fifth installment of New York Times -bestselling author Balogh's Westcott series.

title: Bring It on Home: Peter Grant, Led Zeppelin, and Beyond--The Story of Rock's Greatest Manager
author: Mark Blake
description: The authorized biography of the most notorious rock manager of all time, Peter Grant, best known for his work with Led Zeppelin.

title: In Search of the Canary Tree
author: Lauren E. Oakes
description: Field research into why yellow-cedar trees are dying and how people dependent on it are coping with a changing environment.

title: What Would Mrs. Astor Do?: The Essential Guide to the Manners and Mores of the Gilded Age
author: Cecelia Tichi
description: An illustrated romp with America’s Gilded Age leisure class—and those angling to join it.

title: The Kremlin Letters: Stalin's Wartime Correspondence with Churchill and Roosevelt
author: David Reynolds
description: The fruit of a unique British-Russian scholarly collaboration, this volume collects a majority of the messages Joseph Stalin exchanged with Allied leaders Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt during the Second World War. Ranging from intimate personal greetings to weighty salvos about diplomacy and strategy, this book reveals the political machinations and human stories behind the Allied triumvirate.

title: Gods and Robots: Myths, Machines, and Ancient Dreams of Technology
author: Adrienne Mayor
description: The untold story of how the ancients imagined robots and other forms of artificial life―and even invented real automated machines.

title: What We Talk about When We Talk about Rape
author: Sohaila Abdulali
description: In the tradition of Rebecca Solnit, an examination of sexual assault and the global discourse on rape told through the perspective of a survivor, writer, counselor, and activist.

title: Being John Lennon: A Restless Life
author: Ray Connolly
description: From the author of Being Elvis , who was an acquaintance of Lennon, this biography offers a look at the phases in the life of one of the world's most iconic rock musicians.

title: Insane Mode: How Elon Musk's Tesla Sparked an Electric Revolution to End the Age of Oil
author: Hamish McKenzie
description: A former Tesla communications employee narrates the story of Tesla, arguing that Elon Musk's 'insane mode' leadership has been the key to the company's success, heralding the end to the era of gasoline-powered transportation.

title: The Jewish American Paradox: Embracing Choice in a Changing World
author: Robert H. Mnookin
description: A Harvard law professor argues for a more inclusive American-Jewish community that embraces diversity and debate.

title: My Sister, the Serial Killer
author: Oyinkan Braithwaite
description: A darkly satirical novel about a Nigerian woman whose younger sister has a very inconvenient habit of killing her boyfriends.

title: The Long Take: A Noir Narrative
author: Robin Robertson
description: Shortlisted for the 2018 Man Booker Prize, a poet's noir narrative that tells the story of a D-Day veteran in postwar America.

title: Hardly Children
author: Laura Adamczyk
description: Children learn to navigate a treacherous world—and childish adults help create that treachery—in these stories from first-time author Adamczyk.

title: All the Lives We Never Lived
author: Anuradha Roy
description: The 2015 Man Booker nominee returns with a story about an Indian horticulturist looking back on his abandonment by his mother as India’s fight for independence merged into World War II.

title: The Silent Ones: A Father Anselm Thriller
author: William Brodrick
description: Father Anselm faces the most difficult and troubling case of his life in this newest addition to this contemporary series.

title: Little Dancer Aged Fourteen: The True Story Behind Degas's Masterpiece
author: Camille Laurens
description: Little Dancer Aged Fourteen uncovers the story of the real dancer behind Degas’s now-iconic sculpture, and the struggles of late 19th century Parisian life.

title: Why We Dream: The Transformative Power of Our Nightly Journey
author: Alice Robb
description: Science journalist and lucid dreamer Alice Robb explores revelatory research to uncover why we dream and how we can improve our dream life.

title: Smash!: Green Day, the Offspring, Bad Religion, Nofx, and the '90s Punk Explosion
author: Ian Winwood
description: A group biography of '90s punk rock told through the prism of Green Day, The Offspring, NOFX, Rancid, Bad Religion, Social Distortion, and more.

title: Hungover: The Morning After and One Man's Quest for the Cure
author: Shaughnessy Bishop-Stall
description: One intrepid reporter's quest to learn everything there is to know about hangovers, trying all of the cures he can find and explaining how (and if) they work, all so rest of us don't have to.

title: Newcomer
author: Keigo Higashino, Trans. by Giles Murray
description: Demoted back to local policing from the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department’s Homicide Division, Kyochiro Kaga makes a deep impression on the quiet Nihonbashi Precinct.

title: Why Women Have Better Sex Under Socialism
author: Kristen R. Ghodsee
description: From paid maternity leave to employment assurances, an argument for the benefits of socialism for women.

title: Tony's Wife
author: Adriana Trigiani
description: Set in the Big Band era of the 1940s and World War II, this is the story of two talented working class kids who marry and become a successful singing act, until time, temptation, and the responsibilities of home and family derail their dreams.

title: No One at the Wheel: Driverless Cars and the Road of the Future
author: Samuel I Schwartz
description: New York City's former traffic commissioner describes how driverless vehicle technology will transform highways, cities, workplaces, and laws in the United States and across the globe.

title: Barking with the Big Dogs: On Writing and Reading Books for Children
author: Natalie Babbitt
description: A collection of essays and speeches by the author of Tuck Everlasting , Natalie Babbitt.

title: Dreaming in Turtle: A Journey Through the Passion, Profit, and Peril of Our Most Coveted Prehistoric Creatures
author: Peter Laufer
description: An exploration into the world of turtles across the globe; Laufer charts the lore, love, and peril to a beloved species.

title: Lies Sleeping
author: Ben Aaronovitch
description: The seventh book of the bestselling Rivers of London urban fantasy series returns to the adventures of Peter Grant, detective and apprentice wizard, as he solves magical crimes in the city of London.

title: City of Broken Magic
author: Mirah Bolender
description: Mirah Bolender's adventure fantasy debut, City of Broken Magic , features a bomb squad that defuses magic weapons.

title: Fire & Blood: 300 Years Before a Game of Thrones (a Targaryen History)
author: George R.R. Martin
description: The author of A Song of Ice and Fire , the inspiration for HBO’s Game of Thrones , offers an in-depth "history" of the Targaryen family—and its legendary dragons.

title: I Am Young
author: M. Dean
description: Stories in this book, thematically bound by relationship flux and the impact of culture, Dean experiments beautifully with style and storytelling devices in each piece.

title: Extinctions
author: Josephine Wilson
description: Josephine Wilson’s award-winning novel explores many kinds of extinction―natural, racial, national, and personal―and what we might do to prevent them.

title: Homeward Hound
author: Rita Mae Brown
description: In Brown's latest novel starring 'Sister' Jane Arnold, the revelry of the Christmas hunt is interrupted by the discovery of a dead body, and 'Sister' Jane and her company of loyal hounds work to uncover who has killed a beloved hunting club faithful.

title: So Many Doors
author: Oakley Hall
description: From Pulitzer Prize finalist Oakley Hall, So Many Doors is about the death of a beautiful woman and the farmers driving graders and bulldozers to tame the American West.

title: The Circuit: A Tennis Odyssey
author: Rowan Ricardo Phillips
description: From award-winning poet and sportswriter Phillips, a lyrical, genre-defying account of the 2017 tennis season.

title: Russia Without Putin: Money, Power and the Myths of the New Cold War
author: Tony Wood
description: A member of the editorial board of New Left Review offers an analysis of Russia as a nation much less under the sway of Vladimir Putin than Western media supposes, with the President merely a figurehead for anti-democratic institutions that would continue in the same vein with a different leader.

title: Just Giving: Why Philanthropy Is Failing Democracy and How It Can Do Better
author: Rob Reich
description: A professor and co-director for the Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society at Stanford University considers whether philanthropy—often an exercise in unaccountable power, the conversion of private assets into public influence—represents a threat to democracy.

title: The Mystery of the Exploding Teeth: And Other Curiosities from the History of Medicine
author: Thomas Morris
description: Historian Thomas Morris has assembled a collection of tales from the annals of medicine about mysterious illnesses, horrifying operations, dubious treatments, and other puzzling cases and practices from bygone eras.

title: The Comforts of Home: A Simon Serrailler Mystery
author: Susan Hill
description: Chief Superintendent Simon Serrailler faces his most difficult case yet in the ninth installment of Susan Hill's British crime series.

title: Schadenfreude: The Joy of Another's Misfortune
author: Tiffany Watt Smith
description: A cultural historian and the author of The Book of Human Emotions investigates one of humans' most "ethically ambiguous" emotions, for which English does not have an exact translation and therefore borrows the German.

title: Nothing Is Lost: Selected Essays
author: Ingrid Sischy
description: A collection of three decades' worth of profiles and essays by the late South African-born editor at Artforum and Interview on figures from Nicole Kidman to Jeff Koons.

title: Winter War: Hoover, Roosevelt, and the First Clash Over the New Deal
author: Eric Rauchway
description: The history of the most acrimonious presidential handoff in American history--and of the origins of twentieth-century liberalism and conservatism.

title: How to Love the Universe: A Scientist's Odes to the Hidden Beauty Behind the Visible World
author: Stefan Klein, Trans. by Mike Mitchell
description: In 10 short chapters of lyrical prose, a German physicist uses everyday objects and events as a springboard to meditate on the beauty of the underlying science.

title: Delayed Response: The Art of Waiting from the Ancient to the Instant World
author: Jason Farman
description: A media studies scholar offers an exploration—and celebration—of waiting throughout history, considering its importance for connection, understanding, and intimacy.

title: Love in the New Millennium
author: Can Xue, trans. by Annelise Finegan Wasmoen
description: In this darkly comic novel, a group of women inhabit a world of constant surveillance, where informants lurk in the flower beds and false reports fly. Conspiracies abound in a community that normalizes paranoia and suspicion. Some try to flee—whether to a mysterious gambling bordello or to ancestral homes that can be reached only underground through muddy caves, sewers, and tunnels. Others seek out the refuge of Nest County, where traditional Chinese herbal medicines can reshape or psychologically transport the self.

title: City of Champions: An American Story of Leather Helmets, Iron Wills and the High School Kids from Jersey Who Won It All
author: Hank Gola
description: It was 1939. The Depression loosened its grip on America, yet World War II loomed. Meanwhile, high school football was cresting as one of the country’s most popular pastimes. In an era before big money and television engulfed sports, schoolboys shared newspaper headlines and glory with the pros and college players, and drew crowds in the tens of thousands.

title: America, Compromised
author: Lawrence Lessig
description: The Roy L. Furman Professor of Law and Leadership at Harvard Law School offers a sweeping indictment of contemporary American institutions and the corruption that besets them.

title: The Word Pretty
author: Elisa Gabbert
description: Combining elements of criticism, meditation, and personal essay, this book reveals a poet's attention turned to subjects from translation to aphorism, from unreliable memory to beauty and the male gaze.

title: A Ladder to the Sky
author: John Boyne
description: A psychodrama following one brilliant, ruthless man who will stop at nothing in his pursuit of success.

title: Insomnia
author: Marina Benjamin
description: In this personal narrative—part lyrical memoir and part philosophical inquiry—about a condition that is on the rise, Benjamin treats insomnia as an experience, not a disorder, and traces its influences on the arts and sciences throughout history as well as on her own life.

title: The April 3rd Incident
author: Yu Hua, Trans. by Allan H. Barr
