description: Seven dark, challenging short stories written from 1987-91, in the wake of China’s Cultural Revolution.

title: The End of the End of the Earth
author: Jonathan Franzen
description: A new collection of personal essays from a self-proclaimed 'depressive pessimist' and 'angry, bird-loving misfit.'

title: Blueprint: How DNA Makes Us Who We Are
author: Robert Plomin
description: A top behavioral geneticist makes the case that DNA inherited from our parents at the moment of conception can predict our psychological strengths and weaknesses.

title: Fed Up: Emotional Labor, Women, and the Way Forward
author: Gemma Hartley
description: Gemma Hartley, the journalist who ignited a national conversation on "emotional labor," dives into the unpaid, invisible work women have shouldered for too long—and offers an impassioned vision for creating a better future for us all.

title: The Patch
author: John McPhee
description: An 'album quilt,' an artful assortment of nonfiction writings by The New Yorker staff writer John McPhee that have not previously appeared in any book.

title: God in the Qur'an
author: Jack Miles
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of God: A Biography , an informative portrait of the God of Islam, the world's second largest, fastest-growing, and perhaps most tragically misunderstood religion.

title: Seduction: Sex, Lies, and Stardom in Howard Hughes's Hollywood
author: Karina Longworth
description: In this popular history, the creator of You Must Remember This probes the inner workings of Hollywood’s glamorous golden age through the stories of some of the dozens of actresses pursued by Howard Hughes, to reveal how the millionaire mogul’s obsessions with sex, power and publicity trapped, abused, or benefitted women who dreamt of screen stardom.

title: In the Galway Silence
author: Ken Bruen
description: The latest novel in Ireland's most distinctive crime fiction series, In the Galway Silence , finds former cop Jack Taylor up against a vigilante assassin who goes by the name 'Silence'--and the consequences quickly become personal.

title: Death and Other Holidays
author: Marci Vogel
description: In this winner of the Miami Book Fair de Groot Prize for Best Novella, life is coming fast at 20-something April. All the heavy stuff of adulthood—including the death of a loved one—seems to have happened to her all at once, leaving her reeling, and challenging her wit and grit in ways she never imagined.

title: Witness: Lessons from Elie Wiesel's Classroom
author: Ariel Burger
description: In the vein of Tuesdays with Morrie , a devoted protégé and friend of one of the world's great thinkers takes us into the sacred space of the classroom, showing Holocaust survivor and Nobel Peace Prize recipient Elie Wiesel not only as an extraordinary human being, but as a master teacher.

title: Seventeen
author: Hideo Yokoyama, Trans. by Louise Heal Kawai
description: The author of Six Four narrates a thriller about an investigative journalist in charge of overseeing his newsroom's coverage of a plane crash.

title: New Selected Poems
author: Thom Gunn, Ed. Clive Wilmer
description: Thom Gunn has been described as 'one of the most singular and compelling poets in English during the past half-century' ( Times Literary Supplement ). This New Selected Poems , compiled by his friend Clive Wilmer and accompanied by insightful notes, is the first edition to represent the full arc of Gunn’s inimitable career.

title: Heirs of the Founders: The Epic Rivalry of Henry Clay, John Calhoun and Daniel Webster, the Second Generation of American Giants
author: H.W. Brands
description: From New York Times bestselling historian H. W. Brands comes the story of how, in nineteenth-century America, a new set of political giants battled to complete the unfinished work of the Founding Fathers and decide the future of our democracy.

title: Muck
author: Dror Burstein, Trans. by Gabriel Levin
description: In a modern-dress retelling of the Biblical book of Jeremiah, two young poets in Jerusalem are about to have their lives turned upside down in a story that dramatizes the eternal dispute between poetry and power, between faith and practicality, and between haves and have-nots.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: An intimate memoir from the former First Lady of the United States.

title: Limetown: The Prequel to the #1 Podcast
author: Cote Smith, Zack Akers, Skip Bronkie
description: From the creators of the #1 podcast Limetown, a prequel about a teenager who learns of a mysterious research facility where over three hundred people have disappeared—including her uncle—with clues that become the key to discovering the secrets of this strange town.

title: The British in India: A Social History of the Raj
author: David Gilmour
description: A portrait of the lives of the British in India, from the seventeenth century to Independence.

title: Proof of Collusion: How Trump Betrayed America
author: Seth Abramson
description: For the first time, the full record of how a US president compromised American foreign policy in exchange for financial gain and covert election assistance.

title: A Light of Her Own
author: Carrie Callaghan
description: A vivid portrait of a remarkable artist, A Light of Her Own is a richly-woven story of grit against the backdrop of Rembrandt and an uncompromising religion.

title: Late-Life Love: A Memoir
author: Susan Gubar
description: During a difficult year, acclaimed writer Susan Gubar celebrates her lasting partnership and the reciprocity of lovers in later life.

title: Let's Go (So We Can Get Back): A Memoir of Recording and Discording with Wilco, Etc.
author: Jeff Tweedy
description: The singer, guitarist, and songwriter—best known for his work with Wilco—opens up about his past, his songs, the music, and the people that have inspired him.

title: Vita Nostra
author: Sergey and Marina Dyachenko, Trans. by Julia Meitov Hersey
description: Punishingly intense academic pressure transforms a university student into a transcendent being in this harrowing fantasy novel by a married Ukrainian couple, the first in a trilogy.

title: The Western Wind
author: Samantha Harvey
description: A story of faith, guilt, and the freedom of confession from a novelist who has been nominated for the Man Booker Prize, the Women’s Prize for Fiction, and The Guardian First Book Award.

title: Bringing Down the Colonel: A Sex Scandal of the Gilded Age, and the "powerless" Woman Who Took on Washington
author: Patricia Miller
description: Journalist Patricia Miller tells the story of Madeline Pollard, an unlikely nineteenth-century women’s rights crusader. After an affair with a prominent politician left her 'ruined,' Pollard brought the man―and the hypocrisy of America’s control of women’s sexuality―to trial. And, surprisingly, she won.

title: Madame Victoria
author: Catherine LeRoux
description: In 2001, a woman’s skeleton was found in the woods overlooking Montreal’s Royal Victoria Hospital. Assigned the name Madame Victoria, her remains were placed in a box in an evidence room and, eventually, forgotten. But not by Catherine Leroux, who constructs in her form-bending Madame Victoria twelve different histories for the unknown woman.

title: Creatures of Want and Ruin
author: Molly Tanzer
description: This sequel to Creatures of Will and Temper picks up in 1927 Long Island, where Ellie West fishes by day and sells moonshine by night to the citizens of her home town. But after Ellie's father joins a church whose parishioners possess supernatural powers and a violent hatred for immigrants, Ellie finds she doesn't know her beloved island, or her father, as well as she thought.

title: American Overdose: The Opioid Tragedy in Three Acts
author: Chris McGreal
description: A portrait of a uniquely American epidemic—its devastating consequences and conclusions.

title: The Breakthrough: Immunotherapy and the Race to Cure Cancer
author: Charles Graeber
description: From the New York Times bestselling author of The Good Nurse , The Breakthrough draws on the experiences of patients, physicians, and researchers to explain the revolutionary development of immunotherapy as a treatment for cancer and how that information is being harnessed to create more effective patient therapies.

title: The Shadows We Hide
author: Allen Eskens
description: In the sequel to the national bestseller The Life We Bury , Joe Talbert returns to investigate the murder of the father he never knew, and to reckon with his own family's past.

title: The Curse of Bigness: Antitrust in the New Gilded Age
author: Tim Wu
description: From the man who coined the term 'net neutrality' and who has made significant contributions to our understanding of antitrust policy and wireless communications, comes a call for tighter antitrust enforcement and an end to corporate bigness.

title: Einstein's Monsters: The Life and Times of Black Holes
author: Chris Impey
description: The latest volume from the University of Arizona astronomy professor and science writer explores the astonishing science of black holes and their role in understanding the history and future of our universe.

title: The Allies: Roosevelt, Churchill, Stalin, and the Unlikely Alliance That Won World War II
author: Winston Groom
description: Best-selling author Winston Groom tells the complex story of how Franklin Roosevelt, Winston Churchill, and Joseph Stalin—the three iconic and vastly different Allied leaders—aligned to win World War II and created a new world order.

title: Dear Zealots
author: Amos Oz, Trans. by Jessica Cohen
description: From the Israeli writer, journalist, and intellectual, Dear Zealots offers three essays that speak directly to our present age on the rise of zealotry in Israel and around the world.

title: Che: A Revolutionary Life
author: John Lee Anderson and José Hernández
description: The graphic adaptation of an biography of the iconic revolutionary Che Guevara.

title: We Can Save Us All
author: Adam Nemett
description: Welcome to The Egg, an off-campus geodesic dome where David Fuffman and his crew of alienated Princeton students train for what might be the end of days: America is in a perpetual state of war, climate disasters create a global state of emergency, and scientists believe time itself may be collapsing.

title: Night of Miracles
author: Elizabeth Berg
description: Berg’s sequel to The Story of Arthur Truluv checks in with Arthur’s friends, neighbors, and beneficiaries.

title: Thanks a Thousand: A Gratitude Journey
author: A J Jacobs
description: After being dared by his son, A. J. Jacobs decided to thank every single person involved in producing his morning cup of coffee. The resulting journey takes him across the globe and transforms his life.

title: Empire of Sand
author: Tasha Suri
description: A nobleman's daughter with magic in her blood. An empire built on the dreams of enslaved gods. Empire of Sand is Tasha Suri's Mughal India-inspired debut fantasy.

title: Rival Queens: The Betrayal of Mary, Queen of Scots
author: Kate Williams
description: From the New York Times bestselling author of Becoming Queen Victoria , a new history of Mary Queen of Scots and Elizabeth I that reveals how the most important relationship of their life―their friendship―changed them forever.

title: The Once and Future Worker: A Vision for the Renewal of Work in America
author: Oren Cass
description: In this re-evaluation of American society, economics, and public policy, Oren Cass challenges our basic assumptions about what prosperity means and where it comes from to reveal how we lost our way.

title: K-Punk: The Collected and Unpublished Writings of Mark Fisher
author: Mark Fisher
description: Edited by Darren Ambrose and with a foreword by Simon Reynolds, this volume collects the work of acclaimed British writer, political activist, and lecturer Mark Fisher, whose "K-Punk" blog became a cult favorite among disenchanted intellectuals compelled by his unique takes on film, television, music, and politics.

title: Quarterback: Inside the Most Important Position in the National Football League
author: John Feinstein
description: The esteemed sports journalist takes a deep look at the uniquely coveted and hallowed position of NFL quarterback through the lens of five top players in that position, taking readers inside their unique experiences of playing and holding the keys to their multibillion-dollar teams.

title: Handsome Johnny: The Life and Death of Johnny Rosselli: Gentleman Gangster, Hollywood Producer, CIA Assassin
author: Lee Server
description: A definitive rags-to-riches biography of Al Capone’s 'Man in Hollywood,' Johnny Rosselli.

title: The Females
author: Wolfgang Hilbig, trans. Isabel Fargo Cole
description: It begins with a factory laborer who ogles women in secret on the job. When those same women mysteriously vanish from their small town, the worker sets out on a hallucinatory journey to find them.

title: Fox 8: A Story
author: George Saunders, Illustrated by Chelsea Cardinal
description: From the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Lincoln in the Bardo , a story about the unintended consequences unleashed by our quest to tame the natural world—featuring black-and-white illustrations by Chelsea Cardinal.

title: An Almost Perfect Christmas
author: Nina Stibbe
description: From the author of Love, Nina , a hilarious account of the highs and lows of Christmas season

title: John Marshall: The Man Who Made the Supreme Court
author: Richard Brookhiser
description: A senior editor of National Review and biographer of several founding fathers turns the spotlight on John Marshall, one of America's most revered chief justices who elevated the stature of the Supreme Court.

title: A Rebel in Gaza: Behind the Lines of the Arab Spring, One Woman's Story
author: Asmaa al-Ghoul and Selim Nassib, Trans. by Mike Mitchell
description: The Arab Spring and siege of Gaza told by young Palestinian journalist Asmaa al-Ghoul, human rights activist and peace-prize winner.

title: Everything Lost Is Found Again: Four Seasons in Lesotho
author: Will McGrath
description: Winner of the Disquiet Open Borders Book Prize in 2017, this memoir recounts the writer's 20 months living with his wife in the southern African kingdom of Lesotho, whose people are full of a spirit of joyful absurdity, resolve, and affection for strangers even as they are devastated by the AIDS epidemic.

title: Vile Days: The Village Voice Art Columns, 1985-1988
author: Gary Indiana
description: Edited by Bruce Hainley, this collection of one of New York's most renowned art critics' columns from The Village Voice documents the city's 1980s art scene from the front lines.

title: Those Who Go by Night
author: Andrew Gaddes
description: A gruesome murder in a sleepy 14th-century English village sets the stage for a taut drama laced with witchcraft, depravity, and long-buried secrets in Andrew Gaddes' debut.

title: The Spy Who Was Left Behind: Russia, the United States, and the True Story of the Betrayal and Assassination of a CIA Agent
author: Michael Pullara
description: Trial lawyer Michael Pullara unravels his decade-long investigation of the 1993 murder of CIA officer Freddie Woodruff in the Soviet Republic of Georgia—disguised as a carjacking but ultimately ordered by KGB agents and covered up in Moscow as well as in Washington.

title: Wit's End: What Wit Is, How It Works, and Why We Need It
author: James Geary
description: The bestselling author of The World in a Phrase and the deputy curator at Harvard University’s Nieman Foundation for Journalism offers an exploration of wit, considering this intellectual phenomenon through the lens of psychology, folktales, visual art, literary history, and other traditions.

title: Money and Government: The Past and Future of Economics
author: Robert Skidelsky
description: An eminent political economist from Great Britain offers a critical examination of economics's past and future, and how it needs to change.

title: Voices: How a Great Singer Can Change Your Life
author: Nick Coleman
description: The esteemed British music writer and editor, who has experienced intermittent bouts of deafness, explores the meaning of singing, how it works, and his relationship to some of the last century's most important musical acts.

title: The Tale of Cho Ung: A Classic of Vengeance, Loyalty, and Romance
author: Sookja Cho
description: One of the most widely read and beloved stories of Choson-era Korea, the anonymously written tale—translated here into English for the first time—recounts the adventures of protagonist Cho Ung as he overcomes obstacles and grows into a heroic young man.

title: As a City on a Hill: The Story of America's Most Famous Lay Sermon
author: Daniel T. Rodgers
description: A Princeton history professor explores how the Puritan John Winthrop's influential speech—"A Model of Christian Charity"—at New England's founding has been misused for nearly four centuries. Winthrop's famous remark that the colony would "be as a city upon a hill" has been quoted out of context to mean American exceptionalism rather than the warning a closer look at Winthrop's speech reveals.

title: City of a Million Dreams: A History of New Orleans at Year 300
author: Jason Berry
description: Author Jason Berry orchestrates a parade of vibrant personalities. The profiles of this extraordinary cast furnish the narrative of this beloved city, famous the world over for mysterious rituals as people dance when they bury their dead.

title: Insurrecto
author: Gina Apostol
description: A multi-layered, many-voiced novel about two women, a Filipino translator and an American filmmaker, who go on a road trip in Duterte’s Philippines, collaborating and clashing in the writing of a film script about a massacre during the Philippine-American War.

title: A Year with Nature: An Almanac
author: Marty Crump
description: Combining science and aesthetics, this almanac offers daily affirmations of the extraordinary richness of biodiversity and our enduring beguilement by its beauty. With a text by herpetologist and natural history writer Marty Crump and a cornucopia of original illustrations by Bronwyn McIvor, this quirky quotidian reverie gazes across the globe, media, and time as it celebrates date-appropriate natural topics ranging from the founding of the National Park Service to annual strawberry, garlic, shrimp, hummingbird, and black bear festivals.

title: The Earth Dies Streaming: Film Writing, 2002-2018
author: A.S. Hamrah
description: A survey of essays contemplating modern cinema by the longtime film critic of n+1 , which featured many of the pieces collected here, as did The Baffler, Bookforum, Harper's , and other publications.

title: Is It Still Good to Ya?: Fifty Years of Rock Criticism, 1967-2017
author: Robert Christgau
description: Encompassing a career spanning six decades, Is It Still Good to Ya? sums up the career of rock critic Robert Christgau, whose album and concert reviews, essays, and reflections on his career tackle the whole of pop music, from Louis Armstrong to M.I.A..

title: The Feral Detective
author: Jonathan Lethem
description: Phoebe Siegler hires investigator Charles Heist to help her find her friend’s missing daughter, Arabella, and the unlikely pair navigates the California desert to locate Arabella, who is caught in the middle of a violent standoff that only Heist, mysteriously, can end.

title: Evening in Paradise: More Stories
author: Lucia Berlin
description: Following her critically acclaimed, posthumous story collection, A Manual for Cleaning Women , Lucia Berlin gets an encore in this careful selection of her remaining, previously uncollected tales.

title: Paris Echo
author: Sebastian Faulks
description: American historian Hannah intends to immerse herself in World War II research in Paris, wary of paying much attention to the city where a youthful misadventure once left her dejected. But a chance encounter with Tariq, a Moroccan teenager whose visions of the City of Lights as a world of opportunity and rebirth starkly contrast with her own, disrupts her plan.

title: Forever and a Day: A James Bond Novel
author: Anthony Horowitz
description: Readers learn about the birth of a legend—how James Bond grew into an illustrious career that began in the brutal underworld of the French Riviera.

title: Anthony Powell: Dancing to the Music of Time
author: Hilary Spurling
description: The author of the award-winning, two-volume Matisse: A Life , now gives us the biography of literary master Anthony Powell—the critic, editor, and novelist known as "the English Proust"—that, at the same time, takes us deep into 20th century London literary life.

title: Churchill: Walking with Destiny
author: Andrew Roberts
description: By the award-winning author of Napoleon and The Storm of War , this biography based on extensive new material aims to reveal the true genius of the controversial British man, statesman, and leader.

title: Those Who Knew
author: Idra Novey
description: From the acclaimed author of Ways to Disappear , a new novel about what a powerful politician thinks he can get away with and the group of misfits who finally bring him down.

title: The Kinship of Secrets
author: Eugenia Kim
description: From the author of The Calligrapher's Daughter comes the story of two sisters—one raised in the United States, the other in South Korea—and the family that bound them together even as the Korean War kept them apart.

title: Welcome Home: A Memoir with Selected Photographs and Letters
author: Lucia Berlin
description: Before Lucia Berlin died, she was working on a book of previously unpublished autobiographical sketches called Welcome Home .

title: The New Order
author: Karen E. Bender
description: Bender generally uses world events as the background for fiction focused on domestic life, but these 11 stories make our current sociopolitical landscape the subject.

title: Jeeves and The King of Clubs
author: Ben Schott
description: A new Jeeves and Wooster novel, penned in homage to P.G. Wodehouse by bestselling author Ben Schott, in which literature's favorite gentleman and his gentleman's personal gentleman become spies in service to the Crown.

title: In Extremis: The Life and Death of the War Correspondent Marie Colvin
author: Lindsey Hilsum
description: The International Editor for Channel 4 News in England offers a look into the extraordinary life of one of the most celebrated war correspondents of the last century, drawing on her diaries, reportage, and interviews with those who knew her until her death in Syria in 2012.

title: The Man in the Glass House: Philip Johnson, Architect of the Modern Century
author: Mark Lamster
description: The award-winning architectural critic and biographer considers the life and work of one of the last century's most influential and controversial architectural masters, who, for a time, also happened to be a fascist and Nazi sympathizer.

title: An Elderly Lady Is Up to No Good
author: Helene Tursten, Trans. by Marlaine Delargy
description: In these linked stories by the popular Swedish crime writer, an irascible 88-year-old woman has no family, no friends, and no qualms about a little murder for the right reason.

title: Sophisticated Giant: The Life and Legacy of Dexter Gordon
author: Maxine Gordon
description: The wife of the legendary tenor saxophonist who died in 1990 explores his legacy through a blend of biography, memoir, and research that draws on interviews and a selection of Dexter’s personal letters.

title: Monument: Poems New and Selected
author: Natasha Trethewey
description: This new collection from the two-time U.S. Poet Laureate and Pulitzer Prize winner gathers poems from Domestic Work , Bellocq's Ophelia , Native Guard , Congregation , and Thrall , while also including new work written over the last decade.

title: The Day That Went Missing: A Family's Story
author: Richard Beard
description: Winner of the PEN/Ackerley Prize 2018. On a family summer holiday in Cornwall in 1978, Richard and his younger brother Nicholas are jumping in the waves. Suddenly, Nicholas is out of his depth. One moment he's there, the next he's gone.

title: Lost Lake: A Detective Gemma Monroe Mystery
author: Emily Littlejohn
description: A new novel from Emily Littlejohn, the author of acclaimed debut Inherit the Bones , featuring Colorado police officer Gemma Monroe.

title: Born to Be Posthumous: The Eccentric Life and Mysterious Genius of Edward Gorey
author: Mark Dery
description: An expansive biography of Edward Gorey, the eccentric master of macabre cartoons, stories, and books.

title: In Byron's Wake: The Turbulent Lives of Lord Byron's Wife and Daughter: Annabella Milbanke and ADA Lovelace
author: Miranda Seymour
description: A portrait of two remarkable women, revealing how two turbulent lives were always haunted by the spirit of the father whom Ada never knew: Lord Byron.

title: Nine Perfect Strangers
author: Liane Moriarty
description: From the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Big Little Lies . Could ten days at a health resort really change you forever? In Liane Moriarty’s latest page-turner, nine perfect strangers are about to find out.

title: We Begin in Gladness: How Poets Progress
author: Craig Morgan Teicher
description: The 2018 winner of the Academy of American Poets' Lenore Marshall Poetry Prize explores the ways that poets develop poems, a career, and a life.

title: Ways to Hide in Winter
author: Sarah St Vincent
description: In the wintery silences of Pennsylvania’s Blue Ridge Mountains, a woman befriends a mysterious foreigner, and sets this debut novel in motion.

title: My One and Only Duke
author: Grace Burrowes
description: From a New York Times bestselling author comes the story of the unconventional Wentworth family in this charming new series with a Cinderella twist.

title: The War Before the War: Fugitive Slaves and the Struggle for America's Soul from the Revolution to the Civil War
author: Andrew Delbanco
description: A Columbia University American Studies professor offers a sweeping study of how fugitive slaves seeking freedom from their Southern overseers—and the laws surrounding their status in the North—contributed to the U.S. Civil War and affected politics in late 18th and early 19th centuries.

title: The Naked Woman
author: Armonia Somers, Trans. by Kit Maude
description: A feminist classic from 1950s Uruguay, The Naked Woman was met with scandal and outrage due to its erotic content, cynicism, and stylistic ingenuity. The novel follows Rebeca Linke's ardent, ultimately tragic, attempt to free herself from a hostile society.

title: Never Home Alone
author: Rob Dunn
description: A natural history of the wilderness in our homes, from the microbes in our showers to the crickets in our basements

title: Wolves of Eden
author: Kevin McCarthy
description: The Civil War may be over, but in this historical novel, the battle for the West is only just beginning.

title: Someone Like Me
author: M. R. Carey
description: After fending off a brutal attack by her ex-husband, a woman fears for her sanity. The truth is something far more terrifying.

title: An Agent of Utopia
author: Andy Duncan
description: Stories that borrow from American folklore, history, and a plethora of literary sources to forge fantasy worlds that are intimately familiar.

title: A Shot in the Dark: A Constable Twitten Mystery
author: Lynne Truss
description: The shooting of an acerbic reviewer during the premiere of a play at the Theatre Royal opens endless avenues of investigation for the incompetents of the Brighton Constabulary in this effervescent farce.

title: Why Religion?: A Personal Story
author: Elaine Pagels
description: Why is religion still around in the 21st century? Why do so many still believe? And how do various traditions still shape the way people experience everything from sexuality to politics, whether they are religious or not? In Why Religion? Elaine Pagels looks to her own life to help address these questions.

title: An Unexplained Death
author: Mikita Brottman
description: An Unexplained Death is an obsessive investigation into a mysterious death at the Belvedere―a once-grand hotel―and a poignant, gripping meditation on suicide and voyeurism

title: Unholy Land
author: Lavie Tidhar
description: The author of the Campbell and Neukom award-winning novel Central Station returns with an alternate-history tale in which Palestina, a Jewish state founded in the early 20th century, is building a vast border wall to keep out African refugees. Protagonist Lior Tirosh—a semi-successful author of pulp fiction—has meanwhile become a suspect in a string of murders while being stalked across possible-future dimensions.

title: Civil War Barons: The Tycoons, Entrepreneurs, Inventors, and Visionaries Who Forged Victory and Shaped a Nation
author: Jeffry D. Wert
description: From the author of nine books on the U.S. Civil War, including Cavalryman of the Lost Cause and A Glorious Army , this volume puts the spotlight on the capitalists behind the war effort—men of vision, organizational talent, and capital, who took advantage of the opportunity to create and market products that sustained Union troops, affected military strategy and tactics, and made the killing fields even deadlier.

title: The Life of Saul Bellow: Love and Strife, 1965-2005
author: Zachary Leader
description: This second volume of The Life of Saul Bellow opens with Bellow at 49 having won wealth and acclaim for his work, achievements that will only continue as he churns out more great fiction and wins major awards from the Pulitzer to the Nobel. Meanwhile, his non-writing life is in tumult, with controversies over his positions on social issues and family relationships marked by strife and instability.

title: The Colors of All the Cattle: No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency
author: Alexander McCall Smith
description: In the 19th installment of the beloved No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency series, Mma Ramotswe runs for a seat on the Gaborone City Council so that she can oppose developers' plans to build the flashy Big Fun Hotel next to a graveyard. Meanwhile, her mentee Charlie volunteers to be the lead investigator in a hit-and-run case to prove he's ready to be more than an apprentice.

title: The William H. Gass Reader
author: William H. Gass
description: Before he died in 2017, the three-time winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award and other literary honors selected 50 of his own essays, short stories, and novels to include in this compendious volume.

title: Gene Machine: The Race to Decipher the Secrets of the Ribosome
author: Venki Ramakrishnan
description: The winner of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry narrates the race to understand the structure of the ribosome—a finding that advanced our knowledge of all life—alongside a human story of his own unlikely journey to the top of the science profession.

title: Murder, She Wrote: Manuscript for Murder
author: Jessica Fletcher
description: Jessica Fletcher investigates a mysterious manuscript with deadly consequences in the latest entry in this USA Today bestselling series.

title: Beyoncé in Formation
author: Omise’eke Tinsley
description: A unique take on Beyoncé’s 2016 album and video Lemonade and its implications for 21st-century black feminism.

title: City of Ash and Red
author: Pyun Hye-young, Trans. by Sora Kim-Russell
description: A man’s new job in an unfamiliar country becomes a fast descent into a psychological and literal version of hell.

title: Top Dog
author: Jens Lapidus,
description: Talk about your star-crossed lovers. When Lapidus reunites Teddy Maksumic, who served eight years for a kidnapping he didn’t commit, with newly independent lawyer Emelie Jansson, it’s every man, woman, and child for themselves

title: A Tale of Two Murders
author: Laura Thompson
description: An exhaustive look into the passionate love affair that led to one of the most infamous murders in 1920s England.

title: Northwood: A Novella
author: Maryse Meijer
description: A novella about a woman's obsession with a brutal, violent lover that questions what we think about art, female sexuality, and intimacy.

title: The Best Bad Things
author: Katrina Carrasco
description: It is 1887, and Alma Rosales is on the hunt for stolen opium. Trained in espionage by the Pinkerton Detective Agency―but dismissed for bad behavior and a penchant for going undercover as a man―Alma now works for Delphine Beaumond, the seductive mastermind of a West Coast smuggling ring.

title: As Kingfishers Catch Fire: Birds & Books
author: Alex Preston
description: Weaving writing about birds into a personal narrative, As Kingfishers Catch Fire is as much about the joy of reading and writing as it is about the thrill of wildlife.

title: The Lonesome Bodybuilder: Stories
author: Yukiko Motoya, trans. by Asa Yoneda
description: Eleven surreal tales, set in the offices, zoos, bus stops, boutiques, and homes of contemporary Japan.

title: Wasn't That a Time: The Weavers, the Blacklist, and the Battle for the Soul of America
author: Jesse Jarnow
description: The untold story of the Weavers, the hit-making folk-pop quartet destroyed with the aid of the United States government--and who changed the world, anyway.

title: Peace at Last: A Portrait of Armistice Day, 11 November 1918
author: Guy Cuthbertson
description: In this portrait of Armistice Day, which ranges from midnight to midnight, Guy Cuthbertson brings together news reports, literature, memoirs, and letters to show how the people on the street, as well as soldiers and prominent figures like D. H. Lawrence and Lloyd George, experienced a strange, singular day of great joy, relief, and optimism.

title: Big Week: The Biggest Air Battle of World War II
author: James Holland
description: The largely untold story of the dramatic Allied air campaign against Germany that was a turning point in World War II and ultimately crucial to the success of D-Day and the Allied invasion of Europe.

title: Since When
author: Bill Berkson
description: Frank O'Hara, Marilyn Monroe, John Cage, Allen Ginsberg--champagne-soaked postwar Manhattan and bohemian 1960s San Francisco revisited in Berkson's memoirs.

title: The Little Snake
author: A.L. Kennedy
description: A magical fable about the journey we all take through life, about love and family, about war and resilience, about how we live in this world, and how we leave it.

title: Fugitive Red
author: Jason Starr
description: Jack and Maria's marriage is shaky when a friend tells Jack about a new extramarital dating website. Jack follows up and meets Sophia--who goes by the name Fugitive Red. A steamy online affair ensues, but when goes to meet Sophia in person, he finds her dead--and he becomes the prime suspect.

title: Nighttown
author: Timothy Hallinan
description: Reluctant P.I. to the perfidious, Junior Bender, may be L.A.’s smoothest operator but when he breaks one of the cardinal rules of burglary (don’t take scores that you’re being paid way too much for) he finds himself once again on the wrong side of, well, the wrong side.

title: You Don’t Own Me
author: Mary Higgins Clark
description: Under Suspicion producer Laurie Moran’s fifth dive into crimes past has to overcome a major obstacle: the reluctance of the leading suspect to participate in the enterprise.

title: The Indispensable Composers
author: Anthony Tommasini
description: The Chief Classical Music Critic of The New York Times explores the question of musical greatness.

title: The Eternal City: A History of Rome
author: Ferdinand Addis
description: A historian tells the story of Rome through the dramatic key moments in its history: from its mythic founding in 753 BC to the release of Fellini's La Dolce Vita in 1960 and the Occupy riots of 2011.

title: Sea of Greed
author: Clive Cussler and Graham Brown
description: The world's oil supply is vanishing, the stock market is plummeting, and the key to saving the future seems to be a baffling historical mystery. Can the NUMA crew crack it in time? Sea of Greed is the suspenseful new NUMA Files novels from the #1 New York Times -bestselling grand master of adventure.

title: Hitler and the Habsburgs: The Führer's Vendetta Against the Austrian Royals
author: James Longo
description: An exploration of a little-known part of World War II history: how Adolf Hitler's hatred of the children of the assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand prompted him to deport the Archduke's sons to the Dachau concentration camp—and how their family fought back.

title: A Black Fox Running
author: Brian Carter
description: Originally published in 1981 by the late British artist—and now considered a classic—this is the story of Wulfgar, the dark-furred fox of Dartmoor, and of his nemesis, Scoble the trapper, in the seasons leading up to the pitiless winter of 1946.

title: Body & Soul: A Frank Elder Mystery
author: John Harvey
description: In the last novel in the British crime writer's series about Frank Elder, the titular private eye grapples with his 23-year-old daughter's abuse by an older artist who ends up dead—with Katherine the main suspect in his murder.

title: How to Be Alone: If You Want To, and Even If You Don't
author: Lane Moore
description: The award-winning comedian, writer, actor, and musician offers advice on how to survive young adulthood without the support of family or a romantic partner, providing illustrative anecdotes from from her hardscrabble upbringing and journey to artistic success in New York.

title: A Christmas Revelation
author: Anne Perry
description: The latest holiday novel by the bestselling author of The Sheen on the Silk is set in 1860s London, where an orphan boy named Worm witnesses a woman's kidnapping in the days leading up to Christmas. His plans to rescue her are upended when he discovers that she's in the midst of trying to bring to justice men who murdered her father—a task Worm and his friend try to assist her with.

title: Lost Time: Lectures on Proust in a Soviet Prison Camp
author: Józef Czapski
description: The first translation from the original French lectures on Proust by the Polish painter and writer Józef Czapski, who astonishingly delivered them in a Soviet prison camp during World War II without a single page of text available for reference.

title: A Savage Order: How the World's Deadliest Countries Can Forge a Path to Security
author: Rachel Kleinfeld
description: A senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace offers an analysis of why some democracies, including our own, are crippled by extreme violence and how they can regain security.

title: The Re-Origin of Species: A Second Chance for Extinct Animals
author: Torill Kornfeldt, Trans. by Fiona Graham
description: Swedish Journalist Torill Kornfeldt travelled the world to meet the scientists working to bring extinct animals back from the dead, and she narrates their laboratory adventures here.

title: Mortal Republic: How Rome Fell Into Tyranny
author: Edward J. Watts
description: The author of The Final Pagan Generation offers a new history of the fall of the Roman Republic that explains why Rome exchanged freedom for autocracy after a period of political corruption, social unrest, and civil wars.

title: Past Tense: A Jack Reacher Novel
author: Lee Child
description: Family secrets come back to haunt Jack Reacher in this thriller from #1 New York Times bestselling author Lee Child.

title: Hesse: The Wanderer and His Shadow
author: Gunnar Decker, Trans. by Peter Lewis
description: Against Nazi dictatorship, the disillusionment of Weimar, and Christian austerity, Hermann Hesse's stories inspired a nonconformist yearning for universal values to supplant fanaticism in all its guises. He reenters our world through this biography as a champion of spiritual searching in the face of mass culture and the disenchanted life.

title: Gaudeamus
author: Mircea Eliade trans. Christopher Bartholomew
description: In this portrait of youth, Eliade recounts the fictional version of his university years in late 1920’s Bucharest. This follow-up to Diary of a Short-Sighted Adolescent reveals a keen observer of human behavior, a seeker of truth and spiritual fulfillment whose path would eventually lead him to become the ultimate historian of 20th-century religions.

title: Let the People See: The Story of Emmett Till
author: Elliott J. Gorn
description: Using this new evidence and a broadened historical context, Elliott J. Gorn delves into the story of Emmett Till and why it still resonates today.

title: Daughters of the Lake
author: Wendy Webb
description: In the bestselling gothic suspense novelist's latest, recently divorced Kate Granger has retreated to her parents’ home on Lake Superior to pull herself together, only to discover the body of a murdered woman and an infant washed into the shallows. As the drowned woman reaches out from the grave, Kate must work with her—if only in dreams—to right the sinister wrongs of the past.

title: Girls on the Line
author: Jennie Liu
description: In this novel that addresses the effects of China's One-Child Policy, orphans and friends Luli and Yun work together in a factory until Yun, pregnant, disappears and Luli must confront the dangers of the outside world to find her.

title: Gentleman Jack: A biography of Anne Lister, Regency Landowner, Seducer and Secret Diarist
author: Angela Steidele Trans. by Katy Derbyshire
description: Anne's diaries lay hidden for many years, before scholars were brave enough to crack their code. Her erotic confessions and lively letters tell the story of an extraordinary woman. In this new book, author Angela Steidele gives a fresh perspective on the life of a cult historical figure.

title: Future Sounds: The Story of Electronic Music from Stockhausen to Skrillex
author: David Stubbs
description: David Stubbs charts the evolution of electronic music from the earliest mechanical experiments in the late nineteenth century to the pre-World War I inventions of the Futurist Luigi Russolo, author of the Art Of Noises manifesto.

title: The Library of Ice
author: Nancy Campbell
description: A vivid and perceptive book combining memoir, scientific and cultural history with a bewitching account of landscape and place, which will appeal to readers of Robert Macfarlane, Roger Deakin and Olivia Laing.

title: The Children of Harvey Milk: How LGBTQ Politicians Changed the World
author: Andrew Reynolds
description: Part political thriller, part meditation on social change, part love story, The Children of Harvey Milk tells the stories of courageous men and women around the world who came forward to make their voices heard during the struggle for equal rights.

title: Ghostographs: An Album
author: Maria Romasco Moore
description: Brief, crystalline stories combine with vintage photographs to illuminate the hidden terrain of childhood and the pain of growing up in one imagined town at the edge of an abyss where the narrator comes of age among family, friends, and phantoms.

title: A Different Drummer
author: William Melvin Kelley
description: This debut novel first published in 1962 to accolades comparing the author to James Baldwin and William Faulkner imagines an alternative history in which all black residents move away from an imaginary Southern state following a rebellion in 1957 by a young black farmer who is the descendant of slaves.

title: Homeland
author: Walter Kempowski, Trans. by Charlotte Collins
description: It is 1988, the year before the Berlin Wall came down. Jonathan Fabrizius, a journalist living in West Germany, is asked to travel to the contested lands of former East Prussia - where the Nazi legacy lives on in buildings and fortifications - to write about the route for a car rally, and come face to face with his painful family history, and devastating questions about ordinary Germans' complicity in the war.

title: Alice Isn't Dead
author: Joseph Fink
description: From the co-author of Welcome to Night Vale comes a fast-paced thriller about a truck driver searching across America for the wife she had long assumed to be dead.

title: Family Trust
author: Kathy Wang
description: Members of a Chinese-American family based in Silicon Valley deal with the passing of their patriarch. As news of Stanley Huang's bleak diagnosis settles in, his ex-wife and adult children all face other complications in their lives.

title: The Proposal
author: Jasmine Guillory
description: After a disastrous and highly public proposal gone wrong, a no-nonsense freelance writer rebounds with her knight in shining armor.

title: Thomas Cromwell: A Revolutionary Life
author: Diarmaid MacCulloch
description: Since the 16th century, we have been fascinated by Henry VIII and the man who stood beside him, guiding him, enriching him, and enduring the king's insatiable appetites and violent outbursts until Henry ordered his beheading in July 1540. After a decade of sleuthing in the royal archives, Diarmaid MacCulloch has emerged with a new understanding of Henry's mercurial chief minister, the inscrutable Thomas Cromwell.

title: Elevation
author: Stephen King
description: An eerie-but-sweet new novel from the master of American horror. In the small town of Castle Rock, Scott comes down with a mysterious illness that causes him to lose weight, and is engaged in a low grade—but escalating—battle with the lesbians next door whose dog regularly drops his business on Scott’s lawn. When Scott finally understands the prejudices they face—including his own—he tries to help.

title: Dark Sacred Night
author: Michael Connelly
description: Detective Renée Ballard is working the night beat and returns to Hollywood Station in the early hours to find a stranger rifling through old file cabinets. The intruder is retired detective Harry Bosch, working a cold case that has gotten under his skin. Ballard can't let him go through department records, but she wants in.

title: The Letters of Sylvia Plath Vol 2: 1956-1963
author: Sylvia Plath
description: The second volume in the definitive, complete collection of the letters of Pulitzer Prize-winning poet, Sylvia Plath, from the early years of her marriage to Ted Hughes to the final days leading to her suicide in 1963.

title: The Accident on the A35: An Inspector Gorski Investigation
author: Graeme MacRae Burnet
description: In the followup to Burnet's Man Booker-nominated The Disappearance of Adèle Bedeau , Detective Gorski investigates the death by car accident of a respected solicitor. At the same time, the solicitor's rebellious son, drunk on Jean Paul Sartre novels, is conducting an investigation of his own. Their independent, dual inquiries lead the reader down a twisted road marked by seedy back rooms and bar brawls.

title: Horsemen of the Sands
author: Leonid Yuzefovich, trans. by Marian Schwartz
description: Two novellas from contemporary Russian author, Leonid Yuzefovich.

title: Brainstorm: Detective Stories from the World of Neurology
author: Suzanne O'Sullivan
description: A leading neurologist recounts some of her most astonishing, challenging cases, which demonstrate how crucial the study of epilepsy has been to our understanding of the brain.

title: Mad, Bad, Dangerous to Know: The Fathers of Wilde, Yeats and Joyce
author: Colm Tóibín
description: A study of Irish culture, history, and literature told through the lives and work of three men—William Wilde, John Butler Yeats, and John Stanislaus Joyce—and the complicated, influential relationships they had with their famous sons.

title: Rampage
author: James M. Scott
description: An account of the World War II Battle of Manila, describing the 29 days of systematic rape, pillage, plunder, and murder committed by Japanese troops against innocent Filipino men, women, and children as American forces fought to liberate a city that was once called the Pearl of the Orient.

title: Marooned
author: Joseph Kelly
description: An insightful re-examination of the 1607 Jamestown settlement, the story of which is beginning to replace the Mayflower’s as America’s founding myth.

title: After Emily
author: Julie Dobrow
description: The untold story of the extraordinary mother and daughter who brought Emily Dickinson’s genius to light.

title: The White Darkness
author: David Grann
description: By the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Killers of the Flower Moon , a true story of adventure and obsession in the Antarctic, illustrated with color photographs.

title: I Might Regret This: Essays, Drawings, Vulnerabilities, and Other Stuff
author: Abbi Jacobson
description: Anecdotes, observations, and reflections collected during a solo cross-country drive from the co-creator and co-star of the hit series Broad City .

title: I Am Dynamite!: A Life of Nietzsche
author: Sue Prideaux
description: A biography for anyone seeking to understand history's most misunderstood philosopher.

title: Love in Catalina Cove
author: Brenda Jackson
description: For a Louisiana woman–turned–New Yorker, going home to her coastal town means facing an old loss—and finding new possibilities in love and life.

title: Shotguns and Stagecoaches: The Brave Men Who Rode for Wells Fargo in the Wild West
author: John Boessenecker
description: The true stories of the Wild West heroes who guarded the iconic Wells Fargo stagecoaches and trains, battling colorful thieves, vicious highwaymen, and robbers armed with explosives.

title: Beastie Boys Book
author: Michael Diamond
description: A panoramic experience that tells the story of Beastie Boys, by band members ADROCK and Mike D, with contributions from Amy Poehler, Colson Whitehead, Spike Jonze, Wes Anderson, Luc Sante, and more.

title: Bing Crosby: Swinging on a Star: The War Years, 1940-1946
author: Gary Giddins
description: The second book in Giddins's study, following Bing Crosby: A Pocketful of Dreams: The Early Years, 1903-1940 .

title: The Vampire: A New History
author: Nick Groom
description: An authoritative new history of the vampire, two hundred years after it first appeared on the literary scene.

title: Finding Baba Yaga: A Short Novel in Verse
author: Jane Yolen
description: A young woman discovers the power to speak up and take control of her fate.

title: Toddler-Hunting
author: Taeko Kōno, Trans. by Lucy North
description: A lively translation of post-war stories from the Japanese master of the unsettling tale, who died in 2015.

title: The Spite Game
author: Anna Snoekstra
description: Mercilessly bullied in high school, Ava knows she needs to put the past behind her and move on, but she can’t—not until she’s exacted precise, catastrophic revenge on the people who hurt her the most.

title: Uneasy Lies the Crown
author: Tasha Alexander
description: In Uneasy Lies the Crown , the thrilling new mystery in Tasha Alexander's bestselling series, Lady Emily and her husband Colin must stop a serial killer whose sights may be set on the new king, Edward VII.

title: Dissolve
author: Sherwin Bitsui
description: Drawing upon Navajo traditions and language, Sherwin Bitsui composes a passage through the American Southwest.

title: Slowhand: The Life and Music of Eric Clapton
author: Philip Norman
description: The bestselling biographer of iconic musicians from Buddy Holly to the Rolling Stones turns his spotlight on the Rock 'n' Roll Hall of Fame's only three-time inductee, reporting on his distinctive and scandalous childhood, coming of age in the 1960s British rock scene, his struggle with addiction, and his later years of quieter pursuits.

title: Dark Winter
author: Anthony J. Tata
description: Responding to a U.S. military computer-system failure, an elite group of American operatives must prevent pending nuclear strikes.

title: The Governesses
author: Anne Serre, Trans. by Mark Hutchinson
description: In this U.S. debut of a major French writer, three young governesses taunt their employers and literally devour neighborhood men who are drawn by their nubile energies.

title: Living with the Gods: On Beliefs and Peoples
author: Neil MacGregor
description: The acclaimed art-history writer and former director of London's National Gallery and of the British Museum examines the ways in which different societies have understood and articulated their places in the cosmic scheme, coupling his narrative explorations with photos of spiritual objects and works of art.

title: The Incomplete Book of Running
author: Peter Sagal
description: The host of NPR's hit quiz show Wait Wait ... Don't Tell Me! and a columnist for Runner's World shares stories, advice, lessons, and warnings from his running experiences.

title: When Women Ruled the World: Six Queens of Egypt
author: Kara Cooney
description: An accessible spin through the corridors of power in ancient Egypt, corridors that converged on thrones on which women reigned.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird: A Graphic Novel
author: Harper Lee, Illustrated by Fred Fordham
description: The classic novel about the explosion of racial hate in an Alabama town—seen through the eyes of a girl whose father defends a black man accused of rape—is reimagined through the graphic lens of illustrator Fred Fordham.

title: Keeping at It: The Quest for Sound Money and Good Government
author: Paul Volcker, Christine Harper
description: The life story of the former chairman of the Federal Reserve, whose integrity provides the inspiration we need as our constitutional system and political tradition are being tested to the breaking point.

title: How to Behave Badly in Elizabethan England
author: Ruth Goodman
description: Goodman explores the gamut of misconduct in Stuart and Tudor England, including offensive speech and gestures, the perverse delights of mockery and ridicule, the ripostes of physical violence, and a gallery of repellent habits and repulsive displays of bodily functions.

title: Beautiful Sinner: A Devil's Rock Novel
author: Sophie Jordan
description: In the latest installment of Jordan's Devil's Rock novels, reporter Gabriella is trapped in a supply closet with her old high school crush, Cruz Walsh, who was imprisoned for years for a crime he didn't commit and—to Gabriella's surprise—has been in love with her since high school.

title: The Monster Baru Cormorant
author: Seth Dickinson
description: In the sequel to the geopolitical fantasy The Traitor Baru Cormorant , protagonist Baru is now the cryptarch Agonist―a secret lord of the empire she's vowed to destroy. Hunted by a mutinous admiral, haunted by the wound which has split her mind in two, Baru has a chance to trigger a war that will consume the Masquerade.

title: Omer Pasha Latas: Marshal to the Sultan
author: Ivo Andrić Trans. by Celia Hawkesworth
description: An epic by Nobel Prize-winner Ivo Andrić about power, identity, and Islam set in 19th-century Ottoman Bosnia and Istanbul.

title: Abbott
author: Saladin Ahmed, Illustrated by Sami Kivelä
description: The Hugo Award-nominated novelist and author of Black Bolt presents the search of one woman—a hard-nosed reporter in 1970s Detroit—for the supernatural truth about the city's political corruption and its contribution to the destruction of her family.

title: The Rain Watcher
author: Tatiana De Rosnay
description: The author of the bestselling World War II novel Sarah's Key offers a contemporary family drama set in Paris: As the Malegarde family gathers to celebrate the patriarch's 70th birthday, a natural disaster strikes, forcing family members' hidden fears and secrets to the surface.

title: Between Two Millstones, Book 1: Sketches of Exile, 1974-1978
author: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
description: On the centenary of the birth of the Russian Nobel Prize winner, this memoir begins during Solzhenitsyn's exile from the Soviet Union after the publication of The Gulag Archipelago , following his trials and tribulations around Europe and the United States.

title: Suicidal: Why We Kill Ourselves
author: Jesse Bering
description: The author of Perv: The Sexual Deviant in All of Us and director of the Centre for Science Communication at the University of Otago in New Zealand investigates the motivations behind what he describes as the "call to oblivion," mixing research with personal reflection.

title: Sentinel
author: Francesca Lidia Viano
description: The story of the improbable campaign that created America’s most enduring monument.

title: Don Quixote of La Mancha
author: Miguel De Cervantes and Ilan Stavans
description: In this graphic adaptation of the 17th century Spanish masterpiece—considered by many to be the first modern novel—cultural commentator Ilan Stavans and illustrator Roberto Weil reimagine Cervantes’s tale in ways that are both faithful and irreverent.

title: Carry Her Home: Stories
author: Caroline Bock
description: A winner of the Washington Writers’ Publishing House prize, this collection of 47 stories includes flash and full-length works loosely based on the lives of the writer's parents' in the 1960s to the present day.

title: Friday Black
author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah
description: This debut collection explores the mortal dangers and frustrations of being young and black in America in surreal and satirical stories, exploring scenarios ranging from the acquittal of a white man in the beheading five black children to a theme park specializing in the simulated murder of "criminal" minorities.

title: Little
author: Edward Carey
description: This historical novel explores Revolutionary Paris through the fictionalized eyes of the orphan who grew up to become Madame Tussaud.

title: The Gradual Disappearance of Jane Ashland
author: Nicolai Houm, Trans. by Anna Paterson
description: An American woman wakes up alone in a tent in the Norwegian mountains, where a storm rages and she has no map, no compass, no food, and a dead phone. How she ended up there, and the tragic details of her life, emerge over the course of this novel.

title: Debussy: A Painter in Sound
author: Stephen Walsh
description: A biography of one of the greatest and most popular of modern composers that also deeply investigates his much-loved music.

title: Everything Under
author: Daisy Johnson
description: Shortlisted for the 2018 Man Booker Prize, a reimagining of the Oedipus myth set on the canals of Oxford.

title: Retablos
author: Octavio Solis
description: Seminal moments, rites of passage, crystalline vignettes--a memoir about growing up brown at the U.S./Mexico border.

title: Nine Pints: A Journey Through the Money, Medicine, and Mysteries of Blood
author: Rose George
publisher: Metropolitan Books/ Henry Holt and Company
description: An exploration of blood, the life-giving substance with the power of taboo, the value of diamonds and the promise of breakthrough science.

title: The Reckoning
author: John Grisham
description: The Reckoning delivers John Grisham's signature layers of legal suspense with a Southern Gothic twist.

title: The Fox
author: Frederick Forsyth
description: Former chief of the British Secret Intelligence Service Adrian Weston is awoken in the middle of the night by a phone call from the Prime Minister. Her news is shocking: the Pentagon, the NSA, and the CIA have been hacked simultaneously, their seemingly impenetrable firewalls breached by an unknown enemy known only as 'The Fox.'

title: An Untouched House
author: Willem Frederik Hermans, Trans. by David Colmer
description: First published in Dutch in 1951, An Untouched House takes a hard look at the compromises a person is willing to make in order to survive, told through the lens of a Dutch soldier who meets and cooperates with a group of Nazis during World War II.

title: Listen to the Marriage
author: John Jay Osborn
description: Unfolding over the course of ten months and taking place entirely in the marriage counselor’s office, John Jay Osborn’s Listen to the Marriage is the story of a fractured couple in a moment of crisis, and of the person who tries to get them to see each other again.

title: Red Moon
author: Kim Stanley Robinson
description: A novel of space exploration and political revolution from The New York Times bestselling author.

title: Training School for Negro Girls
author: Camille Acker
description: In her debut collection, Acker pays tribute to Washington, D.C.—the Chocolate City—and the changes it went through during the last years of the 20th century.

title: A Cloud in the Shape of a Girl
author: Jean Thompson
description: From National Book Award finalist and the New York Times bestselling author of The Year We Left Home , comes a family saga about three generations of women who struggle to find freedom and happiness in their small Midwestern college town.

title: Useful Phrases for Immigrants: Stories
author: May-Lee Chai
description: Eight stories illuminate the hopes and fears of Chinese immigrants and their descendants.

title: Shadow and Ice
author: Gena Showalter
description: Knox of Iviland, the most ruthless warrior in All War history, has spent his life fighting others to the death, winning new realms for his king. Now the stakes are higher than ever. If he prevails in the battle for Earth, his slave bands will be removed. Victory is his sole focus…until he meets her.

title: Go To My Grave
author: Catriona McPherson
description: A rousing gothic tale of past and present in a Galloway beach house.

title: Sugar Land
author: Tammy Lynne Stoner
description: The long, wondrous life of a mostly closeted Texas lesbian, from teenage years in the kitchen at the men's prison to old age in a trailer off RR 23, with the 20th century rolling by in the background.

title: Let It Bang: A Young Black Man's Reluctant Odyssey Into Guns
author: RJ Young
description: A story of race, guns, and self-protection in America today, through the quest of a young black man learning to shoot a handgun to relate to his father-in-law.

title: The Line
author: Martin Limón
description: George Sueño and Ernie Bascom return for their thirteenth outing, which takes them from Seoul to the DMZ in their most politically charged murder case yet.

title: The Travelling Cat Chronicles
author: Hiro Arikawa, Trans. by Philip Gabriel
description: The tender feelgood story of a man's journey around Japan with a streetcat, told from the cat's perspective.

title: The Rise of Andrew Jackson
author: David S. Heidler and Jeanne T. Heidler
description: High-strung, scarcely literate, combative, vengeful, power-hungry, and corrupt: The adjectives could come from any headline covering presidential politics, but here they center on a president elected in 1828 with a powerful machine behind him.

title: Thin Air
author: Richard K Morgan
description: An atmospheric tale of corruption and abduction set on Mars, from the author of the award-winning science fiction novel Altered Carbon , now a series from Netflix.

title: Find Me Gone
author: Sarah Meuleman
description: From Vogue Amsterdam columnist Sarah Meuleman comes a debut novel about second chances and the lengths one young woman will go to keep her dark secrets sealed in the past.

title: The World According to Tom Hanks: The Life, the Obsessions, the Good Deeds of America's Most Decent Guy
author: Gavin Edwards
description: The author of The Tao of Bill Murray and other pop-cultural books profiles one of the film industry's most beloved stars, drawing on research and interviews to provide insight into his optimism and integrity.

title: The Count of 9
author: Erle Stanley Gardner
description: From the world-famous creator of Perry Mason, Erle Stanley Gardner comes another baffling case for the Cool & Lam detective agency.

title: Astounding
author: Alec Nevala-Lee
description: A laser-sharp study of science fiction's golden age, the product of a small circle of writers and their guiding editor.

title: How the Internet Happened: From Netscape to the iPhone
author: Brian McCullough
description: Tech-guru Brian McCullough delivers a history of the internet, why it exploded, and how it changed everything.

title: Marilla of Green Gables
author: Sarah McCoy
description: The beloved Anne of Green Gables gets a prequel in this novel that follows character Marilla Cuthbert, here a 13-year-old who takes on the responsibility of a farm wife after the death of her mother and, later, the larger political cause of abolition.

title: Don't Let Go
author: Michel Bussi, Trans. by Sam Taylor
description: From one of France's bestselling authors, the tale of wealthy Parisians Martial and Liane Bellion, who are enjoying the perfect family vacation on the island of Réunion—until Liane disappears and Martial becomes the prime suspect. When he and his daughter also go missing, a manhunt on the island begins.

title: Wanamaker's Temple: The Business of Religion in an Iconic Department Store
author: Nicole C. Kirk
description: From the Frank and Alice Schulman Chair of Unitarian Universalist History and assistant professor at Meadville Lombard Theological School, Wanamaker’s Temple examines how and why the eponymous entrepreneur blended business and religion in his Philadelphia retail store, offering a historical exploration of the relationships between religion, commerce, and urban life in the late 19th and early 20th century.

title: Drawn to Berlin
author: Ali Fitzgerald
description: Fitzgerald’s graphic memoir entwines political and personal displacement.

title: The Anna Karenina Fix: Life Lessons from Russian Literature
author: Viv Groskop
description: A love letter to Russian literature and an exploration of the answers these writers found to life’s questions.

title: The Collector: The Story of Sergei Shchukin and His Lost Masterpieces
author: Natalya Semenova
description: A biography of Sergei Shchukin, the great collector who changed the face of Russia's art world.

title: Dirty Plotte: The Complete Julie Doucet
author: Julie Doucet
description: The feminist 1990s comic series Dirty Plotte is collected here along with Doucet's other works from that period, including My New York Diary , rarer previously unpublished material, and essays about her comics legacy and influence.

title: The Last Pass: Cousy, Russell, the Celtics, and What Matters in the End
author: Gary M. Pomerantz
description: Historian, journalist, and Stanford University lecturer Pomerantz offers a portrait of Bob Cousy, the Hall of Fame Boston Celtics captain who led the team to its first six championships. At 90, Cousy looks back with regret about failing to adequately defend his teammate Bill Russell, who faced intense racism despite the fact that he was crucial in driving the Celtics to glory.

title: Pulse
author: Michael Harvey
description: In 1970s Boston, two detectives are flummoxed when they investigate the murder of a young man whose brother claims to have known the details of the killing before it ever happened. The subsequent investigation leads the detectives deep into the Fitzsimmons brothers’ past, where they find heartbreaking loss, sordid characters, and metaphysical conspiracies.

title: Applied Ballardianism
author: Simon Sellars
description: An existential odyssey weaving together lived experience and theoretical insight, this startling autobiographical hyperfiction surveys and dissects a world where everything connects and global technological delirium is the norm.

title: The Job: Work and Its Future in a Time of Radical Change
author: Ellen Ruppel Shell
description: Critically acclaimed journalist Ellen Ruppel Shell uncovers the true cost—political, economic, social, and personal—of America's mounting anxiety over jobs, and what we can do to regain control over our working lives.

title: The Midnight Witness
author: Sara Blaedel, Trans. by Mark Kleine
description: Rookie homicide detective Louise Rick makes her debut in this thrilling #1 international bestseller that launched 3 million copy bestselling writer Sara Blaedel's incredible career.

title: The Three Beths
author: Jeff Abbott
description: A psychologically intense and emotionally gripping new suspense novel about a daughter's desperate search for her missing mother—one that may lead her closer to home than she ever anticipated.

title: Leaders: Myth and Reality
author: Stanley McChrystal, with Jeff Eggers and Jason Mangone
description: Stanley McChrystal, the retired US Army general and bestselling author of Team of Teams , profiles thirteen great leaders to show that leadership is not what you think it is—and never was.

title: Help!
author: Thomas Brothers
description: The story of how creative cooperation inspired two of the world’s most celebrated musical acts.

title: Robert Graves: From Great War Poet to Good-bye to All That (1895-1929)
author: Jean Moorcroft Wilson
description: A sensitive rendering of the poet’s formative years.

title: I'll Be There for You: The One about Friends
author: Kelsey Miller
description: The author of Big Girl: How I Gave Up Dieting and Got a Life offers a cultural history of the hit '90s sitcom that remains popular in syndication, exploring all aspects of the show, from its unlikely origins to the societal conditions that amplified its success and contributed to now-controversial decisions, such as all-white casting and storylines that featured homophobia and fat-phobia.

title: Restless Lightning
author: Richard Baker
description: In this second book in the Breaker of Empires series, Lieutenant Sikander North is assigned to a remote outpost in the crumbling Tzoru Empire, where an alien uprising presents a number of seemingly insurmountable challenges that could mean his disgrace or redemption.

title: The Mental Load: A Feminist Comic
author: Emma
description: In her first book of comic strips, French cartoonist Emma reflects on social and feminist issues by means of simple line drawings, dissecting the "mental load"—all that invisible and unpaid organizing, list-making, and planning—that so many women carry through daily life.

title: Rock Critic Law: 101 Unbreakable Rules for Writing Badly about Music
author: Michael Azerrad
description: The esteemed music journalist and author of Our Band Could Be Your Life and Come As You Are: The Story of Nirvana offers an illustrated guidebook for unambitious writers of music reportage and criticism.

title: Dungeons and Dragons Art and Arcana: A Visual History
author: Kyle Newman, Jon Peterson, Michael Witwer, and Sam Witwer
description: An illustrated guide to the history and evolution of the beloved role-playing game told through the paintings, sketches, illustrations, and visual ephemera behind its creation, growth, and continued popularity.

title: Frail Sister
author: Karen Green
description: This unique hybrid of collage art and literature narrates the adventurous and traumatic life of Constance, a character based on Green's aunt. Told in letters, photographs, documents, and other materials, Constance's story begins in the dirt-poor town of Oil City, Pennsylvania, during the Great Depression and moves to Italy, where Constance toured with the USO during World War II.

title: The Tiger Flu
author: Larissa Lai
description: A novel about a community of parthenogenic women under siege after the end of the world.

title: Thanks a Lot Mr. Kibblewhite: My Story
author: Roger Daltrey
description: The front man of The Who draws on years of careful introspection in an anecdotal memoir of his rise from poverty to rock-and-roll stardom, sharing insights into the creative processes behind iconic hits and his relationship with band members.

title: The Blue Kingfisher
author: Erica Wright
description: What happens when a master of disguise tries to be herself for once? If you’re private investigator Kat Stone, trouble seems to find you with or without your favorite wig.

title: Vendetta
author: Iris Johansen
description: In the latest installment of the bestselling author's Eve Duncan series, Rachel and Brandon race against the clock to bring terrorist ringleader Huber down before he can orchestrate a disaster that will lay waste to half the country—while fighting a growing attraction to each other, which could prove just as dangerous as Huber himself.

title: Charlie Company's Journey Home: The Forgotten Impact on the Wives of Vietnam Veterans
author: Andrew Wiest
description: The author of The Boys of '67: Charlie Company's War follows up with a story focused on the wives of those "boys" as they struggled to keep their families together during their husbands' service and after—when post-traumatic stress and other consequences of battle began to appear.

title: Red Flags: Why XI's China Is in Jeopardy
author: George Magnus
description: An Oxford University economic analyst explores various circumstances that threaten China's continued economic rise.

title: Seattleness: A Cultural Atlas
author: Tera Hatfield, Jenny Kempson, and Natalie Ross
description: Through both experiential and data-driven cartography, this illustrated guide to Seattle covers a range of topics—including UFO sightings, pinball legacies, gray skies, frontier psychology, strong women, and strong coffee. Infographic visuals emerge from deep dives into data, unraveling over 50 real and strange narratives about the green metropolis.

title: Uberland: How Algorithms Are Rewriting the Rules of Work
author: Alex Rosenblat
description: A technology ethnographer reports on the four years she spent studying Uber—riding with and interviewing the company's drivers in more than two dozen cities—to understand the complicated politics of popular technologies that are manipulating both workers and consumers.

title: Lost Mars: Stories from the Golden Age of the Red Planet
author: Ed. by Mike Ashley
description: The acclaimed anthologist collects stories from the 19th and 20th centuries in which Mars became an object of fascination for writers interested in life on other planets and its implication for humans—with entries from the likes H.G. Wells, Ray Bradbury, and J. G. Ballard, as well as hard-to-find stories by forgotten writers from the genre.

title: Leaving the Gay Place: Billy Lee Brammer and the Great Society
author: Tracy Daugherty
description: The biographer of Joan Didion, Joseph Heller, and Donald Barthelme sets his sights on a lesser-known literary figure who spiraled tragically downward after the publication of his acclaimed 1961 Texas political novel, The Gay Place , based on his time working for Senator Lyndon B. Johnson.

title: Unsheltered
author: Barbara Kingsolver
description: From the award-winning author of Flight Behavior , The Lacuna , and The Poisonwood Bible , a novel alternating between two centuries focusing on two struggling people: present day Willa Knox—whose middle-class life crumbles when the magazine she built her career around folds and the college where her husband had tenure shuts down—and 19th Century science teacher Thatcher Greenwood, who is grappling with a headmaster hostile to his wish to discuss Darwin’s theory of evolution.

title: The Library Book
author: Susan Orlean
description: The author of The Orchid Thief reopens the unsolved mystery of the most catastrophic library fire in American history (the 1986 Los Angeles Public Library blaze) and delivers a love letter to a beloved institution—our libraries.

title: Melmoth
author: Sarah Perry
description: Haunted by past misdeeds, a self-exiled English translator encounters the uncanny in snow-covered Prague.

title: The Winters
author: Lisa Gabriele
description: After a whirlwind romance, a young woman returns to the opulent, secluded Long Island mansion of her new fiancé Max Winter. But all is not as it appears. The house is steeped in the memory of Max’s first wife Rebekah, who haunts the young woman’s imagination, while his very alive teenage daughter Dani makes her life a living hell.

title: Vietnam: An Epic Tragedy, 1945-1975
author: Max Hastings
description: An exploration of the Vietnam War from the acclaimed New York Times bestselling author of The Secret War .

title: Heavy
author: Kiese Laymon
description: A challenging memoir about black-white relations, income inequality, mother-son dynamics, Mississippi byways, lack of personal self-control, education from kindergarten through graduate school, and so much more.

title: The Big Fella
author: Jane Leavy
description: Babe Ruth 'made impossible events happen.' Aided by his crucial partnership with Christy Walsh—business manager, spin doctor, damage control wizard, and surrogate father, all stuffed into one tightly buttoned double-breasted suit—Ruth drafted the blueprint for modern athletic stardom.

title: A Well-Behaved Woman: A Novel of the Vanderbilts
author: Therese Anne Fowler
description: A fictionalized portrait of the Gilded Age socialite and suffragist who famously followed her own advice: 'First marry for money, then marry for love.'

title: The Lake On Fire
author: Rosellen Brown
description: The Lake on Fire begins among 19th-century Jewish immigrants on a failing Wisconsin farm. Dazzled by lore of the American dream, Chaya and her strange, brilliant, young brother Asher stow away to Chicago; what they discover there, however, is a Gilded Age as empty a façade as the beautiful Columbian Exposition luring thousands to Lake Michigan’s shore.

title: Riddance: Or: The Sybil Joines Vocational School for Ghost Speakers & Hearing-Mouth Children
author: Shelley Jackson
description: In Riddance , children with speech impediments attend a school in Massachusetts to learn how to channel the dead. Written in the form of transcripts, found documents, and archival material, the novel is a disquieting supernatural investigation into life after death.

title: Frederick Douglass: Prophet of Freedom
author: David W. Blight
description: Winner of the 2019 Pulitzer Prize for History, a biography of the most important African-American of the 19th century: Frederick Douglass, the escaped slave who became the greatest orator of his day and one of the leading abolitionists and writers of the era.

title: She Wants It: Desire, Power, and Toppling the Patriarchy
author: Jill Soloway
description: From the creator of the Emmy and Golden Globe-winning series Transparent , a memoir of personal transformation set against the profound cultural upheaval and shifting power dynamics that continue to shape our society.

title: American Dialogue
author: Joseph J. Ellis
description: An eminent historian illuminates the 'messy moment' of the nation’s founding and its implications for contemporary America.

title: Adult Teeth
author: Jeremy T Wilson
description: In his debut collection Adult Teeth , Wilson presents a cast of characters who grapple with life's big concerns: marriage, friendship, parenthood, death.

title: Napoleon: A Life
author: Adam Zamoyski
description: Historian Adam Zamoyski cuts through the mythology and explains Napoleon against the background of the European Enlightenment, and what he was himself seeking to achieve.

title: Everything's Trash, But It's Okay
author: Phoebe Robinson
description: New York Times bestselling author and star of 2 Dope Queens Phoebe Robinson is back with a new timely essay collection on gender, race, dating, and the dumpster fire that is our world.

title: This Will Only Hurt a Little
author: Busy Philipps
description: A highly candid, tell-all memoir from the former Dawson's Creek star and cult-favorite actress.

title: A Mind Unraveled
author: Kurt Eichenwald
description: A journalist recounts his decadeslong struggle with epilepsy.

title: Evergreen Tidings From the Baumgartners
author: Gretchen Anthony
description: A stodgy Midwestern socialite is forced to re-evaluate many of her deeply held beliefs in this comic family drama.

title: Destroy All Monsters: The Last Rock Novel
