author: Jeff Jackson
description: An epidemic of violence is sweeping the country: musicians are being murdered onstage in the middle of their sets by members of their audience. Are these random copycat killings, or is something more sinister at work?

title: Them: Why We Hate Each Other—And How to Heal
author: Ben Sasse
description: The Republican U.S. Senator from Nebraska assesses and proposes solutions to the tension and pessimism of modern America caused, he theorizes, by increasing social isolation and the collapse of traditional community connections.

title: Ruth Bader Ginsburg: A Life
author: Jane Sherron de Hart
description: An account of the life—private, public, legal, philosophical—of the 107th Supreme Court Justice, one of the most profound and profoundly transformative legal minds of our time. A book fifteen years in work, written with the cooperation of Ruth Bader Ginsburg herself and based on many interviews with the justice, her husband, her children, her friends, and her associates.

title: Shell Game: A V.I. Warshawski Novel
author: Sara Paretsky
description: Legendary sleuth V.I. Warshawski returns to the Windy City to save an old friend’s nephew from a murder arrest. As V.I. investigates, the detective soon finds herself tangling with the Russian mob, ISIS backers, and a shady network of stock scams and stolen art that stretches from Chicago to the East Indies and the Middle East.

title: In the Hurricane's Eye: The Genius of George Washington and the Victory at Yorktown
author: Nathaniel Philbrick
description: The story of the year that won the Revolutionary War from the New York Times bestselling author of In the Heart of the Sea and Valiant Ambition .

title: Fryderyk Chopin: A Life and Times
author: Alan Walker
description: A biography of the Polish composer by a leading authority on Chopin and his time.

title: Children of God
author: Lars Petter Sveen, Trans. Guy Puzey
description: The New Testament comes to life in these interconnected stories about the lives of the characters on the margins of the second half of the Christian Bible—thieves, Roman soldiers, prostitutes, lepers, healers, and the occasional disciple.

title: The Pan-Industrial Revolution: How New Manufacturing Titans Will Transform the World
author: Richard D'Aveni
description: A look at what will happen to global industry as 3-D printing becomes a worldwide phenomenon with far-reaching effects that most corporate and governmental leaders have yet to anticipate.

title: Grand Improvisation: America Confronts the British Superpower, 1945-1957
author: Derek Leebaert
description: A new understanding of the post World War II era, showing what occurred when the British Empire wouldn’t step aside for the rising American superpower―with global insights for today.

title: Trinity
author: Louisa Hall
description: A kaleidoscopic novel about Robert Oppenheimer—father of the atomic bomb—as told by seven fictional characters.

title: Anniversaries
author: Uwe Johnson, Trans. by Damion Searls
description: Gesine Cresspahl, a 34-year-old single mother and German émigré to Manhattan during the Vietnam War era, navigates daily life alternating between sharp attention to the world around her and extended reminiscences about her German childhood during World War II, in which her father worked for the resistance as a British spy but later spent time in a Soviet prison camp.

title: In the House in the Dark of the Woods
author: Laird Hunt
description: In this horror story set in colonial New England, a law-abiding Puritan woman goes missing. Or perhaps she has fled or abandoned her family. Or perhaps she's been kidnapped, and set loose to wander in the dense woods of the north. Alone and possibly lost, she meets another woman in the forest. Then everything changes.

title: Night Train
author: Thom Jones
publisher: Little, Brown and Company and Knopf
description: A generous posthumous selection from Jones' (1945-2016) three short story collections along with seven new works.

title: Almost Everything: Notes on Hope
author: Anne Lamott
description: The beloved author reflects on how to cultivate hope and wisdom at a time of polarized politics and anxiety about climate change, the future of democracy, and other social problems that have troubled the nation's waters.

title: Fierce Enigmas: A History of the United States in South Asia
author: Srinath Raghavan
description: A senior fellow at the Centre for Policy Research in New Delhi argues that, for 230 years, America's engagement with India, Afghanistan, and Pakistan has been characterized by short-term thinking and unintended consequences as America has sought to remake the world in its image. A clarion call to fundamentally rethink our approach to the region.

title: The Kingfisher Secret
author: Anonymous
description: Her code name is Kingfisher. Her mission: to seduce and marry a man of wealth and political influence. Now she must protect a terrifying secret.

title: Glimmer of Hope
author: The March for Our Lives Founders
description: Glimmer of Hope tells the story of how a group of teenagers raced to channel their rage and sorrow into action, and went on to create one of the largest youth-led movements in global history.

title: My Love Story
author: Tina Turner
description: Tina Turner—the long-reigning queen of rock & roll and living legend—sets the record straight about her illustrious career and complicated personal life in this memoir.

title: Deck the Hounds: An Andy Carpenter Mystery
author: David Rosenfelt
description: This Christmas mystery, featuring criminal defense lawyer Andy Carpenter and his faithful golden retriever, Tara, showcases Rosenfelt’s trademark humor and larger-than-life characters.

title: Brief Answers to the Big Questions
author: Stephen Hawking
description: The world-famous cosmologist and #1 bestselling author of A Brief History of Time leaves us with his final thoughts on the biggest questions facing humankind.

title: 1619: Jamestown and the Forging of American Democracy
author: James Horn
description: James Horn sheds new light on the year that gave birth to the great paradox of our nation: slavery in the midst of freedom. This portentous year marked both the origin of the most important political development in American history, the rise of democracy, and the emergence of what would in time become one of the nation's greatest challenges: the corrosive legacy of racial inequality that has afflicted America since its beginning.

title: Treason of Hawks
author: Lila Bowen
description: The climactic conclusion to the award-winning fantasy series. Rhett Walker is looking for peace, the memories of all he's lost haunting his dreams.

title: Famous Adopted People
author: Alice Stephens
description: When Lisa wakes up inside a palatial mountain compound, the captive of a glamorous, surgically-enhanced blonde named Honey, she soon realizes she is going to learn about her past whether she likes it or not. What happens next only could in one place: North Korea.

title: You Were Always Mine
author: Nicole Baart
description: The acclaimed author of Little Broken Things returns with another drama about a single mother who becomes embroiled in a mystery that threatens to tear apart what’s left of her family.

title: An Uncivil War
author: Greg Sargent
description: A gimlet-eyed look at the mean corridors of power in Washington, with a welcome reminder that this, too, shall—might?—pass.

title: A Very Large Expanse of Sea
author: Tahereh Mafi
description: A contemporary novel about fear, first love, and the devastating impact of prejudice.

title: Liberated Spirits: Two Women Who Battled Over Prohibition
author: Hugh Ambrose
description: The passage of the 18th Amendment (banning the sale of alcohol) and the 19th (women's suffrage) in the same year is no coincidence. These two Constitutional Amendments enabled women to redefine themselves and their place in society in a way historians have neglected to explore. Liberated Spirits describes how the fight both to pass and later to repeal Prohibition was driven by women, as exemplified by two remarkable women in particular.

title: I Am Behind You
author: John Ajvide Lindqvist
description: Four families wake up one morning in their trailer on an ordinary campsite. However, during the night something strange has happened. Everything outside the camping grounds has disappeared, and the world has been transformed into an endless expanse of grass. Can any of them find a way back to reality?

title: Townies: And Other Stories of Southern Mischief
author: Eryk Pruitt
description: A collection of southern-fried crime stories from Eryk Pruitt, one of the best new crime fiction writers working today. Townies, and Other Tales of Southern Mischief collects, for the first time, Pruitt's short fiction in a single volume.

title: The Big Book of Female Detectives
author: Otto Penzler
description: Otto Penzler's new anthology brings together the most cunning, resourceful, and brilliant female sleuths in mystery fiction. A Vintage Crime/Black Lizard Original.

title: The Darkness: A Thriller
author: Ragnar Jónasson
description: Spanning the icy streets of Reykjavik, the Icelandic highlands and cold, isolated fjords, The Darkness is an atmospheric thriller from Ragnar Jónasson.

title: Capitalism in America: A History
author: Alan Greenspan
description: From the former Fed Chairman and an Economist writer and historian, the full, epic story of America's evolution from a small patchwork of threadbare colonies to the most powerful engine of wealth and innovation the world has ever seen.

title: The Collector's Apprentice
author: B A Shapiro
description: A tale about the lengths to which people will go for their obsession, whether it be art, money, love, or vengeance.

title: The Craftsman
author: Sharon Bolton
description: British crime writer Sharon Bolton's latest standalone follows a police officer named Florence Lovelady, whose son goes missing under circumstances that seem all too familiar to those of a string of child murders she thought she had long ago resolved—with the assistance of some local witches.

title: The Consuming Fire
author: John Scalzi
description: In this second volume in The Interdependency series, humanity's interstellar empire is on the verge of collapse and a civil war, and Interdependency leader Emperox Grayland II prepares to take action to prevent catastrophe.

title: A Massacre in Mexico: The True Story Behind the Missing Forty-Three Students
author: Anabel Hernandez, Trans. by John Washington
description: The award-winning author of Narcoland investigates the 2014 disappearance of a group of students in Iguala, Mexico, alleging their murder at the hands of local police and a government cover-up stemming from deep corruption and collaboration between Mexican politicians and drug cartels.

title: Chalk: The Art and Erasure of Cy Twombly
author: Joshua Rivkin
description: A poet's attempt to chronicle the life of the notoriously elusive visual artist becomes an obsessive hunt across the globe for leads, one that he narrates and intersperses with meditations and reflections on Twombly—and his own life—as he goes.

title: Operation Columba: The Secret Pigeon Service: The Untold Story of World War II Resistance in Europe
author: Gordon Corera
description: The little-known tale of how British intelligence secretly used homing pigeons as part of a clandestine espionage operation to gather information, communicate, and coordinate with members of the Resistance to defeat the Nazis in occupied Europe during World War II.

title: The Novel of Ferrara
author: Giorgio Bassani, Trans. by Jamie McKendrick
description: Collected for the first time in English, Giorgio Bassani's novellas and stories trace the transformation of a close-knit Jewish community in an Italian town as Mussolini's Racial Laws go into effect and begin the process of dehumanization that will ultimately send many of the townspeople to their deaths by the Nazis.

title: Every Breath
author: Nicholas Sparks
description: Nicholas Sparks returns with a story about a chance encounter that becomes a touchstone for two vastly different individuals - transcending decades, continents, and the bittersweet workings of fate.

title: Sketchtasy
author: Mattilda Bernstein Sycamore
description: Sketchtasy takes place in that late-night moment when everything comes together, and everything falls apart—it’s an urgent, glittering, devastating novel about the perils of queer world-making in the mid-‘90s.

title: Nantucket Counterfeit
author: Steven Axelrod
description: The fifth Henry Kennis mystery takes us into the closed, gossip-riddled, back-stabbing world of Nantucket's community theater.

title: Wasteland
author: W. Scott Poole
description: Poole brings a scholar's eye and a devotee's heart to a study of the literary, film, and artistic incarnations of horror from the World War I period to today.

title: Sleep of Memory
author: Patrick Modiano, trans. by Mark Polizzotti
description: Patrick Modiano's first book since his Nobel Prize is a tapestry that brings together memory, esoteric encounters, and fragmented sensations

title: The Hell of Good Intentions: America’s Foreign Policy Elite and the Decline of U.S. Primacy
author: Stephen M. Walt
description: The New York Times –bestselling author dissects the faults and foibles of recent American foreign policy.

title: 8-Bit Apocalypse: The Untold Story of Atari's Missile Command
author: Alex Rubens
description: The first history of Atari's Missile Command , and its unforeseen effects on its creators and the culture.

title: The Black Khan: Book Two of the Khorasan Archives
author: Ausma Zehanat Khan
description: In this second installment of an epic fantasy quartet, a powerful band of women must use their magic to defeat an oppressive dark regime. After facing setbacks, they have another chance to obtain the Bloodprint—a text that may hold the secret to overthrowing the regime—but they must first contend with the Black Khan, a master of treachery.

title: Impeachment: An American History
author: Jon Meacham
description: Four experts on the American presidency review the only three impeachment cases from history--against Andrew Johnson, Richard Nixon, and Bill Clinton--and explore its power and meaning for today.

title: A Nation Forged by Crisis: A New American History
author: Jay Sexton
description: A new history of the United States revealing that crises--not unlike those of the present day--have determined our nation's course from the start.

title: Dawn of the Code War: America's Battle Against Russia, China, and the Rising Global Cyber Threat
author: John P Carlin
description: The inside story of how America's enemies launched a cyberwar against us-and how we've learned to fight back.

title: Hearing Beethoven: A Story of Musical Loss and Discovery
author: Robin Wallace
description: A musicologist and Beethoven scholar weaves a dual narrative about the way deafness transformed the life and practice of the great composer as well as that of his late wife, Barbara, who lost her hearing as a consequence of radiation administered to treat a brain tumor.

title: The New Mind Readers: What Neuroimaging Can and Cannot Reveal about Our Thoughts
author: Russell A. Poldrack
description: The Albert Ray Lang Professor of Psychology at Stanford University looks at the origins, development, and future of brain-imaging technology that is increasingly being used to decode our thoughts and experiences―and how this raises sometimes troubling questions about their application in domains such as marketing, politics, and the law.

title: Mutiny at Vesta
author: R.E. Stearns
description: In this second space adventure in the Shieldrunner Pirates trilogy, Adda and Iridian have survived the murderous Artificial Intelligence that tried to kill them—but now they'll need all of their ingenuity to escape the evil megacorporation that wants to own them

title: One Day in December
author: Josie Silver
description: After Laurie, a recent university graduate in London, spots the man of her dreams at a bus stop and vows to find him, her wish comes true: He returns to her life, only this time as Jack, her best friend Sarah's new boyfriend. For the sake of Sarah, Laurie puts her feelings on hold for a decade as she navigates her awkward new friendship with Jack and seeks satisfaction elsewhere.

title: Don't Hide the Madness: William S. Burroughs in Conversation with Allen Ginsberg
author: William S. Burroughs and Allen Ginsberg
description: Edited by the musician and poet Steven Taylor, this conversation between the two Beat icons was prompted by the London Observer assigning Ginsberg to interview Burroughs before the release of the David Cronenberg film of Burroughs’ novel Naked Lunch . Released here in full for the first time, the days-long discussion coincided with the shamanic exorcism of the demon Burroughs believed caused him to fatally shoot his common law wife, Joan Vollmer, in 1951.

title: An Unlikely Journey: Waking Up from My American Dream
author: Julian Castro
description: The keynote speaker at the 2012 DNC, former San Antonio mayor and Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, Julian Castro, tells his life story.

title: Creating Things That Matter: The Art and Science of Innovations That Last
author: David Edwards
description: Most things we create will not matter. This book is about creating things that do, from a master innovator who brings science and art together in his cutting-edge labs.

title: What We Owe
author: Golnaz Hashemzadeh Bonde, trans. by Elizabeth Clark Wessel
description: Winner of the Dayton Literary Peace Prize, What We Owe follows Nahid, who has six months left to live. At fifty, she is no stranger to loss. But now, as she stands on the precipice of her own death—just as she has learned that her daughter Aram is pregnant with her first child—Nahid is filled with both new fury and long dormant rage. Her life back home in Iran, and living as a refugee in Sweden, has been about survival at any cost. How to actually live, she doesn’t know; she has never had the ability or opportunity to learn.

title: Thin Rising Vapors
author: Seth Rogoff
description: Thin Rising Vapors is a novel about an enduring yet fragile friendship, and the allure of nature and faith.

title: The Man Who Wrote the Perfect Novel
author: Charles J. Shields
description: A biography of a nearly forgotten mid-20th-century American writer—John Williams, the author of Stoner , a novel little known in its day that has in recent years developed a cult following.

title: Simple Machines
author: Ian Morris
description: At summer’s end, Tom leaves for Madison where he falls in with an unusual and ultimately destructive crowd. As the book approaches a climax, friends from home Grey and Callie reappear with trouble of their own, and Tom is forced to choose between old loyalties and a new sense of belonging.`

title: That Was Something
author: Dan Callahan
description: This debut novel tells the story of Bobby Quinn, who looks back on his college years at New York University in the 1990s and his intense relationships with a wunderkind photographer and a beautiful cinephile femme fatale who is consumed by her love for silent-era films.

title: Professor at Large
author: John Cleese
description: In this probing collection of essays and lectures given during his tenure as Cornell University's 'professor at large,' Cleese reminds us that his intelligence and wit extend well beyond Monty Python and Fawlty Towers.

title: Demolition Night
author: Ross Barkan
description: Sundra Glassgarden is trapped in a world she desperately wants to change. Archie London trawls the city for secrets. Set in a dystopian future and 1970s New York, Demolition Night is a novel about love and destiny and technology's grim promise, about the utopias we can never have-and why we keep struggling anyway.

title: Duty to Warn
author: Sara Kersting
description: While treating Robert Percy, a burly factory worker, psychologist David Malden unlocks not only his patient’s memories of childhood abuse but also an upwelling violence. When Percy abruptly departs Buffalo for rural Michigan, where he grew up in a series of foster homes, Malden fears that his patient seeks revenge. Concerned with his liability under Duty to Warn laws, Malden sets out after the troubled young man.

title: The Writer's Map: An Atlas of Imaginary Lands
author: Ed. by Huw Lewis-Jones
description: An "atlas" of the worlds created by the West's most culturally significant fantasists—from medieval times through Harry Potter —this collection encompasses not only the maps themselves but essays on their imagining by the likes of David Mitchell and Cressida Cowell.

title: Wobble
author: Rae Armantrout
description: Poems written on the shifting ground of imminent systemic collapse.

title: Unnatural Habitats & Other Stories
author: Angela Mitchell
description: In this debut collection, seven connected stories set in the Ozarks explore the relationships between people, place, and the changing culture of rural America through the lens of characters involved in various shady or troubling predicaments.

title: Celestial Bodies
author: Jokha Alharthi, trans. by Marilyn Booth
description: Winner of the 2019 Man Booker International Prize, Celestial Bodies is set in the village of al-Awafi in Oman. We encounter three sisters: Mayya, who marries after a heartbreak; Asma, who marries from a sense of duty; and Khawla, who rejects all offers while waiting for her beloved. These three women and their families witness their home evolve from a traditional, slave-owning society to the crossroads of its complex present.

title: The Witch Elm
author: Tana French
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: A standalone thriller from the bestselling author of the Dublin Murder Squad series. Struggling to recover from his a brutal attack, beginning to understand that he might never be the same man again, Toby takes refuge at his family's ancestral home to care for his dying uncle Hugo. Then a skull is found in the trunk of an elm tree in the garden—and as detectives close in, Toby is forced to face the possibility that his past may not be what he has always believed.

title: Holy Ghost
author: John Sandford
description: The eleventh Virgil Flowers novel from bestselling thriller writer Sandford. A drolly fraudulent plan to reverse the fortunes of a declining Minnesota town hits a snag in the form of a much more serious spate of felonies, which warrants a call to the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension.

title: Killing Commendatore
author: Haruki Murakami, Trans. by Philip Gabriel and Ted Goossen
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Literary", "Literature in Translation"]
description: A labyrinthine, magical realist new novel from the acclaimed author of Kafka on the Shore and IQ84 . A thirty-something portrait painter in Tokyo is abandoned by his wife and finds himself holed up in the mountain home of a famous artist, Tomohiko Amada. When he discovers a previously unseen painting in the attic, he unintentionally opens a circle of mysterious circumstances.

title: The Souls of Yellow Folk: Essays
author: Wesley Yang
description: The National Magazine Award-winning writer's debut collection of essays on race and gender.

title: White Dancing Elephants
author: Chaya Bhuvaneswar
description: A woman grieves a miscarriage, haunted by the Buddha's birth. An artist with schizophrenia tries to survive hatred and indifference in small-town India by turning to the beauty of sculpture and dance. Orphans in India get pulled into a strange "rescue" mission aimed at stripping their mysterious powers. Winner of the 2017 Dzanc Short Story Collection Prize, White Dancing Elephants explores feminist, queer, religious, and immigrant stories.

title: Bitter Orange
author: Claire Fuller
description: In the latest from the author of Our Endless Numbered Days and Swimming Lessons , a dying woman looks back on a troubling summer 20 years earlier, in 1969, when her work researching the architecture and grounds of a decrepit mansion introduces her to an attractive bohemian couple that soon becomes her obsession.

title: November Road
author: Lou Berney
description: As a shocked nation mourns the assassination of John F. Kennedy, two lost souls looking for a new chance at life find each other along the wide-open Western highways.

title: The Clockmaker’s Daughter
author: Kate Morton
description: The story of a love affair and a mysterious murder that cast their shadows across generations, set in England from the 1860's until the present day.

title: Wrecked
author: Joe Ide
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: Isaiah Quintabe--IQ for short--has never been more successful, or felt more alone. A series of high-profile wins in his hometown of East Long Beach have made him so notorious that he can hardly go to the corner store without being recognized. So when a young painter approaches IQ for help tracking down her missing mother, it's not just the case Isaiah's looking for, but the human connection.

title: Mycroft and Sherlock
author: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Anna Waterhouse
description: It is 1872, and a series of gruesome murders is the talk of London. Mycroft Holmes--now twenty-six and a force to be reckoned with at the War Office--has no interest in the killings; however, his brother Sherlock has developed a distasteful fascination for the macabre to the detriment of his studies, much to Mycroft's frustration.

title: One Part Woman
author: Perumal Murugan, Trans. by Aniruddhan Vasudevan
description: Set in South India during the British colonial, One Part Woman tells the story of a couple, Kali and Ponna, who are unable to conceive, much to the concern of their families―and the crowing amusement of Kali’s male friends. Kali and Ponna try anything to have a child, including making offerings at different temples, atoning for past misdeeds of dead family members, and even circumambulating a mountain supposed to cure barren women, but all to no avail.

title: The Game
author: George Howe Colt
description: One of the most thrilling games in the history of college football serves as a window to the turbulent 1960s and as a mirror for our present.

title: Death in Paris
author: Emilia Bernhard
description: A pair of middle-aged Parisian expatriates investigate a death everyone thinks is accidental.

title: Invisible: The Forgotten Story of the Black Woman Lawyer Who Took Down America’s Most Powerful Mobster
author: Stephen L. Carter
description: The grandson of Eunice Hunton Carter tells the remarkable story of his grandmother's unlikely transcendence of racial barriers to be appointed to the New York City special prosecutor’s office, where she helped bring down the gangster Lucky Luciano in 1936.

title: The Invisible Emperor
author: Mark Braude
description: A history of Napoleon’s short first exile, rendered in short, punchy chapters.

title: The Next Person You Meet in Heaven
author: Mitch Albom
description: Albom returns to the scene of previous literary crime: heaven, that is, and the realm of departed folks who are only too glad to dispense advice.

title: Man With a Seagull on His Head
author: Harriet Paige
description: As Ray gazes at the sea, a woman in the distance suddenly turns to face him―and a dying seagull falls from the sky, knocking him unconscious. When Ray wakes up, he’s inexplicably compelled to paint the woman’s image, obsessively and repeatedly. Discovered by a power couple of Outsider Art, he becomes one of the most celebrated artists of the century.

title: Presidents of War
author: Michael Beschloss
description: From a preeminent presidential historian comes a saga of America’s wartime chief executives.

title: Godsend
author: John Wray
description: Inspired by the story of John Walker Lindh, the American Taliban, Whiting Award-winning author John Wray explores the circumstances that could impel a young American to abandon identity and home to become an Islamist militant.

title: Bridge of Clay
author: Markus Zusak
publisher: Alfred A. Knopf Books for Young Readers
description: The story of five brothers who bring each other up in a world run by their own rules. As the Dunbar boys love and fight and learn to reckon with the adult world, they discover the moving secret behind their father’s disappearance.

title: 99 Ways to Die (A Taipei Night Market Novel #3)
author: Ed Lin
description: In Taipei, Taiwan, the kidnapping of a Mainlander billionaire throws national media into a tizzy—not least because of the famous victim’s vitriolic anti-immigration politics.

title: The Reckonings: Essays
author: Lacy M. Johnson
description: From the author of the memoir The Other Side , this collection of 12 essays explores the concept of justice and its intersection with race, gender, class, environmentalism, and other complex subjects.

title: The Age of Walls: How Barriers Between Nations Are Changing Our World
author: Tim Marshall
description: Tim Marshall, the New York Times bestselling author of Prisoners of Geography , examines the borders, walls, and boundaries that divide countries and their populations.

title: My Squirrel Days
author: Ellie Kemper
description: Comedian and star of The Office and Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt Ellie Kemper examines her life and career in a series of essays.

title: Jerome Robbins: A Life in Dance
author: Wendy Lesser
description: The founder and editor of The Threepenny Review considers the life of this master choreographer, dancer, and stage director as well as offers analyses of some of his seminal works.

title: The Phoenix Empress
author: K Arsenault Rivera
description: K Arsenault Rivera's second novel, The Phoenix Empress , is the continuation of a new epic fantasy trilogy. As the Imperial Army gathers against a demonic invasion, Shizuka must do all she can with an empire on the brink of civil war.

title: Samuel Johnson's Eternal Return
author: Martin Riker
description: After he dies, Samuel Johnson inhabits one body after the next, waiting for a chance to return to his son.

title: Rainsongs
author: Sue Hubbard
description: An English woman’s journey to her dead husband’s Kerry summer cottage leads to a series of discoveries

title: Power Ball
author: Rob Neyer
description: The former ESPN columnist and analytics pioneer dramatically recreates an action-packed 2017 game between the Oakland A’s and eventual World Series Champion Houston Astros to reveal the myriad ways in which Major League Baseball has changed over the last few decades.

title: If You Ask Me: Essential Advice from Eleanor Roosevelt
author: Eleanor Roosevelt
description: A selection of letters from the First Lady's "If You Ask Me" advice column, which she began publishing in May 1941 in Ladies Home Journal and, later, in McCalls . Edited by Mary Jo Binker, these candid letters to and from average Americans living in the 1940s through the early 1960s grapple with issues ranging from civil rights, health care, and education to divorce, motherhood, and childrearing.

title: Interior States: Essays
author: Meghan O'Gieblyn
description: A collection that centers around two core (and related) issues of American identity: faith, in general and the specific forms Christianity takes in particular; and the challenges of living in the Midwest when culture is felt to be elsewhere.

title: The Big Book of the Dead
author: Marion Winik
description: The Big Book of the Dead , is a collection of portraits of the dead, their compressed narratives weaving a unusual, richly populated memoir.

title: White
author: Deni Ellis Bechard
description: Lost in his own misunderstanding of privilege and the myth of whiteness, a journalist trails Richmond Hew—one of the most nefarious figures in the conservation world—to the Congo, where he uncovers a tapestry of corruption, racial tensions, and his own complicity in colonial-historical oppression.

title: Open Your Eyes
author: Paula Daly
description: Paula Daly returns with a tale of domestic suspense that follows a bestselling crime novelist's tragic turn from fictional perpetrator into real-life victim.

title: Bright Ruin
author: Vic James
description: The rules are simple, the system cruel: the lower classes must give ten years in service to Britain’s powerfully gifted rulers. With one uprising crushed by the glittering elite, commoners and aristocrats alike now take sides for a final confrontation. Risking everything to end a bright and shining tyranny, Abi, Luke, and Silyen find themselves bound by a single destiny.

title: The Lies We Told
author: Camilla Way
description: The author of Watching Edie returns with a new novel of dark psychological suspense that explores how those closest to us have the most to hide.

title: In the Night Wood
author: Dale Bailey
description: In this contemporary fantasy, the grieving biographer of a Victorian fantasist finds himself slipping inexorably into the supernatural world that consumed his subject.

title: Crisis
author: Felix Francis
description: Francis’ latest attempt to find a new approach to skulduggery in the world of horse racing revolves around a hero who’d rather be anywhere else than solving a surprisingly old-fashioned whodunit.

title: The Corrosion of Conservatism: Why I Left the Right
author: Max Boot
description: Warning that the Trump presidency presages America's decline, the political commentator recounts his extraordinary journey from lifelong Republican to vehement Trump opponent.

title: Winter in Paradise
author: Elin Hilderbrand
description: A woman's seemingly idyllic life comes to a crashing halt when her husband dies on the Caribbean island of St. John, where she and her children discover his shocking secret—the other family he has managed to hide.

title: The Burn Zone: A Memoir
author: Renee Linnell
description: By the age of fifteen, Renee had lost almost everyone she loved; seeking answers, she set out on a quest for spiritual enlightenment and understanding—only to find herself entrenched in a Buddhist cult.

title: Behold, America: The Entangled History of "America First" and "The American Dream"
author: Sarah Churchwell
description: The author of Careless People: Murder, Mayhem, and the Invention of the Great Gatsby unpacks the rhetorical history of two phrases—the "American dream" and "America First"—that once embodied opposing visions for America that resonate in complicated ways with the present.

title: When You Find Me
author: P. J. Vernon
description: A psychological suspense about marriage and madness. Visiting her family’s South Carolina estate, socialite Gray Godfrey wakes from a night out to an empty bed. Her husband Paul is gone and a thrashing hangover has wiped her memory clean.

title: The League: How Five Rivals Created the NFL and Launched a Sports Empire
author: John Eisenberg
description: The author of That First Season and Ten-Gallon War takes a look back at the origins of the National Football League. Although it is a multibillion-dollar phenomenon today, the league was initially a risky venture by five owners who simultaneously competed against and supported one another to build a successful business.

title: In My Father’s House
author: Fox Butterfield
description: A pathbreaking examination of our huge crime and incarceration problem that looks at the influence of the family--specifically one Oregon family with a generations-long legacy of lawlessness.

title: The Cryotron Files
author: Iain Dey and Douglas Buck
description: The riveting true story of Dudley Buck, the American computer scientist whose pioneering work with microchips placed him firmly in the sights of the KGB

title: Beneath the Citadel
author: Destiny Soria
description: Cassa, the orphaned daughter of rebels, and friends Alys, Evander, and Newt, fight back against the high council of Eldra, which has ruled for centuries based solely on ancient prophesies.

title: The Future is Female
author: Lisa Yaszek
description: A story collection, edited by Yaszek, billing itself as a set of science-fiction classics written by women.

title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
author: Hazel Gaynor
description: A historical novel inspired by true events, and the extraordinary female lighthouse keepers of the past two hundred years.

title: Einstein's Shadow: A Black Hole, a Band of Astronomers, and the Quest to See the Unseeable
author: Seth Fletcher
description: The features editor at Scientific American traces the efforts of an elite scientific team who tested Einstein's theory of relativity during a historic mission to photograph a black hole, addressing key questions about time, space, and the nature of the universe.

title: Questioning Minds: The Letters of Guy Davenport and Hugh Kenner
author: Guy Davenport and Hugh Kenner
description: Edward M. Burns edits and annotates four decades' worth of correspondence between two friends who were among the most respected Modernist scholars of the 20th century.

title: Hearth: A Global Conversation on Identity, Community, and Place
author: Ed. by Annick Smith and Susan O'Connor
description: In this multicultural anthology of prose, poetry, and photography, esteemed artists consider the enduring importance and shifting associations of the hearth—a metaphor for what many seek in a time made uncertain by climate change, mass immigration, the refugee crisis, and the dislocating effects of technology.

title: Imagine John Yoko
author: John Lennon and Yoko Ono
description: Compiled and curated by Yoko Ono, this volume offers an intimate look into the making of John Lennon's classic Imagine album and the experiences that surrounded it during its recording in 1971.

title: The Waiter
author: Matias Faldbakken, trans. by Alice Menzies
description: Disturbances in the routines of an old restaurant unhinge the head waiter in this droll, understated debut novel by a Norwegian artist and writer.

title: Silicon City: San Francisco in the Long Shadow of the Valley
author: Cary McClelland
description: A portrait of San Francisco transformed by the tech boom.

title: Like a Sword Wound
author: Ahmet Altan
description: Here is a Turkish saga reminiscent of War and Peace , written in contemporary prose that traces not only the social currents of the time but also the erotic and emotional lives of its characters. The female characters in Altan's gripping saga will upend prejudices about Turkey, the Middle East, and Muslim nations.

title: Weather Woman
author: Cai Emmons
description: When an MIT Ph.D. student in atmospheric sciences decides to drop out and become a television meteorologist, she discovers she has the power to change the weather, raising questions about science and intuition, women and power, and what the earth needs from humans.

title: Four Soldiers
author: Hubert Mingarelli, trans. Sam Taylor
description: A novel of war, revolution, youth, and friendship by the French author of A Meal in Winter .

title: The Nationalist Revival: Trade, Immigration, and the Revolt Against Globalization
author: John B Judis
description: Political analyst John B. Judis investigates the question, 'Why Has Nationalism Come Roaring Back?'

title: Muhammad: Prophet of Peace Amid the Clash of Empires
author: Juan Cole
description: A University of Michigan history professor explores Islam and the Qur’an through the lens of the Prophet Muhammad, who he argues preached peace and inclusivity.

title: Mina
author: Kim Sagwa, trans. by Bruce Fulton & Ju-Chan Fulton
description: In her English debut, award-winning Korean author Kim Sagwa delivers a complex portrait of modern-day adolescence.

title: Not All Dead White Men: Classics and Misogyny in the Digital Age
author: Donna Zuckerberg
description: The editor-in-chief of the prize-winning online Classics magazine Eidolon explores—and seeks to debunk—the way Alt-Right men's groups have deployed superficial readings of ancient texts to justify a misogynist and white supremacist worldview.

title: Power, Pleasure, and Profit: Insatiable Appetites from Machiavelli to Madison
author: David Wootton
publisher: Belknap Press: An Imprint of Harvard University Press
description: A British history professor guides readers through four centuries of Western thought to show how new ideas about politics, ethics, and economics stepped into a gap opened up by religious conflict and the Scientific Revolution. As ideas about godliness and Aristotelian virtue faded, theories about the rational pursuit of power, pleasure, and profit moved to the fore.

title: The Patron Saint of Lost Girls
author: Maureen Aitken
description: Winner of the 2016 Nilsen Literary Prize for a First Novel, this set of linked stories follows Mary as she grows up in Detroit during the 1970s and 1980s, when the city experiences a downward turn into economic struggle and violence. Mary tries to conjure the spirits of protection to confront the social ills of her community, and she moves to cities across the Midwest looking for work and a better life.

title: If You See Me, Don’t Say Hi
author: Neel Patel
description: The 11 stories in Patel’s debut find his characters—mostly first-generation Indian-Americans; usually young, or youngish; often in Midwestern cities—navigating love, loss, and disappointment.

title: Ghosts in the Schoolyard
author: Eve L. Ewing
description: 'Failing schools. Underprivileged schools. Just plain bad schools.' Rooting her exploration in the historic African American neighborhood of Bronzeville, Ewing reveals that this issue is about much more than just schools.

title: The Beautiful Cure
author: Daniel M. Davis
description: The immune system holds the key to human health. In The Beautiful Cure , leading immunologist Daniel M. Davis describes how the scientific quest to understand how the immune system works.

title: Square Eyes
author: Luke Jones and Anna Mill
description: Set in a future in which the boundaries between memory, dreams, and the digital world start to blur, this graphic novel introduces readers to Fin—an inventor who gets kicked off her society's all-encompassing network after inventing a powerful new program that may be implicated in people's disappearances and other unsavory developments.

title: The Politics of Petulance: America in an Age of Immaturity
author: Alan Wolfe
description: A Boston College political science professor and the author of of One Nation, After All argues that Americans are mired in an age of political immaturity, one not grounded in any one ideology but rather in a failure to value character of would-be leaders, to accept the complexity of government and society, and to remain skeptical without being suspicious.

title: Gone So Long
author: Andre Dubus III
description: From the author of House of Sand and Fog , a novel about an ailing ex-convict in his 60s who pays a visit to the daughter he hasn't seen since the night he murdered her mother in a moment of jealous madness in 1973.

title: Virgil Wander
author: Leif Enger
description: The first novel in ten years from award-winning author Leif Enger, Virgil Wander follows the inhabitants of a Midwestern town in their quest to revive its flagging heart. Suffering from a concussion and possibly hallucinations after his car plunges into the icy Lake Superior, Virgil, the middle-aged town clerk and owner of a decrepit money pit of a movie theater, decides to take his emergence from the lake as a sign of rebirth.

title: A Spark of Light
author: Jodi Picoult
description: From the bestselling author of Small Great Things , a novel, told in reverse, about a hostage situation in a Mississippi women's health/abortion clinic.

title: All You Can Ever Know: A Memoir
author: Nicole Chung
description: Nicole Chung investigates the mysteries and complexities of her transracial adoption. A chronicle of unexpected family for anyone who has struggled to figure out where they belong.

title: Craving
author: Esther Gerritsen, Trans. by Michele Hutchison
description: The unconventional U.S. debut of prizewinning Dutch author Gerritsen. Diagnosed with a terminal illness, a mother known for her lack of empathy reunites with her daughter, but will the pair finally be able to connect?

title: There Will Be No Miracles Here
author: Casey Gerald
description: A memoir of a religious, gay black man coming to terms with his own nuanced achievement of the American dream in the new millennium.

title: Things to Make and Break
author: May-Lan Tan
description: These eleven short fictions evoke the microcosmic worlds every human relationship contains. In every one of these tales, we meet indelibly real and unforgettable people, a cast of rebels and dreamers trying to transform themselves, forge new destinies, or simply make the moment last.

title: The Ravenmaster: My Life with the Ravens at the Tower of London
author: Christopher Skaife
description: The first behind-the-scenes account of life with the legendary ravens at the world’s eeriest monument

title: On a Sunbeam
author: Tillie Walden
description: On a Sunbeam is a graphic novel about a girl who travels to the ends of the universe to find a long lost love, from acclaimed author Tillie Walden.

title: Good and Mad
author: Rebecca Traister
description: In this resounding polemic against political, cultural, and personal injustices in America, Traister studies women’s anger as a tool for change.

title: Full Disclosure
author: Stormy Daniels
description: Stormy Daniels tells her whole story for the first time: what it's like to be a leading actress and director in the adult film business, her journey from a rough childhood in Louisiana onto the national stage, and her interaction with Donald Trump that led to the nondisclosure agreement and behind-the-scenes attempts to intimidate her.

title: Reagan: An American Journey
author: Bob Spitz
description: A young man is born into poverty and raised in a series of flyspeck towns in the Midwest by a pious mother and an alcoholic, largely absent father. From there, the path is only very dimly lit, but it leads him, thanks to his great charm and greater luck, to a career as a radio sportscaster, and then, a, fatefully, to Hollywood. And the rest, as they say, is history.

title: Firefly
author: Henry Porter
description: From the refugee camps of Greece to the mountains of Macedonia, a thirteen-year-old boy is making his way to Germany and to safety. Codenamed “Firefly,” he holds vital intelligence: unparalleled insight into a vicious ISIS terror cell, and details of their plans. But the terrorists are hot on his trail, determined he won’t live to pass on the information.

title: Impossible Owls: Essays
author: Brian Phillips
description: A globe-spanning book of essays that chronicle some of the modern world’s most uncanny, unbelievable, and spectacular oddities.

title: A History of France
author: John Julius Norwich
description: An eminent British historian weaves a vivid tapestry of France’s past.

title: On Desperate Ground: The Marines at the Reservoir, the Korean War's Greatest Battle
author: Hampton Sides
description: From the New York Times bestselling author of Ghost Soldiers and In the Kingdom of Ice , a chronicle of the extraordinary feats of heroism by Marines called on to do the impossible during the greatest battle of the Korean War.

title: The Fifth Risk
author: Michael Lewis
description: Lewis turns timely political reporting he published in Vanity Fair into a book about federal government bureaucracies during the first year of the Donald Trump presidency.

title: The Conspiracy Against the Human Race: A Contrivance of Horror
author: Thomas Ligotti
description: His fiction is known to be some of the most terrifying in the genre of supernatural horror, but Thomas Ligotti's first nonfiction book may be even scarier. Drawing on philosophy, literature, neuroscience, and other fields of study, Ligotti takes the lens of his imagination and turns it on his audience, causing them to grapple with the brutal reality that they are living a meaningless nightmare, and anyone who feels otherwise is simply acting out an optimistic fallacy.

title: 1,000 Books to Read Before You Die
author: James Mustich
description: Discover new titles in a book that’s as compulsively readable, entertaining, surprising, and enlightening as the 1,000-plus titles it recommends.

title: Behind the Throne
author: Adrian Tinniswood
description: From bedchambers to ballrooms, a revealing portrait of daily life among the royals.

title: Fame
author: Justine Bateman
description: Now in her early 50s, the actress best known as a teenager on Family Ties lashes back at the distortions and toxicity of celebrity-obsessed culture.

title: Belonging: A German Reckons with History and Home
author: Nora Krug
description: Winner of the 2019 National Book Critics Circle Award for Autobiography, a graphic memoir by award-winning artist Nora Krug, telling the story of her attempt to confront the hidden truths of her family’s wartime past in Nazi Germany and to comprehend the forces that have shaped her life, her generation, and history.

title: The Greatest Love Story Ever Told
author: Nick Offerman and Megan Mullally
description: In an oral history that reads like playful conversation, two popular TV stars discuss how they came together and stayed together.

title: News of Our Loved Ones
author: Abigail DeWitt
description: Set in France and America, News of Our Loved Ones is an examination of love and loss, beauty and the cost of survival, witnessed through two generations of one French family, whose lives are all touched by the tragic events surrounding the D-Day bombings in Normandy.

title: Priest of Bones (War of the Rose Throne, Book One)
author: Peter McLean
description: The war is over, and army priest Tomas Piety heads home with Sergeant Bloody Anne at his side. But things have changed while he was away: his crime empire has been stolen and the people of Ellinburg—his people—have run out of food and hope and places to hide. Tomas sets out to reclaim what was his with help from Anne, his brother, Jochan, and his new gang: the Pious Men. But when he finds himself dragged into a web of political intrigue once again, everything gets more complicated.

title: Always Look on the Bright Side of Life: A Sortabiography
author: Eric Idle
description: From the beloved comic performer, founding member of Monty Python, and creator of Spamalot comes a memoir about growing up in post-war England, the road to an illustrious career in comedy, and the friends he met along the way.

title: Storm Lake: A Chronicle of Change, Resilience, and Hope from a Heartland Newspaper
author: Art Cullen
description: From a 2017 Pulitzer-winning newspaperman, an ode to America's heartland as seen in small-town Iowa—a story of reinvention and resilience, environmental and economic struggle, and surprising diversity and hope.

title: Seven Types of Atheism
author: John Gray
description: The Oxford philosopher offers a critique of atheism, which, in its various iterations, tends to emulate the same problematic ideas atheists condemn in Judeo-Christian religions.

title: An Easy Death
author: Charlaine Harris
description: In the opening novel of Harris' new series, set in a dangerous and largely lawless alternate United States, a young gunslinger for hire hits the trail to track down a descendant of Rasputin.

title: Becoming Mrs. Lewis
author: Patti Callahan
description: Patti Callahan seems to have found the story she was born to tell in this tale of unlikely friendship turned true love between Joy Davidman and C. S. Lewis, that tests the bounds of faith and radically alters both of their lives.

title: A History of America in Ten Strikes
author: Erik Loomis
description: A fresh history of American labor and the strikes that resulted from companies’ mistreatment of workers.

title: The Red and the Blue
author: Steve Kornacki
description: From MSNBC correspondent Steve Kornacki, a sweeping history of the birth of political tribalism in the 1990s—one that brings critical new understanding to our current political landscape from Clinton to Trump

title: The Flame
author: Leonard Cohen
description: The Flame is the final work from Leonard Cohen, featuring poems, excerpts from his private notebooks, lyrics, and hand-drawn self-portraits, The Flame offers an unprecedentedly intimate look inside the life and mind of a singular artist.

title: On Sunset
author: Kathryn Harrison
description: A notable novelist and nonfiction writer’s account of the once-wealthy grandparents who raised her and their fall from financial grace.

title: Under My Skin
author: Lisa Unger
description: It’s been a year since Poppy’s husband, Jack, was brutally murdered during his morning run through Manhattan’s Riverside Park. In the immediate aftermath, Poppy spiraled into an oblivion of grief, disappearing for several days only to turn up ragged and confused wearing a tight red dress she didn’t recognize.

title: The Sadness of Beautiful Things
author: Simon Van Booy
description: Stories of brief bonds forged in unlikely places, from the Frank O'Connor Short Story Award-winning author.

title: The Night In Question
author: Nic Joseph
description: A ride-share driver might make much more than her usual fare in this humorous Chicago-based thriller.

title: City of Light: The Making of Modern Paris
author: Rupert Christiansen
description: The story of how one of the world's most beloved cities was transformed in the mid-19th century from an industrial enclave to the architectural jewel we know today.

title: False Calm: A Journey Through the Ghost Towns of Patagonia
author: Maria Sonia Cristoff, trans. by Katherine Silver
description: Part reportage, part personal essay, part travelogue, False Calm explores Patagonia’s complicated legacy through the lost stories of its people and the desolate places they inhabit.

title: What If This Were Enough?: Essays
author: Heather Havrilesky
description: By the critic, memoirist, and advice columnist behind "Ask Polly," a collection of essays tackling our obsession with self-improvement and urging readers to embrace the imperfections of the everyday

title: Gandhi: The Years That Changed the World, 1914-1948
author: Ramachandra Guha
description: In the second of Guha's two-volume biography of Gandhi, the Indian political icon enters epic struggles to deliver India from British rule, to forge harmonious relations between India's Hindu and Muslim populations, to end the pernicious Hindu practice of untouchability, and to develop India's economic and moral self-reliance.

title: Alaskan Holiday
author: Debbie Macomber
description: Debbie Macomber brings us to the Alaskan wilderness for a magical Christmas tale about finding love where it’s least expected.

title: Blood Communion: A Tale of Prince Lestat
author: Anne Rice
description: Part of The Vampire Chronicles, Blood Communion tells the story of Lestat and the formation of the Blood Communion.

title: So Far So Good
author: Ursula K Le Guin
description: Redolent of myths, history, nursery rhymes, and the natural world, Le Guin bookends a long, daring, and prolific career in this final book of verse.

title: What's Left of the Night
author: Ersi Sotiropoulos, Trans. by Karen Emmerich
description: A novel based on the visit to Paris by C.P. Cavafy, one of the 20th century's greatest poets, filled with lyrical observations and infused with erotic desire.

title: Once and Forever: The Tales of Kenji Miyazawa
author: Kenji Miyazawa, Trans. by John Bester
description: In this re-release of a 1993 English collection of stories, one of Japan's most beloved writers and poets weaves strangely magical tales—with roots in Japanese folklore and European fairy-tales—that deal with corruption, bad luck, and some other of life's darker forces.

title: The Apprentice: Trump, Russia and the Subversion of American Democracy
author: Greg Miller
description: From two-time Pulitzer Prize–winning Washington Post national security reporter Greg Miller, the truth about Vladimir Putin’s covert attempt to destroy Hillary Clinton and help Donald Trump win the presidency, its possible connections to the Trump campaign, Robert Mueller’s ensuing investigation of the president and those close to him, and the mystery of Trump’s steadfast allegiance to Putin.

title: Scribe
author: Alyson Hagy
description: A dystopian novel about the power of storytelling. When a brutal civil war ravages the country, and contagious fever has decimated the population, a woman ekes out a lonely living on the family farmstead by bartering her letter-writing skills.

title: Dracul
author: Dacre Stoker & J. D. Barker
description: A prequel to the Gothic classic Dracula , based on original author notes and co-written by a family descendant, reveals the iconic vampire's origin story, the early years of Bram Stoker, and the tale of the enigmatic woman who connected them.

title: Kill the Queen
author: Jennifer Estep
description: Seventeenth in line for the throne and without obvious magical powers, Lady Everleigh hides in the shadows of the royal court of Bellona, a kingdom steeped in gladiator tradition. But when her cousin Vasilia takes the throne by force and massacres the royal family, Lady Everleigh survives, builds her magical powers, and joins a gladiator troupe in the first series installment of A Crown of Shards .

title: The Search for Atlantis: A History of Plato's Ideal State
author: Steve P. Kershaw
description: An exploration of the legend of Atlantis and its enduring influence on Western culture—from its origins in antiquity to the modern era.

title: Jean Harley Was Here
author: Heather Taylor Johnson
description: When a beloved woman dies, she leaves behind grief-stricken family and friends, each of whom has a unique perspective on her character and life.

title: The Forgotten: How the People of One Pennsylvania County Elected Donald Trump and Changed America
author: Ben Bradlee Jr.
description: The Boston Globe reporter visits Luzerne County, Pennsylvania—a Democratic stronghold that voted for Barack Obama in two Presidential elections but went for Donald J. Trump in 2016—to see what sparked such a turnabout and its implications for the future of the country.

title: Zero Sum Game
author: S.L. Huang
description: Cas Russell wields math as a superpower: The vector calculus blazing through her head lets her smash through armed men twice her size and dodge every bullet in a gunfight. But does she stand a chance against someone with a power that rivals her own, someone who is intent on becoming the world’s puppet master?

title: War of the Wolf
author: Bernard Cornwell
description: Bernard Cornwell’s epic story of the making of England continues in this eleventh installment in the bestselling Saxon Tales series—the basis of the Netflix television series The Last Kingdom .

title: Paradise Rot
author: Jenny Hval, Trans. by Marjam Idriss
description: A lyrical debut novel from a musician and artist renowned for her sharp sexual and political imagery.

title: Anne Frank's Diary: The Graphic Adaptation
author: Anne Frank
description: The only graphic adaptation of Frank's diary authorized by the Anne Frank Foundation. It remains faithful to the original, while the illustrations interpret and add layers of visual meaning this classic work of Holocaust literature.

title: The Collected Stories of Diane Williams
author: Diane Williams
description: With an introduction by Ben Marcus, this volume collects over three hundred new and previously published short, or "flash," fictions—distilled works examining moments, characters, relationships, and innuendo.

title: The Best of the Best Horror of the Year: 10 Years of Essential Short Horror Fiction
author: Edited by Ellen Datlow
description: Selections from the first decade of Ellen Datlow's annual Best Horror of the Year anthology series are collected in a single anniversary volume.

title: Devil's Day
author: Andrew Michael Hurley
description: The Costa award-winning author of The Loney offers another unsettling tale, this time set in the Endlands moors, where a man returns with his pregnant wife to inherit his family farm and encounters the evil that haunts the community where he grew up.

title: Hitler's American Friends: The Third Reich's Supporters in the United States
author: Bradley W. Hart
description: This look back at the United States in the years preceding World War II shines a spotlight on the historically ignored—though politically significant—group of homegrown antagonists that sought to protect and promote Hitler, leave Europeans (and especially European Jews) to fend for themselves, and elevate the Nazi regime.

title: The Stranger Game
author: Peter Gadol
description: "The stranger game" involves choosing someone out of a crowd and following them, an initially digital pastime that has entered the real world and lead to disappearances—including Rebecca's boyfriend Ezra, whom she emulates by trying the game for herself.

title: The Dream Daughter
author: Diane Chamberlain
description: The bestselling author of Necessary Lies and other novels offers a time-traveling tale in which protagonist Carly Sears moves between the Vietnam War era and 2001 in search of a way to save her baby's life.

title: Even Darkness Sings: From Auschwitz to Hiroshima: Finding Hope and Optimism in the Saddest Places on Earth
author: Thomas H. Cook
description: The Edgar Award-winning crime novelist tries his hand at a memoir-in-essays that takes him to locations across the globe where humans have suffered deeply and committed some of the worst atrocities in history.

title: Exit Strategy: The Murderbot Diaries
author: Martha Wells
description: In the fourth installment of the Hugo, Nebula, Alex, and Locus award-winning Murderbot Diaries series, Murderbot manages to defy its own programming and decides to help the only human who ever showed it respect.

title: Dominion
author: Peter Ackroyd
description: The fifth volume in the acclaimed author’s history of England.

title: We Are the Nerds: The Birth and Tumultuous Life of Reddit, the Internet's Culture Laboratory
author: Christine Lagorio-Chafkin
description: Reddit hails itself as 'the front page of the Internet.' It's the third most-visited website in the United States. Based on Christine Lagorio-Chafkin's exclusive access to Reddit's founders, this is its story.

title: The Hollow of Fear
author: Sherry Thomas
description: In the third installment of her "Lady Sherlock" series, Charlotte Holmes investigates the death of her dear friend Lord Ingram's wife while Scotland Yard closes in on its prime suspect—Ingram himself.

title: A Dream Called Home: A Memoir
author: Reyna Grande
description: After her first memoir, The Distance Between Us , was named a finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award, Reyna Grande offers a followup describing her journey from the precarious life of an undocumented youth to the achievement of her dream of being celebrated author.

title: My Darling Winston: The Letters Between Winston Churchill and His Mother
author: Edited by David Lough
description: An edited collection of the personal letters between Winston Churchill and his mother, Jenny Jerome, between 1881—when Churchill was just six—and 1921, the year of Jerome's death. Many published for the first time, the letters offer insight into one of the 20th century's most admired—and reviled—figures as well as the outsized personality of his mother, who was a powerful force in her own right.

title: The Second Rider
author: Alex Beer, Trans. by, Tim Mohr
description: A deeply satisfying debut novel by the new star of Austrian crime fiction.

title: The Last Breath
author: Danny Lopez
description: Unemployed newspaper reporter Dexter Vega is hired to investigate the drowning of Liam Fleming, the son of a wealthy real estate investor in Siesta Key.

title: Under the Knife: A History of Surgery in 28 Remarkable Operations
author: Arnold van de Laar, Trans. by Andy Brown
description: Surgeon Arnold van de Laar uses his own experience and expertise to tell this engrossing history of surgery through 28 famous operations―from Louis XIV and Einstein to JFK and Houdini.

title: The Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy 2018
author: Ed. by N.K. Jemisin
description: Jemisin, the latest guest editor for this series, has chosen stories with themes similar to the ones that appear in her own short story collection, How Long ’til Black Future Month? .

title: Moon of the Crusted Snow
author: Waubgeshig Rice
description: A daring post-apocalyptic novel from a powerful rising literary voice

title: Anaphora
author: Kevin Goodan
description: Goodan creates a heightened, frantic and piercing dialogue that grapples with mental illness, stigmas, relationships, and morality in the landscape of rural America.

title: Best of Enemies: The Last Great Spy Story of the Cold War
author: Eric Dezenhall and Gus Russo
description: The story of the improbable friendship between two Cold War spies, CIA case officer Jack Platt and KGB agent Gennady Vasilenko, as well as an exploration of the distinctions between the Russian and American methods of conducting espionage and the painful birth of the new Russia, whose leader, Vladimir Putin, dreams he can roll back to the ideals of the old USSR.

title: A Knife in the Fog
author: Bradley Harper
description: Sherlock Holmes’ creator and a crusading British journalist team up to hunt for Jack the Ripper.

title: Classic American Crime Fiction of the 1920s
author: Edited by Leslie S. Klinger
description: The Edgar-winning anthologist collects and annotates five of the most famous crime novels of the 1920s, presenting anew some of the most admired authors of the era.

title: Out of Season
author: Antonio Manzini, Trans. by Antony Shugaar
description: In the latest installment of the Italian bestselling author's series about Deputy Police Chief Rocco Schiavone, Rocco investigates a high-profile kidnapping while dealing with other big problems—a prison escapee who is out for revenge and confusion in the bedroom.

title: For Colored Girls Who Have Considered Politics
author: Donna Brazile, Yolanda Caraway, Leah Daughtry, Minyon Moore, and Veronica Chambers
description: Four women who call themselves The Colored Girls—and have worked behind the scenes in national politics for over 30 years—describe their journeys into public service that took them to positions on the Presidential campaigns of Jesse Jackson, Walter Mondale, Michael Dukakis, Bill Clinton, Al Gore, Barack Obama, and Hillary Rodham Clinton.

title: LikeWar: The Weaponization of Social Media
author: Emerson T. Brooking and P.W. Singer
description: Two defense experts describe how social media has been weaponized by state hackers and rogue terrorists who have seized upon Twitter and Facebook to create chaos and destruction.

title: Consumed
author: J.R. Ward
description: A Massachusetts firefighter injured on the job finds new purpose as an arson investigator and discovers that looking for the sources of fires can be just as dangerous as trying to put them out.

title: The Warm South: How the Mediterranean Shaped the British Imagination
author: Robert Holland
description: An exploration of the impact of the Mediterranean on British culture, ranging from the mid-eighteenth century to today.

title: Heresy
author: Melissa Lenhardt
description: In this novel told through journal entries, interviews, and newspaper columns, uncover the hidden history of America's first and only all-female gang in the American West.

title: Art Comic
author: Matthew Thurber
description: A skewering of the art world as told by an author familiar with absurdity.

title: Mad Scenes and Exit Arias: The Death of the New York City Opera and the Future of Opera in America
author: Heidi Waleson
description: From the Wall Street Journal 's opera critic, a wide-ranging narrative history of how and why the New York City Opera went bankrupt―and what it means for the future of the arts.

title: Flyover Country: Poems
author: Austin Smith
description: A new collection about violence and the rural Midwest.

title: Museum of the Americas
author: J Michael Martinez
description: Winner of the 2017 National Poetry Series Competition, selected by Cornelius Eady—an exploration in verse of imperial appropriation and Mexican American cultural identity

title: That Thin, Wild Mercury Sound: Dylan, Nashville, and the Making of Blonde on Blonde
author: Daryl Sanders
description: A Nashville music journalist explores the making of the album that put his city on the rock-music map, setting the record straight on much of the misinformation surrounding the story of how Dylan's masterpiece came to be made by drawing on many eyewitness accounts never before published.

title: Hey, Marfa: Poems
author: Jeffrey Yang
description: A lyric and visual meditation on place, nature, and art rippling out from Marfa, Texas

title: Valley Forge
author: Bob Drury
description: The #1 New York Times bestselling authors of The Heart of Everything That Is return with one of the most underappreciated chapters in American history: the story of the Continental Army’s six-month transformation in Valley Forge.

title: The So Blue Marble
author: Dorothy B. Hughes
description: In this reissue of the 1940 debut of one of the 20th century's most respected mystery writers, three well-heeled villains terrorize New York's high society in pursuit of a rare and powerful gem.

title: The Lost History of Liberalism: From Ancient Rome to the Twenty-First Century
author: Helena Rosenblatt
description: A history professor at the Graduate Center, City University of New York debunks the popular myth of liberalism as a uniquely Anglo-American tradition centered on individual rights. She shows that it was the French Revolution that gave birth to liberalism and Germans who transformed it.

title: The Taiga Syndrome
author: Cristina Rivera Garza, trans. by Jill Levine and Aviva Kana
description: A fairy tale run amok, The Taiga Syndrome follows an unnamed female Ex-Detective as she searches for a couple who has fled to the far reaches of the earth.

title: You've Been So Lucky Already: A Memoir
author: Alethea Black
description: From the author of the short-fiction collection I Knew You’d Be Lovely comes a memoir about grief and illness—and the wit and wisdom it takes to survive it.

title: Empire of Enchantment
author: John Zubrzycki
description: Drawing on ancient religious texts, early travelers' accounts, colonial records, modern visual sources, and magicians' own testimony, Empire of Enchantment is a vibrant narrative of India's magical traditions, from Vedic times to the present day.

title: Wild Milk
author: Sabrina Orah Mark
description: Mark turns her poet's eye to the sublimely surreal in this collection of domestic oddities.

title: Love Songs for a Lost Continent
author: Anita Felicelli
description: From the glittering heat of India's Pink City to the palm-lined streets of Silicon Valley and the vanilla-bean fields of Madagascar, this debut story collection explores characters searching for identity in the seemingly narrow spaces of their everyday lives.

title: River Bodies
author: Karen Katchur
description: In this series opener, an emotionally vulnerable woman is drawn back to her hometown—right into the middle of a murder investigation.

title: Wilde Stories 2018: The Year's Best Gay Speculative Fiction
author: Steve Berman
description: The eleventh and final volume in the series that offered readers the best gay-themed stories of the strange, uncanny, and fantastical. Work by such authors as Richard Bowes, Sam J. Miller, Sean Eads, and John Chu.

title: At Dusk
author: Hwang Sok-yong Trans. by Sora Kim-Russell
description: In the evening of his life, a wealthy man begins to wonder if he might have missed the point.

title: The Twenty-Seventh Letter of the Alphabet: A Memoir
author: Kim Adrian
description: As her aging mother plunges into ever-deeper realms of drug-fueled paranoia and mental illness, Adrian excavates memories of her troubled childhood by cataloguing memories, anecdotes, and bits of family lore in the form of a glossary.

title: Future Politics: Living Together in a World Transformed by Tech
author: Jamie Susskind
description: A lawyer and past Fellow of Harvard University's Berkman Center for Internet and Society argues that rapid and relentless innovation in a range of technologies—from artificial intelligence to virtual reality—will increase the control large corporate tech companies have over our lives, challenging readers to rethink concepts of freedom, power, property, and democracy while recommending ways to regain control.

title: Theophrastus' Characters: An Ancient Take on Bad Behavior
author: James Romm, Trans. by Pamela Mensch
description: The more things change, the more they stay the same: Theophrastus' Characters , a classical Greek text newly translated for a modern audience, is a festival of fault-finding.

title: Oranges
author: Gary Eldon Peter
description: Winner of the Many Voices Project Competition by New Rivers Press, this collection of linked short stories follows Michael Dolin, a gay man whose life and loves are shaped by the AIDS crisis, Midwestern social strictures, and limiting expectations for men.

title: Down Along the Piney: Ozarks Stories
author: John Mort
description: This winner of the Richard Sullivan Prize in Short Fiction from the University of Notre Dame—the author's fourth short-story collection—portrays the unsung, amusing, brutal, yet hopeful lives of ordinary people from Florida, California, Mexico, Chicago, the Texas Panhandle, and the Ozarks.

title: Night Moves
author: Jessica Hopper
description: Written in taut, mesmerizing, often hilarious scenes, Night Moves captures the fierce friendships and small moments that form us all. Drawing on her personal journals from the aughts, Jessica Hopper chronicles her time as a DJ, living in decrepit punk houses, biking to bad loft parties with her friends, exploring Chicago deep into the night.

title: Transcription
author: Kate Atkinson
description: A WWII novel from the author of Life After Life and A God in Ruins . Juliet Armstrong is 18 years old and all alone in the world when she’s recruited by MI5 to transcribe meetings of British citizens sympathetic to the Nazi cause. Soon, she’s pulled even deeper into the world of espionage, a world she will ultimately discover is hard to escape.

title: The Shape of the Ruins
author: Juan Gabriel Vasquez, Trans. by Anne McClean
description: In this auto-fictional novel from the author of The Sound of Things Falling , a man is arrested at a museum for attempting to steal the bullet-ridden suit of a murdered Colombian politician, few notice. But soon this thwarted theft takes on greater meaning as it becomes a thread in a widening web of popular fixations with conspiracy theories, assassinations, and historical secrets—on that haunts those who feel they know the truth behind these killings.

title: Waiting for Eden
author: Elliot Ackerman
description: Wounded terribly in an explosion in Iraq three years ago (an explosion which killed his friend, the novel's narrator), a soldier awaits his death in a burn center in San Antonio as his wife grieves and agonizes over whether or not he should be taken off life support.

title: The Caregiver
author: Samuel Park
description: A novel about a young Brazilian woman arrives undocumented in Los Angeles, where she becomes a home caregiver for a patient dying of cancer who dredges up painful memories of her mother.

title: An Absolutely Remarkable Thing
author: Hank Green
description: The comic debut novel from popular vlogger, musician, and educator Green combines science fiction and mystery with philosophical musings about the perils of internet fame. A young graphic artist inspires worldwide hysteria when she accidentally makes first contact with an alien.

title: Beautiful Country Burn Again
author: Ben Fountain
description: In a work of reportage set over the course of 2016, the author of Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk recounts a surreal year of politics and an exploration of the third American existential crisis.

title: Your Duck Is My Duck
author: Deborah Eisenberg
description: From the author of Twilight of the Superheroes and winner of the PEN/Faulkner Award-winner comes a new short story collection which focuses on the wayward lives and tragic vanities of upper-class Americans.

title: The King and the Catholics
author: Antonia Fraser
description: Acclaimed popular historian and novelist Fraser rehearses the half-century of maneuvering that culminated in the 1829 liberation of English and Irish Catholics from crushing de jure discrimination.

title: The Poison Squad
author: Deborah Blum
description: A history of the late-19th-century crusade for food safety, led by a pioneering scientist who fought hard against 'chemically enhanced and deceptive food manufacturing practices,' some of which we still see today.

title: Hiking With Nietzsche
author: John Kaag
description: A philosopher’s journey into the life, writings, and mountains of Nietzsche—and ultimately into himself.

title: The Lady is Daring
author: Megan Frampton
description: Lady Olivia refuses to repeat her siblings’ scandalous mistakes. Instead, she will marry the lord rejected by her sister and help with his good works. When he resists, Olivia forms another plan: win his lordship’s admiration by helping his illegitimate best friend find a bride.

title: A Notorious Vow: The Four Hundred Series
author: Joanna Shupe
description: With the fate of her disgraced family resting on her shoulders, Lady Christina Barclay has arrived in New York City from London to quickly secure a wealthy husband. But when her parents settle on an intolerable suitor, Christina turns to her reclusive neighbor, a darkly handsome and utterly compelling inventor, for help.

title: The Order of the Day
author: Eric Vuillard, Trans. by, Mark Polizzotti
description: Winner of the Prix Goncourt in 2017, a behind-the-scenes account of the manipulation, hubris, and greed that together led to Nazi Germany’s annexation of Austria.

title: The Sisters of the Winter Wood
author: Rena Rossner
description: In a mix of historical fiction and fantasy, Rossner's debut weaves a richly detailed story of Jewish identity and sisterhood.

title: Ninth Street Women: Lee Krasner, Elaine de Kooning, Grace Hartigan, Joan Mitchell, and Helen Frankenthaler: Five Painters and the Movement
author: Mary Gabriel
description: A chronicle of five women who dared to enter the male-dominated world of 20th century abstract painting—not as muses but as artists. From their cold-water lofts, where they worked, drank, fought, and loved, these pioneers burst open the door to the art world for themselves and countless others to come.

title: Life in Culture
author: Lionel Trilling and Adam Kirsch
description: A generous sampling of letters that displays the rich intellectual life of mid-20th-century America’s leading critic as well as his staunchly even temperament and many second thoughts.

title: The Beggar and Other Stories
author: Gaito Gazdanov, trans. by Bryan Karetnyk
description: Translated for the first time, several short stories by Gaito Gazdanov, author of The Spectre of Alexander Wolf .

title: Who Is Michael Ovitz?
author: Michael Ovitz
