title: Whistle in the Dark
author: Emma Healey
description: When a teenage girl turns up four days after disappearing, unable or unwilling to say what happened while she was gone, her mother struggles to unravel the mystery of her absence and connect with her troubled daughter.

title: Only to Sleep: A Philip Marlowe Novel
author: Lawrence Osborne
description: Philip Marlowe returns in a 1980s Mexico-set novel, commissioned by the Raymond Chandler estate, by acclaimed British writer and journalist Obsourne.

title: The Briefing: Politics, the Press, and the President
author: Sean Spicer
description: A first-hand, behind-the-scenes account of Sean Spicer's tenure as President Trump's press secretary, shedding new light on the controversies of the Trump administration's first year.

title: Mary B: A Novel: An Untold Story of Pride and Prejudice
author: Katherine J Chen
description: In this debut novel, the plain and overlooked Mary Bennet of Jane Austen's beloved Pride and Prejudice gets to tell her own story, which is filled with all the love and excitement she lacked in the 19th century original.

title: A Noise Downstairs
author: Linwood Barclay
description: A college professor thinks his typewriter may be possessed and connected with a murderer, but his wife and therapist fear he may be losing his mind.

title: Hits and Misses: Stories
author: Simon Rich
description: A collection of comic stories inspired by a former Saturday Night Live writer's real experiences in Hollywood, chronicling the absurdity of fame and the humanity of failure in a world dominated by social media influencers and reality TV stars.

title: Ghosted
author: Rosie Walsh
description: Sarah thinks she has met the love of her life—until he disappears after leaving for a long-booked vacation, setting Sarah off on a mission to find him.

title: The Last Thing I Told You
author: Emily Arsenault
description: A psychological thriller about the murder of a psychologist in a quiet New England town, told from an unreliable former patient.

title: America for Beginners
author: Leah Franqui
description: A prim widow from India travels to California—in the company of a guileless but resourceful Bangladeshi immigrant and an struggling young East Coast actress—to learn the truth about what happened to the son who was declared dead shortly after he revealed his sexual orientation to their traditional family.

title: You're on an Airplane: A Self-Mythologizing Memoir
author: Parker Posey
description: Parker Posey opens up about the art of acting, life on the set, and the realities of its accompanying fame.

title: How to Love a Jamaican: Stories
author: Alexia Arthurs
description: Sweeping from close-knit island communities of Jamaica to the streets of New York City and Midwestern university towns, these eleven stories form a portrait of a nation, a people, and a way of life.

title: Killing It: An Education
author: Camas Davis
description: Camas Davis tells her unexpected journey from knowing magazine editor to humble butcher.

title: Annex (The Violet Wars)
author: Rich Larson
description: The story of two young outsiders who must find a way to fight back against the aliens who have taken over their city.

title: Jell-O Girls: A Family History
author: Allie Rowbottom
description: A memoir about one of America's most iconic products told from one of the inheritors of the massive wealth it's created since 1899, when the author's relative bought the patent and perhaps got more than he bargained for—a family "cursed" by tragedy and generations of women molded by the company's patriarchal advertisements.

title: I Can't Date Jesus: Love, Sex, Family, Race, and Other Reasons I've Put My Faith in Beyoncé
author: Michael Arceneaux
description: In the style of New York Times bestsellers You Can’t Touch My Hair , Bad Feminist , and I’m Judging You , a collection of alternately hysterical and soul‑searching essays about what it is like to grow up as a creative, sensitive black man in a world that constantly tries to deride and diminish your humanity.

title: Now My Heart Is Full: A Memoir
author: Laura June
description: In Now My Heart is Full , Laura June explores how raising her daughter forced her to confront this tragic legacy and recognize the connective tissue that binds generations of women together. As she documents in beautiful and irreverent prose the pain and joy of raising a child, Laura shows how, even a generation later, we still do not have the language to fully discuss the change that a woman undergoes when she becomes a parent and finds that, to her surprise, she has more in common with her mother than she ever knew.

title: Inappropriation
author: Lexi Freiman
description: A riotous, wildly irreverent coming of age story about a late bloomer's search for identity and acceptance amid the social, sexual, and technological challenges of our modern era.

title: The Desert and the Sea: 977 Days Captive on the Somali Pirate Coast
author: Michael Scott Moore
description: Michael Scott Moore's memoir of his three years of being held captive by Somali pirates.

title: Pretend We Live Here
author: Genevieve Hudson
description: Genevieve Hudson explores the idea of home and what it means to find one: in the body, in the world, in other people.

title: Tooth and Nail: The Making of a Female Fight Doctor
author: Linda D. Dahl
description: The memoir of surgeon Linda D. Dahl and how she became the first female ringside boxing doctor in New York City.

title: Devil’s Mile
author: Alice Sparberg Alexiou
description: A lively portrait of New York’s 'other street,' once a byword for urban degradation and now just another site of gentrification.

title: A Memory of the Future
author: Elizabeth Spires
description: In A Memory of the Future , critically acclaimed poet Elizabeth Spires reflects on selfhood and the search for a core identity. Inspired by the tradition of poetic interest in Zen, Spires explores the noisy space of the mind, interrogating the necessary divide between the social persona that navigates the world and the artist’s secret self.

title: Record of a Spaceborn Few
author: Becky Chambers
description: Return to the sprawling universe of the Galactic Commons, as humans, artificial intelligence, aliens, and some beings yet undiscovered explore what it means to be a community in the third adventure in the multi-award-nominated science fiction Wayfarers series.

title: All Your Perfects
author: Colleen Hoover
description: Quinn and Graham's perfect love is threatened by their imperfect marriage. The memories, mistakes, and secrets that they have built up over the years are now tearing them apart. The one thing that could save them might also be the very thing that pushes their marriage beyond the point of repair.

title: From a Low and Quiet Sea
author: Donal Ryan
description: In this new novel by the Man Booker-nominated author of The Spinning Heart , three men—one of whom has fled the Syrian war with his family—search for a version of home, their lives moving inexorably towards a reckoning that will draw them all together.

title: Cottage by the Sea
author: Debbie Macomber
description: Rocked by tragedy, Annie Marlow returns to the one place she knows she can heal: the cottage by the sea where she spent many happy childhood holidays with her family. There, Annie meets an unlikely group of people who begin to heal her broken spirit. However, the opportunity of a lifetime challenges her decision to remain in the haven – and with the man – she has come to call home.

title: New Dark Age: Technology and the End of the Future
author: James Bridle
description: A British visual artist, journalist, and 'New Aesthetic' champion offers nightmarish prophecies on the descent into darkness.

title: Give Me Your Hand
author: Megan Abbott
description: From the Edgar-award winning writer of Dare Me is a twisted tale of two high school friends who share a dark secret, one that comes back to haunt them as adults in the laboratory where both women—now scientists—work in an atmosphere of tense competition.

title: The Mere Wife
author: Maria Dahvana Headley
description: A retelling of Beowulf set in contemporary American suburbia, told from the perspective of Grendel and his mother.

title: The Death of Truth: Notes on Falsehood in the Age of Trump
author: Michiko Kakutani
description: How did truth become an endangered species in contemporary America? Former New York Times critic Michiko Kakutani examines the cultural forces that contributed to this gathering storm. In social media and literature, television, academia, and politics, she identifies the trends that have combined to elevate subjectivity over factuality, science, and common values.

title: OK, Mr. Field
author: Katharine Kilalea
description: Mr. Field wants a new life, a life cleansed of the old one’s disappointments. A concert pianist on the London scene coping with the sudden end of his career and marriage, Mr. Field is left alone in a decaying house. He finds himself unglued from reality and possessed by a longing for a perverse kind of intimacy.

title: Homeplace: A Southern Town, a Country Legend, and the Last Days of a Mountaintop Honky-Tonk
author: John Lingan
description: In the tradition of Joe Pageant's Deer Hunting With Jesus and J. D. Vance's Hillbilly Elegy , an intimate account of social change, country music, and a vanishing way of life as a Shenandoah town collides with the twenty-first century

title: Blood & Ivy: The 1849 Murder That Scandalized Harvard
author: Paul Collins
description: A true-crime chronicle of a murder among the upper crust of Harvard Medical School in the middle of the 19th century.

title: The Dead
author: Christian Kracht, Trans. by Daniel Bowles
description: Meeting characters such as a "pistol-packing" Charlie Chaplin along the way, a Swiss filmmaker travels to Japan to make a film meant to aggrandize Nazi Germany while secretly in cahoots with Jewish critics to make an allegorical film that will warn the world of the horrors of the Third Reich.

title: The Secret Habit of Sorrow: Stories
author: Victoria Patterson
description: In these 16 short stories, a band of misfit characters deal with the loss of loved ones, addiction, abuse, and disappointment.

title: The Wrong Heaven
author: Amy Bonnaffons
description: In this debut story collection, Jesus and Mary lawn ornaments come to life, women become horses, and other strange scenarios play out against the backdrop of workaday life.

title: Hullmetal Girls
author: Emily Skrutskie
description: Aisha Un-Haad, 17, and 18-year-old Key Tanaka have risked everything for new lives as mechanically enhanced soldiers. When an insurrection forces dark secrets to surface, the fate of humanity is in the hands of these young heroines in this epic space adventure.

title: The Family Tabor
author: Cherise Wolas
description: Set over the course of a single weekend, with alternating narration among the five Tabors, this novel reckons with the nature of the stories we tell ourselves and our family and the price we pay for second chances.

title: Baby Teeth: A Novel
author: Zoje Stage
description: A battle of wills between mother and daughter reveals the frailty and falsehood of familial bonds.

title: The Other Woman
author: Daniel Silva
description: The actions of real-life British intelligence agent Kim Philby, who defected to the Soviet Union in 1963, drive bestseller Silva’s 18th novel featuring Israeli art restorer and spy Gabriel Allon.

title: The Sinners
author: Ace Atkins
description: With his longtime deputy Lillie Virgil now working up in Memphis, Quinn Colson finds himself having to fall back on some brand-new deputies to help him out, but with Old West-style violence breaking out, and his own wedding on the horizon, this is without a doubt Colson's most trying time as sheriff.

title: Crux: A Cross-Border Memoir
author: Jean Guerrero
description: A daughter’s quest to understand her charismatic and troubled father, an immigrant who crosses borders both real and illusory—between sanity and madness, science and spirituality, life and death.

title: The Annotated Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: The first fully annotated edition of Raymond Chandler’s 1939 classic The Big Sleep features hundreds of notes and images alongside the full text of the novel and is an essential addition to any crime fiction fan’s library.

title: The Late Bloomers' Club
author: Louise Miller
description: Two headstrong sisters, a small town's efforts to do right by the community, and the power of a lost dog to summon true love.

title: Hunting Party
author: Agnaes Desarthe, Trans. by Christiana Hills
description: The unsuspecting member of a hunting party in the French countryside, Tristan is out of place. He has no intention of killing anything, so when his shot inadvertently grazes a rabbit, he saves the animal soon finds himself deeply connected to the wounded rabbit.

title: Laughing Shall I Die: Lives and Deaths of the Great Vikings
author: Tom Shippey
description: Weighing the evidence of Viking sagas and poems against the accounts of the Vikings’ victims, Tom Shippey plumbs the complexities of Viking psychology and recounts tales from Old Norse literature to evoke a medieval culture of war, marauding, and storytelling.

title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
author: Ottessa Moshfegh
description: From the author of Eileen , a novel about a young woman's efforts to duck the ills of the world by embarking on an extended hibernation with the help of one of the worst psychiatrists in the annals of literature and the battery of medicines she prescribes.

title: A Terrible Country
author: Keith Gessen
description: A Terrible Country is the first novel in ten years from n+1 founding editor Keith Gessen. Faced with dismal academic job prospects and a withering personal life, Andrei leaves New York to spend the summer in Moscow to care for his elderly grandmother (and to collect her tales of Stalinist Russia—a research topic that might finally get him a job).

title: The Cost of Living
author: Deborah Levy
description: This "living autobiography" critiques of the roles that society assigns to us and the politics of breaking with the usual gendered rituals, considering the subtle erasure of women's names, spaces, and stories in the modern everyday.

title: The Poisoned City: Flint's Water and the American Urban Tragedy
author: Anna Clark
description: Clark's The Poisoned City recounts the story of Flint's poisoned water through the people who caused it, suffered from it, and exposed it. It is a chronicle of one town, made precarious by the neglect of infrastructure and the erosion of democratic decision making.

title: Clock Dance
author: Anne Tyler
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Breathing Lessons offers a new tale about family, the kind we're born with and the kind we choose for ourselves.

title: The Last Cruise
author: Kate Christensen
description: The 1950s vintage ocean liner Queen Isabella is making her final voyage before heading to the scrapyard, but when a time of crisis begins, the ship's passengers and workers find themselves facing the unknown together in an unexpected and startling test of their characters.

title: A Carnival of Losses: Notes Nearing Ninety
author: Donald Hall
description: In this posthumous essay collection, the former poet laureate of the United States riffs on old age, reminisces about his past, and remembers the poets of his generation.

title: Orchid and the Wasp
author: Caoilinn Hughes
description: A language-driven debut novel from Irish poet Hughes. Gael Foess, daughter of a self-interested investment banker and a once-formidable orchestral conductor, and sister to a vulnerable younger brother, strives to build a life raft in the midst of economic and familial collapse. Moving by wits alone, she cuts a swathe through the leather-lined, coke-dusted social clubs of London, the New York gallery scene, and the birth-throes of the Occupy movement.

title: Hope Never Dies: An Obama Biden Mystery
author: Andrew Shaffer
description: Vice President Joe Biden is fresh out of the Obama White House and feeling adrift when his favorite railroad conductor dies in a suspicious accident, leaving behind an ailing wife and a trail of clues. To unravel the mystery, "Uncle Joe" re-teams with the only man he's ever fully trusted: the 44th president of the United States. Together they'll plumb the darkest corners of Delaware, traveling from cheap motels to biker bars and beyond, as they uncover the sinister forces advancing America's opioid epidemic.

title: Nevada Days
author: Bernardo Atxaga, Trans. by Margaret Jull Costa
description: A Basque novelist takes a detour in Reno and contemplates his Spanish heritage alongside the American desert landscape. A blend of autobiography and fiction.

title: No One Tells You This: A Memoir
author: Glynnis MacNicol
description: Over the course of her fortieth year, which chronicles, Glynnis embarks on a revealing journey of self-discovery that continually contradicts everything she'd been led to expect. An exploration of modern womanhood.

title: From the Corner of the Oval: A Memoir
author: Beck Dorey-Stein
description: As Beck Dorey-Stein learns to navigate White House protocols and more than once runs afoul of the hierarchy, [she] becomes romantically entangled with a consummate D.C. insider, and suddenly the political becomes all too personal

title: Give People Money: How a Universal Basic Income Would End Poverty, Revolutionize Work, and Remake the World
author: Annie Lowrey
description: From a contributing editor of The Atlantic , an analysis of various programs around the world that have found benefits in providing direct cash payments to people in need and a meditation on how such a policy might fare in the United States.

title: The Fall of Wisconsin: The Conservative Conquest of a Progressive Bastion and the Future of American Politics
author: Dan Kaufman
description: A Wisconsin native who identifies as a progressive advocate contrasts the history of his state with the drastic changes during the past decade that have surprised politicians, journalists, academics, and countless voters.

title: The Price You Pay
author: Aidan Truhen
description: All is good in the life of Jack Price. His drug operation is the Amazon of cocaine trafficking...but then: His downstairs neighbor is professionally executed. That the murder is a sign for Jack becomes perfectly clear a few days later when he arrives home and is beaten to a bloody pulp by a squad of enforcers. Now revenge is on his mind.

title: The Wonderful Mr. Willughby: The First True Ornithologist
author: Tim Birkhead
description: In his too-short life, Francis Willughby helped found the Royal Society, differentiated birds through identification of their distinguishing features, and asked questions that were, in some cases, centuries ahead of their time. Tim Birkhead describes and celebrates how Willughby's endeavors set a standard for the way birds—and indeed the whole of natural history—should be studied.

title: What We Were Promised
author: Lucy Tan
description: Set in modern Shanghai, a debut by a Chinese-American writer about a prodigal son whose unexpected return forces his newly wealthy family to confront painful secrets and unfulfilled promises.

title: Buzz: The Nature and Necessity of Bees
author: Thor Hanson
description: This book presents the natural and cultural history of bees including how bees are central to our harvests, our mythologies and our existence.

title: Indianapolis: The True Story of the Worst Sea Disaster in U.S. Naval History and the Fifty-Year Fight to Exonerate an Innocent Man
author: Lynn Vincent and Sara Vladic
description: The true story of the worst sea disaster in U.S. naval history--the sinking of the USS Indianapolis days after it delivered the components of the atomic bomb from California to the Pacific Islands in the most highly classified naval mission of the war—and the fifty-year fight to exonerate an innocent man.

title: The Prison Letters of Nelson Mandela
author: Nelson Mandela, Ed. by Sahm Venter
description: Whether providing unwavering support to his also-imprisoned wife or outlining a human-rights philosophy that resonates today, The Prison Letters of Nelson Mandela reveals the heroism of a man who refused to compromise his moral values in the face of extraordinary punishment. Ultimately, these letters position Mandela as one of the most inspiring figures of the twentieth century.

title: The Summer Wives
author: Beatriz Williams
description: Twenty years after being banished from Winthrop Island, Miranda Schuyler returns to find justice for the man she once loved.

title: The Widower's Notebook: A Memoir
author: Jonathan Santlofer
description: The Widower's Notebook is a portrait of a marriage, an account of the complexities of finding oneself single again after losing your spouse, and a story of the enduring power of familial love.

title: Comemadre
author: Roque Larraquy, Trans. by Heather Cleary
description: In the outskirts of Buenos Aires in 1907, a doctor becomes involved in a misguided experiment that investigates the threshold between life and death. One hundred years later, a celebrated artist goes to extremes in search of aesthetic transformation, turning himself into an art object. How far are we willing to go, Larraquy asks, in pursuit of transcendence?

title: The Lido
author: Libby Page,
description: An octogenarian and a young journalist unite to save a neighborhood pool in London in this debut novel.

title: The Boatbuilder
author: Daniel Gumbiner
description: Seeking a new start after recovering from a head injury and opioid addiction, a young man travels to a Northern California town where he begins building boats with a mentor and establishing a sense of community.

title: Land of Smoke
author: Sara Gallardo, trans. by Jessica Sequeira
description: Every story reveals the way that the habits of everyday life can become unknowable and unpredictable. Recently rediscovered, Sara Gallardo is a major Latin American writer whose stories delve into magical realism.

title: The Garden Party
author: Grace Dane Mazur
description: A rehearsal dinner brings together two disparate families.

title: Half Moon Bay
author: Alice LaPlante
description: Jane loses everything when her teenage daughter is killed in a senseless accident. Wanting to start a new life, Jane moves to Half Moon Bay. And then children begin to disappear.

title: An Ocean of Minutes
author: Thea Lim
description: America is in the grip of a deadly flu pandemic. When Frank catches the virus, his girlfriend Polly will do whatever it takes to save him, even if it means risking everything. A literary love story about two people who are at once mere weeks and many years apart.

title: Just a Shot Away: Peace, Love, and Tragedy with the Rolling Stones at Altamont
author: Saul Austerlitz
description: A historical retrospective on the dark side of the Summer of Love and the end of an era.

title: Early Work
author: Andrew Martin
description: A debut novel about a directionless would-be writer, living in Virginia with his long-term girlfriend, who embarks on an affair with a charismatic, sexually adventurous young woman.

title: The Girl from Blind River
author: Gale Massey
description: Everyone says the Elders family are nothing but cheats, thieves, and convicts―a fact nineteen-year old Jamie Elders has been trying desperately to escape. She may have the natural talent of a poker savant, but her dreams of going pro and getting the hell out of the tiny town of Blind River, New York are going nowhere fast. Especially once she lands in a huge pile of debt to her uncle Loyal.

title: The Seas
author: Samantha Hunt
description: A 19-year-old woman from a remote fishing village is convinced she is a mermaid and falls deeply in love with an older fisherman who is an Iraq war veteran suffering from PTSD.

title: All These Beautiful Strangers
author: Elizabeth Klehfoth
description: A young woman haunted by a family tragedy is caught up in a dangerous web of lies and deception involving a secret society in this psychological thriller.

title: New Poets of Native Nations
author: Ed. by Heid E. Erdrich
description: A landmark anthology celebrating twenty-one native poets first published in the twenty-first century.

title: The Furnace: A Graphic Novel
author: Prentis Rollins
description: Professor Walton Honderich participated in a government prison program and committed an act that led to the death of his friend, the brilliant physicist Marc Lepore, and resulted in unimaginable torment for an entire class of people across the United States.

title: The Lost Country
author: William Gay
description: A young drifter odysseys through the gothic menagerie that is rural Tennessee in Gay’s posthumously published novel.

title: Interior
author: Thomas Clerc, Trans. by Jeffrey Zuckerman
description: A French academic’s detailed description of his Paris apartment and its contents is full of humor and brainy mischief.

title: Tell Me What You Want: The Science of Sexual Desire and How It Can Help You Improve Your Sex Life
author: Justin J Lehmiller
description: What do Americans really want when it comes to sex? And is it possible for us to get what we want? Justin J. Lehmiller, one of the country's leading experts on human sexuality, has made it his career's ambition to answer these questions.

title: Her Pretty Face
author: Robyn Harding
description: A friendship between two very different women is threatened when long-buried secrets rise to the surface.

title: The Road to Walden: 12 Life Lessons from a Sojourn to Thoreau's Cabin
author: Kevin Dann
description: The acclaimed author of Expect Great Things: The Life and Search of Henry David Thoreau traverses on foot from Manhattan to Walden Pond, retracing Thoreau's steps and unlocking the practical principles of the mystic's life in the woods.

title: Astroball: The New Way to Win It All
author: Ben Reiter
description: The Astros were the worst baseball team in half a century, but they were more than just bad: they were an embarrassment, a club that didn't even appear to be trying to win ... But three years later, the critics were proved improbably, astonishingly wrong. How had the Astros pulled off the impossible?

title: The Romanov Empress: A Novel of Tsarina Maria Feodorovna
author: C W Gortner
description: Narrated by the mother of Russia's last tsar, this novel brings to life the story of Maria Feodorovna, who witnessed the excessive splendor and tragic downfall of the Romanovs.

title: Metamorphica: Fiction
author: Zachary Mason
description: An adaptation of Ovid's epic poem Metamorphosis that reimagines the stories of Narcissus, Pygmalion and Galatea, Midas, Atalanta, and even Ovid himself.

title: Godspeed: A Memoir
author: Casey Legler
description: At fifteen, Casey Legler is already one of the fastest swimmers in the world. She is also an alcoholic, isolated from her family, and incapable of forming lasting connections with those around her. Casey gives language to loneliness in this story of survival.

title: The New Inheritors
author: Kent Wascom
description: In 1914, with the world on the brink of war, Isaac, a nature-loving artist whose past is mysterious to all, including himself, meets Kemper, a defiant heiress caught in the rivalry between her brothers.

title: Latchkey: Book Two in the Archivist Wasp Saga
author: Nicole Kornher-Stace
description: "In a ruined land, ghosts thirst for blood, artifacts from high tech military experiments are unearthed like fossils, and gods demand horrific sacrifice. Latchkey continues the story begun in Nicole Kornher-Stace's acclaimed Archivist Wasp Saga Series ."

title: Suicide Club: A Novel about Living
author: Rachel Heng
description: In a near future in which some humans are chosen as "lifers," living 300 years or more if they meet high standards, one lifer is drawn into the mysterious world of the Suicide Club, a network of powerful individuals and rebels who reject society's pursuit of immortality, and instead chose to live and die on their own terms.

title: Shit Is Real
author: Aisha Franz
description: A brokenhearted woman drifts into depression as she occupies her traveling neighbor's apartment in this graphic novel where base human desires and functions alternate with dreamlike symbolism to create a tension-filled tale of the nightmare that is modern life.

title: Eden
author: Andrea Kleine
description: A struggling performance artist in New York grapples with the childhood abduction of her sister and its lingering effects on her adult life.

title: The Blurry Years
author: Eleanor Kriseman
description: A coming-of-age story featuring a twisted mother-daughter relationship, set against the sleazy backdrop of late-seventies and early-eighties Florida.

title: Spinning Silver
author: Naomi Novik
description: Miryem is the daughter and granddaughter of moneylenders, but her father’s inability to collect his debts has left his family on the edge of poverty—until Miryem takes matters into her own hands. Hardening her heart, the young woman sets out to claim what is owed and soon gains a reputation for being able to turn silver into gold.

title: Love War Stories
author: Ivelisse Rodriguez
description: Puerto Rican girls are brought up to want one thing: true love. Yet they are raised by women whose lives are marked by broken promises, grief, and betrayal. This collection documents how these “love wars” break out across generations as individuals find themselves caught in the crosshairs of romance, expectations, and community.

title: Eager: The Surprising, Secret Life of Beavers and Why They Matter
author: Ben Goldfarb
description: Environmental journalist Ben Goldfarb describes how integral beavers are to building healthier ecosystems for humans and non-humans alike and introduces us to 'Beaver Believers,' a coalition of scientists, ranchers, and passionate citizens who are trying to champion these "hardy rodents."

title: How to Be Famous
author: Caitlin Moran
description: From celebrated British journalist and broadcaster Moran. Johanna Morrigan (AKA Dolly Wilde) has it all: at eighteen, she lives in her own flat in London and writes for the coolest music magazine in Britain. But Johanna is miserable. The man of her dreams, John Kite, has just made it big in 1994’s hot new BritPop scene. Suddenly John exists on another plane of reality: that of the Famouses.

title: Don't Make Me Pull Over!: An Informal History of the Family Road Trip
author: Richard Ratay
description: A nostalgic look at the golden age of family road trips—a halcyon era that culminated in the latter part of the twentieth century, before portable DVD players, iPods, and Google Maps.

title: Dear Mrs. Bird
author: AJ Pearce
description: When Emmy sees a job posting at the London Evening Chronicle , her dreams of becoming a Lady War Correspondent seem achievable. But the job turns out to be working as a typist for the fierce and renowned advice columnist, Henrietta Bird. Mrs. Bird is very clear: letters containing any Unpleasantness must go straight in the bin. But when Emmy reads these poignant notes, she is unable to resist responding.

title: The Pre-War House and Other Stories
author: Alison Moore
description: This collection of short fiction about the unhomeliness of home: Fractured families, domestic claustrophobia, and the unseen menace of the everyday.

title: What to Read and Why
author: Francine Prose
description: Prose considers why the works of literary masters such as Mary Shelley, Charles Dickens, George Eliot, and Jane Austen have endured, and shares intriguing insights about modern authors whose words stimulate our minds and enlarge our lives, including Roberto Bolaño, Karl Ove Knausgaard, Jennifer Egan, and Mohsin Hamid.

title: The Darker the Night, the Brighter the Stars: A Neuropsychologist's Odyssey Through Consciousness
author: Paul Broks
description: The Darker the Night, The Brighter the Stars is a story that unfolds through the centuries, along the path of humankind’s constant quest to discover what makes us human, and the answers that consistently slip out of our grasp.

title: Northland: A 4000-Mile Journey Along America's Forgotten Border
author: Porter Fox
description: Travel writer Porter Fox narrates the history of the United States' border with Canada along with his own experiences traveling the 4,000-mile trek over a three-year period of camping, hiking, and adventure.

title: Safe Houses
author: Dan Fesperman
description: A young woman discovers a nefarious truth at the heart of the CIA's operations in postwar Berlin and goes on the run for her life; years later she's gruesomely murdered along with her husband, and her daughter begins to chase down these startling secrets from her past.

title: The Monarchy of Fear: A Philosopher Looks at Our Political Crisis
author: Martha C. Nussbaum
description: From one of the world’s most celebrated moral philosophers comes an examination of the current political crisis and recommendations for how to mend our divided country.

title: City of Devils: The Two Men Who Ruled the Underworld of Old Shanghai
author: Paul French
description: In 1940, Lucky Jack and Dapper Joe bestrode the Shanghai Badlands like kings, while all around the Solitary Island was poverty, starvation, and war. They thought they ruled Shanghai, but the city had other ideas.

title: Verdi: The Man Revealed
author: John Suchet
description: John Suchet attempts to get under the skin of perhaps the most private composer who ever lived. Suchet reveals the true character of this great artist―and the art for which he will be forever known.

title: The Billionaire Raj: A Journey Through India's New Gilded Age
author: James Crabtree
description: A vivid portrayal of the country’s new billionaire class draws an analogy with America’s 19th-century Gilded Age.

title: The Calculating Stars
author: Mary Robinette Kowal
description: This looming threat from a meteorite that fell to earth and obliterated much of the east coast...calls for a radically accelerated effort to colonize space, and requires a much larger share of humanity to take part in the process. 2019 Nebula Award winner.

title: Black Chamber
author: S M Stirling
description: The first novel in a brand-new alternate history series where Teddy Roosevelt is president for a second time right before WWI breaks out, and on his side is the Black Chamber, a secret spy network watching America's back.

title: The Banker's Wife
author: Cristina Alger
description: When a plane crash leaves no trace of a wealthy passenger, Swiss banker Matthew Werner, his young widow is left with a legacy of secrets that intersect with the investigation of a journalist that implicates some of the financial industry's most powerful men.

title: City of Lies: A Poison War Novel
author: Sam Hawke
description: In this first novel of the Poison Wars series, the fate of the corrupt city-state Silatra is in the hands of the heir of its assassinated Chancellor, who along with his sibling and companion must defend it from a military siege.

title: The Last Time I Lied
author: Riley Sager
description: In the latest thriller from the bestselling author of Final Girls , a young woman returns to her childhood summer camp to uncover the truth about a tragedy that happened there fifteen years ago.

title: The Dying of the Light
author: Robert Goolrick
description: Forced into a marriage of convenience to save her family's estate, blue-blooded Southern belle Diana, coming of age just after World War I, sacrifices everything, including love, to become the wife of a man she cannot abide, until fate intervenes.

title: The Promise of the Grand Canyon: John Wesley Powell's Perilous Journey and His Vision for the American West
author: John F Ross
description: With The Promise of the Grand Canyon , John Ross recreates John Wesley Powell's expedition along the Colorado River in all its glory and terror, but Powell's second (unheralded) career as a scientist, bureaucrat, and land-management pioneer concerns us today.

title: Unclean Jobs for Women and Girls: Stories
author: Alissa Nutting
description: Throughout these seventeen stories spread across time, space, and differing planes of reality, we encounter a host of women and girls in a wide range of unusual jobs and uncanny circumstances.

title: It All Falls Down
author: Sheena Kamal
description: The troubled Nora Watts searches for the truth about her father’s supposed suicide in Kamal’s follow-up to The Lost Ones .

title: After the Monsoon: An Ernst Grip Novel
author: Robert Karjel
description: A thriller set in the terrorist- and pirate-infested world of the Horn of Africa—where the sea caresses the desert, alliances shift like sand, and a Swedish detective can count on nothing but his own shrewdness to survive.

title: The Moment Before Drowning
author: James Brydon
description: French Resistance hero investigates a murder in a small Breton town while awaiting his own trial.

title: Spymaster: A Thriller
author: Brad Thor
description: Best-selling thriller writer Brad Thor returns with the latest installment in the adventures of Scot Harvath, who this time must thwart Russia from achieving world domination and the nefarious goals such power portends.

title: Wired
author: Julie Garwood
description: A beautiful computer genius and a bad-boy FBI agent must collaborate—in more ways than one—in the steamy new suspense novel from the New York Times -bestselling author.

title: Empress: The Astonishing Reign of Nur Jahan
author: Ruby Lal
description: Historian Ruby Lal reframes the historical narrative about a Muslim woman who co-ruled an empire with her husband, Jahangir of India, deconstructing her reputation as a haughty temptress and revealing her to be “a devoted wife, a wise and just queen, a shrewd politician.”

title: The World Is a Narrow Bridge
author: Aaron Thier
description: Young Miami couple Murphy and Eva have almost decided to have a baby when Yahweh, the Old Testament God, appears to Eva and makes an unwelcome demand: He wants her to be his prophet and embark with Murphy on a wild road trip across the country to fulfill incomprehensible demands and arcane rituals as they go.

title: Can You Tolerate This?: Essays
author: Ashleigh Young
description: A collection of essays on youth and aging, ambition and disappointment, Katherine Mansfield tourism and New Zealand punk rock, and the limitations of the body.

title: The Contest: The 1968 Election and the War for America's Soul
author: Michael Schumacher
description: 1968—rife with riots, assassinations, anti–Vietnam War protests, and realpolitik—was one of the most tumultuous years in the twentieth century, culminating in one of the most consequential presidential elections in American history. The Contest tells the story of that contentious election.

title: Patient Care: Death and Life in the Emergency Room
author: Paul Seward, MD
description: From a physician with a half century of experience practicing in the emergency room, a memoir reflecting on treating patients and exploring the ethical questions that arise when caring for a stranger in their moment of crisis.

title: The King's Witch: Frances Gorges Historical Trilogy, Book I
author: Tracy Borman
description: The first in a trilogy of historical novels set at the dramatic endpoint of the Tudor reign and the dangerous start of the Stuart era.

title: The Intermission
author: Elyssa Friedland
description: A couple puts their marriage on hold for six months to find out if they’re better together or apart.

title: Trickster Feminism
author: Anne Waldman
description: Mythopoetics, shape shifting, quantum entanglement, Anthropocene blues, litany and chance operation play inside the field of these intertwined poems, which coalesced out of months of protests with some texts penned in the streets

title: The Book of Hidden Things
author: Francesco Dimitri
description: Three men investigate the increasingly strange circumstances surrounding their old friend’s disappearance from a small Italian town.

title: A Long Island Story
author: Rick Gekoski
description: A novel about 1950s America, a marriage in crisis, and a family falling apart at the seams.

title: Between Hope and Fear: A History of Vaccines and Human Immunity
author: Michael Kinch
description: A comprehensive history of the science of vaccination.

title: The Night Visitor
author: Lucy Atkins
description: In this new noir thriller from the bestselling author of The Missing One and The Other Child , Professor Olivia Sweetman appears to have it all: a high-flying career as a TV presenter and historian, three children, and a talented husband. But her life has spiraled into deceit, and the narrative tracks just how far she'll go to save her reputation.

title: The Last Mosaic
author: Elizabeth Cooperman and Thomas Walton
description: Collaborators Elizabeth Cooperman and Thomas Walton gather impressions from the ruinous streets in and around Rome. The result is a literary mosaic that aligns itself with the ecstatic baroque of Bernini, the concentrated vision of Caravaggio, and the sublime uncertainty of Keats, as it resists the forces of "another dark age."

title: Making Oscar Wilde
author: Michele Mendelssohn
description: The untold story of Wilde's career through the lens of his 1882 America tour, during which the nation's racist attitudes—specifically of the anti-Black variety—led critics to deride Wilde in minstrel shows and cartoons, linking Wilde's Irish heritage with that of Africans. Racist himself, a humiliated Wilde drew upon minstrel tropes to compose what are now some of his most celebrated comedies.

title: The Ascent of John Tyndall: Victorian Scientist, Mountaineer, and Public Intellectual
author: Roland Jackson
description: This biography describes the colorful life and achievements of a crucial but overlooked scientific figure in Victorian Britain, who established the physical basis of the greenhouse effect and why the sky is blue as well as maintained an impressive life outside science as a mountaineer, writer, and man-about-town.

title: Go Ask Fannie
author: Elisabeth Hyde
description: Told in three parts, roving between then and now, Go Ask Fannie tells of the life and death of Lillian Blair, the over-bearing, bickering, but loving children who look for ways to connect with one another in her absence, and the inner lives we hide from our families.

title: We Don't Live Here Anymore: Collected Short Stories and Novellas, Volume 1
author: Andre Dubus
description: This first volume of three collecting the work of the late celebrated writer includes writings from the Separate Flights (1975) and Adultery & Other Choices (1977), introduced by Ann Beattie.

title: Conan Doyle for the Defense: The True Story of a Sensational British Murder, a Quest for Justice, and the World's Most Famous Detective Writer
author: Margalit Fox
description: New York Times senior writer Fox brings to life a forgotten cause célèbre in this page-turning account of how mystery-writer-turned-real life sleuth Arthur Conan Doyle helped exonerate a man who was wrongfully convicted of murder.

title: Dead Girls: Essays on Surviving an American Obsession
author: Alice Bolin
description: Alice Bolin examines iconic American works from the essays of Joan Didion and James Baldwin to Twin Peaks , Britney Spears, and Serial , illuminating the widespread obsession with women who are abused, killed, and disenfranchised, and whose bodies (dead and alive) are used as props to bolster men’s stories.

title: Confessions of the Fox
author: Jordy Rosenberg
description: A rollicking love story set in the 18th century London of notorious thieves and queer subcultures, this genre-bending debut tells a story of gender, desire, and liberation.

title: Squeezed: Why Our Families Can't Afford America
author: Alissa Quart
description: Families today are squeezed on every side-from high childcare costs and harsh employment policies to workplaces without paid family leave or even dependable and regular working hours. Alissa Quart examines the lives of many middle-class Americans who can now barely afford to raise children.

title: Trail of Lightning
author: Rebecca Roanhorse
description: Maggie Hoskie is a Dinâetah monster hunter, a supernaturally gifted killer. When a small town needs help finding a missing girl, Maggie is their last best hope. But what Maggie uncovers about the monster is much more terrifying than anything she could imagine.

title: My Twenty-Five Years in Provence: Reflections on Then and Now
author: Peter Mayle
description: The author Peter Mayle, champion of all things Provence, here in a final volume of all new writing, offers ... recollections from his twenty-five years in the South of France, lessons learned, culinary delights enjoyed, and changes observed

title: Summerland
author: Hannu Rajaniemi
description: Loss is a thing of the past. Murder is obsolete. Death is just the beginning. In 1938, death is no longer feared but exploited. Since the discovery of the afterlife, the British Empire has extended its reach into Summerland, a metropolis for the recently deceased.

title: The Unpunished Vice: A Life of Reading
author: Edmund White
description: From the winner of the 2018 PEN/Saul Bellow Award for Career Achievement in American Fiction, a look back at favorite books and a consideration of what makes a work of lasting literary genius.

title: An Excellent Choice: Panic and Joy on My Solo Path to Motherhood
author: Emma Brockes
description: A gay British journalist in her late 30s decides to become pregnant, moving with her girlfriend to the United States for artificial insemination, fertility treatments, and, ultimately, a new home.

title: All We Ever Wanted
author: Emily Giffin
description: Nina Browning is living the good life after marrying into Nashville's elite. Her husband's tech business is booming, and her adored son, Finch, is bound for Princeton. At the heart of the lies and scandal, Tom, Nina, and Lyla are forced together—all questioning their closest relationships, asking themselves who they really are, and searching for the courage to live a life of true meaning.

title: I Will Be Complete: A Memoir
author: Glen David Gold
description: From the best-selling author of Carter Beats the Devil and Sunnyside , a memoir told in three parts: about growing up in the wake of the destructive choices of an extremely unconventional mother.

title: Salt Lane
author: William Shaw
description: Juggling the case, her aging mother, her teenage daughter, and the loneliness of country life, Detective Alexandra Cupidi must discover who killed a local woman, who she really was, and how she managed to reconnect with her long lost son, apparently from beyond the grave.

title: How Did Lubitsch Do It?
author: Joseph McBride
description: Joseph McBride analyzes Ernst Lubitsch's films in rich detail in the first in-depth critical study to consider the full scope of his work in both his native and adopted lands. McBride explains the "Lubitsch Touch," shows how the director challenged American attitudes toward romance and sex, and offers revealing insights into his working methods.

title: The Secrets Between Us
author: Thrity Umrigar
description: Bhima, the main character of Thrity Umrigar’s national bestseller The Space Between Us , returns: the former servant struggles against the circumstances of class and misfortune to forge a new path for herself and her granddaughter in modern India.

title: The Cabin at the End of the World
author: Paul Tremblay
description: A horror-thriller from Bram Stoker Award-winning author Tremblay. Eric and Andrew are vacationing with their seven-year-old daughter, Wen, at remote Gaudet Lake in New Hampshire when their cabin is invaded by a quartet of weapons-wielding strangers, each of whom has been driven there by a shared vision: that the world will end unless one member of this family sacrifices another.

title: One for the Rogue
author: Manda Collins
description: After they join forces to solve a mystery, geologist Gemma Hastings and fossil hunter Lord Cameron Lisle may instead find love in the thrilling conclusion to the Studies in Scandal series.

title: The Trial and Execution of the Traitor George Washington
author: Charles B Rosenberg
description: Drawing inspiration from an actual kidnapping plot hatched in 1776 by a member of Washington's own Commander-in-Chief's Guards, this novel envisions what would take place if the leader of America's fledgling rebellion were taken from the nation at the height of the war, imperiling any chance of victory.

title: A Steep Price
author: Robert Dugoni
description: When a missing woman turns up dead at the bottom of a well, Tracy Crosswhite must find out who killed her and if it had to do with an arranged marriage, while also hiding the secret of her own pregnancy.

title: Son of Hitler
author: Anthony Del Col & Geoff Moore, Illustrated by Jeff McComsey
description: A graphic novel set during the 1944 Allied invasion of Europe, in which British Special Operations agent Cora Brown maneuvers Pierre, the illegitimate son of Hitler, as a chess piece in an elaborate game to kill the führer.

title: The Race to Save the Romanovs: The Truth Behind the Secret Plans to Rescue the Russian Imperial Family
author: Helen Rappaport
description: A dramatic account of the grim 1918 countdown toward the deaths of Tsar Nicholas II and his family.

title: Unbeaten: Rocky Marciano's Fight for Perfection in a Crooked World
author: Mike Stanton
description: The son of poor Italian immigrants, with short arms and stubby legs, Rocky Marciano accomplished a feat that eluded legendary heavyweight champions like Joe Louis, Jack Dempsey, Muhammad Ali, and Mike Tyson: He never lost a professional fight. His record was a perfect 49-0. This is his story.

title: Midnight Blue
author: Simone van der Vlugt, trans. by Jenny Watson
description: From Simone Van Der Vlugt comes her European bestselling novel of a young woman's rise as a painter in Holland's Golden Age.

title: Mine: A Novel of Obsession
author: J L Butler
description: Divorce lawyer Francine Day is one big case away from securing her place among London's legal elite. She has spent years methodically building her career but her work ethic isn't enough to keep her from falling for her charismatic and suave new client, Martin Joy ... But something about her new lover doesn't add up.

title: Lady Be Good
author: Amber Brock
description: Set in the 1950s, Lady Be Good marks Amber Brock's return, sweeping readers into the world of the mischievous, status-obsessed daughter of a hotel magnate and the electric nightlife of three iconic cities: New York, Miami, and Havana.

title: Spying on Whales: The Past, Present, and Future of Earth's Most Awesome Creatures
author: Nick Pyenson
description: A paleontologist and self-styled whale chaser weaves his own adventures into a rich account of the largest creatures on our planet.

title: The Hospital
author: Ahmed Bouanani
description: From the late Moroccan writer and filmmaker—whose work was often censored—this translated novel draws on Bouanani’s own experiences as a tuberculosis patient in a hospital that begins to feel increasingly like a prison or a strange nightmare.

title: White Fragility: Why It's So Hard for White People to Talk about Racism
author: Robin J Diangelo
description: Explores counterproductive reactions white people have when discussing racism that serve to protect their positions and maintain racial inequality

title: Many Love: A Memoir of Polyamory and Finding Love(s)
author: Sophie Lucido Johnson
description: A writer and illustrator reveals how she went from serial monogamist to happily married polyamorist.

title: Unthinkable: An Extraordinary Journey Through the World's Strangest Brains
author: Helen Thomson
description: A user-friendly tour of the brain and the curious things that go on inside of it, from splendidly practical visions to debilitating hallucinations.

title: Any Man
author: Amber Tamblyn
description: A violent serial rapist is on the loose, who goes by the name Maude. She hunts for men at bars, online, at home— the place doesn’t matter, neither does the man. Her victims then must live the aftermath of their assault in the form of doubt, shame and alienation.

title: Aroused: The History of Hormones and How They Control Just about Everything
author: Randi Hutter Epstein
description: A guided tour through the strange science of hormones and the age-old quest to control them.

title: School of Velocity
author: Eric Beck Rubin
description: A successful pianist with a wife and child becomes psychologically disturbed by hallucinations that lead him to look back on his adolescence in the Netherlands, particularly the nature of his close friendship with an actor who now lives in the United States.

title: Remind Me Again What Happened
author: Algonquin Books
description: A woman’s amnesia strains her relationships with her husband and her best friend.

title: Seeds of Science: Why We Got It So Wrong on Gmos
author: Mark Lynas
description: An environmental science writer takes a deep look at the ramifications of genetically modified organisms over the past four decades.

title: Refuge
author: Ming Lauren Holden
description: Refuge is a collection of lyric essays about a young woman's life as a budding writer and an international development and aid worker. Spanning twelve years and multiple continents, it focuses in large part on her advocacy and theater work with refugees.

title: The Immeasurable World: Journeys in Desert Places
author: William Atkins
description: Will Atkins decided to travel in six of the world's driest, hottest places...each of his travel narratives weaves aspects of natural history, historical background, and present-day reportage into a tapestry that reveals the human appeal of these often inhuman landscapes.

title: The Winter Father: Collected Short Stories and Novellas, Volume 2
author: Andre Dubus
description: Richard Russo introduces this second volume of collected works by the late celebrated writer, which includes the much anthologized "A Father's Story" and other tales.

title: Number One Chinese Restaurant
description: The Beijing Duck House is not only a beloved go-to setting for hunger pangs and celebrations; it is its own world, inhabited by waiters and kitchen staff who have been fighting, loving, and aging within its walls for decades. When disaster strikes, this working family’s controlled chaos is set loose, forcing each character to confront the conflicts that fast-paced restaurant life has kept at bay.

title: The Great Believers
author: Rebecca Makkai
description: A novel spanning 30 years and two continents takes the reader on a journey, both intimate and sweeping, through the 1980s AIDS crisis in Chicago and its residual effects on the contemporary lives of survivors.

title: Room to Dream
author: David Lynch and Kristine McKenna
description: In this memoir, David Lynch...opens up about a lifetime of extraordinary creativity, the friendships he has made along the way and the struggles he has faced to bring his projects to fruition.

title: The Melody
author: Jim Crace
description: One night, Busi is wrested from bed by noises in his courtyard and then stunned by an attacking intruder-his hands and neck are scratched, his face is bitten. Busi can't say what it was that he encountered, exactly, but he feels his assailant was neither man nor animal.

title: American Sonnets for My Past and Future Assassin
author: Terrance Hayes
description: In seventy poems bearing the same title, Terrance Hayes explores the meanings of American, of assassin, and of love in the sonnet form. Written during the first two hundred days of the Trump presidency, these poems are haunted by the country's past and future eras and errors, its dreams and nightmares.

title: Old in Art School: A Memoir of Starting Over
author: Nell Irvin Painter
description: Following her retirement from Princeton University, celebrated historian Dr. Nell Irvin Painter surprised everyone in her life by returning to school―in her sixties―to earn a BFA and MFA in painting. In Old in Art School , she travels from her beloved Newark to the prestigious Rhode Island School of Design and struggles with the unstable balance between the pursuit of art and the inevitable, sometimes painful demands of a life fully lived.

title: The Shepherd's Hut
author: Tim Winton
description: The Shepherd’s Hut is a tale of unlikely friendship and yearning, at once brutal and lyrical.

title: History of Violence: A Novel
author: Edouard Louis, Trans. Lorin Stein
description: History of Violence is international bestselling French author Edouard Louis's autobiographical novel about surviving a shocking sexual assault and coping with the post-traumatic stress disorder of its aftermath.

title: Tell the Machine Goodnight
author: Katie Williams
description: A science fiction novel about technology’s potential and its moral failings, Tell the Machine Goodnight imagines a near future in which lives are altered by a happiness machine.

title: The Perfect Couple
author: Elin Hilderbrand
description: The Otis-Winbury wedding promises to be an event to remember: the groom's wealthy parents have spared no expense to host a lavish ceremony at their oceanfront estate. But it's going to be memorable for all the wrong reasons after tragedy strikes: a body is discovered in Nantucket Harbor just hours before the ceremony-and everyone in the wedding party is suddenly a suspect.

title: When Katie Met Cassidy
author: Camille Perri
description: Katie Daniels has just been dumped by her fiancé when she finds herself seated across a negotiating table from Cassidy Price, a sexy, self-assured woman wearing a man's suit. When Katie Met Cassidy is a romantic comedy about gender and sexuality, and the importance of figuring out who we are in order to go after what we truly want.

title: You Were Made for This
author: Michelle Sacks
description: For fans of The Woman in the Window and The Perfect Nanny , Michelle Sacks' You Were Made For This explores the darkest sides of marriage, motherhood, and friendship.

title: Murder on the Left Bank
author: Cara Black
description: A confession fifty years in the making puts everyone’s favorite Paris détéctive très chic, Aimée Leduc, on a collision course with the 'Hand,' a cabal of corrupt Parisian cops among who masterminded her father's murder.

title: The Killing Habit: A Tom Thorne Novel
author: Mark Billingham
description: Tom Thorne is handed a case that he doesn’t take too seriously, until a spate of animal killings points to the work of a serial killer.

title: Wicked and the Wallflower
author: Sarah MacLean
description: The first novel in New York Times bestselling author MacLean's new series about three brothers bound by a secret they cannot escape–and the women who bring them to their knees.

title: Providence
author: Caroline Kepnes
description: Best friends in small-town New Hampshire, Jon and Chloe share a bond so intense that it borders on the mystical. But before Jon can declare his love for his soul mate, he is kidnapped, his plans for a normal life permanently dashed.

title: Slowly We Die
author: Emelie Schepp
description: A tragic incident on the operating table leaves a patient damaged for life and leads a young surgeon to abandon his profession as a physician… Now, years later, a series of senseless, gruesome murders are rocking the same medical community.

title: Find You in the Dark
author: Nathan Ripley
description: A family man with a habit of digging up the past catches the attention of a serial killer who wants anything but his secrets uncovered.

title: The Skaar Invasion
author: Terry Brooks
description: The Skaar Invasion is the second book of the four-part Shannara series. The Four Lands are under siege. Wielding a magical ability virtually impossible to combat, mysterious invaders defeat the most fearsome Troll armies, then focus their savagery on the Druid order—and all hope seems lost.

title: Bring Me Back
author: B. A. Paris
description: Finn and Layla are young, in love, and on vacation. They’re driving along the highway when Finn decides to stop at a service station to use the restroom. When he returns Layla is gone―never to be seen again. Ten years later Finn is engaged to Layla’s sister, Ellen. Then Finn gets a phone call. Someone from his past has seen Layla―hiding in plain sight. Long-lost items from Layla’s past that keep turning up around Finn and Ellen’s house. If Layla is alive―and on Finn’s trail―what does she want?

title: We Begin Our Ascent
author: Joe Mungo Reed
description: We Begin Our Ascent dances between tragic and comic, exploring the cost of ambition and the question of what gives our lives meaning. Reed melds the themes of great marital dramas like Revolutionary Road . Throughout, readers are drawn inside the cycling world and treated to sports-writing.

title: Yes We (Still) Can: Politics in the Age of Obama, Twitter, and Trump
author: Dan Pfeiffer
description: From Obama's former communications director...comes a colorful account of how politics, the media, and the Internet changed during the Obama presidency and how Democrats can fight back in the Trump era.

title: Why to Kill a Mockingbird Matters: What Harper Lee's Book and the Iconic American Film Mean to Us Today
author: Tom Santopietro
description: Tom Santopietro, an author well-known for his writing about American popular culture, delves into the heart of the beloved classic and shows readers why To Kill a Mockingbird matters more today than ever before.

title: Born Trump: Inside America's First Family
author: Emily Jane Fox
description: Who is Donald J. Trump? To truly understand America’s forty-fifth president, argues Vanity Fair journalist Emily Jane Fox, you must know his children, whose own stories provide the key to unlocking what makes him tick.

title: Like to Die: A McKenzie Novel
author: David Housewright
description: In the 15th installment of his Rushmore McKenzie novels, the hero— who has become an occasional unlicensed private investigator—tries to help his friend Erin get to the bottom of the mysterious harassment she's been experiencing at her growing food business.

title: The House of Islam
author: Ed Husain
description: Today, Islam is to many in the West an alien force, with Muslims held in suspicion. Failure to grasp the inner workings of religion and geopolitics has haunted American foreign policy for decades and has been decisive in the new administration's controversial orders. The House of Islam addresses key questions and points of disconnection.

title: Stranger on Earth
author: Richard Jones
description: Richard Jones constructs a narrative where beauty and revelation are found in first loves, foreign places, and captivating landscapes.

title: What the Eyes Don't See: A Story of Crisis, Resistance, and Hope in an American City
author: Mona Hanna-Attisha
description: In the heart of the world's wealthiest nation, one hundred thousand people were poisoned by the water supply for two years- with the knowing complicity of their government. Written by the pediatrician who helped turn the crisis into a movement for change.

title: Revenant Gun
author: Yoon Ha Lee
description: Shuos Jedao is awake... and nothing is as he remembers. He's a teenager, a cadet-a nobody-in the body of an old man; a general in command of an elite force. And he's the most feared, and reviled, man in the galaxy.

title: The Shades
author: Evgenia Citkowitz
description: A year has passed since Catherine and Michael Hall lost their teenage daughter in a car accident, leaving them and their son, Rowan, reeling in the aftermath of the tragedy. After Catherine withdraws from her life to Hamden ... a young woman, appears at the house claiming to have once lived there, all is not what it seems.

title: Little Panic: Dispatches from an Anxious Life
author: Amanda Stern
description: A memoir about growing up in New York City with undiagnosed panic disorder and how it manifested in addiction, troubled relationships, and other problems.

title: Witchmark
author: C. L. Polk
description: In a world reminiscent of Edwardian England in the shadow of a World War, cabals of noble families use their magical gifts to control the fates of nations, while one young man seeks only to live a life of his own.

title: Chemistry Lessons
author: Meredith Goldstein
description: Advice columnist Goldstein's YA debut features a teen science whiz in Cambridge, Massachusetts, who has recently lost her mother to cancer and her boyfriend to the vicissitudes of young love. Using her science chops, she tries to crack the chemical equation for lasting love and instead wreaks havoc on herself and the young men in her life.

title: The Perfect Weapon: War, Sabotage, and Fear in the Cyber Age
author: David E Sanger
description: From The New York Times 's national security correspondent, this report offers a broad view of how cyber technology has been weaponized by democracies, dictators, and terrorists.

title: The Throwaway: A Thriller
author: Michael Moreci
description: Mark Strain had it all: beautiful wife, a baby on the way, and a skyrocketing career as a D.C. lobbyist. But when Mark is violently abducted from his home by masked men, everything he knows is turned upside down.

title: The Ambition Decisions: What Women Know about Work, Family, and the Path to Building a Life
author: Hana Schank
description: As they faced unexpectedly fraught decisions about their own lives, journalists Hana Schank and Elizabeth Wallace found themselves wondering about the women they'd graduated alongside. What happened to these women who seemed set to reap the rewards of second-wave feminism, on the brink of taking over the world?

title: Uncensored: My Life and Uncomfortable Conversations at the Intersection of Black and White America
author: Zachary R Wood
description: Still in his early 20s, Wood chronicles his arduous upbringing as a black male, including his 15 minutes of fame (so far) while a college student.

title: The Trigger: Narratives of the American Shooter
author: Daniel J Patinkin
description: A curious exercise in the annals of gun violence, highlighting the life stories of six who turned to the gun for a solution.

title: Playthings
author: Alex Pheby
description: A fictionalized account of nineteenth-century German judge Daniel Paul Schreber—one of Freud's famous case studies—and his final descent into madness.

title: The Equations of Life: How Physics Shapes Evolution
author: Charles S. Cockell
description: In The Equations of Life , biologist Charles S. Cockell makes the forceful argument that the laws of physics narrowly constrain how life can evolve, making evolution's outcomes predictable.

title: The Bonanza King: John MacKay and the Battle Over the Greatest Riches in the American West
author: Gregory Crouch
description: The Bonanza King traces the rags-to-riches frontier story of Irish immigrant John Mackay, describing how in mid-nineteenth-century Nevada he outmaneuvered the pernicious 'Bank Ring' monopoly and thousands of rivals to take control of the history-making Comstock Lode.

title: The Anomaly
author: Michael Rutger
description: An online reality show goes looking for a long-rumored cave in the Grand Canyon, with horrific consequences.

title: Bad Advice: Or Why Celebrities, Politicians, and Activists Aren't Your Best Source of Health Information
author: Paul Offit
description: Paul A. Offit shares wisdom on the dos and don'ts of battling misinformation. From conspiracy theories linking vaccines to autism to Holocaust and climate-change denial, Bad Advice is a guide to taking on quack experts and self-appointed activists.

title: The Lost Vintage
author: Ann Mah
description: A wine expert in training visits her family’s vineyard in Burgundy only to discover a cellar full of secrets.

title: Barons of the Sea: And their Race to Build the World's Fastest Clipper Ship
author: Steven Ujifusa
description: Sweeping story of the nineteenth-century American dynasties who battled for dominance of the tea and opium trades.

title: Demi-Gods
author: Eliza Robertson
description: It is 1950, and Willa's mother has a new beau. The arrival of his blue-eyed, sun-kissed sons at Willa's summer home signals the end of her safe childhood. Nine-year-old Willa is drawn to the strange and solitary younger brother, Patrick. Left to their own devices, Willa is swept up in Patrick's wicked games.

title: The Freeze-Frame Revolution
author: Peter Watts
description: In this futuristic narrative, Watts' human characters are bound to a ship (Eriophora) and spend 66 million years creating interstellar wormhole gates while simultaneously exploring their purpose in a warped world.

title: The Debatable Land: The Lost World Between Scotland and England
author: Graham Robb
description: Graham Robb finds that the 2,000-year-old map of Ptolemy unlocks a central mystery of British history.

title: A Place for Us
author: Fatima Farheen Mirza
description: In this first novel from Sarah Jessica Parker's new imprint, a wedding reunites an estranged brother from his Indian-Muslim American family, each member of which struggles to balance their various cultural identities.

title: Good Trouble: Stories
author: Joseph O'Neill
description: A collection of eleven stories about the way we live now from the best-selling author of Netherland .

title: Who Is Vera Kelly?
author: Rosalie Knecht
description: A madcap literary spy thriller set in 1960s Argentina as Vera, working for the CIA, becomes stuck in the country during a hostile takeover.

title: Starless
author: Jacqueline Carey
description: Destined from birth to serve as protector of the princess Zariya, Khai is trained in the arts of killing and stealth by a warrior sect in the deep desert; yet there is one profound truth that has been withheld from him.

title: Bearskin
author: James A McLaughlin
description: A country noir in which a fugitive from a Mexican cartel takes refuge in a forest preserve in the wilds of Virginia where he finds himself becoming obsessed with catching a group of bear poachers.

title: Rising: Dispatches from the New American Shore
author: Elizabeth Rush
description: Harvey. Maria. Irma. Sandy. Katrina. We live in a time of unprecedented hurricanes and catastrophic weather events, a time when it is increasingly clear that climate change is neither imagined nor distant―and that rising seas are transforming the coastline of the United States in irrevocable ways.

title: Life in the Garden
author: Penelope Lively
description: From the only author to have won both the Man Booker Prize and the Carnegie medal for children’s fiction, this meditation on gardens offers a mix of history, personal reflection, and readings of literature and art featuring this peculiar green space.

title: Convenience Store Woman
author: Sayaka Murata, Trans. by Ginny Tapley Takemori
description: Keiko Furukura had always been considered a strange child, and her parents always worried how she would get on in the real world, so when she takes on a job in a convenience store while at university, they are delighted for her. In the convenience store, she finds a predictable world. She feels comfortable in her life, but is aware that she is not living up to society’s expectations. When a similarly alienated but cynical and bitter young man comes to work in the store, he will upset Keiko’s contented stasis―but will it be for the better?

title: Springfield Confidential: Jokes, Secrets, and Outright Lies from a Lifetime Writing for the Simpsons
author: Mike Reiss and Mathew Klickstein
description: From a producer who has been with The Simpsons since its inception in 1989, this volume offers an inside look into the longest-running scripted prime-time show in television history, with insights into characters, episodes, and professional relationships.

title: Light of the Stars: Alien Worlds and the Fate of the Earth
author: Adam Frank
description: Astrophysicist and NPR commentator on what the latest research on the existence and trajectories of alien civilizations may teach us about our own.

title: The Secret Life of Cows
author: Rosamund Young
description: Rosamund Young distills a lifetime of organic farming wisdom, describing the surprising personalities of her cows and other animals.

title: Fight No More: Stories
author: Lydia Millet
description: Twelve interlocking stories set in Los Angeles describe a broken family through the homes they inhabit.

title: Mad Boy
author: Nick Arvin
description: Young Henry Phipps is on a quest to realize his dying mother’s last wish: to be buried at sea, surrounded by her family. Not an easy task, but Henry’s stubborn determination knows no bounds.

title: And Then We Danced: A Voyage Into the Groove
author: Henry Alford
description: Tackling a wide range of forms (including ballet, hip-hop, jazz, ballroom, tap, contact improvisation, Zumba, swing), this grand tour takes us through the works and careers of luminaries ranging from Bob Fosse to George Balanchine, Twyla Tharp to Arthur Murray.

title: Tom Clancy: Line of Sight
author: Mike Maden
description: Twenty-six years ago, Dr. Cathy Ryan restored the eyesight of a young Bosnian girl who had been injured during an attack in the Bosnian War. Today, her son, Jack Ryan Jr. has agreed to track down the young woman and deliver a letter from his mother. What he finds shocks them both.

title: The Removes
author: Tatjana Soli
description: As the first wave of pioneers travel westward to settle the American frontier, two women discover their inner strength when their lives are irrevocably changed by the hardship of the wild west in The Removes , a historical novel from New York Times bestselling and award-winning author Tatjana Soli.

title: Jar of Hearts
author: Jennifer Hillier
description: This is the story of three best friends: one who was murdered, one who went to prison, and one who's been searching for the truth all these years. While everyone thinks they finally know the truth, there are dark secrets buried deep. And what happened that fateful night is more complex and more chilling than anyone really knows.

title: The Collected Stories of Machado de Assis
author: Joaquim Maria Machado de Assis, Trans. by Margaret Jull Costa and Robin Patterson
description: The complete stories of Machado de Assis finally appear in English for the first time in this new translation. Widely acclaimed as the progenitor of twentieth-century Latin American fiction, Machado de Assis (1839–1908)—the son of a mulatto father and a washerwoman, and the grandson of freed slaves—has been hailed in his lifetime as Brazil's greatest writer.

title: Famous Father Girl: A Memoir of Growing Up Bernstein
author: Jamie Bernstein
description: The oldest daughter of revered composer Leonard Bernstein offers a rare look at her father on the centenary of his birth—illuminating a man, a city, and an era that defined modern culture—in a deeply intimate memoir.

title: The Color of Bee Larkham's Murder
author: Sarah J Harris
description: A mystery about a boy with synesthesia–a condition that causes him to see colors when he hears sounds–who tries to uncover what happened to his beautiful neighbor, and if he was ultimately responsible.

title: The Pharaoh Key
author: Douglas Preston and Lincoln Child
description: When his former employer goes missing, Gideon Crew, reeling from his terminal diagnosis, pursues the long-awaited translation of the Phaistos Disc, an ancient tablet that could end or save his life.

title: Lying in Wait
author: Liz Nugent
description: In 1980s Dublin, Lydia Fitzsimons seems to have the perfect life—wife of Andrew, a respected judge, and mistress of Avalon. But her husband's murder of Annie Doyle, accidental or not, sets into motion a dark downward spiral.

title: Amity and Prosperity: One Family and the Fracturing of America
author: Eliza Griswold
description: In Amity and Prosperity , Pulitzer Prize-winning poet and journalist Eliza Griswold tells the story of the energy boom’s impact on a small town at the edge of Appalachia and one woman’s transformation from a struggling single parent to an unlikely activist.

title: Low Chicago: A Wild Cards Novel
author: George R. R. Martin
description: In Low Chicago , a gang of criminals scattered throughout the past threaten the stability of the world in George R. R. Martin's latest Wild Cards adventure.

title: Red Card: How the U.S. Blew the Whistle on the World's Biggest Sports Scandal
author: Red Card, Ken Bensinger
description: The definitive, shocking account of the FIFA scandal—the biggest international corruption case of recent years, spearheaded by US investigators, involving dozens of countries, and implicating nearly every aspect of the world’s most popular sport, soccer, including its biggest event, the World Cup.

title: Modernists and Mavericks: Bacon, Freud, Hockney and the London Painters
author: Martin Gayford
description: An account of the painting scene in London from the Second World War to the 1970s, illustrated by documentary photographs and the works themselves, by a member of the artists' inner circle.

title: The Traitor's Niche
author: Ismail Kadare, Trans. by John Hodgson
description: At the heart of the Ottoman Empire, a niche is carved into ancient stone. Here, the sultan displays the severed heads of his adversaries. People flock to see the latest head and gossip about the state of the empire: the province of Albania is demanding independence again, and the niche awaits a new trophy. The Traitor’s Niche is a surreal tale of tyranny and rebellion, in a land where armies carry scarecrows, state officials ban entire languages, and the act of forgetting is more complicated than remembering.

title: My German Brother
author: Chico Buarque (trans. by) Alison Entrekin
description: Ciccio... dicovers a decades-old letter ... The letter reveals an illicit affair his father carried on while posted in Nazi-era Berlin, an affair that resulted in the birth of a baby boy. Ciccio develops a fascination for his mysterious German brother.

title: Antisocial Media: How Facebook Disconnects Us and Undermines Democracy
author: Siva Vaidhyanathan
description: In Antisocial Media , Siva Vaidhyanathan explains how Facebook devolved from an innocent social site hacked together by Harvard students into a force that, while it may make personal life just a little more pleasurable, makes democracy a lot more challenging. It's an account of the hubris of good intentions, a missionary spirit, and an ideology that sees computer code as the universal solvent for all human problems.

title: The Book of Essie
author: Meghan MacLean Weir
description: A novel of family, fame, and religion that tells the story of the seventeen-year-old daughter of an evangelical preacher, star of the family's hit reality show, and the secret pregnancy that threatens to blow their entire world apart.

title: The Verdun Affair
author: Nick Dybek
description: Set in Europe in the aftermath of World War I and Los Angeles in the 1950s, The Verdun Affair is about a lonely young man, a beautiful widow, and the amnesiac soldier whose puzzling case binds them together even as it tears them apart.

title: About Betty's Boob
author: Vero Cazot and Julie Rocheleau
