description: After losing her breast to a mastectomy, Betty also loses her boyfriend and job, but she gains a new lease on life after joining a burlesque troupe.

title: Splinter in the Blood
author: Ashley Dyer
description: A debut suspense novel, filled with secrets, tension, mystery, and cold-blooded murder, in which a police officer on the hunt for a serial killer is brutally attacked, and only his partner knows the truth about what happened—and who did it.

title: A Reaper at the Gates
author: Sabaa Tahir
description: Helene Aquilla, the Blood Shrike, is desperate to protect her sister's life and the lives of everyone in the Empire. But she knows that danger lurks on all sides ... Beyond the Martial Empire and within it, the threat of war looms ever larger.

title: Blown
author: Mark Haskell Smith
description: When a Wall Street trader rips off $17 million of his brokerage’s cash, it initiates an island-hopping chase across the Caribbean.

title: The Royal Art of Poison: Filthy Palaces, Fatal Cosmetics, Deadly Medicine, and Murder Most Foul
author: Eleanor Herman
description: A work of pop history that traces the use of poison as a political—and cosmetic—tool in the royal courts of Western Europe from the Middle Ages to the Kremlin today.

title: Ayiti
author: Roxane Gay
description: A set of brief, tart stories mostly set amid the Haitian-American community and circling around themes of violation, abuse, and heartbreak.

title: Tasting the Past: The Science of Flavor and the Search for the Origins of Wine
author: Kevin Begos
description: After a chance encounter with an obscure Middle Eastern red, journalist Kevin Begos embarks on a ten-year journey to seek the origins of wine.

title: Gigged: The End of the Job and the Future of Work
author: Sarah Kessler
description: A business journalist who has written for Quartz and Mashable takes a closer look at the shifting tides of work in the United States, from the norm of a steady nine-to-five to contingent "gigs" that offer workers greater flexibility—and precarity.

title: The Design of Childhood: How the Material World Shapes Independent Kids
author: Alexandra Lange
description: From building blocks to city blocks, an exploration of how children's playthings and physical surroundings affect their development.

title: We Are Where the Nightmares Go and Other Stories
author: C Robert Cargill
description: A collection of short stories that illuminate the strange, humorous, fantastical, and downright diabolical things that tantalize and terrorize us: demons, monsters, zombie dinosaurs, and Death itself.

title: Near-Death Experiences . . . and Others
author: Robert Gottlieb
description: This new collection from editor Robert Gottlieb features twenty or so pieces he’s written mostly for The New York Review of Books , ranging from reconsiderations of American writers such as Dorothy Parker, Thornton Wilder and Thomas Wolfe, the actor-assassin John Wilkes Booth, the movie star Mary Astor, and Donald Trump.

title: Advice for Future Corpses
author: Sallie Tisdale
publisher: Touchstone; First Edition, First Printing edition
description: Sallie Tisdale offers a thought-provoking, yet practical perspective on death and dying in Advice for Future Corpses . Informed by her many years working as a nurse, with more than a decade in palliative care, Tisdale provides a frank and direct meditation on the inevitable.

title: The Strange
author: Jérôme Ruillier
description: The story of one undocumented immigrant’s journey, told by the people who employ him, feed him, and report on him

title: Siren Song: My Life in Music
author: Seymour Stein
description: A memoir detailing the 1966 founding of Sire Records and the author’s journey through six decades in the music industry discovering talent like the Talking Heads , the Ramones , Madonna , and many others.

title: The Tidings of the Trees
author: Wolfgang Hilbig, trans. Isabel Fargo Cole
description: Where once was a beautiful wood now stands a desolate field smothered in ash and garbage, and here a young man named Waller has terrorizing encounters with grotesque figures named 'the garbagemen.'

title: Upstate
author: James Wood
description: A British father goes to visit his daughter, a philosophy professor at an American university, in Upstate New York, where snowy weather keeps the family inside, contemplating the human condition.

title: Florida
author: Lauren Groff
description: In her new collection of short stories, Lauren Groff brings the reader into a physical world that is at once domestic and wild—a place where the hazards of the natural world lie waiting to pounce, yet the greatest threats and mysteries are still of an emotional, psychological nature.

title: Kudos
author: Rachel Cusk
description: The final installment of Cusk's award-winning auto-fictional Outline Trilogy, which sees her observant writer protagonist Faye travel to a European literary festival, where she has a series of conversations with strangers and family.

title: In Search of Mary Shelley: The Girl Who Wrote Frankenstein
author: Fiona Sampson
description: To mark the bicentenary of Frankenstein , this new biography seeks to build a more nuanced portrait of Mary Shelley, particularly her early years and the formative experiences that influenced her authorship of the sui generis novel.

title: Sick: A Memoir
author: Porochista Khakpour
description: The Iranian-born writer and creative writing professor’s memoir of her struggle with trauma, drug addiction, mental illness, and late-stage Lyme disease.

title: There There
author: Tommy Orange
description: Winner of the 2019 National Book Critics Circle John Leonard Prize (for Best First Book), Orange’s debut novel offers a kaleidoscopic look at Native American life in Oakland, California, through the experiences and perspectives of 12 characters.

title: Reporter: A Memoir
author: Seymour M. Hersh
description: A memoir of renowned investigative journalist Seymour Hersh's life as a reporter.

title: Mirror, Shoulder, Signal
author: Dorthe Nors, Trans. by Misha Hoekstra
description: A novel about one woman in search of herself when there’s no one to ask for directions; short-listed for the Man Booker International Prize.

title: Flash: The Making of Weegee the Famous
author: Christopher Bonanos
description: The city editor at New York Magazine and author of Instant: The Story of Polaroid offers a portrait of the elusive Arthur Fellig, or Weegee the Famous—a photographer, psychic, and pioneer. Flash was the recipient of the 2019 National Book Critics Circle Award for Biography.

title: Wait, Blink: A Perfect Picture of Inner Life: A Novel
author: Gunnhild Øyehaug, Trans. by Kari Dickson
description: Wait, Blink is the first English-language translation of award-winning Norwegian author Gunnhild Øyehaug’s novel of interwoven stories following a group of artistic women pursuing their ambitions despite endless distractions and disappointments.

title: Never Anyone But You
author: Rupert Thomson
description: The true story of a love affair between two extraordinary women becomes a literary tour de force in this novel that recreates the surrealist movement in Paris and the horrors of the two world wars with incandescence and intimacy.

title: The World as It Is: A Memoir of the Obama White House
author: Ben Rhodes
description: A former speechwriter looks back on his time in the Obama White House, offering his impressions of the 44th U.S. President and the uneasy political terrain between idealism and reality.

title: How Hard Can It Be?
author: Allison Pearson
description: In this sequel to her bestseller I Don't Know How She Does It , protagonist Kate Reddy is pushing 50 and struggling with menopause, a husband in the throes of a midlife crisis, a daughter who likes to send "sexts," and a lackluster return to the work force.

title: A People's History of the Vampire Uprising
author: Raymond A. Villareal
description: In this fictional oral history, an FBI agent, a war veteran turned nurse, a campaign manager and other key players unravel how a population of vampires, or "Gloamings," rose from a virus run amok to become an elite social group people are dying to join.

title: The Good Mothers: The Story of the Three Women Who Took on the World's Most Powerful Mafia
author: Alex Perry
description: A feminist saga of true crime and justice, The Good Mothers is the story of a high-stakes battle pitting a brilliant, driven woman fighting to save a nation against ruthless mafiosi fighting for their existence. Caught in the middle are three women fighting for their children and their lives. Not all will survive.

title: Tinderbox: The Untold Story of the Up Stairs Lounge Fire and the Rise of Gay Liberation
author: Robert W. Fieseler
description: Buried for decades, the Up Stairs Lounge tragedy has only recently emerged as a catalyzing event of the gay liberation movement. In revelatory detail, Robert W. Fieseler chronicles the tragic event that claimed the lives of 31 men and one woman on June 24, 1973, at a New Orleans bar, the largest mass murder of gays until 2016.

title: Frenemies: The Epic Disruption of the Advertising Industry (and Why This Matters)
author: Ken Auletta
description: Frenemies is Ken Auletta's reckoning with an industry under existential assault. He enters the rooms of the ad world's most important players, some of them business partners, some adversaries, many "frenemies," a term whose ubiquitous use in this industry reveals the level of anxiety, as former allies become competitors, and accusations of kickbacks and corruption swirl.

title: Unbound: Transgender Men and the Remaking of Identity
author: Arlene Stein
description: An intimate portrait of a new generation of transmasculine individuals as they undergo gender transitions. Award-winning sociologist Arlene Stein takes us into the lives of four strangers who find themselves together in a sun-drenched surgeon’s office, having traveled to Florida from across the United States in order to masculinize their chests.

title: Goodbye, Sweet Girl
author: Kelly Sundberg
description: Kelly Sundberg chronicles how her marriage devolved from a love story into a shocking tale of abuse—examining the tenderness and violence entwined in the relationship, why she endured years of physical and emotional pain, and how she eventually broke free.

title: Tonight I'm Someone Else
author: Chelsea Hodson
description: In this collection of essays, Chelsea Hodson probes her own desires to examine where the physical and the proprietary collide. She asks what our privacy, our intimacy, and our own bodies are worth in the increasingly digital world of liking, linking, and sharing.

title: The Lost Family
author: Jenna Blum
description: The New York Times bestselling author of Those Who Save Us creates a vivid portrait of marriage, family, and the haunting grief of World War II in this narrative that spans a generation, from the 1960s to the 1980s.

title: The Good Son
author: You-Jeong Jeong, Translated by Chi-Young Kim
description: Early one morning, Yu-jin wakes up covered in blood and discovers his mother's murdered body, lying in a pool of blood at the bottom of the stairs of their stylish Seoul duplex. He can't remember much about the night before; having suffered from seizures for most of his life, Yu-jin often has trouble with his memory. The Good Son explores the mysteries of mind and memory, and the twisted relationship between a mother and son.

title: The Kiss Quotient
author: Helen Hoang
description: The Kiss Quotient is about an autistic woman who takes a methodical approach to learning about sex that results in an unexpected lesson in love. In her debut novel, Hoang offers that math may not be the only thing that unites the universe as predictive algorithms challenge inexplicable emotions.

title: Brother in Ice
author: Alicia Kopf, Trans. by Mara Faye Lethmen
description: This hybrid novel―part research notes, part fictionalized diary, and part travelogue―uses the stories of polar exploration to make sense of the protagonist’s own concerns as she comes of age as an artist, a daughter, and a sister to an autistic brother.

title: Rising in Flames: Sherman's March and the Fight for a New Nation
author: J D Dickey
description: In Rising in Flames , Dickey expounds the details of William Sherman's legendary march through Georgia—including crippling the heart of the South's economy, freeing thousands of slaves, and marking the beginning of a new era.

title: The Word is Murder
author: Anthony Horowitz
description: The New York Times bestselling author of Magpie Murders and Moriarty , Anthony Horowitz continues to reinvent the classic crime novel, this time writing a fictional version of himself as the Watson to a modern-day Holmes.

title: When Life Gives You Lululemons
author: Lauren Weisberger
description: Lauren Weisberger drops Emily Charlton, Miranda Priestly’s uber catty assistant from The Devil Wears Prada , into the suburbs of Connecticut. Emily, now in her 30s, is living in Los Angeles with a husband and a career as an image consultant—a career that is suddenly floundering—when she gets a desperate summons to Greenwich, Connecticut.

title: Invitation to a Bonfire
author: Adrienne Celt
description: The story of a dangerous love triangle, inspired by the infamous Nabokov marriage, with a psychological thriller at its core.

title: Strange Stars: David Bowie, Pop Music, and the Decade Sci-Fi Exploded
author: Jason Heller
description: A Hugo Award-winning author and music journalist explores the weird and wild story of when rock ’n’ roll met the sci-fi world of the 1970s.

title: Social Creature
author: Tara Isabella Burton
description: A novel about a small-town girl trying to survive in New York and become part of the city's literati, who forms an intense friendship with a troubled socialite, leading to extreme consequences.

title: The Third Bank of the River: Power and Survival in the Twenty-First-Century Amazon
author: Chris Feliciano Arnold
description: A sweeping look at the war over the Amazon―as activists, locals, and indigenous tribes struggle to save it from the threat of loggers, drug lords, and corrupt cops and politicians.

title: Half Gods
author: Akin Kumarasamy
description: Half Gods brings together the exiled, the disappeared, and the seekers. Following the fractured origins and destines of two brothers named after demigods from the ancient epic the Mahabharata, readers become close with a family struggling with the reverberations of the past in their lives.

title: Those Wild Wyndhams: Three Sisters at the Heart of Power
author: Claudia Renton
description: Claudia Renton's debut book is a detailed portrait of three dazzlingly beautiful, wildly rich Wyndham sisters. These women are part of the four hundred families that made up Britain's ruling class, at the center of cultural and political life in late-Victorian/Edwardian Britain. captures their complex, idiosyncratic lives; their opulent, privileged world; their romantic, roiling age.

title: Still Lives
author: Maria Hummel
description: When a provocative painter goes missing on the opening night of her L.A. show about the media coverage of famous murdered women, a museum copywriter falls back on her investigative roots.

title: Southernmost
author: Silas House
description: After years of work and worship in a rural Tennessee evangelical congregation, pastor Asher Sharp begins to doubt his faith when he alone offers help to a local gay couple in the wake of a devastating flood, leading to a crisis in his marriage and a sudden separation from his only son. Unwilling to let Justin live with his mother, Asher absconds with his son to Key West in search of his estranged brother, Luke.

title: The Book of M
author: Peng Shepherd
description: One afternoon at an outdoor market in India, a man’s shadow disappears—an occurrence science cannot explain. He is only the first. The phenomenon spreads like a plague, and while those afflicted gain a strange new power, it comes at a horrible price: the loss of all their memories.

title: What Truth Sounds Like: Robert F. Kennedy, James Baldwin, and Our Unfinished Conversation about Race in America
author: Michael Eric Dyson
description: What Truth Sounds Like examines the events surrounding the 1963 meeting between Robert F. Kennedy and James Baldwin in New York City, as well as its impact on race relations in the United States from then to now.

title: Lorna Simpson Collages
author: Lorna Simpson
description: Using advertising photographs of black women (and men) drawn from vintage issues of Ebony and Jet magazines, the collages of world-renowned artist Lorna Simpson explore the richly nuanced language of hair.

title: How Democracy Ends
author: David Runciman
description: In How Democracy Ends , David Runciman argues that we are trapped in outdated twentieth-century ideas of democratic failure. We need new ways of thinking the unthinkable-a twenty-first-century vision of the end of democracy, and whether its collapse might allow us to move forward to something better.

title: Small Country
author: Gaël Faye, Trans. by Sarah Ardizzone
description: The bestselling debut novel by French-Rwandan rapper Faye. An evocative coming-of-age story set in Burundi in 1992, about a young boy, a lost childhood and a shattered homeland.

title: Us Against You
author: Fredrik Backman
description: Beartown is home to tough, hardworking people who don’t expect life to be easy or fair. Yet, no matter how difficult times get, they’ve always been able to take pride in their local ice hockey team. The big game approaches between Beartown and rival town Hed, but by the time the last goal is scored, a resident of Beartown will be dead.

title: My Girls
author: Todd Fisher
description: A tribute to the lives of Carrie Fisher and Debbie Reynolds written by the person who knew them best, Todd Fisher's poignant memoir is filled with stories of growing up among Hollywood royalty and illustrated with never-before-seen photos and memorabilia.

title: Something in the Water
author: Catherine Steadman
description: Newlyweds – Mark and Erin – embark on a dream honeymoon to the tropical island of Bora Bora, where they enjoy the sun, the sand, and each other. Then, while scuba diving in the crystal blue sea, they find something in the water. Suddenly the newlyweds must make a dangerous choice: to speak out or to protect their secret.

title: Sweet and Low: Stories
author: Nick White
description: In these stories, Nick White deconstructs the core qualities of Southern fiction, exposing deeply flawed and fascinating characters--promiscuous academics, aging podcasters, woodpecker assassins, and lawnmower enthusiasts, among others.

title: Death Notice, Translated by Zac Haluza
author: Haohui Zhou
description: An elite police squad hunts a manipulative mastermind out to publically execute criminals the law cannot reach. A thriller and deadly game of cat-and-mouse from one of China's most popular authors.

title: The Captives
author: Debra Jo Immergut
description: The story of a woman convicted of a brutal crime, the prison psychologist who recognizes her as his high-school crush—and the charged reunion that sets off a chain of events with dangerous consequences for both.

title: A Stone's Throw: An Ellie Stone Mystery
author: James W. Ziskin
description: August 1962. A suspicious fire claims a tumbledown foaling barn on the grounds of the once-proud Tempesta Stud Farm, halfway between New Holland and Saratoga Springs, NY. The blaze, one of several in recent years at the abandoned farm, barely prompts a shrug from the local sheriff. That is until 'girl reporter' Ellie Stone, first on the scene, uncovers a singed length of racing silk in the rubble of the barn. And it's wrapped around the neck of one of two charred bodies buried in the ashes.

title: Lincoln's Last Trial: The Murder Case That Propelled Him to the Presidency (Original)
author: Dan Abrams and David Fisher
description: Twenty-two-year-old Peachy Quinn Harrison went on trial for murder in Springfield, Illinois. Abraham Lincoln, who had been involved in more than three thousand cases-including more than twenty-five murder trials-during his two-decades-long career, was hired to defend him. This was to be his last great case as a lawyer.

title: Vanishing Frontiers: The Forces Driving Mexico and the United States Together
author: Andrew D Selee
description: Wall or no wall, deeply intertwined social, economic, business, cultural, and personal relationships mean the US-Mexico border is more like a seam than a barrier, weaving together two economies and cultures.

title: American Eden: David Hosack, Botany, and Medicine in the Garden of the Early Republic
author: Victoria Johnson
description: The untold story of Hamilton’s―and Burr’s―personal physician, whose dream to build America’s first botanical garden inspired the young Republic.

title: Sex and the City and Us: How Four Single Women Changed the Way We Think, Live, and Love
author: Jennifer Keishin Armstrong
description: A look back at the development, writing, filmmaking, and cultural influence of Sex and the City 20 years after it first aired on HBO.

title: Autumn in Venice: Ernest Hemingway and His Last Muse
author: Andrea di Robilant
description: The story of Hemingway's love affair with both the city of Venice and the muse he found there—a vivacious eighteen-year-old who inspired the man thirty years her senior to complete his great final work.

title: London Rules
author: Mick Herron
description: In the latest in the Gold and Steel-Dagger-winning Slough House series, MI5 agents are struggling with personal problems: repressed grief, various addictions, retail paralysis, and the nagging suspicion that their newest colleague is a psychopath. Plus someone is trying to kill Roddy Ho. But collectively, they're about to rediscover their greatest strength—that of making a bad situation much, much worse.

title: The Secret Token: Myth, Obsession, and the Search for the Lost Colony of Roanoke
author: Andrew Lawler
description: A sweeping account of America's oldest unsolved mystery, the people racing to unearth its answer, and the sobering truths-about race, gender, and immigration-exposed by the Lost Colony of Roanoke

title: The Comeback: Greg Lemond, the True King of American Cycling, and a Legendary Tour de France
author: Daniel de Vise
description: Greg LeMond stunned the sporting world by becoming the first American to win the Tour de France...nine months later, LeMond lay in a hospital bed, his life in peril, his career as a bicycle racer seemingly over.

title: First in Line: Presidents, Vice Presidents, and the Pursuit of Power
author: Kate Andersen Brower
description: explores the lives and roles of thirteen vice presidents of the modern era, discussing the complicated relationship between president and vice president and how this connection influenced each vice president's political future.

title: Days of Awe: Stories
author: A. M. Homes
description: With her signature humor and compassion, A.M. Homes exposes the heart of an uneasy America in her new collection - exploring our attachments to each other through characters who aren't quite who they hoped to become, though there is no one else they can be.

title: Rough Beauty: Forty Seasons of Mountain Living
author: Karen Auvinen
description: A memoir from an award-winning poet who ventures into the wilderness to seek answers to life's big questions and finds her way back after losing everything she thought she needed

title: Tiny Crimes: Very Short Tales of Mystery and Murder
author: Ed. by Lincoln Michel & Nadxieli Nieto
description: Forty flash fiction tales of murder and mystery from authors such as Amelia Gray, Brian Evenson, Elizabeth Hand, Carmen Maria Machado, Benjamin Percy, Laura van den Berg and more.

title: Mother American Night: My Life in Crazy Times
author: John Perry Barlow and Robert Greenfield
description: Tales of the hippie highway by Grateful Dead lyricist and internet pioneer Barlow.

title: Bruce Lee: A Life
author: Matthew Polly
description: A biography—featuring dozens of rarely seen photographs—of film legend Bruce Lee, who made martial arts a global phenomenon, bridged the divide between Eastern and Western cultures, and smashed long-held stereotypes of Asians and Asian-Americans.

title: The Terrible: A Storyteller's Memoir
author: Yrsa Daley-Ward
description: In a mix of poetry and prose, Yrsa Daley-Ward narrates her life story from its "terrible" childhood and young adulthood through her discovery of art and greater balance.

title: Homelands: Four Friends, Two Countries, and the Fate of the Great Mexican-American Migration
author: Alfredo Corchado
description: A México Border correspondent for The Dallas Morning News reflects on the United States' complicated relationship with its neighbor to the south as well as his and his friends' experiences as Mexican immigrants.

title: In the Distance with You
author: Carla Guelfenbein, Trans. by John Cullen
description: Winner of the prestigious Spanish-language Alfaguara Prize in 2015, this novel pivots around an aging cult novelist—modeled on Clarice Lispector—and several characters whose identities are mysteriously intertwined with the writer.

title: Brief Cases
author: Jim Butcher
description: An all-new Dresden Files story headlines this urban fantasy short story collection starring the Windy City’s favorite wizard.

title: Night-Gaunts and Other Tales of Suspense
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: A collection reveling in the uncanny and in conversation with other creative minds, Night-Gaunts and Other Tales of Suspense interrogates human impulses.

title: Sweet Black Waves
author: Kristina Pérez
description: Debut author Pérez launches a lush fantasy trilogy about about warring countries, family secrets, and star-crossed lovers – and a young woman gifted with magical healing abilities that evolve beyond her control.

title: The Last Lobster: Boom or Bust for Maine's Greatest Fishery?
author: Christopher White
description: An environmental journalist turns in a somber story of vanishing fisheries and ways of life Down East.

title: Visible Empire
author: Hannah Pittard
description: The real-life crash of a charter plane full of Atlanta's white elite is the inspiration for a fictional examination of race, class, love, and betrayal.

title: Subscribed: Why the Subscription Model Will Be Your Company's Future - And What to Do about It
author: Tien Tzuo
description: Tzuo shows how to use subscriptions to build lucrative, ongoing one-on-one relationships with your customers. This may require reinventing substantial parts of your company, from your accounting practices to your entire IT architecture, but the payoff can be enormous.

title: Rivers
author: Martin Michael Driessen, Trans. by Jon Reeder
description: Three stories spanning countries and eras, but they are all connected by, and reliant on, the unpredictable power and languid beauty of rivers that give life as quickly as they take it away.

title: Long Players: A Love Story in Eighteen Songs
author: Peter Coviello
description: A passionate, heartfelt story about the many ways we fall in love: with books, bands and records, friends and lovers, and the families we make.

title: Major Dudes: A Steely Dan Companion
author: Barney Hoskyns
description: The ultimate anthology of Steely Dan, one of the defining and bestselling rock acts of the last half-century

title: The Wreckage of Eden
author: Norman Lock
description: A nineteenth-century army chaplain confesses his loss of faith in god and country to his first love, poet Emily Dickinson.

title: Oceans Ventured: Winning the Cold War at Sea
author: John Lehman
description: The former Secretary of the Navy under U.S. President Ronald Reagan recounts the Navy's decisive role in ending the Cold War, bolstering his narrative with recently declassified documents.

title: A Little Piece of Light: A Memoir of Hope, Prison, and a Life Unbound
author: Donna Hylton with Kristine Gasbarre
description: From her life as an abused child and young adult to her transformation into a criminal justice-reform activist, a woman recounts her self-reinvention in prison, where she served more than 25 years for her role in a kidnapping and second-degree murder.

title: The Emperor of Shoes
author: Spencer Wise
description: From a new voice in literary fiction, a transfixing story about an expatriate in southern China and his burgeoning relationship with a seamstress intent on inspiring dramatic political change.

title: No Good Alternative: Volume Two of Carbon Ideologies
author: William T. Vollmann
description: An eye-opening look at the consequences of coal mining and oil and natural gas production—the second of a two volume work by award-winning author William T. Vollmann on the ideologies of energy production and the causes of climate change

title: The Optickal Illusion
author: Rachel Halliburton
description: A debut novel brimming with envy, lust, and corruption at the heart of eighteenth century London's art world

title: Nine Lives: My Time as the West's Top Spy Inside Al-Qaeda
author: Aimen Dean
description: As one of al-Qaeda’s most respected scholars and bomb-makers, Aimen Dean rubbed shoulders with the mastermind of the 9/11 attacks and swore allegiance to Osama bin Laden himself. His job was already one of the most dangerous in the world. But what the others didn’t know was that he was working undercover for MI6.

title: This Young Monster
author: Charlie Fox
description: This Young Monster is a hallucinatory celebration of artists who raise hell, transform their bodies, anger their elders and show their audience dark, disturbing things. What does it mean to be a freak? Why might we be wise to think of the present as a time of monstrosity? And how does the concept of the monster irradiate our thinking about queerness, disability, children and adolescents? This Young Monster gets high on a whole range of riotous art as its voice and form shape-shift, all in the name of dealing with the strange wonders of what Nabokov once called ‘monsterhood’. Ready or not, here they come...

title: The President Is Missing
author: Bill Clinton & James Patterson
publisher: Little, Brown and Company and Knopf
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: President Bill Clinton partners with bestselling author James Patterson in a thriller about an under-fire president who goes undercover to try and foil a cyberterrorism plot.

title: Orca: How We Came to Know and Love the Ocean's Greatest Predator
author: Jason M. Colby
description: Drawing on interviews, official records, private archives, and his own family history, Jason M. Colby tells the story of how people came to love the ocean's greatest predator. Historically reviled as dangerous pests, killer whales were dying by the hundreds, even thousands, by the 1950s–the victims of whalers, fishermen, and even the US military.

title: Accidentally Like a Martyr: The Tortured Art of Warren Zevon
author: James Campion
description: Drawing on interviews with singer-songwriter Warren Zevon’s family, friends, and industry associates, as well as on secondary resources, journalist Campion explores 10 songs and three albums that he believes offer the best insight into Zevon’s life and art.

title: A Handbook of Disappointed Fate
author: Anne Boyer
description: A collection of the Whiting award-winning poet Anne Boyer's interrogative writing on poetry, capitalism, death, love, lambs, and other impossible questions.

title: Calypso
author: David Sedaris
description: From the veteran humorist, a collection of deeply personal, darkly funny essays focusing on middle age and mortality.

title: The Death of Mrs. Westaway
author: Ruth Ware
description: When Hal is mistakenly informed that she has inherited a fortune, she plays the part of the heiress in order to pay off her debts, a ruse that lands her at the center of a mysterious and frightening series of events.

title: Some Trick: Thirteen Stories
author: Helen DeWitt
description: From the author of The Last Samurai and Lightning Rods , Helen DeWitt returns with a collection of stories that explore the peculiar mind of the creative genius and the headache-inducing social and capitalistic systems with which it must contend.

title: No Ashes in the Fire: Coming of Age Black and Free in America
author: Darnell L. Moore
description: A journalist and Black Lives Matter activist recounts his difficult adolescence in Camden, NJ, where poverty and institutional racism undergirded the violence and homophobia he faced as a young queer person determined to make his life count.

title: Energy: A Human History
author: Richard Rhodes
description: The Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award-winning author of The Making of the Atomic Bomb takes a broader look at power in his latest, tracing five centuries of human energy development from coal to solar and some of the lesser-known technologies that cropped up along the way.

title: Shelter in Place
author: Nora Roberts
description: It was a typical evening at a mall outside Portland, Maine. Then the shooters arrived. The chaos and carnage lasted only eight minutes before the killers were taken down. But for those who lived through it, the effects would last forever.

title: To the Moon and Back
author: Karen Kingsbury
description: This is a story of two people who lost their parents in the same national tragedy—two people desperate to find each other and the connection they shared in a day that changed everything.

title: She Has Her Mother's Laugh: The Powers, Perversions, and Potential of Heredity
author: Carl Zimmer
description: Award-winning New York Times columnist and science writer Carl Zimmer presents his perspective on what we pass along from generation to generation.

title: Tailspin: The People and Forces Behind America's Fifty-Year Fall—And Those Fighting to Reverse It
author: Steven Brill
description: An examination of 1) how and why major American institutions no longer serve us as they should, causing a deep rift between the vulnerable majority and the protected few, and 2) how some individuals and organizations are laying the foundation for real, lasting change.

title: My Brother Moochie: Regaining Dignity in the Face of Crime, Poverty, and Racism in the American South
author: Issac J. Bailey
description: At the age of nine, Issac J. Bailey saw his hero, his eldest brother, taken away in handcuffs, not to return from prison for thirty-two years. Bailey tells the story of their relationship and of his experience living in a family suffering from guilt and shame.

title: The Dante Chamber
author: Matthew Pearl
description: In the follow-up to his popular The Dante Club , Pearl enlists Christina Rossetti, Robert Browning, Alfred Tennyson, and Dr. Oliver Wendell Holmes to decipher literary clues that may solve a series of murders in London, the next victim of which may be Rossetti's brother Gabriel.

title: Too Wilde to Wed
author: Eloisa James
description: In the latest in the Wildes of Lindow Castle series, Lord Roland Northbridge Wilde is surprised after time away from home to find his ex-fiancé working as a governess at his family's castle, and he's determined to win her back.

title: Ten Arguments for Deleting Your Social Media Accounts Right Now
author: Jaron Lanier
description: A virtual reality pioneer makes a case for saying goodbye to Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and their ilk, which he calls addictive and blames for undermining real-world relationships and institutions.

title: The Honey Farm: A Novel
author: Harriet Alida Lye
description: Lily King meets Patricia Highsmith in this slyly seductive debut set on an eerily beautiful farm teeming with secrets.

title: There Are No Grown-Ups: A Midlife Coming-Of-Age Story
author: Pamela Druckerman
description: The author confronts the realities of being forty, examining how the modern forties are less associated with midlife than in the past and discussing the disconnects of social media, the French perspectives about libido, and the challenges of raising kids while caring for aging parents.

title: The Wind in My Hair: My Fight for Freedom in Modern Iran
author: Masih Alinejad
description: A memoir from an Iranian journalist in exile about leaving her country, challenging tradition and sparking an online movement against compulsory hijab.

title: See You Again in Pyongyang: A Journey Into Kim Jong Un's North Korea
author: Travis Jeppesen
description: The first American to complete a university program in North Korea recounts his experience living under a dictatorship, where his status as a foreigner segregated him from much of the native population and kept him under the constant watch of tour guides.

title: Armand V
author: Dag Solstad, Trans. by Steven T. Murray
description: From a three-time winner of the Norwegian Critics’ Prize for Literature, 99 "footnotes" stand in for a novel the reader is told is missing, unfolding bits of narrative and observations about the title character, a disillusioned Norwegian diplomat.

title: T Singer
author: Dag Solstad, Trans. by Tiina Nunnally
description: A winner of the Norwegian Critics Prize for Literature, this novel follows a librarian as he ruminates about his failed writing career, troubled friendships, and relationship with his wife and daughter.

title: The Summer I Met Jack
author: Michelle Gable
description: A fictionalized account of Alicia Corning Clark, the Polish refugee who became a New York socialite, and her 1950s love affair with John F. Kennedy.

title: Never Lost Again: The Google Mapping Revolution That Sparked New Industries and Augmented Our Reality
author: Bill Kilday
description: The behind-the-scenes narrative of the creation of Google Maps and the rag-tag team that built it and changed how the world navigates.

title: Sexographies
author: Gabriela Wiener, trans. by Jennifer Adcock and Lucy Greaves
description: Renowned Peruvian journalist Gabriela Wiener records infiltrating the most dangerous Peruvian prison, participating in sexual exchanges in swingers clubs, and more—all while exploring immigration, maternity, fear of death, ugliness, and threesomes.

title: The Outsider
author: Stephen King
description: From horror master Stephen King, a monster story wrapped in a police procedural. After Detective Ralph Anderson arrests a popular local Little League coach for the gristly murder of a young boy, the case take an even darker, altogether more supernatural turn.

title: Cult X
author: Fuminori Nakamura, Trans. by Kalau Almony
description: From Japanese literary crime sensation Fuminori Nakamura, a novel about a man whose search for his missing girlfriend leads him to a sinister, sex-obsessed cult in the heart of Tokyo.

title: Sabrina
author: Nick Drnaso
description: Sabrina is LA Times Book Prize winner Nick Drnaso's second novel and rendering of a sterile, modern world, where relationships are without intimacy and meaning is lost through glowing computer screens. In this graphic novel, Drnaso confronts and criticizes our modern world and its byproducts (namely fake news).

title: The High Season
author: Judy Blundell
description: A drama unfolds on Memorial Day weekend in a seaside town on Long Island, where protagonist Ruthie contends with trouble in love, work and with her teenage daughter, whose secret relationship has the whiff of danger.

title: The Glitch
author: Elisabeth Cohen
description: A highly ambitious Silicon Valley CEO thinks her life is under control until she loses her young daughter and, on the 20th anniversary of her strike by lightning, she meets someone who appears to be, literally, a younger version of herself.

title: Star of the North
author: D. B. John
description: In this thriller confronting North Korea's brutal dictatorship, readers follow three interwoven storylines: a CIA operative in search of her sister, whom she suspects was kidnapped by the regime, a North Korean peasant, and an elite North Korean Diplomat whose family ties to a political dissident threaten his livelihood and life.

title: The Restless Wave: Good Times, Just Causes, Great Fights, and Other Appreciations
author: John McCain and Mark Salter
description: Written while confronting a mortal illness, McCain looks back with appreciation on his years in the Senate, his historic 2008 campaign for the presidency against Barack Obama, and his crusades on behalf of democracy and human rights in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

title: A View of the Empire at Sunset
author: Caryl Phillips
description: From the author of The Lost Child , a fictionalized account of the tumultuous early decades of Jean Rhys's life in Europe, where the author of Wide Sargasso Sea moved from the Caribbean at 16.

title: Ruthless Tide: The Heroes and Villains of the Johnstown Flood, America's Astonishing Gilded Age Disaster
author: Al Roker
description: A new history celebrating the heroes of the Johnstown Flood—the deadliest flood in U.S. history—from NBC host and weather authority Al Roker.

title: Chosen Country: A Rebellion in the West
author: James Pogue
description: An inside look at America’s militia movement that shows a country at the crossroads of class, culture, and insurrection.

title: Facts and Fears: Hard Truths from a Life in Intelligence
author: James R. Clapper
description: The Pentagon's top intelligence official under presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama, Clapper recounts his lengthy career in Washington and sounds a warning about weakened democracy under President Donald Trump, who he argues owes his office to the interference of Russia in the 2016 U.S. election.

title: 84K
author: Claire North
description: In this dystopian novel, The Company has taken over all aspects of life, and anything goes as long as you're willing to pay for it—including criminal activity such as assault and murder.

title: The Unknowns: The Untold Story of America's Unknown Soldier and Wwi's Most Decorated Heroes Who Brought Him Home
author: Patrick K O'Donnell
description: The award-winning author of Washington's Immortals profiles the World War I soldiers involved in the selection and interment of the Unknown Soldier in Arlington National Cemetery.

title: Origin Story: A Big History of Everything
author: David Christian
description: In Origin Story , Christian takes readers on a ride through the entire 13.8 billion years we've come to know as 'history.'

title: Sh*tshow!: The Country's Collapsing . . . and the Ratings Are Great
author: Charlie Leduff
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist sets off on a trip across the country to document what he sees as an unraveling nation, stopping in Ferguson, Flint, Cliven Bundy's ranch, and Donald Trump's campaign for the Presidency.

title: Proust's Duchess: How Three Celebrated Women Captured the Imagination of Fin-De-Siecle Paris
author: Caroline Weber
description: A look at the glittering world of turn-of-the-century Paris through a study of the three aristocrat women Marcel Proust used to create his supreme fictional character, the Duchesse de Guermantes of In Search of Lost Time .

title: MEM
author: Bethany C. Morrow
description: A young woman’s personality is the result of a startling experimental procedure, leaving her to struggle with the question of who she really is.

title: Rock Steady: Brilliant Advice from My Bipolar Life
author: Ellen Forney
description: Rock Steady is a self-help survival guide of tips, tricks, and tools on how to survive being bipolar by someone who has been through it all and come out stronger in the end.

title: Taty Went West
author: Nikhil Singh
description: A teenage runaway gets kidnapped and must confront inner and outer demons in a chaotic world full of evangelizing robot nuns, Buddhist punks, and the ominous Dr. Dali.

title: Last Instructions: A Thriller
author: Nir Hezroni
description: Agent 10483, a psychopathic former Israeli spy, is busy trying to shut down the spy organization he once worked for and plotting his revenge against the key individuals who he deems responsible for the Organization’s betrayal against him. Now, he's traveling the world in a quest to find a hidden nuclear warhead to use against them.

title: Harvey Milk: His Lives and Death
author: Lillian Faderman
description: A lively and engaging biography of the first openly gay man elected to public office in the United States, a man fiercely committed to protecting all minorities

title: Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup
author: John Carreyrou
description: A Pulitzer Prize winning reporter at The Wall Street Journal charts the rise and fall of Theranos, one of Silicon Valley's hottest health-care startups that, after attracting hundreds of millions of dollars in investment from the likes of Joe Biden and Betsy DeVos, turned out to be a fraud

title: Rome: A History in Seven Sackings
author: Matthew Kneale
description: A sprawling city with an ancient history, Rome defies a neat narrative of its past.

title: The Ashtray (or the Man Who Denied Reality)
author: Errol Morris
description: In 1972, philosopher of science Thomas Kuhn threw an ashtray at Errol Morris. This book is the result.

title: Robin
author: Dave Itzkoff
description: From New York Times culture reporter Dave Itzkoff, an in-depth biography of brilliant-but-troubled comedian and actor Robin Williams, who took his own life in 2014.

title: A Shout in the Ruins
author: Kevin Powers
description: Set in Virginia during the Civil War and a century beyond, this novel explores the brutal legacy of violence and exploitation in American society as it examines the fates of the inhabitants of Beauvais Plantation and their descendants.

title: Last Stories
author: William Trevor
description: In these 10 posthumous tales by the esteemed Irish writer, ordinary people confront obstacles ranging from death to adultery with their own peculiar outlooks and coping mechanisms.

title: Chernobyl: The History of a Nuclear Catastrophe
author: Serhii Plokhy
description: Award-winning author and Harvard history professor Serhii Plokhy unravels the political and industrial mistakes and obfuscations that resulted in the worst nuclear disaster in world history, the explosion of a reactor at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Soviet Ukraine on April 26, 1986.

title: How It Happened
author: Michael Koryta
description: After a troubled teen, no stranger to the law, admits to her involvement in a brutal murder, Rob Barrett, an FBI investigator and interrogator stakes his reputation on her confession only to have the information she provided prove false.

title: When Einstein Walked with Gödel: Excursions to the Edge of Thought
author: Jim Holt
description: A collection of essays on some of the game-changing ideas in philosophy, mathematics, and science, and the people who thought them up.

title: Familiar Things
author: Hwang Sok-Yong
description: From one of South Korea's foremost writers, an examination of the darker side of modernization through the micro-society of a rubbish dump and a haunting reminder to us all to be careful of what we throw away.

title: How to Change Your Mind: What the New Science of Psychedelics Teaches Us about Consciousness, Dying, Addiction, Depression, and Transcendence
author: Michael Pollan
description: The bestselling author of The Omnivore's Dilemma explores the history and resurgence of LSD and psilocybin as medicinal treatments for depression, addiction, and anxiety as well as sources of spiritual enlightenment, with which Pollan documents his own experiences.

title: Tin Man
author: Sarah Winman
description: From internationally bestselling author Sarah Winman comes an unforgettable and heartbreaking novel celebrating love in all its forms, and the little moments that make up the life of one man.

title: The Ensemble
author: Aja Gabel
description: Forging a familial bond over their shared artistic talents and secrets, four young people navigate a cutthroat world and their complex relationships with each other, as ambition, passion, and love reinforce and divide them throughout the course of their lives.

title: The Favorite Sister
author: Jessica Knoll
description: When five hyper-successful women agree to appear on a reality series set in New York City called Goal Diggers , the producers never expect the season will end in murder…

title: Saving Central Park: A History and a Memoir
author: Elizabeth Barlow Rogers
description: The story of how one woman's long love affair with New York's Central Park led her to organize its rescue from a state of serious decline, returning it to the beautiful place of recreational opportunity and spiritual sustenance that it is today.

title: Pops: Fatherhood in Pieces
author: Michael Chabon
description: For the September 2016 issue of GQ , Michael Chabon wrote a piece about accompanying his son, then thirteen, to Paris Men’s Fashion Week. What emerged was a deep respect for his son's passion. The piece quickly became a viral sensation. Using that story as a centerpiece, this collection of essays explores the meaning of fatherhood.

title: When the Center Held: Gerald Ford and the Rescue of the American Presidency
author: Donald Rumsfeld
description: A political memoir of the presidency of Gerald Ford as seen through the eyes of Donald Rumsfeld, Ford's former secretary of defense, chief of staff, and longtime personal confidant.

title: Damnation Island: Poor, Sick, Mad, and Criminal in 19th-Century New York
author: Stacy Horn
description: On a two-mile stretch of land in New York’s East River, a 19th-century horror story was unfolding: Blackwell's, the site of a lunatic asylum, two prisons, an almshouse, and a number of hospitals. Conceived as the most modern, humane incarceration facility the world ever seen, Blackwell’s Island quickly became, in the words of a visiting Charles Dickens, “a lounging, listless madhouse.”

title: The Lives of the Surrealists
author: Desmond Morris
description: A 90-year-old zoologist and Surrealist painter offers a collection of biographical essays on Marcel Duchamp, Salvador Dalí, and other Surrealist artists, many of whom he knew personally.

title: The Last Cowboys: A Pioneer Family in the New West
author: John Branch
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist writes about his three years with a family that is trying to make ends meet on a Utah ranch by dabbling in the rodeo, unfurling a history of the American West in the process.

title: Three Days in Moscow: Ronald Reagan and the Fall of the Soviet Empire
author: Bret Baier, Catherine Whitney
description: From Fox News anchor Baier, a nostalgic account of the Reagan era and the end of the Cold War.

title: Letters to My Palestinian Neighbor
author: Yossi Klein Halevi
description: Attempting to break the impasse between Israelis and Palestinians, the Israeli commentator and award-winning author of Like Dreamers directly addresses his Palestinian neighbors.

title: I'm Keith Hernandez: A Memoir
author: Keith Hernandez
description: An assessment of the game's past, present, and future-a memoir that showcases one of baseball's most unique and experienced minds at his very best.

title: So Lucky
author: Nicola Griffith
description: An autobiographical novel about a confident woman forced to confront an unnerving new reality when in the space of a single week her wife leaves her and she is diagnosed with multiple sclerosis.

title: The Trials of Nina McCall: Sex, Surveillance, and the Decades-Long Government Plan to Imprison "Promiscuous" Women
author: Scott W. Stern
description: The nearly forgotten story of the American Plan, a government program to regulate women's bodies and sexuality—and how they fought back—told through the lens of one of its survivors.

title: Paper Ghosts: A Novel of Suspense
author: Julia Heaberlin
description: A woman takes a road trip across Texas with an elderly man with dementia, hoping to awaken secrets about the death of her sister, whom she believes the man murdered despite being acquitted for the crime.

title: Kickflip Boys: A Memoir of Freedom, Rebellion, and the Chaos of Fatherhood
author: Neal Thompson
description: What makes a good father, and what makes one a failure? Does less-is-more parenting inspire independence and strength, or does it encourage defiance and trouble? Kickflip Boys is the story of a father’s struggle to understand his willful skateboarder sons, challengers of authority and convention, to accept his role as a vulnerable “skate dad,” and to confront his fears that the boys are destined for an unconventional and potentially fraught future.

title: As Time Goes By
author: Derek Taylor
description: First published in 1973, this re-release offers an insider's account of the 1960s music industry by one of the Beatles' most trusted friends and a new foreword by Jon Savage.

title: Do This for Me
author: Eliza Kennedy
description: A high-powered attorney and mother of two disastrously self-destructs when her husband's affair comes to light.

title: In Praise of Wasting Time
author: Alan P Lightman
description: Professor Alan Lightman investigates the creativity born from allowing our minds to freely roam, without attempting to accomplish anything and without any assigned tasks.

title: Imperial Twilight: The Opium War and the End of China's Last Golden Age
author: Stephen R. Platt
description: A look into 18th and 19th century attempts by Western interests to "open" China and the first Opium War that ultimately brought down China's position as the world's dominant power.

title: The Flying Tigers: The Untold Story of the American Pilots Who Waged a Secret War Against Japan
author: Sam Kleiner
description: Before the United States officially entered World War II, the country secretly sent American pilots to China to help its defense against the Japanese.

title: Bullshit Jobs: A Theory
author: David Graeber
description: London School of Economics anthropologist Graeber makes argument against the rise of meaningless, unfulfilling jobs, and their consequences.

title: The Queen of Sorrow: Book Three of the Queens of Renthia
author: Sarah Beth Durst
description: In this finale of the Queens of Renthia trilogy, Naelin's children are kidnapped by spirits and, blaming the defeated Queen Merecot of Semo for the kidnapping, Naelin is ready to start a war.

title: All the Answers
author: Michael Kupperman
description: The Eisner Award-winning writer and artist tries to uncover details about his secretive father's experiences as a once-world-famous radio and television personality on the show Quiz Kids , before his memories are erased by dementia.

title: The Mirage Factory: Illusion, Imagination, and the Invention of Los Angeles
author: Gary Krist
description: The birth of modern-day Los Angeles viewed through the prism of three of its most ardent advocates.

title: A Million Drops
author: Victor del Árbol, Trans. Lisa Dillman
description: A mystery...extending over decades, generations, and nations as it attempts to illuminate the deepest mystery of all—the evil within the human soul.

title: The Storm
author: Arif Anwar
description: In the weeks leading up to the expiration of his visa, a recent PhD graduate and father unravels his history that meaningfully connects various lives in 1942 Burma, 1946 India, 1970 Bangladesh, and the post-9/11 United States.

title: A Girl Stands at the Door: The Generation of Young Women Who Desegregated America's Schools
author: Rachel Devlin
description: A new history of school desegregation in America, revealing how girls and women led the fight for interracial education. The struggle to desegregate America's schools was a grassroots movement, and young women were its vanguard. Historian Rachel Devlin tells the remarkable stories of these desegregation pioneers.

title: Brothers of the Gun: A Memoir of the Syrian War
author: Marwan Hisham, illustrated by Molly Crabapple
description: Marwan was there to witness and document firsthand the Syrian war, from its inception to the present. Illustrated with more than eighty ink drawings by Molly Crabapple, Brothers of the Gun is a ground-level reflection on the Syrian revolution—and how it bled into international catastrophe and global war.

title: Sex Money Murder: A Story of Crack, Blood, and Betrayal
author: Jonathan Green
description: A portrait of the crack epidemic and violent drug wars that once ravaged the Bronx.

title: Transparent City
author: Ondjaki, trans. by Stephen Henighan
description: In a crumbling apartment block in the Angolan city of Luanda, families work, laugh, scheme, and get by. In the middle of it all is the melancholic Odonato, nostalgic for the country of his youth and searching for his lost son. As his hope drains away and as the city outside his doors changes beyond all recognition, Odo-nato’s flesh becomes transparent and his body increasingly weightless.

title: Pretend I'm Dead
author: Jen Beagin
description: The story of a cleaning lady on a quest for self-acceptance after her relationship with a lovable junkie goes awry.

title: Jane Seymour, the Haunted Queen
author: Alison Weir
description: This third book in the epic Six Tudor Queens series follows young Jane Seymour from her installment at court as a lady-in-waiting to Queen Katherine of Aragon through her marriage to King Henry VIII, whom she witnesses invalidate his marriage to Katherine, marry then murder Anne Boleyn—in pursuit of Jane herself.

title: Lives of the Eminent Philosophers
author: Diogenes Laertius, Trans. by Pamela Mensch
description: A new translation of the stories about ancient philosophers first compiled in the third century AD by Diogenes Laertius, augmented by footnotes, illustrations, and scholarly essays.

title: The Art of Racing in the Rain
author: Garth Stein
description: This bestseller features Enzo, the canine narrator with a philosopher's soul who unspools a tale about his owner Denny, a race-car driver who faces overwhelming obstacles as he navigates his career and family life.

title: The Strange and True Tale of Horace Wells, Surgeon Dentist: A Novel
author: Michael Downs
description: In 1844, Horace Wells, a Connecticut dentist, encountered nitrous oxide, or laughing gas--then an entertainment for performers in carnival-like theatrical acts--and began administering the gas as the first true anesthetic. His discovery would change the world, reshaping medicine and humanity's relationship with pain.

title: That Kind of Mother
author: Rumaan Alam
description: A novel set in Washington D.C. in the late 1980s about a privileged white woman who adopts her black nanny's son when the latter dies in childbirth.

title: Barracoon: The Story of the Last "Black Cargo"
author: Zora Neale Hurston
description: A newly published work from the author of the American classic Their Eyes Were Watching God illuminates the horror and injustices of slavery as it tells the true story of one of the last-known survivors of the Atlantic slave trade—abducted from Africa on the last "Black Cargo" ship to arrive in the United States.

title: Warlight
author: Michael Ondaatje
description: A new historical novel from the author of The English Patient . Decades after World War II, Nathaniel Williams reflects on his experiences in 1945, when his parents left him and his sister in the care of a mysterious neighbor.

title: My Ex-Life
author: Stephen McCauley
description: After 30 years apart, a woman reaches out to her first ex-husband—whom she'd divorced after learning he was gay—and the former couple spend a summer together sorting through the difficulties of middle age, including two new ex-relationships from which each is recovering.

title: Spring
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard, Trans. by by Ingvild Burkey
description: In the third of his Seasons Quartet, Knausgaard writes a letter to his youngest daughter meditating on his ideas and past experiences while recounting his family's daily activities, from which his wife is conspicuously and troublingly absent.

title: Milk!: A 10,000-Year Food Fracas
author: Mark Kurlansky
description: From the author of Salt and Cod , this culinary history and recipe book considers milk as a long-controversial source of nourishment and flavor across many cultures and millenia.

title: Belly Up
author: Rita Bullwinkel
description: A collection of weird short stories that contains ghosts, mediums, a lover obsessed with the sound of harps tuning, teenage girls who believe they are actually plants, gulag prisoners who outsmart a terrible warden, and carnivorous churches. Throughout these grotesque and tender stories, characters question the bodies they've been given and what their bodies require to be sustained.

title: Our Kind of Cruelty
author: Araminta Hall
description: A psycho-sexual thriller about a wealthy couple, Mike and Verity, whose relationship is built on a game in which Verity allows herself to be semi-seduced in a bar in order that Mike should appear at a crucial moment and rescue her. When Verity falls for someone else, Mike becomes increasingly unhinged and delusional.

title: From Cold War to Hot Peace: An American Ambassador in Putin’s Russia
author: Michael McFaul
description: From the Stanford Kremlinologist who served as U.S. ambassador to Russia from 2012 to 2014, and has since been sanctioned by Vladimir Putin, comes a revelatory account of U.S.-Russia relations from 1989 to the present, told through his experience working for President Barack Obama and witnessing the tightening of Putin's grip firsthand.

title: The Destiny Thief: Essays on Writing, Writers and Life
author: Richard Russo
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist offers nine essays on writing craft, his favorite wordsmiths, friendship, and what it takes to pursue one's intellectual and artistic passions.

title: Tyrant: Shakespeare on Politics
author: Stephen Greenblatt
description: World-renowned Shakespeare scholar Stephen Greenblatt explores the playwright's insight into bad (and often mad) rulers.

title: The Perfectionists: How Precision Engineers Created the Modern World
author: Simon Winchester
description: The bestselling author of The Professor and the Madman returns with this quirky history of the precision engineers whose meticulous tinkering has kept the world running, blending his research with memoir and meditations.

title: Paul Simon: The Life
author: Robert Hilburn
description: From the author of Johnny Cash , 2013, a new biography on the personal experiences and creative processes of one of modernity's most esteemed songwriters.

title: Against Memoir: Complaints, Confessions & Criticisms
author: Michelle Tea
description: Queer culture icon Tea’s first-ever collection of journalistic writing. As she blurs the line between telling other people’s stories and her own, she turns an investigative eye to the genre that’s nurtured her entire career―memoir―and considers the price that art demands be paid from life.

title: The Soul of America: The Battle for Our Better Angels
author: Jon Meacham
description: The Pulitzer Prize winning historian reviews the United States' long battle against racism, nativism, and sexism to make the case that similar struggles roiling contemporary politics can be defeated now as they have been in the past.

title: Atticus Finch: The Biography
author: Joseph Crespino
description: Who was the real Atticus Finch? The publication of Go Set a Watchman in 2015 forever changed how we think about him. Once seen as a paragon of decency, he was reduced to a small-town racist. How are we to understand this transformation? Historian Joseph Crespino draws on exclusive sources to reveal how Harper Lee's father provided the central inspiration for each of her books.

title: The Crooked Staircase: A Jane Hawk Novel
author: Dean Koontz
description: In the latest in Koontz's Jane Hawk series, the eponymous heroine continues her struggle to dodge the FBI and government forces trying to take her down, finding herself on the edge of losing it all at Lake Tahoe.

title: What Should Be Wild
author: Julia Fine
description: A young girl with the power to kill or resurrect people with her touch grows up hidden from the world until her father disappears and she must venture out into society.

title: The High Tide Club
author: Mary Kay Andrews
description: A 99-year-old terminally ill heiress hires a lawyer to contact the descendants of her old friends, members of the eponymous High Tide Club, to save her island and make amends. Little do they know the scandal and potentially fatal risk that will ensue from their meeting.

title: Blackout
author: Alex Segura
description: In the latest novel in Alex Segura’s Pete Fernandez Mystery series, startling new evidence in a cold case that's haunted Pete drags the exiled PI back to his hometown of Miami. But as Pete and his partner Kathy Bentley delve deeper into the unsolved murder, they become entangled in Miami’s obsession with a charismatic and dangerous cult leader and his even more menacing followers.

title: Tomb of the Unknown Racist
author: Blanche McCrary Boyd
description: In this last novel in Boyd's trilogy about a complicated heroine, Ellen thinks she has settled into an uneventful middle age when she discovers her family's connections to white supremacist groups and launches a hunt for her long-lost brother, who may have kidnapped his daughter's mixed-race children.

title: Like Brothers
author: Jay Duplass and Mark Duplass
description: The seemingly ubiquitous filmmakers behind Jeff, Who Lives at Home , Wild, Wild Country , and HBO's Togetherness open up about their unlikely rise to fame producing low-budget fare, advice to aspiring filmmakers, and their interests and obsessions.

title: Compulsory Games
author: Robert Aickman
description: The 20th century's British master of "strange stories" gets a reboot with this new volume of his tales edited by Victoria Nelson, several of them previously unpublished.

title: Figures in a Landscape: People and Places
author: Paul Theroux
description: In his latest collection of essays, the eclectic writer takes a helicopter ride with Elizabeth Taylor, goes surfing with Oliver Sacks, tours a dominatrix's dungeon, and weighs in on his literary heroes.

title: Our Towns: A 100,000-Mile Journey Into the Heart of America
author: Deborah Fallows and James Fallows
description: A married academic and correspondent for The Atlantic take a journalistic road trip to dozens of small towns to get to know the people and understand what keeps the community vibrant despite declines elsewhere in the United States.

title: Kindest Regards: New and Selected Poems
author: Ted Kooser
description: A selection from five decades of work from the former U.S. Poet Laureate known for his understated, intimate vision of everyday life.

title: Come West and See: Stories
author: Maxim Loskutoff
description: In these linked stories, the American West has become a space of alienation for misfits and outcasts as well as a battleground between the government and an imagined rural separatist movement.

title: Lost Empress: A Novel
author: Sergio De La Pava
description: A shockingly hilarious novel that tackles, with equal aplomb, both America’s most popular sport and its criminal justice system.

title: Twilight of the Gods: A Journey to the End of Classic Rock
author: Steven Hyden
description: The author of the critically acclaimed Your Favorite Band is Killing Me offers an eye-opening exploration of the state of classic rock, its past and future, the impact it has had, and what its loss would mean to an industry, a culture, and a way of life.

title: Junk
author: Tommy Pico
description: Building on IRL and Nature Poem , Tommy Pico's Junk is a breathless, book-length break-up poem that explores the experience of loss and erasure, both personal and cultural.

title: The World-Ending Fire: The Essential Wendell Berry
author: Wendell Berry
description: From the revered poet, novelist, and environmentalist, these 31 essays selected by Paul Kingsnorth span five decades of work addressing issues ranging from small farming and economics to feminism and civil disobedience.

title: I Find Your Lack of Faith Disturbing: Star Wars and the Triumph of Geek Culture
author: A.D. Jameson
description: In this analysis-cum-manifesto, the author explores how and why once-marginalized "geek culture" has found its way into the mainstream even as, he argues, comics and other geeky art forms are underestimated by "prestige critics."

title: The Abolition of Species
author: Dietmar Dath, Trans. by Samuel P. Willcocks
description: After mankind's near-extermination, a kingdom of animals harnessing biotechnology wages a multi-planetary war against a new form of artificial intelligence.

title: Night Beast and Other Stories
author: Ruth Joffre
description: In this debut short-fiction collection, women grapple with the pains of various kinds of love in tales that incorporate the real, real, surreal, and speculative.

title: The Great Revolt: Inside the Populist Coalition Reshaping American Politics
author: Salena Zito, Brad Todd
description: In The Great Revolt Salena Zito and Brad Todd challenge readers to view the winning 2016 coalition through the lens of not only partisan realignment but also of broader cultural change-and beyond the prism of a single candidacy-Dust jacket flap.

title: A Theory of Love
author: Margaret Bradham Thornton
description: Helen Gibbs, a British journalist on assignment on the west coast of Mexico, meets Christopher Delavaux, an intriguing half-French, half-American lawyer-turned-financier who has come alone to surf. Living lives that never stop moving, from their first encounter in Bermeja to marriage in London, Helen and Christopher must decide how much they exist for themselves and how much they exist for each other.

title: Queer City: Gay London from the Romans to the Present Day
author: Peter Ackroyd
description: Ackroyd looks at the metropolis in a whole new way—through the history and experiences of its gay population. He takes us right into this hidden city, celebrating its diversity, thrills, and energy on the one hand; but reminding us of its very real terrors, dangers, and risks on the other.

title: The Order of Time
author: Carlos Rovelli, Trans. by Erica Segre and Simon Carnell
description: Why do we remember the past and not the future? What does it mean for time to 'flow? Do we exist in time or does time exist in us? Italian theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli invites us to consider questions about the nature of time that continue to puzzle physicists and philosophers alike.

title: A Short History of Drunkenness: How, Why, Where, and When Humankind Has Gotten Merry from the Stone Age to the Present
author: Mark Forsyth
description: An exploration of how, throughout history, each civilization has found a way to celebrate, or to control, the eternal human drive to get sloshed.

title: Rubik
author: Elizabeth Tan
description: The dead aren’t really gone, they persist as phone numbers, social media accounts, newsletter recipients, and as members of fan-fiction forums. Digital ghosts move and connect us: we feel we know people we have only seen online just as corporations masquerade as familiar friends. Rubik , a darkly comedic meta novel in interconnected stories, follows Elena Rubik, her best friend Jules Valentine, and wannabe investigative reporter April Kuan, as a viral marketing scheme’s motivations become cause for concern.

title: Celestial Bodies: How to Look at Ballet
author: Laura Jacobs
description: Dance critic Laura Jacobs offers an introductory history of ballet as well as a meditation on its aesthetic principles and cultural cache.

title: An Honorable Seduction
author: Brenda Jackson
description: A Navy SEAL must make a choice between duty and desire.

title: The Language of Kindness: A Nurse's Story
author: Christie Watson
description: A memoir about the experiences of a hospital nurse in London, focusing on the overlooked importance of kindness and compassion.

title: The Mercy Seat
author: Elizabeth H. Winthrop
description: On the eve of his execution, eighteen year old Willie Jones sits in his cell in New Iberia awaiting his end. As various members of the township consider and reflect on what Willie’s execution means, a complex portrait of a Jim Crow era Southern community emerges.

title: A Brotherhood of Spies: The U-2 and the Cia's Secret War
author: Monte Reel
description: High-flying history of the U-2 spy plane program and its unlikely clutch of fathers.

title: For Those Who Know the Ending
author: Malcolm Mackay
description: As a captured Czech killer sits bound in a Glasgow warehouse awaiting his fate, Mackay provides a series of flashbacks detailing the events that brought him to such a dire spot.

title: My Life as a Spy: Investigations in a Secret Police File
author: Katherine Verdery
description: Katherine Verdery analyzes the 2,781 page surveillance file the Romanian secret police compiled on her during her research trips to Transylvania in the 1970s and 1980s. Reading it led her to question her identity and also revealed how deeply the secret police was embedded in everyday life.

title: To Throw Away Unopened: A Memoir
author: Viv Albertine
description: From the guitarist of the all-women punk bank The Slits, a memoir about growing up working class, family, and the way childhood trauma can extend, despite our best efforts, into middle age and beyond.

title: Our Story: A Memoir of Love and Life in China
author: Rao Pingru, Trans. by Nicky Harman
description: In this mix of narrative and illustration, a man tells the story of his relationship with his wife from its blissful beginnings in pre-Maoist China through the hardships of the Cultural Revolution, during which he spent years in a re-education camp.

title: Lighting the Fires of Freedom: African American Women in the Civil Rights Movement
author: Janet Dewart Bell
description: Through wide-ranging conversations with nine African American women, several now in their nineties with decades of untold stories, we hear what ignited and fueled their activism in the U.S. Civil Rights movement.

title: The Aviator
author: Eugene Vodolazkin, Trans. by Lisa C. Hayden
description: A man wakes up in a hospital bed, with no idea who he is or how he came to be there. The only information the doctor shares with him is his name.

title: Indecency
author: Justin Phillip Reed
description: Winner of the 2018 National Book Award for Poetry, this collection of poems pushes at the boundaries of selfhood, skin, culture, sexuality, and blood.

title: R E D
author: Chase Berggrun
description: R E D is an erasure of Bram Stoker's Dracula . A long poem in 27 chapters, R E D excavates from Stoker's text an original narrative of violence, sexual abuse, power dynamics, vengeance, and feminist rage while wrestling with the complexities of gender, transition, and monsterhood.

title: Mourning
author: Eduardo Halfon
description: A mysterious family tragedy inspires a journey across the globe, into the past, and through the tangled memories of childhood.

title: Artificial Condition: The Murderbot Diaries
author: Martha Wells
description: It has a dark past - one in which a number of humans were killed. A past that caused it to christen itself Murderbot. But it has only vague memories of the massacre that spawned that title, and it wants to know more.

title: The Patrick Melrose Novels
author: Edward St Aubyn
description: Collected into one volume for the first time, all five installments of Edward St. Aubyn's celebrated Patrick Melrose novels.

title: Rooted Cosmopolitans: Jews and Human Rights in the Twentieth Century
author: James Loeffler
description: Focusing on the lives of five key activists, this volume explores the Jewish contributions to the emergence of international human rights standards, culminating in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.

title: World War II at Sea: A Global History
author: Craig L. Symonds
description: A comprehensive naval history of the Second World War presenting the chronology of the naval war, from The London Conference of 1930 to the surrender in Tokyo Bay in 1945.

title: The Mars Room
author: Rachel Kushner
description: From the author of The Flamethrowers . It's 2003 and Romy Hall is at the start of two consecutive life sentences at Stanville Women's Correctional Facility, deep in California's Central Valley. Outside is the world from which she has been severed: the San Francisco of her youth and her young son, Jackson. Inside is a new reality: thousands of women hustling for the bare essentials needed to survive.

title: Motherhood
author: Sheila Heti
description: In this meditative novel, a female writer explores her internal debate over whether to have children, recording her thoughts, conversations with loved ones and fortune tellers, and consultations with the I Ching.

title: Miss Subways
author: David Duchovny
description: One woman's trippy, mystical journey down parallel tracks of time and love. On the way, Emer will battle natural and supernatural forces to find her true voice, power, and destiny. A fairy tale of love lost and regained and an ode to New York.

title: The Pisces
author: Melissa Broder
description: A comic, sexual debut novel, from the author of So Sad Today , about a disaffected academic struggling with a breakup who moves to LA and begins a passionate affair with a merman.

title: A Lucky Man: Stories
author: Jamel Brinkley
description: A debut short story collection which explores issues of race, class, and masculinity across three decades of New York City’s history.

title: Welcome to Lagos
author: Chibundu Onuzo
description: When the army officer Chike Ameobi is ordered to kill innocent civilians, he knows it is time to desert his post. As he travels toward Lagos with Yẹmi, his junior officer, and into the heart of a political scandal involving Nigeria’s education minister, Chike becomes the leader of a new platoon, a rag-tag band of runaways who share his desire for a different kind of life.

title: Love and Ruin
author: Paula McLain
description: The author of The Paris Wife returns to the subject of Ernest Hemingway in a novel about his passionate, stormy marriage to Martha Gellhorn—a fiercely independent, ambitious young woman who would become one of the greatest war correspondents of the twentieth century.

title: Slave Old Man
author: Patrick Chamoiseau, Trans. by Linda Coverdale
description: From a Prix Goncourt writer hailed by Milan Kundera as the "heir of Joyce and Kafka," a novel, first published in France in 1997, about an escaped slave in Martinique and the killer hound that pursues him.

title: The Queen's Embroiderer: A True Story of Paris, Lovers, Swindlers, and the First Stock Market Crisis
author: Joan DeJean
description: Against the backdrop of France's first stock-market crash, the son of the eponymous Queen's embroiderer and daughter of a greedy financier strike up an ill-fated romance, battling the disapproval of their families as well as the changing tides of French life leading to the Revolution of 1789.

title: Captive Audience: On Love and Reality TV
author: Lucas Mann
description: An intimate portrait of a marriage intertwined with a meditation on reality TV that reveals surprising connections and the meaning of an authentic life.

title: Limelight: A Novel
author: Amy Poeppel
