description: Allison Brinkley--wife, mother, and former unflappable optimist--discovers that a carefully weighed decision to pack up and move her family from suburban Dallas to the glittery chaos of Manhattan may have been more complicated than she and her husband initially thought.

title: The Garbage Times/White Ibis: Two Novellas
author: Sam Pink
description: In these linked novellas, a narrator navigates two differently unsavory circumstances: in one, a dirty job as a bouncer/cleaning staff at a Chicago dive bar, and in the other, family life with his girlfriend's bourgeois middle class relatives in Florida.

title: Not That Bad: Dispatches from Rape Culture
author: Edited by Roxane Gay
description: In this anthology edited by Roxane Gay, bestselling author of Bad Feminist and Hunger , a diverse group of writers disclose their experiences with sexual harassment, aggression, and assault as well as the shame and belittlement that has too often been a consequence of speaking out.

title: Mr. Flood's Last Resort: A Novel
author: Jess Kidd
description: When Maud Drennan is hired as caretaker of Cathal Flood, she finds his old manor house to be haunted with ghosts as well as dark secrets surrounding the death of the old man's wife.

title: Adjustment Day
author: Chuck Palahniuk
description: "People pass the word only to those they trust most: Adjustment Day is coming. They've been reading a mysterious book and memorizing its directives. They are ready for the reckoning. When Adjustment Day arrives, it fearlessly makes real the logical conclusion of every separatist fantasy, alternative fact, and conspiracy theory lurking in the American psyche.

title: The Perfect Mother
author: Aimee Molloy
description: A group of new mothers in Brooklyn decide to take a night off at the bar, leaving their children in the hands of those they think will keep them safe. But a nightmare and media frenzy ensues after one woman's baby is kidnapped.

title: It's Always the Husband
author: Michele Campbell
description: Kate, Aubrey, and Jenny first met as college roommates and soon became inseparable, despite being as different as three women can be. As an unlikely friendship formed, the three of them swore they would always be there for each other. But twenty years later, one of them is standing at the edge of a bridge, and someone is urging her to jump. How did it come to this?

title: Two Kinds of Truth
author: Michael Connelly
description: Harry Bosch, exiled from the LAPD, is working cold cases for the San Fernando Police Department when all hands are called out to a local drugstore, where two pharmacists have been murdered in a robbery. To get to the people at the top, Bosch must risk everything and go undercover in the shadowy world of organized pill mills.

title: The Electric Woman: A Memoir in Death-Defying Acts
author: Tessa Fontaine
description: A memoir about a writer's time performing in a traveling sideshow tour after spending three years with her mother as she endured a series of debilitating strokes.

title: The Judge Hunter
author: Christopher Buckley
description: The latest comic novel from Christopher Buckley, a hapless Englishman embarks on a dangerous mission to the New World in pursuit of two judges who helped murder a king.

title: Young Washington: How Wilderness and War Forged America's Founding Father
author: Peter Stark
description: Outside correspondent Peter Stark considers George Washington's early days as a brash young soldier for the British Empire in the wild Ohio Valley before and during the French and Indian War, formative experiences that Stark argues molded the less-than-heroic character of the first President of the United States.

title: Adventures of a Young Naturalist: The Zoo Quest Expeditions
author: David Attenborough
description: Living legend and presenter of BBC's Planet Earth series Sir David Attenborough tells the story of how he began his career as a broadcaster and a naturalist in his own words.

title: Into the Raging Sea: Thirty-Three Mariners, One Megastorm, and the Sinking of El Faro
author: Rachel Slade
description: On October 1, 2015, Hurricane Joaquin barreled into the Bermuda Triangle and swallowed the container ship El Faro whole, resulting in the worst American shipping disaster in thirty-five years. No one could fathom how a vessel equipped with satellite communications, a sophisticated navigation system, and cutting-edge weather forecasting could suddenly vanish—until now.

title: The Poppy War
author: R. F. Kuang
description: The Poppy War is an epic historical military fantasy, inspired by the bloody history of China’s twentieth century and filled with treachery and magic, in the tradition of Ken Liu’s Grace of Kings and N.K. Jemisin’s Inheritance Trilogy.

title: The Optimistic Decade
author: Heather Abel
description: This novel takes us into the lives of five unforgettable characters at a utopian camp with a charismatic leader. It is a sweeping saga of idealism, love, class, and a piece of land that changes everyone who lives on it.

title: The Happiness Curve: Why Life Gets Better After 50
author: Jonathan Rauch
description: A senior fellow at the Brookings Institution investigates and ultimately affirms scientific claims of a U-shaped trajectory of happiness and offers tips to endure the midlife slump.

title: Chasing New Horizons: Inside the Epic First Mission to Pluto
author: Alan Stern and David Grinspoon
description: A behind-the-scenes account of the science, politics, egos, and public expectations that shaped the New Horizons' mission to Pluto and beyond.

title: Asperger's Children: The Origins of Autism in Nazi Vienna
author: Edith Sheffer
description: An exploration of the chilling history behind an increasingly common diagnosis.

title: Atlas of a Lost World: Travels in Ice Age America
author: Craig Childs
description: A travelogue through prehistory that traces the arrival of the first people in North America at least twenty thousand years ago and the artifacts that tell of their lives and fates.

title: The Map of Salt and Stars
author: Jennifer Zeynab Joukhadar
description: The story of two girls living eight hundred years apart—a modern-day Syrian refugee seeking safety and a medieval adventurer apprenticed to a legendary mapmaker—places today's headlines in the sweep of history, where the pain of exile and the triumph of courage echo again and again.

title: Mothers: An Essay on Love and Cruelty
author: Jacqueline Rose
description: In this book-length essay, cultural critic Rose looks at literature, politics, and popular cultural to investigate the way Western society simultaneously romanticizes and vilifies mothers, making them into scapegoats for human failings.

title: Trip: Psychedelics, Alienation, and Change
author: Tao Lin
description: From the author of Taipei , Tao Lin's first work of non-fiction offers a blend of memoir into his experiments with psychedelic drugs and biographical exploration of the life and teachings of Terence McKenna, an advocate of psychotropic drug use who died in 2000.

title: Darwin's Ghosts
author: Ariel Dorfman
description: On his 14th birthday, Fitzroy Foster discovers that photographs of him do not reveal his own image but that of a stranger, whose identity reveals some unsavory truths about Fitzroy's family's involvement in the abuse of indigenous peoples during the 19th century.

title: A Spy Named Orphan: The Enigma of Donald Maclean
author: Roland Philipps
description: Drawing on a wealth of previously classified files and unseen family papers, A Spy Named Orphan documents the life of Donald Maclean .

title: The Fair Chase: The Epic Story of Hunting in America
author: Philip Dray
description: An award-winning historian tells the story of hunting in America, showing how this sport has shaped our national identity.

title: He
author: John Connolly
description: A novel about the comedian Stan Laurel's wildly successful and tender partnership with Oliver Hardy during the anarchy of early Hollywood.

title: Someone to Care
author: Mary Balogh
description: Two years after the death of the Earl of Riverdale, his family has overcome the shame of being stripped of their titles and fortune--except for his onetime countess, Viola. With her children grown and herself no longer part of the social whirl of the ton, she is uncertain where to look for happiness.

title: Love That Bunch
author: Aline Kominsky-Crumb
description: An expanded and updated edition of the 1990 cult-class comics memoir about the author's evolution from seemingly run-of-the-mill Jewish teenager from Long Island to feminist comics icon in San Francisco to housewife living in France with her husband, the infamous R. Crumb, and their daughter.

title: Only Human
author: Sylvain Neuvel
description: Rose Franklin has devoted her adult life to solving the mystery she accidentally stumbled upon as a child: a huge metal hand buried beneath the ground outside Deadwood, South Dakota. The discovery set in motion a cataclysmic chain of events with geopolitical ramifications, as giant robots descended on Earth's cities. The mysterious invaders retreated, disappearing from the shattered planet . . . but they took the scientist and her crew with them. Now, after nearly ten years on another world, Rose returns to find a devastating new war—this time between humans.

title: House of Nutter: The Rebel Tailor of Savile Row
author: Lance Richardson
description: A journalist's first book resurrects the forgotten but once-influential British fashion designer Tommy Nutter, whose wild suits dressed the likes of The Beatles, Mick Jagger, and Elton John.

title: Kicks: The Great American Story of Sneakers
author: Nicholas Smith
description: A history of the athletic shoe, or sneaker, from the beaches and croquet courts of the wealthy elite to streetwear ubiquity and, more recently, a collector's market for connoisseurs who call themselves "sneakerheads."

title: The Island Dwellers
author: Jen Silverman
description: Eleven interconnected stories that take place in expat bars, artist colonies, train stations, and matchbox apartments in the United States and Japan. Characters crisscross through these transient spaces, loving, hurting, and leaving each other as they experience the loneliness and dangerous freedom that comes with being an outsider.

title: Beautiful Music
author: Michael Zadoorian
description: Set in early 1970s Detroit, a divided city still reeling from its violent race riot of 1967, Beautiful Music is the story of one young man's transformation through music. Danny Yzemski is a husky, pop radio–loving loner balancing a dysfunctional homelife with the sudden harsh realities of freshman year at a high school marked by racial turbulence.

title: Still Life with Two Dead Peacocks and a Girl: Poems
author: Diane Seuss
description: Still Life with Two Dead Peacocks and a Girl takes its title from Rembrandt’s painting, a dark emblem of femininity, violence, and the viewer’s own troubled gaze. In Diane Seuss’s new collection, the notion of the still life is shattered and Rembrandt’s painting is presented across the book in pieces―details that hide more than they reveal until they’re assembled into a whole

title: The Tragedy of Benedict Arnold: An American Life
author: Joyce Lee Malcolm
description: A re-examination of one of young America's most complicated figures: the war hero turned infamous traitor, Benedict Arnold.

title: A Handful of Ashes
author: Rob McCarthy
description: In the new Dr. Harry Kent thriller, a follow-up to 2016's The Hollow Men , a whistleblowing doctor commits suicide—or so it seems. When it turns out to be murder, Harry digs deeper to uncover the truth, in this mix of detective novel and medical drama.

title: In Dust and Ashes: Hanne Wilhelmsen Book Ten
author: Anne Holt, Trans. by Anne Bruce
description: In the last of the Norwegian writer's Hanne Wilhelmsen series, Wilhelmsen's protege Detective Henrik Holme looks into a potential wrongful murder conviction from a case more than 15 years earlier that might be connected to a different kidnapping and suicide.

title: The Assault on Intelligence: American National Security in an Age of Lies
author: Michael V Hayden
description: This critique of the forces threatening the American intelligence community, beginning with President Trump himself, outlines how the country's democratic structures and processes are under stress and discusses effective responses.

title: The Lonely Witness
author: William Boyle
description: Allesandra—a minor character from Boyle's critically acclaimed Gravesend —makes a cameo in this follow-up that unravels the story of Allesandra's ex-lover Amy, a woman in her 30s with a sordid past who witnesses a murder and finds herself drawn to the killer.

title: Break.Up: A Novel in Essays
author: Joanna Walsh
description: A writer goes traveling through Europe to distract herself from the end of an online romance, meditating on heartbreak, loneliness, and love in the digital age.

title: The Moralist: Woodrow Wilson and the World He Made
author: Patricia O'Toole
description: Veteran biographer Patricia O'Toole takes a look at the 28th U.S. President through the lens of his moral convictions, which played a decisive role in this policies—and their consequences—at home and abroad.

title: Restless Souls
author: Dan Sheehan
description: Three friends reunite in 1990s Dublin when one returns from a stint reporting on the Bosnian War, an experience that has left him grappling with PTSD and sends the trio on an overseas journey for a cure to an experimental clinic on the California coast.

title: You Think It, I'll Say It: Stories
author: Curtis Sittenfeld
description: In these 10 short-stories, the best-selling author of Prep and American Wife explores and satirizes the disappointments, foibles, and small joys of middle-class life.

title: The Feather Thief: Beauty, Obsession, and the Natural History Heist of the Century
author: Kirk Wallace Johnson
description: In 2009, a flautist robbed the British Museum of Natural History's Tring museum, stealing hundreds of historic bird specimens he sold on the black market for rare feathers among the practitioners of salmon fly-tying. This true-crime novel investigates the heist, the fly-tying underworld, and the efforts by a rival of Charles Darwin to preserve rare birdskins for posterity.

title: Beneath a Ruthless Sun
author: Gilbert King
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Devil in the Grove , a true crime book exploring the aftermath of the 1957 rape of a white woman named Blanche Knowles, the wife of a wealthy citrus baron in Lake County, Fla., a locale notorious for trumped-up prosecutions of black men.

title: The Hellfire Club
author: Jake Tapper
description: The debut political thriller from CNN's chief Washington correspondent. After a mysterious fatal car accident kills his predecessor, Congressman Charlie Marder struggles to navigate the dangerous waters of 1950s Washington, D.C., where he finds an underworld of backroom deals, secret societies, and a conspiracy at the highest levels of the government.

title: Property: Stories Between Two Novellas
author: Lionel Shriver
description: From the author of We Need to Talk About Kevin , a collection of ten short stories and two novellas that explores the idea of property in every meaning of the word.

title: Chasing Hillary: Ten Years, Two Presidential Campaigns, and One Intact Glass Ceiling
author: Amy Chozick
description: A dishy blend of political reportage and memoir of the 2016 election, as seen through the eyes of the New York Times reporter who gave eight years of her life to covering the First Woman President who wasn't.

title: The Best Cook in the World: Tales from My Momma's Table
author: Rick Bragg
description: A cookbook, food memoir, and tribute to the author's mother, who managed in spite of poverty to create feasts from foraged greens, small game, and other lovingly prepared ingredients in the Deep South.

title: West
author: Carys Davies
description: When widowed mule breeder Cy Bellman reads in the newspaper that colossal ancient bones have been discovered in the salty Kentucky mud, he sets out from his small Pennsylvania farm to see for himself if the rumors are true: that the giant monsters are still alive and roam the uncharted wilderness beyond the Mississippi River. Promising to write and to return in two years, he leaves behind his only daughter, Bess, to the tender mercies of his taciturn sister and heads west.

title: The Emissary
author: Yoko Tawada, Trans. by Margaret Mitsutani
description: Winner of the 2018 National Book Award for Translated Literature (and by the celebrated surrealist author of Memoirs of a Polar Bear ), The Emissary is a slim, tender dystopian novel set in an isolated, post-disaster Japan, focusing on a sick-but-cheery boy and his great-grandfather.

title: Theory of Bastards
author: Audrey Schulman
description: In a dystopian near future, Dr. Francine Burk has won a MacArthur "Genius" Fellowship for her studies of bonobos' sexual habits and the implications for human beings, scholarship she is trying to pursue further at a research institute in Missouri when a natural disaster strikes.

title: Caddyshack: The Making of a Hollywood Cinderella Story
author: Chris Nashawaty
description: Behind the scenes of the cult movie, Caddyshack

title: War on Peace: The End of Diplomacy and the Decline of American Influence
author: Ronan Farrow
description: Winner of the 2018 Pulitzer Prize in Public Service and a former U.S. State Department official under President Obama, Ronan Farrow writes a blend of memoir and analysis of the decades-long dismantling of diplomacy in favor of militarization, which has reached a tipping point under President Trump.

title: Twisted Prey
author: John Sandford
description: Lucas Davenport confronts an old nemesis, now a powerful U.S. senator, in this #1 New York Times -bestselling new novel in the Prey series.

title: Shattered Mirror: An Eve Duncan Novel
author: Iris Johansen
description: In the latest in the Eve Duncan series, the titular heroine receives a burned skull in the mail, which she reconstructs to reveal the face of a beautiful woman, getting tangled up in the hunt for her killer.

title: The Girl Who Smiled Beads: A Story of War and What Comes After
author: Clemantine Wamariya and Elizabeth Weil
description: Clemantine Wamariya was six years old when she and her fifteen-year-old sister, Claire, fled the Rwandan massacre and spent the next six years migrating through seven African countries, searching for safety—perpetually hungry, imprisoned and abused, enduring and escaping refugee camps, finding unexpected kindness, witnessing inhuman cruelty. In The Girl Who Smiled Beads , Clemantine provokes us to look beyond the label of “victim” and recognize the power of the imagination to transcend even the most profound injuries and aftershocks.

title: Rail
author: Kai Carlson-Wee
description: Set against a landscape of rail yards and skate parks, Kai Carlson-Wee’s debut collection captures a spiritual journey of wanderlust, depression, brotherhood, and survival.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Dinosaurs: A New History of a Lost World
author: Steve Brusatte
description: The dinosaurs. Sixty-six million years ago, the Earth’s most fearsome creatures vanished. Today they remain one of our planet’s great mysteries. Now The Rise and Fall of the Dinosaurs reveals their extraordinary, 200-million-year-long story as never before.

title: Moon Brow
author: Shahriar Mandanipour, Trans. by Sara Khalili
description: A story of love and war narrated by two angel scribes perched on the shoulders of a shell-shocked Iranian soldier who’s searching for the mysterious woman haunting his dreams.

title: The Desert and Its Seed
author: Jorge Barón Biza, Trans. by Camilo Ramirez
description: An undiscovered modern Argentinian classic, based on the tragic lives of the renowned Raúl Barón Biza (a wealthy politician and notorious writer) and his wife Rosa Clotilde Sabattini.

title: Time Was
author: Ian McDonald
description: Two British soldiers during World War II fall into a forbidden love that continues after their disappearance across time, during which they leave each other clues in books of poetry that are ultimately found by narrator Emmett.

title: Richard III: England's Most Controversial King
author: Chris Skidmore
description: From historian Chris Skidmore, this new biography of Richard III offers a nuanced portrait of one of England's most reviled monarchs and weighs the documentary evidence surrounding his rumored murder of his nephews so that he could usurp the crown.

title: 1983: Reagan, Andropov, and a World on the Brink
author: Taylor Downing
description: An award-winning documentarian and historian, Downing tells the nerve-wracking tale of our close call with nuclear war after NATO launched a wargame exercise that the Soviets mistook for a real attack.

title: President Carter: The White House Years
author: Stuart E. Eizenstat
description: The definitive history of the Carter Administration from the man who participated in its surprising number of accomplishments―drawing on his extensive and never-before-seen notes.

title: Live Work Work Work Die: A Journey Into the Savage Heart of Silicon Valley
author: Corey Pein
description: A scathing, sardonic exploration of Silicon Valley tech culture, laying bare the greed, hubris, and retrograde politics of an industry that aspires to radically transform society for its own benefit.

title: Edge of Chaos: Why Democracy Is Failing to Deliver Economic Growth—And How to Fix It
author: Dambisa Moyo
description: An internationally acclaimed economist, Moyo proposes steps for overhauling liberal democracy in order to boost the stagnant global economy she sees as the cause of widespread social unrest.

title: Do Angels Need Haircuts?
author: Lou Reed
description: This volume captures the period of poetic apprenticeship Lou Reed began after he left The Velvet Underground in 1970, gathering poems, photographs and ephemera from this era, including previously unreleased audio of the 1971 St. Mark’s Church reading.

title: Companions
author: Christina Hesselholdt Trans. Paul Russell Garrett
description: Camilla, Charles, Alma, Edward, Alwilda, and Kristian are a circle of friends hurtling through mid-life. Structured as a series of monologues jumping from one friend to the next, Companions follows their loves, ambitions, pains, and anxieties as they age, fall sick, have affairs, grieve, host dinner parties and move around the world.

title: Carnet de Voyage
author: Craig Thompson
description: A new expanded version of the travel journal Thompson penned on his book tour in Europe and Africa for his acclaimed graphic memoir Blankets .

title: The Pope Who Would Be King: The Exile of Pius IX and the Emergence of Modern Europe
author: David I. Kertzer
description: The Pulitzer Prize–winning author of The Pope and Mussolini takes on the story of the bloody revolution that stripped the pope of political power and signaled the birth of modern Europe

title: The Linden Tree
author: Cesar Aira, Trans. by Chris Andrews
description: In this work of auto-fiction, Aira describes growing up in a small Argentinian town under the shadow of Peronism.

title: Alt-Right: From 4chan to the White House
author: Mike Wendling
description: Exploring links between Alt-Right rhetoric, hate crimes, and terrorism, Mike Wendling shows that the evidence connecting them is undeniable.

title: A Higher Loyalty: Truth, Lies, and Leadership
author: James B Comey
description: A memoir from the ex-FBI director whose firing by President Trump, over the FBI's investigation of Russian government interference in the 2016 election, sparked a furor.

title: How to Write an Autobiographical Novel: Essays
author: Alexander Chee
description: From the author of The Queen of the Night , an essay collection exploring his education as a man, writer, and activist—and how we form our identities in life and in art.

title: God Save Texas: A Journey into the Soul of the Lone Star State
author: Lawrence Wright
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning author of The Looming Tower explores the history, culture, and politics of Texas, while holding the stereotypes up for rigorous scrutiny.

title: The Only Story
author: Julian Barnes
description: In the latest from Man Booker Prize winner Julian Barnes, an aging man looks back on the defining romance of his life, a consuming and ill-fated affair he began at 19 with a woman more than twice his age.

title: Blackfish City
author: Sam J. Miller
description: A mysterious woman called the "orcamancer" arrives to challenge the status quo in Qaanaaq, a floating city in the Arctic Circle just barely surviving after the climate wars and overrun by political corruption, poverty, and a disease called "the breaks."

title: Brown: Poems
author: Kevin Young
description: James Brown. John Brown's raid. Brown v. the Topeka Board of Ed. The New Yorker poetry editor and prize-winning author of Blue Laws meditates on all things "brown" in this new collection.

title: The Art of the Wasted Day
author: Patricia Hampl
description: Having recently lost her husband, and in an effort to discover the value of daydreaming and leisure, the author sets out on a journey that will take her to the homes of people who famously wasted time daydreaming, but were better for it.

title: Meghan: A Hollywood Princess
author: Andrew Morton
description: A biography of the American actress that focuses on her early life, acting career, humanitarian work, and her relationship with Prince Harry.

title: Head on: A Novel of the Near Future
author: John Scalzi
description: Hilketa is a frenetic and violent pastime where players attack each other with swords and hammers, seeking their opponents' heads. Since the players are "threeps," robot-like bodies controlled by people with Haden's Syndrome, they aren't supposed to undergo any real harm. But when a star athlete drops dead on the playing field, FBI Agents Chris Shane and Leslie Vann are called in to investigate in this sequence to Lock In .

title: Love and Death in the Sunshine State: The Story of a Crime
author: Cutter Wood
description: A hybrid memoir and true crime story. When the owner of a Florida motel goes missing, a writer who had been a guest at the motel becomes drawn into the investigation, carrying its facts beyond the actual case and into his own life.

title: The Comedown: A Novel
author: Rebekah Frumkin
description: When a drug deal goes horribly wrong—and a suitcase (which may or may not contain a quarter of a million dollars) disappears—the dealer and his addicted client become entangled in one another's lives in a series of strange events.

title: Renaissance Woman: The Life of Vittoria Colonna
author: Ramie Targoff
description: This biography explores the life and writings of Vittoria Colonna, a pivotal figure in the Italian Renaissance whose popular poetry was the first published by an Italian woman, a fact often overlooked in narratives that focus instead on her close friendship with Michelangelo.

title: Broadway: A History of New York City in Thirteen Miles
author: Fran Leadon
description: An architectural, cultural, and social history of the development of one of Manhattan's most famous streets.

title: The Elizas
author: Sara Shepard
description: From the bestselling author of Pretty Little Liars , a thriller about writer Eliza Fontaine, whose debut novel seems a little too real when she's found at the bottom of a hotel pool and she launches an investigation to find a possible attacker.

title: Disoriental
author: Négar Djavadi, Trans. by Tina Kover
description: As she contemplates having children of her own, 25-year-old punk rocker Kimiâ’s Sadr unravels tales from generations of her family's history in Iran, the nation she fled 15 years earlier after the 1978-1979 revolution.

title: The Home for Unwanted Girls
author: Joanna Goodman
description: Philomena meets Orphan Train in this suspenseful, provocative novel filled with love, secrets, and deceit—the story of a young unwed mother who is forcibly separated from her daughter at birth and the lengths to which they go to find each other.

title: The Fallen
author: David Baldacci
description: The closer Amos Decker comes to the truth, the deadlier it gets in #1 New York Times bestselling author David Baldacci's latest Memory Man thriller.

title: Then She Was Gone
author: Lisa Jewell
description: Ellie Mack was the perfect daughter. She was fifteen, the youngest of three. She was beloved by her parents, friends, and teachers. She and her boyfriend made a teenaged golden couple. She was days away from an idyllic post-exams summer vacation, with her whole life ahead of her. And then she was gone.

title: Noir
author: Christopher Moore
description: A spoof on the classic noir set in 1947 San Francisco, where protagonist Sammy falls for a blonde bombshell named Stilton, or the Cheese, whilst a UFO is rumored to be hovering along the Pacific coast in Washington State near Mount Rainer.

title: Last Shot (Star Wars): A Han and Lando Novel
author: Daniel Jose Older
description: Han Solo, Lando Calrissian, the droid L3-37, and Chewbacca try to claim a prize for the discovery of a mysterious transmitter, but they must contend with its evil creator Fyzen Gor.

title: Mr. Lear: A Life of Art and Nonsense
author: Jenny Uglow
description: A look into the life of the Victorian era's most beloved poet of "nonsense" verse, who was far less jolly than his whimsical lyrics let on.

title: Basic Black with Pearls
author: Helen Weinzweig
description: A lost feminist classic that is equal parts domestic drama and international intrigue. Shirley and Coenraad’s affair has been going on for decades, but her longing for him is as desperate as ever. But something has happened, and Coenraad sends Shirley (who prefers to be known as “Lola Montez”) to Toronto, the last place she wants to go.

title: The Efficiency Paradox: What Big Data Can't Do
author: Edward Tenner
description: An exploration of the two-sided nature of advancing technology: Although it has made it easier to keep in touch with friends, find a ride, and order takeout, it may also be limiting our capacity to find creative solutions or insights that require more time and space for the mind to meander and struggle.

title: Acid West: Essays
author: Joshua Wheeler
description: A debut book of essays that takes readers on a trip through the muck of American myths that have settled in the desert of our country's underbelly.

title: The Burning Shores: Inside the Battle for the New Libya
author: Frederic Wehrey
description: From a senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, this books narrates the unraveling of Libya after the ouster of Muammar Qadhafi and seven years of troubled intervention by Western nations.

title: Big Guns
author: Steve Israel
description: From congressman-turned-novelist Steve Israel, a madcap satire about the gun lobby and American political system in all its hubris and corruption.

title: If We Had Known
author: Elise Juska
description: English professor Maggie Daley and her college-student daughter struggle with guilt, fear, and the dangerous bonds of family in the aftermath of a mass shooting in their small New England town when it is revealed that the gunman had been one of Maggie's students.

title: Rise Up Women!: The Remarkable Lives of the Suffragettes
author: Diane Atkinson
description: This history chronicles the militant, bodies-in-the-street tactics of the women's suffrage movement in Great Britain, with special attention to the contributions of the working-class suffragettes who fought for the right to vote.

title: Futureface: A Family Mystery, an Epic Quest, and the Secret to Belonging
author: Alex Wagner
description: A hybrid work of memoir and journalism in which CBS News anchor Wagner, daughter of a Burmese immigrant mother and an Irish-Luxembourgian-American father from Iowa, recounts a genealogical voyage through Burma, Europe, and the Internet that shook her understanding of family history.

title: The Saint of Wolves and Butchers
author: Alex Grecian
description: A Nazi hunter and his dog arrive in Kansas in the 1950s to take down their latest target

title: The Big Ones: How Natural Disasters Have Shaped Us (and What We Can Do about Them)
author: Lucy Jones
description: By the world-renowned seismologist, a riveting history of natural disasters, their impact on our culture, and new ways of thinking about the ones to come.

title: This Little Art
author: Kate Briggs
description: Taking her own experience of translating Roland Barthes’s lecture notes as a starting point, the author threads various stories together to give us this portrait of translation.

title: Terrible Blooms
author: Melissa Stein
description: In her second poetry collection, Melissa Stein subverts the old trope and trappings of femininity with sound-rich lyric and punch.

title: The Girl from Kathmandu: Twelve Dead Men and a Woman's Quest for Justice
author: Cam Simpson
description: A look into how U.S. military contractors in Iraq have participated in human trafficking, told from the perspective of Kamala Magar, a widow of one of twelve Nepalese workers killed in 2004 by terrorists on their way to work for a subsidiary of Halliburton.

title: Fox
author: Dubravka Ugrešić, Trans. by Ellen Elias-Bursać
description: From a winner of the Neustadt International Prize for Literature, Ugrešić's latest genre-bending novel offers a meditation on the writing life, in particular the literary "footnotes" or unnoticed people propelled into timelessness through the biographies and novels of others.

title: The Truth about Animals: Stoned Sloths, Lovelorn Hippos, and Other Tales from the Wild Side of Wildlife
author: Lucy Cooke
description: A zoologist, filmmaker, and founder of the Sloth Appreciation Society debunks myths and replaces them with surprising facts about 13 animals, from the sloth to the hippopotamus.

title: Buttermilk Graffiti: A Chef's Journey to Discover America's New Melting-Pot Cuisine
author: Edward Lee
description: Edward Lee decided to hit the road and spent two years uncovering food narratives from every corner of the country. What can food tell us about the people behind it? What about the traditions, the innovations, the memories?

title: The Dream of Reason
author: Jenny George
description: In this debut collection from the winner of the 2015 "Discovery" Boston Review Poetry Prize, the poet meditates on the death of humans and animals—with a focus on pigs—and captures surreal moments of perception.

title: Liar's Candle
author: August Thomas
description: Penny Kessler, a young intern at the U.S. Embassy in Ankara, Turkey, is wanted by both the CIA and Turkish forces after a viral photograph of her at the scene of a terrorist attack turns her into an unwitting pawn in international gamesmanship.

title: The Darkening Age: The Christian Destruction of the Classical World
author: Catherine Nixey
description: A look at the destructive rise of Christianity, showing how its radical followers ravaged vast swathes of classical culture, plunging the world into an era of dogma and intellectual darkness.

title: The Atrocities
author: Jeremy C. Shipp
description: From the Bram Stoker Award-nominated author of Cursed , this Gothic horror tells the tale of a woman who discovers that the girl she has been hired to tutor is dead.

title: Girls Are Coming Out of the Woods
author: Tishani Doshi
description: Indian poet and professional dancer Tishani Doshi's latest collection explores violence against women and girls by giving abused and silenced bodies a chance to speak at last.

title: Cove
author: Cynan Jones
description: After man in a kayak gets struck by lightning, he awakens in a psychological haze and struggles to survive as he drifts, lost, in isolated waters.

title: Macbeth
author: Jo Nesbø, Trans. by Don Bartlett
description: Shakespeare's celebrated tragedy gets an update, reimagined as a noir police drama set in a down-on-its luck, drug-addled industrial town during the 1970s.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: This follow-up to the Orange Prize-winning The Song of Achilles follows Circe, the banished witch daughter of Helios, as she hones her powers and interacts with famous mythological beings before a conflict with one of the most vengeful Olympians forces her to choose between the worlds of the gods and mortals.

title: Sharp: The Women Who Made an Art of Having an Opinion
author: Michelle Dean
description: From literary critic Michelle Dean, a portrait of ten women writers who managed to make their voices heard amid a culture of sexism.

title: Country Dark
author: Chris Offutt
description: A noir-inflected novel set across three decades in rural Kentucky, about a Korean War veteran's determination to protect his family at all costs, and to seek revenge on those who have wronged them.

title: Maker of Patterns: An Autobiography Through Letters
author: Freeman Dyson
description: Both recalling his life story and recounting many of the major advances in Twentieth-Century science, a renowned physicist shares his autobiography through letters.

title: Empire of Guns: The Violent Making of the Industrial Revolution
author: Priya Satia
description: This novel reframes the Industrial Revolution, the expansion of British empire, and the emergence of industrial capitalism by presenting them as inextricable from the gun trade.

title: Space Opera
author: Catherynne M. Valente
description: Decibel Jones and the Absolute Zeroes have been chosen to represent their planet on the greatest stage in the galaxy. And the fate of Earth lies in their ability to rock.

title: Air Traffic: A Memoir of Ambition and Manhood in America
author: Gregory Pardlo
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning poet, his first work of prose: a memoir of a family's bonds and a meditation on race, addiction, fatherhood, ambition, and American culture.

title: Natural Causes: An Epidemic of Wellness, the Certainty of Dying, and Killing Ourselves to Live Longer
author: Barbara Ehrenreich
description: Offers insight into healthcare practices, identifying the cellular sources of aging and illness and revealing that aggressive treatments provide an illusion of control and survivability at the cost of life quality.

title: And Now We Have Everything: On Motherhood Before I Was Ready
author: Meaghan O'Connell
description: When twenty something writer Meaghan O'Connell got accidentally pregnant in her twenties and decided to keep the baby, she realized that the book she needed—an honest, agenda-free reckoning with the emotional and existential impact of motherhood—didn't exist. So she decided to write it herself.

title: Heads of the Colored People
author: Nafissa Thompson-Spires
description: A debut collection of darkly satirical stories examining the concept of black identity in this so-called post-racial era.

title: The Changeling
author: Joy Williams
description: In this 40th anniversary edition of Joy Williams's legendary second novel, an alcoholic mother is convinced after an accident that her baby has been replaced with another, which she takes with her to live on a surreal Northeastern island owned by her husband's wealthy family.

title: Fascism: A Warning
author: Madeleine Albright
description: Former Secretary of State Madeline Albright offers this guidebook for understanding fascism and the conditions under which authoritarians seize power, pointing to historical examples such as Hitler and Mussolini and sounding the warning bell for the contemporary rise of "anti-democratic" leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump.

title: Giant: Elizabeth Taylor, Rock Hudson, James Dean, Edna Ferber, and the Making of a Legendary American Film
author: Don Graham
description: A look behind the scenes at the making of the classic film about Texas and the more critical portrait in Edna Ferber's 1952 novel by the same name, which caused an uproar among Lone Star Staters who felt unfairly represented.

title: After Anna
author: Lisa Scottoline
description: When Maggie's estranged 17-year-old daughter Anna comes to live with her and her new husband and stepson, Anna ends up dead and Maggie's husband accused of the murder. In her search for the truth, Maggie uncovers even uglier secrets.

title: Indian Horse
author: Richard Wagamese
description: An Ojibway man struggling to recover from substance abuse looks back on his youth, during which he was forced to endure one of Canada's notoriously abusive residential schools for the forced assimilation of indigenous children and found solace, for a time, in the game of hockey.

title: The China Mission: George Marshall's Unfinished War, 1945-1947
author: Daniel Kurtz-Phelan
description: The executive editor of Foreign Affairs narrates the tale of George Marshall's attempt to intervene after World War II in China, ultimately failing to prevent Mao's Communist takeover.

title: Not Enough: Human Rights in an Unequal World
author: Samuel Moyn
publisher: Belknap Press: An Imprint of Harvard University Press
description: Yale law and history professor Samuel Moyn considers why economic egalitarianism has not emerged as a commitment among proponents of human rights who, Moyn argues, have focused on state violations of political rights at the expense of broader social and economic justice.

title: The Thief: A Novel of the Black Dagger Brotherhood
description: Protagonist Sola Morte has given up a life of crime to take care of her grandmother, but she can't keep her mind off of Assail, a former lover whom she has no idea is a vampire.

title: The Sixth Day
author: Catherine Coulter and J.T. Ellison
description: Special agents Nicholas Drummond and Michaela Caine take on a ruthless mastermind in the fifth thriller in the A Brit in the FBI series.

title: Shoot First
author: Stuart Woods
description: In the latest Stone Barrington novel, he must defend a woman whose business—and life—are under threat. From the sun-soaked Florida shores to an idyllic English country retreat, Stone embarks on a quest to protect his lovely new companion while searching for the mastermind behind the plot against her.

title: Beyond Measure: Essays
author: Rachel Z. Arndt
description: An essay collection that meditates on daily life and the way numbers, from mileage to body weight, inform and sometimes overtake our consciousness.

title: The Second O of Sorrow
author: Sean Thomas Dougherty
description: This new poetry collection confronts the illness of a partner, parenthood, and the daily moments of joy and grief in Ohio's Rust Belt.

title: The Duchess: Camilla Parker Bowles and the Love Affair That Rocked the Crown
author: Penny Junor
description: A biography of the controversial woman whose charisma charmed Prince Charles away from his marriage to Princess Diana and could make her the next Queen of England.

title: Cenzontle
author: Marcelo Hernandez Castillo
description: Chosen by Brenda Shaughnessy for the A. Poulin, Jr. prize, Cenzontle explores through a blend of surreal and narrative lyricism the vicissitudes of daily life, family, and love as a Mexican immigrant brought as a child to the United States.

title: The Plant Messiah: Adventures in Search of the World's Rarest Species
author: Carlos Magdalena
description: Carlos Magdalena is not your average horticulturist. He's a man on a mission to save the world's most endangered plants. First captivated by the flora of his native Spain, he has travelled to the remotest parts of the globe in search of exotic species. Renowned for his pioneering work, he has committed his life to protecting plants from man-made ecological destruction and thieves hunting for wealthy collectors.

title: Eisenhower vs. Warren: The Battle for Civil Rights and Liberties
author: James F. Simon
description: James F. Simon captures the bitter feud between President Dwight D. Eisenhower and Chief Justice Earl Warren that framed the tumultuous future of the modern civil rights movement.

title: Berenice Abbott: A Life in Photography
author: Julia Van Haaften
description: From the founding curator of the New York Public Library’s photography collection, a biography of the iconic 20th century American photographer, documentary modernist, author, and inventor.

title: The Library: A Catalogue of Wonders
author: Stuart Kells
description: Kells and his family became "Library Tourists" to research this history of the spaces dedicated to the collection and preservation of books, which spans from the ancient Great Library of Alexandria through contemporary archives and the bibliophiles who tend to them.

title: Woman of the Ashes: A Novel
author: Mia Couto Trans. by David Brookshaw
description: Alternating between the voices of Imani and Germano, Mia Couto’s Woman of the Ashes combines vivid folkloric prose with extensive historical research to give a spellbinding and unsettling account of war-torn Mozambique at the end of the nineteenth century.

title: Black Swans: Stories
author: Eve Babitz
description: In the latest re-release of her cult books, the Los Angeles bon vivant charts the descent of her jet set into middle age and the failures of her generation to look beyond their narcissism to confront systemic social problems.

title: The Prodigal Tongue: The Love-Hate Relationship Between American and British English
author: Lynne Murphy
description: An American linguist teaching in England explores the sibling rivalry between British and American English, offering insight into the peculiarities and origins of each version of the language.

title: Not Here
author: Hieu Minh Nguyen
description: A poetry collection about a queer Vietnamese American body in confrontation with whiteness, trauma, family, and nostalgia.

title: Misère: The Visual Representation of Misery in the 19th Century
author: Linda Nochlin
description: In Misère , famed art historian Linda Nochlin reveals how, in the new form of civilization produced by the Industrial Revolution, in which the phenomenal growth of wealth occurred alongside an expansion of squalor, writers and artists of the nineteenth century used their craft to come to terms with what were often new and unprecedented social, material, and psychological circumstances.

title: No Immediate Danger: Volume One of Carbon Ideologies
author: William T. Vollmann
description: The National Book Award-winning author of Europe Central examines the many causes of climate change, from industrial manufacturing and agricultural practices to fossil fuel extraction, economic demand for electric power, and the yearning of people all over the world to live in comfort.

title: You All Grow Up and Leave Me: A Memoir of Teenage Obsession
author: Piper Weiss
description: Set against Manhattan's elite prep school scene, a highly unsettling blend of true crime and memoir that offers an intimate and thought-provoking portrait of privileged girlhood.

title: Fire Dance
author: Ilana C. Myer
description: Palace intrigue, espionage, diplomacy, and dark magic are behind the story of one woman's epic mission to stop a magical conflagration.

title: Oceanic
author: Aimee Nezhukumatathil
description: With an encyclopedic range of subjects, Nezukumatathil takes a wide-angle look at our planet, its vulnerabilities, and the human condition in her poetry.

title: My Patients and Other Animals: A Veterinarian's Stories of Love, Loss, and Hope
author: Suzy Fincham-Gray
description: A moving memoir of a life spent in the company of animals—a veterinarian sheds light on the universal experience of loving, healing, and losing our beloved pets, and the many ways they change our lives.

title: Gateway to the Moon
author: Mary Morris
description: From award-winning novelist Mary Morris comes the story of a remote New Mexican town coming to grips with a dark history it never imagined. Luis de Torres, a Spanish Jew, accompanies Columbus as his interpreter on his voyage to America. Over the centuries, de Torres’ descendants travel from Spain and Portugal to Mexico, finally settling in the hills of New Mexico. Five hundred years later, Miguel Torres finds himself trying to understand the mystery that surrounds him and the town he grew up in.

title: The End of the French Intellectual: From Zola to Houellebecq
author: Shlomo Sand
description: A contemporary history professor from the University of Tel Aviv explores his disillusionment with French intellectual life, which he sees as transformed from a liberal force into a conservative one driven by Islamophobia.

title: Show Trial: Hollywood, HUAC, and the Birth of the Blacklist
author: Thomas Doherty
description: Thomas Doherty tells the story of the 1947 hearings into alleged Communist subversion in the movie industry. Show Trial is a character-driven inquiry into how the HUAC hearings ignited the Hollywood blacklist, providing a new history of one of the most influential events of the postwar era.

title: Daughters of the Winter Queen: Four Remarkable Sisters, the Crown of Bohemia, and the Enduring Legacy of Mary, Queen of Scots
author: Nancy Goldstone
description: The story of Elizabeth Stuart, the daughter of James I, and her four daughters raised in exile during the Dutch Golden Age, tracing how their lives shaped a three-decade war and fulfilled the promises of their great-grandmother, Mary Queen of Scots.

title: Ecstasy
author: Mary Sharratt
description: Gustav Klimt gave Alma her first kiss. Gustav Mahler fell in love with her at first sight and proposed only a few weeks later. Bauhaus founder Walter Gropius abandoned all reason to pursue her. Poet and novelist Franz Werfel described her as 'one of the very few magical women that exist.' But who was this woman who brought these most eminent of men to their knees?

title: A Breath After Drowning
author: Alice Blanchard
description: Kate Wolfe has been living with more than a decade of guilt after her sister's murder when she learns from a retired detective that her sister may have been one of many victims of a serial killer.

title: Building and Dwelling: Ethics for the City
author: Richard Sennett
description: Richard Sennett traces the anguished relation between how cities are built and how people live in them, from ancient Athens to twenty-first-century Shanghai

title: Blood Moon: An American Epic of War and Splendor in the Cherokee Nation
author: John Sedgwick
description: The story of the century-long feud between two rival Cherokee chiefs from the early years of the United States through the infamous Trail of Tears and into the Civil War.

title: Sophia of Silicon Valley
author: Anna Yen
description: Sophia Young lucks into a job that puts her directly in the path of Scott Kraft, the eccentric CEO of an animated film studio. As Scott Kraft’s right-hand woman, whip-smart Sophia is in the eye of the storm, sometimes floundering, sometimes nearly losing relationships and her health, but ultimately learning what it means to take charge of her own future the way the men around her do.

title: The Kremlin Ball
author: Curzio Malaparte, Trans. by Jenny McPhee
description: The first English edition of this surrealist study of Russia's Communist "aristocracy," which arose after the revolution and ultimately tumbled into Stalin's Great Terror, first published after the Italian writer's death in 1957.

title: Eventide
author: Therese Bohman, Trans. by Marlaine Delargy
description: An art professor at Stockholm University who has just ended an 11-year-relationship navigates through and meditates on her place in academia as well as in the realms of love and eroticism.

title: Lion Cross Point
author: Masatsugu Ono, Trans. by Angus Turvill
description: By the winner of the Akutagawa Prize, Japan's most prestigious literary award, this novel explores the mind of an orphaned ten-year-old boy who has moved to his family's home village, where he is cared for by strangers and remains haunted by his traumatic past.

title: The Trauma Cleaner: One Woman's Extraordinary Life in the Business of Death, Decay, and Disaster
author: Sarah Krasnostein
description: The biography of one of the people responsible for tidying up homes in the wake of natural―and unnatural―catastrophes and fatalities.

title: Bring the War Home: The White Power Movement and Paramilitary America
author: Kathleen Belew
description: In this expansive history of the white-power movement, Belew deconstructs the myth of the "lone wolf" perpetrators of white-supremacist violence and points to the reality of their movement within nationally organized networks of racist terrorist groups that consolidated around a sense of betrayal of veterans of the Vietnam War.

title: The Indian World of George Washington: The First President, the First Americans, and the Birth of the Nation
author: Colin G. Calloway
description: A Professor of History and Native American Studies at Dartmouth College offers a new look into the first U.S. President by considering him through the lens of his relationship with the Indian tribes and nations with which he by turns collaborated and battled.

title: Nobody's Girl Friday: The Women Who Ran Hollywood
author: J.E. Smyth
description: Historian J.E. Smyth challenges the idea that Hollywood has always been dominated by men, charting the deep involvement of women in all aspects of the film industry in the Golden Age of cinema.

title: The Female Persuasion
author: Meg Wolitzer
description: A coming-of-age story about what it means to be an empowered modern woman, focusing on a shy college student's relationship with a feminist icon.

title: The Recovering: Intoxication and Its Aftermath
author: Leslie Jamison
description: An exploration of addiction that blends memoir, cultural history, literary criticism, and journalistic reportage to analyze the role of stories in conveying the addiction experience, sharing insights based on the lives of artists whose achievements were shaped by addiction.

title: See What Can Be Done
author: Lorrie Moore
description: The celebrated fiction writer collects three decades' worth of essays and reviews on culture, politics, writing craft, and books.

title: Two Sisters: A Father, His Daughters, and Their Journey Into the Syrian Jihad
author: Åsne Seierstad, Trans. by Seán Kinsella
description: Two Norwegian-raised sisters of Somali descent secretly travel to Syria to join the Islamic State, devastating their family and sending their father on a mission to find them.

title: The Overstory
author: Richard Powers
description: National Book Award and Pulitzer Prize winner Richard Powers offers an ode to trees, which in this novel can communicate not only with one another but with humans, nine of whom have special arboreal ties that lead to their campaign to save North America's few remaining acres of virgin forest.

title: Look Alive Out There: Essays
author: Sloane Crosley
description: A collection of witty personal essays from the author of I Was Told There'd Be Cake and The Clasp .

title: First Person
author: Richard Flanagan
description: From the Man Booker Prize-winning author of The Narrow Road to the Deep North , a semi-autobiographical novel of a ghost writer writing the memoir of a notorious con man, and the chilling events that unfold as their lives become increasingly intertwined.

title: America Is Not the Heart
author: Elaine Castillo
description: A novel about three generations of Filipina women in one family struggling to balance the promise of the American dream and the unshakeable grip of history.

title: Varina
author: Charles Frazier
description: A novel set during and decades after the Civil War, from the author of Cold Mountain . Her marriage prospects limited, teenage Varina Howell agrees to wed the much-older widower Jefferson Davis, with whom she expects the secure life of a Mississippi landowner. Davis instead pursues a career in politics and is eventually appointed president of the Confederacy, placing Varina at the white-hot center of one of the darkest moments in American history.

title: How to Be Safe
author: Tom McAllister
description: A biting social novel about a recently suspended high school English teacher who is named a person of interest in the police investigation of a mass shooting at her school, and the chaos and irrationality that follows the tragedy.

title: Inseparable: The Original Siamese Twins and Their Rendezvous with American History
author: Yunte Huang
description: The story of America's most famous nineteenth-century Siamese twins, Chang and Eng Bunker (1811–1874)—twins conjoined at the sternum by a band of cartilage and a fused liver, who were “discovered” in Siam by a British merchant in 1824, and went on to become wealthy celebrities in the Jacksonian US South.

title: Space Odyssey: Stanley Kubrick, Arthur C. Clarke, and the Making of a Masterpiece
author: Michael Benson
description: Celebrating the fiftieth anniversary of the film’s release, the story of the making of 2001: A Space Odyssey , acclaimed today as one of the greatest films ever made, including the inside account of how director Stanley Kubrick and writer Arthur C. Clarke created this cinematic masterpiece.

title: The Oracle Year
author: Charles Soule
description: Awakening from a dream with more than one hundred predictions about the future in his head, an unassuming Manhattan bassist becomes one of the world's most powerful men and hides his identity behind an online persona that is targeted by greedy corporations and dangerous enemies.

title: Border Districts: A Fiction
author: Gerald Murnane
description: An aging man moves from a bustling city to a 'border' town, where he settles down to map his mental landscape, contemplating his memories and impressions in poetic detail.

title: Something Wonderful: Rodgers and Hammerstein's Broadway Revolution
author: Todd S. Purdum
description: In this portrait of Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II, readers learn how one of the most successful musical partnerships collaborated - and often clashed - to develop some of the most innovative and popular stage shows of the 20th century.

title: Wade in the Water: Poems
author: Tracy K Smith
description: A new poetry collection by Tracy K. Smith, the Poet Laureate of the United States, in which she ties America’s contemporary moment both to our nation’s fraught founding history and to a sense of the spirit, the everlasting.

title: No Way Home: A Memoir of Life on the Run
author: Tyler Wetherall
description: A memoir of growing up on the run--and what happens when it comes to a stop.

title: Wonderblood
author: Julia Whicker
description: In this dystopian tale set 500 years hence, a mad cow-like disease called "Bent Head" has ravaged Earths' population, the remaining members of which practice magic and violent sacrifice.

title: Women in Sunlight
author: Frances Mayes
description: In the latest from the bestselling author of Under the Tuscan Sun , an expat writer living in a Tuscan village gets an idea for her book when four older American women come to town for a year-long vacation in which they deepen their friendship, rediscover their talents, and otherwise thrive.

title: Rocket Men: The Daring Odyssey of Apollo 8 and the Astronauts Who Made Man's First Journey to the Moon
author: Robert Kurson
description: The inside, lesser-known story of NASA's boldest and riskiest mission: Apollo 8.

title: Make Trouble: Standing Up, Speaking Out, and Finding the Courage to Lead
author: Cecile Richards
description: From the outgoing president of Planned Parenthood Federation of America and daughter of the firebrand Texas Governor, a memoir about learning to lead and make change, based on a lifetime of fighting for women's rights and social justice.

title: The Promise and the Dream: The Untold Story of Martin Luther King, Jr. and Robert F. Kennedy
author: David Margolick
description: Fifty years after they were both murdered, journalist David Margolick explores the untold story of the complex and ever-evolving relationship between these two American icons.

title: On Grand Strategy
author: John Lewis Gaddis
description: Ten essays that look back at the strategic thinking of history's most iconic military leaders, from Pulitzer Prize–winning historian Gaddis.

title: Eunice: The Kennedy Who Changed the World
author: Eileen McNamara
description: From Pulitzer Prize-winning Boston Globe journalist, a biography of Eunice Kennedy Shriver--the fifth of nine Kennedy children and lifelong advocate for people with cognitive disabilities.

title: The Road to Unfreedom: Russia, Europe, America
author: Timothy Snyder
description: Yale history professor and the author of On Tyranny returns with a look at the rise of fascism told through the lens of Russia's evolution since the end of the Cold War, particularly Vladimir Putin's messianic drive to take down liberal democracy in Europe and the United States.

title: The Consciousness Instinct: Unraveling the Mystery of How the Brain Makes the Mind
author: Michael S. Gazzaniga
description: One of the world's leading neuroscientists tackles the problem of consciousness, combining philosophical thought on the subject with contemporary research to unravel the mystery of perception and our sense of ourselves and the world.

title: Lawn Boy
author: Jonathan Evison
description: The bestselling author of The Revised Fundamentals of Caregiving gives us the story of Mike Muñoz, an intelligent young man struggling to balance his desire to make his mark on the world with a grinding job landscaping the lawns of rich folks and a home life bogged down by poverty and illness.

title: Bluff
author: Michael Kardos
description: Bluff takes us deep inside the fraught and fascinating world of a modern magician who becomes obsessed with magic's dark twin--the underworld of the card cheat.

title: Darwin Comes to Town: How the Urban Jungle Drives Evolution
author: Menno Schilthuizen
description: A senior research scientist at Naturalis Biodiversity Center in the Netherlands tracks the fast pace of evolutionary change among animals in world cities, which are adapting in strange and surprising ways to the rapidly spreading human development that has destroyed their natural habitats.

title: Eye Level: Poems
author: Jenny Xie
description: In this collection chosen by former U.S. Poet Laureate Juan Felipe Herrera for the Walt Whitman Award from the Academy of American Poets, Jenny Xie ponders the sights and sounds of life in New York, her travels in Asia, and the experience of growing up as a Chinese immigrant in New Jersey.

title: My Dear Hamilton: A Novel of Eliza Schuyler Hamilton
author: Stephanie Dray and Laura Kamoie
description: From the New York Times bestselling authors of America’s First Daughter comes the epic story of Eliza Schuyler Hamilton—a revolutionary woman who, like her new nation, struggled to define herself in the wake of war, betrayal, and tragedy. In this haunting, moving, and beautifully written novel, Dray and Kamoie used thousands of letters and original sources to tell Eliza’s story as it’s never been told before—not just as the wronged wife at the center of a political sex scandal—but also as a founding mother who shaped an American legacy in her own right.

title: Golden Prey
author: John Sandford
description: Lucas Davenport's first case as a U.S. marshal takes him into unexplored territory in this thrilling novel in the #1 New York Times -bestselling Prey series.

title: The Man Who Caught the Storm: The Life of Legendary Tornado Chaser Tim Samaras
author: Brantley Hargrove
description: A biography of the life and death of Tim Samaras, an amateur "storm chaser" whose derring-do and technological innovations earned him a place of prominence in the university-educated world of tornado scientists.

title: Asking for a Friend: Three Centuries of Advice on Life, Love, Money, and Other Burning Questions from a Nation Obsessed
author: Jessica Weisberg
description: A historical look at the advice columnists, gurus, and talking heads who for centuries have driven America's popular and profitable self-help industry.

title: Paris by the Book
author: Liam Callanan
description: A missing person, a grieving family, a curious clue: a half-finished manuscript set in Paris. Heading off in search of its author, a mother and her daughters find themselves in France, rescuing a failing bookstore and drawing closer to unexpected truths.

title: My American Dream: A Life of Love, Family, and Food
author: Lidia Matticchio Bastianich
description: Lidia Matticchio Bastianich's memoir that touches on her close-knit family, her dedication and endless passion for food that ultimately led to multiple restaurants, many cookbooks, and twenty years on public television as the host of her own cooking show.

title: Stream System: The Collected Short Fiction of Gerald Murnane
author: Gerald Murnane
description: A collection of stories written by Australian writer Gerald Murnane.

title: Denmark Vesey's Garden: Slavery and Memory in the Cradle of the Confederacy
author: Ethan J Kytle, Blain Roberts
description: Denmark Vesey’s Garden reveals the deep roots of these controversies and traces them to the heart of slavery in the United States: Charleston, South Carolina, where almost half of the U.S. slave population stepped onto our shores, where the first shot at Fort Sumter began the Civil War, and where Dylann Roof shot nine people at Emanuel A.M.E. Church, the congregation of Denmark Vesey, a black revolutionary who plotted a massive slave insurrection in 1822.

title: Can't Help Myself: Lessons & Confessions from a Modern Advice Columnist
author: Meredith Goldstein
description: Advice columnist from the Boston Globe, Meredith Goldstein, shares a memoir via stories and letters revealing her own search for answers to relationship issues and the like.

title: Yellow Negroes and Other Imaginary Creatures
author: Yvan Alagbé, Trans. by Donald Nicholson-Smith
description: A collection of work about race and immigration in Paris by one of France's most revered cult comic book artists.

title: The Death of Democracy: Hitler's Rise to Power and the Downfall of the Weimar Republic
author: Benjamin Carter Hett
description: From a City University of New York history professor, an exploration of how the Nazi Party came to power through the failures of the Weimar Republic and the shortsightedness of German politicians.

title: Things That Make White People Uncomfortable
author: Michael Bennett and David Zirin
description: With The Nation 's David Zirin, Super Bowl Champion and three-time Pro Bowler Michael Bennett writes about growing up in the racist Deep South, charts his rise to the NFL, and explores the development of his activism in Black Lives Matter and other social-justice movements.

title: The Phantom Atlas: The Greatest Myths, Lies and Blunders on Maps
author: Edward Brooke-Hitching
description: The Phantom Atlas is a guide to the world not as it is, but as it was imagined to be. It's a world of ghost islands, invisible mountain ranges, mythical civilizations, ship-wrecking beasts, and other fictitious features introduced on maps and atlases through mistakes, misunderstanding, fantasies, and outright lies.

title: Sugar: The World Corrupted: From Slavery to Obesity
author: James Walvin
description: Historian James Walvin looks at the history of our collective sweet tooth, exploring how slavery enabled mass consumption of the difficult-to-farm crop and transformed the tastes and health of the Western world.

title: Because We Are Bad: OCD and a Girl Lost in Thought
author: Lily Bailey
description: A British model describes her life-long battle with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder, which since childhood has taken the form of an "other" living inside her and compelling her harmful thoughts and actions.

title: Ritz and Escoffier: The Hotelier, the Chef, and the Rise of the Leisure Class
author: Luke Barr
description: Luke Barr transports readers to turn-of-the-century London and Paris to discover how celebrated hotelier César Ritz and famed chef Auguste Escoffier joined forces at the Savoy Hotel to spawn the modern luxury hotel and restaurant, where women and American Jews mingled with British high society, signaling a new social order and the rise of the middle class.

title: Greeks Bearing Gifts
author: Philip Kerr
description: The 13th and first posthumous novel in the Bernie Gunther series finds the former Nazi-collaborating sleuth in Munich in 1956 with a new name and a dead-end career as an insurance-claims adjuster, which sends him on an investigation of a claim by a former Wehrmacht soldier who served in Greece during the war.

title: Dread Nation
author: Justina Ireland
description: In this reimagined history of the United States, the U.S. Civil War has ended with Confederate and Union soldiers risen from the dead, zombies who are combated by black and brown-skinned Americans who have been conscripted to fight them.

title: The War on Normal People: The Truth about America's Disappearing Jobs and Why Universal Basic Income Is Our Future
author: Andrew Yang
description: From entrepreneur Andrew Yang, the founder of Venture for America, a look at how new technologies are erasing millions of jobs and the steps he thinks America should take, including instituting a universal basic income, to stabilize our economy.

title: The Neuroscientist Who Lost Her Mind: My Tale of Madness and Recovery
author: Barbara K. Lipska
description: As a deadly cancer spread inside her brain, leading neuroscientist Barbara Lipska was plunged into madness—only to miraculously survive with her memories intact. In the tradition of My Stroke of Insight and Brain on Fire , this memoir recounts her ordeal, and explains its lessons about the brain and mind.

title: Making Things Right: The Simple Philosophy of a Working Life
author: Ole Thorstensen
description: Making Things Right is a portrayal of a tightknit working community, a story about the blood, sweat, and frustration involved in doing a job well and the joys in seeing a vision take shape.

title: Animals Eat Each Other
author: Elle Nash
description: A girl with no name embarks on a fraught three-way relationship with Matt, a Satanist and a tattoo artist, and his girlfriend Frances, a new mom.

title: State of Resistance: What California's Dizzying Descent and Remarkable Resurgence Mean for America's Future
author: Manuel Pastor
description: USC Sociology professor Pastor considers California’s political history and the lessons that can be drawn from it on issues like immigration, socioeconomic policies, and labor reform.

title: Cave of Bones
author: Anne Hillerman
description: Anne Hillerman’s fourth novel in the New Mexico-set detective series that extends the work of her late father, Tony Hillerman, featuring Navajo tribal police officers Joe Leaphorn, Jim Chee, and Bernadette “Bernie” Manuelito.

title: Blue Self-Portrait
author: Noémi Lefebvre, Trans. by Sophie Lewis
description: On a flight from Berlin to Paris, a woman haunted by composer Arnold Schoenberg’s self-portrait reflects on her romantic encounter with a pianist.

title: Betwixt-And-Between: Essays on the Writing Life
author: Betwixt and Between
description: A book on writing craft that eschews didacticism in favor of digression, reflection, imagination, and capturing visceral experience.

title: Lexington and Concord: The Battle Heard Round the World
author: George C Daughan
description: An award-winning historian reinterprets the battle that launched the American Revolution.

title: Weeping Waters
author: Karin Brynard
description: In this winner of the University of Johannesburg Debut Prize in 2012, Inspector Albertus Beeslaar—a white police officer—has abandoned tough Johannesburg for a backwater post but finds himself back in the thick of it when his new community is rocked by a crime syndicate. Beeslaar works to train rookie local cops—who are black—stirring racial tensions among those who share a common goal of peace.

title: Christian: The Politics of a Word in America
author: Matthew Bowman
description: History professor Matthew Bowman delves into the ongoing struggle over the potent word "Christian," not merely to settle theological disputes but to discover its centrality to American politics.

title: The Seminarian: Martin Luther King Jr. Comes of Age
author: Patrick Parr
description: Drawing on archival materials and interviews, this book investigates Martin Luther King Jr.'s years at the Crozer Theological Seminary, where his courses, relationships, and early preaching laid the intellectual foundation for the future Nobel laureate.

title: Bad Stories: What the Hell Just Happened to Our Country
author: Steve Almond
description: The New York Times bestselling author and one half of the Dear Sugars podcast duo with Cheryl Strayed reckons with the election of President Donald Trump as a failure of storytelling, in which the American public has come to believe more than a dozen "bad stories" he charts and rebuts in this essay collection.

title: The House of Remembering and Forgetting
author: Filip David and Trans. by Christina Pribicevic-Zoric
description: Mosaic, non-linear and semi-autobiographical, this book is reminiscent in style of Kurt Vonnegut's Slaughterhouse-Five and in theme of the works of Primo Levi. In documenting the stories of child survivors, it is a moving and necessary addition to the literature of the Holocaust.

title: Evolution of Desire: A Life of René Girard
author: Cynthia L. Haven
description: In this mix of biography, memoir, and primer on the ideas of René Girard (1923-2015), Cynthia L. Haven traces the evolution of Girard's thought—particularly on mimetic desire—in parallel with his life and times.

title: The Practicing Stoic: A Philosophical User's Manual
author: Ward Farnsworth
description: This book brings the insights of all the Stoic philosophers together for the first time, systematically presenting what they said on topics ranging from "virtue" to "death."

title: Tangerine
author: Christine Mangan
description: A Hitchcockian noir set in 1950s Morocco. Arriving in Tangier with her new husband, only to encounter the estranged best friend she has not seen in more than a year, Alice allows her friend to introduce her to the rhythms and culture of the city, but is quickly stifled by the woman's controlling nature.

title: The Chandelier
author: Clarice Lispector, Trans. by Benjamin Moser & Magdalena Edwards
description: The iconic Brazilian writer's 1946 second novel, translated into English for the first time, is the story of two siblings and the secrets that bind them together.

title: Bob Honey Who Just Do Stuff
author: Sean Penn
description: An absurdist dystopian novel and Trump-era satire by the actor Sean Penn, about an eccentric man who moonlights as an assassin.

title: I Was Anastasia
author: Ariel Lawhon
description: Novelist Ariel Lawhon imagines the lives of Anastasia Romanov, the daughter of the Tsar thought to be executed in 1918 by the Bolsheviks, and Anna Anderson, the woman who claimed to be Anastasia, revealing herself after surviving the Revolution in hiding.

title: Selfie: How We Became So Self-Obsessed and What It's Doing to Us
author: Will Storr
description: A book exploring the obsession with the self. Storr takes the reader on a journey from the shores of Ancient Greece, through the Christian Middle Ages, to the self-esteem evangelists of 1980s California, the rise of narcissism and the 'selfie' generation, and right up to the era of hyper-individualism in which we live now.

title: Tiger Woods
author: Jeff Benedict & Armen Keteyian
description: Benedict and Keteyian construct a psychological profile of an African American child programmed by an attention-grabbing father and the original Tiger Mom to be the "chosen one" to change not just the game of golf, but the world as well. But at what cost?

title: Jackrabbit Smile (Hap and Leonard)
author: Joe R. Lansdale
description: Judith Mulhaney's daughter, Jackrabbit, has been missing for five years and Hap and Leonard take the case. It isn't long until they find themselves mixed up in a revivalist cult that believes Jesus will return flanked by an army of lizard-men-- solving a murder to boot.

title: To Change the Church: Pope Francis and the Future of Catholicism
author: Ross Douthat
description: Whether Francis or his critics are right won't just determine whether he ends up as a hero or a tragic figure for Catholics--it will determine whether he's a hero or a gambler who's betraying both his church and his civilization into the hands of its enemies.

title: Searching for Stars on an Island in Maine
author: Alan Lightman
description: In this collection of essays, the bestselling author of Einstein's Dreams tries to square science with spirituality, drawing on experiences from his own life as well as the lives of history's great secular and religious thinkers.

title: The Sun Does Shine: How I Found Life and Freedom on Death Row
author: Anthony Ray Hinton, co-written with Lara Love Hardin
description: After being wrongfully convicted of two murders and an attempted murder in 1985, Anthony Ray Hinton spent 30 years on death row, an experience he recounts in this memoir that explores how his relationships, spirituality, and love of literature allowed him to survive and even forgive those in the criminal justice system he nonetheless condemns as racist and broken.

title: Neruda: The Poet's Calling
author: Mark Eisner
description: A portrait of Pablo Neruda, one of the most intriguing and influential figures in Latin American history.

title: To Die But Once: A Maisie Dobbs Novel
author: Jacqueline Winspear
description: During the months following Britain's declaration of war on Germany during World War II, Maisie Dobbs investigates the disappearance of a young apprentice working on a hush-hush government contract and must contend with one of the London underworld's most powerful men trying to profit from wartime opportunism.

title: Who We Are and How We Got Here: Ancient DNA and the New Science of the Human Past
author: David Reich
description: Harvard genetics professor David Reich tells the story of human origins recently revealed as much more complicated than originally thought thanks to advances in genetics technology, which offer new insights into ancient human innovations in archeology, linguistics, and the written word.

title: The Solitary Twin
author: Harry Mathews
description: In this posthumous novel by the avant-garde writer, a small town is intrigued by two male twins who do not associate with one another but share a lover, dress in similar clothes, and have other uncanny connections that inspire two couples to try to unravel the twins' secrets.

title: The Queens of Innis Lear
author: Tessa Gratton
description: In this reimagining of Shakespeare's King Lear , the titular king has become obsessed with star prophesy, an art he's taught his youngest daughter, Elia, whom he nonetheless exiles from the island of Innis Lear when she refuses to flatter him lavishly enough, leaving him in the hands of his two older, greedier daughters.

title: Faith: A Journey for All
author: Jimmy Carter
description: The 39th U.S. President investigates the meaning of faith and the role it has played in his own life as well as in American life and policy.

title: The Beekeeper: Rescuing the Stolen Women of Iraq
author: Dunya Mikhail, Trans. by Max Weiss
