description: An Iraqi journalist and poet living in New York returns to her home country to document the stories of Yazidi women who were enslaved by ISIS (Daesh) as well as that of a beekeeper who organized elaborate rescue missions to bring the women home.

title: Battleship Yamato: Of War, Beauty and Irony
author: Jan Morris
description: An extraordinary--and strikingly illustrated--reflection on the meaning of war from author Jan Morris.

title: The Disappeared
author: C. J. Box
description: The latest installment in the Wyoming-set Joe Pickett series from "the king of cowboy noir," C. J. Box.

title: The Girl Who Was Taken
author: Charlie Donlea
description: The night they go missing, high school seniors Nicole Cutty and Megan McDonald are at a beach party in their small town of Emerson Bay, North Carolina. Police launch a massive search, but hope is almost lost—until Megan escapes from a bunker deep in the woods. . . . A year later, the bestselling account of her ordeal has made Megan a celebrity. It’s a triumphant story, except for one inconvenient detail: Nicole is still missing.

title: The Whispering Room: A Jane Hawk Novel
author: Dean Koontz
description: “No time to delay. Do what you were born to do. Fame will be yours when you do this.” These are the words that ring in the mind of mild-mannered, beloved schoolteacher Cora Gundersun—just before she takes her own life, and many others’, in a shocking act of carnage. When the disturbing contents of her secret journal are discovered, it seems certain that she must have been insane. But Jane Hawk knows better.

title: John Ashbery: They Knew What They Wanted: Collages and Poems
author: John Ashbery
description: One of the most influential poets of the last century was also a collage artist, and this book pairs selections of his associative poetry with prints of his surreal assemblages, revealing how one artistic practice informed the other.

title: You Can Stop Humming Now: A Doctor's Stories of Life, Death, and in Between
author: Daniela Lamas
description: A pulmonary and critical care doctor meditates on the role of medical professionals and their interventions in the lives of patients, several of whom she chronicles in their struggles with extreme illness.

title: A Spy in Canaan: How the FBI Used a Famous Photographer to Infiltrate the Civil Rights Movement
author: Marc Perrusquia
description: A Memphis journalist unravels the double life of the Civil Rights Movement's most famous photographer as an FBI informant, chronicling Ernest Withers' monumental betrayal as well as his own dramatic reporting of the story.

title: Pogrom: Kishinev and the Tilt of History
author: Steven J. Zipperstein
description: Separating historical fact from fantasy, a retelling of the story of Kishinev, a riot that transformed the course of twentieth-century Jewish history.

title: Cruel Futures
author: Carmen Gimenez Smith
description: Examines subjects as divergent as Alzheimers, Medusa, mumblecore, and mental illness in taut poems. An analysis of popular culture, as well as an exploration of the many social roles that women occupy as mother, daughter, lover, and the resulting struggle to maintain personhood—all in a late capitalist America.

title: The Italian Teacher
author: Tom Rachman
description: From the author of The Imperfectionists , a warmly satirical novel about a man living in the shadow of, and trying to prove himself to, his famous painter father.

title: Just the Funny Parts ... and a Few Hard Truths About Sneaking into the Hollywood Boys' Club
author: Nell Scovall
description: Writer, producer, and director Nell Scovell reveals life behind the curtain at many iconic television sitcoms and comedies, where she was often the only woman in the room.

title: Class Matters: The Strange Career of an American Delusion
author: Steve Fraser
description: An exploration of the hidden history of class in American life.

title: The Pleasure Shock: The Rise of Deep Brain Stimulation and Its Forgotten Inventor
author: Lone Frank
description: A neurobiologist and science writer remembers Robert G. Heath, a controversial psychiatrist whose brain experiments earned him a reputation among his critics as a monster, an identity the writer complicates.

title: Stray City
author: Chelsey Johnson
description: Heartbreak leads a member of Portland's "Lesbian Mafia" to quietly experiment with heterosexual romance, a secret that becomes impossible to keep when she becomes pregnant.

title: The Punishment She Deserves: A Lynley Novel
author: Elizabeth George
description: In the 20th novel in Elizabeth George's Inspector Thomas Lynley series, Detective Sergeant Barbara Havers investigates the death of a respected deacon in scenic Ludlow, where she suspects foul play and uncovers many secrets beneath the bucolic surface of the town

title: Aetherial Worlds
author: Tatyana Tolstaya, Trans. by Anya Migdal
description: In her first book in English in over two decades, Tatyana Tolstaya mixes memoir, fiction, and magic to produce tales that comment poetically on modern life in Russia, the United States, and beyond.

title: The Wife's Tale: A Personal History
author: Aida Edemariam
description: A journalist from The Guardian narrates the extraordinary life of her Ethiopian grandmother, a child bride, born in 1916, who lived through the country's invasion by Fascist Italy.

title: The Eight Mountains
author: Paolo Cognetti, Trans. by Simon Carnell
description: Winner of the Strega Prize, Italy’s highest literary honor, this coming-of-age novel about a young man from Milan who spends summers in the Italian Alps muses on the effects of the mountain landscape on one's life and relationships.

title: Patriot Number One: American Dreams in Chinatown
author: Lauren Hilgers
description: The deeply reported story of a Chinese dissident who moved from rural China to New York City, and how he and his wife try to forge a life between two worlds.

title: The Gunners
author: Rebecca Kauffman
description: A novel about a once-close-kint group of childhood friends who come together after ten years when one of their members commits suicide.

title: Alternate Side
author: Anna Quindlen
description: The Nolans live a charmed life on Manhattan's Upper West Side, until a violent incident over a parking spot reveals the fault-lines of race, class, and monogamy shifting beneath the surface of their seemingly idyllic neighborhood.

title: The Temptation of Forgiveness: A Commissario Guido Brunetti Mystery
author: Donna Leon
description: In the 27th novel in Donna Leon's bestselling mystery series, Commissario Guido Brunetti tries to help a family friend who fears her son is dabbling in drugs, uncovering a longstanding scam with disturbing unintended consequences.

title: What Is Real?: The Unfinished Quest for the Meaning of Quantum Physics
author: Adam Becker
description: What Is Real? is a gripping story on the battle of ideas and the courageous scientists who dared to stand up for the truth of quantum physics.

title: The Space Barons: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and the Quest to Colonize the Cosmos
author: Christian Davenport
description: A journalist from The Washington Post follows Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, and others who are working toward - and battling for control over - a future in which humans may eventually live on planets other than Earth.

title: American Histories
author: John Edgar Wideman
description: An extended meditation on family, history, and loss, American Histories is short story collection that weaves together historical fact, philosophical wisdom, and deeply personal autobiographical vignettes.

title: William Howard Taft
author: Jeffrey Rosen
description: From the American Presidents series, a biography of the 27th President of the United States--the only man to serve as both President and Chief Justice.

title: The Age of Eisenhower: America and the World in the 1950s
author: William I Hitchcock
description: An expansive account of the presidency of Dwight D. Eisenhower, drawing extensively on declassified material from the Eisenhower Library, the CIA and Defense Department, and troves of unpublished documents.

title: Why Baseball Matters
author: Susan Jacoby
description: Passionate baseball fan takes a tough-minded look at America's most traditional game in our twenty-first-century culture of digital distraction.

title: (((Semitism))): Being Jewish in America in the Age of Trump
author: Jonathan Weisman
description: A short contemplation on how Jews are viewed in America since the election of Donald J. Trump, and how we can move forward to fight anti-Semitism.

title: Every Note Played
author: Lisa Genova
description: A once accomplished concert pianist, Richard now has ALS. As he becomes increasingly paralyzed and is no longer able to live on his own, Karina becomes his reluctant caretaker. As Richard's muscles, voice, and breath fade, both he and Karina try to reconcile their past before it's too late.

title: Bury What We Cannot Take: A Novel
author: Kirstin Chen
description: Against the backdrop of early Maoist China, this captivating and emotional tale follows a brother, a sister, a father, and a mother as they grapple with their agonizing decision, its far-reaching consequences, and their hope for redemption.

title: Never Remember: Searching for Stalin's Gulags in Putin's Russia
author: Masha Gessen, photographs by Misha Friedman
description: A hybrid work of essay and photography. Drawing on years of interviews, research, and travel, Gessen and photographer Friedman reflect on complex Russian attitudes to the legacy of the gulag.

title: Trenton Makes
author: Tadzio Koelb
description: A woman carves out her share of the American Dream by living as a man.

title: In a Day's Work: The Fight to End Sexual Violence Against America's Most Vulnerable Workers
author: Bernice Yeung
description: Investigative journalist Bernice Yeung exposes the epidemic of sexual violence levied against women farmworkers, domestic workers, and janitorial workers and charts their quest for justice in the workplace.

title: The Street Philosophy of Garry Winogrand
author: Geoff Dyer, Garry Winogrand
description: Dyer takes the viewer/reader on a wildly original journey through both iconic and unseen images from the archive, including eighteen previously unpublished color photographs taken by Garry Winogrand.

title: The Sparsholt Affair
author: Alan Hollinghurst
description: From the winner of the Man Booker Prize, a multi-generational portrait of gay life that plumbs the complex relationships of a remarkable family and the effect a highly public midcentury scandal has on their legacy.

title: Whiskey
author: Bruce Holbert
description: Three generations of a hardscrabble family in Washington State struggle with tough lives, bad choices, and alcohol.

title: Pure Hollywood: And Other Stories
author: Christine Schutt
description: Pure Hollywood brings us into private worlds of corrupt familial love, intimacy, longing, and danger. From an alcoholic widowed actress living in desert seclusion to a young mother whose rejection of her child has terrible consequences, from a newlywed couple who ignore the violent warnings of a painter burned by love to an eerie portrait of erotic obsession, each story is an imagistic snapshot of what it means to live and learn, love and hurt.

title: Russian Roulette: The Inside Story of Putin's War on America and the Election of Donald Trump
author: Michael Isikoff, David Corn
description: Russian Roulette is a story of political skullduggery unprecedented in American history. It weaves together tales of international intrigue, cyber espionage, and superpower rivalry. After U.S.-Russia relations soured, as Vladimir Putin moved to reassert Russian strength on the global stage, Moscow trained its best hackers and trolls on U.S. political targets and exploited WikiLeaks to disseminate information that could affect the 2016 election.

title: Memento Park: A Novel
author: Mark Sarvas
description: A son learns more about his father than he ever could have imagined when a mysterious piece of art is unexpectedly restored to him.

title: The Flight Attendant
author: Chris Bohjalian
description: A flight attendant wakes up next to a dead man and must clear her name - and elude the real killers - now that she is the prime suspect for the murder.

title: Disappointment River: Finding and Losing the Northwest Passage
author: Brian Castner
description: This writer and explorer traces Alexander Mackenzie's 1789 Canadian river journey to discover the Northwest Passage. Where Mackenzie was blocked by subarctic ice, global warming has cleared the path for Castner, whose book merges a history of Mackenzie's travels with his own observations.

title: The Life to Come
author: Michelle de Kretser
description: Set in Australia, France, and Sri Lanka, The Life to Come is about the stories we tell and don't tell ourselves as individuals, as societies, and as nations. Driven by a vivid cast of characters, it explores necessary emigration, the art of fiction, and ethnic and class conflict.

title: The Merry Spinster: Tales of Everyday Horror
author: Mallory Ortberg
description: A collection of darkly playful stories based on classic folk and fairy tales (but with a feminist spin) that find the sinister in the familiar and the familiar in the alien.

title: Men and Apparitions
author: Lynne Tillman
description: An exploration of modern masculinity, told from the perspective of Ezekiel Hooper Stark, a 30-something ethnographer and assistant professor who sifts through photographs to construct the narratives of family and strangers.

title: Paris Metro
author: Wendell Steavenson
description: After a war correspondent marries and has a child with the son of an Iraqi executed by Saddam Hussein, she finds herself in Paris, where she falls prey to prejudice and paranoia while implicated in unexpected ways in terrorism.

title: To the Edges of the Earth: 1909, the Race for the Three Poles, and the Climax of the Age of Exploration
author: Edward J. Larson
description: A narrative of the most adventurous year of all time, when three expeditions simultaneously raced to the top, bottom, and heights of the world.

title: No Turning Back: Life, Loss, and Hope in Wartime Syria
author: Rania Abouzeid
description: No Turning Back tells the tragedy of the Syrian War through the dramatic stories of four young people seeking safety and freedom in a shattered country.

title: The Parking Lot Attendant: A Novel
author: Nafkota Tamirat
description: A coming-of-age story about a girl in Boston's tightly-knit Ethiopian community who falls under the spell of a charismatic hustler out to change the world.

title: Graffiti Palace
author: A.G. Lombardo
description: Inspired by Homer's The Odyssey , this debut novel narrates a young man's difficult journey home to his lover during the outbreak of the 1965 Watts rebellion in Los Angeles.

title: Let Me Lie
author: Clare Mackintosh
description: A young woman digs into family secrets to understand why - or if - her parents committed suicide, unless whoever doesn't want her to know blocks her path.

title: Picasso and the Painting That Shocked the World
author: Miles J. Unger
description: When Pablo Picasso painted Les Demoiselles d’Avignon , now considered a Modernist masterpiece credited with sparking Cubism, the painting was widely reviled for reasons Miles J. Unger unpacks in this book that considers not only Picasso's genius but the peculiarities of the Parisian art world that birthed Les Demoiselles .

title: Anatomy of a Miracle: A Novel
author: Jonathan Miles
description: In this novel that purports to be written by an investigative reporter, a paralyzed combat veteran miraculously regains use of his legs, setting off an international sensation that enthralls the Vatican, social media, and Reality TV.

title: Laura & Emma
author: Kate Greathead
description: A novel spanning 1980 to 1995 in which Laura, a offbeat woman in her early 30s from Manhattan’s Upper East Side who attempts to balance her progressive ideals with the lavish lifestyle she lives thanks to a trust fund, finds herself pregnant from a one night stand and decides to keep the baby.

title: Visionary Women: How Rachel Carson, Jane Jacobs, Jane Goodall, and Alice Waters Changed Our World
author: Andrea Barnet
description: Four interlinked biographical essays offer a window into the life of each woman while considering how their seemingly disparate concerns - pesticides, urban renewal, chimpanzee behavior, and farm-to-table dining - spurred Americans in the 1960s to consider their connection to the world around them, a psychological shift that continues to influence society.

title: Feast Days
author: Ian MacKenzie
description: A young wife relocates with her financier husband to Sao Paulo, where her life of cushy privilege juxtaposes the crime, protests, refugees, and gentrification that roil around her as she contends with expat life and a newly rocky marriage.

title: The Rising Sea
author: Clive Cussler and Graham Brown
description: An alarming rise in the world's sea levels--much larger than could be accounted for by glacier melt--sends Kurt Austin, Joe Zavala, and the rest of the NUMA scientific team rocketing around the globe in search of answers.

title: The Last Watchman of Old Cairo
author: Michael David Lukas
description: The arrival of a mysterious package sets the son of a Jewish mother and a Muslim father on a journey to Cairo to unravel the shared history that connects the two sides of his family, with characters appearing from medieval Cairo, Victorian England, and contemporary Berkley.

title: The Price of the Haircut: Stories
author: Brock Clarke
description: A collection of short stories bursting with absurdist plot twists and laced with wit.

title: Ghost Of
author: Diana Khoi Nguyen
description: Winner of the Omnidawn Open Poetry Book Prize, Ghost Of is a mourning song. By working with, in, and around the photographs that her brother left behind (from which he cut himself out before his death), Nguyen wrestles with what remains.

title: What Drowns the Flowers in Your Mouth: A Memoir of Brotherhood
author: Rigoberto González
description: A chronicle of the complexities of Latino masculinity and the bond between two brothers haunted by traumas of their childhood.

title: Free Woman: Life, Liberation and Doris Lessing
author: Lara Feigel
description: Overcome by midlife ennui, a Reader in Modern Literature and Culture at King's College London begins a rigorous study of Doris Lessing's oeuvre and life, on which she decides to model and document her own experiments in "free" living.

title: Census
author: Jesse Ball
description: When a unnamed widower receives notice from a doctor that he doesn’t have long left to live, he is struck by the question of who will care for his adult son—a son whom he fiercely loves, a boy with Down syndrome. With no recourse in mind, and with a desire to see the country on one last trip, the man signs up as a census taker for a mysterious governmental bureau and leaves town with his son.

title: Cloudbursts
author: Thomas McGuane
description: A career-spanning compendium of short stories, mostly set in Big Sky Country, from one of the contemporary American masters of the form.

title: Speak No Evil
author: Uzodinma Iweala
description: In this coming-of-age novel, the son of Nigerian immigrants struggles with his gay identity and his parents' sharp disapproval.

title: The House of Broken Angels
author: Luis Alberto Urrea
description: In his final days, beloved and ailing patriarch Miguel Angel de La Cruz, affectionately called Big Angel, has summoned his entire Mexican-American clan for one last legendary birthday party. But as the party approaches, his mother, nearly one hundred, dies herself, leading to a farewell doubleheader in a single weekend.

title: Unmasked
author: Andrew Lloyd Webber
description: A memoir of the charmed life and times of the hit Broadway composer of Jesus Christ Superstar , Evita , and Cats through the mid-1980s production of The Phantom of the Opera .

title: Happiness
author: Aminatta Forna
description: From the author of The Hired Man , a novel bringing an American scientist and a Ghanaian psychologist together in London in a hunt for a missing boy--and an expansive tale of loss, hope, love, compassion, culture, and the true meaning of happiness.

title: Raw: My Journey into the Wu-Tang
author: Lamont
description: A founding member of the legendary Wu-Tang Clan narrates his journey from childhood poverty to celebrity in one of hip-hop's most influential acts.

title: The Sandman
author: Lars Kepler, Trans. by Neil Smith
description: Detectives go undercover in a psychiatric ward to trick Sweden's most notorious serial killer into revealing the whereabouts of his accomplice, the Sandman, and the woman he helped kidnap as a girl more than a decade earlier.

title: Bachelor Nation
author: Amy Kaufman
description: From Los Angeles Times entertainment journalist Kaufman, Bachelor Nation draws on interviews with producers and fans to present a behind-the-scenes look at the reality television phenomenon and explores the show's cultural influence and significance.

title: Barbed Wire Heart
author: Tess Sharpe
description: The daughter of a Northern California meth kingpin must decide whether to continue the family business after her father's death or begin a new life apart from the violent world in which she grew up.

title: A Tokyo Romance
author: Ian Buruma
description: A young man escapes a life of privilege in the 1970's by traveling to Japan, where he immerses himself in the country's erotic avant-garde theater and art worlds.

title: The Adulterants
author: Joe Dunthorne
description: A not-very-successful thirtysomething freelance writer in London stumbles into a comedic downward spiral as he struggles to behave like an adult in response to his impending fatherhood.

title: Ask Me about My Uterus: A Quest to Make Doctors Believe in Women's Pain
author: Abby Norman
description: Abby Norman connects her own diagnosis of endometriosis, ignored for years by doctors as a psychological problem, with a much longer history of women's pain being overlooked or misinterpreted as mental illness.

title: Brazen: Rebel Ladies Who Rocked the World
author: Pénélope Bagieu
description: A graphic textbook that profiles 30 women, whose diverse lives and work changed the world.

title: Awayland
author: Ramona Ausubel
description: In this short-story collection, humans, Cyclops, and other characters encounter familiar problems in fantastic landscapes.

title: Tomb Song
author: Julián Herbert, Trans. by Christina MacSweeney
description: A work of autobiographical fiction by Mexican poet Herbert. As he sits by his dying mother, a son immerses himself in his memories of his childhood and youth while he investigates the complex relationship with his former prostitute mother, his own children and his country.

title: Agatha Christie: A Mysterious life
author: Laura Thompson
description: A biography of the great mystery writer, drawn from Christie's letters, papers, and notebooks, as well as interviews with her grandson, daughter, son-in-law and their living relations.

title: The Woman's Hour: The Great Fight to Win the Vote
author: Elaine Weiss
description: Following a handful of remarkable women who led their respective forces into battle, along with appearances by Woodrow Wilson, Warren Harding, Frederick Douglass, and Eleanor Roosevelt, The Woman's Hour is an inspiring story of activists winning their own freedom in one of the last campaigns forged in the shadow of the Civil War, and the beginning of the great twentieth-century battles for civil rights.

title: The Last Wild Men of Borneo: A True Story of Death and Treasure
author: Carl Hoffman
description: Two modern adventurers sought a treasure possessed by the legendary 'Wild Men of Borneo.' One found riches. The other vanished forever into an endless jungle. Had he shed civilization--or lost his mind? Global headlines suspected murder. Lured by these mysteries, New York Times bestselling author Carl Hoffman journeyed to find the truth, discovering that nothing is as it seems in the worlds last Eden, where the lines between sinner and saint blur into one.

title: Can It Happen Here?: Authoritarianism in America
author: Cass R. Sunstein
description: In this thought-provoking collection of essays, these distinguished thinkers and theorists explore the lessons of history, how democracies crumble, how propaganda works, and the role of the media, courts, elections, and 'fake news' in the modern political landscape--and what the future of the United States may hold.

title: Girls Burn Brighter: A Novel
author: Shobha Rao
description: Poornima and Savitha have three strikes against them: they are poor, they are ambitious, and they are girls. After her mother's death, Poornima has very little kindness in her life. She is left to care for her siblings until her father can find her a suitable match. So when Savitha enters their household, Poornima is intrigued by the joyful, independent-minded girl. Suddenly their Indian village doesn't feel quite so claustrophobic, and Poornima begins to imagine a life beyond arranged marriage. But when a devastating act of cruelty drives Savitha away, Poornima leaves behind everything she has ever known to find her friend.

title: The Infernal Library: On Dictators, the Books They Wrote, and Other Catastrophes of Literacy
author: Daniel Kalder
description: Since the days of the Roman Empire dictators have written books. But in the twentieth-century despots enjoyed unprecedented print runs to (literally) captive audiences. How did the production of literature become central to the running of regimes? What do these books reveal about the dictatorial soul?

title: The Last Equation of Isaac Severy: A Novel in Clues
author: Nova Jacobs
description: A woman, part of the quirky and brilliant Severy clan, must deliver her deceased grandfather's secret equation safely to a trusted colleague before it ends up in the wrong hands.

title: Gun Love
author: Jennifer Clement
description: A novel about a twelve-year-old raised in a car in Central Florida by a single mother who gets involved with a gunrunner, with tragic consequences.

title: Berlin Alexanderplatz
author: Alfred Döblin, Trans. by Michael Hofmann
description: A murderer ex-convict returns to the sordid streets of Berlin's Alexanderplatz and his nihilistic life of crime in Michael Hofmann's new translation of this modernist, Weimar-era classic.

title: Trick
author: Domenico Starnone, Trans. by Jhumpa Lahiri
description: From the celebrated Italian novelist. An older man, an illustrator, reluctantly comes from Milan, where he is currently living, to Naples, where he grew up, to look after his grandson while his daughter and son-in-law attend an academic conference. Once there, he must confront the ghosts of his past.

title: Wrestling with the Devil: A Prison Memoir
author: Ngugi Wa Thiong'o
description: From the renowned Kenyan novelist, essayist, and academic, a prison memoir from his time incarcerated under the totalitarian regime of Jomo Kenyatta in 1978.

title: Astral Weeks: A Secret History of 1968
author: Ryan H. Walsh
description: The making and production of Van Morrison's Astral Weeks becomes a flashpoint around which this book investigates the peculiar counterculture of Boston, where Morrison lived and recorded the acclaimed album.

title: Tomorrow Will Be Different: Love, Loss, and the Fight for Trans Equality
author: Sarah McBride
description: A memoir from the activist who became the first transgender person to speak at a national political convention in 2016 at the age of twenty-six.

title: The Escape Artist
author: Brad Meltzer
description: Nola Brown's body was found on a plane that mysteriously fell from the sky as it left a secret military base in the Alaskan wilderness. Her commanding officer and the US government verify that she is dead. But Jim "Zig" Zigarowski has just found out the truth: Nola is still alive. And on the run.

title: The Return of Marco Polo's World: War, Strategy, and American Interests in the Twenty-First Century
author: Robert D. Kaplan
description: Nearly two decades of American foreign policy and its makers receive analysis in this collection of essays by a journalist cum advisor to the Pentagon.

title: The Cloister
author: James Carroll
description: National Book Award-winner James Carroll draws parallels between the 12th and 20th centuries, exploring the deadly consequences of medieval Catholic Church doctrine that might have been thwarted by renegade monk Peter Abelard, whose now-famous relationship with the nun Heloise echoes that of the novel's protagonists, a priest and Holocaust survivor who meet in 1950s Manhattan.

title: Doing Harm: The Truth about How Bad Medicine and Lazy Science Leave Women Dismissed, Misdiagnosed, and Sick
author: Maya Dusenbery
description: The editorial director of Feministing.com offers a widely researched account of bias in the medical world against women, who are often given inadequate, inappropriate, and even dangerous treatment.

title: Memphis Rent Party: The Blues, Rock & Soul in Music's Hometown
author: Robert Gordon
description: In this collection of reviews, profiles, and features, longtime Memphis music writer Robert Gordon unravels the iconoclastic personalities and communal spirit of Memphis's music scene.

title: Camp Austen: My Life as an Accidental Jane Austen Superfan
author: Ted Scheinman
description: Although Ted Scheinman wanted to leave clotted cream and Yorkshire pudding in his past, he found himself in grad school organizing the first ever UNC-Chapel Hill Jane Austen Summer Camp, a weekend-long event that sits somewhere between an academic conference and superfan extravaganza.

title: Broad Band: The Untold Story of the Women Who Made the Internet
author: Claire L. Evans
description: Women are not ancillary to the history of technology; they turn up at the very beginning of every important wave. But they've often been hidden in plain sight, their inventions and contributions touching our lives in ways we don't even realize-- until now.

title: Dancing Bears: True Stories of People Nostalgic for Life Under Tyranny
author: Witold Szablowski, Antonia Lloyd-Jones
description: This translation of Witold Szablowski Taancznace niedazwiedzie tells the stories of getting bears to dance and the unexpected unhappiness that hit Eastern Europeans when given freedom.

title: The Hunger
author: Alma Katsu
description: A tense and gripping reimagining of one of America's most fascinating historical moments: the Donner Party with a supernatural twist.

title: Bring Out the Dog: Stories
author: Will Mackin
description: The eleven stories in Will Mackin’s debut collection draw from his many deployments with a special operations task force in Iraq and Afghanistan. Together, the stories in Bring Out the Dog offer a portrait of the absurdity and poetry that define life in the most elite, clandestine circles of modern warfare. It is a world of intense bonds, ancient credos, and surprising compassion—of success, failure, and their elusive definitions.

title: If I Die Tonight
author: Alison Gaylin
description: A tale of psychological suspense from the author of the Edgar Award-nominated What Remains of Me , in which a seemingly open-and-shut police case with a clear-cut hero and villain turns out to be anything but simple.

title: The People vs. Democracy: Why Our Freedom Is in Danger and How to Save It
author: Yascha Mounk
description: From India to Turkey, from Poland to the United States, authoritarian populists have seized power. Two core components of liberal democracy--individual rights and the popular will--are at war, putting democracy itself at risk. In plain language, Yascha Mounk describes how we got here, where we need to go, and why there is little time left to waste.

title: Orbán: Hungary's Strongman
author: Paul Lendvai
description: A Hungarian-Austrian journalist charts the rise of Hungary's Prime Minister Victor Orbán from his days as a progressive, anti-communist upstart to his current rightwing, anti-immigrant Nationalism and ties to Russia's Vladimir Putin.

title: The Affliction
author: C. Dale Young
description: A novel told in short stories, The Affliction is a fiction debut by an award-winning poet full of characters across America and the Caribbean.

title: House of McQueen
author: Valerie Wallace
description: A collection of poetry inhabiting the life and work of Alexander McQueen.

title: Mine: Essays
author: Sarah Viren
description: Winner of the River Teeth Literary Nonfiction Prize. Mining her own life and those of others, Sarah Viren considers the contingencies of ownership alongside the realities of loss in this debut essay collection.

title: Harbor of Spies: A Novel of Historic Havana
author: Robin Lloyd
description: A portrait of Spanish colonial Havana at a time when the city was flush with sugar wealth and filled with signs of the American Civil War. It is a realistic look at Cuba’s role in the war, and the importance of the scores of blockade running ships- both sail and steam- that ran the gauntlet of the Union blockade from Havana into the Gulf of Mexico.

title: Chicago
author: David Mamet
description: A gangster thriller set in mobbed-up 1920s Chicago—a city where some people knew too much, and where everyone should have known better—by the Oscar-nominated screenwriter of The Untouchables and Pulitzer Prize–winning playwright of Glengarry Glen Ross .

title: Time Pieces: A Dublin Memoir
author: John Banville
description: From the Man Booker Prize-winning author of The Sea and the Benjamin Black mysteries, a memoir, complemented by photographs, that unfolds around the author's recollections, experience, and imaginings of Dublin.

title: Eat the Apple
author: Matt Young
description: A memoir of the Iraq war and its consequences on the psyche of a young man.

title: A Long Way From Home
author: Peter Carey
description: From two-time Booker Prize winner Peter Carey, a novel that circumnavigates 1954 Australia, revealing as much about the country/continent as it does about three audacious individuals who take part in the infamous 10,000-mile race, the Redex Trial.

title: Green Sun
author: Kent Anderson
description: The long-awaited final chapter in Anderson's trilogy about Vietnam veteran Hanson. After several years teaching English literature in Idaho, Hanson has returned to police work as a beat cop in the economically devastated neighborhoods of East Oakland in 1983.

title: Behemoth: A History of the Factory and the Making of the Modern World
author: Joshua B. Freeman
description: This history traces the rise and transformation of the factory from its birth in 18th century England across Europe, the United States, Stalinist Russia, and contemporary China.

title: The Cadaver King and the Country Dentist
author: Radley Balko & Tucker Carrington
description: After two three-year-old girls were raped and murdered in rural Mississippi, law enforcement pursued and convicted two innocent men: Kennedy Brewer and Levon Brooks. Together they spent a combined thirty years in prison before finally being exonerated in 2008. Meanwhile, the real killer remained free. The Cadaver King and the Country Dentist recounts the story of how the criminal justice system allowed this to happen, and of how two men built successful careers on the back of that structure.

title: I'll Be Gone in the Dark: One Woman's Obsessive Search for the Golden State Killer
author: Michelle McNamara
description: McNamara’s posthumously published book tells the nightmarish story of the Golden State Killer, the neighborhoods he terrorized, and her own tale of true-crime addiction.

title: Stealing the Show: How Women Are Revolutionizing Television
author: Joy Press
description: TV writer Joy Press chronicles the rise of women in television from Murphy Brown through Transparent , detailing the challenges and triumphs of representing the female experience in a male-dominated industry.

title: We the Corporations: How American Businesses Won Their Civil Rights
author: Adam Winkler
description: In this legal history, Winkler shows corporations as integral to the foundation of the United States and traces their steady accumulation of "civil rights" over the last 200 years, with the Citizens United Supreme Court decision just one in a long series of corporate legal victories.

title: The Neighborhood
author: Mario Vargas Llosa, Trans. by Edith Grossman
description: In this pulpy detective story, a cast of characters from tabloid journalism to the upper echelons of Lima society navigate the corrupt and violent years of Alberto Fujimori's 1990s presidency.

title: Basketball: Great Writing About America's Game
author: Alexander Wolff
description: From the street game to March Madness to Jordan and LeBron, the greatest writing about the grit, grace, and glory of basketball.

title: Don't Call Me Princess: Essays on Girls, Women, Sex and Life
author: Peggy Orenstein
description: Don’t Call Me Princess offers a crucial evaluation of where we stand today as women—in our work lives, sex lives, as mothers, as partners—illuminating both how far we’ve come and how far we still have to go.

title: Fatal Discord: Erasmus, Luther, and the Fight for the Western Mind
author: Michael Massing
description: In this dual biography of Erasmus and Luther, a journalist narrates the rivalry between these two revolutionary thinkers of the Renaissance and Reformation and how it inspired and enriched each others' ideas.

title: My Father's Wake: How the Irish Teach Us to Live, Love, and Die
author: Kevin Toolis
description: Drawing on his experiences reporting abroad as well as the deaths of his own father and brother, journalist Kevin Toolis critiques the sanitized nature of death and mourning in the Western world.

title: The Tangled Lands
author: Paolo Bacigalupi and Tobias S. Bucknell
description: In this collaborative novel told in four parts, the people of a fallen empire struggle to survive and stop the growth of a toxic bramble that envelops the land, fed by the use of magic that has been outlawed but continues to be practiced in secret by many.

title: A Good Day for Seppuku: Stories
author: Kate Braverman
description: Women of varying degrees of economic privilege navigate fraught relationships with friends, lovers, parents, and their own minds in this collection of evocative stories.

title: Summer Hours at the Robbers Library
author: Sue Halpern
description: The Robbers Library becomes a home-away-from-home for a cast of misfit characters looking to make sense of their lives, including teenaged Sunny, who's doing community service, librarian Kit, and Rusty, a down-on-his luck Wall Street banker.

title: The Sea Beast Takes a Lover
author: Michael Andreasen
description: A headless little sister, a "Rocketboy," and an amorous sea creature who mistakes a ship for a potential mate are just some of the strange characters that populate these stories that explore family, love, loss, and adventure.

title: The Hush
author: John Hart
description: In this sequel to The Last Child , protagonist Johnny Merrimon and his lawyer friend Jack work together to defend Hush Arbor - the land Johnny inherited that is haunted by the ghosts of slaves - from those who think they have a claim to it.

title: Chefs, Drugs and Rock & Roll: How Food Lovers, Free Spirits, Misfits and Wanderers Created a New American Profession
author: Andrew Friedman
description: An all-access history of the evolution of the American restaurant chef.

title: A Princess in Theory: Reluctant Royals
author: Alyssa Cole
description: Between grad school and multiple jobs, Naledi Smith doesn’t have time for fairy tales…or patience for the constant e-mails claiming she’s betrothed to an African prince.

title: The Liar's Girl
author: Catherine Ryan Howard
description: Will Hurley was an attractive, charming, and impressive student at Dublin's elite St. John's College--and Ireland's most prolific serial killer. Freshman Alison Smith moved to the Big Smoke to enroll in St. John's and soon fell hard for Will Hurley. Her world bloomed—and then imploded when Liz, her best friend, became the latest victim of the Canal Killer—and the Canal Killer turned out to be the boy who'd been sleeping in her bed.

title: The House of Erzulie
author: Kirsten Imani Kasai
description: This novel tells the eerily intertwined stories of an ill-fated young couple in the 1850s and the troubled historian who discovers their writings in the present day.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: A memoir about a young girl who, kept out of school, leaves her Mormon anti-government survivalist family and goes on to earn a PhD from Cambridge University.

title: Sunburn
author: Laura Lippman
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: A steamy psychological suspense novel set in Baltimore in the summer of 1995 that pays homage to The Postman Always Rings Twice .

title: What Are We Doing Here?: Essays
author: Marilynne Robinson
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of the Gilead trilogy, new essays on theological, political, and contemporary themes.

title: Political Tribes: Group Instinct and the Fate of Nations
author: Amy Chua
description: Yale Law School professor Amy Chua offers a new prescription for reversing our foreign policy failures and overcoming our destructive political tribalism at home.

title: Down the River Unto the Sea
author: Walter Mosley
description: From the author of the Easy Rawlins series, a former NYPD cop once imprisoned for a crime he did not commit must solve two cases: that of a man wrongly condemned to die, and his own.

title: Without Precedent: Chief Justice John Marshall and His Times
author: Joel Richard Paul
description: The story of John Marshall who, as chief justice, statesman, and diplomat, played a pivotal role in the founding of the United States.

title: Monster Portraits
author: Del Samatar and Sofia Samatar
description: Part memoir of Somali-American siblings who grew up in the 1980s, part imaginative "bestiary," this unique hybrid of art and text meditates upon "Otherness" as a form of monstrousness.

title: Ambiguity Machines
author: Vandana Singh
description: Scientists and other characters in this book of stories travel through time, deal with the aftermath of climate change, and otherwise navigate the complexities of living in worlds distant, but not so different, from our own.

title: Straying
author: Molly McCloskey
description: Mourning the death of her mother, a woman looks back on her failed marriage and the role she played in destroying it.

title: Secrets We Kept: Three Women of Trinidad
author: Krystal A Sital
description: A memoir which digs into the sufferings of three generations of women living within brutal patriarchal confines in Trinidad.

title: All the Names They Used for God
author: Anjali Sachdeva
description: Hailing from different centuries and continents, these stories' characters confront life-threatening or life-changing situations, armed with their unique and sometimes superhuman gifts.

title: Blue Dreams: The Science and the Story of the Drugs That Changed Our Minds
author: Lauren Slater
description: A psychologist offers a history of drugs to treat mental illness, connecting it with her own experience taking Prozac and other medications that have saved her mind but ravaged her body.

title: Victorious Century: The United Kingdom, 1800-1906
author: David Cannadine
description: Princeton historian David Cannadine lays out an expansive history of the United Kingdom in the 19th century, with special attention to the high politics that shaped the Empire.

title: The Watergate: Inside America’s Most Infamous Address
author: Joseph Rodota
description: A biography of Washington's most famous apartment complex--the buildings with a thousand stories of the notables who have lived there.

title: The Food Explorer: The True Adventures of the Globe-Trotting Botanist Who Transformed What America Eats
author: Daniel Stone
description: Foods thought commonplace in the United States, such as the zucchini and lemon, owe their bounty to the early 20th century global travels of botanist David Fairchild, whose efforts are chronicled in this history.

title: Superfans: Into the Heart of Obsessive Sports Fandom
author: George Dohrmann
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning sports journalist investigates the psychologies of extreme sports fans, whose favorite teams provide deep sources of identity and community, the consequences of which run the gamut from life-enriching to pathological.

title: A Dangerous Woman: American Beauty, Noted Philanthropist, Nazi Collaborator--The Life of Florence Gould
author: Susan Ronald
description: In this biography, the arts patron Florence Gould is revealed to be not only a ruthless socialite but a Nazi collaborator who profiteered during World War II by collecting looted and other suspiciously acquired artworks.

title: It's Better Than It Looks: Reasons for Optimism in an Age of Fear
author: Gregg Easterbrook
description: In this antidote to apocalyptic thinking, Gregg Easterbrook charts heartening statistics for humanity across the globe - historically lower crime rates, longer life, greater prosperity - and offers encouragement for combating remaining challenges, such as climate change.

title: The Future of Humanity: Terraforming Mars, Interstellar Travel, Immortality, and Our Destiny Beyond Earth
author: Michio Kaku
description: The author of The Future of the Mind traverses the frontiers of astrophysics, artificial intelligence, and technology to offer a vision of man's future in space, from settling Mars to traveling to distant galaxies.

title: Where the Dead Sit Talking
author: Brandon Hobson
description: Set in rural Oklahoma during the late 1980s, Where the Dead Sit Talking is a Native American coming-of-age story. With his single mother in jail, Sequoyah, a fifteen-year-old Cherokee boy, keeps mostly to himself, living with his emotions pressed deep below the surface. At least until he meets seventeen-year-old Rosemary, and they bond over their shared Native American background.

title: Virgin: Poems
author: Analicia Sotelo
description: Winner of the Jake Adam York Prize, Sotelo walks the line between autobiography and myth-making. These poems explore femininity, history, love, and what it means to be an artist.

title: Sirens
author: Joseph Knox
description: A thriller about a damaged undercover detective navigating a web of politicians, drug lords, missing persons, and his own flawed department.

title: Eloquent Rage: A Black Feminist Discovers Her Superpower
author: Brittney Cooper
description: A monthly columnist on race and gender for Cosmopolitan and a professor of gender and Africana studies at Rutgers University writes here in the Black feminist tradition of Audre Lorde to remind Black women that anger is a powerful source of energy that can provide the strength to keep on fighting.

title: The Château
author: Paul Goldberg
description: A dark, madcap satire from the author of The Did . Adrift and broke after losing his job at the Washington Post , William Katzenelenbogen descends into Trump-ian madness while visiting his estranged father in South Florida.

title: Farewell to the Horse: A Cultural History
author: Ulrich Raulff, Trans. by Ruth Ahmedzai Kemp
description: A cultural history of the horse and humankind’s relation to it.

title: Mrs.
author: Caitlin Macy
description: A modern society novel about the gossipy lives of well-off parents in New York City’s Upper East Side. When Philippa Lye’s shadowy past comes to light, an insulated society is forced to confront the rot at its core.

title: Young China: How the Restless Generation Will Change Their Country and the World
author: Zak Dychtwald
description: From single-child pressure, to test taking madness and the frenzy to buy an apartment as a prerequisite to marriage, from one-night-stands to an evolving understanding of family, Young China offers a portrait of the generation who will define what it means to be Chinese in the modern era.

title: Freshwater
author: Akwaeke Emezi
description: A haunting debut novel set in contemporary Nigeria and the US, about a girl of Igbo ethnicity whose nature is both human and divine. She was born with multiple selves, each under the domain of a different ogbanje , dark spirits of the Igbo belief system.

title: White Houses
author: Amy Bloom
description: A love story inspired by the relationship between Eleanor Roosevelt and “first friend,” Associated Press reporter Lorena Hickok.

title: Winter Kept Us Warm
author: Anne Raeff
description: Ulli is a young woman squatting in a dismal, empty Berlin apartment, one year after the WWII has ended, when she meets two American soldiers. The novel follows the trio through the next six decades of their lives?from Berlin to postwar Manhattan, 1960s Los Angeles, and contemporary Morocco.

title: The Kremlin's Candidate
author: Jason Matthews
description: A counterintelligence chief and her lover, who is a C.I.A. agent, learn of Vladimir Putin’s plan to assassinate a United States official.

title: Enlightenment Now
author: Steven Pinker
description: A case for using reason, science and humanism to counter pessimistic views of Western civilization from Harvard psychology professor Steven Pinker.

title: All the Pieces Matter: The Inside Story of The Wire
author: Jonathan Abrams
description: An oral history of the creation and development of the series "The Wire."

title: The Marshall Plan: The Dawn of the Cold War
author: Benn Steil
description: The award-winning author of The Battle of Bretton Woods reveals the history behind the Marshall Plan.

title: The World Only Spins Forward: The Ascent of Angels in America
author: Isaac Butler & Dan Kois
description: In this oral history, Butler and Kois narrate the development, production, critical reception, and cultural iconography of Tony Kushner's Angels in America , the classic play about the 1980s AIDS crisis and its devastating effects on those who lived through it.

title: Madness is Better Than Defeat
author: Ned Beauman
description: In this comic thriller that begins in 1938 and extends through the mid- 20th century, a corrupt CIA agent uncovers mystery and intrigue at a Honduras temple over which two rival groups have been fighting: filmmakers who want to use it as a backdrop for a screwball comedy and explorers who want to move the temple to New York.

title: Vengeance
author: Zachary Lazar
description: From John Updike Award-winner Zachary Lazar, an autobiographical novel that blurs the lines between fiction and true crime, about a journalist who befriends an inmate at Louisiana's Angola prison. As he attempts to unravel the truth behind the man's supposed crime, he is also confronted with his own past, and re-examines American notions of guilt and penance, racial bias, and the inherent perversity of punitive justice.

title: The Triumph of Christianity: How a Forbidden Religon Swept the World
author: Bob D. Ehrman
description: A historical analysis of how Christianity grew from a tiny group of believers in the Roman world to a mass movement that swept the globe.

title: Built: The Hidden Stories Behind Our Structures
author: Roma Agrawal
description: Drawing on her own biography as much as her technical expertise, a London-based structural engineer explains how buildings, bridges, and other structures have come to be built and meditates upon their impact on our lives.

title: Leftover in China
author: Roseann Lake
description: This book looks into the lives of China's sheng nü, or “leftover women,” the well-educated, high-achieving female professionals who are the backbone of China's economy but the source of public shame due to their unmarried condition.

title: The Lost Girls of Camp Forevermore
author: Kim Fu
description: After a group of girls gets stranded on a remote island, the experience haunts them into adulthood in unexpected ways.

title: Pride and Prometheus
author: John Kessel
description: Mary Bennet from Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice meets Victor from Mary Shelley's Frankenstein just in time to help the scientist deal with his creature's request for a mate.

title: The Queen of Hearts
author: Kimmery Martin
description: The bond between two best friends, a pediatric cardiologist and a trauma surgeon, threatens to break when a former colleague returns to unearth a long-buried secret.

title: Some Hell
author: Patrick Nathan
description: In the aftermath of his father's suicide, a teenage boy struggles to navigate life with his siblings and mother while awakening to his own homosexuality.

title: Fisherman's Blues: A West African Community at Sea
author: Anna Badkhen
description: A journalist who reports from the Global South, Badkhen embeds herself with a West African fishing community struggling to make a living as they must compete with Western fishing corporations.

title: Song of a Captive Bird
author: Jasmin Darznik
description: A biographical novel about the trailblazing Iranian poet Forugh Farrokhzad, exploring her sexual and creative liberation as well as the threat she posed to social order in prerevolutionary Iran.

title: Hotel Silence
author: Audur Ava Ólafsdóttir, Trans. by Brian FitzGibbon
description: Contemplating suicide after his wife leaves him, a middle-aged man takes a trip and becomes engaged with the people he finds at the end of his journey.

title: Don't Skip Out on Me: A Novel
author: Willy Vlautin
description: Determined to prove his worth, a half-Paiute, half-Irish ranch hand who was abandoned by his parents, tries to become a champion boxer in Mexico and Las Vegas only to realize that he cannot change his identity or outrun his destiny.

title: The Radicals: A Novel
author: Ryan McILvain
description: "When Eli first meets Sam Westergard, he is dazzled by his new friend's charisma. The two young men bond over their commitment to socialism, both in theory and in practice... As part of the same socialist group, Eli realizes that some of his fellow intellectuals are more deeply--and dangerously--devoted to the cause than others.

title: The Driest Season: A Novel
author: Meghan Kenny
description: A raw, compelling family saga set in Wisconsin farm country during World War II.

title: High-Risers: Cabrini-Green and the Fate of American Public Housing
author: Ben Austen
description: In this years-long reporting project on Chicago's Cabrini-Green, journalist Ben Austen narrates the political and cultural currents that led to the rise and fall of one of the nation's most notorious housing projects as well as the complicated lives of several long-time residents, who lost beloved homes and communities when the complex was finally demolished in 2011.

title: The Ghost Notebooks
author: Ben Dolnick
description: When a couple leaves New York City to run an old museum in the Hudson Valley, they must contend with spiritual and psychological forces beyond their control.

title: All the Castles Burned
author: Michael Nye
description: A coming of age novel about Owen, a young man from a troubled, working-class family, who receives a scholarship to a prestigious private academy where he falls under the influence of Carson, an enigmatic upperclassman. When Owen's father is arrested for a shocking and unexpected crime, his family is torn apart, and Owen's anger and fear are carefully manipulated by Carson's mercurial and increasingly dangerous personality.

title: Love
author: Hanne Ørstavik, Trans. by Martin Aitken
description: First published in Norway in 1997 and now translated into English for the first time, this novella explores the complicated bond between a mother and her son who, on the eve of his ninth birthday, goes out selling lottery tickets for his sports club while she has her own adventures elsewhere.

title: Wallis in Love: The Untold Life of the Duchess of Windsor, the Woman Who Changed the Monarchy
author: Andrew Morton
description: In Wallis In Love , acclaimed biographer Andrew Morton offers a fresh portrait of Wallis Simpson in all her vibrancy and brazenness as she transformed from a hard-nosed gold-digger to charming chatelaine.

title: Cringeworthy: A Theory of Awkwardness
author: Melissa Dahl
description: Melissa Dahl invites you to follow her into all sorts of mortifying moments, drawing on personal experience and in-depth psychological research to answer life's questions on why certain situations are awkward.

title: All for Nothing
author: Walter Kempowski, Trans. by Anthea Bell
description: A wealthy family tries--and fails--to seal themselves off from the chaos of post-World War II life surrounding them.

title: Left Bank: Art, Passion, and the Rebirth of Paris, 1940-50
author: Agnes Poirier
description: A group portrait of the mid-20th century artists and thinkers whose lives, loves, collaborations, and passions were forged against the destruction of World War II and the post-war rebirth of Paris.

title: Sadness Is a White Bird
author: Moriel Rothman-Zecher
description: A young man is preparing to serve in the Israeli army while also trying to reconcile his close relationship to two Palestinian siblings with his deeply ingrained loyalties to family and country.

title: Call Me Zebra
author: Azareen Van der Vliet Oloomi
description: From the author Azeen Van der Vliet Oloomi, we are brought into the world of our main character Zabra, who is currently taking refuge in books during a war. Can literature, bickering companionship, and a trek to the other side of the world free Zebra from her past?

title: The Rub of Time
author: Martin Amis
description: A collection of Martin Amis' acerbic essays, reportage and criticism on literature, politics, sport, and general miscellany, written between 1986 and 2016.

title: Feel Free
author: Zadie Smith
description: Winner of the 2019 National Book Critics Circle Award for Criticism, a new collection of essays from Zadie Smith focusing on literature, art, film, politics, and cultural criticism.

title: The Friend
author: Sigrid Nunez
description: Winner of the 2018 National Book Award for Fiction, The Friend tells the story of an unnamed middle-aged writing professor in the aftermath of her best friend and mentor's suicide. She is bequeathed his well-behaved beast of a dog and begins to interrogate her grief.

title: Asymmetry
author: Lisa Halliday
description: Told in three distinct and uniquely compelling sections, Asymmetry explores the imbalances that spark and sustain many of our most dramatic human relations: inequities in age, power, talent, wealth, fame, geography, and justice.

title: An American Marriage
author: Tayari Jones
description: Winner of the 2019 Women's Prize for Fiction, An American Marriage is a novel about Celestial and Roy, a young, upwardly mobile black couple in Atlanta, whose marriage is torn apart when Roy is incarcerated for a crime he didn't commit.

title: Heart Berries
author: Terese Marie Mailhot
description: Terese Marie Mailhot’s memoir of coming of age on the Seabird Island Indian Reservation in the Pacific Northwest after a profoundly dysfunctional upbringing.

title: The Line Becomes a River: Dispatches from the Border
author: Francisco Cantú
description: An ex–Border Patrol agent finds himself on both sides of the battle over illegal immigration in this memoir of his time patrolling the Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas borders from 2008 to 2012.

title: I Am, I Am, I Am: Seventeen Brushes with Death
author: Maggie O'Farrell
description: Novelist Maggie O'Farrell's memoir-in-essays of the near-death experiences that have punctuated and defined her life.

title: Brave
author: Rose McGowan
description: A memoir and scathing indictment of sexism and sexual abuse in Hollywood, from actress and activist Rose McGowan.

title: Directorate S: The C.I.A. and America's Secret Wars in Afghanistan and Pakistan
author: Steve Coll
description: Winner of the 2019 National Book Critics Circle Award for Nonfiction, a sequel to the Pulitzer Prize Ghost Wars , the story of America's intelligence, military, and diplomatic efforts to defeat Al Qaeda and the Taliban in Afghanistan and Pakistan since 9/11.

title: Self-Portrait with Boy
author: Rachel Lyon
description: A novel set in 1990s New York about an ambitious young female artist who accidentally photographs a boy falling to his death—an image that could jumpstart her career, but would also devastate her most intimate friendship.

title: The Kings of Big Spring: God, Oil, and One Family's Search for the American Dream
author: Bryan Mealer
description: Bryan Mealer’s memoir and narrative history tells the story of four generations of his family, and in so doing, tells a story of how America came to be.

title: The Great Alone
author: Kristin Hannah
description: In this portrait of human frailty and resilience, Kristin Hannah reveals the indomitable character of the modern American pioneer and the spirit of a vanishing Alaska.

title: How to Stop Time
author: Matt Haig
description: From the author of Reasons to Stay Alive , a love story about a seemingly ordinary 41-year-old London teacher who happens to have a rare condition that causes him to age fifteen times slower than a normal person, and his struggle to live an ordinary life despite having been alive for over 400 years.

title: A False Report: A True Story of Rape in America
author: T. Christian Miller and Ken Armstrong
description: Based on the Pulitzer Prize-winning 2016 article, a true crime book about a Seattle teenager who was charged with lying about having been raped, and the detectives who followed a winding path to arrive at the truth.

title: Only Child
author: Rhiannon Navin
description: A novel about the aftermath of a school shooting, told from the point of view of a first-grader who hid with his class in a closet while his brother and 18 others were massacred.

title: Look for Me
author: Lisa Gardner
description: Sergeant Detective D.D. Warren teams up with a torture survivor to find a missing teenager whose family members were gunned down.

title: Starlings
author: Jo Walton
description: Award-winning sci-fi novelist and essayist Walton shares her poetry, a play, and assorted short fiction, accompanied by lengthy insights about writing each work.

title: The Seabird's Cry
author: Adam Nicolson
description: From NYT best-selling author Adam Nicolson, a poetic meditation on the mysterious, endangered lives of seabirds and their hold on the human mind.

title: Daphne
author: Will Boast
description: In his debut novel, Rome Prize winner Boast reimagines the myth of Daphne and Apollo as a contemporary romance in which fear of intimacy is further complicated by the digital age's constant stream of numbing stimulation.

title: The Heart is a Shifting Sea
author: Elizabeth Flock
description: This examination of love, marriage, and the state of modern India traces the experiences of three different Mumbai couples whose realities are shaped by disparate views regarding independence, parenthood, gender roles, and religion.

title: Force of Nature
author: Jane Harper
description: An Australia-set thriller and follow-up to Harper's bestselling The Dry . When five colleagues are forced to go on a corporate retreat in the wilderness, they reluctantly pick up their backpacks and start walking down the muddy path. But one of the women doesn’t come out of the woods. And each of her companions tells a slightly different story about what happened.

title: How to Fix the Future
author: Andrew Keen
description: Andrew Keen, a leading critic of the dangers that the Internet poses to our culture and society, writes about the ways in which we can preserve our humanity in a digital world.

title: Going for a Beer
author: Robert Coover
description: This story collection charts the short fiction experiments of one of the postwar generation's most celebrated postmodern writers.

title: Back Talk
author: Danielle Lazarin
description: This debut short fiction collection investigates women's inner lives, their desires, needs and secrets.

title: Empty Set
author: Veronica Gerber Bicecci, Trans. by Christina MacSweeney
description: The woman at the heart of this novel sees love as a cosmic experience, and she seeks to understand her own relationship through geometry, ice cores, and tree rings.

title: Only Killers and Thieves
author: Paul Howarth
description: Two brothers vie for power in the Australian frontier of the 1880s, where racism and cruelty poisons the soil.

title: Semiosis
author: Sue Burke
description: Humans who have colonized another planet learn over generations to live among its sentient creatures that appear very different from themselves.

title: Beautiful Days: Stories
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: A new collection of stories by American master Joyce Carol Oates, mysterious and surreal, and perfectly pitched for the confusion of the current political landscape.

title: The House of Impossible Beauties: A Novel
author: Joseph Cassara
description: A gritty and gorgeous debut that follows a cast of gay and transgender club kids navigating the Harlem ball scene of the 1980s and ’90s, inspired by the real House of Xtravaganza made famous by the seminal documentary Paris Is Burning .

title: Text Me When You Get Home: The Evolution and Triumph of Female Friendship
author: Kayleen Schaefer
description: A journalist investigates female friendship and discovers just how supportive and life-affirming they can be to a generation of women who are marrying later in life or not at all.

title: The Atomic City Girls: A Novel
author: Janet Beard
description: When the bombing of Hiroshima brings the truth about Oak Ridge into devastating focus, June must confront her ideals about loyalty, patriotism, and war itself.

title: The Which Way Tree
author: Elizabeth Crook
description: Early one morning in the remote hill country of Texas, a panther savagely attacks a family of homesteaders, mauling a young girl named Samantha and killing her former-slave mother, whose final act is to save her daughter's life. Tenacious Samantha then sets out into the Texas frontier to avenge her mother's death.

title: Child of a Mad God: A Tale of the Coven
author: R.A. Salvatore
description: Protagonist Aoelyn comes into her magical powers on her 18th birthday and tries to use them to fight the evil haunting her people while looking beyond it for a new place to call home.

title: Look for Me
author: Lisa Gardner
description: Detective D. D. Warren and Find Her 's Flora Dane return to search for a missing 16-year-old girl after her four family members are found killed in this mystery that, in addition to murder, considers social issues such as foster care, PTSD, and gang violence.

title: Everything Happens for a Reason: And Other Lies I've Loved
author: Kate Bowler
description: A memoir of battling from a Duke University Divinity professor who at 35 was diagnosed with Stage IV cancer.

title: The Audacity of Inez Burns: Dreams, Desire, Treachery & Ruin in the City of Gold
author: Stephen G. Bloom
description: In The Audacity of Inez Burns , Stephen G. Bloom, reveals a jagged slice of lost American history. From Inez’s riveting tale of glamour and tragedy, he has created a brilliant, compulsively readable portrait of an unforgettable woman during a moment when America’s pendulum swung from compassion to criminality by punishing those who permitted women to control their own destinies.

title: House Witness
author: Mike Lawson
description: The new novel in Mike Lawson's series takes political fixer Joe DeMarco to New York for behind-the-scenes work on a high-stakes murder case, as the five witnesses, one by one, start to withdraw.

title: Victorians Undone: Tales of the Flesh in the Age of Decorum
author: Kathryn Hughes
description: Victorians Undone follows five iconic figures of the nineteenth century as they encounter the world not through their imaginations or intellects but through their bodies.

title: The New Negro: The Life of Alain Locke
author: Jeffrey C. Stewart
description: Winner of the 2019 Pulitzer Prize for Biography and the 2018 National Book Award for Nonfiction, The New Negro is a comprehensive biography of the 20th-century philosopher, curator, and prime mover of the Harlem Renaissance.

title: The Monk of Mokha
author: Dave Eggers
description: From the author of The Circle and What Is the What , the true story of a young Yemeni-American man, raised in San Francisco, who dreams of resurrecting the ancient art of Yemeni coffee but finds himself trapped in Sana'a by civil war.

title: This Will Be My Undoing
author: Morgan Jerkins
description: A collection of linked essays interweaving commentary on pop culture, feminism, black history, misogyny, and racism with Jerkins' own experiences to confront the very real challenges of being a black woman today.

title: Jefferson's Daughters: Three Sisters, White and Black, in a Young America
author: Catherine Kerrison
description: The story of Thomas Jefferson's three daughters — two white and free, one black and enslaved — and the divergent paths they forged in a newly independent America.

title: Building the Great Society: Inside Lyndon Johnson's White House
author: Joshua Zeitz
description: A behind-the-scenes study, Politico contributing editor Joshua Zeitz researches the Lyndon B. Johnson’s presidency and the White House staffers fundamental to the administration's successes and failures.

title: This Is What Happened
author: Mick Herron
description: Adrift in London, twenty-six-year-old Maggie Barnes meets M15 agent Harvey Wells and unknowingly becomes his new recruit in an international spy plot.

title: Dark in Death
author: J. D. Robb
description: The latest installment in Robb's In Death crime series, which focuses on the travails of Lieutenant Eve Dallas in a near-future New York City.

title: Still Me
author: Jojo Moyes
description: Louisa Clark moves to New York and is torn between high society and the life she enjoys at a vintage clothing store.

title: Smoketown: The Untold Story of the Other Great Black Renaissance
author: Mark Whitaker
description: The story of the other great Renaissance of black culture, influence, and glamour burst forth joyfully in what may seem an unlikely place—Pittsburgh, PA—from the 1920s through the 1950s.

title: Experience on Demand
author: Jeremy Bailenson
description: The founding director of Stanford University’s Virtual Human Interaction Lab provides a history of virtual reality technology and an in-depth look at how it can be harnessed to improve our everyday lives.

title: 1947: Where Now Begins
author: Elisabeth Asbrink, Trans. by Fiona Graham
description: Weaving a narrative of family history alongside that of major world events during 1947, Elisabeth Asbrink reveals the connectedness among seemingly unrelated occurrences and the crucial significance of the titular year to our present.

title: Rise and Kill First: The Secret History of Israel's Targeted Assassinations
author: Ronen Bergman
description: An assessment of Israel's state-sponsored assassination programs that evaluates the protective beliefs that are instituted into every Israeli citizen, the role of assassination in the state's history, and the ethical challenges of Israel's policies on targeted killings.

title: The Wizard and the Prophet: Two Remarkable Scientists and Their Dueling Visions to Shape Tomorrow's World
author: Charles C. Mann
description: From the author of 1491 and 1493 comes an incisive portrait of the two little-known twentieth-century scientists, Norman Borlaug and William Vogt, whose diametrically opposed views shaped our ideas about the environment.

title: Eternal Life
author: Dara Horn
description: A novel set in contemporary New York about a woman who been alive for several thousand years, all because of a promise she made centuries ago in Old Jerusalem to forgo physical death for all eternity to save her child.

title: Frankenstein in Baghdad
author: Ahmed Saadawi, Trans. by Jonathan Wright
description: Winner of the International Prize for Arabic Fiction A darkly humorous contemporary take on the Frankenstein story. In US-occupied Baghdad, a junk dealer's creation, assembled from the body parts of victims killed in bomb blasts, stalks the city looking for revenge.

title: Winter
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard, Trans. by Ingvild Burkey
description: The second book in his series of seasonal meditations, Karl Ove Knausgaard continues with some austere thoughts on nature and life in a cold climate after the birth of his daughter.

title: The Milk Lady of Bangalore: An Unexpected Adventure
author: Shoba Narayan
description: Shoba Narayan,the culture writer and cookbook author, leaves New York City to reconnect with her Bangalorean roots in this story about cows, Indian culture, and the strength of female friendship.

title: The Sky Is Yours
author: Chandler Klang Smith
description: A sprawling, genre-defying epic. In the burned-out, futuristic city of Empire Island, three young people navigate a crumbling metropolis constantly under threat from a pair of dragons that circle the skies.

title: Norwich: One Tiny Vermont Town's Secret to Happiness and Excellence
author: Karen Crouse
description: In her debut, New York Times sportswriter Karen Crouse explores why a small town in Vermont has become the 'perfect incubator for developing the ideal Olympic athlete.'

title: Brass
author: Xhenet Aliu
description: A novel about a young woman coming of age in a gritty industrial city of abandoned brass factories in Connecticut, and her affair with an Albanian line cook at a local diner.

title: The Gambler: How Penniless Dropout Kirk Kerkorian Became the Greatest Deal Maker in Capitalist History
author: William C. Rempel
description: Investigative reporter William C. Rempel delivers a solid biography of billionaire Kirk Kerkorian.

title: The Juniper Tree
author: Barbara Comyns
description: A reissue of Barbara Comyns’ 1986 inversion of the Brothers Grimm’s macabre tale The Juniper Tree .

title: A Kind of Mirraculas Paradise: A True Story About Schizophrenia
author: Sandra Allen
description: After receiving her schizophrenic Uncle Bob's manuscript, Sandra Allen uses his autobiographical work as a creative nonfiction piece and tracks his descent into mental illness.

title: Peach
author: Emma Glass
description: Using hypervisceral prose, Emma Glass's debut details a young woman's experiences in the aftermath of her rape.

title: Hippie Food: How Back-to-the-Landers, Longhairs, and Revolutionaries Changed the Way We Eat
author: Jonathan Kauffman
description: In this gastronomic study, San Francisco Chronicle James Beard Award–winning food journalist Kauffman investigates the gradual integration of organic food choices into public consumption.

title: 12 Rules for Life: An Antidote to Chaos
author: Jordan B. Peterson
description: The 2018 bestselling self-help book by controversial Canadian clinical psychologist and psychology professor Jordan Peterson. The book includes abstract ethical principles about life influenced by and based on biology, literature, religion, myths, clinical experience and scientific research.

title: The Colonial Conquest: The Confines of the Shadow Volume I
author: Alessandro Spina, trans. by André Naffis-Sahely
description: The Colonial Conquest is the first volume of Alessandro Spina's epic, The Confines of the Shadow, a sequence of novels and short stories that map the transformation of Libya, particularly the coastal city of Benghazi, under the pressure of Italian colonization.

title: The Lie and How We Told It
author: Tommi Parrish
description: A fine art graphic novel about two old friends, grown apart, who run into one another by chance and spend an evening catching up.

title: Eternal Life
author: Dara Horn
description: A two-time winner of the National Jewish Book Award for Fiction offers the story of Rachel, who in this novel has lived for 2,000 years, since she made a spiritual bargain to save the life of her first son back in Roman-occupied Jerusalem. Her recent troubles―widowhood, a failing business, an unemployed middle-aged son―are only the latest in a litany spanning dozens of countries, scores of marriages, and hundreds of children.

title: Peach
author: Emma Glass
description: In this lyrical debut, a young woman named Peach struggles to survive in the aftermath of a sexual assault, entering an oddly nightmarish reality in which her parents can't seem to comprehend that anything has happened to their daughter.

title: Facing the Abyss: American Literature and Culture in the 1940s
author: George Hutchinson
description: George Hutchinson offers readings of individual works and the larger intellectual and cultural scene to reveal the 1940s as a period of profound and influential accomplishment.

title: Loaded: A Disarming History of the Second Amendment
author: Roxanne Dunbar-Ortiz
description: A deeply-researched history of gun culture and how it reflects race and power in the United States.

title: All-American Murder
author: James Patterson & Alex Abramovich
description: An investigation of NFL player Aaron Hernandez's first-degree murder conviction and the mystery of his own shocking and untimely death.

title: The Largesse of the Sea Maiden: Stories
author: Denis Johnson
description: The death-haunted last collection of stories from National Book Award winner Denis Johnson.

title: How Democracies Die
author: Steven Levitsky and Daniel Ziblatt
description: Harvard University government professors Steven Levitsky and Daniel Ziblatt analyze the parallels between Donald Trump’s ascent and the fall of other democracies.

title: The Square and the Tower: Networks and Power, from the Freemasons to Facebook
author: Niall Ferguson
description: From the acclaimed historian and author of The Ascent of Money , a recasting of the turning points in world history, including the one we're living through, as a collision between old power hierarchies and new social networks.

title: Munich
author: Robert Harris
description: From the author of Fatherland and the Cicero Trilogy, a new spy thriller set against the backdrop of the fateful Munich Conference of September 1938.

title: Red Clocks
author: Leni Zumas
description: Red Clocks imagines an America in which every embryo is granted rights of life, liberty, and property, and five different women navigate these new barriers alongside age-old questions surrounding motherhood, identity, and freedom.

title: The Stowaway: A Young Man’s Extraordinary Adventure to Antarctica
author: Laurie Gwen Shapiro
description: The story of a scrappy teenager from New York’s Lower East Side who stowed away on the Roaring Twenties’ most remarkable feat of science and daring: an expedition to Antarctica.

title: Everything Here is Beautiful
author: Mira T. Lee
description: A debut novel of two sisters and their emotional journey through love, loyalty, and heartbreak, and an exploration of a young woman’s quest to find fulfillment and a life unconstrained by her mental illness.

title: Oliver Loving
author: Stefan Merrill Block
description: In Stefan Merrill Block's third novel, a school shooting in West Texas is revisited ten years later from the perspective of a family it changed forever.

title: Walk in the Fire
author: Steph Post
