description: A southern crime thriller and sequel to 2017's Lightwood . Fresh out of prison, Judah Cannon has returned to rural Silas, Fla. with his sights set on assuming the lead role in his family’s criminal enterprise, left vacant after his father died in a fiery gun battle involving a ruthless Pentecostal preacher and an outlaw biker club.

title: Trumpocracy: The Corruption of the American Republic
author: David Frum
description: Atlantic senior editor David Frum argues how Trump's current administration is negatively affecting the US democracy and why this political decline needs to be interrupted.

title: The Girls in the Picture
author: Melanie Benjamin
description: As Hollywood's glitzy silent film era rises and falls, the collaborative friendship and creative partnership between screenwriter Frances Marion and actress Mary Pickford revolutionizes the industry in this historical fiction.

title: Heartland
author: Ana Simo
description: A mixture of sci-fi, surreal horror, and dystopian satire, this debut novel tells the chaotic story of a thwarted lover's intricate revenge plot against her ex's former lover.

title: When They Call You a Terrorist: A Black Lives Matter Memoir
author: Patrisse Khan-Cullors and Asha Bandele
description: Co-written with asha bandele, the activist and co-founder of the Black Lives Matter movement patrisse khan-cullors draws a clear line, from her early life to her political activism, about being black in a country militarized against her community.

title: So You Want to Talk About Race
author: Ijeoma Oluo
description: In thoughtful essays geared toward facilitating difficult conversations about race, Oluo, an editor at large at the Establishment , assesses the racial landscape of contemporary America.

title: City of Endless Night
author: Douglas Preston and Lee Child
description: When Grace Ozmian, the beautiful and reckless daughter of a wealthy tech billionaire, first goes missing, the NYPD assumes she has simply sped off on another wild adventure. Until the young woman's body is discovered in an abandoned warehouse in Queens, the head nowhere to be found.

title: It's Even Worse Than You Think
author: David Cay Johnston
description: A Pulitzer Prize winning journalist, David Cay Johnston maps the weakening of the federal government and democratic institutions as a result of the various actions, and inaction, of the Trump administration.

title: A Treacherous Curse
author: Deanna Raybourn
description: Members of an Egyptian expedition fall victim to an ancient mummy’s curse in this Veronica Speedwell mystery novel.

title: Her Adult Life: Stories
author: Jenn Scott
description: The characters who populate Jenn Scott’s debut collection are both trapped and adrift. Stuck in dead-end jobs or stagnant relationships or simply caught in the grip of their own inertia, they opt out, act out, and strike out, searching for emotional sustenance in a landscape of pointless patterns and dwindling hopes. In situations that delight and discomfit, Scott explores the complicated, or simple, ways in which we settle.

title: The Immortalists
author: Chloe Benjamin
description: In 1969, four siblings visit a fortune teller, who tells each child the date of their death. We follow the Gold siblings both separately and together over the next four decades and see how these revelations affect their choices, their behavior, and their relationships with one another.

title: The Perfect Nanny
author: Leila Slimani, Trans. by Sam Taylor
description: Winner of France's 2016 Prix Goncourt, Slimani's tale of a murderous nanny explores race, class, motherhood, and domesticity in the tenth arrondissement of Paris.

title: Neon in Daylight
author: Hermione Hoby
description: A young British woman ditches both her boyfriend and her Ph.D. program for a temporary reprieve catsitting in New York City during the heatwave of 2012, and finds herself enmeshed in the lives of a charismatic aging writer and his free-spirited daughter.

title: This Could Hurt
author: Jillian Medoff
description: In this workplace drama, intrigue swirls around HR executive Rosa Guerrero and her team in the wake of the economic crisis.

title: Winter
author: Ali Smith
description: The second novel in Ali Smith’s seasonal cycle casts an eye over a post-truth era in a story rooted in history and memory.

title: Fire Sermon
author: Jamie Quatro
description: Maggie is entirely devoted to her husband Thomas, their two beautiful children, and to God? Until what begins as a platonic intellectual and spiritual exchange between writer Maggie and poet James transforms into an erotically-charged bond that challenges Maggie’s sense of loyalty and morality, drawing her deeper into the darkness of desire.

title: The Most Dangerous Man in America: Timothy Leary, Richard Nixon and the Hunt for the Fugitive King of LSD
author: Bill Minutaglio and Steve L. Davis
description: Covering a 28-month period, Bill Minutaglio and Steven L. Davis's second nonfiction collaboration details the Nixon administration's international pursuit of Timothy Leary.

title: A Girl in Exile
author: Ismail Kadare, Trans. by John Hodgson
description: From the Man Booker International Prize-winner, a parable of totalitarianism set during the latter part of Albania's decades-long Stalinist dictatorship about a writer caught up in a governmental investigation of a young woman's suicide.

title: Gnomon
author: Nick Harkaway
description: A sprawling science fiction novel set in a futuristic London where all of society is monitored and controlled by a seemingly beneficial AI called 'The System.' When a suspected dissident dies in government custody, a trusted state inspector and a true believer in the System, is assigned to find out what went wrong.

title: The Road Not Taken: Edward Lansdale and the American Tragedy in Vietnam
author: Max Boot
description: A reframing of our understanding of the Vietnam War told through a chronicle of the adventurous life of legendary CIA operative Edward Lansdale, the man said to be the fictional model for Graham Greene’s The Quiet American , whose "hearts and minds" approach could have dramatically altered the war, had it been taken on board by the US government.

title: The Afterlives
author: Thomas Pierce
description: After suffering cardiac arrest and a five-minute clinical death, 33-year-old commercial loan officer Jim Byrd is outfitted with an experimental defibrillator called a HeartNet. Soon after, Jim and his new wife, Annie, find themselves tangling with holograms, psychics, and messages from the beyond.

title: The Maze at Windermere
author: Gregory Blake Smith
description: A novel made up of five parallel stories, from Colonial times to the present, all set in Newport, Rhode Island, which examines race, class, gender, sexual identity, war and love in America through the lens of Newport’s history

title: Off the Charts: The Hidden Lives and Lessons of American Child Prodigies
author: Ann Hulbert
description: From the author of Raising America , an exploration of child genius told through the stories of fifteen exceptionally gifted children.

title: Grist Mill Road
author: Christopher J. Yates
description: Twenty-six years after three friends are bound together by a terrible and seemingly senseless crime, they meet again in New York City, with even more devastating results.

title: King Zeno
author: Nathaniel Rich
description: In the wake of an Axman murder case, the lives of a jazz musician, a police detective, and a corporate executive intertwine in 1918-19 New Orleans.

title: Tears of Salt: A Doctor's Story
author: Pietro Bartolo and Lidia Tilotta, Trans. by Chenxin Jiang
description: Told from his medical clinic on the remote island of Lampedusa, Dr. Pietro Bartolo discusses his efforts dealing with the health crises of refugees traveling between Italy and Africa.

title: Peculiar Ground
author: Lucy Hughes-Hallett
description: The Costa Award-winning author of The Pike makes her literary fiction debut with a sprawling historical novel in the spirit of Wolf Hall and Atonement —a great English country house novel, spanning three centuries, that explores themes of immigration and exclusion.

title: The Wife Between Us
author: Greer Hendricks and Sarah Pekkanen
description: The Wife Between Us exposes the secret complexities of an enviable marriage — and the dangerous truths we ignore in the name of love.

title: The Transition
author: Luke Kennard
description: Longlisted for the Desmond Elliott Prize for fiction, Luke Kennard's debut novel discusses the repercussions a young writer faces after he avoids jail time by signing up for a suspicious life-skills scheme called The Transition.

title: When: The Scientific Secrets of Perfect Timing
author: Daniel H. Pink
description: A researcher explores how the scientific secrets of good timing can help an individual flourish professionally, personally, and generally.

title: Fools and Mortals
author: Bernard Cornwell
description: Set in the gossipy world of Elizabethan theater, Cornwell's 55th book fictionizes a complicated business-brother relationship between Richard and William Shakespeare.

title: Woman at 1,000 Degrees
author: Hallgrímur Helgason, Trans. by Brian FitzGibbon
description: While "alone in a garage, together with a laptop computer and an old hand grenade," an elderly woman recounts her episodic life permanently scarred by World War II.

title: The Widows of Malabar Hill
author: Sujata Massey
description: The first in a new mystery series set in 1920s India: Perveen Mistry, Bombay’s first female lawyer, is investigating a suspicious will on behalf of three Muslim widows living in full purdah when the case takes a turn toward the murderous.

title: Heavens on Earth: The Scientific Search for the Afterlife, Immortality, and Utopia
author: Michael Shermer
description: A scientific exploration into humanity’s obsession with the afterlife and quest for immortality from the author and skeptic Michael Shermer.

title: The Job of the Wasp
author: Colin Winnette
description: In this gothic coming-of-age tale, a new arrival at an isolated school for orphaned boys quickly comes to realize there is something wrong with his new home.

title: Getting Off: One Woman's Journey Through Sex and Porn Addiction
author: Erica Garza
description: An essayist details her bracing chronicle with sex addiction and the erotic dependency attached.

title: The Epic City: The World on the Streets of Calcutta
author: Kushanava Choudhury
description: Torn between living in the United States and India, Kushanava Choudhury writes about the good, the bad, and difficult of the one place that continues to call him back: Calcutta.

title: The Boat People: A Novel
author: Sharon Bala
description: A 35-year-old Sri Lankan refugee has survived the harrowing experiences of civil war, a prison camp, and a perilous ocean voyage to Canada—but his journey has only begun, as he and his young son navigate the morass of the refugee system.

title: Phone
author: Will Self
description: A giant new novel from Booker-shortlisted Will Self completes his Neo-modernist trilogy, begun with Umbrella , and continued with Shark . An exploration of technology and psychopathology from World War I to WikiLeaks, a story of love, death, and madness.

title: Beneath the Sugar Sky
author: Seanan McGuire
description: Beneath the Sugar Sky , the third book in McGuire's Wayward Children series, returns to Eleanor West's Home for Wayward Children in a standalone contemporary fantasy for fans of all ages. At this magical boarding school, children who have experienced fantasy adventures are reintroduced to the "real" world.

title: Hollywood's Eve: Eve Babitz and the Secret History of L.A.
author: Lili Anolik
description: An exploration of the life of the hard-partying and well-connected memoirist and fiction writer, whose irreverent takes on Los Angeles bohemian culture in the 1960s and 1970s has earned her a place as a beloved cult figure and scribe.

title: Fire and Fury: Inside the Trump White House
author: Michael Wolff
description: Michael Wolff's explosive, and controversial, insider account of the chaotic inner workings of the Trump White House.

title: A State of Freedom
author: Neel Mukherjee
description: A novel in five stories of displacement and migration in contemporary India. Five characters, in very different circumstances?from a domestic cook in Mumbai, to a vagrant and his dancing bear, to a girl who escapes terror in her home village for a new life in the city?find out the meanings of dislocation and the desire for more.

title: The Woman in the Window
author: A. J. Finn
description: A Hitchcockian thriller about an agoraphobic New York woman who believes she witnessed a shocking crime in a neighboring house.

title: The Music Shop
author: Rachel Joyce
description: From the author of The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry , a love story set in London in 1988 in which the music-obsessed owner of a record store (frequented by crew of charming eccentrics) falls for a mysterious woman.

title: Cræft: An Inquiry Into the Origins and True Meaning of Traditional Crafts
author: Alexander Langlands
description: From a British archaeologist and medieval historian, an investigation into how ancient craftsmen used their skill, available natural resources and especially cræft to solve the problems that life threw at them.

title: Robicheaux
author: James Lee Burke
description: Set in the towns and backwoods of Louisiana, Dave Robicheaux discovers he may have committed the homicide he’s investigating, and works to clear his name and make sense of the murder.

title: Furnishing Eternity: A Father, a Son, a Coffin, and a Measure of Life
author: David Giffels
description: In his third memoir, journalist David Giffels and his father confront questions over grief and mortality as they bond over the building of the author's coffin.

title: The Nothing
author: Hanif Kureishi
description: A fêted filmmaker is confined by old age and ill health to his apartment and begins to suspect that his younger wife is having an affair.

title: The Bomb Maker
author: Thomas Perry
description: Suspenseful from beginning to end, the Explosive Ordnance Unit of the LAPD battles a methodical bomber whose principal target seems to be them.

title: Late Essays: 2006-2017
author: J. M. Coetzee
description: A new collection of twenty-three literary essays from the Nobel Prize–winning author J. M. Coetzee.

title: Green: A Novel
author: Sam Graham-Felsen
description: A coming-of-age novel about race, privilege, and the struggle to rise in America propelled by an unforgettable narrator, who just so happens to be one of the only white kids at his middle school.

title: Halsey Street
author: Naima Coster
description: Penelope Grand has scrapped her failed career as an artist in Pittsburgh and moved back to Brooklyn to keep an eye on her ailing father. She’s accepted that her future won’t be what she’d dreamed, but now, as gentrification has completely reshaped her old neighborhood, even her past is unrecognizable.

title: The Mannequin Makers
author: Craig Cliff
description: When a young Maori man arrives on the morning train one day in 1903--announcing the imminent visit of a famous strongman--the entire town of Marumaru, New Zealand turns out to greet him, except one. Colton Kemp, a department store window-dresser, is at home, watching his beloved wife die in premature childbirth. Tormented by grief, he hatches a plan to make his name and thwart his rival, the silent and gifted Carpenter: over the next sixteen years he will raise his newborn twins in secrecy and isolation, to become human mannequins in the world's most lifelike window display.

title: The Complete Poems of A.R. Ammons
author: A.R. Ammons & Robert M. West
description: A collection in two volumes of A.R. Ammons poetry.

title: An Uncommon Reader: A Life of Edward Garnett, Mentor and Editor of Literary Genius
author: Helen Smith
description: The biography of the most important English-language editor of the early twentieth century.

title: The Only Girl in the World
author: Maude Julien, Trans. by Adriana Hunter
description: A harrowing memoir of an abusive childhood written by a french psychotherapist whose survivalist parents imprisoned and tortured her for years.

title: Charles Darwin: Victorian Mythmaker
author: A.N. Wilson
description: A radical reappraisal of Charles Darwin from the bestselling author of Victoria: A Life .

title: Moral Combat: How Sex Divided American Christians and Fractured American Politics
author: R. Marie Griffith
description: A sweeping look at the roots of today’s culture wars over abortion, sexual identity, and the intersection of sexuality and racial differences, Griffith studies the great schism between religious conservatives and progressives about women's control over their bodies.

title: Witch Wife
author: Kiki Petrosino
description: The poems of Witch Wife are spells, obsessive incantations to exorcise or celebrate memory, to mourn the beloved dead, to conjure children or keep them at bay, to faithfully inhabit one's given body. They are also concerned with dismantling received ideas about contemporary American womanhood. What does it mean to be a wife or mother who feels ambivalent about motherhood? How are these roles further complicated for women of color in the United States?

title: Fortress America: How We Embraced Fear and Abandoned Democracy
author: Elaine Tyler May
description: Fortress America charts the rise of a muscular national culture, undercutting the common good. Instead of a thriving democracy of engaged citizens, we have become a paranoid, bunkered, militarized, and divided vigilante nation.

title: Black and Blur
author: Fred Moten
description: In Black and Blur —the first volume in his consent not to be a single being trilogy—Fred Moten engages in a capacious consideration of the place and force of blackness in African diaspora arts, politics, and life, exploring a wide range of thinkers, musicians, and artists.

title: Elmet
author: Fiona Mozley
description: Cathy and Daniel live with their father, John, in the remote woods of Yorkshire, in a house the three of them built themselves. John is a gentle brute of a man, a former enforcer who fights for money when he has to, but who otherwise just wants to be left alone to raise his children. When a local landowner shows up on their doorstep, their precarious existence is threatened, and a series of actions is set in motion that can only end in violence.

title: The Doomsday Machine: Confessions of a Nuclear War Planner
author: Daniel Ellsberg
description: From the whistle-blower who revealed the Pentagon Papers, an eyewitness exposé of the dangers of America's Top Secret, seventy-year-long nuclear policy that continues to this day.

title: Spy of the First Person
author: Sam Shepard
description: The late actor, playwright, and author's final work: a lyrical, autobiographical novella exploring memory, illness, and mortality.

title: Improv Nation
author: Sam Wasson
description: A sweeping history of Improv comedy in America.

title: No Time to Spare
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A collection of spirited, wry reflections on aging, literature, and America’s moral life, taken from the blog of speculative fiction icon, and one of America's greatest living writers, Ursula K Le Guin.

title: Parental Discretion Is Advised: The Rise of N.W.A and the Dawn of Gangsta Rap
author: Gerrick D. Kennedy
description: A chronicle of the rise, fall, and legacy of N.W.A, one of America’s most revered and iconic enduring music groups, who put their stamp on pop culture, black culture, and who changed hip-hop music forever.

title: The World Goes On
author: László Krasznahorkai, Trans. by George Szirtes, Ottilie Mulzet & John Batki
description: A collection of 20 gloomy, menacing stories from the celebrated Hungarian writer and 2015 Man Booker International Prize-winner.

title: Three Daughters of Eve
author: Elif Shafak
description: From the author of The Bastard of Istanbul , a novel in which the mugging and attempted assault of a wealthy Turkish woman on her way to an upper-crust dinner party causes her to think back over a close friendship with two other young Muslim women, and their relationship to a charismatic professor, at Oxford University fifteen years previous.

title: The Vanishing Princess
author: Jenny Diski
description: The first American edition of the only story collection from beloved late writer Jenny Diski—darkly funny, subversive, sexy, and eccentric tales from one of the most original and intelligent voices of our time.

title: The Years, Months, Days
author: Yan Lianke, Trans. by Carlos Rojas
description: Two eerie, fantastical novellas set in rural China, from Franz Kafka Award-winner/Man Booker International Prize finalist Lianke.

title: Year One
author: Nora Roberts
description: The first book in a post apocalyptic fiction trilogy from bestselling romance author Nora Roberts. When the world as they know it ends, the survivors of a mysterious plague are faced with a new world in which both dark and light magic are rising.

title: The Saboteur: The Aristocrat Who Became France's Most Daring Anti-Nazi Commando
author: Paul Kix
description: This biography illuminates an unsung hero of the French Resistance during World War II and his daring exploits as a résistant trained by Britain’s Special Operations Executive.

title: Daughters of the Air
author: Anca L. Szilágyi
description: A gritty debut novel with fairytale elements; in 1980, a girl flees to New York City as she grapples with her father's disturbing disappearance in Argentina's Dirty War.

title: Goddess of Anarchy: The Life and Times of Lucy Parsons, American Radical
author: Jacqueline Jones
description: From prize-winning historian Jacqueline Jones comes a new portrait of writer and activist Lucy Parsons and the turbulent age in which she lived.

title: Exact Thinking in Demented Times: The Vienna Circle and the Epic Quest for the Foundations of Science
author: Karl Sigmund
description: The mathematician and professor Karl Sigmund details the personal, intellectual, and social interactions of the Vienna Circle, a small band of Viennese intellectuals whose work profoundly altered the course of Western philosophy.

title: The Demon Crown
author: James Rollins
description: The twelfth volume in James Rollins's Sigma Force series, the Sigma Force members travel around the globe to prevent "a biological Pearl Harbor" involving deadly wasps.

title: The Last Man Who Knew Everything: The Life and Times of Enrico Fermi, Father of the Nuclear Age
author: David N. Schwartz
description: With a finite amount of resources, David N. Schwartz thoroughly details Italian-American physicist Enrico Fermi's life and his great achievements in the field of physics.

title: Insidious Intent
author: Val McDermid
description: Psychologist Tony Hill and former detective Carol Jordan are called upon to investigate when single women are beginning to disappear from weddings in the north of England.

title: Ultraluminous
author: Katherine Faw
description: A raw, intense novel about a high-end, girlfriend-experience prostitute and heroin addict who has just returned to her native New York City after more than a decade abroad?in Dubai, with a man she recalls only as the Sheikh.

title: Mrs. Caliban
author: Rachel Ingalls
description: A reissue of Ingalls feted and then forgotten 1982 surrealist novella about a lonely, grieving California housewife's passionate affair with a 6' 7" humanoid sea creature who has escaped from a government lab.

title: The Man Who Made the Movies: The Meteoric Rise and Tragic Fall of William Fox
author: Vanda Krefft
description: The biography of William Fox is a story of ambition, greed, and genius unfolding at the dawn of modern America.

title: I Couldn't Even Imagine That They Would Kill Us: An Oral History of the Attacks Against the Students of Ayotzinapa
author: John Gibler
description: Harrowing personal narratives describing how Mexican authorities killed, injured, and disappeared scores of students and others in a still-unsolved crime.

title: Ramp Hollow: The Ordeal of Appalachia
author: Steven Stoll
description: A searching economic and political history of a dispossessed, impoverished Appalachia that progress has long eluded.

title: Dawn of the New Everything: Encounters with Reality and Virtual Reality
author: Jaron Lanier
description: A cross between a personal memoir and history of virtual reality technology, computer scientist and entrepreneur Jaron Lanier takes a look back at technology through his life.

title: The Story of Arthur Truluv
author: Elizabeth Berg
description: A gentle, heartwarming novel about two octogenarians in a small Missouri town who come to the aid of a vulnerable pregnant teenager.

title: Avedon: Something Personal
author: Norma Stevens and Steven M. L. Aronson
description: An intimate biography of legendary fashion and portrait photographer Richard Avedon.

title: Gold Dust Woman: The Biography of Stevie Nicks
author: Stephen Davis
description: From the author of Hammer of the Gods , an unauthorized biography of the iconic Fleetwood Mac musician.

title: Uncommon People: The Rise and Fall of the Rock Stars
author: David Hepworth
description: An elegy to the age of the Rock Star, featuring Chuck Berry, Elvis, Madonna, Bowie, Prince, and more, from music journalist David Hepworth.

title: The Years
author: Annie Ernaux, Trans. by Alison L. Strayer
description: From the author of A Woman’s Story and A Man’s Place comes Annie Ernaux’s memoir and the story of a generation.

title: The People vs. Alex Cross
description: In the latest novel in the Alex Cross series, the eponymous hero confronts a grueling trial for murder despite his claims that he fired his weapon in self-defense.

title: Prairie Fires: The American Dreams of Laura Ingalls Wilder
author: Caroline Fraser
description: The first comprehensive historical biography of Laura Ingalls Wilder, the beloved author of the Little House on the Prairie books.

title: Seduced by Mrs. Robinson
author: Beverly Gray
description: On the occasion of the iconic film’s fiftieth birthday, Beverly Gray offers a close reading of ‘The Graduate’ along with vivid details from behind the scenes of the production.

title: Future Home of the Living God
author: Louise Erdrich
description: From the National Book Award-winning author of LaRose and The Round House , a portrait of a young woman fighting for her life and her unborn child against oppressive forces that manifest in the wake of a cataclysmic event. In a dystopian U.S., Congress has expanded a set of policies that began as the Patriot Act so that pregnant women can be “sequestered in hospitals in order to give birth under controlled circumstances."

title: Bunk: The Rise of Hoaxes, Humbug, Plagiarists, Phonies, Post-Facts, and Fake News
author: Kevin Young
description: Award-winning poet and critic Kevin Young tours us through a rogue’s gallery of hoaxers, plagiarists, forgers, and fakers?from the humbug of P. T. Barnum and Edgar Allan Poe to the unrepentant bunk of JT LeRoy and Donald J. Trump. Bunk traces the history of the hoax as a peculiarly American phenomenon, examining what motivates hucksters and makes the rest of us so gullible, and analyzing how American hoaxes have intersected with race and racism.

title: The Vanity Fair Diaries: 1983 - 1992
author: Tina Brown
description: A portrait of the flash and dash and power brokering of the Excessive Eighties in New York and Hollywood, from the iconic former editor-in-chief of Vanity Fair .

title: Artemis
author: Andy Weir
description: From the author of The Martian , a near-future thriller set on a lunar colony about a young Muslim woman, short on money and prospects, who, after agreeing to carry out a lucrative heist, finds herself embroiled in an elaborate conspiracy.

title: Promise Me, Dad
author: Joe Biden
description: A memoir, from the former Vice President, of a turbulent political year that co-incided with his son Beau's brain cancer diagnosis, and eventual death.

title: Debriefing: Collected Stories
author: Susan Sontag, Ed. by Benjamin Taylor
description: A collection of short fiction from the late famed intellectual Susan Sontag.

title: The Extra Woman
author: Joanna Scutts
description: From the flapper to The Feminine Mystique , a cultural history of single women in the city through the reclaimed life of glamorous guru Marjorie Hillis.

title: Strangers in Budapest
author: Jessica Keener
description: A novel following an American couple and their young son as they learn to survive in 1990s Budapest.

title: Improvement
author: Joan Silber
description: A novel about a young single mother living in New York, her eccentric aunt, and the decisions they make that have unexpected implications for the world around them.

title: Don't Save Anything
author: James Salter
description: A collection of essays, articles, and profiles from the author of A Sport and a Pastime and Light Years .

title: Cartoon County: My Father and His Friends in the Golden Age of Make-Believe
author: Cullen Murphy
description: The story of a tight-knit circle of cartoonists clustered in southwest Connecticut after World War II, written by the former Atlantic editor Murphy?the son of a man at the heart of this artistic milieu.

title: The City of Brass
author: S. A. Chakraborty
description: A fantasy debut in which in which the future of a magical Middle Eastern kingdom rests in the hands of a clever and defiant young con artist with miraculous healing gifts.

title: War in 140 Characters: How Social Media Is Reshaping Conflict in the Twenty-First Century
author: David Patrikarakos
description: Drawing on his war reporting experiences in Ukraine, journalist David Patrikarakos explores how social media has changed the way the world fights and consumes war – what it means for the future.

title: Patrick Leigh Fermor: A Life in Letters
author: Patrick Leigh Fermor, Sel. and Ed. by Adam Sisman
description: A collection of correspondence to friends and family for more than half a century, recounting the noted British traveler and writer’s adventures over a long life.

title: Sleep No More: Six Murderous Tales
author: P. D. James
description: Six previously uncollected murder mystery stories from the late, great British writer P. D. James, author of Death Comes to Pemberley .

title: Queen Victoria's Matchmaking: The Royal Marriages That Shaped Europe
author: Deborah Cadbury
description: Deborah Cadbury digs deeper into Queen Victoria’s extensive brood, their intermarriages, and their wars.

title: Balancing Acts: Behind the Scenes at London's National Theatre
author: Nicholas Hytner
description: Nicholas Hytner, a celebrated director, shares his memories from his 12 years as the head of one of the world’s most famous theater companies.

title: Ice
author: Anna Kavan
description: The 50th anniversary edition of Anna Kavan’s masterpiece of literary science fiction.

title: The Gifted Generation: When Government Was Good
author: David Goldfield
description: A history of the post-World War II decades, during which an activist federal government guided the country toward the first real flowering of the American dream.

title: Heather, the Totality
author: Matthew Weiner
description: From the creator of Mad Men comes a noirish debut novel about family, power, and privilege.

title: The Wine Lover's Daughter
author: Anne Fadiman
description: Anne Fadiman examines her relationship with her father, Clifton Fadiman, a renowned literary critic, editor, and radio host whose greatest love was wine.

title: The Revolution of Marina M.
author: Janet Fitch
description: A long, sweeping historical saga of the Russian Revolution, as seen through the eyes of a young woman of privilege who aches to break free of the constraints of her genteel life.

title: Franklin D. Roosevelt: A Political Life
author: Robert Dallek
description: A biography of Roosevelt by the bestselling biographer of An Unfinished Life: JFK 1917-1963 , focusing on FDR's career as an incomparable politician, uniter, and deal maker.

title: The End We Start From
author: Megan Hunter
description: A Cli-Fi debut novel about new motherhood, birth and renewal. As London is submerged below floodwaters, a woman gives birth to her first child, Z. Days later, she and her baby are forced to leave their home in search of safety. They head north through a newly dangerous country seeking refuge from place to place. The story traces fear and wonder as the baby grows, thriving and content against all the odds.

title: The Midnight Line: A Jack Reacher Novel
author: Lee Child
description: The latest novel in Child's wildly popular Jack Reacher thriller series. A search for the owner of a pawned woman's West Point ring brings Reacher into contact with an elaborate South Dakota and Wyoming opioid-distribution syndicate.

title: Wonder Valley
author: Ivy Pochoda
description: When a teen runs away from his father’s mysterious commune, he sets in motion a domino effect that will connect six characters desperate for hope and love, set across the sun-bleached canvas of Los Angeles.

title: The Quantum Spy
author: David Ignatius
description: An espionage thriller about rival U.S. and Chinese agencies seeking to develop the world's first “quantum computer," a machine that could decrypt the undecryptable and do it thousands of times faster than any existing supercomputer.

title: Lenin: The Man, the Dictator, and the Master of Terror
author: Victor Sebestyen
description: The first major biography of Lenin in English in nearly two decades.

title: The Dawn Watch: Joseph Conrad in a Global World
author: Maya Jasanoff
description: A blending of biography, history, and literary criticism which explores the life and times of Joseph Conrad, his turbulent age of globalization and our own.

title: Kids These Days: Human Capital and the Making of Millennials
author: Malcolm Harris
description: An editor at the New Inquiry talks about the causes and effects of the coming crises his millennial generation will face.

title: Troublemakers: Silicon Valley's Coming of Age
author: Leslie Berlin
description: Stanford University archivist Leslie Berlin looks back on Silicon Valley's early years and illuminates the overlooked figures who helped fuel the expansion of the tech industry.

title: Keeping On Keeping On
author: Alan Bennett
description: This is the third installment of dramatist and author Alan Bennett's collection of diaries and essays, covering 2005 to 2015.

title: Brolliology: A History of the Umbrella in Life and Literature
author: Marion Rankine
description: A whimsical, illustrated history of the umbrella's surprising place in life and literature.

title: Radio Free Vermont
author: Bill McKibben
description: A debut novel from author and environmentalist McKibben about a band of Vermont radicals, led by a 72-year-old radio host, who decide that their state might be better off as its own republic.

title: Spineless: The Science of Jellyfish and the Art of Growing a Backbone
author: Juli Berwald
description: A close look at the biology and behavior of jellyfish combined with a personal history of the author, a former ocean scientist who was pulled back to the sea by these enigmatic creatures.

title: Incest
author: Christine Angot, Trans. by Tess Lewis
description: A daring autofictional novel that made Christine Angot one of the most controversial figures in contemporary France literature recounts the narrator's incestuous relationship with her father.

title: They Can't Kill Us Until They Kill Us
author: Hanif Abdurraqib
description: In essays that have been published by the New York Times , MTV, and Pitchfork, among others?along with original, previously unreleased essays?Willis-Abdurraqib uses music and culture as a lens through which to view our world.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer, Trans. by Emily Wilson
description: The landmark first translation of The Odyssey by a woman into English that matches Homer's musical prose line by line.

title: The Inner Life of Animals: Love, Grief, and Compassion – Surprising Observations of a Hidden World
author: Peter Wohlleben, Trans. by Jane Billinghurst
description: Following The Hidden Life of Trees , Peter Wohlleben uses his personal observations and the latest scientific research to discuss how animals think, feel, and know in the same way as humans.

title: It's All Relative: Adventures Up and Down the World’s Family Tree
author: A.J. Jacobs
description: A humorous genealogical study/memoir in which Esquire contributing editor Jacobs muses on the nature of family and the interconnectedness of humanity while trying to organize the world's largest family reunion.

title: Playing with Fire: The 1968 Election and the Transformation of American Politics
author: Lawrence O'Donnell
description: From the host of MSNBC’s The Last Word with Lawrence O'Donnell , an account of "the presidential election that changed everything," the tumultuous race that created American politics as we know it today.

title: God: A Human History
author: Reza Aslan
description: The author of Zealot and host of Believer explores humanity’s quest to make sense of the divine."

title: Mean
author: Myriam Gurba
description: Part true crime book, part memoir, part ghost story, Mean is the tale of experimental poet Myriam Gurba’s coming of age as a queer, mixed-race Chicana and victim of sexual assault, as well as an investigation into the rape and murder of a young immigrant woman in the California town where they both lived.

title: The Last Girl: My Story of Captivity, and My Fight Against the Islamic State
author: Nadia Murad
description: Nadia Murad, a human rights activist and UNODC Goodwill Ambassador, tells her account of surviving religious genocide and life in captivity under the Islamic State.

title: Giving Up the Ghost
author: Hilary Mantel
description: The renowned English critic and novelist summons the ghosts of her childhood and youth.

title: Women & Power: A Manifesto
author: Mary Beard
description: Based on a lecture from the London Review of Books lecture series. Noted classicist and essayist Beard looks deep into the past and hard at the present to examine the power of women—and more often, their powerlessness—in a world of impatient men.

title: The King Is Always Above the People
author: Daniel Alarcón
description: A collection of stories about immigration, broken dreams, Los Angeles gang members, Latin American families, and other tales of high stakes journeys, from the author of War by Candlelight and At Night We Walk in Circles .

title: Stalin: Waiting for Hitler, 1929-1941
author: Stephen Kotkin
description: The second volume in the definitive biography of Joseph Stalin, covering collectivization and the Great Terror up to the conflict with Hitler’s Germany.

title: Hiddensee: A Tale of the Once and Future Nutcracker
author: Gregory Maguire
description: From the revisionist fairy tale author of Wicked and After Alice , a novel inspired by a timeless holiday legend, intertwining the story of the famous Nutcracker with the life of the mysterious toy maker named Drosselmeier who carves him.

title: In the Midst of Winter
author: Isabel Allende
description: From the Chilean-American magical realist author of The House of the Spirits , a novel about two NYU professors and a Guatemalan nanny, thrown together during a Brooklyn blizzard, who find themselves with a body to dispose of.

title: Bobby Kennedy: A Raging Spirit
author: Chris Matthews
description: An in-depth portrait of Bobby Kennedy's political career, by Hardball anchor and Kennedy and Nixon author Matthews.

title: The Three Lives of James Madison: Genius, Partisan, President
author: Noah Feldman
description: Organizing this biography into three distinct parts, Harvard constitutional-law scholar Noah Feldman reexamines James Madison's identity as a Revolutionary thinker, political partisan, and wartime president.

title: Invocation to Daughters
author: Barbara Jane Reyes
description: Feminist experimental poetry in the tradition of Audre Lorde and Theresa Hak Kyung Cha from a prominent Filipina American poet. A 2018 California Book Award Finalist.

title: The River of Consciousness
author: Oliver Sacks
description: From the beloved late neurologist and author, a collection of essays that displays Sacks's passionate engagement with the most compelling and seminal ideas of human endeavor: evolution, creativity, memory, time, consciousness, and experience.

title: Sticky Fingers: The Life and Times of Jann Wenner and Rolling Stone Magazine
author: Joe Hagan
description: The first definitive biography of Jann Wenner, the iconic founder of Rolling Stone magazine, and a romp through the hothouses of rock and roll, politics, media, and Hollywood, from the Summer of Love to the Internet age.

title: Ghosts of the Tsunami
author: Richard Lloyd Parry
description: From the Japan correspondent of the (London) Times , a piercing look at the communities ravaged by the earthquake and tsunami that hit the country in 2011.

title: The Rooster Bar
author: John Grisham
description: The latest legal thriller from John Grisham, centered around a shady, for-profit law school and the three young law students who investigate its murky dealings.

title: Vacationland: True Stories from Painful Beaches
author: John Hodgman
description: A collection of dourly comic essayistic stories about aging, parenthood, and white male privilege from writer and comedian Hodgman.

title: Strange Weather
author: Joe Hill
description: Four short horror novellas from the author of Horns and The Fireman .

title: Friends Divided: John Adams and Thomas Jefferson
author: Gordon S. Wood
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning historian of the American Revolutionary period, a dual biography of two of America's most enduringly fascinating figures, whose partnership helped birth a nation, and whose subsequent falling out did much to fix its course.

title: I Can't Breathe: A Killing on Bay Street
author: Matt Taibbi
description: From the Rolling Stone contributing editor, a work of literary journalism that explores the roots and repercussions of the infamous killing of Eric Garner by the New York City police.

title: An American Family: A Memoir of Hope and Sacrifice
author: Khizr Khan
description: A memoir and immigrant story by the Muslim American Harvard-trained lawyer, Gold Star father, and 2016 DNC speaker whose son was tragically killed in Iraq in 2004.

title: Calder: The Conquest of Time: The Early Years: 1898-1940
author: Jed Perl
description: The first in a two-volume biography of America’s greatest twentieth-century sculptor, Alexander Calder.

title: 100 Amazing Facts About the Negro
author: Henry Louis Gates Jr.
description: A compendium of historical curiosities intended to illuminate the sheer complexity and diversity of being “Negro” in the world.

title: Ka
author: John Crowley, Illustrated by Melody Newcomb
description: From the author of Little, Big (1981), a fantasy novel set in a bleak, dystopia world, about a man who tells the story of an immortal crow named Dar Oakley and his impossible lives and deaths in the land of Ka.

title: The Thin Light of Freedom
author: Edward L. Ayers
description: Continuing from his 2004 Bancroft Prize winner In the Presence of Mine Enemies , this following volume tells the story of the Civil War's final years in the Great Valley between the Blue Ridge and Appalachian mountains.

title: The Fear and the Freedom
author: Keith Lowe
description: In this third volume of his historical series, Keith Lowe follows his study of the anarchy and devastation of postwar Europe with a global overview of the political, social, and cultural effects of the war.

title: The Story of the Jews Volume 2: Belonging
author: Simon Schama
description: In this second volume on the history of the Jews, Simon Schama follows the lives of various Jewish figures across the globe after 1492 to the end of the nineteenth century.

title: The Second Coming of the KKK
author: Linda Gordon
description: From two-time Bancroft Prize-winning historian Gordon, an investigation into the cultural and societal conditions that led to the resurgence of the KKK during the 1920s.

title: Hank and Jim: The Fifty-Year Friendship of Henry Fonda and James Stewart
author: Scott Eyman
description: The story of the remarkable friendship of two Hollywood legends who, though different in many ways, maintained a close friendship that endured all of life’s twists and turns.

title: The Water Will Come: Rising Seas, Sinking Cities, and the Remaking of the Civilized World
author: Jeff Goodell
description: A journalistic investigation of what will happen to the world's coastal regions as climate change elevates sea levels and conjures up extreme weather.

title: Christmas: A Biography
author: Judith Flanders
description: Judith Flanders explores the Christmas holiday, from the original festival through present day traditions.

title: Blood Brothers: The Story of the Strange Friendship between Sitting Bull and Buffalo Bill
author: Deanne Stillman
description: The little known story of the unlikely friendship of two famous figures of the American West—Buffalo Bill Cody and Sitting Bull—told through their time in Cody’s Wild West show in the 1880s.

title: Messiah: The Composition and Afterlife of Handel's Masterpiece
author: Jonathan Keates
description: Keates’s fast-paced history of Handel's 'Messiah' provides a glimpse into the dynamic character of the oratorio.

title: American Radical
author: Tamer Elnoury, Kevin Maurer
description: For the first time, an active, Muslim American FBI agent reveals his experience infiltrating and bringing down a terror cell in North America.

title: The Book of Dust: La Belle Sauvage
author: Philip Pullman
description: The acclaimed fantasy author of The Golden Compass returns to the parallel world of Lyra Belacqua and His Dark Materials for the first volume in a new epic adventure trilogy in which daemons, alethiometers, and the Magisterium all play a part.

title: Reckless Daughter: A Portrait of Joni Mitchell
author: David Yaffe
description: A new biography of the musical icon, telling the story of how the blond girl with the guitar became a superstar of folk music in the 1960s, a key figure in the Laurel Canyon music scene of the 1970s, and the songwriter who spoke resonantly to, and for, audiences across the country.

title: Smile
author: Roddy Doyle
description: From the Booker Prize-winning author of Paddy Clarke Ha Ha Ha and the Barrytown Trilogy, a novel about a recently-separated middle-aged writer who spends his evenings sitting quietly in a Dublin pub, until the appearance of an obnoxious man who claims to be a former classmate stirs up memories of their time in a Christian Brothers school.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
author: Walter Isaacson
description: A new biography of the famed Italian Renaissance polymath from the author of Steve Jobs , Einstein , and Benjamin Franklin .

title: Uncommon Type
author: Tom Hanks
description: A debut collection of seventeen short stories from Oscar-winning actor Tom Hanks.

title: The Letters of Sylvia Plath Volume 1: 1940-1956
author: Sylvia Plath, ed. by Peter K. Steinberg & Karen V. Kukil
description: The first volume of the iconic poet and writer's collected correspondence with more than 120 people, including family, friends, contemporaries, and colleagues.

title: Righteous
author: Joe Ide
description: The follow-up to Ide's Edgar Award-nominated debut crime novel ( IQ ), focusing on an East Long Beach private investigator's search for the truth behind his brother's death.

title: The Collected Essays of Elizabeth Hardwick
author: Elizabeth Hardwick, selected by Darryl Pinckney
description: The first-ever collection of essays from across Elizabeth Hardwick's illustrious writing career.

title: Death in the Air
author: Kate Winkler Dawson
description: Focusing on five days in the winter of 1952 in London, a dual historical narrative of an iconic city menaced by both a serial killer and a cloud of toxic smog.

title: Where the Past Begins
author: Amy Tan
description: An intimate writer's memoir from the author of The Joy Luck Club , told in a collage of journal entries, letters and meditations on a wide range of subjects, from writing and memory to music, language and family.

title: James Wright: A Life in Poetry
author: Jonathan Blunk
description: A biography of the brilliant but troubled mid-century American poet.

title: Oriana Fallaci
author: Cristina De Stefano, Trans. by Marina Harss
description: A biography of the most famous Italian journalist of the twentieth century, an inspiring and often controversial woman who defied the codes of reportage.

title: The Floating World
author: C. Morgan Babst
description: A debut novel about a New Orleans family fracturing in the wake of Hurricane Katrina.

title: Endurance: A Year in Space, A Lifetime of Discovery
author: Scott Kelly
description: Astronaut Scott Kelly, a four-time veteran of off-planet missions, retells his year aboard the International Space Station and offers a personal view of astronautics.

title: The Butchering Art: Joseph Lister's Quest to Transform the Grisly World of Victorian Medicine
author: Lindsey Fitzharris
description: Medical historian and popular blogger Lindsey Fitzharris narrates the quest of a tenacious 19th-century doctor to save his patients; in the process, he transformed the world of surgery and medicine.

title: Deep Freeze
author: John Sandford
description: In the 10th Virgil Flowers novel, Virgil returns to Trippton, Minnesota, to dig into twenty years’ worth of traumas, feuds, and bad blood after a woman is found dead in a block of ice.

title: What You Did Not Tell: A Russian Past and the Journey Home
author: Mark Mazower
description: An exploration of the sacrifices and silences that marked a generation and their descendants revitalizes the history of a socialism erased from memory.

title: The Doll's Alphabet
author: Camilla Grudova
description: A debut story collection that is by turns childlike and naive, grotesque and very dark: the marriage of Angela Carter and Margaret Atwood.

title: A Natural
author: Ross Raisin
description: A closeted gay soccer player and an injured teammate’s estranged wife offer an intimate picture of life in the lower reaches of professional British football.

title: American Wolf: A True Story of Survival and Obsession in the West
author: Nate Blakeslee
description: The story of the reintroduction of wolves into Yellowstone National Park and its aftermath, focusing on O-Six, the famous matriarch of the Lamar Canyon pack.

title: Renoir: An Intimate Biography
author: Barbara Ehrlich White
description: An intimate portrait of the complex artist in images of his paintings, his own words, and the words of his contemporaries.

title: Guantánamo Diary: Restored Edition
author: Mohamedou Ould Slahi, Ed. by Larry Siems
description: In November 2001, Mohamedou Ould Slahi was arrested and later imprisoned as a suspected terrorist by the U.S. government in Guantánamo Bay, where he languished for 14 years despite no charges ever being brought against him. Penned while in detention, his memoir's original publication in 2015 was heavily redacted by the government, while the restored edition fills in blacked out text recounting Slahi's experiences—including torture—in Guantánamo.

title: Outside Is the Ocean
author: Matthew Lansburgh
description: Three days after her twentieth birthday, a young woman who grew up in Germany during World War II crosses the Atlantic to start a new life. Outside Is the Ocean traces Heike’s struggle to find love and happiness in America.

title: Grant
author: Ron Chernow
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Washington and Alexander Hamilton , a massive new biography of the civil war general and president Ulysses S. Grant.

title: The Power
author: Naomi Alderman
description: Winner of the 2017 Baileys Women's Prize for Fiction. A speculative fiction novel in which a genetic mutation causes girls across the world suddenly acquire the power to conduct electricity and thereby alter the world order.

title: Turtles All the Way Down
author: John Green
description: The latest novel from the celebrated YA author of The Fault in Our Stars focuses on a teenage girl's struggles with anxiety and Obsessive Compulsive Disorder.

title: The Rules of Magic
author: Alice Hoffman
description: A prequel to Hoffman's 1995 novel Practical Magic . At the beginning of the 1960s, three unique and charismatic New York teenagers, part of the Owens family of witches, come to terms with their gifts during one summer in the tiny Massachusetts town where their eccentric aunt lives.

title: Code Girls
author: Liza Mundy
description: A previously untold history of the American women who served as codebreakers during World War II.

title: Red Famine: Stalin's War on Ukraine
author: Anne Applebaum
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Gulag , a detailed historical account arguing that that Stalin’s 1929 plan for agricultural collectivization, which resulted in a famine that claimed the lives of millions, was designed to rid the burgeoning Soviet Union of Ukrainian peasants.

title: The Secret Life: Three True Stories of the Digital Age
author: Andrew O'Hagan
description: From Booker-nominated novelist O'Hagan, three essays that explore identity in the digital age through three figures: Julian Assange, the founder of Wikileaks; Craig Steven Wright, who may or may not be the creator of bitcoin; and Ronald “Ronnie” Pinn, who, despite a U.K. passport, mailing address, and gaggle of Facebook friends, is not real.

title: The Apparitionists
author: Peter Manseau
description: A story of faith and fraud in post–Civil War America, told through the lens of a photographer who claimed he could capture images of the dead.

title: The State of Affairs: Rethinking Infidelity
author: Esther Perel
description: Iconic couples’ therapist and author of Mating in Captivity Esther Perel returns with a provocative look at relationships through the lens of infidelity.

title: Catapult
author: Emily Fridlund
description: A collection of short stories about the hidden strangeness and emptiness that lingers beneath the surface of childhood, adolescence, marriage, and family life.

title: Destination Casablanca
author: Meredith Hindley
description: The real-life drama of the refugees, resistance fighters and Allied spies who flowed through Casablanca in the build-up to Operation Torch in November 1942, when some 33,000 American soldiers stormed the beaches of French Morocco.

title: Lou Reed: A Life
author: Anthony DeCurtis
description: A biography of the Velvet Underground frontman and alternative rock icon, by Rolling Stone writer DeCurtis.

title: Here in Berlin
author: Cristina Garcia
description: A lonely, nameless Visitor spends several months in Berlin during 2013, absorbing the stories of dozens of people whose lives have been shaped, or twisted out of shape, by the Second World War and its aftermath.

title: Vivian Maier: A Photographer’s Life and Afterlife
author: Pamela Bannos
description: A investigation into artistic authority, appropriation, legacy and copyright through a biography of the Chicago nanny who wandered the city for decades, constantly snapping photographs, which were unseen until they were discovered in a seemingly abandoned storage locker, after which she was heralded, posthumously, as one of the 20th century's greatest street photographers.

title: Nightmare in Berlin
author: Hans Fallada, trans. by Allan Blunden
description: The first English translation of Fallada's 1947 novel. The story of a man, Dr Doll, and his wife, who are taking shelter in the German countryside, haunted by nightmarish images at night, when the Russians invade. They return to Berlin after the end of the war, and attempt to resume their lives, but confronting the reality of life in the devastated city, they fall into morphine addiction.

title: The Gourmands' Way
author: Justin Spring
description: A culinary biography of six writers on food and wine whose lives and careers intersected in mid-twentieth-century France.

title: Lost Kingdom: The Quest for Empire and the Making of the Russian Nation
author: Serhii Plokhy
description: Covering the late 15th century through the present, Lost Kingdom focuses specifically on the Russian nationalism, exploring how leaders from Ivan the Terrible to Vladimir Putin instrumentalized identity to achieve their imperial and great-power aims.

title: Devotions: The Selected Poems of Mary Oliver
author: Mary Oliver
description: Spanning more than five decades of her work, Mary Oliver's Devotions showcases the interconnectness of all living things and her ongoing interest in the natural world.

title: Hoover: An Extraordinary Life in Extraordinary Times
author: Kenneth Whyte
description: A comprehensive biography of the 31 President of the United States, reassessing his life and legacy.

title: Ferocity
author: Nicola Lagioia, Trans. by Antony Shugaar
description: Winner of the 2015 Strega Prize, Italy's preeminent prize for fiction. A family saga and a cinematic portrait of the moral and political corruption of an entire society.

title: Texas Blood: Seven Generations Among the Outlaws, Ranchers, Indians, Missionaries, Soldiers, and Smugglers of the Borderlands
author: Roger D. Hodge
description: Roger D. Hodge, the national editor of The Intercept , takes a loping tour of the Lone Star State and the historical paths to, through, and from it.

title: The End of Policing
author: Alex S. Vitale
description: This book attempts to spark public discussion by revealing the tainted origins of modern policing as a tool of social control. It shows how the expansion of police authority is inconsistent with community empowerment, social justice—even public safety.

title: In the Distance
author: Hernan Diaz
description: A young Swedish immigrant finds himself penniless and alone in California. The boy travels East in search of his brother, moving on foot against the great current of emigrants pushing West. Driven back again and again, he meets naturalists, criminals, religious fanatics, swindlers, Indians, and lawmen, and his exploits turn him into a legend. A finalist for the 2018 PEN/Faulkner Award, the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, and the 2019 winner of the Whiting Award.

title: Mrs. Osmond
author: John Banville
description: A sequel to Henry James' The Portrait of a Lady , John Banville's novel takes this masterpiece and reworks it into a contemporary setting that carries new plot twists.

title: Manhattan Beach
author: Jennifer Egan
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of A Visit From the Goon Squad , an historical novel set in WWII New York about a young woman who becomes a diver in a Naval ship yard and strikes up a relationship with a local gangster who may be connected to her father's disappearance.

title: We Were Eight Years in Power: An American Tragedy
author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
description: Winner of the 2018 Dayton Literary Peace Prize, a collection of 8 essays, written between 2008 and 2016 with added contemporary introductions to each, from the National Book Award–winning author of Between the World and Me , reflecting on race, Barack Obama’s presidency and its jarring aftermath—including the election of Donald Trump, and his own evolution as a writer.

title: Fresh Complaint
author: Jeffrey Eugenides
description: The first collection of short stories from the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Middlesex and The Virgin Suicides .

title: Her Body and Other Parties
author: Carmen Maria Machado
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "LGBTQ Stories", "Literary", "Story Collections"]
description: A collection of genre-bending short stories that weave fables, urban legends, gothic literature, and popular culture to create striking narratives about female selfhood and sexuality.

title: The Future Is History: How Totalitarianism Reclaimed Russia
author: Masha Gessen
description: Winner of the 2017 National Book Award for Non Fiction. From acclaimed Russian-American journalist Gessen, an examination of Russia in the post-Soviet period, when the public’s hopes for democracy devolved within a restricted society. Structured around the experiences of four principal individuals who came of age in the aftermath of the U.S.S.R.’s collapse.

title: Ali: A Life
author: Jonathan Eig
description: The first unauthorized biography of its kind of Muhammad Ali, from an author with unique access to Ali’s inner circle.

title: A Bold and Dangerous Family
author: Caroline Moorehead
description: An intimate history of the family who mounted a campaign against Mussolini and the rise of fascism in Italy, one which ultimately cost the two sons their lives.

title: Reservoir 13
author: Jon McGregor
description: A slow-burning literary mystery about a 13-year-old girl’s disappearance from a small English village, and the effect it has on the people of the village in the years that follow.

title: Origin
author: Dan Brown
description: The fifth book in The Da Vinci Code author's Robert Langdon series, this time focusing on the murder of a genius former student of Langdon's before he can make an earth-shattering announcement that will change how every world religion is seen.

title: Dunbar
author: Edward St. Aubyn
description: Part of the Hogarth Shakespeare series, in which contemporary novelists reimagine the Bard's iconic plays as. The author of the Patrick Melrose novels brings King Lear to the modern era in the story of a once-powerful head of a global media empire and his scheming daughters.

title: The Nine-Tailed Fox
author: Martin Limón
description: In the 12th mystery of Martin Limón's Sergeants Sueño and Bascom series, U.S. Army CID agents George Sueño and Ernie Bascom investigate the disappearance of three American soldiers serving in 1970s South Korea.

title: Logical Family
author: Armistead Maupin
description: A memoir from the author of the Tales of the City series, chronicling his odyssey from the conservative, racist old South to freewheeling San Francisco, and his evolution from curious youth to ground-breaking writer and gay rights pioneer.

title: Why We Sleep
author: Matthew Walker, PhD
description: From the Director of UC Berkeley’s Sleep and Neuroimaging Lab, an exploration of sleep that explains how we can harness its transformative power to change our lives for the better.

title: Admissions: Life as a Brain Surgeon
author: Henry Marsh
description: A retired British neurosurgeon delivers the follow-up to his debut memoir, Do No Harm: Stories of Life, Death, and Brain Surgery . Marsh reflects on his life, career, volunteer work in Ukraine and Nepal, and thoughts on dying and death.

title: Nine Continents
author: Xiaolu Guo
description: A memoir from acclaimed Chinese writer and filmmaker Guo about her coming of age in an inhospitable country, and determination to seek a life beyond the limits of its borders.

title: The Obama Inheritance: Fifteen Stories of Conspiracy Noir
author: Ed. by Gary Phillips
description: Noir meets diverse voices and transforms the genre into an over-the-top, transcendental psychedelic thriller ride in this collection of fifteen pulpy stories of conspiracy noir, riffing on the numerous fictions spun about the 44th president of the U.S.

title: theMystery.doc
author: Matthew McIntosh
description: A mammoth, shapeshifting postmodern literary novel. Rooted in the western United States in the decade post-9/11, the book follows a young writer and his wife as he attempts to write the follow-up to his first novel, searching for a form that will express the world as it has become, even as it continually shifts all around him.

title: Schlesinger: The Imperial Historian
author: Richard Aldous
description: The first major biography of preeminent historian and intellectual Arthur Schlesinger Jr., a Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer and member of Kennedy’s White House.

title: Paris in the Present Tense
author: Mark Helprin
description: From the author of Winter's Tale , a Paris-set novel in which seventy-four-year-old Jules Lacour?a maître at Paris-Sorbonne, cellist, widower, veteran of the war in Algeria, and child of the Holocaust?must find a balance between his strong obligations to the past and the attractions and beauties of life and love in the present.

title: The Last Ballad
author: Wiley Cash
description: Inspired by the events of an actual textile-mill strike in 1929, Wiley Cash creates the picture of one woman’s desperation.

title: To the Back of Beyond
author: Peter Stamm, Trans. by Michael Hoffman
description: After Thomas unexpectedly walks out on his family and onto a trek acros the countryside, To the Back of Beyond follows him and his wife Astrid on their separate paths.

title: The Chicago Cubs: Story of a Curse
author: Rich Cohen
description: In 2016, the Chicago Cubs won the World Series for the first time since 1908—and thereby hangs this tale.

title: Scalia Speaks
author: Antonin Scalia
description: Edited by the justice's son and one of his law clerks, this definitive collection of the late Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia's finest speeches covers topics as varied as the law, faith, virtue, pastimes, and his heroes and friends.

title: Adults in the Room
author: Yanis Varoufakis
description: A chronicle of charismatic former Greek finance minister Yanis Varoufakis' battles with the leaders of the troika (the European Commission, the EU’s executive body; the European Central Bank; and the International Monetary Fund) during the 2014–2015 stages in his country’s ongoing debt crisis.

title: The Glass Eye
author: Jeannie Vanasco
description: The night before her father dies, eighteen-year-old Jeannie Vanasco promises she will write a book for him. But this isn't the book she imagined. The Glass Eye is Jeannie's struggle to honor her father, her larger-than-life hero but also the man who named her after his daughter from a previous marriage, a daughter who died. It is also an examination of the author's lifelong battle with crippling bipolar disorder and depression.

title: Ballad of the Anarchist Bandits
author: John Merriman
description: A true crime account of six terrifying months in 1911-1912, when the citizens of Paris were gripped by a violent crime streak. A group of anarchist bandits, motivated by the rampant inequality and poverty in Paris, went on a rampage throughout the city and its suburbs, robbing banks and wealthy Parisians, killing anyone who got in their way.

title: Bible Nation: The United States of Hobby Lobby
author: Candida R. Moss and Joel S. Baden
description: An investigation in how the billionaire evangelical Christian owners of Hobby Lobby are using a vast private fortune to promote personal faith in the public sphere.

title: The Prague Sonata
author: Bradford Morrow
description: A literary quest novel that travels from Nazi-occupied Prague to turn-of-the-millennium New York as a young musicologist seeks to solve the mystery behind an eighteenth-century sonata manuscript

title: The Collector of Lives: Giorgio Vasari and the Invention of Art
author: Ingrid Rowland & Noah Charley
description: A biography of biographer Giorgio Vasari that reveals how a Renaissance scholar reshaped the visual world.

title: The Taste of Empire: How Britain's Quest for Food Shaped the Modern World
author: Lizzie Collingham
description: A history of the British Empire told through twenty meals, arguing that food was one of the driving forces of empire and helped form the eating habits of the entire modern world.

title: The Dangerous Case of Donald Trump: 27 Psychiatrists and Mental Health Experts Assess a President
author: Ed. by Bandy X. Lee and Robert Jay Lifton
description: Mental health professionals and others make the case that Donald Trump is mentally ill, dangerous, or both.

title: The Relive Box and Other Stories
author: T.C. Boyle
description: A new collection from T.C. Boyle, one of the contemporary American masters of the short story, focusing on the decline of nature and the takeover of technology in modern society.

title: Martin Luther: The Man Who Rediscovered God And Changed the World
author: Eric Metaxas
description: A biography of Martin Luther, whose monumental faith and courage gave birth to the ideals of liberty, equality, and individualism that lie at the heart of modern life.

title: Dogs at the Perimeter
author: Madeleine Thien
description: Thirty years after Janie experiences as a child the terrible violence carried out by the Khmer Rouge and loses everything she holds dear, she lives in Montreal and struggles to find grace in the world.

title: The Dawn of Detroit: A Chronicle of Bondage and Freedom in the City of the Straits
author: Tiya Miles
description: A MacArthur genius grant winner and professor at the University of Michigan, Miles investigates Detroit's metropolitan history as a center of the Northern slave trade.

title: Greater Gotham: A History of New York City from 1898 to 1919
author: Mike Wallace
description: The follow-up to Wallace's Pulitzer Prize-winning history of New York, chronicling the swings of prosperity and downturn, from the 1898 skyscraper-driven boom to the Bankers' Panic of 1907, the labor upheaval, and violent repression during and after the First World War.

title: Go, Went, Gone
author: Jenny Erpenbeck, Trans. by Susan Bernofsky
description: Winner of Germany's Thomas Mann prize, a novel about a retired Berlin classics professor who becomes invested in the lives of a number of African refugees who are suffering under humanitarian and political bureaucracy.

title: Sleeping Beauties
author: Stephen King & Owen King
description: A horror/fantasy novel about a rural Appalachian town, whose primary employer is a women's prison, dealing with the global pandemic of sleeping sickness that has affected only women--with terrifying results.

title: Five-Carat Soul
author: James McBride
description: A debut collection of short stories from the National Book Award-winning author of The Good Lord Bird .

title: True Gentlemen: The Broken Pledge of America’s Fraternities
author: John Hechinger
description: An exposé by George Polk Award-winner Hechinger, of American fraternity life, revealing the vast gulf between its founding ideals and the realities of its impact on colleges and the world at large.

title: Don't Let Go
author: Harlan Coben
description: For fifteen years, Nap has been searching, both for Maura and for the real reason behind his brother's death. And now, it looks as though he may finally find what he's been looking for.

title: The Woman Who Smashed Codes: The True Story of Love, Spies, and the Unlikely Heroine Who Outwitted America's Enemies
author: Jason Fagone
description: The true story of the greatest codebreaking duo that ever lived, an American woman and her husband who invented the modern science of cryptology together and used it to confront the evils of their time.

title: Bunny Mellon: The Life of an American Style Legend
author: Meryl Gordon
description: A new biography of Bunny Mellon, the style icon and American aristocrat who designed the White House Rose Garden for her friend JFK and served as a living witness to 20th Century American history

title: The Last Castle: The Epic Story of Love, Loss, and American Royalty in the Nation's Largest Home
author: Denise Kiernan
description: The true story behind the magnificent Gilded Age mansion Biltmore—the largest, grandest residence ever built in the United States.

title: After the Eclipse: A Mother's Murder, a Daughter's Search
author: Sarah Perry
description: A memoir of a mother’s murder, a daughter’s coming-of-age in the wake of immense loss, and her mission to know the woman who gave her life.

title: Provenance
author: Ann Leckie
description: From the author of the Hugo, Nebula, and Arthur C. Clarke Award-winning novel Ancillary Justice , a cosy space opera set in the same universe about a young woman who, seeking the approval of her foster mother, takes a desperate gamble and finds herself in the middle of an interplanetary conspiracy.

title: Difficult Women: A Memoir of Three
author: David Plante
description: A reprint of David Plante’s polarizing memoir of his friendships with three influential women in the literary world: Jean Rhys, Sonia Orwell, and Germaine Greer.

title: Gorilla and the Bird: A Memoir of Madness and a Mother's Love
author: Zack McDermott
description: A tale of madness and self-destruction, a social justice lawyer details his battle with bipolar disorder and how his mother's stalwart presence furthered his recovery.

title: Fast Falls the Night
author: Julia Keller
description: In the sixth book of Julia Keller's Bill Elkins series, Prosecutor Bill Elkins searches for the drug source that's causing the heroin epidemic in his Appalachian hometown.

title: The Ninth Hour
author: Alice McDermott
description: From National Book Award-winner McDermott, a novel spanning the twentieth century of a widow and her daughter and the nuns who serve their Irish-American community in Brooklyn.

title: Reset: My Fight for Inclusion and Lasting Change
author: Ellen Pao
description: A memoir by a former chief of staff and junior partner at a tech venture capital firm who sued her company for gender discrimination in 2012.

title: The Good People
author: Hannah Kent
description: From the author of Burial Rites , a novel based on true events in early nineteenth century Ireland, about three women drawn together to rescue a disabled child from a superstitious community.

title: Alone: Britain, Churchill, and Dunkirk: Defeat Into Victory
author: Michael Korda
description: Combining epic history with family stories, Michael Korda chronicles the outbreak of World War Two and the great events that led to Dunkirk.

title: Thanks, Obama: My Hopey, Changey White House Years
author: David Litt
description: A comic, coming-of-age memoir by former Obama speechwriter Litt about his time working for the president.

title: Murderous Mistral: A Provence Mystery
author: Cay Rademacher, Trans. by Peter Millar
description: In International Dagger Award–shortlisted author Cay Rademacher's novel, Capitaine Roger Blanc travels from Paris to Provence to solve a chain of murders in this French countryside city.

title: This Blessed Earth
author: Ted Genoways
description: Following a Nebraska farmer and his family over the course of a year, Genoways examines the obstacles farmers face today, including climate change, dwindling underground water supplies, oil and gas pipeline encroachment, market price fluctuations and the always unpredictable weather.

title: The Cuban Affair
author: Nelson DeMille
description: From the author of Plum Island and Nightfall comes this new novel of a U.S. Army combat veteran about to set sail on a life-or-death cruise mission while the “Cuban Thaw” is underway between Havana and Washington.

title: Nomadland
author: Jessica Bruder
description: A book of immersive, investigative journalism about low-income Americans eking out a living while driving from locale to locale for seasonal employment.

title: One Nation After Trump: A Guide for the Perplexed, the Disillusioned, the Desperate, and the Not-Yet Deported
author: E.J. Dionne Jr. & Norman J. Ornstein & Thomas E. Mann
description: A call to action from three of Washington's premier political scholar-journalists, One Nation After Trump explains the threat posed by the Trump presidency and offers solutions for how to counter it.

title: The Man from the Train
author: Bill James & Rachel McCarthy James
description: Father-daughter duo Bill James and Rachel McCarthy James dive into historical records to crack an unsolved century-old mystery surrounding one of the deadliest serial killers in American history.

title: Swallowing Mercury
author: Wioletta Greg, Trans. by Eliza Marciniak
description: In the debut novel from poet Wioletta Greg, Wiola looks back on her youth in a close-knit, agricultural community in 1980s Poland.

title: A First-Class Catastrophe: The Road to Black Monday, the Worst Day in Wall Street History
author: Diana B. Henriques
description: From the author of The Wizard of Lies comes a thorough account of the crash of 1987 and a cautionary tale of how the U.S. financial system nearly collapsed.

title: Landslide: True Stories
author: Minna Proctor
description: A collection of interconnected personal essays which explore the author’s complicated relationship with her mother—who was diagnosed with cancer at age fifty-seven and died fifteen years later—and the ways in which their connection was long the “prime mover” of Proctor’s life, the subtle force coursing beneath her adulthood.

title: Haunted
author: James Patterson & James O. Born
description: The latest installment in James Patterson's Detective Michael Bennet thriller series.

title: The Origin of Others
author: Toni Morrison, foreword by Ta-Nehisi Coates
description: What is race and why does it matter? Why does the presence of Others make us so afraid? America's foremost novelist reflects on themes that preoccupy her work and dominate politics: race, fear, borders, mass movement of peoples, desire for belonging.

title: Forest Dark
author: Nicole Krauss
description: From the author of The History of Love , a cerebral novel set in present-day Israel in which two visiting Jewish Americans—one a young wife, mother, and novelist, the other an elderly philanthropist—experience transcendence.

title: What Happened
author: Hillary Rodham Clinton
description: A political memoir in which Hillary Rodham Clinton reveals what she was thinking and feeling during one of the most controversial and unpredictable presidential elections in history.

title: The Girl Who Takes an Eye for an Eye
author: David Lagercrantz
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: The latest novel in the Lisbeth Salander Millennium series (taken over by David Largercrantz after Stieg Larsson's death), in which our heroine finds herself serving a two-month sentence in Flodberga, the only maximum security women’s prison in Sweden.

title: An Odyssey: A Father, a Son, and an Epic
author: Daniel Mendelsohn
description: An account of the lessons learned by a son and his father—the younger a Classics professor, the elder deciding, at the age of 81, to sit in on his son's University seminar—as they study the Greek epic together.

title: Letters to Memory
author: Karen Tei Yamashita
description: An experimental history of the author's family made up of a patchwork of documents, photographs, and letters sent during the World War II Japanese internment camps in the United States.

title: A Column of Fire
author: Ken Follett
description: The third historical novel set around the fictional city of Kingsbridge from the author of The Pillars of the Earth and World Without End . In 1558, the ancient stones of Kingsbridge Cathedral look down on a city torn apart by religious conflict. As power in England shifts precariously between Catholics and Protestants, royalty and commoners clash, testing friendship, loyalty, and love.

title: Ranger Games
author: Ben Blum
