description: A true crime investigation of why the author's cousin—a straight-laced young man in an elite Army Ranger battalion—chose to follow the guidance of a sociopathic superior officer and become the getaway driver in an armed robbery of a Tacoma bank.

title: Afterglow (a dog memoir)
author: Eileen Myles
description: From the trailblazing New York poet and writer, an experimental, kaleidoscopic portrait of a beloved confidant: the pit bull called Rosie.

title: Unstoppable: My Life So Far
author: Maria Sharapova
description: A memoir from professional tennis player Maria Sharapova about her immigration saga, introduction to the sport, rivalry with Serena Williams, and recent ban for testing positive for an outlawed substance.

title: The Rise and Fall of Adam and Eve
author: Stephen Greenblatt
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author and Harvard professor, an examination of the enduring appeal and manifold interpretations of the biblical story of Adam and Eve.

title: Bluebird, Bluebird
author: Attica Locke
description: A southern noir thriller about the collision of race and justice in small town America. When a racially-motivated double murder stirs up a hornet's nest of tension in the desolate town of Lark, TX (pop. 178), a black Texas ranger is called upon to investigate.

title: World Without Mind: The Existential Threat of Big Tech
author: Franklin Foer
description: From the former Editor-in-Chief of The New Republic , a scathing critique of Big Tech culture, breaking down the collective history and impact of giant corporations such as Amazon, Facebook, and Google.

title: Solar Bones
author: Mike McCormack
description: Winner of the Goldsmiths Prize and the Irish Book Awards Novel of the Year, a novel told through the stream-of-conscious recollections of a middle-aged engineer from the west of Ireland briefly returned from the dead on All Soul’s Day, November 2008.

title: The Internationalists: How a Radical Plan to Outlaw War Remade the World
author: Oona A. Hathaway and Scott J. Shapiro
description: Two Yale scholars adopt a fundamentally revisionist perspective on the oft-dismissed Kellogg-Briand Peace Pact of 1928, positing that the agreement “marked the beginning of the end” of war between states.

title: A Loving, Faithful Animal
author: Josephine Rowe
description: A debut novel by the winner of the 2016 Elizabeth Jolley Prize. Set in rural Australia in 1990, a portrait of the splintering of a family whose patriarch is haunted by his experiences in Vietnam.

title: The Impossible Presidency: The Rise and Fall of America's Highest Office
author: Jeremi Suri
description: A history of the American presidency, arguing that the successful presidents of the past created unrealistic expectations for every president since JFK, with enormously problematic implications for American politics.

title: The Twelve-Mile Straight
author: Eleanor Henderson
description: A dark, historical novel that delves into the fractures of race, class, and family in rural Georgia. In a house full of secrets, two babies-one light-skinned, the other dark-are born to Elma Jesup, a white sharecropper’s daughter. Accused of her rape, field hand Genus Jackson is lynched and dragged. In the aftermath, the farm’s inhabitants are forced to contend with their complicity in a series of events that left a man dead and a family irrevocably fractured.

title: Devotion (Why I Write)
author: Patti Smith
description: From the renowned musician and author Patti Smith, a slim exploration of the nature of creative invention in the form of a novella bookended by by a pair of personal reflections. Part of the "Why I Write" series, based on the Windham-Campbell lectures delivered annually at Yale University.

title: Unbelievable
author: Katy Tur
description: A personal take on the two bizarre years NBC journalist Katy Tur spent covering the Donald Trump campaign, during which time she was frequently singled out by Trump in his attacks on the media.

title: For Two Thousand Years
author: Mihail Sebastian, Trans. by Philip Ó Ceallaigh
description: First published in Romania in 1934, a new translation of a Romanian Jewish man's fictional diary as he grows isolated in the interwar years, caught between anti-Semitism and Zionism.

title: David Bowie: A Life
author: Dylan Jones
description: An oral biography of the late musical icon, drawn from nearly 200 interviews with Bowie's friends,

title: Istanbul: A Tale of Three Cities
author: Bettany Hughes
description: Beginning in prehistory, Bettany Hughes researches Istanbul's historical and cultural evolution from Byzantium to Constantinople to Istanbul.

title: Bloodlines: The True Story of a Drug Cartel, the FBI, and the Battle for a Horse-Racing Dynasty
author: Melissa del Bosque
description: In her first book, award-winning journalist Melissa del Bosque investigates how two FBI agents work to take down members of a drug cartel wrapped up with quarter horse racing in Texas.

title: Why Write? Collected Nonfiction 1960-2013
author: Philip Roth
description: A collection of Philip Roth’s essential statements on literature, his novels, and the writing life.

title: Ordinary Beast: Poems
author: Nicole Sealey
description: Nicole Sealey's poems explore notions of race, sexuality, gender, myth, history, and embodiment.

title: Storming the Wall: Climate Change, Migration, and Homeland Security
author: Todd Miller
description: Fast-paced frontline reportage chronicling how climate change is accelerating migration, border build-up, and militarization in the US and beyond. Recipient of the 2018 Izzy Award for Excellence in Investigative Journalism.

title: Calling a Wolf a Wolf
author: Kaveh Akbar
description: This 2017 Foreword INDIES Book of the Year and winner of many other awards recounts the poet's battle with alcoholism and sobriety, and the questioning of the self and its instincts within the context of this never-ending fight.

title: Little Fires Everywhere
author: Celeste Ng
description: A novel set in an Cleveland suburb in the late 1990s that traces the intertwined fates of the picture-perfect Richardson family and the enigmatic mother and daughter who upend their lives when they move to town.

title: Sing, Unburied, Sing
author: Jesmyn Ward
description: Winner of the 2017 National Book Award for Fiction. From the 2011 National Book Award-winning author of Salvage the Bones , an intimate, mystical portrait of racial tensions in the modern-day American South focusing on a few days the lives of a fractured Mississippi Gulf Coast family and the histories and ghosts that haunt it.

title: A Legacy of Spies
author: John Le Carré
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: The iconic spy writer, author of The Spy Who Came in From the Cold and Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy , returns to the world of George Smiley for the first time in more than twenty-five years, this time focusing on Smiley's former protégé, who is summoned to London to answer questions about a Cold War mission gone wrong.

title: The Golden House
author: Salman Rushdie
description: A sprawling portrait of the current American climate, spanning the years from the Obama inauguration to the current political moment. The Golden House focuses on a mysterious billionaire and his three adult sons who change their names and move to New York City in an attempt to reinvent themselves after tragedy.

title: Cuz: The Life and Times of Michael A.
author: Danielle S. Allen
description: A memoir in which Harvard professor and author Allen illuminates the path that led to her cousin Michael’s incarceration at age 15 and to his murder at 29, less than a year after his release.

title: Dinner at the Center of the Earth
author: Nathan Englander
description: From the author of What We Talk About When We Talk About Anne Frank . Part absurdist farce, part romance, part political thriller that unfolds in the highly charged territory of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, focusing on the complex relationship between a secret prisoner and his guard.

title: The World of Tomorrow
author: Brendan Mathews
description: A sprawling historical novel about three Irish brothers (on the run from the IRA) and their mad-cap adventures in New York during the week of the World's Fair in 1939.

title: Sourdough
author: Robin Sloan
description: From the author of Mr. Penumbra’s 24-Hour Bookstore , a novel about a software engineer at a soulless San Francisco robotics company who inherits a very special type of sourdough starter culture that opens up a whole new world for her.

title: Tales of Two Americas: Stories of Inequality in a Divided Nation
author: Ed. by John Freeman
description: A collection of short fiction, essays, narrative journalism and poetry, through which thirty-six major contemporary writers examine life in a deeply divided America—including Anthony Doerr, Ann Patchett, Roxane Gay, Rebecca Solnit, Hector Tobar, Joyce Carol Oates, Edwidge Danticat, Richard Russo, Eula Bliss, Karen Russell, and more.

title: A Disappearance in Damascus
author: Deborah Campbell
description: Winner of the Hilary Weston Writers’ Trust Prize for Nonfiction. A Canadian journalist covering the plight of Iraqis who fled to Syria a decade ago enlists the help of an Iraqi woman in Damascus, only for the woman to be arrested and disappeared.

title: At the Strangers' Gate
author: Adam Gopnik
description: A longtime New Yorker contributor writes about his early years in the city—the 1980s principally—ruminating about art and artists, love and apartments, writing and reading and speaking, and the city that he loves.

title: Draft No. 4: On the Writing Process
author: John McPhee
description: A series of playful essays that serve as a guide to writing long-form nonfiction, by the legendary author, teacher and New Yorker contributor John McPhee.

title: Fantasyland: How America Went Haywire
author: Kurt Andersen
description: A sweeping history of America in which Andersen argues that what’s happening in our country today—this post-factual, 'fake news' moment we’re all living through—is not something new, but rather the ultimate expression of our national character.

title: Gorbachev: His Life and Times
author: William Taubman
description: A biography of the transformational world leader by the Pulitzer Prize–winning author of Khrushchev .

title: Liner Notes
author: Loudon Wainwright III
description: In this memoir, musician and actor Wainwright details the family history his lyrics have referenced and the fractured relationships among generations: the alcoholism, the infidelities, the competitiveness—as well as the closeness, the successes, and the joy.

title: Coming to My Senses: The Making of a Counterculture Cook
author: Alice Waters
description: A memoir from veteran chef and restaurateur Alice Waters, taking the reader from Waters’ childhood in suburban New Jersey to her travels in Europe, to her time in Berkeley, culminating with the opening night of Chez Panisse in 1971.

title: The Vietnam War: An Intimate History
author: Geoffrey C. Ward and Ken Burns
description: A illustrated, collaborative history of the Vietnam War and its various impacts—the companion volume to Ken Burns' 2017 multipart PBS documentary.

title: Mayhem: A Memoir
author: Sigrid Rausing
description: A searing memoir about how the author watched the horrific toll drug addiction took on her brother, the heir to the Tetra Park fortune, and his wife despite their wealth and privilege.

title: Don't Call Us Dead
author: Danez Smith
description: A visceral collection of poetry from Lambda Literary Award-winner Smith, contemplating the assaults on the black, male body in America?police brutality, violence, and AIDS.

title: Sisters
author: Lily Tuck
description: A short, psychological novel from National Book Award-winner Tuck about the inner life of a woman obsessed with her husband’s first wife.

title: Blurred Lines: Rethinking Sex, Power, and Consent on Campus
author: Vanessa Grigoriadis
description: National Magazine Award–winning journalist Grigoriadis explores sexual assault, rape culture, and sexual politics at American universities, arguing that the issue is murkier than previously presented.

title: The Riviera Set
author: Mary S. Lovell
description: The Riviera Set reveals the story of the group of people who lived, partied, bed-hopped and politicked at the Château de l'Horizon near Cannes, over the course of forty years from the time when Coco Chanel made southern French tans fashionable in the twenties to the death of the playboy Prince Aly Khan in 1960.

title: Border: A Journey to the Edge of Europe
author: Kapka Kassabova
description: A lyrical travelogue which explores the spiritual, psychological, and emotional qualities of the area around the shared frontiers of Turkey, Greece, and Bulgaria.

title: The Witch: A History of Fear, from Ancient Times to the Present
author: Ronald Hutton
description: Why have societies all across the world feared witchcraft? This book delves deeply into its context, beliefs, and origins in Europe’s history.

title: The Child Finder
author: Rene Denfeld
description: Naomi was once a lost girl, and now she is an investigator who must use her unique insights to find a missing little girl.

title: The Unfinished Palazzo: Life, Love and Art in Venice
author: Judith Mackrell
description: The Guardian dance critic Judith Mackrell connects the lives of three unique 20th-century women: Luisa Casati, Doris Castlerosse, and Peggy Guggenheim.

title: A Thirst for Empire: How Tea Shaped the Modern World
author: Erika Rappaport
description: An expansive history of how the global tea industry influenced the international economy and the rise of mass consumerism.

title: George & Lizzie
author: Nancy Pearl
description: George and Lizzie is an intimate story of new and past loves, the scars of childhood, and an imperfect marriage at its defining moments.

title: Secrets in Death: An Eve Dallas Novel
author: J. D. Robb
description: The latest installment of Robb's In Death mystery series, set in near-future New York, where Lt. Eve Dallas must separate rumors from reality when a woman who traffics in other people’s secrets is silenced.

title: The Taking of K-129: How the CIA Used Howard Hughes to Steal a Russian Sub in the Most Daring Covert Operation in History
author: Josh Dean
description: The tale of how the CIA, the U.S. Navy, and America’s most eccentric mogul worked to steal the nuclear-armed Soviet submarine K-129 from the bottom of the Pacific Ocean.

title: Being Mortal
author: Atul Gawande
description: Medicine has triumphed in modern times. But when it comes to the inescapable realities of aging and death, what medicine can do often runs counter to what it should. Through eye-opening research and gripping stories of his own patients and family, Atul Gawande, a practicing surgeon, reveals the suffering this dynamic has produced.

title: The Republic for Which It Stands: The United States during Reconstruction and the Gilded Age, 1865-1896
author: Richard White
description: From the Oxford History of the United States series, an examination of Reconstruction and the Gilded Age as the seedbed of modern America.

title: The Burning Girl
author: Claire Messud
description: From the author of The Woman Upstairs , a novel about the fraught nature of adolescent female friendship, focusing on two teenage girls who grow up and grow apart in a small Massachusetts town.

title: My Absolute Darling
author: Gabriel Tallent
description: A harrowing debut novel set in the woods of Northern California in which a 14-year-old girl struggles to escape her father’s emotional and physical abuse.

title: I’ll Have What She’s Having: How Nora Ephron’s Three Iconic Films Saved the Romantic Comedy
author: Erin Carlson
description: A backstage look at the making of Nora Ephron's revered trilogy— When Harry Met Sally , You've Got Mail , and Sleepless in Seattle —which brought romantic comedies back to the fore.

title: All the Dirty Parts
author: Daniel Handler
description: From the author of the Series of Unfortunate Events series, a novel about a promiscuous and perpetually horny teenage boy whose quest to have sex with as many girls as possible is complicated by the changing relationship with his gay best friend, and the arrival of a vivacious young woman who challenges his double standards.

title: Life 3.0: Being Human in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
author: Max Tegmark
description: How will Artificial Intelligence affect crime, war, justice, jobs, society and our very sense of being human? The founder of the Future of Life Institute explores one of the most intriguing scientific frontiers, artificial general intelligence, and how humans can grow along with it.

title: The Resurrection of Joan Ashby
author: Cherise Wolas
description: When Joan finds herself unexpectedly pregnant, she is stunned by her husband's delight, his instant betrayal of their pact. She makes a fateful, selfless decision then, to embrace her unintentional family.

title: Autumn
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard, Trans. by Ingvild Burkey
description: Taking the form of a letter to his unborn daughter, the first book in an new autobiographical quartet based on the four seasons from the author of the My Struggle series.

title: The Red-Haired Woman
author: Orhan Pamuk, Trans. by Ekin Oklap
description: From the Nobel Prize-winning author of Snow and My Name Is Red , a fable of fathers and sons and the desires that come between them.

title: Stay With Me
author: Ayobami Adebayo
description: A debut novel exploring the intense pressure to have children on one couple across two decades, set against the backdrop of the politically tumultuous 1980s and 90s in Nigeria.

title: The House of Government
author: Yuri Slezkine
description: The story of the Russian revolution and its aftermath told through the activities and individual stories of the inhabitants of the House of Government, Europe’s largest residential building.

title: Montpelier Parade
author: Karl Geary
description: A debut novel set in 1980s Dublin about an unconventional love affair between a lonely, working class teenage boy and a glamorous but troubled older woman.

title: Midwinter Break
author: Bernard MacLaverty
description: From the author of Cal , a quiet novel about an elderly Northern Irish couple, their marriage in crisis, who take a winter trip to Amsterdam.

title: Eastman Was Here
author: Alex Gilvarry
description: A satirical novel, set in New York and Saigon in 1973, about a Norman Mailer-esque literary lion, his fame faded, who accepts an assignment covering the last days of the Vietnam war in an attempt to revive his respectability as a writer and win back his wife.

title: Freud: The Making of an Illusion
author: Frederick Crews
description: A debunking of the legend of Sigmund Freud, focusing on Freud’s early career, from 1884 to 1900.

title: Sargent's Women
author: Donna M. Lucey
description: A biography, based on original letters and diaries, illuminating four extraordinary women painted by the iconic Gilded Age high-society portraitist John Singer Sargent.

title: Young Jane Young
author: Gabrielle Zevin
description: A novel that looks at the fallout from a Monica Lewinsky-esque political sex scandal between a young intern and a married Florida congressman through five different perspectives.

title: The Heart's Invisible Furies
author: John Boyne
description: From the author of The Boy In the Striped Pajamas , a sweeping portrait of one man’s life over the course of 70 years, revealing the personal and societal toll of Ireland’s repression of homosexuality.

title: The History of Bees
author: Maja Lunde
description: A "Cli-Fi" novel following three generations of beekeepers from the past, present, and future (a 19th-century British biologist, a millennial-era American beekeeper and a Chinese hand-pollinator on the cusp of a dystopian 22nd century) weaving a story of their relationship to the bees—and to their children and one another—against the backdrop of an urgent, global crisis.

title: The Saboteur
author: Andrew Gross
description: In 1943 Norway, Kurt Nordstrum and his team of patriotic fighters must pull off the impossible in order to disrupt activity at a Nazi atomic research factory.

title: The Shadow in the Garden: A Biographer's Tale
author: James Atlas
description: A literary critic, magazine editor, memoirist, novelist, and founder of the Lippert/Viking Penguin Lives series of biographies, Atlas, who has penned acclaimed and controversial biographies of Saul Bellow and Delmore Schwartz, digs deep into his own psyche to explain why he became attracted to the craft of biography

title: Letters to His Neighbor
author: Marcel Proust, Trans. by Lydia Davis
description: Recently discovered letters from Proust to a Paris neighbor show the author’s kindness even when he complained about the noise.

title: Against the Grain: A Deep History of the Earliest States
author: James C. Scott
description: James C. Scott's written account studies how first agrarian states were born of accumulations of domestications as a way of gaining control of reproduction, which contradicts the standard narrative about earliest civilizations.

title: Stay with Me
author: Ayobami Adebayo
description: Ever since they first met and fell in love at university, Yejide and Akin have agreed: polygamy is not for them. But four years into their marriage—after consulting fertility doctors and healers, and trying strange teas and unlikely cures—Yejide is still not pregnant. She assumes she still has time—until her in-laws arrive on her doorstep with a young woman they introduce as Akin’s second wife. Furious, shocked, and livid with jealousy, Yejide knows the only way to save her marriage is to get pregnant. Which, finally, she does—but at a cost far greater than she could have dared to imagine. Shortlisted for the 2017 Baileys Women’s Prize for Fiction.

title: After Kathy Acker
author: Chris Kraus
description: A biography, from the author of I Love Dick , of the late experimental novelist, punk poet, playwright, essayist, postmodernist and sex-positive feminist writer Kathy Acker.

title: Home Fire
author: Kamila Shamsie
description: A reimagining of Antigone set in contemporary London, focusing on two Muslim families whose lives are entangled by politics and conflict.

title: Poetry Will Save Your Life
author: Jill Bialosky
description: From Norton executive editor Bialosky, a coming-of-age memoir organized around forty-three remarkable poems by poets such as Robert Frost, Emily Dickinson, Wallace Stevens and Sylvia Plath.

title: The World Broke in Two
author: Bill Goldstein
description: The story of the intersecting lives and works of revered authors Virginia Woolf, T. S. Eliot, E. M. Forster and D. H. Lawrence during 1922, the birth year of modernism.

title: The Mountain
author: Paul Yoon
description: A collection of short stories set throughout the world—from the Hudson Valley to the Russian Far East—across periods of time after World War II.

title: Why Poetry
author: Matthew Zapruder
description: A call for a return to reading poetry and an argument for poetry’s accessibility to all readers, weaving personal anecdote with literary analysis to argue for poetry’s necessity.

title: Wild Things: The Joy of Reading Children’s Literature as an Adult
author: Bruce Handy
description: A nostalgic ramble through classic children’s literature, from fairy tales to The Very Hungry Caterpillar , exploring the tales themselves and the backstories of their creators.

title: The Stone Sky
author: N. K. Jemisin
description: Winner of the 2018 Hugo Award for best science-fiction novel, the concluding volume in Jemisin's post-apocalyptic Broken Earth fantasy trilogy.

title: Notes on a Foreign Country
author: Suzy Hansen
description: A non fiction book blending history, memoir, and political analysis. After moving to Turkey in 2007, journalist Hansen questions the notion of American exceptionalism.

title: The Once and Future Liberal: After Identity Politics
author: Mark Lilla
description: A Columbia University Humanities professor argues that liberals and progressives have become so preoccupied with individual identities that they have failed to formulate and express any vision for what ought to bind the nation together.

title: Ghost of the Innocent Man: A True Story of Trial and Redemption
author: Benjamin Rachlin
description: During the last two decades, more than two thousand American citizens have been wrongfully convicted. Ghost of the Innocent Man brings us one of the most dramatic of those cases and provides a picture of the national scourge of wrongful conviction and of the opportunity for meaningful reform.

title: Good Booty: Love and Sex, Black and White, Body and Soul in American Music
author: Ann Powers
description: A sweeping history of popular music in the United States examining how popular music shapes fundamental American ideas and beliefs, allowing us to communicate difficult emotions and truths about our most fraught social issues, most notably sex and race.

title: Hail to the Chin: Further Confessions of a B Movie Actor
author: Bruce Campbell and Craig Sanborn
description: The anecdotal sequel to cult B-movie actor Bruce Campbell's bestselling memoir.

title: A Kind of Freedom
author: Margaret Wilkerson Sexton
description: A multigenerational exploration of systemic racism in America focusing on a black family in New Orleans from the 1940s onwards.

title: Half-light: Collected Poems 1965-2016
author: Frank Bidart
description: Winner of the 2017 National Book Award for Poetry. The collected poems of three time Pulitzer Prize-finalist Frank Bidart.

title: The People Are Going to Rise Like the Waters Upon Your Shore
author: Jared Yates Sexton
description: An impressionistic firsthand account of the events that shaped the 2016 presidential election and the cultural forces that divided both parties and powered Donald Trump into the White House.

title: I Know a Secret: A Rizzoli & Isles Novel
author: Tess Gerritsen
description: Two separate homicides, at different locations, with unrelated victims, have more in common than just being investigated by Boston PD detective Jane Rizzoli and medical examiner Maura Isles. In both cases, the bodies bear startling wounds—yet the actual cause of death is unknown.

title: The Locals
author: Jonathan Dee
description: From the author of The Privileges , the residents of a small, struggling community in the Berkshires have their world overturned by a billionaire who, in the wake of the 9/11 attacks, moves to town and is elected mayor.

title: Stanton: Lincoln’s War Secretary
author: Walter Stahr
description: A biography of Abraham Lincoln’s indispensable but controversial Secretary of War, Edwin Stanton, the man the president entrusted with raising the army that preserved the Union.

title: The Misfortune of Marion Palm
author: Emily Culliton
description: A debut novel about a Brooklyn Heights wife and mother who has embezzled a small fortune from her children's private school and makes a run for it, leaving behind her trust fund poet husband, his maybe-secret lover, her two daughters, and a school board who will do anything to find her.

title: The Great Quake
author: Henry Fountain
description: A non fiction account of the biggest earthquake in North American recorded history — the 1964 Alaska earthquake that demolished the city of Valdez and swept away the island village of Chenega — and the geologist who hunted for clues to explain how and why it took place.

title: The Kelloggs: The Battling Brothers of Battle Creek
author: Howard Markel
description: The saga of brothers John and Will Kellogg, whose lifelong competition and enmity toward one another changed America’s notion of health and wellness from the mid-nineteenth to the mid-twentieth centuries.

title: The Good Daughter
author: Karin Slaughter
description: A violent psychological thriller about two sisters, reunited by a school shooting having grown apart in the wake of a terrifying home invasion twenty-eight years previous that left their mother dead.

title: Life in Code: A Personal History of Technology
author: Ellen Ullman
description: A politically charged memoir of life in the data trenches by computer pioneer Ullman, author of the cult insider account of the digital revolution, Close to the Machine .

title: The Bettencourt Affair: The World's Richest Woman and the Scandal That Rocked Paris
author: Tom Sancton
description: A chronicle of the nearly decade-long scandals and legal drama surrounding world's richest woman Liliane Bettencourt and the uber-wealthy family behind the L’Oréal empire.

title: Why Buddhism is True: The Science and Philosophy of Meditation and Enlightenment
author: Robert Wright
description: A journey through psychology, philosophy, and a great many silent retreats to show how and why meditation can serve as the foundation for a spiritual life in a secular age.

title: The Book of Emma Reyes
author: Emma Reyes, trans. Daniel Alarcón
description: A memoir of a painter Emma Reyes' harrowing childhood in Bogotá, comprised of letters written over the course of 30 years and hailed as an instant classic when first published in Colombia in 2012, nearly a decade after the death of its author.

title: Warner Bros: The Making of an American Movie Studio
author: David Thomson
description: From film historian Thomson, a look behind the scenes at the legendary Warner Brothers film studio, where four immigrant brothers transformed themselves into the moguls and masters of American fantasy. Part of Yale University Press' Jewish Lives series.

title: Zapped: From Infrared to X-rays, the Curious History of Invisible Light
author: Bob Berman
description: Science writer Bob Berman tells the story of all the light we cannot see, from its historical, cultural, and technological significances to modern society.

title: Surfing with Satre
author: Aaron James
description: In this meditation between philosophy and surfing, Aaron James explores epistemology, metaphysics, and ethics.

title: You Can Do Anything: The Surprising Power of a "Useless" Liberal Arts Education
author: George Anders
description: Forbes contributor George Anders argues the usefulness of a major in the liberal arts.

title: Mrs. Fletcher
author: Tom Perrotta
description: From the author of Little Children and The Leftovers . A sexual comedy of errors focusing on a suburban woman who, when her casually misogynistic son goes off to college, develops a fixation with online porn that spills out perilously into her real life.

title: The Seventh Function of Language
author: Laurent Binet, Trans. by Sam Taylor
description: From the author of HhHH , a madcap, irreverent French theory/detective story mash-up that’s part mystery and part satire, turning Roland Barthes’s accidental death in 1980 into a murder investigation set against French intellectual life.

title: New People
author: Danzy Senna
description: A darkly comic novel about race and identity set in Brooklyn in the mid-1990s. Seemingly perfect 27-year-old Maria and her college sweetheart Khalil, both mixed-race, are planning their wedding. They’re also the stars of a new documentary about interracial couples. When Maria develops a fixation with a mysterious black poet, things begin to unravel.

title: Sour Heart
author: Jenny Zhang
description: A debut story collection that, in seven loosely-connected tales, conjures the experience of adolescence through the eyes of Chinese American girls growing up in New York City.

title: See What I Have Done
author: Sarah Schmidt
description: A dark, claustrophobic reimagining of the Lizzie Borden story: one of the most infamous murder cases in American history.

title: Conscience of a Conservative
author: Jeff Flake
description: Republican Senator Jeff Flake takes his party to task for embracing nationalism, populism, xenophobia, and the anomalous Trump presidency.

title: Beast
author: Paul Kingsnorth
description: From the author of The Wake , a novel about Edward Buckmaster, a man alone on an empty moor in the west of England. What he has left behind we don’t yet know. What he faces is an existential battle with himself, the elements, and something he begins to see in the margins of his vision: some creature that is tracking him, the pursuit of which will become an obsession.

title: The Blinds
author: Adam Sternbergh
description: A hybrid of crime, western, and science fiction genres set in a tiny hardscrabble town in Texas where all inhabitants have had their memories erased, owing to the fact that in a past life they were either witnesses to, or perpetrators of, unspeakable crimes.

title: Morningstar
author: Ann Hood
description: Novelist and short story writer Hood chronicles her life through the books that shaped her.

title: From Holmes to Sherlock
author: Mattias Boström
description: Swedish author and Sherlock Holmes expert Mattias Boström recreates the full story behind the legend, analyzing the work of "the men and women who created an icon," from a young Arthur Conan Doyle taking notes on his medical professor's powers of observation to the people behind the modern-day TV sensation Sherlock .

title: The Grip of It
author: Jac Jemc
description: A literary horror novel about a young couple, their marriage in trouble due to the husband's gambling addiction, who are haunted by their newly purchased home.

title: Happiness: A Memoir
author: Heather Harpham
description: A memoir from playwright Harpham about parenting her sick child, Gracie, and navigating her complex feelings toward Gracie's father.

title: A Boy in Winter
author: Rachel Seiffert
description: A portrait of the experiences of several characters in a small Ukrainian town on the day the Nazi troops arrive to round up the Jews in November, 1941.

title: The Dark Net
author: Benjamin Percy
description: A techno-horror thriller in which a small band of misfits must counteract a full-scale digital demon possession of a near-future Portland.

title: Safe
author: Ryan Gattis
description: A crime novel set in Los Angeles in 2008 in which a safecracker and recovering drug addict, haunted by the memory of his dead girlfriend, tries to avoid a gang of drug dealers long enough to make one last score.

title: The Half-Drowned King
author: Linnea Hartsuyker
description: The first volume in an historical trilogy about the blood-soaked Viking warriors of ninth-century Norway.

title: Vengeance Is Mine, All Others Pay Cash
author: Eka Kurniawan, Trans. by Annie Tucker
description: A pulpy, visceral, darkly comic tale of sex, violence and comeuppance about an Indonesian teenager who, after witnessing a violent rape, is rendered impotent and grows up picking fights with strangers to release his frustration.

title: Birdcage Walk
author: Helen Dunmore
description: The final novel from Dunmore, who passed away in 2017, explores the impact of the French Revolution on 1790s England within the context of a gothic romance.

title: Brave Deeds
author: David Abrams
description: From the author of Fobbit , a novel set over a single afternoon following a squad of six AWOL soldiers as they attempt to cross war-torn Baghdad on foot to attend the funeral of their beloved platoon sergeant.

title: Are You Sleeping
author: Kathleen Barber
description: A psychological thriller about a mega-hit podcast that reopens a murder case and threatens to unravel the carefully constructed life of the victim’s daughter.

title: The Cooking Gene: A Journey Through African American Culinary History in the Old South
author: Michael W. Twitty
description: A memoir of Southern cuisine and food culture that traces the paths of the author's ancestors (black and white) through the crucible of slavery to show its effects on our food today. Winner of the 2018 James Beard Foundation's Book Of The Year Award.

title: The Unwomanly Face of War
author: Svetlana Alexievich, Trans. by Richard Pevear & Larissa Volokhonsky
description: An oral history of women in World War II across Europe and Russia—from the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature.

title: Madame Zero
author: Sarah Hall
description: A collection of dark, sensual, and disturbing short stories.

title: Fierce Kingdom
author: Gin Phillips
description: A thriller about a mother and her four-year-old son who, during an afternoon trip to the zoo, find themselves caught up in a mass shooting.

title: Gather the Daughters
author: Jennie Melamed
description: A dystopian novel set in an unspecified future about a patriarchal colony living on an island off the US, and the young woman who begin to resist the ancestor worship, controlled breeding, and strict rationing of knowledge and history that keeps them subjugated.

title: Sons and Soldiers
author: Bruce Henderson
description: The little-known saga of young German Jews, dubbed The Ritchie Boys, who fled Nazi Germany in the 1930s, came of age in America, and returned to Europe at enormous personal risk as members of the U.S. Army to fight against Nazism.

title: I Am the Brother of XX
author: Fleur Jaeggy, Trans. by Gini Alhadeff
description: A collection of dark, lyrical short stories of madness, loss, and murder, from Swiss-Italian writer Jaeggy, author of Sweet Days of Discipline .

title: The Lying Game
author: Ruth Ware
description: From the author of The Woman in Cabin 10 , a psychological thriller about four women, childhood friends from boarding school in England, who are brought back together when a terrible secret from their past resurfaces.

title: What She Ate: Six Remarkable Women and the Food That Tells Their Stories
author: Laura Shapiro
description: A culinary historian’s short takes on six famous women through the lens of food and cooking—what they ate and how their attitudes toward food offer surprising new insights into their lives.

title: Vanishing New York: How a Great City Lost Its Soul
author: Jeremiah Moss
description: A chronicle of gentrification in the twenty-first century and a love letter to lost New York by the creator of the blog Vanishing New York .

title: Careers for Women
author: Joanna Scott
description: A novel set across four decades about a group of women navigating professional life in the oppressive working world of the Fifties and Sixties under the mentorship of their supervisor, the famed Lee Jaffe of the Port Authority.

title: These Possible Lives
author: Fleur Jaeggy, trans. by Minna Zallman Proctor

title: The Epiphany Machine
author: David Burr Gerrard
description: An sprawling alternate history novel wherein a young man’s life is upended by a the existence of a mysterious device that purports to tattoo a description of your true self on your arm.

title: The Late Show
author: Michael Connelly
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: From the bestselling author of the Harry Bosch crime books comes the first novel in a new series focusing on Renée Ballard, a fierce young detective exiled to the night shift after filing a sexual-harassment charge against her boss and now fighting to prove herself on the LAPD's toughest beat.

title: Beautiful Animals
author: Lawrence Osborne
description: A psychological thriller set on a Greek island in which two young, affluent women--one older and amoral, the other more naive--find a Syrian migrant washed up on the shore and come up with an ill-advised plan to help him.

title: Devil's Bargain: Steve Bannon, Donald Trump, and the Storming of the Presidency
author: Joshua Green
description: The inside story of the partnership between Steve Bannon and Donald Trump—the key to understanding the rise of the alt-right, the fall of Hillary Clinton, and the hidden forces that drove the greatest upset in American political history.

title: Arbitrary Stupid Goal
author: Tamara Shopsin
description: A quirky, non-linear memoir about the author's unconventional upbringing in and around what was then her parents' old-fashioned corner grocery store/restaurant in Greenwich Village.

title: The Fallen
author: Ace Atkins
description: The seventh volume in Atkins' Quinn Colson crime series. Reluctantly back in the saddle as the sheriff of Tibbehah County, Mississippi, former Army ranger Colson goes up against a trio of bank robbers as cunning as they are clueless.

title: Less
author: Andrew Sean Greer
description: A comic novel from the author of The Confessions of Max Tivoli . Facing his erstwhile boyfriend’s wedding to another man, his 50th birthday, and his publisher’s rejection of his latest manuscript, a miserable midlist novelist decides to accept every literary invitation he's received and sets off around the world.

title: The Incest Diary
author: Anonymous
description: An anonymously written memoir about a woman who was violently and repeatedly raped by her father throughout her childhood and teenage years, and the effect that abuse had on her life thereafter.

title: Caesar's Last Breath: Decoding the Secrets of the Air Around Us
author: Sam Kean
description: An breezy and irreverent popular science book that runs through the periodic table, around the globe, and across time to tell the story of the air we breathe.

title: Ants Among Elephants: An Untouchable Family and the Making of Modern India
author: Sujatha Gidla
description: The true story of an untouchable family in India and their struggles with the country's discriminatory caste system.

title: Refuge
author: Dina Nayeri
description: A novel about the lifetime relationship between a father and a daughter, seen through the prism of global immigration and the contemporary refugee experience.

title: The Dark Dark
author: Samantha Hunt
description: A collection of stories that blends the literary and the fantastic and brings us characters on the verge?girls turning into women, women turning into deer, people doubling or becoming ghosts, and more.

title: Like a Fading Shadow
author: Antonio Muñoz Molina
description: Blurring fiction, memoir, and biography in a blending of two stories: James Earl Ray’s 10-day excursion to Lisbon while on the run after assassinating Martin Luther King Jr. in 1968, and the author’s own research trip to the same city in 1987 when writing his first novel.

title: Sex and Rage
author: Eve Babitz
description: The popular rediscovery of Eve Babitz continues with this reissue of her novel, originally published in 1979, about a dreamy young girl moving between the planets of Los Angeles and New York City.

title: Moving Kings
author: Joshua Cohen
description: A novel in which two young veterans of the last Gaza War come to Brooklyn to work for a cousin's moving company for a year. Moving Kings interweaves the housing crisis in America’s poor black and Hispanic neighborhoods with the world's oldest conflict, in the Middle East.

title: Bed-Stuy Is Burning
author: Brian Platzer
description: A novel set over the course of one day in the rapidly gentrifying Brooklyn neighborhood of Bed-Stuy, focusing on a disgraced former rabbi, now investment banker, and his family, who get caught up in the protests which erupt in the wake of a cop shooting a young black boy in a nearby park.

title: The Art of Death: Writing the Final Story
author: Edwidge Danticat
description: Part of Graywolf Press' "The Art Of" writing craft series. At once a personal account of Danticat's mother dying from cancer and a deeply considered reckoning with the ways that other writers have approached death in their own work.

title: American Fire: Love, Arson, and Life in a Vanishing Land
author: Monica Hesse
description: A true crime story about a bizarre spree that occurred in rural Accomack County, Va.: a series of over 80 arsons, of predominantly abandoned buildings, committed by a local couple.

title: What We Lose
author: Zinzi Clemmons
description: A poetic debut novel about a young, light-skinned African-American woman coming of age in Philadelphia, trying to connect the dislocated pieces of her life as her mother succumbs to cancer. A meditation on race, sex, family, and country.

title: The Sarah Book
author: Scott McClanahan
description: The Sarah Book is Scott McClanahan's continuation of the semi-autobiographical story he's been writing over the years about his life in West Virginia. This one is a raw portrait of the destruction of his marriage.

title: Goodbye, Vitamin
author: Rachel Khong
description: A debut comic drama novel about a woman who, having been broken up with by her fiancee, moves home to find her family struggling with her history professor father's recent Alzheimer's diagnosis.

title: Conversations With Friends
author: Sally Rooney
description: A novel set in contemporary Dublin about female friendship, lust, jealousy, and the unexpected complications of adulthood in the 21st century. Two young woman, former girlfriends but now just close friends, fall in with an enigmatic older couple.

title: The Great Nadar: The Man Behind the Camera
author: Adam Begley
description: A biography of the fabled 19th Century Parisian photographer, adventurer, and pioneer.

title: Roots, Radicals and Rockers: How Skiffle Changed the World
author: Billy Bragg
description: The first in-depth history of Skiffle––a music movement which originated in the U.K. in the mid-1950s and had its origins in American jazz, country, and R&B––from its origins in Britain’s postwar traditional jazz movement to its eventual eclipse by rock’n’roll.

title: Final Girls
author: Riley Sager
description: A debut psychological thriller. Quincy Carpenter became a Final Girl when she survived the massacre that killed five of her college friends. Years later, when another Final Girl commits suicide, Quincey is thrown back into the media spotlight and the cracks begin to appear in her carefully constructed new life.

title: Pages for Her
author: Sylvia Brownrigg
description: A novel about two women, Flannery and Anne, each at a personal turning point, and the circumstances that lead to their reunion, set twenty years after their brief but passionate affair, chronicled in Sylvia Brownrigg's earlier novel, Pages for You .

title: Jane Austen at Home
author: Lucy Worsley
description: A portrait of Jane Austen's world through the lens of the homes in which she lived and worked throughout her life.

title: When the English Fall
author: David Williams
description: A novel, told through the diary entries of a farmer, that questions whether a peaceful and nonviolent community can survive when civilization falls apart. When a catastrophic solar storm brings about the collapse of modern civilization, an Amish community in Pennsylvania is caught up in the devastating aftermath.

title: The Chickenshit Club: Why the Justice Department Fails to Prosecute Executives
author: Jesse Eisinger
description: From Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Jesse Eisinger, an account of corporate greed and impunity, and the reckless, often anemic response from the Department of Justice, that asks the question: Why were no bankers put in prison after the financial crisis of 2008?

title: So Much Things to Say: The Oral History of Bob Marley
author: Roger Steffens
description: An oral history of the legendary reggae singer, drawn from interviews with more than seventy-five friends, business managers, relatives and confidants?many speaking publicly for the first time.

title: Tropic of Kansas
author: Christopher Brown
description: A dystopian novel set in a contemporary America which is no more. Broken into warring territories, its center has become a wasteland DMZ known as 'the Tropic of Kansas.' Two travelers appear in this arid American wilderness: Sig, the fugitive orphan of political dissidents, and his foster sister Tania, a government investigator whose search for Sig leads her into her own past—and towards an unexpected future.

title: The Darkening Web: The War for Cyberspace
author: Alexander Klimburg
description: Cybersecurity strategist Klimburg examines why we underestimate the consequences of states’ ambitions to project power in cyberspace at our peril.

title: A Twenty Minute Silence Followed by Applause
author: Shawn Wen
description: An extended lyrical essay that paints a portrait of the iconic mime artist (and former French Resistance fighter) Marcel Marceau.

title: Among the Living and the Dead
author: Inara Verzemnieks
description: A memoir in which the Latvian world of her grandmother draws the writer, an American journalist, back to the old country to re-create a vanished life between farm and war.

title: Grace
author: Paul Lynch
description: A sweeping, Dickensian story of a young girl on a life-changing journey across nineteenth-century Ireland on the eve of the Great Famine.

title: A Life of Adventure and Delight
author: Akhil Sharma
description: A collection of eight stories, from the author of Family Life , following modern Indians at home and abroad as they face the trials of marriage, parenthood, and assimilation.

title: Dirt Road
author: James Kelman
description: A novel, by Booker Prize-winner Kelman, about a teenage boy who travels with his father from Scotland to Alabama to visit with relatives after the death of his mother. In the American South, he becomes swept up into the world of zydeco and blues

title: Gork, the Teenage Dragon
author: Gabe Hudson
description: A comic, genre-bending, coming-of-age tale about an anthropomorphic adolescent dragon trying to win the heart of a more popular classmate at a macho military academy.

title: Down a Dark Road: A Kate Burkholder Novel
author: Linda Castillo
description: In the ninth installment of the Kate Burkholder series, Kate who grew up Amish struggles to separate her past from the present.

title: Henry David Thoreau: A Life
author: Laura Dassow Walls
description: On the 200th anniversary of his birth comes a new biography of the iconic American naturalist and writer Henry David Thoreau.

title: All We Shall Know
author: Donal Ryan
description: Set in contemporary rural Ireland, a novel about a woman who blows up her already-dying marriage by sleeping with, and getting pregnant by, a 17-year-old Traveller boy she was teaching to read, and of the intense bond that forms between her and another young outcast in the community.

title: Who Is Rich?
author: Matthew Klam
description: From the author of Sam the Cat , a satire of love, sex, money, and politics that unfolds over four wild days in so-called 'paradise.' Rich, a middle-aged, once celebrated graphic novelist, contemplates whether or not to leave his wife and children for a student at an East Coast artist's retreat.

title: Woolly
author: Ben Mezrich
description: From the author of The Accidental Billionaires , The true story of a group of young geneticists working to make fantasy reality by sequencing the DNA of a frozen woolly mammoth harvested from above the Arctic circle, and splicing elements of that sequence into the DNA of a modern elephant.

title: To the New Owners: A Martha's Vineyard Memoir
author: Madeleine Blais
description: A chronicle, from Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Blais, of the final days and robust history of her family's time at their vacation home on Martha's Vineyard.

title: The Reason You're Alive
author: Matthew Quick
description: From the author of The Silver Linings Playbook , a novel about a Vietnam vet who, after a car accident and a brain tumor diagnosis, embarks on a quixotic crusade to track down his nemesis from the war.

title: Queen of Bebop: The Musical Lives of Sarah Vaughan
author: Elaine M. Hayes
description: A chronicle of the life of jazz singer Sarah Vaughan, one of the most influential and innovative musicians of the twentieth century.

title: Draw Your Weapons
author: Sarah Sentilles
description: A meditation on war, art, torture, and memory––focusing on a WWII conscientious objector and a former Abu Ghraib prison guard––told through a combination of memoir, history, reporting, visual culture, literature, and theology.

title: The Last Hack
author: Christopher Brookmyre
description: A cyber-thriller, the latest in Brookmyre's Jack Parlabane series. Blackmailed by an online stranger calling himself Zodiac, young black Glaswegian hacker Samantha Morpeth teams with scuffling journalist Parlabane in an attempt to turn the tables on her foe.

title: A Flag Worth Dying For: The Power and Politics of National Symbols
author: Tim Marshall
description: Combining geopolitics with world history, a droll examination of flags and their symbols—how their power is used to unite and divide populations and intimidate enemies.

title: The Graybar Hotel
author: Curtis Dawkins
description: A debut collection of short stories set mostly in prisons from an author currently serving a life sentence without parole for a drug-related homicide.

title: Out in the Open
author: Jesús Carrasco
description: A bleak, fable-like novel about a boy, fleeing from his pursuers across an arid desert landscape of an unknown country, in search of sanctuary.

title: South Pole Station
author: Ashley Shelby
description: A comic novel focusing on a young woman who, in the wake of her brother's suicide, moves to one of the most remote places on earth, where scientists, artists, and support personnel live, work, argue, and pout inside a geodesic dome.

title: The Last Laugh
author: Lynn Freed
description: A comic novel about three self-proclaimed “old bags” who run off to a Greek island for a year in order to unshackle the reins of family and lovers, only to find that it isn't so easy to get away from it all.

title: Made for Love
author: Alissa Nutting
description: From the author of Tampa , a novel set in the near future about a woman who, after running out on her marriage to a megalomaniacal tech company CEO, moves into a trailer park for senior citizens with her aging father and his extremely life-like sex doll.

title: Kill All Normies: Online Culture Wars From 4Chan And Tumblr To Trump And The Alt-Right
author: Angela Nagle
description: An investigation of online culture wars from 4Chan and Tumblr to Trump and the Alt-Right.

title: Golden Hill
author: Francis Spufford
description: The first novel from acclaimed nonfiction author Francis Spufford follows the adventures of a mysterious young man in mid-eighteenth century Manhattan, thirty years before the American Revolution.

title: Modern Gods
author: Nick Laird
description: A novel set in Ulster and Papua New Guinea telling the parallel stories of two sisters, Alison and Liz, and the buried secrets of sectarian violence that emerge when they come together in their small hometown in Northern Ireland for Alison's wedding.

title: The Child
author: Fiona Barton
description: The follow-up to Barton's mystery debut The Widow , a novel in which three women's lives become entwined when a newborn's skeleton is discovered beneath a bulldozed London building site.

title: Toscanini: Musician of Conscience
author: Harvey Sachs
description: On the 150th anniversary of his birth comes this biography of the conductor Arturo Toscanini, who transcended his own field, becoming a figure of such renown that it was often impossible not to see some mention of the maestro in the daily headlines.

title: Spoonbenders
author: Daryl Gregory
description: A novel about three generations of the Telemachus family, whose eccentric members possess extraordinary psychic abilities.

title: Shark Drunk
author: Martin Strøksnes
description: The true story of two friends, the author and the eccentric artist Hugo Aasjord, as they embark on a wild pursuit of the infamous Greenland Shark—whose meat contains a toxin that, when consumed, has been known to make people drunk and hallucinatory—all from a tiny rubber boat.

title: But Seriously
author: John McEnroe
description: A second memoir from John McEnroe, in which the former tennis player talks about his post-tennis life and struggle to reinvent himself as a father, broadcaster, and author.

title: Off the Cliff: How the Making of Thelma & Louise Drove Hollywood to the Edge
author: Becky Aikman
description: A behind-the-scenes look at the making of the 1991 feminist classic, drawing on exclusive interviews with the cast and crew.

title: The Windfall
author: Diksha Basu
description: A comedy of manners set in modern day India in which a family suddenly come in to an enormous and unexpected sum of money, and move from their housing complex in East Delhi to the super-rich side of town.

title: River Under the Road
author: Scott Spencer
description: From the author of Endless Love , a novel set in a Hudson River estate that traces the lives of two couples through snapshots of parties throughout their marriages.

title: The Destroyers
author: Christopher Bollen
description: A literary thriller in which a former rich kid, now fleeing from the emotional and financial fallout from his brother's death, accepts an old friend's offer to stay with him and his entourage on the beautiful and mysterious Greek island of Patmos, where things take a dark turn.

title: So Many Olympic Exertions
author: Anelise Chen
description: Blending elements of memoir and sports writing, Anelise Chen’s debut novel follows Athena Chen, a graduate student who, at the start of the novel, has just found out her ex-boyfriend has committed suicide. Through anecdotes and close readings of moments in the sometimes harrowing world of sports, the novel questions the validity of our current narratives of success.

title: Chester B. Himes: A Biography
author: Lawrence P. Jackson
description: A biography of the groundbreaking but troubled African American author.

title: The Force
author: Don Winslow
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: An epic police procedural from the author of The Cartel , set against the backdrop of racial tensions between the cops and community in present day Harlem, about a group of renegade New York detectives led by antihero Denny Malone.

title: The One Device: The Secret History of the iPhone
author: Brian Merchant
description: The secret history of the invention that changed everything-and became the most profitable product in the world.

title: Too Fat Too Slutty Too Loud: The Rise and Reign of the Unruly Woman
author: Anne Helen Petersen
description: From BuzzFeed culture writer Anne Helen Petersen comes an analytical look at how female celebrities are pushing boundaries of what it means to be an "aceptable" woman.

title: Be Free or Die
author: Cate Lineberry
description: A non fiction book about a little-known figure in American history, Robert Smalls, whose daring escape from slavery during the Civil War helped convince Lincoln and the country that African Americans were extraordinarily capable of fighting for their freedom.

title: Our Little Racket
author: Angelica Baker
description: A novel set in Greenwich, Connecticut, at the beginning of the 2008 financial crisis, about five women whose lives are dramatically changed by the downfall of a financial titan they are all connected to.

title: The Boy Who Loved Too Much: A True Story of Pathological Friendliness
author: Jennifer Latson
description: The poignant story of a boy’s coming-of-age complicated by Williams syndrome, a genetic disorder that makes people biologically incapable of distrust.

title: Love Like Blood
author: Mark Billingham
description: The latest novel in Billingham's London-set Detective Tom Thorne crime series. When Detective Nicola Tanner's lover is brutally murdered, she and Thorne realize that the crime is connected to Tanner's recent work on a string of cold-case honor killings.

title: Housman Country
author: Peter Parker
description: Part biography, part cultural history; an exploration of the poet A. E. Housman and the influence of his particular brand of Englishness.

title: The Smack
author: Richard Lange
description: A LA crime thriller in which a down-on-his luck grifter, with a drug-addicted AWOL daughter, is talked into taking part in a dangerous get rich quick scheme.

title: Hunger: A Memoir of (My) Body
author: Roxane Gay
description: A memoir from celebrated essayist and fiction author Roxane Gay, in which the writer uses her own emotional and psychological struggles, including the fallout from a brutal sexual assault as a child, as a means of exploring our shared anxieties over pleasure, consumption, appearance, and health.

title: So Much Blue
author: Percival Everett
description: From the author of Erasure . The story of a middle-aged artist working on a painting he won't allow anyone to see, and of the two formative events of his past: an affair ten years previous with a young Parisian woman, and a 1979 trip to an El Salvador on the verge of war to search for his friend's missing brother.

title: The Changeling
author: Victor LaValle
description: A melding of horror, fantasy, and social consciousness realism, The Changeling is a dark, modern-day fairy tale about a devoted father's confrontation with otherworldly evil after his family is torn apart.

title: You Don't Have To Say You Love Me
author: Sherman Alexie
description: A memoir, told in both poetry and prose, from National Book Award-winning author Alexie, focusing on his troubled mother and childhood on a Spokane Indian reservation in Washington.

title: The Marsh King's Daughter
author: Karen Dionne
description: A psychological suspense novel; the story of the daughter of an escaped convict who tracks her father through the wilderness while reflecting upon her childhood as his prisoner.

title: Blind Spot
author: Teju Cole
description: A lyrical essay in photographs paired with text, from the author of Open City .

title: The Accomplished Guest
author: Ann Beattie
description: A new collection of stories from Beattie, set along the East Coast from Maine to Key West, exploring unconventional friendships, frustrated loves, mortality, and aging.

title: No is Not Enough
author: Naomi Klein
description: Activist and journalist Klein argues that Trump is not an aberration but a logical extension of the worst, most dangerous trends of the past half-century—the very conditions that have unleashed a rising tide of white nationalism the world over. It is not enough, she tells us, to merely resist, to say "no." Our historical moment demands more: a credible and inspiring “yes."

title: A House Among the Trees
author: Julia Glass
description: From National Book Award-winner Glass, the story of an unusual bond between a world-famous writer and his assistant. When the revered children's book author Mort Lear dies accidentally at his Connecticut home, he leaves his property and all its contents to his trusted assistant, Tomasina Daulair, who is moved by his generosity but dismayed by the complicated and defiant directives in his will.

title: Lincoln and the Abolitionists
author: Fred Kaplan
description: An exploration of how Abraham Lincoln’s and John Quincy Adams’ experiences with slavery and race shaped their differing viewpoints.

title: The Chalk Artist
author: Allegra Goodman
description: A Boston-set novel in which an idealistic schoolteacher gets her artist boyfriend a job with her father’s video game company even as she's losing a promising student to the addiction of online gaming.

title: The Songs We Know Best: John Ashbery's Early Life
author: Karin Roffman
description: The first major account of the early years of the Pulitzer Prize-winning poet, drawn from interviews with Ashbury as well as his childhood diaries.

title: The Rise and Fall of D.O.D.O.
author: Neal Stephenson and Nicole Galland
description: A collaborative near-future thriller combining history, science, magic, mystery, intrigue, and adventure. When Melisande Stokes, an expert in linguistics and languages, accidently meets military intelligence operator Tristan Lyons in a hallway at Harvard University, it is the beginning of a chain of events that will alter their lives and human history itself.

title: The City Always Wins
author: Omar Robert Hamilton
description: A debut novel from the cofounder of the Palestinian Festival of Literature which chronicles the aftermath of the 2011 uprising in Tahrir Square through the experiences of Khalil, an Egyptian-Palestinian-American; Mariam, his Egyptian girlfriend; and their colleagues at Chaos, which they’ve founded in response to the state-controlled media.

title: Democracy in Chains: The Deep History of the Radical Right’s Stealth Plan for America
author: Nancy MacLean
description: An exposé of the libertarian right’s relentless campaign to eliminate unions, suppress voting, privatize public education, and change the Constitution, focusing on the man MacLean calls the plan's true architect: the Nobel Prize-winning political economist James McGill Buchanan.

title: The Close Encounters Man
author: Mark O'Connell
description: Mark O'Connell, founder of the UFO blog High Strangeness , details the life of the Air Force astronomer J. Allen Hynek and his contributions to the UFO community.

title: Uncomfortably Happily
author: Yeon-Sik Hong, Trans. by Hellen Jo
description: A graphic novel about when the gentler pace and stillness of the countryside replace the roar of the city, but your editor keeps calling.

title: Kingdom Cons
author: Yuri Herrera, Trans. by Lisa Dillman
description: The third novel of Herrera's loose Mexican underworld trilogy to be translated into English. In the court of the King, a narco boss in an unnamed territory in Mexico, everyone knows their place. But as the Artist wins hearts and egos with his ballads, uncomfortable truths emerge that shake the Kingdom to its core. Part surreal fable and part crime romance, Kingdom Cons questions the price of keeping your integrity in a world ruled by patronage and power.

title: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
author: Arundhati Roy
description: The first novel in 20 years from the author of The God of Small Things , The Ministry of Utmost Happiness begins with the story of a young Delhi hermaphrodite named Anjum, and continues onward as an intimate journey of many years across the Indian subcontinent—from the cramped neighborhoods of Old Dehli and the roads of the new city to the mountains and valleys of Kashmir and beyond, where war is peace and peace is war.

title: The Answers
author: Catherine Lacey
description: With a debilitating but undiagnosable illness and mounting debt, a young woman takes a job as an Emotional Girlfriend in a “Girlfriend Experiment”?the brainchild of a wealthy and infamous actor who has hired a team of biotech researchers to solve the problem of how to build and maintain the perfect romantic relationship.

title: Hue 1968: A Turning Point of the American War in Vietnam
author: Mark Bowden
description: From the author of Black Hawk Down , the story of the centerpiece of the Tet Offensive and a turning point in the American War in Vietnam.

title: The Bright Hour: A Memoir of Living and Dying
author: Nina Riggs
description: Nina Riggs was just thirty-seven years old when initially diagnosed with breast cancer—one small spot. Within a year, the mother of two sons, ages seven and nine, and married sixteen years to her best friend, received the devastating news that her cancer was terminal.

title: Grief Cottage
author: Gail Godwin
description: A novel about a boy, sent to live with his prickly great-aunt on an island in South Carolina after his parents are killed in a car crash, who becomes obsessed with a ruined cottage.

title: The Essex Serpent
author: Sarah Perry
description: Winner of the Fiction Book of the Year at the British Book Awards. An historical novel, set in late nineteenth-century England, about an intellectually minded young widow, a pious vicar, and a rumored mythical serpent that explores questions about science and religion, skepticism, and faith, independence and love.

title: Lonesome Lies Before Us
author: Don Lee
description: A quiet novel about down-on-his-luck alt-country singer who gets one last shot at stardom when his old flame and singing partner reappears in his life.

title: Camino Island
author: John Grisham
description: A breezy, non-legal thriller from Grisham, about a novelist struggling with writer's block who is hired by an shadowy company to travel to Camino Island to see if she can track down a number of priceless F. Scott Fitzgerald manuscripts recently stolen from Princeton library.

title: Stephen Florida
author: Gabe Habash
description: Stephen Florida follows a college wrestler in his senior season, when every practice, every match, is a step closer to greatness and a step further from sanity. Profane, manic, and tipping into the uncanny, it's a story of loneliness, obsession, and the drive to leave a mark.

title: The Prisoner in His Palace
author: Will Bardenwerper
description: The story of the months months of Saddam Hussein's life, from the time he was captured to his hanging, focusing on his relationship with the twelve US military policemen ordered to guard him.

title: Magpie Murders
author: Anthony Horowitz
description: A novel within a novel, a pastiche of of Agatha Christie and the classic English detective story, from the bestselling author of Moriarty and Trigger Mortis .

title: Swell
author: Jill Eisenstadt
description: From the author of From Rockaway . In the immediate wake of 9/11, a young family uproots their lives in Manhattan to resettle in a ramshackle Rockaway beach house—and, over the course of one momentous weekend, finds a whole lot more drama than they bargained for.

title: Everybody's Son
author: Thrity Umrigar
description: Fro the author of The Space Between Us . A neglected 9-year-old biracial child adopted by a powerful white family grows up to fulfill his potential only to confront a secret which will recast his entire sense of self.

title: Do Not Become Alarmed
author: Maile Meloy
description: What begins as a relaxing vacation becomes something far more sinister as three families on a cruise are separated from their children during a shore excursion in Central America.

title: If I Understood You, Would I Have This Look on My Face?
author: Alan Alda
description: Award-winning actor Alan Alda tells the story of his quest to learn how to communicate better, and to teach others to do the same.

title: Cockfosters
author: Helen Simpson
description: Nine stories that take up the preoccupations and fixations of time's passing and of middle age and that take us from today's London and Berlin to the wild west of the USA and the wilder shores of Mother Russia.

title: Defectors
author: Joseph Kanon
description: A Cold War spy thriller set in 1961 about two brothers, former CIA agents, reunited in Moscow twelve years after the elder defected to Russia as a spy.

title: The Retreat of Western Liberalism
author: Edward Luce
description: Financial Times Washington correspondant Luce argues that Western liberal democracy is facing its greatest threat since the second world war.

title: Kennedy and King
author: Steven Levingston
description: Kennedy and King traces the emergence of two of the twentieth century's greatest leaders, their powerful impact on each other and on the shape of the civil rights battle between 1960 and 1963.

title: The Gypsy Moth Summer
author: Julia Fierro
description: It is the summer of 1992 and a gypsy moth invasion blankets Avalon Island. Ravenous caterpillars disrupt early summer serenity on Avalon, an islet off the coast of Long Island, which underscores the tension boiling to the surface of the islanders’ lives.

title: The Best Land Under Heaven: The Donner Party in the Age of Manifest Destiny
author: Michael Wallis
description: Cutting through 160 years of mythmaking, historian Michael Wallis presents the ultimate cautionary tale of America’s westward expansion.

title: Black Moses
author: Alain Mabanckou, Trans. by Helen Stevenson
description: A darkly comic coming of age tale about the misfortunes of a Congolese orphan in the 1970s, from one of Francophone Africa's most acclaimed writers.

title: Fly Me
author: Daniel Riley
description: The year is 1972 and Suzy Whitman, a young Vassar graduate, has followed her glamorous older sister to the Southern California beach town of Sela del Mar where the two work as air stewardess and Suzy gets caught up in the worlds of drug smuggling and skyjacking.

title: Would Everybody Please Stop?
author: Jenny Allen
description: A collection of humorous essays about metropolitan life, family, divorce, and aging from a writer, performer, and frequent New Yorker contributor.

title: The Long Haul: A Trucker's Tales of Life on the Road
author: Finn Murphy
description: A philosophical moving trucker shares stories from a life on the open road.

title: Dear Cyborgs
author: Eugene Lim
description: In a small Midwestern town, two Asian American boys bond over their outcast status and a mutual love of comic books. Meanwhile, in an alternative or perhaps future universe, a team of superheroes ponder modern society during their time off. Between black-ops missions and rescuing hostages, they swap stories of artistic malaise and muse on the seemingly inescapable grip of market economics.

title: You'll Never Know Dear
author: Hallie Ephron
description: A psychological suspense novel about three generations of women haunted by a little girl’s disappearance, and the porcelain doll that may hold the key to the truth.

title: She Rides Shotgun
author: Jordan Harper
description: In Jordan Harper's first novel, he explores the tale about an ex-con’s efforts to protect his young daughter.

title: Beren and Lúthien
author: J.R.R. Tolkien, Ed. by Christopher Tolkien
description: Three versions of a foundation tale in J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle Earth universe (and a key part of The Silmarillion ). The story of the human Beren and the elf Lúthien, and their star-crossed romance, which was itself inspired by Tolkien's relationship with his wife.

title: From Warm Center to Ragged Edge
author: Jon K. Lauck
description: A scholarly history which examines the academic and cultural derision suffered by the Midwest, calling for a return to a healthy regionalism.

title: Theft by Finding: Diaries (1977-2002)
author: David Sedaris
description: Humor writer David Sedaris has kept a diary for the last forty years. Theft by Finding , the first of two volumes, is the story of how a drug-abusing dropout with a weakness for the International House of Pancakes and a chronic inability to hold down a real job became one of the funniest people on the planet.

title: The Descent of Man
author: Grayson Perry
description: What does it mean to be male in the 21st Century? Award–winning artist Grayson Perry explores what masculinity is: from sex to power, from fashion to career prospects, and what it could become––with illustrations throughout.

title: Al Franken, Giant of the Senate
author: Al Franken
description: From Senator Al Franken comes the story of an award-winning comedian who decided to run for office and then discovered why award-winning comedians tend not to do that.

title: Kingdom of Olives and Ash: Writers Confront the Occupation
author: Ed. by Ayelet Waldman and Michael Chabon
description: A groundbreaking collection of essays by celebrated international writers bears witness to the human cost of fifty years of Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza.

title: The Russian Revolution: A New History
author: Sean McMeekin
description: Historian Sean McMeekin traces the events which ended Romanov rule, ushered the Bolsheviks into power, and introduced Communism to the world.

title: Touch
author: Courtney Maum
description: A satirical novel in the spirit of Maria Semple and Jess Walter about a New York City trend forecaster who finds herself wanting to overturn her own predictions, move away from technology, and reclaim her heart.

title: Boundless
author: Jillian Tamaki
description: A eclectic collection of graphic short stories, focusing on the interior lives of a range of subjects, from the Eisner-winning author of SuperMutant Magic Academy .

title: Destined for War: Can America and China Escape Thucydides’s Trap?
author: Graham Allison
description: An exploration of why Thucydides’s Trap (a deadly pattern of structural stress that results when a rising power challenges a ruling one) is the best lens for understanding U.S.-China relations in the twenty-first century.

title: Cattle Kingdom: The Hidden History of the Cowboy West
author: Christopher Knowlton
description: A history of the boom-and-bust cycles of the cattle industry in the wildest days of the Wild West.

title: Isadora
author: Amelia Gray
description: A portrait of the "mother of modern dance," Isadora Duncan, whose life was marked by scandal and tragedy.

title: Dragon Teeth
author: Michael Crichton
description: From the author of Jurassic Park , a posthumously discovered historical adventure novel set in the Wild West during the golden age of fossil hunting.

title: Augustown
author: Kei Miller
description: A novel set in Kingston in 1982, a boy’s schoolroom punishment opens a window into the roiling, mystical history of an impoverished Jamaican community.

title: Churchill & Orwell: The Fight for Freedom
author: Thomas E. Ricks
description: From Pulitzer Prize–winning historian Ricks, a dual biography of Winston Churchill and George Orwell, who preserved democracy from the threats of authoritarianism, from the left and right alike.

title: Shtum
author: Jem Lester
description: A darkly comic autobiographal novel about the strains of raising an autistic child, and the relationship between fathers and sons.

title: The Long Drop
author: Denise Mina
description: A crime thriller, from Scottish feminist noir writer Mina, set inspired by the Burnside murders, a true crime spree by Scotland's most notorious serial killer that horrified Glasgow in the late 1950s.

title: Chemistry
author: Weike Wang
description: A coming-of-age debut novel about a young Chinese American scientist who must recalibrate her life when her academic career goes off track.

title: The Exile
author: Cathy Scott-Clark and Adrian Levy
description: An investigative account of the decade between 9/11 and 2011 when Osama bin Laden evaded capture, told through the eyes of those who witnessed it: bin Laden's four wives and many children, his deputies and military strategists, his spiritual advisor, the CIA, Pakistan's ISI, and many others who have never before told their stories.

title: Wild Ride: Inside Uber's Quest for World Domination
author: Adam Lashinsky
description: The untold story of Uber’s meteoric rise, and the massive ambitions of its controversial founder and CEO Travis Kalanick.

title: The Hue and Cry at Our House
author: Benjamin Taylor
description: A memoir of boyhood tracing the 12 months that followed the author's shaking hands with JFK on the morning of the president's assassination. Looking back on the love and tension within his family, the childhood friendships that lasted and those that didn’t, he reflects upon the outsized impact our larger American story had on his own.

title: Standard Deviation
author: Katherine Heiny
description: A comic debut novel about a second marriage. Introverted, middle-aged Graham has been married for 12 years to his talkative, eccentric, younger second wife Audra, and he’s beginning to wonder whether they’re really suited for each other.

title: Rich People Problems
author: Kevin Kwan
