description: The final installment of Kwan's Crazy Rich Asians trilogy. A comic novel of a family riven by fortune, an ex-wife driven psychotic with jealousy, a battle royal fought through couture gown sabotage, and the heir to one of Asia's greatest fortunes locked out of his inheritance.

title: Shadow Man
author: Alan Drew
description: Ben Wade, a former LAPD detective now working homicide in the southern Orange County town of Rancho Santa Elena, is forced to confront his own dark past in investigating a series of killings.

title: Broken River
author: J. Robert Lennon
description: A family drama and murder mystery. When Brooklyn artist Karl Jandek moves with his novelist wife, Eleanor, to an upstate home in Broken River, N.Y., to save their failing marriage, they neglect to tell their adolescent daughter, Irina, that the house’s previous owners were brutally murdered on its grounds a decade earlier. As things unravel, the family is watched by a spectral presences known as The Observer.

title: Bad Dreams and Other Stories
author: Tessa Hadley
description: A short story collection focusing on young women coming of age in Britain of the 1950s/60s and today.

title: Testimony
author: Scott Turow
description: From the bestselling author of Presumed Innocent , a legal thriller in which an Illinois prosecutor seeks to learn who annihilated a group of refugee gypsies in Bosnia.

title: Ernest Hemingway: A Biography
author: Mary V. Dearborn
description: The first full biography of Ernest Hemingway in more than fifteen years, drawing upon a wide array of never-before-used material.

title: Do I Make Myself Clear?: Why Writing Well Matters
author: Harold Evans
description: A guide to writing English the proper way by one of the greatest newspaper editors of our time.

title: There's a Mystery There: The Primal Vision of Maurice Sendak
author: Jonathan Cott
description: A book about the life and work and creative inspirations of the great children's book genius Maurice Sendak.

title: Give a Girl a Knife
author: Amy Thielen
description: A food memoir chronicling one woman’s journey from her rural Midwestern hometown to the intoxicating world of New York City fine dining—and back again—in search of her culinary roots.

title: Otis Redding: An Unfinished Life
author: Jonathan Gould
description: A biography of Otis Redding, The King of Soul, timed to coincide with the 50th anniversary of Redding's iconic performance at the 1967 Monterey Pop Festival.

title: The Fact of a Body: A Murder and a Memoir
author: Alexandria Marzano-Lesnevich
description: A blending of memoir and true-crime journalism. In 2003, working as a summer intern at a Louisiana law firm that defends clients sentenced to death, the author discovered the case of a child’s murder by a confessed pedophile. Passionately opposed to capital punishment, she realized that she wanted this client to die. That response—unsettling and unexpected—incited an interest in the case that became nothing less than an obsession.

title: Florence in Ecstasy
author: Jessie Chaffee
description: A young American woman arrives in Florence from Boston, knowing no one and speaking little Italian. But Hannah is isolated in a more profound way, estranged from her own identity after a bout with starvation that has left her life and body in ruins. She is determined to recover in Florence, a city saturated with beauty, vitality, and food?as well as a dangerous history of sainthood for women who starved themselves for God.

title: The Mighty Franks
author: Michael Frank
description: A memoir in which a writer reflects on his Hollywood screenwriter aunt’s erratic behavior and overbearing influence on his life.

title: Things to Do When You're Goth in the Country
author: Chavisa Woods
description: A collection of dark short stories about outsiders living in rural Illinois, focusing on poverty, self-destructiveness, militarism, otherness, and queerness.

title: New Boy
author: Tracy Chevalier
description: Part of the Hogarth Shakespeare series. A retelling of Othello , set in a middle school in suburban Washington in the 1970s.

title: Chuck Klosterman X
author: Chuck Klosterman
description: A collection of humorous essays about pop culture from sports and music journalist (and former New York Times Magazine Ethicist) Klosterman.

title: Papi: My Story
author: David Ortiz and Michael Holley
description: A memoir by former Boston Red Sox player David Ortiz: one of the game’s greatest, most clutch sluggers and beloved personalities

title: Coach Wooden and Me
author: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
description: Basketball legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar explores his 50-year friendship with Coach John Wooden, one of the most enduring and meaningful relationships in sports history.

title: The Vanishing American Adult
author: Ben Sasse
description: A parenting advice guide from Sasse, a junior Senator from Nebraska, about how to raise hard-working, engaged citizens.

title: The Autonomous City: A History of Urban Squatting
author: Alexander Vasudevan
description: A radical history of squatting in Europe and North America and the struggle for the right to remake the city.

title: Wrestling With His Angel: The Political Life of Abraham Lincoln Vol. II
author: Sidney Blumenthal
description: Volume II of Blumenthal’s four part biography, The Political Life of Abraham Lincoln , covering his "wilderness years," revealing the future president’s genius during the most decisive period of his political life when he seizes the moment, finds his voice, and helps create a new political party.

title: Not One Day
author: Anne Garréta, Trans. by Emma Ramadan
description: An experimental, intimate, erotic, and sometimes bitter recounting of loves and lovers past, exploring the interplay between memory, fantasy, and desire.

title: No Middle Name: The Complete Collected Jack Reacher Short Stories
author: Lee Child
description: A new Jack Reacher novella and eleven previously published stories, together for the first time in one pulse-pounding collection.

title: Kintu
author: Jennifer Nansubuga Makumbi
description: First published in Kenya in 2014, Kintu is a multilayered narrative that reimagines the history of Uganda through the cursed bloodline of the Kintu clan.

title: House of Names
author: Colm Tóibín
description: From the author of Brooklyn , a retelling of the ancient Greek myth of Clytemnestra and her children.

title: Men Without Women
author: Haruki Murakami, Trans. by Philip Gabriel & Ted Goossen
description: A collection of seven short stories about men who have lost the women in their lives, from the celebrated Japanese author.

title: Since We Fell
author: Dennis Lehane
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: A psychological thriller about a former television journalist turned shut-in, her marriage to a private investigator, disintegrating mental state, and the conspiracy she is sucked into; from the author of Shutter Island and Mystic River .

title: The Purple Swamp Hen
author: Penelope Lively
description: A new collection of short stories from the Booker Prize-winning author, focusing on the themes of history, family, and relationships.

title: Mother Land
author: Paul Theroux
description: A darkly comic novel set in a Cape Cod town about a family held together and torn apart by its narcissistic matriarch.

title: The Road to Camelot: Inside JFK’s Five-Year Campaign
author: Thomas Oliphant and Curtis Wilkie
description: A behind-the-scenes account of John F. Kennedy’s wily campaign to the White House, beginning with his bold, failed attempt to win the vice presidential nomination in 1956.

title: Love and Trouble
author: Claire Dederer
description: An intimate, comic memoir about Dederer's attempt to reconcile the sexually liberated teenager she was with the woman she has become.

title: October: The Story of the Russian Revolution
description: On the centenary of the Russian Revolution, celebrated "weird" fiction writer China Miéville tells the extraordinary story of this pivotal moment in history.

title: Saints for All Occasions
author: J. Courtney Sullivan
description: A novel about two Irish Catholic sisters who emigrate to America in the 1950s, their estrangement, and the lives they lead over the next five decades.

title: Rising Star: The Making of Barack Obama
author: David Garrow
description: A hefty, controversial account of Barack Obama's formative years, focusing on his early romantic relationships, from the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Bearing the Cross .

title: Woman No. 17
author: Edan Lepucki
description: From the author of California . In the Hollywood Hills, a smart, damaged mother of two hires a nanny so she can work on a memoir—but the magnetic younger woman has secrets of her own and things soon take a darker turn.

title: The Thirst: A Harry Hole Novel
author: Jo Nesbø, Trans. by Neil Smith
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: A new thriller from the bestselling Scandinavian crime author of Police and The Snowman in which Inspector Harry Hole is called back to active duty to hunt down a serial murderer who targets his victims on Tinder.

title: The Gift
author: Barbara Browning
description: In the midst of the Occupy movement, Barbara Andersen begins spamming people indiscriminately with ukulele covers of sentimental songs. A series of inappropriate intimacies ensues, including an erotically charged correspondence and then collaboration with an extraordinarily gifted and troubled musician living in Germany.

title: Aliens: The World's Leading Scientists on the Search for Extraterrestrial Life
author: Jim Al-Khalili
description: A book of essays in which scientists from around the world weigh in on the latest advances in the search for intelligent life in the universe and discuss just what that might look like.

title: The Outer Beach: A Thousand-Mile Walk on Cape Cod's Atlantic Shore
author: Robert Finch
description: A chronicle of a nature writer’s fifty-year relationship with an iconic American landscape: Cape Cod's Atlantic shore.

title: Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine
author: Gail Honeyman
description: A sweetly comic novel about an oddball woman, living a solitary life after a traumatic childhood, who is prompted to come out of her shell by a crush on a musician and a friendship with a colleague.

title: Be Like the Fox: Machiavelli In His World
author: Erica Benner
description: The story of how Machiavelli?arguably the most misunderstood thinker of all time?fought to change his corrupt world.

title: The Evolution of Beauty
author: Richard O. Prum
description: A major reimagining of how evolutionary forces work, arguing that mating preferences—what Darwin termed 'the taste for the beautiful'—create the extraordinary range of ornament in the animal world.

title: Priestdaddy
author: Patricia Lockwood
description: A comic family memoir about having a married Catholic priest for a father.

title: Into the Water
author: Paula Hawkins
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: From the author of The Girl on the Train , a thriller set in a small English town where women have been drowning in mysterious circumstances for generations.

title: Between Them: Remembering My Parents
author: Richard Ford
description: Richard Ford's first work of nonfiction: a narrative of memory and parental love.

title: Women Who Work: Rewriting the Rules for Success
author: Ivanka Trump
description: A peppy book of advice for wealthy women on how they can succeed in life and business, from the First Daughter and Advisor to the last ever President of the United States.

title: The Dinner Party
author: Joshua Ferris
description: The first collection of darkly humorous short stories from the author of To Rise Again at a Decent Hour .

title: Salt Houses
author: Hala Alyan
description: Winner of the 2018 Dayton Literary Peace Prize, a debut novel beginning in 1963 which tracks the displacement and dispersal of four generations of a Palestinian family.

title: My Life with Bob: Flawed Heroine Keeps Book of Books, Plot Ensues
author: Pamela Paul
description: New York Times Book Review Editor Pamela Paul has kept a record of every book she's read for the past 28 years. In My Life With Bob , she tells the story of her life through the books that have shaped it.

title: The End of Eddy
author: Édouard Louis, Trans. by Michael Lucey
description: An harrowing autobiographical novel about growing up gay in a working-class town in rural France.

title: No One Can Pronounce My Name
author: Rakesh Satyal
description: A sweetly comic novel set a suburb outside Cleveland, where a community of Indian Americans has settled into lives that straddle the divide between Eastern and Western cultures.

title: Mockingbird Songs: My Friendship with Harper Lee
author: Wayne Flynt
description: A portrait of one of the most famous and beloved authors in the canon of American literature—a collection of letters between Harper Lee and one of her closest friends that reveals the famously private writer as never before, in her own words.

title: Miss Burma
author: Charmaine Craig
description: The story of one family during the most violent and turbulent years of Burmese history; a novel of love and war, colonialism and ethnicity, and the ties of blood.

title: The Leavers
author: Lisa Ko
description: The winner of the 2016 PEN/Bellwether Prize for Fiction; a novel about an undocumented Chinese mother who suddenly disappears and the young American-born son she leaves behind.

title: Trajectory
author: Richard Russo
description: A collection of three short stories and a novella from the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Empire Falls .

title: Fen
author: Daisy Johnson
description: A dark debut short story collection set in the fenlands of England, mixing realism with folklore, reminiscent of the work of Angela Carter.

title: Inheritance from Mother
author: Minae Mizumura, Trans. by Juliet Winters Carpenter
description: In a novel of female endurance and obligation, Mitsuki, the 'semi-neglected daughter' of the Katsura family, must not only bear the lion’s share of caring for her elderly parents, but must also steel herself for the failure of her marriage.

title: A Man and His Presidents: The Political Odyssey of William F. Buckley Jr.
author: Alvin S. Felzenberg
description: An admiring look at the career of William F. Buckley Jr., the conservative political commentator, activist, and public contrarian.

title: American Kingpin
author: Nick Bilton
description: The true story of the man who built a billion-dollar online drug empire from his bedroom (the Silk Road, a clandestine Web site hosted on the Dark Web where anyone could trade anything—drugs, hacking software, forged passports, counterfeit cash, poisons—free of the government’s watchful eye)—and almost got away with it.

title: Deep Thinking: Where Machine Intelligence Ends and Human Creativity Begins
author: Garry Kasparov with Mig Greengard
description: An account, by Russian political activist and former chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov, of his 1997 battle with IBM supercomputer Deep Blue and what his loss to the machine taught him about the nature of artificial intelligence.

title: Behave: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
author: Robert M. Sapolsky
description: From a celebrated neurobiologist and primatologist, an examination of human behavior, both good and bad, and an answer to the question: Why do we do the things we do?

title: Jane Austen: The Secret Radical
author: Helena Kelly
description: A reassessment of the life and work of Jane Austen that makes clear how Austen has been misread for the past two centuries and that shows us how she intended her books to be read and revealing how subversive and daring a writer she was.

title: Proving Ground
author: Peter Blauner
description: A sweeping crime novel in which the murder of a high-profile liberal lawyer in Brooklyn puts his Iraq War veteran son and two detectives on a collision course to uncover the truth.

title: Anatomy of Terror: From the Death of bin Laden to the Rise of the Islamic State
author: Ali Soufan
description: Former FBI special agent Ali Soufan dissects bin Laden’s brand of jihadi terrorism and its major offshoots.

title: Knowing the Score
author: David Papineau
description: An investigation into what sports can teach us about philosophy (and what philosophy can teach us about sports).

title: Robert B. Parker's Little White Lies
author: Ace Atkins
description: In the forty-fifth book of Robert B. Parker series, a woman conned by a former lover enlists Boston’s most storied private eye in her cause and then has second and third thoughts.

title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
description: What is the nature of space and time? How do we fit within the universe? How does the universe fit within us? Celebrated astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson acts as a guide.

title: Jane Crow: The Life of Pauli Murray
author: Rosalind Rosenberg
description: A biography of the African-American activist and lawyer Pauli Murray, who played pivotal roles in both the modern civil rights and women's movements, all while struggling with the issue of her own gender identity.

title: Hamlet Globe to Globe
author: Dominic Dromgoole
description: An account, by the former director of the Globe Theater in London, of the adventure of taking Shakespeare’s tragedy to nearly 200 countries across the world.

title: Anything is Possible
author: Elizabeth Strout
description: A novel in linked stories and a sequel of sorts to 2016's My Name is Lucy Barton , from the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Olive Kitteridge , focusing on the intimate personal lives of ordinary people in the town of Amgash, Illinois.

title: Borne
author: Jeff VanderMeer
description: From the author of the Southern Reach trilogy, a science fiction novel in which a young scavenger in a near-future city plagued by experimental horrors from the Company finds and nurtures a bizarre, shape-shifting creature.

title: Hostage
author: Guy Delisle
description: The story of Doctors Without Borders administrator Christophe André, who was kidnapped by armed men and kept handcuffed to a radiator in solitary confinement in Chechnya for three months.

title: Startup
author: Doree Shafrir
description: A feminist satire about the tech industry by a Senior Culture Writer at Buzzfeed.

title: The Last Neanderthal
author: Claire Cameron
description: The story of two women --a pregnant neanderthal woman and a modern day archeologist-- separated by millennia but linked by an epic journey that will transform them both.

title: Last Hope Island: Britain, Occupied Europe, and the Brotherhood That Helped Turn the Tide of War
author: Lynne Olson
description: An account of how Britain became the base of operations for the exiled leaders of Europe in their desperate struggle to reclaim their continent from Hitler in the early days of WWII.

title: I'd Die For You: And Other Lost Stories
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald, Ed. Anne Margaret Daniel
description: A collection of the last complete unpublished short stories and film treatments written by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

title: Option B: Facing Adversity, Building Resilience, and Finding Joy
author: Sheryl Sandberg and Adam M. Grant
description: From Facebook COO Sandberg, written in the wake of her husband's sudden death, a book about building resilience and moving forward after life’s inevitable setbacks.

title: Walkaway
author: Cory Doctorow
description: Set in the mid-21st century, when anyone can 3-D print pretty much whatever they need in terms of food, shelter and clothes, the novel follows a trio in their 20s — Hubert, Seth and Natalie — as they abandon the world of corrupt plutocrats and leave behind their possessions, debts, jobs and dysfunctional families.

title: The Witchfinder's Sister
author: Beth Underdown
description: A literary historical thriller based on the devastating witch hunts in 1640s England conducted by “Witchfinder General” Matthew Hopkins, told from the perspective of his pregnant sister.

title: Beartown
author: Fredrik Backman
description: From the author of My Name is One . A novel about an isolated and decaying Swedish town whose inhabitants desperately want their youth hockey team to win the championship, believing it will be a path to economic revival. When the star player is accused of sexual assaulting the general manager's teenage daughter, the town must grapple with its conscience.

title: The Teeth of the Comb & Other Stories
author: Osama Alomar, Trans. by C. J. Collins
description: A collection of short, disquieting fables from Syrian writer Alomar that comment on the nature of humanity and the current political climate.

title: Jefferson: Architect of American Liberty
author: John B. Boles
description: A full-scale biography of Thomas Jefferson that emphasizes his creative paradoxes and accomplishments.

title: Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat: Mastering the Elements of Good Cooking
author: Samin Nosrat, Illus. by Alice MacNoughton
description: A visionary master class in cooking that distills decades of professional experience into just four simple elements, from the woman declared 'America’s next great cooking teacher' by Alice Waters.

title: A Line Made By Walking
author: Sara Baume
description: A novel about a young artist's search for meaning and healing in rural Ireland, from the author of Spill Simmer Falter Wither

title: Killers of the Flower Moon: The Osage Murders and the Birth of the FBI
author: David Grann
description: From the author of The Lost City of Z , a true-life murder mystery about one of the most monstrous crimes in American history.

title: Imagine Wanting Only This
author: Kristen Radtke
description: A graphic memoir about loss, love, and confronting grief through an investigation of ruined and abandoned places.

title: A Grace Paley Reader
author: Grace Paley, Ed. by Kevin Bowen
description: A collection of writing—stories, essays, and poetry—from the iconic author and political activist.

title: Shattered: Inside Hillary Clinton's Doomed Campaign
author: Jonathan Allen and Amie Parnes
description: The story of the missteps Hillary Clinton and her team made to lose the 2016 election.

title: The Golden Legend
author: Nadeem Aslam
description: A searing novel set in contemporary Pakistan, the story of a Muslim widow and her Christian neighbors whose community is consumed by violent religious intolerance.

title: Janesville: An American Story
author: Amy Goldstein
description: A Washington Post reporter’s intimate account of the fallout from the closing of a General Motors’ assembly plant in Janesville, Wisconsin—Paul Ryan’s hometown—and a larger story of the hollowing of the American middle class.

title: Move Fast and Break Things
author: Jonathan Taplin
description: The story of how a small group of libertarian entrepreneurs began in the 1990s to hijack the original decentralized vision of the Internet, in the process creating three monopoly firms––Facebook, Amazon and Google––that now determine the future of the music, film, television, publishing and news industries.

title: The Book of Joan
author: Lidia Yuknavitch
description: A science-fiction novel set in the near future about a heroine—a reimagined Joan of Arc—poised to save a world ravaged by war, violence, and greed, and forever change history.

title: My Cat Yugoslavia
author: Pajtim Statovci, Trans. by David Hackston
description: Winner of Finland's highest literary honor for a debut novel. Told in two intertwined stories: the first of Bekim, a young gay Kosovar immigrant in Finland and the relationship he strikes up with an abrasive talking cat; the second of his mother and her marriage to an abusive, domineering man.

title: The American Spirit: Who We Are and What We Stand For
author: David McCullough
description: A collection of speeches by the Pulitzer Prize– and National Book Award–winning historian and biographer.

title: Locking Up Our Own: Crime and Punishment in Black America
author: James Forman Jr.
description: An investigation, by a Yale Law School professor and former D.C. public defender, into mass incarceration in the US, with a focus on the part played by African-Americans in shaping criminal justice policy.

title: Tender: Stories
author: Sofia Samatar
description: 19 eerie short stories from award-winning Somali American fantasy writer Samatar.

title: Spoils
author: Brian Van Reet
description: An Iraq War novel set in 2003 focusing on the deadly connections between a female American soldier, an American tank crewman, and a fervent jihadist insurgent.

title: Fallout
author: Sara Paretsky
description: The latest novel in Paretsky's VI Warshawsky private detective series in which the P.I. travels to Kansas when her god-daughter asks for help with a missing persons case.

title: Fear City: New York's Fiscal Crisis and the Rise of Austerity Politics
author: Kim Phillips-Fein
description: A history of 1970s New York City on the edge of financial collapse?and an anatomy of the austerity politics that continue to shape the world today.

title: This Fight is Our Fight: The Battle to Save America's Middle Class
author: Elizabeth Warren
description: Elizabeth Warren offers a timely book about why our middle class is under siege and how we can win the fight to save it.

title: G-Man
author: Stephen Hunter
description: From Pulitzer Prize winner Stephen Hunter, the latest episode in the Bob Lee Swagger saga, which finds Bob uncovering his family’s secret tommy gun war with 1930s gangsters like John Dillinger and Baby Face Nelson.

title: The Road to Jonestown: Jim Jones and Peoples Temple
author: Jeff Guinn
description: From the author of Manson , the story of megalomaniac Indiana preacher Jim Jones, who was responsible for the Jonestown Massacre in the jungles of Guyana in 1978—the largest murder-suicide in American history.

title: Sunshine State
author: Sarah Gerard
description: A combination of memoir and essay collection which explores Florida as a microcosm of the most pressing economic and environmental perils haunting our society.

title: Every Night I Dream of Hell
author: Malcolm Mackay
description: A hard-boiled Scottish noir from the author of The Glasgow Trilogy.

title: Void Star
author: Zachary Mason
description: A science-fiction novel portraying a late-22nd-century Earth as a dark and desperate world populated by drones, slums, rising tides, longevity treatments, and artificial intelligence.

title: Hourglass
author: Dani Shapiro
description: A memoir about marriage and memory, about the frailty and elasticity of our most essential bonds, and about the accretion, over time, of both sorrow and love.

title: Music of the Ghosts
author: Vaddey Ratner
description: A novel about a woman who returns to Cambodia, the country she fled as a child during the Khmer Rouge regime, to speak to a man who claims to have been in prison with her father.

title: Too Much and Not the Mood
author: Durga Chew-Bose
description: A debut collection of personal essays about identity and culture.

title: Tell Me How It Ends: An Essay in 40 Questions
author: Valeria Luiselli
description: From the author of The Story of My Teeth , an essay focusing on the damning confrontation between the American dream and the reality of undocumented children seeking a new life in the US.

title: Exes
author: Max Winter
description: A tragicomic novel about a Rhode Island man trying to process his brother’s suicide by annotating the memories of the quirky people who knew him.

title: Dig If You Will the Picture: Funk, Sex, God and Genius in the Music of Prince
author: Ben Greenman
description: A unique and kaleidoscopic look into the life, legacy, and electricity of the pop legend Prince and his wideranging impact on our culture.

title: Make Trouble
author: John Waters
description: Originally a speech given to the graduating students of the Rhode Island School of Design, Make Trouble is an illustrated manifesto from the filmmaker and pop culture icon John Waters.

title: Letterman: The Last Giant of Late Night
author: Jason Zinoman
description: New York Times comedy critic Jason Zinoman delivers the definitive story of the life and artistic legacy of David Letterman.

title: The Givers: Wealth, Power, and Philanthropy in a New Gilded Age
author: David Callahan
description: An inside look at the secretive world of elite philanthropists––and how they're quietly wielding ever more power to shape American life in ways both good and bad.

title: The Souls of China: The Return of Religion After Mao
author: Ian Johnson
description: From the Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist, a portrait of religion in China today—its history, the spiritual traditions of its Eastern and Western faiths, and the ways in which it is influencing China’s future.

title: The Stars Are Fire
author: Anita Shreve
description: A novel about the aftermath of the Great Fires of Maine in 1947, told from the perspective of Grace, a housewife in a struggling marraige who finds a chance to restart her life in the wake of the disaster.

title: Where the Water Goes: Life and Death Along the Colorado River
author: David Owen
description: A downstream adventure into the heart of one of America’s most important water systems examining where our water comes from and where it all goes.

title: The New Urban Crisis
author: Richard Florida
description: From the author of The Creative Class . A book about how our cities are increasing inequality, deepening segregation, and failing the middle class, as well as a diagnosis of our economic ills and a prescription for more inclusive cities capable of ensuring growth and prosperity for all.

title: An American Sickness
author: Elisabeth Rosenthal
description: An investigation into our dysfunctional healthcare system and a proposal as to how it can be fixed.

title: The Shadow Land
author: Elizabeth Kostova
description: A novel form the author of The Historian . Having traveled to Sofia, Bulgaria, hoping that life abroad will salve the wounds left by the loss of her beloved brother, a woman comes into possession of a mysterious urn and sets out to discover its meaning.

title: Long Black Veil
author: Jennifer Finney Boylan
description: In this thriller, a night of post-college mischief between six friends turns into a haunting cold case.

title: One Perfect Lie
author: Lisa Scottoline
description: A fraudulent teacher enters into the staff of Central Valley High School and a trail of mysteries follow.

title: Such Small Hands
author: Andrés Barba, trans. by Lisa Dillman
description: Life changes at the orphanage the day seven-year-old Marina shows up. She is different from the other girls: at once an outcast and object of fascination. As Marina struggles to find her place, she invents a game whose rules are dictated by a haunting violence.

title: An Echo of Murder
author: Anne Perry
description: In the twenty-third novel of the William Monk series, Anne Perry delves into the diverse population of Victorian London, whose disparate communities force Monk to rethink his investigative techniques — lest he be caught in the crosshairs of violent bigotry.

title: No One Is Coming To Save Us
author: Stephanie Powell Watts
description: A Great Gatsby reboot focusing on the wounds of a down-and-out African-American family in the contemporary South.

title: American War
author: Omar El Akkad
description: A dystopian novel about a second American Civil War, a devastating plague, and one family caught deep in the middle—a story that asks what might happen if America were to turn its most devastating policies and deadly weapons upon itself.

title: Leo Durocher: Baseball's Prodigal Son
author: Paul Dickson
description: The first full biography of Leo Durocher, one of the most colorful and important figures in baseball history.

title: The Evangelicals: The Struggle to Shape America
author: Frances FitzGerald
description: From Pulitzer Prize-winner FitzGerald, a history of the Evangelical movement in America—from the Puritan era to the 2016 presidential election.

title: Nevertheless
author: Alec Baldwin
description: A memoir from the outspoken actor, chronicling the highs and lows of his life and career.

title: What It Means When a Man Falls From the Sky
author: Lesley Nneka Arimah
description: A speculative debut collection, focusing on young women in Nigeria, which explores the ties that bind parents and children, husbands and wives, lovers and friends to one another and to the places they call home.

title: Somebody With a Little Hammer
author: Mary Gaitskill
description: A collection of essays and reviews spanning two decades on matters literary, social, cultural, and personal from acclaimed author Gaitskill.

title: Prince Charles: The Passions and Paradoxes of an Improbable Life
author: Sally Bendell Smith
description: From the author of Elizabeth the Queen comes the first major biography of Prince Charles in more than twenty years.

title: Unwanted Advances: Sexual Paranoia Comes to Campus
author: Laura Kipnis
description: A polemic, from feminist cultural critic and professor Kipnis, arguing that the stifling sense of sexual danger sweeping American campuses doesn't empower women, it impedes the fight for gender equality.

title: Marlena
author: Julie Buntin
description: A coming of age novel about the intense friendship between two teenage girls living in rural Michigan town.

title: Foxlowe
author: Eleanor Wasserberg
description: A gothic thriller about a child raised in a insidious commune on the English moors.

title: The Gatekeepers: How the White House Chiefs of Staff Define Every Presidency
author: Chris Whipple
description: The first in-depth, behind-the-scenes look at the White House Chiefs of Staff, whose actions—and inactions—have defined the course of our country.

title: A Little More Human
author: Fiona Maazel
description: A novel that blends science fiction, satire, farce, and literary mystery. A mind-reading nursing assistant who moonlights as a superhero wakes up from an alcohol-induced stupor to photographs which seem to show him assaulting an unknown woman.

title: The Islamic Enlightenment: The Struggle Between Faith and Reason, 1798 to Modern Times
author: Christopher de Bellaigue
description: An account of the political and social reformations that transformed the lands of Islam in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

title: Thunder in the Mountains: Chief Joseph, Oliver Otis Howard, and the Nez Perce War
author: Daniel J. Sharfstein
description: The story of Chief Joseph, Oliver Otis Howard, and the Nez Perce War of 1877 between the US army and several bands of the New Perce tribe of Native Americans.

title: Living in the Weather of the World
author: Richard Bausch
description: A new collection of stories from an iconic writer of American short fiction.

title: What to Do About the Solomons
author: Bethany Ball
description: A multigenerational family saga set in Israel, New York, and Los Angeles that explores the secrets and gossip-filled lives of a kibbutz community near Jerusalem

title: Hallelujah Anyway: Rediscovering Mercy
author: Anne Lamott
description: A book of essays from spiritual author Lamott exploring the idea of mercy and how we can embrace it.

title: The Zoo: The Wild and Wonderful Tale of the Founding of London Zoo
author: Isobel Charman
description: Set in the heart of swirling, Dickensian London, the history of a unique institution and the incredible characters?human and animal?that populated it.

title: Tell Me How This Ends Well
author: David Samuel Levinson
description: A darkly comic novel. In a near-future fraught with violent anti-Semitism, three disgruntled siblings at a family Passover in Los Angeles focus on patricide.

title: Dark Side of the Moon
author: Les Wood
description: Boddice, a crime lord looking over his shoulder for good reason, has assembled an unlikely band of misfit crooks to steal a famous diamond worth millions, known as The Dark Side of the Moon.

title: The Twelve Lives of Samuel Hawley
author: Hannah Tinti
description: A coming of age novel about a girl whose tortured, career criminal father tries to make a new life for the pair in the hometown of his late wife.

title: Richard Nixon: The Life
author: John A. Farrell
description: An unsparing biography of "our darkest president."

title: Casey Stengel: Baseball's Greatest Character
author: Marty Appel
description: Sports journalist Appel investigates the baseball career and personal life of the legendary Casey Stengel.

title: The Women in the Castle
author: Jessica Shattuck
description: Set at the end of World War II, in a crumbling Bavarian castle that once played host to all of German high society, a story of three widows, resisters of Nazism, whose lives and fates become intertwined.

title: My Darling Detective
author: Howard Norman
description: In Nova Scotia in 1977, an aspiring librarian strives to get to the bottom of a decades-old murder in this wry foray into noir by National Book Award-finalist Norman.

title: Compass
author: Mathias Enard, Trans. by Charlotte Mandell
description: The winner of France's Prix Goncourt award. A novel that looks at the intersections between Europe and the Islamic World, told over the course of a single fitful night, from the perspective of an Austrian musicologist worrying about his health.

title: Sonora
author: Hannah Lillith Assadi
description: A fevered, lyrical debut about two young women drawn into an ever-intensifying friendship set against the stark, haunted landscape of the Sonoran desert and the ecstatic frenzy of New York City.

title: The Ambulance Drivers: Hemingway, Dos Passos, and a Friendship Made and Lost in War
author: James McGrath Morris
description: After meeting for the first time on the front lines of World War I, two aspiring writers forge an intense twenty-year friendship and write some of America's greatest novels, giving voice to a "lost generation" shaken by war.

title: A Really Big Lunch
author: Jim Harrison
description: A collection of exuberant food writing and meditations on life from the late, great Jim Harrison.

title: Bright Air Black
author: David Vann
description: A lyrical retelling of the life of one of ancient mythology’s most fascinating and notorious women, Medea, and her exploits with Jason and the Argonauts.

title: Ice Ghosts: The Epic Hunt for the Lost Franklin Expedition
author: Paul Watson
description: The true story of the greatest cold case in Arctic history?and how the rare mix of marine science and Inuit knowledge finally led to the recent discovery of the shipwrecks, from Pulitzer Prize–winning photojournalist Watson.

title: The Collapsing Empire
author: John Scalzi
description: The first book in a new Space Opera series, centered around battle between dynastic mercantile families, and The Flow, an extradimensional field available at certain points in space-time, which can take us to other planets around other stars.

title: The Novel of the Century: The Extraordinary Adventure of Les Misérables
author: David Bellos
description: The definitive biography of one of the world's most iconic novels.

title: Mississippi Blood
author: Greg Iles
description: The final installment in the Iles' Natchez Burning trilogy, focusing on Penn Cage, his family, and the enemies bent on destroying them.

title: Wait Till You See Me Dance
author: Deb Olin Unferth
description: A collection of sharp-edged short stories, blending the normal with the weird, from the NBCC Award-winning author.

title: The Tea Girl of Hummingbird Lane
author: Lisa See
description: A woman from the Akha tribe of China’s Yunnan province becomes a tea entrepreneur as her daughter grows up in California.

title: The Devil and Webster
author: Jean Hanff Korelitz
description: The first female president of an elite New England college grapples with student protest in this satirical novel.

title: No One Cares About Crazy People
author: Ron Powers
description: A social history of mental illness in America paired with the deeply personal story of Pulitzer Prize-winner Powers's sons' battles with schizophrenia.

title: The First Love Story: Adam, Eve, and Us
author: Bruce Feiler
description: A journey across four continents and 4,000 years exploring how Adam and Eve introduced the idea of love into the world.

title: The Spider Network: The Wild Story of a Math Genius, a Gang of Backstabbing Bankers, and One of the Greatest Scams in Financial History
author: David Enrich
description: The true story of how a math genius named Tom Hayes, a handful of outrageous confederates, and a deeply corrupt banking system ignited one of the greatest financial scandals in history.

title: Our Short History
author: Lauren Grodstein
description: A novel structured as a book written by a dying woman to her six-year-old, so that he will have a guide to life without her.

title: Ike and McCarthy
author: David A. Nichols
description: The story of how President Dwight Eisenhower masterminded the downfall of the anti-Communist demagogue Senator Joseph McCarthy.

title: A Colony in a Nation
author: Chris Hayes
description: A book by MSNBC's Chris Hayes about U.S. race relations, primarily the black experience, and law and order as they are experienced across the country.

title: The Moth Presents All These Wonders
author: Ed. by Catherine Burns
description: Celebrating the 20th anniversary of the live storytelling series The Moth, 45 true stories about risk, courage, and facing the unknown, drawn from the best ever told on their stages.

title: Stranger in a Strange Land
author: George Prochnik
description: Taking his lead from his subject, Gershom Scholem––the 20th century thinker who cracked open Jewish theology and history with a radical reading of Kabbalah––Prochnik, a convert to Judaism, combines biography and memoir to counter our contemporary political crisis with a reimagining of the future of Israel.

title: A Simple Favor
author: Darcey Bell
description: A single mother's life is turned upside down when her best friend vanishes in this debut thriller in the vein of Gone Girl and The Girl on the Train .

title: Basic Income: A Radical Proposal for a Free Society and a Sane Economy
author: Philippe Van Parijs and Yannick Vanderborght
description: Two professors of economic and political science, make an ethical and philosophical argument for the provision of universal basic income.

title: A Closed and Common Orbit
author: Becky Chambers
description: A character-driven Space Opera focusing on the motley crew of the spaceship Wayfarer in this space opera—the sequel to Chambers' The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet .

title: Pax Americana
author: Kurt Baumeister
description: 2034: Evangelical secret agents, fast food moguls, the voice of God in computer software, violence in the Bermuda Triangle! George W. Bush's foreign policy vindicated by a quick victory in Iraq, lucrative invasions of Egypt and Syria followed, bringing unparalleled prosperity to America and setting off thirty years of right-wing rule.

title: The Idiot
author: Elif Batuman
description: The debut novel from New Yorker staff writer Batuman. The year is 1995, and email is new. Selin, the contemplative daughter of Turkish immigrants, arrives for her freshman year at Harvard and begins an email correspondence with Ivan, an older mathematics student from Hungary.

title: White Tears
author: Hari Kunzru
description: A ghost story, a murder mystery, a meditation on race and cultural appropriation, and a love letter to all the forgotten geniuses of American music. White Tears focuses on two white, twenty-something New Yorkers obsessed with tracking down rare recordings.

title: You Say to Brick: The Life of Louis Kahn
author: Wendy Lesser
description: A major exploration of the architect Louis Kahn's life and work.

title: The Rules Do Not Apply
author: Ariel Levy
description: A memoir from New Yorker staff writer Levy, about overcoming dramatic loss and finding reinvention.

title: New York 2140
author: Kim Stanley Robinson
description: A Cli-Fi novel set in New York in the year 2140, focusing on several residents of an apartment building in Manhattan after global warming has caused almost all of the world’s coastlines to go underwater.

title: Temporary People
author: Deepak Unnikrishnan
description: A novel in linked stories in which guest workers of the United Arab Emirates embody multiple worlds and identities and long for home. Winner of the inaugural Restless Books Prize for New Immigrant Writing

title: Heretics
author: Leonardo Padura, Trans. by Anna Kushner
description: A sweeping detective novel of art theft, anti-Semitism, contemporary Cuba, and crime from a renowned Cuban author.

title: Sorry to Disrupt the Peace
author: Patrick Cottrell
description: A darkly-comic debut novel. Helen Moran is thirty-two years old, single, and partially employed as a guardian of troubled young people in New York. Upon hearing that her adoptive brother has committed suicide, she returns to Milwaukee to search for answers.

title: Marilyn in Manhattan: Her Year of Joy
author: Elizabeth Winder
description: Marilyn in Manhattan focuses on a year the star spent in New York recalibrating her career and diving into theater, art, and literature.

title: The Djinn Falls in Love
author: Ed. by Mahvesh Murad & Jared Shurin
description: A collection of new and classic tales of the fearsome Djinn, from bestselling, award-winning and breakthrough international writers.

title: The Fall of Lisa Bellow
author: Susan Perabo
description: When a middle school girl is abducted in broad daylight, a fellow student and witness to the crime copes with the tragedy in an unforgettable way.

title: The Gulf: The Making of An American Sea
author: Jack E. Davis
description: A sweeping environmental history of the Gulf of Mexico that considers the ravages of nature and man on the region.

title: Jerzy
author: Jerome Charyn
description: A fictionalized biography. The rise and fall of controversial Polish-American novelist Jerzy Kosinski emerges in an offbeat way through real and imagined figures in his life.

title: The Vine That Ate The South
author: J.D. Wilkes
description: A wild, Southern Gothic fantasia set in a forgotten part of western Kentucky about two men on a quest to confirm a local legend.

title: The Crisis of the Middle-Class Constitution
author: Ganesh Sitaraman
description: Ganesh Sitaraman argues that a strong and sizable middle class is a prerequisite for America’s constitutional system.

title: Charlton Heston: Hollywood's Last Icon
author: Marc Eliot
description: A biography of one of the legends of Hollywood's Golden Age.

title: Martin Luther: Renegade and Prophet
author: Lyndal Roper
description: A substantial new look at the life of Martin Luther, published to coincide with the 500-year anniversary of his revolutionary theses.

title: The Great Cat and Dog Massacre: The Real Story of World War Two's Unknown Tragedy
author: Hilda Kean
description: In September 1939, four hundred thousand cats and dogs were massacred in Britain. The government, vets, and animal charities all advised against this killing. This is the story of why thousands of British citizens lined up to voluntarily euthanize household pets.

title: The Family Gene
author: Joselin Linder
description: A memoir of a young woman’s quest to uncover the truth about her likely fatal genetic disorder that opens a window onto the exploding field of genomic medicine.

title: The Wanderers
author: Meg Howrey
description: A genre-bending novel set in the very near future in which three astronauts and their families must endure the effects of a training simulation for a pioneering deep-space mission.

title: One of the Boys
author: Daniel Magariel
description: A debut novel, set in the stark landscape of New Mexico, about about two young brothers contending with the love they have for their abusive, drug addict father.

title: Before the War
author: Fay Weldon
description: A comic novel set in London in 1922 which tells the story of Vivian, the intelligent but tall and ungainly only daughter of the head of a major publishing house, and her marriage to a struggling young writer.

title: Bleaker House
author: Nell Stevens
description: A girl, a laptop, and a waddle of penguins. A memoir in which a young writer, aiming to find somewhere to finally finish her novel, ends up on a frozen island at the bottom of the world.

title: Swimmer Among the Stars
author: Kanishk Tharoor
description: An imaginative debut short story collection which draws equally from ancient history and current events.

title: The Forgotten Girls: A Stevens and Windermere Novel
author: Owen Laukkanen
description: Kirk Stevens and Carla Windermere investigate the murder of a runaway found on the snowy railroad tracks in Boundry County, Idaho.

title: Exit West
author: Mohsin Hamid
description: From the author of The Reluctant Fundamentalist , a love story that imagines the forces that transform ordinary people into refugees -- and the impossible choices that follow -- as they’re driven from their homes to the uncertain embrace of new lands.

title: South and West: From a Notebook
author: Joan Didion
description: From the National Book Award-winning author: two extended excerpts from her never-before-seen notebooks––writings that offer a glimpse into the mind and process of a legendary writer.

title: The Stranger in the Woods
author: Michael Finkel
description: The true story of a man who lived alone in the woods of Maine for 27 years, not out of anger at the world, but simply because he preferred to live on his own.

title: Ill Will
author: Dan Chaon
description: Two sensational unsolved crimes—one in the past, another in the present—are linked by one man’s memory and self-deception in this dark literary mystery from National Book Award finalist Dan Chaon.

title: The Night Ocean
author: Paul La Farge
description: A novel about secrets and scandals, psychiatry and pulp fiction, inspired by the lives of H.P. Lovecraft and his circle.

title: All Grown Up
author: Jami Attenberg
description: From the author of The Middlesteins comes a comic novel about a thirty-nine-year-old single, childfree woman who defies convention as she seeks connection.

title: Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich
author: Norman Ohler
description: A narrative that explores a surprising perspective on World War II: Nazi Germany and Hitler's all-consuming reliance on drugs.

title: The Mother of All Questions
author: Rebecca Solnit
description: In a follow-up to her national bestseller Men Explain Things to Me , Rebecca Solnit offers commentary on women who refuse to be silenced, misogynistic violence, the fragile masculinity of the literary canon, the gender binary, the recent history of rape jokes, and much more.

title: The Hearts of Men
author: Nickolas Butler
description: A novel of intertwining friendships and families set in the Northwoods of Wisconsin at a beloved Boy Scout summer camp.

title: Madame President: The Extraordinary Journey of Ellen Johnson Sirleaf
author: Helene Cooper
description: The story of Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, leader of the Liberian women’s movement, winner of the Nobel Peace Prize, and the first democratically elected female president in African history.

title: Spaceman of Bohemia
author: Jaroslav Kalfar
description: Orphaned as a boy, raised in the Czech countryside by his doting grandparents, Jakub Procházka has risen from small-time scientist to become the country's first astronaut. When a dangerous solo mission to Venus offers him both the chance at heroism he's dreamt of, and a way to atone for his father's sins as a Communist informer, he ventures boldly into the vast unknown.

title: The One-Eyed Man
author: Ron Currie
description: A man whose wife has recently passed away becomes more and more unhinged, refusing to see things in anything but their most literal form. He is given a reality television show where he travels around America asking people invasive questions.

title: Dear Ijeawele, or A Feminist Manifesto in Fifteen Suggestions
author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
description: A few years ago, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie received a letter from a dear friend from childhood, asking her how to raise her baby girl as a feminist. Dear Ijeawele is Adichie's letter of response.

title: The Dark and Other Love Stories
author: Deborah Willis
description: Canadian story-writer Willis' second collection. Thirteen stories which "exist on the edge of danger, where landscapes melt into dreamscapes and every house is haunted."

title: The Weight of This World
author: David Joy
description: An "Appalachian Noir" focusing on Thad Bloom, a damaged veteran of the war in Afghanistan. Thad returns to a dilapidated trailer in North Carolina to settle down when he and a childhood friend stumble upon a windfall of drugs and cash after witnessing the accidental death of their drug dealer.

title: The Erstwhile
author: B. Catling
description: The middle volume in Catling’s alternate history/fantasy trilogy, which began with 2015's The Vorrh , focusing on a a mythical woodland in colonial Africa and the host of creatures that dwell therein.

title: In the Name of the Family
author: Sarah Dunant
description: A novel focusing on the exploits of one of history's most notorious families: the Borgias. A sequel to 2012's Blood and Beauty .

title: March 1917: On the Brink of War and Revolution
author: Will Englund
description: A history of the month that transformed the world’s greatest nations as Russia faced revolution and America entered World War I.

title: Quicksand
author: Malin Persson Giolito
description: Named the Best Swedish Crime Novel of the Year by the Swedish Crime Writers Academy. A mass shooting has taken place at a prep school in Stockholm’s wealthiest suburb. Eighteen-year-old Maja Norberg has spent nine months in jail awaiting trial. Now the time has come for her to enter the courtroom.

title: This Long Pursuit: Reflections of a Romantic Biographer
author: Richard Holmes
description: A meditation on the art of biography that fuses the author’s own experiences with a history of the genre and explores the relationship between fact and fiction.

title: The One-Cent Magenta
author: James Barron
description: An inside look at the obsessive, secretive, and often bizarre world of high-profile stamp collecting, told through the journey of the world’s most sought-after stamp.

title: The Kingdom
author: Emmanuel Carrère
description: A sweeping fictional account of the early Christians, whose unlikely beliefs conquered the world, and an account of the author's own spiritual journal.

title: Ties
author: Domenico Starnone, Trans. by Jhumpa Lahiri
description: A short novel set in Naples about the after-effects of an affair, and subsequent emotional rupture, on a marriage.

title: Catalina Eddy
author: Daniel Pyne
description: A California noir separated into three linked novellas, each focused on a homicide case.

title: Irresistible: The Rise of Addictive Technology and the Business of Keeping Us Hooked
author: Adam Alter
description: Alter, a professor of psychology and marketing at NYU, tracks the rise of behavioral addiction, and explains why so many of today's products are irresistible.

title: Celine
author: Peter Heller
description: The story of Celine, an elegant, aristocratic Brooklyn private eye who specializes in reuniting families, trying to make amends for a loss in her own past.

title: The Accusation: Forbidden Stories from Inside North Korea
author: Bandi, Trans. by Deborah Smith
description: The first work of fiction to be smuggled out of North Korea. Set during the period of Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il’s leadership, the seven stories that make up The Accusation give voice to people living under this most bizarre and horrifying of dictatorships.

title: Eveningland
author: Michael Knight
description: A collection of interconnected stories exploring the lives of characters living in and around Mobile, Ala., in the years preceding the destruction wrought by a fictional hurricane.

title: Wish Lanterns: Young Lives in New China
author: Alec Ash
description: A deep dive exploration into the lives of six Han Chinese Millennials.

title: Edgar & Lucy
author: Victor Lodato
description: A novel by the author of Mathilda Savitch , about the life of a young albino boy in suburban New Jersey who is permanently marked by two tragedies.

title: Camanchaca
author: Diego Zúñiga
description: A long drive across Chile's Atacama desert, traversing 'the worn-out puzzle' of a broken family—a young man's corrosive intimacy with his mother, the obtrusive cheer of his absentee father, his uncle's unexplained death—occupies the heart of this novel from Chilean author and journalist Zúñiga.

title: The Underworld
author: Kevin Canty
description: Inspired by one of America's worst mining disasters, a novel which follows a disparate cast of characters in the mining town of Silverton, Idaho, before and after a disastrous fire in the mine that changes their lives.

title: Dadland
author: Keggie Carew
description: Winner of the 2016 Costa Award for Biography. Blending personal memoir, biography, and World War II military history, the author tells the story of her extraordinary father, from his time as a daring British Special Forces operative in WWII, to his chaotic personal life and eventual decline.

title: Whereas
author: Layli Long Soldier
description: A NBCC Award-winning poetry collection which confronts the coercive language of the United States government in its responses, treaties, and apologies to Native American peoples and tribes, and reflects that language in its officiousness and duplicity back on its perpetrators.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel: The Fates of Human Societies
author: Jared Diamond
description: In this book, book, Jared Diamond argues that geographical and environmental factors shaped the modern world. Guns, Germs, and Steel chronicles the way that the modern world came to be and stunningly dismantles racially based theories of human history. Winner of the Pulitzer Prize, the Phi Beta Kappa Award in Science, the Rhone-Poulenc Prize, and the Commonwealth club of California's Gold Medal.

title: Rabbit Cake
author: Annie Hartnett
description: In this darkly comic debut novel, a young girl named Elvis tries to figure out her place in the world after the death of her mother.

title: The Invention of Angela Carter
author: Edmund Gordon
description: The story of how Angela Carter invented herself – as a new kind of woman and a new kind of writer – and how she came to write such seductive and distinctive masterworks as The Bloody Chamber , Nights at the Circus , and Wise Children .

title: Flâneuse
author: Lauren Elkin
description: Part cultural meander, part memoir, Flâneuse takes us on a distinctly cosmopolitan jaunt that begins in New York, where Elkin grew up, and transports us to Paris via Venice, Tokyo, and London, all cities in which she’s lived.

title: Abandon Me
author: Melissa Febos
description: A memoir in essays, by the author of Whip Smart , that explores the many ways identity and art are shaped by love and loss.

title: Robert Lowell, Setting the River on Fire
author: Kay Redfield Jamison
description: A psychological account of Robert Lowell’s life and mind as well as a narrative of the illness that so affected him.

title: Jonathan Swift: The Reluctant Rebel
author: John Stubbs
description: A biography of the famous satirist and author of Gulliver's Travels .

title: To Be a Machine: Adventures Among Cyborgs, Utopians, Hackers, and the Futurists Solving the Modest Problem of Death
description: An eye-opening journey into a world of visionaries, billionaires, and eccentrics harnessing technology for nothing less than the salvation of mankind.

title: Waking Lions
author: Ayelet Gundar-Goshen
description: Having hit and abandoned an Eritrean migrant on a lonely desert road in present-day Negev, Neurosurgeon Eitan finds his life plunged into chaos when the dead man’s wife, Sirkit, seeks him out to blackmail him with a strange demand.

title: Harmless Like You
author: Rowan Hisayo Buchanan
description: A debut novel set across New York, Connecticut, and Berlin, following Yuki Oyama, a Japanese girl fighting to make it as an artist, and Yuki’s son Jay who, as an adult in the present day, is forced to confront his mother’s abandonment of him when he was only two years old.

title: On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons from the Twentieth Century
author: Timothy Snyder
description: Twenty lessons on how to recognize and resist political tyranny.

title: Animals Strike Curious Poses
author: Elena Passarello
description: 16 essays — traversing history, myth, science, and more — which investigate famous animals named and immortalized by humans.

title: Divided We Stand
author: Marjorie J. Spruill
description: The story of the battle over women's rights and family values that polarized American politics, organized around the 1977 National Women's Conference.

title: Agents of Dreamland
author: Caitlin R. Kiernan
description: A supernatural noir novella in which two agents of a shadowy government group pursue the cult leader.

title: The Complacent Class: The Self-Defeating Quest for the American Dream
author: Tyler Cowen
description: Economist Cowen seeks to persuade readers that American citizens have gotten overly complacent, that a crisis point is near, and that a widespread rebellion may alter the existing order.

title: The Horseman
author: Tim Pears
description: The first novel in a sweeping historical trilogy, beginning in rural, pre-WWI England.

title: The Gene Machine
author: Bonnie Rochman
publisher: Scientific American / Farrar, Straus and Giroux
description: An exploration of the promise and peril of having children in an age of genetic tests and interventions.

title: Lilac Girls
author: Martha Hall Kelly
description: The female prisoners who underwent horrific surgical experiments at the Ravensbrück concentration camp became known as 'the Rabbits.' Kelly's novel rotates portraits of two real-life women involved in this story (an American named Caroline Ferriday, who led a crusade on behalf of the survivors, and Herta Oberheuser, the Nazi surgeon who performed the gruesome operations) with that of a fictional Polish woman, Kasia, loosely based on two of the actual Rabbits.

title: The Hate U Give
author: Angie Thomas
description: After witnessing her friend's death at the hands of a police officer, Starr Carter's life is complicated when the police and a local drug lord try to intimidate her in an effort to learn what happened the night Kahlil died.

title: The Schooldays of Jesus
author: J. M. Coetzee
description: The sequel to The Childhood of Jesus , continuing the journey of Davíd, Simón, and Inés--an unconventional family unit, still on the run through a nameless Spanish-speaking country, now working as farm laborers.

title: Dear Friend, from My Life I Write to You in Your Life
author: Yiyun Li
description: In her first memoir of interconnected essays, award-winning novelist Yiyun Li offers a journey of recovery through literature: a letter from a writer to like-minded readers.

title: A Horse Walks into a Bar
author: David Grossman
description: A searing short novel about the damaged life of a stand-up comic, as revealed in the course of one evening’s performance.

title: Why I Am Not a Feminist: A Feminist Manifesto
author: Jessa Crispin
description: Outspoken critic and Bookslut founder Jessa Crispin offers a searing rejection of contemporary 'lifestyle' feminism and a bracing manifesto for revolution.

title: High Noon: The Hollywood Blacklist and the Making of an American Classic
author: Glenn Frankel
description: The story behind the classic movie High Noon and the toxic political climate in which it was created.

title: A Piece of the World
author: Christina Baker Kline
description: A novel of friendship, passion, and art --focusing on a young disabled woman in mid-century Maine-- inspired by Andrew Wyeth’s mysterious and iconic painting Christina’s World.

title: The World to Come
author: Jim Shepard
description: A collection of ten historical short stories from the National Book Award-nominted writer.

title: Setting Free the Kites
author: Alex George
description: A coming-of-age novel set mostly at an amusement park on the coast of Maine, where two young boys find solace in friendship amid their own family tragedies.

title: Unwarranted: Policing Without Permission
author: Barry Friedman
description: An NYU law professor illuminates many of the often ignored issues surrounding how we police in America and highlights why reform is so urgently needed.

title: Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: From the author of Sapiens , an examination of how our unparalleled ability to control the world around us is turning us into something new.

title: I See You
author: Clare Mackintosh
description: The author of I Let You Go propels readers into a dark and claustrophobic thriller, in which a normal, everyday woman finds herself being stalked on her train commute.

title: Other People: Takes & Mistakes
author: David Shields
description: An assortment of musings, cultural critiques, and memoir from celebrated essayist Shields. An investigation of otherness: the need for one person to understand another person completely, the impossibility of any such absolute knowing, and the erotics of this separation.

title: Running
author: Cara Hoffman
description: A novel about an acclaimed poet and professor as he reminisces about his unscrupulous but exciting youth working in Greece and the people who still haunt him.

title: Shining City
author: Tom Rosenstiel
description: A debut political thriller about two DC fixers hired to vet a Supreme Court nominee, and the series of killings that overlaps with their investigation.

title: Things We Lost in the Fire
author: Mariana Enriquez
description: A collection of female-driven, macabre and politically-charged short stories set in contemporary Argentina.

title: Last Day On Earth
author: Eric Puchner
description: A collection of short stories, ranging from the domestic to the surreal, that look at the cracks underneath the surface of modern life.

title: The Inkblots: Hermann Rorschach, His Iconic Test, and the Power of Seeing
author: Damion Searls
description: The untold story of psychiatrist Hermann Rorschach and his famous inkblot test.

title: Lincoln in the Bardo
author: George Saunders
description: The first novel from celebrated short story writer George Saunders. An historical Buddhist ghost story set in a Georgetown cemetery where a grieving Abraham Lincoln goes to mourn the recent death of his young son, Willie.

title: Cannibalism: A Perfectly Natural History
author: Bill Schutt
description: A wry investigation into our new understanding of cannibalism’s role in biology, anthropology, and history.

title: Shadowbahn
author: Steve Erickson
description: Set in a dystopian near future, Shadowbahn is a chronicle of a weird road trip, a provocative work of alternative history, and a discography of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. A meditation on the meaning of American identity and of America itself.

title: The Dime
author: Kathleen Kent
description: A gritty crime novel about a tough lesbian detective from Brooklyn who takes on the Dallas criminal underground.

title: Insomniac City
author: Bill Hayes
description: A celebration of what Bill Hayes calls 'the evanescent, the eavesdropped, the unexpected' of life in New York City, and an intimate glimpse of his relationship with the late Oliver Sacks.

title: The Dark Flood Rises
author: Margaret Drabble
description: A rumination on what it means to grow old. The novel focuses on Fran, an expert on housing for senior citizens who is herself in her seventies, and her preoccupation with mortality.

title: On Turpentine Lane
author: Elinor Lipman
description: A romantic comedy in which a professional thank-you-note writer buys a house with a past and gets more than she bargained for.

title: We'll Always Have Casablanca: The Life, Legend, and Afterlife of Hollywood's Most Beloved Movie
author: Noah Isenberg
description: For the 75th anniversary of its premiere?the story of how Casablanca was made and why it remains the most beloved of Hollywood films.

title: My Favorite Thing Is Monsters
author: Emil Ferris
description: 15 years in the making, a fictional graphic diary of a 10-year-old girl trying to solve a murder, set against the tumultuous political backdrop of late ’60s Chicago.

title: Glass House: The 1% Economy and the Shattering of the All-American Town
author: Brian Alexander
description: In 1947, Forbes magazine declared Lancaster, Ohio the epitome of the all-American town. Today it is damaged, discouraged, and fighting for its future. In Glass House , journalist Brian Alexander uses the story of one town to show how seeds sown 35 years ago have sprouted to give us Trumpism, inequality, and an eroding national cohesion.

title: There Are More Beautiful Things than Beyoncé
author: Morgan Parker
description: There Are More Beautiful Things Than Beyoncé uses political and pop-cultural references as a framework to explore 21st century black American womanhood and its complexities: performance, depression, isolation, exoticism, racism, femininity, and politics.

title: Identity Unknown: Rediscovering Seven American Women Artists
author: Donna Seaman
description: A rediscovery of seven forgotten American women artists.

title: A Divided Spy
author: Charles Cumming
description: A tale of modern espionage in which former MI6 agent Thomas Kell, who retired following the assassination of his girlfriend, faces off against a handsome and charismatic Russian double agent.

title: All Back Full
author: Robert Lopez
description: Told in a genre-defying style that melds novel with play, All Back Full charts one day in a marriage at once usual and unusual, exploring what we say to each other when we say nothing, and the ways we speak to each other without words.

title: We Were the Lucky Ones
author: Georgia Hunter
description: A novel, based on the author's own family history, about a prosperous, educated Jewish family living in Radom, Poland, and what happens to them after the Germans invade in 1939.

title: Age of Anger
author: Pankaj Mishra
description: How can we explain the origins of the great wave of paranoid hatreds that seem inescapable in our close-knit world? In Age of Anger , Pankaj Mishra answers our bewilderment by casting his gaze back to the eighteenth century before leading us to the present.

title: The Refugees
author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
description: A collection of short stories, focusing on the experiences of refugees, from the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of The Sympathizer .

title: A Separation
author: Katie Kitamura
description: A suspenseful, psychological novel about a woman who travels to a remote part of Greece to find out what has happened to her estranged husband.

title: A Book of American Martyrs
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: The story of two very different and yet intimately linked American families. Luther Dunphy is an ardent Evangelical who envisions himself as acting out God’s will when he assassinates an abortion provider in his small Ohio town while Augustus Voorhees, the idealistic but self-regarding doctor who is killed, leaves behind a wife and children scarred and embittered by grief.

title: Universal Harvester
author: John Darnielle
description: A novel centered around a small, independent video store in the town of Nevada, Iowa, in the late 1990s whose tapes start coming back with mysterious and sometimes terrifying clips spliced in the middle.

title: Norse Mythology
author: Neil Gaiman
description: Neil Gaiman has long been inspired by ancient mythology in creating the fantastical realms of his fiction. Now he turns his attention back to the source, presenting a rendition of the great northern tales of Thor, Odin, Freya and Loki.

title: Autumn
author: Ali Smith
description: The first in a planned quartet of novels. Set in post-Brexit Britain, a young woman's platonic friendship with an older neighbor is at the heart of this meditation on aging, art, love, and affection.

title: Pachinko
author: Min Jin Lee
description: A sweeping saga of exceptional people in exile from a homeland they never knew and caught in the indifferent arc of history, following one Korean family through the 20th Century.

title: Black Edge: Inside Information, Dirty Money, and the Quest to Bring Down the Most Wanted Man on Wall Street
author: Sheelah Kolhatkar
description: The story of the billionaire trader Steven A. Cohen, the rise and fall of his hedge fund, SAC Capital, and the largest insider trading investigation in history.

title: Six Encounters with Lincoln: A President Confronts Democracy and Its Demons
author: Elizabeth Brown Pryor
description: An account of how Abraham Lincoln grappled with the challenges of leadership in an unruly democracy.

title: Elizabeth Bishop: A Miracle for Breakfast
author: Megan Marshall
description: An experimental biography of the poet Elizabeth Bishop, in which the lives of the subject and author are intertwined.

title: Powers of Darkness: The Lost Version of Dracula
author: Bram Stoker & Valdimar Ásmundsson, Trans. by Hans De Roos
description: The first ever translation into English of Bram Stoker and Vladimar Ásmundsson’s Makt Myrkranna , the significantly changed Icelandic version of Stoker's Dracula .

title: The Lonely Hearts Hotel
author: Heather O'Neill
description: Set in New York and Montreal at the outset of the Great Depression, a novel about two gifted orphans – in love with each other since they can remember – whose childhood talents allow them to rewrite their future.

title: My Utmost: A Devotional Memoir
author: Macy Halford
description: A memoir by a young woman from Dallas who moved to New York, exploring the Evangelical Christianity of her childhood and its meaning to her in the present through the classic daily devotional My Utmost for His Highest .

title: The One Inside
author: Sam Shepard
description: The first work of long fiction from the Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright, opening with a man alone in his bed in a trailer park in the desert, thinking back over his life.

title: The Vaccine Race: Science, Politics, and the Human Costs of Defeating Disease
author: Meredith Wadman
description: The controversial story of a major breakthrough in cell biology that led to the conquest of rubella and other devastating diseases.

title: Six Four
author: Hideo Yokoyama
description: A literary blockbuster in Japan in 2011. Fourteen years after a Japanese schoolgirl is kidnapped, the mystery remains unsolved. The police department’s press officer?Yoshinobu Mikami, a former detective who was involved in the original case and who is now himself the father of a missing daughter?is forced to revisit the botched investigation.

title: This Close to Happy
author: Daphne Merkin
description: A vivid memoir of the author's lifelong struggle with depression.

title: All Our Wrong Todays
author: Elan Mastai
description: In a techno-utopian alternate 2016, a down-on-his-luck young man travels back to 1965 and accidentally botches the moment of discovery that made the idyllic future possible.

title: Ghachar Ghochar
author: Vivek Shanbhag
description: A young man's close-knit family is nearly destitute when his uncle founds a successful spice company, changing their fortunes overnight. As they move from a cramped, ant-infested shack to a larger house on the other side of Bangalore, and try to adjust to a new way of life, the family dynamic begins to shift.

title: NK3
author: Michael Tolkin
description: A novel, from the author of The Player , set a dystopian Los Angeles devastated by a weaponized microbe that has been accidentally spread around the globe, deleting human identity.

title: Stalin and the Scientists: A History of Triumph and Tragedy, 1905-1953
author: Simon Ings
description: Stalin and the Scientists tells the story of the many gifted scientists who worked in Russia from the years leading up to the Revolution through the death of the 'Great Scientist' himself, Joseph Stalin. It weaves together the stories of scientists, politicians, and ideologues into an intimate and sometimes horrifying portrait of a state determined to remake the world.

title: Hit Makers: The Science of Popularity in an Age of Distraction
author: Derek Thompson
description: Atlantic senior editor Derek Thompson uncovers the hidden psychology of why we like what we like and reveals the economics of cultural markets that invisibly shape our lives.

title: 300 Arguments
author: Sarah Manguso
description: A collection of 300 aphorisms from one of our most prominent contemporary essayists.

title: The Twenty Days of Turin
author: Giorgio De Maria
description: Written during the height of the 1970s Italian domestic terror, a cult novel, with distinct echoes of Lovecraft and Borges, makes its English-language debut.

title: The Nature Fix: Why Nature Makes us Happier, Healthier, and More Creative
author: Florence Williams
description: An intrepid investigation into nature’s restorative benefits by Outside magazine journalist Florence Williams.

title: The Girl from the Metropol Hotel: Growing Up in Communist Russia
author: Ludmilla Petrushevskaya
description: The prizewinning memoir of iconic Russian writer Petrushevskaya, about coming of age as an enemy of the people and finding her voice in Stalinist Russia.

title: From Bacteria to Bach and Back
author: Daniel C. Dennett
description: One of America’s foremost philosophers offers a major new account of the origins of the conscious mind.

title: Can't Just Stop: An Investigation of Compulsions
author: Sharon Begley
description: The first book to examine the science behind both mild and extreme compulsive behavior—using case studies to understand its deeper meaning and reveal the truth about human compulsion.

title: All the Lives I Want: Essays About My Best Friends Who Happen to Be Famous Strangers
author: Alana Massey
description: From columnist and critic Alana Massey, a collection of essays examining the intersection of the personal with pop culture through the lives of pivotal female figures—from Sylvia Plath to Britney Spears.

title: Amiable With Big Teeth
author: Claude McKay
description: The newly discovered final novel by seminal Harlem Renaissance writer Claude McKay, a portrayal of life in 1930s Harlem and a historical protest for black freedom.

title: What You Don't Know
author: JoAnn Chaney
description: A crime novel in which the exploits of a murderer are viewed from three perspectives: that of his wife, who still loves him; that of a journalist, who made her career because of him; and that of a police detective, who is still obsessed with him.

title: The Impossible Fortress
author: Jason Rekulak
description: A retro coming-of-age story set in a small town in North Jersey in the late 1980s where a 14-year-old boy and his Commodore 64 find love and trouble.

title: The Evening Road
author: Laird Hunt
description: In 1920 Indiana, a threatened lynching becomes a magnet for two women --one white, one black-- navigating different physical and emotional paths.

title: Caught in the Revolution
author: Helen Rappaport
