description: The story of the outbreak of the Russian Revolution, told through eye-witness accounts left by foreign nationals who saw the drama unfold.

title: Locked In: The True Causes of Mass Incarceration—and How to Achieve Real Reform
author: John F. Pfaff
description: An examination of our system of imprisonment, critiquing the causes of and myths surrounding mass incarceration, as well as a path to reform.

title: The Book Thieves: The Nazi Looting of Europe's Libraries and the Race to Return a Literary Inheritance
author: Anders Rydell, trans. by Henning Koch
description: The story of the Nazis' systematic pillaging of Europe's libraries, and the small team of heroic librarians now working to return the stolen books to their rightful owners.

title: Never Caught: The Washingtons' Relentless Pursuit of Their Runaway Slave, Ona Judge
author: Erica Armstrong Dunbar
description: An eye-opening look into America’s First Family, Never Caught is the true story of Ona Judge, George and Martha Washington’s runaway slave who risked everything to escape the nation’s capital and reach freedom.

author: Paul Auster
description: Nearly two weeks early, on March 3, 1947, in the maternity ward of Beth Israel Hospital in Newark, New Jersey, Archibald Isaac Ferguson, the one and only child of Rose and Stanley Ferguson, is born. From that single beginning, Ferguson’s life will take four simultaneous and independent fictional paths. Four identical Fergusons made of the same DNA, four boys who are the same boy, go on to lead four parallel and entirely different lives.

title: The Blood of Emmett Till
author: Timothy B. Tyson
description: Part detective story, part political history, The Blood of Emmett Till draws on a wealth of new evidence, including the only interview ever given by Carolyn Bryant, the white woman in whose name Till was killed. Tyson’s narrative upends what we thought we knew about the most notorious racial crime in American history.

title: The Men in My Life: A Memoir of Love and Art in 1950s Manhattan
author: Patricia Bosworth
description: Acclaimed biographer Patricia Bosworth recalls her emotional coming of age in 1950s New York in this memoir, a story of family, marriage, tragedy, Broadway, and art, featuring a rich cast of well-known literary and theatrical figures from the period.

title: The Original Black Elite: Daniel Murray and the Story of a Forgotten Era
author: Elizabeth Dowling Taylor
description: The story of the inspiring rise and calculated fall of the black elite, from Emancipation through Reconstruction to the Jim Crow Era—embodied in the experiences of an influential figure of the time, academic, entrepreneur, and political activist and black history pioneer Daniel Murray.

title: Rather Be the Devil
author: Ian Rankin
description: The latest novel in Ian Rankin's John Rebus detective series, focusing on a cold case of a glamorous young woman murdered at a luxurious hotel on the same night a famous rock star and his entourage where also staying there.

title: How to Murder Your Life
author: Cat Marnell
description: A candid and darkly humorous memoir of prescription drug addiction and self-sabotage, set in the glamorous world of fashion magazines and downtown nightclubs.

title: The Animators
author: Kayla Rae Whitaker
description: In the male-dominated field of animation, Mel Vaught and Sharon Kisses are a dynamic duo, the friction of their differences driving them. Now, after a decade of striving, the two are finally celebrating the release of their first full-length feature, which transforms Mel’s difficult childhood into a provocative and visually daring work of art. But with their success come doubt and destruction, cracks in their relationship threatening the delicate balance of their partnership.

title: The Upstarts: How Uber, Airbnb, and the Killer Companies of the New Silicon Valley Are Changing the World
author: Brad Stone
description: A look deep inside the new Silicon Valley, focusing on Uber and Airbnb, from the author of The Everything Store .

title: My Husband's Wife
author: Jane Corry
description: A young lawyer finds similarities in her marriage and her first murder case.

title: Behind Her Eyes
author: Sarah Pinborough
description: A psychological thriller told from the perspectives of a woman having an affair with her boss, and his mysterious wife.

title: Victorians Undone: Tales of the Flesh in the Age of Decorum
author: Kathryn Hughes
description: An account of what it was like to live in a Victorian body, bringing the reader through the realms of social history, medical discourse, aesthetic practise and religious observance.

title: Days Without End
author: Sebastian Barry
description: Thomas McNulty, aged barely 17 and having fled the Great Famine in Ireland, signs up for the U.S. Army in the 1850s. With his brother in arms, John Cole, Thomas goes on to fight in the Indian Wars—against the Sioux and the Yurok—and, ultimately, the Civil War.

title: Arthur and Sherlock
author: Michael Sims
description: A book tracing the young Arthur Conan Doyle's creation of Sherlock Holmes and the modern detective story.

title: The Book That Changed America: How Darwin's Theory of Evolution Ignited a Nation
author: Randall Fuller
description: A portrait of a unique moment in American history when the ideas of Charles Darwin reshaped American notions about nature, religion, science and race, focusing on a group of New England intellectuals which including Henry David Thoreau.

title: The Spider and the Fly: A Reporter, a Serial Killer, and the Meaning of Murder
author: Claudia Rowe
description: A combination of memoir and psychological suspense—a female journalist chronicles her unusual connection with a convicted serial killer and her search to understand the darkness inside us.

title: Perfect Little World
author: Kevin Wilson
description: A young woman, fresh out of high school and pregnant with her teacher's baby, joins an eccentric billionaire's utopian Infinity Family Project, in which ten children are raised collectively.

title: Earning the Rockies: How Geography Shapes America's Role in the World
author: Robert D. Kaplan
description: A portrait of the American landscape that shows how geography continues to determine America’s role in the world, from the author of Balkan Ghosts .

title: The True Flag: Theodore Roosevelt, Mark Twain, and the Birth of American Empire
author: Stephen Kinzer
description: A book that brings to life the forgotten political debate that set America’s interventionist course in the world for the twentieth century and beyond.

title: Lara: The Untold Love Story and the Inspiration for Doctor Zhivago
author: Anna Pasternak
description: The story of the love affair between Boris Pasternak, the author of Doctor Zhivago , and Olga Ivinskaya—the true tragedy behind the timeless classic.

title: Dark at the Crossing
author: Elliot Ackerman
description: A contemporary love story set on the Turkish border with Syria. Haris Abadi, an Arab American with a conflicted past, is robbed attempting to cross into Syria and join the fight against Bashar al-Assad's regime. He is taken in by Amir, a charismatic Syrian refugee and former revolutionary, and Amir's wife, Daphne, a sophisticated beauty haunted by grief.

title: The Abominable Mr. Seabrook
author: Joe Ollmann
description: A graphic biography of the infamous early 20th century Journalist William Buehler Seabrook, who participated in voodoo ceremonies, rode camels cross the Sahara desert, communed with cannibals and most notably, popularized the term 'zombie' in the West.

title: A Great Place to Have a War: America in Laos and the Birth of a Military CIA
author: Joshua Kurlantzick
description: The untold story of how America’s secret war in Laos in the 1960s and 1970s transformed the CIA from a loose collection of spies into a military operation and a key player in American foreign policy.

title: The Girl Before
author: JP Delaney
description: A high-tech town house is leased by its wealthy, obsessive architect to a series of women who look just like his dead wife.

title: True South: Henry Hampton and Eyes on the Prize, the Landmark Television Series That Reframed the Civil Rights Movement
author: Jon Else
description: The inside story of Eyes on the Prize , a chronicle of the Civil Rights movement and one of the most important and influential TV shows in history, written by a former producer on the show.

title: Why Time Flies: A Mostly Scientific Investigation
author: Alan Burdick
description: New Yorker staff writer Alan Burdick takes readers on a personal quest to understand how time gets in us and why we perceive it the way we do.

title: Homesick for Another World
author: Ottessa Moshfegh
description: A collection of psychologically dark short stories from the author of Eileen .

title: Human Acts
author: Han Kang
description: In the midst of a violent student uprising in South Korea, a young boy named Dong-ho is shockingly killed. The story of this tragic episode unfolds in a sequence of interconnected chapters as the victims and the bereaved encounter suppression, denial, and the echoing agony of the massacre.

title: Home and Away: Writing the Beautiful Game
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard and Fredrik Ekelund
description: An unusual soccer book, in which the two authors use soccer and the World Cup in Brazil as the arena for reflections on life and death, art and politics, class and literature.

title: Transit
author: Rachel Cusk
description: The second book of a trilogy. In the wake of her family’s collapse, a writer and her two young sons move to London. The process of this upheaval is the catalyst for a number of transitions?personal, moral, artistic, and practical?as she endeavors to construct a new reality for herself and her children.

title: Sirens
author: Joshua Mohr
description: Novelist Joshua Mohr provides an account of his years of substance abuse and culpability in his non-fiction debut. Mohr traces his childhood swilling fuzzy navels as a latch-key kid, through his first failed marriage, parenthood, heart-surgery, and his everyday struggle against relapse.

title: Little Deaths
author: Emma Flint
description: A literary crime novel based on the true story of a troubled Queens cocktail waitress suspected of murdering her children.

title: How America Lost Its Secrets: Edward Snowden, the Man and the Theft
author: Edward Jay Epstein
description: An exposé that challenges the popular image of Edward Snowden as hacker turned avenging angel, while revealing how vulnerable our national security systems have become.

title: Audacity: How Barack Obama Defied His Critics and Created a Legacy That Will Prevail
author: Jonathan Chait
description: Chait, a political columnist for New York magazine, makes the case that, in the eyes of history, Barack Obama will be viewed as one of America’s best and most accomplished presidents.

title: Carve the Mark
author: Veronica Roth
description: The first in a new YA science-fiction series from author of Divergent . On a planet where violence and vengeance rule, in a galaxy where some are favored by fate, everyone develops a currentgift, a unique power meant to shape the future. While most benefit from their currentgifts, Akos and Cyra do not—their gifts make them vulnerable to others’ control. Can they reclaim their gifts, their fates, and their lives, and reset the balance of power in this world?

title: Rumi's Secret: The Life of the Sufi Poet of Love
author: Brad Gooch
description: The first popular biography of Rumi, the thirteenth-century Persian poet revered by contemporary Western readers.

title: The Man Who Shot Out My Eye Is Dead
author: Chanelle Benz
description: A debut short story collection about lives across history marked by violence and longing.

title: Lillian Boxfish Takes a Walk
author: Kathleen Rooney
description: A poet and writer of clever, innovative ad copy, Margaret Fishback was admired in her time but is mostly forgotten now. Rooney's novel is a fictionalized version of Fishback’s story, drawing on real milestones but imagining her subject’s inner life as she travels around New York City.

title: Tears We Cannot Stop: A Sermon to White America
author: Michael Eric Dyson
description: A provocative and deeply personal call for change. Dyson argues that if we are to make real racial progress we must face difficult truths, including being honest about how black grievance has been ignored, dismissed, or discounted.

title: Once We Were Sisters
author: Sheila Kohler
description: When Sheila Kohler was thirty-seven, she received the news that her sister Maxine, only two years older, was killed when her husband drove them off a deserted road in Johannesburg. Stunned, she immediately flew back to the country where she was born, determined to find answers and forced to reckon with his history of violence and the lingering effects of their most unusual childhood.

title: The Futures
author: Anna Pitoniak
description: A novel set at the dawn of the 2008 financial collapse in which a young couple moves to New York City in search of success-only to learn that the lives they dream of may come with dangerous strings attached.

title: The Night Market
author: Jonathan Moore
description: In this near-future thriller, Inspector Ross Carver struggles to discern what happened after he is drugged and removed from a crime scene by six FBI agents.

title: A Really Good Day: How Microdosing Made a Mega Difference in My Mood, My Marriage, and My Life
author: Ayelet Waldman
description: An account of the author's experiment with microdoses of LSD in an effort to treat a debilitating mood disorder, of her quest to understand a misunderstood drug, and of her search for a really good day.

title: Huck Out West
author: Robert Coover
description: The postmodernist novelist turns his iconoclastic eye to a great American classic in this sequel to The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn .

title: The Sleepwalker
author: Chris Bohjalian
description: From the author of The Guest Room , a mystery novel of lies, loss, and buried desire—the story of a wife and mother who vanishes from her bed late one night.

title: The Most Dangerous Place on Earth
author: Lindsey Lee Johnson
description: A debut novel in which kids face every possible pitfall of modern adolescence as they go from eighth grade to senior year of a wealthy San Francisco high school.

title: Fever Dream
author: Samanta Schweblin, Trans. by Megan McDowell
description: A young woman named Amanda lies dying in a rural hospital clinic. A boy named David sits beside her. She’s not his mother. He's not her child. Together, they tell a haunting story of broken souls, toxins, and the power and desperation of family.

title: Nicotine
author: Gregor Hens
description: By turns philosophical and darkly comic, an ex-smoker's meditation on the nature and consequences of his nearly lifelong addiction.

title: A House Full of Females: Plural Marriage and Women's Rights in Early Mormonism, 1835-1870
author: Laurel Thatcher Ulrich
description: An intimate look at the world of early Mormon women whose seemingly ordinary lives belied an astonishingly revolutionary spirit, drive, and determination.

title: Lucky Boy
author: Shanthi Sekaran
description: The story of two mothers--one biological, undocumented and unmoored; the other foster, affluent but unable to conceive--bound together by their love for one little boy.

title: Class
author: Lucinda Rosenfeld
description: A satirical novel about a mother whose life spirals out of control when she's forced to rethink her bleeding heart liberal ideals.

title: Finks: How the C.I.A. Tricked the World's Best Writers
author: Joel Whitney
description: Written by the co-founder of Guernica magazine, Finks is a tale of two CIAs, and how they blurred the line between propaganda and literature. One CIA created literary magazines that promoted American and European writers and cultural freedom, while the other toppled governments, using assassination and censorship as political tools.

title: In the Great Green Room
author: Amy Gary
description: A biography of the vibrant, free-spirited woman behind the beloved children’s classics Goodnight Moon and The Runaway Bunny .

title: Valley of the Gods
author: Alexandra Wolfe
description: Reporter Alexandra Wolfe goes behind-the-curtain to investigate the men and women of Silicon Valley, whose hubris and ambition are changing the world.

title: Lonely Boy: Tales from a Sex Pistol
author: Steve Jones
description: A music autobiography from one of the founders of the iconic punk band.

title: The Dry
author: Jane Harper
description: A thriller set in a parched Australian farming community, in which Federal agent Aaron Falk is called back to his hometown for the funeral of his best friend, Luke, who apparently committed suicide after killing his wife and 6-year-old son.

title: The Bear and the Nightingale
author: Katherine Arden
description: A fantasy novel set in the fourteenth century, at the edge of a Russian wilderness in which history and myth coexist. A young girl must defy her domineering new stepmother in order to protect her family from a threat that seems to have stepped from her nurse’s most frightening tales.

title: Burning Bright
author: Nicholas Petrie
description: The second book in Petrie's Peter Ash crime-thriller series focusing on a combat veteran suffering from PTSD.

title: The Genius of Judaism
description: From world-renowned public intellectual Bernard-Henri Lévy comes a provocative look at the heart of Judaism.

title: Always Happy Hour
author: Mary Miller
description: A debut short story collection that weaves tales of young women?deeply flawed and intensely real?who struggle to get out of their own way. They love to drink and have sex; they make bad decisions with men who either love them too much or too little; and they haunt a Southern terrain of gas stations, public pools, and dive bars.

title: The New Odyssey: The Story of the Twenty-First Century Refugee Crisis
author: Patrick Kingsley
description: A searing account of the current international refugee crisis from the Guardian 's first 'Migration Correspondent.'

title: Rosset: My Life in Publishing and How I Fought Censorship
author: Barney Rosset
description: An autobiography by the late Grove publisher Barney Rosset, focusing on the battles he fought to bring controversial classics such as Lady Chatterley's Lover , Tropic of Cancer , and The Autobiography of Malcom X to American readers.

title: Her Every Fear
author: Peter Swanson
description: Still traumatized by a boyfriend-turned-stalker, an English woman swaps apartments with her cousin in Boston. Soon a series of suspicious happenings are uncovered after the discovery of her next-door neighbor's murder.

title: In the Midnight Hour: The Life & Soul of Wilson Pickett
author: Tony Fletcher
description: The first major biography of the legendary soul singer.

title: Difficult Women
author: Roxane Gay
description: A short story collection from the author of Bad Feminist , focusing on the struggles of women claiming independence for themselves.

title: Selection Day
author: Aravind Adiga
description: From the Booker Prize­–winning author of The White Tiger , a novel about two brothers in a Mumbai slum who are raised by their obsessive father to become cricket stars, and whose coming of age threatens their relationship, future, and sense of themselves.

title: History of Wolves
author: Emily Fridlund
description: A dark coming-of-age novel about a girl, growing up on a northern Minnesota commune long since abandoned by all of its idealistic residents, who is hired as a babysitter by a young couple.

title: Idaho
author: Emily Ruskovich
description: Winner of the 2019 International Dublin Literary Award, Idaho tells the story of Ann and Wade, who have carved out a life for themselves from a rugged landscape in northern Idaho, where they are bound together by more than love. With her husband’s memory fading, Ann attempts to piece together the truth of what happened to Wade’s first wife, Jenny, and to their daughters.

title: The Strays
author: Emily Bitto
description: Set in 1930s Australia, the haunting coming of age story of three sisters and their friend who grow up on the outskirts of their parents' glamorous bohemian lifestyle.

title: Steven Spielberg: A Life in Films
author: Molly Haskell
description: A film-centric portrait of the extraordinarily gifted movie director whose decades-long influence on American popular culture is unprecedented.

title: The House of the Dead: Siberian Exile Under the Tsars
author: Daniel Beer
description: A visceral, hundred-year history of the vast Russian penal colony beyond the Ural mountains in Siberia.

title: The Lost City of the Monkey God
author: Douglas Preston
description: A five-hundred-year-old legend. An ancient curse. A stunning medical mystery. And a pioneering journey into the unknown heart of the world's densest jungle.

title: The Correspondence
author: J.D. Daniels
description: The first collection, a series of six letters written during dark nights of the soul, from a Whiting Writers’ Award winner whose work has become a fixture of The Paris Review and n+1 .

title: Enigma Variations
author: André Aciman
description: A novel divided into five novella-length sections, each focused on a different erotic obsession and possibility.

title: Everything You Want Me to Be
author: Mindy Mejia
description: Everything You Want Me to Be reconstructs a year in the life of a dangerously mesmerizing young woman, during which a small town’s darkest secrets come to the forefront...and she inches closer and closer to her death.

title: Letters to a Young Muslim
author: Omar Saif Ghobash
description: An exploration of what it means to be a Muslim in the twenty-first century from the Ambassador of the UAE to Russia, in the form of letters to the author's son.

title: Scratch: Writers, Money, and the Art of Making a Living
author: Ed. by Manjula Martin
description: A collection of essays from some of today’s most acclaimed authors—from Cheryl Strayed to Roxane Gay to Jennifer Weiner, Alexander Chee, Nick Hornby, and Jonathan Franzen—on the realities of making a living in the writing world.

title: Language at the Speed of Sight: How We Read, Why So Many Can’t, and What Can Be Done About It
author: Mark Seidenberg
description: Internationally renowned cognitive scientist Mark Seidenberg reveals the underexplored science of reading, which spans cognitive science, neurobiology, and linguistics, in order to understand why so many fail to read, and how to change that.

title: War Against War: The American Fight for Peace, 1914-1918
author: Michael Kazin
description: The untold story of the movement that came close to keeping the United States out of the First World War.

title: United: Thoughts on Finding Common Ground and Advancing the Common Good
author: Cory Booker
description: United States Senator and 2020 Democratic presidential candidate Cory Booker makes the case that the virtues of empathy, responsibility, and action must guide our nation toward a brighter future.

title: Books for Living
author: Will Schwalbe
description: An exploration of the power of books to shape our lives in an era of constant connectivity, from the author of The End of Your Life Book Club .

title: The Case Against Sugar
author: Gary Taubes
description: An exposé that makes the case that sugar is the tobacco of the new millennium: backed by powerful lobbies, entrenched in our lives, and making us very sick.

title: Debriefing the President: The Interrogation of Saddam Hussein
author: John Nixon
description: An account of the CIA's interrogation of Saddam Hussein, written by the CIA agent who conducted the questioning.

title: Small Admissions
author: Amy Poeppel
description: A lighthearted comic novel about a young woman who takes a job in an elite Manhattan private school.

title: This Is How It Always Is
author: Laurie Frankel
description: A novel about a woman and her family dealing with her youngest son deciding he wants to be a girl.

title: The Boy Who Escaped Paradise
author: J. M. Lee, Trans. by Chi-Young Kim
description: Ahn Gil­mo, a young math savant, he escapes from the most isolated country in the world and searches for the only family he has left.

title: The Private Life of Mrs. Sharma
author: Ratika Kapur
description: In short novel set in contemporary India in which an urban woman’s private confession becomes a portrait, and perhaps an indictment, of 21st-century globalism.

title: Whatever Happened to Interracial Love?
author: Kathleen Collins
description: A posthumous, never-before-published collection of stories from a brilliant yet little known African American artist and filmmaker whose prescient work has recently resurfaced to wide acclaim.

title: The Undoing Project: A Friendship That Changed Our Minds
author: Michael Lewis
description: From the author of Moneyball, the story of two exceptional psychologists whose friendship and work produced groundbreaking new theories about our perception of reality.

title: The Feud: Vladimir Nabokov, Edmund Wilson, and the End of a Beautiful Friendship
author: Alex Beam
description: The story of how two literary giants destroyed their friendship in a fit of mutual pique and egomania.

title: The Glass Universe: How the Ladies of the Harvard Observatory Took the Measure of the Stars
author: Dava Sobel
description: Popular science writer Sobel continues her project of heralding the many contributions of women to science, this time focusing on the Harvard College Observatory.

title: Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness
author: Peter Godfrey-Smith
description: A biological and philosophical investigation of the octopus, from philosopher and scuba diver Peter Godfrey-Smith.

title: Krazy: George Herriman, a Life in Black and White
author: Michael Tisserand
description: In the tradition of Schulz and Peanuts , a biography of Krazy Kat creator George Herriman that explores the turbulent time and place from which he emerged—and the deep secret he explored through his art.

title: George Lucas: A Life
author: Brian Jay Jones
description: A biography of the influential filmmaker and creator of Star Wars .

title: A Woman Looking at Men Looking at Women
author: Siri Hustvedt
description: A collection of essays on art, feminism, neuroscience, psychology, and philosophy from prize-winning novelist Siri Hustvedt.

title: Christmas Days
author: Jeanette Winterson
description: A collection of stories, paired with recipes, for the holiday season from the author of Why Be Happy When You Could Be Normal? .

title: Against Empathy: The Case for Rational Compassion
author: Paul Bloom
description: In a provocative re-evaluation, Yale psychologist Bloom argues that when it comes to both major policy decisions and the choices we make in our everyday lives, limiting our impulse toward empathy is often the most compassionate choice we can make.

title: In Sunlight or In Shadow: Stories Inspired by the Paintings of Edward Hopper
author: Lawrence Block
description: An anthology of seventeen stories inspired by the paintings of Edward Hopper, including Jeffery Deaver, Joyce Carol Oates, Stephen King, Lee Child, and Robert Olen Butler, among many others.

title: The Gardens of Consolation
author: Parisa Reza
description: A love story and family saga spanning decades of Iranian history and culture, from the fall of the Qajar dynasty to the nationalization of oil.

title: The Moravian Night
author: Peter Handke, Trans. by Krishna Winston
description: Mysteriously summoned to a houseboat on the Morava River, a few friends, associates, and collaborators of an old writer listen as he tells a story that will last until dawn: the tale of the once well-known writer’s recent odyssey across Europe.

title: The Wood for the Trees: One Man's Long View of Nature
author: Richard Fortey
description: From the author of Earth: An Intimate History , a 'biography' of four acres of woodland, evoking a cosmos of living and inanimate things and imagining its millennia of existence.

title: Last Year
author: Robert Charles Wilson
description: In the near future, a time-travel machine known as the Mirror allows citizens of the twenty-first century to visit yesteryear.

title: Searching for John Hughes
author: Jason Diamond
description: Jason Diamond’s memoir of growing up obsessed with the iconic filmmaker’s movies—a preoccupation that eventually convinces Diamond he should write Hughes’ biography.

title: How to Survive a Plague: The Inside Story of How Citizens and Science Tamed AIDS
author: David France
description: The definitive history of the successful battle to halt the AIDS epidemic—from the creator of, and inspired by, the seminal documentary How to Survive a Plague .

title: The Whole Town's Talking
author: Fannie Flagg
description: A sweet portrait of a Midwestern town founded by Swedish immigrants, including both lives and afterlives, from 1889 to 2021, from the author of Fried Green Tomatoes at the Whistle Stop Cafe .

title: The Pursuit of Power: Europe 1815-1914
author: Richard J. Evans
description: From the author of The Third Reich at War , an account of Europe in the age of its global hegemony; the latest volume in the Penguin History of Europe series.

title: Normal
author: Warren Ellis
description: After a futurist has a nervous breakdown in Rotterdam, he’s taken to a secret hospital in rural Oregon that may not be what it seems on the surface.

title: The Beautiful Country and the Middle Kingdom: America and China, 1776 to the Present
author: John Pomfret
description: A history of the two-centuries-old relationship between the United States and China, from the Revolutionary War to the present day.

title: Moonglow
author: Michael Chabon
description: A faux memoir of the novelist’s grandfather, whose life as an engineer, veteran, and felon unlocks themes of heroism and imagination.

title: I'll Take You There
author: Wally Lamb
description: An aging film scholar is visited by elegant Hollywood ghosts bearing interactive home movies of his childhood.

title: The Princess Diarist
author: Carrie Fisher
description: An intimate recollection of what happened behind the scenes on one of the most famous film sets of all time, the first Star Wars movie, focusing on Fisher's affair with Harrison Ford.

title: The Marches: A Borderline Journey Between England and Scotland
author: Rory Stewart
description: The author’s journey along Hadrian’s Wall, which allowed him to explore and answer questions about Scottish nationalism, Rome, Frontiers, and Empires.

title: The Daily Show (The Book): An Oral History
author: Chris Smith & Jon Stewart
description: An oral history of the news satire and talk show as told by Jon Stewart, the correspondents, staff and guests.

title: The Spy
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A novel about Mata Hari, the notorious and probably falsely accused World War I spy, from the author of The Alchemist .

title: Rasputin: Faith, Power, and the Twilight of the Romanovs
author: Douglas Smith
description: On the centenary of the death of Rasputin comes a comprehensive biography of the infamous figure.

title: Thank You for Being Late: An Optimist's Guide to Thriving in the Age of Accelerations
author: Thomas L. Friedman
description: The New York Times columnist gives us a field guide to the twenty-first century and suggests strategies to help us adapt.

title: Conclave
author: Robert Harris
description: The pope is dead. Behind the locked doors of the Sistine Chapel, one hundred and eighteen cardinals from all over the globe will cast their votes in the world's most secretive election. They are holy men. But they have ambition. And they have rivals. Over the next seventy-two hours one of them will become the most powerful spiritual figure on Earth.

title: Toussaint Louverture: A Revolutionary Life
author: Philippe Girard
description: A major new biography of the 19th century Haitian revolutionary leader Toussaint Louverture.

title: Victoria: The Queen
author: Julia Baird
description: An intimate new biography of Queen Victoria

title: Hank: The Short Life and Long Country Road of Hank Williams
author: Mark Ribowsky
description: A portrait of country music’s iconic founding father

title: The Némirovsky Question: The Life, Death, and Legacy of a Jewish Writer in Twentieth-Century France
author: Susan Rubin Suleiman
description: A look into the life and work of controversial French novelist Irène Némirovsky, who had a successful writing career in the 1930s before being deported in 1942 and dying in Auschwitz.

title: Victoria
author: Daisy Goodwin
description: Drawing on Queen Victoria’s diaries, Daisy Goodwin--creator and writer of the PBS/Masterpiece drama Victoria --brings the young nineteenth-century monarch, who would go on to reign for 63 years, to life in this novel.

title: Swing Time
author: Zadie Smith
description: A novel from the author of White Teeth and NW about the love of dance that draws two mixed race girls from a poor area of London to one another, and the different paths their lives take in the years that follow.

title: They Can't Kill Us All: Ferguson, Baltimore, and a New Era in America's Racial Justice Movement
author: Wesley Lowery
description: Conducting hundreds of interviews during the course of over one year reporting on the ground, Washington Post writer Wesley Lowery traveled from Ferguson, Missouri, to Cleveland, Ohio; Charleston, South Carolina; and Baltimore, Maryland; and then back to Ferguson to uncover life inside the most heavily policed, if otherwise neglected, corners of America today.

title: Born a Crime
author: Trevor Noah
description: A memoir in essays from the comedian and Daily Show host about coming of age during the twilight of apartheid and the tumultuous days of freedom that followed.

title: Testimony
author: Robbie Robertson
description: On the 40th anniversary of The Band’s legendary The Last Waltz concert, Robbie Robertson tells his own story of the band that changed music history, his extraordinary personal journey, and his creative friendships with some of the greatest artists of the last half-century.

title: Tranny: Confessions of Punk Rock's Most Infamous Anarchist Sellout
author: Laura Jane Grace
description: The provocative transgender advocate and lead singer of the punk rock band Against Me! provides an account of her search for identity and her true self.

title: Settle for More
author: Megyn Kelly
description: A memoir from the Fox News host and political commentator about her life, journalistic career, treatment by Roger Ailes, and battles with Donald Trump.

title: Bellevue: Three Centuries of Medicine and Mayhem at America's Most Storied Hospital
author: David Oshinsky
description: From a Pulitzer Prize-winning historian comes a history of New York's iconic public hospital that charts the turbulent rise of American medicine.

title: Twenty-Six Seconds: A Personal History of the Zapruder Film
author: Alexandra Zapruder
description: The untold family story behind Abraham Zapruder's film footage of the Kennedy assassination and its lasting impact on both the Zapruder family and the world.

title: Writing to Save a Life
author: John Edgar Wideman
description: An amalgam of research, memoir, and imagination, Writing to Save a Life is an investigation into the death of Louis Till, the father of Emmet Till who was abducted and murdered in Mississippi in 1955 for allegedly whistling at a white woman.

title: Absolutely on Music
author: Haruki Murakami and Seiji Ozawa
description: An intimate conversation about music and writing between the internationally acclaimed, best-selling author and his close friend, the former conductor of the Boston Symphony Orchestra.

title: The Platinum Age of Television
author: David Bianculli
description: Television critic Bianculli traces the evolution of TV from its cultural status as a lesser medium to its current lauded "Platinum Age."

title: Ray & Joan
author: Lisa Napoli
description: A quintessentially American tale of corporate intrigue and private passion: a struggling salesman with a vision fora fast-food franchise that would become one of the world’s most enduring brands, and a woman willing to risk her marriage and her reputation to promote controversial causes that touched her deeply.

title: Set the Boy Free
author: Johnny Marr
description: The long-awaited memoir from the legendary guitarist and cofounder of the seminal British band The Smiths.

title: Our Revolution
author: Bernie Sanders
description: Sanders shares his personal experiences from the campaign trail, recounting the details of his historic primary fight and the people who made it possible. And for the millions looking to continue the political revolution, he outlines his plan for the future.

title: Scrappy Little Nobody
author: Anna Kendrick
description: A collection of humorous autobiographical essays by the Academy Award-nominated actress and star of Up in the Air and Pitch Perfect .

title: Last Girl Before Freeway: The Life, Loves, Losses, and Liberation of Joan Rivers
author: Leslie Bennetts
description: The first major biography of the late, provocative comedian Joan Rivers.

title: The Vanquished: Why the First World War Failed to End
author: Robert Gerwarth
description: An account of the ethnic and state violence that followed the end of World War I?conflicts that would shape the course of the twentieth century.

title: The History of Rock & Roll Volume 1: 1920-1963
author: Ed Ward
description: A history of Rock & Roll from the the rock historian for NPR's Fresh Air .

title: Brothers at Arms: American Independence and the Men of France and Spain Who Saved It
author: Larrie D. Ferreiro
description: The untold story of how the American Revolution's success depended on substantial military assistance provided by France and Spain, and places the Revolution in the context of the global strategic interests of those nations in their fight against England.

title: Wonderland: How Play Made the Modern World
author: Steven Johnson
description: An exuberant investigation into how the human impulse to play has shaped our world.

title: Where Memory Leads
author: Saul Friedlander
description: In this sequel to the classic work of Holocaust literature When Memory Comes , a Pulitzer Prize–winning historian returns to memoir to recount this tale of intellectual coming-of-age on three continents.

title: Judas
author: Amos Oz, Trans. by Nicholas de Lange
description: A love story and coming-of-age novel as well as an allegory for the state of Israel and for the biblical tale from which it draws its title.

title: Memoirs of a Polar Bear
author: Yoko Tawada, Trans. by Susan Bernofsky
description: A historical family saga told from the perspective of three generations of talented writers and performers in East Germany?who happen to be polar bears.

title: The Chemist
author: Stephenie Meyer
description: A stark thriller from the author of the Twilight series in which an ex-agent on the run from her former employers must take one more case to clear her name and save her life.

title: Beryl Bainbridge: Love by All Sorts of Means
author: Brendan King
description: In this first full-length biography of the British novelist, Brendan King draws on a mass of unpublished letters and diaries to reveal the real woman behind the popular image.

title: Orphans of the Carnival
author: Carol Birch
description: The story of a woman with a rare medical condition, branded a freak from birth, who becomes an international sensation but longs for genuine human connection.

title: The Revenge of Analog: Real Things and Why They Matter
author: David Sax
description: Blending psychology and observant wit with reportage, Sax argues for the limited appeal of the purely digital life–and the robust future of the real world outside it.

title: JFK and the Masculine Mystique
author: Steven Watts
description: An examination of the masculine allure JFK represented and how it changed a nation’s impression of what a man and a political leader should embody.

title: Night School
author: Lee Child
description: The latest novel in Lee Child's best-selling Jack Reacher series; a prequel set in 1996 when Reacher is still in the army.

title: Frantumaglia
author: Elena Ferrante, Trans. by Ann Goldstein
description: This book invites readers into Elena Ferrante’s workshop. It offers a glimpse into the drawers of her writing desk. It is a unique depiction of an author who embodies a consummate passion for writing.

title: The Wrong Side of Goodbye (A Harry Bosch Novel)
author: Michael Connelly
description: The latest installment of Connelly's Harry Bosch crime series, in which the recently retired detective must track down a man who may never have existed.

title: Pull Me Under
author: Kelly Luce
description: After receiving news of her father’s death, Rio Silvestri returns to Japan for the first time in 20 years. She travels there alone to confront the terrible childhood secret she’s kept from the people in her new life in Colorado.

title: Eleanor Roosevelt, Volume 3: The War Years and After, 1939-1962
author: Blanche Wiesen Cook
description: A portrait of a marriage and of a woman whose passion and commitment has inspired generations of Americans to seek a decent future for all people.

title: Faithful
author: Alice Hoffman
description: A new novel from the author of Practical Magic . Growing up on Long Island, Shelby Richmond is an ordinary girl until one night an extraordinary tragedy changes her fate. Her best friend’s future is destroyed in an accident, while Shelby walks away with the burden of guilt.

title: Thus Bad Begins
author: Javier Marias, Trans. by Margaret Jull Costa
description: In Madrid in 1980, a young man takes a job as an assistant to an eccentric film director. What unfolds is the story of a couple living in the shadow of a mysterious, unhappy history--a novel about the cruel, tender punishments we exact on those we love.

title: Virgin and Other Stories
author: April Ayers Lawson
description: A collection of stories focusing on a variety of troubled characters searching for solace of both sexual and spiritual varieties in the contemporary South.

title: Valiant Gentlemen
author: Sabina Murray
description: A historical novel which reimagines the lives and intimate friendships of humanitarian and Irish patriot Roger Casement; his closest friend, Herbert Ward; and Ward’s extraordinary wife, the Argentinian-American heiress Sarita Sanford.

title: Kenneth Clark: Life, Art and Civilisation
author: James Stourton
description: A biography of a brilliant polymath –– director of the National Gallery, author, patron of the arts, social lion, and singular pioneer of television –– that also tells the story of the arts in the twentieth century through his astonishing life.

title: Television: A Biography
author: David Thompson
description: Thompson offers a personal celebration of his particular fascinations and a provocative consideration of the ways in which the very mechanics of the medium affect the audience, both as individuals and as a mass culture.

title: By Women Possessed: A Life of Eugene O'Neill
author: Arthur Gelb & Barbara Gelb
description: The third and final volume of a biography of the brilliant but troubled American playwright.

title: A Nation Without Borders: The United States and Its World in an Age of Civil Wars, 1830-1910
author: Steven Hahn
description: Volume 3 in the Penguin History of the United States, a Pulitzer Prize–winning historian’s reinterpretation of the eight decades surrounding the Civil War.

title: Fish in Exile
author: Vi Khi Nao
description: A fragmented, lyrical novel in which a couple mourns the sudden and tragic loss of their children in unusual ways.

title: An Iron Wind: Europe Under Hitler
author: Peter Fritzsche
description: In An Iron Wind , historian Peter Fritzsche draws on diaries, letters, and other first-person accounts to show how civilians in occupied Europe struggled to understand the terrifying reality of living under Hitler.

title: The Spy Who Couldn't Spell
author: Yudhijit Bhattacharjee
description: The true-life account of the FBI’s hunt for the ingenious traitor Brian Regan—known as the Spy Who Couldn’t Spell.

title: The Earth Is Weeping: The Epic Story of the Indian Wars for the American West
author: Peter Cozzens
description: Bringing together a pageant of characters including Custer, Sherman, Grant, and a host of other military and political figures, as well as great native leaders such as Crazy Horse, Sitting Bull, Geronimo, and Red Cloud, The Earth is Weeping is an account of how the West was won…and lost.

title: Norte
author: Edmundo Paz Soldán, Trans. by Valerie Miles
description: A tale of displacement and the very human costs of immigration, in which the lives of a mentally ill savant, a young artist, and a serial killer converge.

title: The Terranauts
author: T.C. Boyle
description: It is 1994, and in the desert near Tillman, Arizona, forty miles from Tucson, a grand experiment involving the future of humanity is underway. As climate change threatens the earth, eight scientists, four men and four women dubbed the 'Terranauts,' have been selected to live for two years under glass in E2, a prototype of a possible off-earth colony.

title: The Boat Rocker
author: Ha Jin
description: From the author of Waiting and War Trash : a political novel that follows an aspiring author, an outrageous book idea, and a lone journalist’s dogged quest for truth in the Internet age.

title: Walk Through Walls
author: Marina Abramovic
description: A memoir from the famous Serbian performance artist, considered by many to be "the grandmother of performance art."

title: The Whistler
author: John Grisham
description: The latest from the bestselling legal thriller author is a high-stakes thrill ride through the darkest corners of the Sunshine State, focusing on Lacy Stoltz, an investigator for the Florida Board on Judicial Conduct.

title: Alfred Hitchcock: A Brief Life
author: Peter Ackroyd
description: A short biography of the extraordinary Alfred Hitchock, the master of suspense.

title: Certain Dark Things
author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
description: An alternate reality novel about gangs of warring narco-vampires in Mexico City, and of the relationship between a young human street teenager, and a jaded female vampire.

title: The Nine of Us: Growing Up Kennedy
author: Jean Kennedy Smith
description: A memoir from Ambassador Jean Kennedy Smith, the last surviving child of Joe and Rose Kennedy about growing up as part of the famous political family.

title: Al Capone: His Life, Legacy, and Legend
author: Deirdre Bair
description: From a National Book Award-winning biographer, the first biography of legendary gangster Al Capone to be produced with the cooperation of his family.

title: Black Elk
author: Joe Jackson
description: The epic life story of the Native American holy man who has inspired millions around the world.

title: We Show What We Have Learned
author: Clare Beams
description: The literary, historic, and fantastic collide in these unsettling magical realist stories. From bewildering assemblies in school auditoriums to the murky waters of a Depression-era health resort, Beams’s landscapes are tinged with otherworldliness.

title: Float
author: Anne Carson
description: From the renowned classicist and MacArthur Prize winner: a new collection, made up of 23 chapbooks, that explores myth and memory, beauty and loss.

title: Not Dead Yet
author: Phil Collins
description: A memoir from the iconic English musician about his personal life and years in the music business.

title: Unmentionable: The Victorian Lady's Guide to Sex, Marriage, and Manners
author: Therese Oneill
description: A comic, illustrated, scandalously honest guide to the secrets of Victorian womanhood.

title: Haunted: On Ghosts, Witches, Vampires, Zombies, and Other Monsters of the Natural and Supernatural Worlds
author: Leo Braudy
description: A book which charts four hundred years of monsters and how they reflect the culture that created them.

title: Martutene
author: Ramon Saizarbitoria, Trans. by Aritz Branton
description: A sprawling novel of post–independence movement Basque life and its discontents.

title: Cockroaches
author: Scholastique Mukasonga, trans. by Jordan Stump
description: Scholastique Mukasonga tells the story of growing up a Tutsi in Hutu-dominated Rwanda--the story of a happy child, a loving family, all wiped out in the genocide of 1994.

title: A Gambler's Anatomy
author: Jonathan Lethem
description: A darkly comic novel about a rakish international backgammon hustler, whose cancer diagnosis forces him to return to Berkley, California, where he comes into conflict with an old school friend turned nefarious property mogul.

title: Mister Monkey
author: Francine Prose
description: A darkly humorous novel that follows the exploits and intrigue of a constellation of characters affiliated with an off-off-off-off Broadway children’s musical.

title: Truevine: Two Brothers, a Kidnapping, and a Mother's Quest
author: Beth Macy
description: An investigative non fiction account about two African-American albino brothers in the Jim Crow South, kidnapped by a circus to perform in its "freak show," and a mother's quest to get them back.

title: Thrill Me: Essays on Fiction
author: Benjamin Percy
description: A collection of essays on how to craft a thrilling read –– in any genre –– from the bestselling author of The Dead Lands .

title: The Girl from Venice
author: Martin Cruz Smith
description: A suspenseful World War II love story set against the beauty, mystery, and danger of occupied Venice.

title: The Fall Guy
author: James Lasdun
description: A psychological thriller in which Charlie, a wealthy banker with an uneasy conscience, invites his troubled cousin Matthew to visit him and his wife in their idyllic mountaintop house. As the days grow hotter, the friendship between the three begins to reveal its fault lines.

title: A Life Discarded: 148 Diaries Found in the Trash
author: Alexander Masters
description: Biographer Alexander Masters uncovers the identity and real history of the secret author of a cache of diaries, spanning over half a century, found in the trash in Cambridge in 2001.

title: The Attention Merchants: The Epic Scramble to Get Inside Our Heads
author: Tim Wu
description: From the author of The Master Switch , an account of how the capture and re-sale of human attention became the defining industry of our time.

title: His Bloody Project
author: Graeme MaCrae Burnet
description: An experimental, "found document" crime novel. A brutal triple murder in a remote Scottish farming community in 1869 leads to the arrest of 17-year-old Roderick Macrae. There is no question that Macrae committed this terrible act. What would lead such a shy and intelligent boy down this bloody path? And will he hang for his crime?

title: The Secret History of Twin Peaks
author: Mark Frost
description: A novel from the co-creator of the landmark series, The Secret History of Twin Peaks enlarges the world of the original series, placing the unexplained phenomena that unfolded there into a vastly layered, wide-ranging history, beginning with the journals of Lewis and Clark and ending with the shocking events that closed the finale.

title: The Eastern Shore
author: Ward Just
description: An intense story of a newspaper editor’s fateful decision to expose a small-town fugitive.

title: The Pope of Physics: Enrico Fermi and the Birth of the Atomic Age
author: Gino Segre and Bettina Hoerlin
description: The first English-language biography of Nobel Prize–winning Italian physicist Enrico Fermi.

title: Of Arms and Artists: The American Revolution Through Painters' Eyes
author: Paul Staiti
description: An original perspective on the American Revolution through the stories of the five great artists whose paintings animated the new American republic.

title: Love for Sale: Pop Music in America
author: David Hajdu
description: A personal, idiosyncratic history of popular music in America.

title: The Tunnels: Escapes Under the Berlin Wall and the Historic Films the JFK White House Tried to Kill
author: Greg Mitchell
description: A Cold War narrative of superpower showdowns, media suppression, and two escape tunnels beneath the Berlin Wall.

title: City of Dreams: The 400-Year Epic History of Immigrant New York
author: Tyler Anbinder
description: The 400-year epic history of immigrant New York.

title: IQ
author: Joe Ide
description: In this debut novel, a young man searches for his brother's murderer in the streets of South Central Los Angeles.

title: Words Are My Matter: Writings about Life and Books, 2000-2016, with a Journal of a Writer's Week
author: Ursula K Le Guin
description: collects talks, essays, introductions to beloved books, and book reviews by Ursula K. Le Guin, one of our foremost public literary intellectuals. It is a manual for investigating the depth and breadth of contemporary fiction — and, through the lens of deep considerations of contemporary writing, a way of exploring the world we are all living in.

title: No Knives in the Kitchens of This City
author: Khaled Khalifa
description: Winner of the Naguib Mahfouz medal for literature. In the once beautiful city of Aleppo, one Syrian family descends into tragedy and ruin. rrepressible Sawsan flirts with militias, the ruling party, and finally religion, seeking but never finding salvation. She and her siblings and mother are slowly choked in violence and decay, as their lives are plundered by a brutal regime.

title: Transoceanic Lights
author: S. Li
description: In this novel about familial love and discord, the strains of displacement, and the hardships of a Chinese family who has immigrated to the US, an overbearing mother must reconcile the immensity of her sacrifice in the midst of a deteriorating marriage. Her only solace is the distant promise of a better life for her son, who spends his days in school longing for the comfort of his homeland.

title: Future Sex
author: Emily Witt
description: A book of essays exploring modern sexuality focusing on Internet dating, Internet pornography, polyamory, and avant-garde sexual subcultures as sites of possibility for the author.

title: Hag-Seed
author: Margaret Atwood
description: Margaret Atwood's novel take on Shakespeare's The Tempest in which a once famous theater director plots his revenge through a staging of the play with an all prisoner cast.

title: The Mothers
author: Brit Bennett
description: A debut novel set in contemporary California which centers on three African-American friends dealing with their community's expectations and their own mistakes.

title: American Philosophy: A Love Story
author: John Kaag
description: Part intellectual history, part memoir, American Philosophy focuses on a young philosopher's quest to save a forgotten library and in doing so turn his life around.

title: Small Great Things
author: Jodi Picoult
description: A novel about a black nurse whose ultimately unsuccessful efforts to save the sick child of a white supremacist couple result in her being charged with with a crime.

title: A Life in Parts
author: Bryan Cranston
description: A memoir—both a coming-of-age story and a meditation on creativity, devotion, and craft—from Bryan Cranston, acclaimed star of one of history’s most successful TV shows, Breaking Bad .

title: Upstream: Selected Essays
author: Mary Oliver
description: A collection of essays in which poet Mary Oliver reflects on her willingness, as a young child and as an adult, to lose herself within the beauty and mysteries of both the natural world and the world of literature.

title: I Am Brian Wilson
author: Brian Wilson with Ben Greenman
description: A memoir by the troubled but brilliant co-founder of The Beach Boys.

title: Unbearable Splendor
author: Sun Yung Shin
description: The third book of poetry from Sun Yung Shin, which mines literature, science fiction, myth and science in examinations of family, identity and the significance of being an immigrant.

title: The Red Car
author: Marcy Dermansky
description: An unconventional road trip novel. Leah is living in Queens with a possessive husband she doesn’t love and a long list of unfulfilled ambitions, when she’s jolted from a thick ennui by a call from the past. Her beloved former boss and friend, Judy, has died in a car accident and left Leah her most prized possession and, as it turns out, the instrument of Judy’s death: a red sports car.

title: Hungry Heart
author: Jennifer Weiner
description: A book of essays from author Jennifer Weiner in which she takes the raw stuff of her life and spins it into a collection of tales of modern-day womanhood.

title: In Wartime: Stories from Ukraine
author: Tim Judah
description: Making his way from the Polish border in the west, through the capital city and the heart of the 2014 revolution, to the eastern frontline near the Russian border, seasoned war reporter Tim Judah brings a rare glimpse of the reality behind the headlines.

title: A Very English Scandal: Sex, Lies, and a Murder Plot at the Heart of the Establishment
author: John Preston
description: A behind-the-scenes look at the desperate, scandalous private life of British MP and champion manipulator Jeremy Thorpe, and the history-making trial that exposed his secrets.

title: Him, Me, Muhammad Ali
author: Randa Jarrar
description: A story collection which moves between realism and fable, history and the present, capturing the lives of Muslim women and men across myriad geographies and circumstances.

title: Homeward Bound: The Life of Paul Simon
author: Peter Ames Carlin
description: An account of the life of beloved American music icon, Paul Simon, by the bestselling rock biographer Peter Ames Carlin.

title: Bolshoi Confidential: Secrets of the Russian Ballet from the Rule of the Tsars to Today
author: Simon Morrison
description: A new history of the Bolshoi Ballet, where visionary performances onstage compete with political machinations backstage.

title: The General vs. the President: MacArthur and Truman at the Brink of Nuclear War
author: H.W. Brands
description: The story of how President Harry Truman and General Douglas MacArthur squared off to decide America's future in the aftermath of World War II.

title: Shock and Awe: Glam Rock and Its Legacy
author: Simon Reynolds
description: A history of glam rock and Its legacy, from the seventies to the twenty-first century.

title: The Man Who Knew: The Life and Times of Alan Greenspan
author: Sebastian Mallaby
description: A biography of one of the most important economic statesmen of our time.

title: Bridget Jones's Baby: The Diaries
author: Helen Fielding
description: Bridget Jones, beloved singleton and global phenomenon, is back with a bump, but who is the father?

title: The Ghosts of Birds
author: Eliot Weinberger
description: A collection of thirty-five essays from accomplished essayist, editor, and translator Eliot Weinberger.

title: The Orchardist
author: Amanda Coplin
description: At the turn of the 20th century in a rural stretch of the Pacific Northwest, a gentle solitary orchardist, Talmadge, tends to apples and apricots. Then two feral, pregnant girls and armed gunmen set Talmadge on an irrevocable course not only to save and protect but to reconcile the ghosts of his own troubled past.

title: The Home Place
author: J. Drew Lanham
description: Dating back to slavery, Edgefield County, South Carolina—a place 'easy to pass by on the way somewhere else'—has been home to generations of Lanhams. In The Home Place , readers meet these extraordinary people, including Drew himself, who over the course of the 1970s falls in love with the natural world around him. As his passion takes flight, however, he begins to ask what it means to be 'the rare bird, the oddity.'

title: Today Will Be Different
author: Maria Semple
description: A novel from the author of Where'd You Go, Bernadette , about a day in the life of Eleanor Flood, forced to abandon her small ambitions and awake to a strange, new future.

title: Nicotine
author: Nell Zink
description: A satirical novel about obsession, idealism, and ownership, centered around a young woman who inherits her bohemian father’s childhood home, only to find it populated by activist squatters.

title: The Trespasser
author: Tana French
genres: ["Fiction", "Hottest Books of the Season", "Mystery, Crime, & Thriller"]
description: The latest novel in French's Dublin Murder Squad crime series, this time focusing on the hard-edged detective Antoinette Conway.

title: Another Day in the Death of America
author: Gary Younge
description: On an average day in America, seven children and teens will be shot dead. In Another Day in the Death of America , award-winning journalist Gary Younge tells the stories of the lives lost during one such day.

title: By Gaslight
author: Steven Price
description: A Victorian era crime novel. William Pinkerton is already famous, the son of the most notorious detective of all time, when he descends into the underworld of Victorian London in pursuit of a new lead on the fabled con Edward Shade. William’s father died without ever finding Shade, but William is determined to drag the thief out of the shadows.

title: All That Man Is
author: David Szalay
description: Somewhere between a novel and a short story collection, nine connected tales interrogating the nature of European manhood.

title: American Ulysses: A Life of Ulysses S. Grant
author: Ronald C. White
description: A major new biography of one of America’s greatest generals—and most misunderstood presidents.

title: News of the World
author: Paulette Jiles
description: In Northern Texas, in the aftermath of the Civil War, an aging traveling news reader agrees to transport a young girl, a former captive of the Kiowa, back to her people in San Antonio.

title: The Wangs vs. the World
author: Jade Chang
description: A comic road trip immigrant tale about a wealthy Chinese-American family that loses it all, and the patriarch's outlandish plan to get back to the top.

title: The Angel of History
author: Rabih Alameddine
description: Set over the course of one night in the waiting room of a psych clinic, The Angel of History follows Yemeni-born poet Jacob as he revisits the events of his life, from his maternal upbringing in an Egyptian whorehouse to his adolescence under the aegis of his wealthy father and his life as a gay Arab man in San Francisco at the height of AIDS.

title: Private Novelist
author: Nell Zink
description: Two comic, experimental novellas, written early in Zink's career, inspired by the work of her friend: the Israeli novelist Avner Shats.

title: Cruel Beautiful World
author: Caroline Leavitt
description: It’s 1969, and sixteen-year-old Lucy is about to run away to live off the grid in rural Pennsylvania, a rash act that will have vicious repercussions for both her and her older sister, Charlotte. As Lucy’s default caretaker for most of their lives, Charlotte’s youth has been marked by the burden of responsibility, but never more so than when Lucy’s dream of a rural paradise turns into a nightmare.

title: The Kid
author: Ron Hansen
description: A new novel from Ron Hansen, the author of The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford , about an iconic American criminal of the old West: legendary outlaw, Billy the Kid.

title: The Mortifications
author: Derek Palacio
description: A family saga set in 1980 about a rural Cuban family torn apart during the Mariel Boatlift.

title: Rogue Heroes
author: Ben Macintyre
description: The history of the SAS, Britain's Secret Special Forces unit that sabotaged the Nazis and changed the nature of war.

title: Crosstalk
author: Connie Willis
description: A genre-bending science fiction romantic comedy that pushes social media, smartphone technology, and twenty-four-hour availability to extremes as one young woman abruptly finds herself with way more connectivity than she ever desired.

title: Ghostland: An American History in Haunted Places
author: Colin Dickey
description: Colin Dickey is on the trail of America's ghosts. Crammed into old houses and hotels, abandoned prisons and empty hospitals, the spirits that linger continue to capture our collective imagination.

title: Something in the Blood: The Untold Story of Bram Stoker, the Man Who Wrote Dracula
author: David J. Skal
description: A biography which reveals the haunted origins of the man who created Dracula and traces the psychosexual contours of late Victorian society.

title: Guilty Thing: A Life of Thomas De Quincey
author: Frances Wilson
description: A biography of the author of Confessions of an English Opium-Eater , one of the most mysterious members of Wordsworth’s circle and the last of the Romantics.

title: A Revolution in Color: The World of John Singleton Copley
author: Jane Kamensky
description: A new history recovering an unknown American Revolution as seen through the eyes of Boston-born painter John Singleton Copley.

title: The Moth Snowstorm: Nature and Joy
author: Michael McCarthy
description: Combining the personal with the polemical, The Moth Snowstorm is a climate change manifesto rooted in experience, and a memoir of the author’s first love: nature.

title: The Explosion Chronicles
author: Yan Lianke, Trans. by Carlos Rojas
description: A Swiftian satire about the ascent of a "fallen fruit" Chinese village named Explosion to a giant city built on vice and presided over by the opportunistic Kong family.

title: Forty Autumns
author: Nina Willner
description: A former American military intelligence officer goes beyond traditional Cold War espionage tales to tell the true story of her family—of five women separated by the Iron Curtain for more than forty years, and their miraculous reunion after the fall of the Berlin Wall.

title: The Most Famous Writer Who Ever Lived
author: Tom Shroder
description: "Shroder revisits the life of his grandfather, the Pulitzer Prize-winning author MacKinlay Kantor's upbringing, and writes not just the life story of one man but a meditation on fame, family secrets and legacies, and what is remembered after we are gone."

title: Napoleon's Last Island
author: Thomas Keneally
description: From the author of Schindler’s List , a novel about the friendship between a quick-witted young woman and one of history’s most intriguing figures, Napoleon Bonaparte, during the final years of his life in exile on St. Helena.

title: Playing Through the Whistle
author: S.L. Price
description: A senior Sports Illustrated writer tells a multigenerational story about Aliquippa, a Pennsylvania steel town gone to seed, and its legendary high school football team.

title: Bridge of Words: Esperanto and the Dream of a Universal Language
author: Esther Schor
description: A biography of a constructed language and the dream of world harmony it sought to realize.

title: Waging War: The Clash Between Presidents and Congress, 1776 to ISIS
author: David J. Barron
description: An timely account of a raging debate: The history of the ongoing struggle between the presidents and Congress over who has the power to declare and wage war.

title: Every Man a Menace
author: Patrick Hoffman
description: Stretching from the Golden Triangle of Southeast Asia to the Golden Gate of San Francisco, Every Man a Menace is a thriller about the making, moving, and selling of ecstasy.

title: I'll Tell You in Person
author: Chloe Caldwell
description: Flailing in jobs, failing at love, getting addicted and un-addicted to people, food, and drugs— I'll Tell You in Person is a frank account of attempts at adulthood and all the less than perfect ways we get there.

title: The Guineveres
author: Sarah Domet
description: Four girls, all named Guinevere, come of age in a convent in wartime. Bored of their life, they come up with a plan to escape.

title: My Own Words
author: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
description: The first book from Ruth Bader Ginsburg since becoming a Supreme Court Justice in 1993—a collection of writings and speeches from the woman who has had a powerful and enduring influence on law, women’s rights, and popular culture.

title: Birth of a Dream Weaver: A Writer's Awakening
description: Birth of a Dream Weaver charts the very beginnings of a writer’s creative output. In this third volume of his memoirs, Kenyan writer Ngugi wa Thiong’o recounts the four years he spent in Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda—threshold years where he found his voice as a playwright, journalist, and novelist, just as Uganda, Kenya, Congo, and other countries were in the final throes of their independence struggles.

title: My Private Property
author: Mary Ruefle
description: A collection of short prose pieces from poet and essayist Mary Ruefle.

title: Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives
author: Tim Harford
description: Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives celebrates the benefits that messiness has in our lives: why it’s important, why we resist it, and why we should embrace it instead.

title: Patricide
author: D. Foy
description: Beyond the story of a boy growing up in a family derailed by a hapless father, Patricide is a brutal search for meaning and identity within the strange secrecy of the family.

title: Born to Run
author: Bruce Springsteen
description: A memoir from the iconic American musician focusing on his family, his formative years, his musical career and his struggles with depression.

title: Mercury
author: Margot Livesy
description: Donald believes he knows all there is to know about seeing. An optometrist in suburban Boston, he is sure that he and his wife, Viv, who runs the local stables, are both devoted to their two children and to each other. Then Mercury—a gorgeous young thoroughbred with a murky past—arrives at Windy Hill and everything changes.

title: Time Travel: A History
author: James Gleick
description: James Gleick tracks the evolution of time travel as an idea that becomes part of contemporary culture.

title: Shirley Jackson: A Rather Haunted Life
author: Ruth Franklin
description: A new biography of the psychological horror writer Shirley Jackson.

title: The Gradual
author: Christopher Priest
description: Alesandro Sussken is a composer living in Glaund, a fascist state constantly at war with another equally faceless opponent. His brother is sent off to fight; his family is destroyed by grief. Occasionally Alesandro catches glimpses of islands in the far distance from the shore, and they feed into the music he composes. But all knowledge of the other islands is forbidden by the military junta, until he is unexpectedly sent on a cultural tour. And what he discovers on his journey will change his perceptions of his home, his music and the ways of the islands themselves.

title: Darling Days
author: iO Tillett Wright
description: A memoir from iO Tillet Wright about coming of age in New York City in the 1980s, having an erratic and mercurial mother, and being born female but adopting a male persona.

title: Eleanor and Hick: The Love Affair That Shaped a First Lady
author: Susan Quinn
description: A intimate account of the love between Eleanor Roosevelt and reporter Lorena Hickok—a relationship that, over more than three decades, transformed both women's lives and empowered them to play significant roles in one of the most tumultuous periods in American history.

title: The Senecans: Four Men and Margaret Thatcher
author: Peter Stothard
description: Blending memoir with ancient and modern politics, Peter Stothard sheds a sideways light on Margaret Thatcher's "believing age," a personal picture of our recent history.

title: The Wonder
author: Emma Donoghue
description: A novel in which an English nurse brought to a small Irish village in 1859 to observe what appears to be a miracle-a girl said to have survived without food for months-soon finds herself fighting to save the child's life.

title: The Lesser Bohemians
author: Eimear McBride
description: A sexually charged novel from the author of A Girl is a Half-Formed Thing . One night an eighteen-year-old Irish girl, recently arrived in London to attend drama school, meets an older man – a well-regarded actor. The clamorous relationship that ensues risks undoing them both.

title: Eyes on the Street: The Life of Jane Jacobs
author: Robert Kanigel
description: The first major biography of the journalist, author and activist Jane Jacobs.

title: Hero of the Empire: The Boer War, a Daring Escape, and the Making of Winston Churchill
author: Candice Millard
description: The story of Winston Churchill's extraordinary and little-known exploits during the Boer War.

title: Reputations
author: Juan Gabriel Vásquez
description: A novel about a political cartoonist at the height of his powers. But this all changes when he's paid an unexpected visit from a young woman who upends his sense of personal history and forces him to re-evaluate his life and work, questioning his position in the world.

title: Blood at the Root: A Racial Cleansing in America
author: Patrick Phillips
description: The history of a notorious racial cleansing in Forsyth County, Georgia, and an examination of the deep roots of racial violence in America.

title: Death's End
author: Cixin Liu, Trans. by Ken Liu
description: The conclusion of the celebrated Chinese science fiction author's Three Body trilogy.

title: Trainwreck: The Women We Love to Hate, Mock, and Fear . . . and Why
author: Sady Doyle
description: Trainwreck dissects a centuries-old phenomenon and asks what it means now, in a time when we have unprecedented access to celebrities and civilians alike, and when women are pushing harder than ever against the boundaries of what it means to 'behave.'

title: Moscow Nights: The Van Cliburn Story-How One Man and His Piano Transformed the Cold War
author: Nigel Cliff
description: The story of a remarkable young Texan pianist, Van Cliburn, who played his way through the wall of fear built by the Cold War, won the hearts of the American and Russian people, and eased tensions between two superpowers on the brink of nuclear war.

title: The Arab of the Future 2
author: Riad Sattouf
description: The darkly humorous second volume of graphic memoir series about the author's childhood in the Middle East.

title: The Gloaming
author: Melanie Finn
description: Pilgrim's husband left her for another woman, stranding her in a Swiss town where she is involved in an accident that leaves three children dead. Cleared of responsibility though overcome with guilt, she absconds to Africa, befriending a series of locals each with their own tragic past.

title: Odes
author: Sharon Olds
description: The latest collection from the Pulitzer Prize-winning poet.

title: A Kingdom of Their Own: The Family Karzai and the Afghan Disaster
author: Joshua Partlow
description: The key to understanding the calamitous Afghan war is the complex, ultimately failed relationship between the Karzai family and the United States, portrayed here by the former Kabul bureau chief for The Washington Post .

title: The Warren
author: Brian Evenson
description: A science fiction novella. When X discovers the existence of another?above ground, outside the protection of the Warren?he must learn what it means to be human, or face the destruction of their two species.

title: Cannibals in Love
author: Mike Roberts
description: A post-9/11 coming-of-age tale told in 18 linked vignettes about the love, self-destruction, absurdity, and ambition that define the millennials.

title: Soul at the White Heat
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: A new collection of critical and personal essays on writing, obsession, and inspiration from National Book Award-winning author Joyce Carol Oates.

title: Looking for The Stranger: Albert Camus and the Life of a Literary Classic
author: Alice Kaplan
description: The story of how a young man in his twenties who had never written a novel turned out a masterpiece that still grips readers more than seventy years later.

title: Nothing Short of Dying: A Clyde Barr Novel
author: Erik Storey
description: Newly sprung from three years in a Juárez prison, Clyde Barr answers an SOS call from his sister Jen, who is being held in the Colorado mountains by a big-time drug supplier.

title: The Underground Railroad
author: Colson Whitehead
genres: ["Fiction", "Historical", "Hottest Books of the Season", "National Book Award Winners"]
description: Winner of the 2017 Pulitzer Prize and the 2016 National Book Award. The chronicle of a young slave's travails as she makes a desperate bid for freedom in an imagined antebellum South where the Underground Railroad is no metaphor.

title: Nutshell
author: Ian McEwan
description: A tale of infedelity, deceit and murder, inspired by Hamlet and told from the unique perspective of a baby inside the womb of one of the plotting protagonists.

title: Commonwealth
author: Ann Patchett
description: From the author of Bel Canto , a novel about how an unexpected romantic encounter irrevocably changes two families’ lives.

title: Jerusalem
author: Alan Moore
description: Employing a kaleidoscope of literary forms and styles that ranges from brutal social realism to extravagant children’s fantasy, from the modern stage drama to the extremes of science fiction, Jerusalem ’s cast of characters includes the living, the dead, the celestial, and the infernal in an intricately woven tapestry that presents a vision of an absolute and timeless human reality in all of its exquisite, comical, and heartbreaking splendor.

title: Loner
author: Teddy Wayne
description: A dark campus novel about an academically gifted but socially awkward young man who becomes obsessed with a glamorous fellow Harvard student, and begins to compromise his morality to be closer to her.

title: Intimations
author: Alexandra Kleeman
description: An unsettling story collection that consists, broadly, of narrative diagrams of the three main stages in a human life: birth, life, and death, from the author of You Too Can Have A Body Like Mine .

title: Avid Reader
author: Robert Gottlieb
description: A memoir from the celebrated editor Robert Gottleib, whose list of authors included Toni Morrison, John Cheever, Doris Lessing, John le Carré, Michael Crichton, Lauren Bacall, Katharine Graham, Robert Caro, Nora Ephron, and Bill Clinton.

title: Little Nothing
author: Marisa Silver
description: The story of a girl, scorned for her physical deformity, whose passion and salvation lie in her otherworldly ability to transform herself and the world around her.

title: Good Vibrations: My Life as a Beach Boy
author: Mike Love & James S. Hirsch
description: A memoir by Mike Love about his five decade career as the front man for The Beach Boys.

title: The Virginity of Famous Men
author: Christine Sneed
description: A short story collection from the author of the novels Paris, He Said and Little Known Facts , and the story collection Portraits of a Few of the People I've Made Cry .

title: A Truck Full of Money: One Man's Quest to Recover from Great Success
author: Tracy Kidder
description: A biographer of a pioneering software prodigy, entrepreneur and philanthropist Paul English.

title: Darktown
author: Thomas Mullen
description: A police procedural set in 1948 Atlanta, exploring a murder, corrupt police, and strained race relations.

title: When in French: Love in a Second Language
author: Lauren Collins
