description: A memoir about what it means to love someone in a second language. The author finds this out for herself when she falls in love with a frenchman, wondering if there are things she doesn't understand about him becasue she has never spoken to him in his native tongue.

title: Children of the New World
author: Alexander Weinstein
description: A short story collection set in a near-future world of social media implants, memory manufacturers, dangerously immersive virtual reality games, and alarmingly intuitive robots.

title: Man of the World: The Further Endeavors of Bill Clinton
author: Joe Conason
description: An examination of Bill Clinton's post-presidential career.

title: Eve Out of Her Ruins
author: Ananda Devi, Trans. by Jeffrey Zuckerman
description: A novel about four young Mauritians trapped in their country's endless cycle of fear and violence, focusing on Eve, whose body is her only weapon and source of power.

title: Wolf Boys: Two American Teenagers and Mexico's Most Dangerous Drug Cartel
author: Dan Slater
description: The story of two American teens recruited as killers for a Mexican cartel, and their pursuit by a Mexican-American detective who realizes the War on Drugs is unwinnable.

title: Shelter in Place
author: Alexander Maksik
description: Set in the Pacific Northwest in the jittery, jacked-up early 1990s, Shelter in Place is a novel about the hereditary nature of mental illness, the fleeting intensity of youth, the obligations of family, and the dramatic consequences of love.

title: What the F: What Swearing Reveals About Our Language, Our Brains, and Ourselves
author: Benjamin K. Bergen
description: An examination, by cognitive behavioral scientist Bergen, about what swearing reveals about our language, our brains and ourselves.

title: Black Wave
author: Michelle Tea
description: A fictionalized memoir set in an alternate 1999. Desperate to quell her addiction to drugs, disastrous romance, and nineties San Francisco, Michelle heads south for LA. But soon it's officially announced that the world will end in one year, and life in the sprawling metropolis becomes increasingly weird.

title: Feminist Fight Club
author: Jessica Bennett
description: Part manual, part manifesto, Feminist Fight Club is a guide to navigating subtle sexism at work, providing real-life career advice and humorous reinforcement for a new generation of professional women.

title: Play Anything: The Pleasure of Limits, the Uses of Boredom, and the Secret of Games
author: Ian Bogost
description: Game designer and philosopher Ian Bogost shows how we can overcome our daily anxiety; transforming the boring, ordinary world around us into one of endless, playful possibilities.

title: Indelible Ink: The Trials of John Peter Zenger and the Birth of America's Free Press
author: Richard Kluger
description: The untold story of the battle to legalize free expression in America by the Pulitzer Prize–winning author of Ashes to Ashes .

title: Here I Am
author: Jonathan Safran Foer
description: Unfolding over four tumultuous weeks in present-day Washington, D.C., Here I Am is the story of a fracturing Jewish-American family in a moment of crisis, set against the backdrop of an impending war in the Middle East.

title: Razor Girl
author: Carl Hiaasen
description: When Lane Coolman's car is bashed from behind on the road to the Florida Keys, what appears to be an ordinary accident is anything but. Behind the wheel of the other car is Merry Mansfield--the eponymous Razor Girl--and the crash scam is only the beginning of events that spiral crazily out of control in this comic novel.

title: Sleeping on Jupiter
author: Anuradha Roy
description: A novel about violence, love, and religion in modern India focusing on a ex-pat photographer retuning to come to terms with her past.

title: The Art of Waiting: On Fertility, Medicine, and Motherhood
author: Belle Boggs
description: An exploration of the natural, medical, psychological, and political facets of fertility.

title: A Gentleman in Moscow
author: Amor Towles
description: A novel set in Russia in 1922, in which Count Alexander Rostov is deemed an unrepentant aristocrat by a Bolshevik tribunal, and is sentenced to house arrest in the Metropol, a grand hotel across the street from the Kremlin. Rostov must now live in an attic room while some of the most tumultuous decades in Russian history are unfolding outside the hotel’s doors.

title: She Made Me Laugh: My Friend Nora Ephron
author: Richard Cohen
description: A memoir of the former Washington Post journalist's friendship with the writer Nora Ephron.

title: American Revolutions: A Continental History 1750-1804
author: Alan Taylor
description: A new history from the two-time Pulitzer winner that recasts our thinking about America’s founding period.

title: Mischling
author: Affinity Konar
description: A novel about twin sisters trying to survive Auchwitz and the horrors of Josef Mengele's "Zoo."

title: Everfair
author: Nisi Shawl
description: A Neo-Victorian alternate history novel that explores the question of what might have come of Belgium's disastrous colonization of the Congo if the native populations had learned about steam technology a bit earlier.

title: The Risen
author: Ron Rash
description: A suspenseful novel about two brothers and their relationship to a magnetic young woman who disappeared one summer decades previous.

title: Against Everything
author: Mark Greif
description: A collection of essays from Mark Greif, the co-founder of n+1 , addressing such key topics in the cultural, political, and intellectual life of our time as the tyranny of exercise, the tyranny of nutrition and food snobbery, the sexualization of childhood, the philosophical meaning of Radiohead, the rise and fall of the hipster, the impact of the Occupy Wall Street movement, and the crisis of policing.

title: Mad Enchantment: Claude Monet and the Painting of the Water Lilies
author: Ross King
description: Mad Enchantment tells the full story behind the creation of the Water Lilies, as the horrors of World War I came ever closer to Paris and Giverny, and a new generation of younger artists, led by Henri Matisse and Pablo Picasso, were challenging the achievements of Impressionism.

title: Strangers in Their Own Land
author: Arlie Russell Hochschild
description: Renowned sociologist Arlie Hochschild embarks on a thought-provoking journey from her liberal hometown of Berkeley, California, deep into Louisiana bayou country—a stronghold of the conservative right.

title: The Fortunes
author: Peter Ho Davies
description: A recasting of American history through the lives of Chinese Americans, reimagining the multigenerational novel through the fractures of immigrant family experience.

title: Substitute: Going to School With a Thousand Kids
author: Nicholson Baker
description: A detailed account of Baker's 28 days working as a K-12 substitute teacher in a Maine public school district.

title: ADHD Nation: Children, Doctors, Big Pharma, and the Making of an American Epidemic
author: Alan Schwarz
description: An account of the widespread misdiagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder—and how its unchecked growth over half a century has made ADHD one of the most controversial conditions in medicine, with serious effects on children, adults, and society.

title: His Final Battle: The Last Months of Franklin Roosevelt
author: Joseph Lelyveld
description: An in depth look at the last months in the life of FDR.

title: We Eat Our Own
author: Kea Wilson
description: Inspired by a true story from the annals of 1970s Italian horror film, the story of a struggling actor in 1970s New York who gets embroiled in a movie director’s unthinkable experiment in the Amazon.

title: Enough Said: What's Gone Wrong with the Language of Politics?
author: Mark Thompson
description: Enough Said tells the story of how we got from the language of FDR and Churchill to that of Donald Trump. It examines the public language we’ve been left with: compressed, immediate, sometimes brilliantly impactful, but robbed of most of its explanatory power.

title: All the Kremlin's Men: Inside the Court of Vladimir Putin
author: Mikhail Zygar
description: Based on an unprecedented series of interviews with Vladimir Putin’s inner circle, this book presents a radically different view of power and politics in Russia. The image of Putin as a strongman is dissolved. In its place is a weary figurehead buffeted—if not controlled—by the men who at once advise and deceive him.

title: Hitler: Ascent, 1889-1939
author: Volker Ullrich
description: A biography of the dictator focusing on Hitler's formative and early political years, focusing on how he experienced his world, formed his political beliefs, and wielded power.

title: The Tetris Effect: The Game that Hypnotized the World
author: Dan Ackerman
description: In this fast-paced business story, reporter Dan Ackerman reveals how Tetris became one of the world’s first viral hits, passed from player to player, eventually breaking through the Iron Curtain into the West.

title: The Revolutionaries Try Again
author: Mauro Javier Cardenas
description: The Revolutionaries Try Again plays out against the lost decade of Ecuador's austerity and the stymied idealism of three childhood friends—an expat, a bureaucrat, and a playwright—who are as sure about the evils of dictatorship as they are unsure of everything else, including each other.

title: Lady Cop Makes Trouble
author: Amy Stewart
description: The second novel in the Kopp Sisters crime series, set in New Jersey on the eve of America's entry into WWI and based on the true story of one of America's first female deputy sheriffs.

title: The Six: The Lives of the Mitford Sisters
author: Laura Thompson
description: The true story of the infamous Milford sisters, born into country-house privilege in the early years of the 20th century, who became prominent as "bright young things" in the high society of interwar London. Then, as the shadows crept over 1930s Europe, the stark?and very public?differences in their outlooks came to symbolize the political polarities of a dangerous decade.

title: Perfume River
author: Robert Olen Butler
description: A novel that examines family ties and the legacy of the Vietnam War through the portrait of a single North Florida family.

title: The White Mirror
author: Elsa Hart
description: Set in early 18th century China. The discovery of a murdered monk prompts a scholar to defer an odyssey of self-discovery to search for justice, unearthing even deeper truths.

title: The Story of a Brief Marriage
author: Anuk Arudpragasam
description: Orphaned by the Sri Lankan civil war, a young man hopes an arranged marriage might make his last days in a refugee camp more meaningful.

title: The Shipwrecked Mind
author: Mark Lilla
description: A short book drawn from a series of essays analyzes the contemporary relevance of the oft-maligned "reactionary," who isn’t retreating into the past so much as reclaiming it.

title: Hidden Figures
author: Margot Lee Shetterly
description: Recently released as a film adaptation, Hidden Figures is an inside look at the World War II–era black female mathematicians who assisted greatly in the United States’ aeronautics industry.

title: The Senator Next Door: A Memoir from the Heartland
author: Amy Klobuchar
description: Minnesota Senator Amy Klobuchar chronicles her heartland journey, from her immigrant grandparents to her middle-class suburban upbringing to her rise in American politics.

title: The Kingdom of Speech
author: Tom Wolfe
description: Tom Wolfe argues that what we think we know about speech and human evolution is wrong, focusing on a critique of Charles Darwin and Noam Chomsky.

title: The Nix
author: Nathan Hill
description: An epic, comic novel about a struggling author's relationship with the political activist mother who abandoned him as a child.

title: Play All: A Bingewatcher’s Notebook
author: Clive James
description: The celebrated former Observer television critic discusses the current Golden Age TV shows he sat down to binge watch upon being diagnosed with cancer.

title: The Dream of Enlightenment: The Rise of Modern Philosophy
author: Anthony Gottlieb
description: The author of the classic The Dream of Reason explains the rise of modern thought.

title: A Great Reckoning
author: Louise Penny
description: The latest mystery novel in Penny's Quebec-set Chief Inspector Gamache series.

title: Surrender, New York
author: Caleb Carr
description: In rural, impoverished Burgoyne County, New York, a pattern of strange deaths begins to emerge. Once famed advisors to the New York City Police Department, Dr. Trajan Jones, a psychological profiler, and Dr. Michael Li, a trace evidence expert, are called in to help solve the crimes.

title: Behold the Dreamers
author: Imbolo Mbue
description: Winner of the 2017 PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction. A novel exploring the struggles of two New York couples — one white and affluent, the other poor Cameroonian immigrants — during the 2008 financial crisis.

title: The Terror Years: From al-Qaeda to the Islamic State
author: Lawrence Wright
description: A collection of articles detailing the path that terror in the Middle East has taken, from the rise of al-Qaeda in the 1990s to the recent beheadings of reporters and aid workers by ISIS.

title: Blood in the Water: The Attica Prison Uprising of 1971 and Its Legacy
author: Heather Ann Thompson
description: An account of the Attica prison uprising of 1971 and its legacy.

title: Trump Revealed: An American Journey of Ambition, Ego, Money, and Power
author: Michael Kranish & Marc Fisher
description: A book examining the rise and psyche of Donald Trump, drawn from in-depth reporting from the Washington Post .

title: The Huntress: The Adventures, Escapades, and Triumphs of Alicia Patterson
author: Alice Arlen and Michael J. Arlen
description: A biography of Alicia Patterson: Aviatrix, Sportswoman, Journalist, Publisher.

title: Falling Awake: Poems
author: Alice Oswald
description: The latest poetry collection from Oswald, who reimagines classical figures such as Orpheus and Tithonus alive in an English landscape together with shadows, flies, villagers, dew, crickets?all characterized in tension between the weight of death and their own willpower.

title: Where the Jews Aren't
author: Masha Gessen
description: The sad and absurd story of Birobidzhan, Russia's Jewish Autonomous Region.

title: Against Democracy
author: Jason Brennan
description: In this trenchant book, Jason Brennan argues that democracy should be judged by its results –– and the results are not good enough.

title: No House to Call My Home: Love, Family, and Other Transgressions
author: Ryan Berg
description: Focusing on the lives and loves of eight unforgettable youth, No House to Call My Home traces their efforts to break away from dangerous sex work and cycles of drug and alcohol abuse, and, in the process, to heal from years of trauma.

title: Riverine: A Memoir from Anywhere but Here
author: Angela Palm
description: An essayistic memoir about the part of rural Indiana where the author grew up, and her high school sweetheart who is now in prison for a double murder.

title: The Girl with the Lower Back Tattoo
author: Amy Schumer
description: A memoir from comedian Amy Schumer in which she mines her past for stories about her teenage years, her family, relationships, and sex and shares the experiences that have shaped who she is.

title: Rise the Dark
author: Michael Koryta
description: Private investigator Mark Novak returns to his old haunts in Montana in pursuit of the man who murdered his wife in Cassadaga, Florida—a strange town known for its psychics.

title: The Selfishness of Others: An Essay on the Fear of Narcissism
author: Kristin Dombek
description: An examination of narcissism and our relationship to it.

title: All at Sea
author: Decca Aitkenhead
description: A memoir of love and loss, of how one couple changed each other’s life, and of what a sudden death can do to the people who survive.

title: The Euro: How a Common Currency Threatens the Future of Europe
author: Joseph E. Stiglitz
description: Nobel Prize–winning economist Joseph E. Stiglitz dismantles the prevailing consensus around what ails Europe, demolishing the champions of austerity while offering a series of plans that he maintains can rescue the continent?and the world?from further devastation.

title: The Obelisk Gate
author: N. K. Jemisin
description: The second novel in the Broken Earth post-apocalyptic fantasy trilogy. Sequel to The Fifth Season .

title: The Art of Rivalry: Four Friendships, Betrayals, and Breakthroughs in Modern Art
author: Sebastian Smee
description: A study of the creative tensions embedded in four separate friendships between artists and the effect of those tensions on their art and the Modernist movement.

title: The Golden Age
author: Joan London
description: Set in a children's polio convalescent home in Western Australia in the 1950s, the novel centers on the budding friendship between two 13-year-old patients, Elsa Briggs and Frank Gold, and the adults around them, who seem to have more difficulty coping than they do.

title: Altamont: The Rolling Stones, the Hells Angels, and the Inside Story of Rock's Darkest Day
author: Joel Selvin
description: The story of the Rolling Stones’ infamous Altamont concert in San Francisco, the disastrous historic event that marked the end of the idealistic 1960s.

title: Ghost Talkers
author: Mary Robinette Kowal
description: A new novel from fantasy author Mary Robinette Kowal featuring the mysterious spirit corps and their heroic work in World War I.

title: Known and Strange Things
author: Teju Cole
description: A collection of more than fifty essays on politics, photography, travel, history, and literature from the author of Open City .

title: How Everything Became War and the Military Became Everything
author: Rosa Brooks
description: A non-fiction book examining what happens when the ancient boundary between war and peace is erased.

title: The Glorious Heresies
author: Lisa McInerney
description: A biting, darkly comic vision of an Irish city plagued by poverty and exploitation, where salvation still awaits in the most unexpected places.

title: The Last Days of New Paris
author: China Miéville
description: A thriller of war that never was—of survival in an impossible city, in which the Nazis and the Surrealist movement face off against one another in Paris.

title: Playing Dead: A Journey Through the World of Death Fraud
author: Elizabeth Greenwood
description: An investigation into the world of death fraud and deliberate disappearance.

title: Another Brooklyn
author: Jacqueline Woodson
description: A novel for adults from National Book Award-winning YA author Woodson, about a young black girl growing up in Brooklyn in the 1970s, and the friendships and dangers that shape her.

title: Scream: A Memoir of Glamour and Dysfunction
author: Tama Janowitz
description: A memoir by the author of Slaves of New York about life and literary fame, in and outside of New York City.

title: I Contain Multitudes: The Microbes Within Us and a Grander View of Life
author: Ed Yong
description: A popular science examination of microbes and the researchers that explore them.

title: Powerhouse: The Untold Story of Hollywood's Creative Artists Agency
author: James Andres Miller
description: The history of Hollywood’s transformation over the past five decades as seen through the agency at the heart of it all.

title: How to Party With an Infant
author: Kaui Hart Hemmings
description: The story of a quirky single mom in San Francisco who tiptoes through the minefields of the 'Mommy Wars' and manages to find friendship and love.

title: Mickey
author: Chelsea Martin
description: Told in a series of vignettes, Mickey is one young woman’s journey to figuring out life (or not) amidst drunken mistakes, reality TV marathons, bathroom sex, and the daydreamed titles of imaginary art installations.

title: The Gardener and the Carpenter: What the New Science of Child Development Tells Us About the Relationship Between Parents and Children
author: Alison Gopnik
description: One of the world's leading child psychologists shatters the myth of 'good parenting,' arguing for a less structured approach to raising children.

title: The Glamour of Strangeness: Artists and the Last Age of the Exotic
author: Jamie James
description: Drawing on his own career as a travel writer and years of archival research uncovering previously unpublished letters and journals, James investigates the powerful connection between art and the exotic, focusing on six historic artists who left home for more far-flung locales.

title: Patient H.M.: A Story of Memory, Madness, and Family Secrets
author: Luke Dittrich
description: The story of the studied human research subject of all time, the amnesic known as Patient H.M., a man who forever altered our understanding of how memory works—and whose treatment (by the author's grandfather) raises deeply unsettling questions about the human cost of scientific progress.

title: The Hero's Body
author: William Giraldi
description: A memoir of motorcycles and muscles, of obsession and grief, and of a young man who learned how to stay alive through literature.

title: Adnan's Story: The Search for Truth and Justice After Serial
author: Rabia Chaudry
description: Family friend and advocate Rabia Chaudry presents new evidence that she maintains dismantles the State's case against Adnan Syed, whose imprisonment for the murder of his ex-girlfriend was the subject of the wildly popular Serial podcast.

title: The Cauliflower
author: Nicola Barker
description: A novel about the building of the spiritual legacy and charisma of Sri Ramakrishna, a Hindu mystic born in the state of Bengal in 1836.

title: War & Turpentine
author: Stefan Hertmans, Trans. by David Mckay
description: A hybrid book about a Flemish man who reconstructs his grandfather's story—his hopes, loves, and art, all disrupted by the First World War—from the notebooks he filled with pieces of his life.

title: White Nights in Split Town City
author: Annie DeWitt
description: Both coming-of-age story and cautionary tale. In her mother's absence, Jean is torn between the adult world and her surreal fantasies of escape as she and Fender build a fort to survey the rumors of their town.

title: Dinosaurs on Other Planets
author: Danielle McLaughlin
description: A collection of short stories set in present day Ireland, in the naturalistic tradition of John McGahern and Claire Keegan.

title: I Will Send Rain
author: Rae Meadows
description: A novel about a woman fighting for her family's survival in the early years of the Dust Bowl.

title: Three Years with the Rat
author: Jay Hosking
description: Jay Hosking's debut novel unravels a young man's journey through a labyrinth of secrets as he tries to find his missing sister.

title: When Watched: Stories
author: Leopoldine Core
description: Through 19 stories, Core's debut short story collection revolves around the intimacy and complexity of human connection in New York City.

title: Good Morning, Midnight
author: Lily Brooks-Dalton
description: In this debut novel, an aging astronomer named Augustine refuses to abandon his work in the Arctic during an emergency evacuation and finds himself all alone but for a mysterious child, Iris, when the airwaves go silent. At the same time, Mission Specialist Sullivan is aboard the Aether on its return flight from Jupiter when Mission Control falls inexplicably silent, and she and her crewmates are forced to wonder if they will ever get home.

title: American Heiress: The Wild Saga of the Kidnapping, Crimes and Trial of Patty Hearst
author: Jeffrey Toobin
description: The wild saga of the kidnapping, crimes and trial of Patty Hearst, from the author of The Run of His Life: The People v. O.J. Simpson .

title: Bright, Precious Days
author: Jay McInerney
description: The third installment of McInerney's examination of the lives of fashionable, and now middle-aged, New York couple Corinne and Russell Calloway.

title: The Accidental Life: An Editor's Notes on Writing and Writers
author: Terry McDonell
description: A memoir about writing and editing life, as well as a look behind the scenes at some of the most influential magazines in America (and the writers who made them what they are).

title: Christodora
author: Tim Murphy
description: A multi-character saga set in an iconic building in New York, focusing on the heartbreak wrought by AIDS and drugs.

title: War Porn
author: Roy Scranton
description: A novel in three nested stories--a group of liberals at a barbecue in Utah, an American soldier deployed to Baghdad, and an Iraqi mathematician on the eve of the invasion--exploring how the Iraq war causes all their lives to intersect.

title: Carousel Court
author: Joe McGinniss, Jr.
description: A portrait of modern marriage in a nation scarred by vanished jobs, abandoned homes, psychotropic cure-alls, infidelity via iPhone, and ruthless choices.

title: The Fire This Time
author: ed. Jesmyn Ward
description: A collection of essays and poems about race in America.

title: Still Here
author: Lara Vapnyar
description: A novel following the intertwined lives of four immigrants in New York City as they grapple with love and tumult, the challenges of a new home, and the absurdities of the digital age.

title: To the Bright Edge of the World
author: Eowyn Ivey
description: A romantic historical adventure novel set in the Alaskan wilderness in the winter of 1885.

title: I Shot the Buddha
author: Colin Cotterill
description: A Dr. Siri mystery with a large cast of characters, some supernatural, set in Loas in 1979.

title: Compartment No. 6
author: Rosa Liksom, Trans. by Lola Rogers
description: A darkly humorous story of two strangers--a young female student and a coarse older man--sharing a compartment on a train journey from Moscow to Mongolia.

title: I'm Supposed to Protect You from All This
author: Nadja Spiegelman
description: A memoir, by the daughter of Art Spiegelman and Francoise Mouly, about the narratives that connect and divide four generations of women on her mother’s side.

title: The Fall of Heaven
author: Andrew Scott Cooper
description: An account of the rise and fall of Iran's glamorous Pahlavi dynasty.

title: Harmony
author: Carolyn Parkhurst
description: The story of how a seemingly 'normal' family could become desperate enough to leave everything behind and move to a child behavioral camp in New Hampshire.

title: How I Became a North Korean
author: Krys Lee
description: The disparate lives of three teenagers converge when they flee their homes, finding themselves in a small Chinese town just across the river from North Korea.

title: The Trees
author: Ali Shaw
description: A post-apocalyptic novel in which a unlikely group of people band together on a quest though the dense forest that has, overnight, overrun the earth.

title: March: Book 3
author: John Lewis, Andrew Aydin and Nate Powell
description: A National Book Award winner and the conclusion of the MARCH trilogy. Congressman John Lewis, an American icon and one of the key figures of the civil rights movement, joins co-writer Andrew Aydin and artist Nate Powell to bring the lessons of history to life for a new generation.

title: Landmarks
author: Robert MacFarlane
description: A celebration of the language of landscape and the power of words to shape our sense of place.

title: Purity
author: Jonathan Franzen
description: The author of the The Corrections and Freedom returns with an epic tale about recent college graduate Purity—also known as "Pip"—who has a load of student-loan debt and a neurotic mother who refuses to reveal Pip's father's identity. When she moves to Bolivia to work for a WikiLeaks-like company run by a mysterious figure named Andreas Wolf, Pip struggles to behave ethically as she is asked to engage in suspicious activities and begins to uncover some important secrets.

title: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child
author: J.K. Rowling, Jack Thorne & John Tiffany
description: Based on an original new story by J.K. Rowling, Jack Thorne and John Tiffany, a new play by Jack Thorne, Harry Potter and the Cursed Child is the eighth story in the Harry Potter series.

title: Heroes of the Frontier
author: Dave Eggers
description: "A darkly comic novel about a mother and her two young children on a journey through an Alaskan wilderness plagued by wildfires and a uniquely American madness."

title: You Will Know Me
author: Megan Abbott
description: Devon is a gymnastics prodigy and Olympic hopeful. For her parents, there are no limits to how far they'll go to help her achieve that dream--until a violent death rocks their close-knit gymnastics community and everything they have worked so hard for is suddenly at risk.

title: The Games: A Global History of the Olympics
author: David Goldblatt
description: A sporting and social history of the modern Olympic games.

title: Neon Green
author: Margaret Wappler
description: In the summer of 1994, when a flying saucer lands in the Allens' backyard, family patriarch and environmental activist Ernest is up in arms. According to the company facilitating the visits, the spaceship is 100 percent non-toxic, but as Ernest's panic increases, so do his questions.

title: Truly Madly Guilty
author: Liane Moriarty
description: A novel about three seemingly happy couples. Moriarty takes on the foundations of our lives: marriage, sex, parenthood, and friendship. She shows how guilt can expose the fault lines in the most seemingly strong relationships.

title: The Unseen World
author: Liz Moore
description: Ada Sibelius is raised by David, her brilliant, eccentric, socially inept single father, who directs a computer science lab in 1980s-era Boston. The lab begins to gain acclaim at the same time that David’s mysterious history comes into question. When his mind begins to falter, leaving Ada virtually an orphan, she is taken in by one of David’s colleagues. Soon she embarks on a mission to uncover her father’s secrets.

title: Good as Gone
author: Amy Gentry
description: A thriller about a kidnapped young woman who suddenly reappears at her family’s doorstep eight years after her late night abduction.

title: Dark Matter
author: Blake Crouch
description: A ordinary college physics professor is knocked unconscious by an attacker and wakes up in an alternate reality where he is the inventor of a device that allows people to traverse the multiverse.

title: Leaving Lucy Pear
author: Anna Solomon
description: Set in 1920s New England, the story of two women who are both mothers to the same unforgettable girl.

title: The Muse
author: Jessie Burton
description: The story of two young women—a Caribbean immigrant in 1960s London, and a bohemian woman in 1930s Spain—and the powerful mystery that ties them together.

title: Revulsion: Thomas Bernhard in San Salvador
author: Horacio Castellanos Moya, Trans. by Lee Klein
description: Moya's famous pastiche, written in the style of the Austrian author Thomas Bernhard and published for the first time in English, ranting against the ills of San Salvadorian society.

title: This Must Be the Place
author: Maggie O'Farrell
description: "A novel set in the wilds of Ireland. A reclusive French film star, her American linguist husband, and their exes, parents, siblings, and children from various marriages feature in a sophisticated story about love."

title: The Hopefuls
author: Jennifer Close
description: "The story of a young wife who follows her husband and his political dreams to Washington, D.C., a city of idealism, gossip, and complicated friendships among the young aspiring elite."

title: The Sunlight Pilgrims
author: Jenni Fagan
description: It's November of 2020, and the world is freezing over. Grieving and ready to build life anew, Dylan heads north to bury his mother's and grandmother's ashes on the Scottish islands where they once lived. Hundreds of miles away, twelve-year-old Estella and her survivalist mother, Constance, scrape by in the snowy, mountainous Highlands, preparing for a record-breaking winter.

title: Monterey Bay
author: Lindsay Hatton
description: A novel set around the creation of the world-famous Monterey Bay Aquarium--and the last days of John Steinbeck's Cannery Row . A portrait of an exceptional woman, a world-famous aquarium, and the beloved town they both call home.

title: Losing It
author: Emma Rathbone
description: A comic novel about a woman who still has her virginity at the age of twenty-six, and the summer she's determined to lose it—and find herself.

title: The Inseparables
author: Stuart Nadler
description: A novel about three generations of smart, articulate women dealing with challenging life passages.

title: Multiple Choice
author: Alejandro Zambra, Trans. by Megan McDowell
description: Written in the form of a Chilean standardized test, Multiple Choice invites the reader to respond to language exercises and short narrative passages through multiple-choice questions that are thought-provoking, usually unanswerable, and often absurd.

title: The Woman in Cabin 10
author: Ruth Ware
description: A psychological thriller set on a cruise ship in whcih a travel writer witnesses a woman being thrown overboard.

title: Revolver
author: Duane Swierczynski
description: In Duane Swierczynski's thriller, the murder of two policeman in mid-1960s Philadelphia has reverberations for successive generations of cops.

title: The Voyeur's Motel
author: Gay Talese
description: A work of narrative journalism, focusing on the time Talese spent with a man who for decades has been using his motel to spy on couples having sex.

title: Pond
author: Claire-Louise Bennett
description: "A book that captures the interior reality of its unnamed protagonist, a young woman living a singular and mostly solitary existence on the outskirts of a small Irish coastal village."

title: A Book About Love
author: Jonah Lehrer
description: Science writer Jonah Lehrer explores the mysterious subject of love.

title: Not Pretty Enough: The Unlikely Triumph of Helen Gurley Brown
author: Gerri Hirshey
description: A biography that shines new light on the life of one of the most vibrant, vexing, and indelible women of the twentieth century.

title: The Heavenly Table
author: Donald Ray Pollack
description: A darkly comic picaresque wide a wide cast of characters, set in rural Ohio in 1917, focusing on three sharecropper brothers turned outlaws, and a well-meaning farmer and his wife.

title: Trials of the Earth: The True Story of a Pioneer Woman
author: Mary Mann Hamilton
description: A diary from the late 19th century. The only known first-person account of one woman's struggles and triumphs taming the Mississippi Delta.

title: Hot Milk
author: Deborah Levy
description: "Sofia, a young anthropologist, has spent much of her life trying to solve the mystery of her mother’s unexplainable illness. She is frustrated with Rose and her constant complaints, but utterly relieved to be called to abandon her own disappointing fledgling adult life. She and her mother travel to the searing, arid coast of southern Spain to see a famous consultant--their very last chance--in the hope that he might cure her unpredictable limb paralysis."

title: You'll Grow Out of It
author: Jessi Klein
description: A memoir from comedian in which she offers-through a collection of real-life stories-her take on a variety of topics she has experienced along her strange journey to womanhood and beyond.

title: Wear and Tear: The Threads of My Life
author: Tracy Tynan
description: Tracy Peacock Tynan grew up in London in the 1950’s and 60s, privy to her literary parents’ glamorous parties and famous friends. In this memoir she tells the story of the time through clothes.

title: Miss Jane
author: Brad Watson
description: Drawing on the story of his own great-aunt, Watson explores the life of Miss Jane Chisolm, born in rural, early-twentieth-century Mississippi with a genital birth defect that would stand in the way of the central 'uses' for a woman in that time and place: sex and marriage.

title: Ninety-Nine Stories of God
author: Joy Williams
description: From Pulitzer Prize finalist Joy Williams, a series of short, fictional vignettes exploring our day-to-day interactions with an ever-elusive and arbitrary God.

title: Brazillionaires: Wealth, Power, Decadence, and Hope in an American Country
author: Alex Cuadros
description: A non-fiction book about a country’s spectacular economic rise and fall, intertwined with the story of Brazil’s wealthiest citizen, Eike Batista.

title: How to Be a Person in the World: Ask Polly's Guide Through the Paradoxes of Modern Life
author: Heather Havrilesky
description: A collection of new letters by the author of the popular advice column Ask Polly, featured weekly on New York Magazine 's The Cut.

title: The Death of Rex Nhongo
author: C. B. George
description: A novel set inn Zimbabwe's capital, in which a gun left in a taxi brings together five marriages.

title: Break in Case of Emergency
author: Jessica Winter
description: An irreverent comedy about friendship, fertility, and fighting for one’s sanity in a toxic workplace.

title: The Wicked Boy: The Mystery of a Victorian Child Murderer
author: Kate Summerscale
description: An investigation of a late-19th-century crime in which a 13-year-old boy murdered his mother.

title: The Last One
author: Alexandra Oliva
description: A post-apocalyptic thriller in which survival is the name of the game, as the line blurs between reality TV and reality itself—and one woman's mind and body are pushed to the limit.

title: Siracusa
author: Delia Ephron
description: An novel about marriage and deceit that follows two couples on vacation in Siracusa, a town on the coast of Sicily, where the secrets they have hidden from one another are exposed and relationships are unraveled.

title: The Invoice
author: Jonas Karlsson
description: A short, satirical parable about a simple man leading a contented existence, who receives an enormous 'happiness tax' bill from the government that forces him to question his outlook on life.

title: Almighty: Courage, Resistance, and Existential Peril in the Nuclear Age
author: Dan Zak
description: An examination of the dangers posed by nuclear weapons, and the inadequate security apparatuses that supposedly keep them from falling into the wrong hands.

title: On Trails
author: Robert Moor
description: An exploration of how trails help us understand the world—from tiny ant trails to hiking paths that span continents, from interstate highways to the Internet.

title: The Devourers
author: Indra Das
description: A mythic saga of India and the Mughal Empire, spanning centuries and lands, involving a race of people at once more than human yet kin to beasts, ruled by instincts and desires blood-deep and ages-old.

title: The House at the Edge of Night
author: Catherine Banner
description: A sweeping saga about four generations of a family who live and love on an enchanting island off the coast of Italy.

title: Dr. Knox
author: Peter Spiegelman
description: In Peter Spiegelman's noir thriller, Dr. Knox, a well-intentioned doctor working in the seedier parts of Los Angeles, gets himself into big trouble.

title: The Trouble with Goats and Sheep
author: Joanna Cannon
description: In a small-town cul-de-sac in rural England, preteen Grace and her friend Tilly set out to find God. What they unknowingly uncover is an ugly neighborhood secret.

title: Bush
author: Jean Edward Smith
description: A biography of President George W. Bush's time in office.

title: Bobby Kennedy: The Making of a Liberal Icon
author: Larry Tye
description: An in-depth biography of Bobby Kennedy.

title: The Return: Fathers, Sons, and the Land in Between
author: Hisham Matar
description: A memoir of the author's journey home to his native Libya in search of the truth behind his father’s disappearance.

title: How to Set a Fire and Why
author: Jesse Ball
description: "A teenage girl. A shattering loss. An obsession with a secret arson club. This is the story of a girl who has nothing and will burn anything."

title: Here Comes the Sun
author: Nicole Dennis-Benn
description: A novel about three women battling for independence while a maelstrom of change threatens their Jamaican village.

title: I Am No One
author: Patrick Flanery
description: A university professor worries about lost privacy and past sins after receiving cartons filled with years of personal data in this blend of psychological and political suspense.

title: Jonathan Unleashed
author: Meg Rosoff
description: "A novel about a young New Yorker’s search for happiness and the two dogs who help him find it."

title: Underground Airlines
author: Ben H. Winters
description: "In an alternate reality America where slavery was never abolished, a gifted young black man calling himself Victor has struck a bargain with federal law enforcement, working as a bounty hunter for the US Marshall Service."

title: Critics, Monsters, Fanatics, and Other Literary Essays
author: Cynthia Ozick
description: A collection of essays confronting the past, present, and future of literary culture.

title: Welcome to the Goddamn Ice Cube: Chasing Fear and Finding Home in the Great White North
author: Blair Braverman
description: A memoir of a young woman reclaiming her courage in the stark landscapes of the north.

title: You Are Having a Good Time
author: Amie Barrodale
description: A collection of short stories about people who drink too much, say the wrong things, want the wrong people.

title: Belgravia
author: Julian Fellowes
description: From the creator of Downton Abbey , the story of a secret that unravels behind the porticoed doors of London's grandest postcode. Set in the 1840s when the upper echelons of society began to rub shoulders with the emerging industrial nouveau riche.

title: Seinfeldia: How a Show About Nothing Changed Everything
author: Jennifer Keishin Armstrong
description: The behind-the-scenes story of two guys who went out for coffee and dreamed up Seinfeld —the cultural sensation that changed television and bled into the real world, altering the lives of everyone it touched.

title: The Transmigration of Bodies
author: Yuri Herrera, trans. Lisa Dillman
description: A plague has brought death to the city. Two feuding crime families with blood on their hands need our hard-boiled hero, The Redeemer, to broker peace. Both his instincts and the vacant streets warn him to stay indoors, but The Redeemer ventures out into the city’s underbelly to arrange for the exchange of the bodies they hold hostage.

title: The Dream Life of Astronauts
author: Patrick Ryan
description: Nine stories, all set in and around Cape Canaveral against the backdrop of landmark events, focusing on regret and hope, relationships and family, and the universal longing for love.

title: Night of the Animals
author: Bill Broun
description: "Over the course of a single night in an authoritarian Britain in 2052, a homeless man named Cuthbert Handley sets out on an astonishing quest: to release the animals of the London Zoo."

title: Oh, Florida!: How America's Weirdest State Influences the Rest of the Country
author: Craig Pittman
description: A loving, humorous exploration of Florida's contradictions and shows how they fit together to make it the most interesting state.

title: The House by the Lake: One House, Five Families, and a Hundred Years of German History
author: Thomas Harding
description: A history Germany, told over a tumultuous century through the personal story of a small wooden house.

title: Problems
author: Jade Sharma
description: "A novel about Maya, a young woman with a smart mouth, time to kill, and a heroin hobby that isn't much fun anymore. Maya's been able to get by in New York on her wits and a dead-end bookstore job for years, but when her husband leaves her and her favorite professor ends their affair, her barely-calibrated life descends into chaos."

title: The Tyrannosaur Chronicles: The Biology of the Tyrant Dinosaurs
author: David Hone
description: A non-fiction book which tracks the rise of these dinosaurs, and presents the latest research into their biology.

title: Brightfellow
author: Rikki Ducornet
description: A feral boy comes of age on a campus decadent with starched sheets, sweating cocktails, and homemade jams.

title: Lions
author: Bonnie Nadzam
description: A portrait of a rural community in a 'living ghost town' in Colorado on the brink of collapse, and the individuals who are confronted with either chasing their dreams or—against all reason—staying where they are.

title: Listen to Me
author: Hannah Pittard
description: A psychological thriller about a forty-something couple, struggling in the wake of the wife's recent mugging, who embark on a road trip that goes badly awry.

title: Look
author: Solmaz Sharif
description: Solmaz Sharif's first book of poetry asks us to see the ongoing costs of war as the unbearable loss of human lives and also the insidious abuses against our everyday speech.

title: Lift: Fitness Culture, from Naked Greeks and Acrobats to Jazzercise and Ninja Warriors
author: Daniel Kunitz
description: A cultural history of fitness, from Greek antiquity to the era of the 'big-box gym' and beyond, exploring the ways in which human exercise and physical ideals have changed over time.

title: The End of the Perfect 10: The Making and Breaking of Gymnastics’ Top Score ?from Nadia to Now
author: Dvora Meyers
description: An account of the controversial world of gymnastics, the recent changes of the scoring system, and why those changes will drive American gymnasts to the top of the sport in the twenty-first century.

title: Let the Devil Out
author: Bill Loehfelm
description: Maureen Coughlin is a rookie beat cop in the New Orleans Police Department. She's already been suspended once, and things are about to get worse.

title: The Fishermen
author: Chigozie Obioma
description: Told by nine-year-old Benjamin, the youngest of four brothers, The Fisherman is the Cain and Abel-esque story of a childhood in Nigeria, in the small town of Akure. The brothers encounter a madman whose mystic prophecy of violence threatens the core of their close-knit family.

title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
author: Becky Chambers
description: Follow a motley crew on an exciting journey through space—and one adventurous young explorer who discovers the meaning of family in the far reaches of the universe—in this acclaimed, Hugo Award-winning space opera.

title: Jackson, 1964: And Other Dispatches from Fifty Years of Reporting on Race in America
author: Calvin Trillin
description: A career-spanning collection of articles on race and racism, from the 1960s to the present, from New Yorker Calvin Trillin.

title: Invincible Summer
author: Alice Adams
description: A debut novel following a tightknit quartet of college friends as they navigate their shifting relationships—and evolving identities—over the course of two decades.

title: We Are Not Such Things: The Murder of a Young American, a South African Township, and the Search for Truth and Reconciliation
author: Justine van der Leun
description: Justine van der Leun reopens the murder of a young American woman in South Africa, an iconic case that calls into question our understanding of truth and reconciliation, loyalty, justice, race, and class.

title: How the Post Office Created America
author: Winifred Gallagher
description: A history of a long underappreciated institution, How the Post Office Created America examines the surprising role of the postal service in our nation’s political, social, economic, and physical development.

title: The Nordic Theory of Everything
author: Anu Partanen
description: A Finnish journalist, now a naturalized American citizen, asks Americans to draw on elements of the Nordic way of life to nurture a fairer, happier, more secure, and less stressful society for themselves and their children.

title: The Bones of Grace
author: Tahmima Anam
description: "A novel about a contemporary Harvard-educated Bangladeshi woman struggling to be true to herself as well as her heritage; the completion of Anam's three-generation trilogy about Bangladesh."

title: Chronicle of a Last Summer
author: Yasmine El Rashidi
description: A debut novel set in Cairo in 1984 in which a young Egyptian woman recounts her personal and political coming of age.

title: The Innocent Have Nothing to Fear
author: Stuart Stevens
description: A dark comedy set at a contested Republican convention, written by a veteran political insider.

title: The Natural Way of Things
author: Charlotte Wood
description: A novel depicting a world where women's sexuality has become a weapon turned against them. The characters, each marked by their own public scandal, are silenced and shackled by a cruel system of corporate control and misogyny.

title: A Hundred Thousand Worlds
author: Bob Proehl
description: A novel in which an ex-actress and her son trek across America, hitting comics conventions along the way.

title: Missing, Presumed
author: Susie Steiner
description: An England-set mystery that brings to life a complex and strong-willed detective assigned to a high-risk missing persons case.

title: The Sun in Your Eyes
author: Deborah Shapiro
description: A road trip story of two women—one rich and alluring, the other just another planet in her dazzling orbit—and their fervid and troubled friendship, rekindled after years of estrangement.

title: The Long Game: How Obama Defied Washington and Redefined America’s Role in the World
author: Derek Chollet
description: An inside assessment of President Obama's foreign policy legacy from a former senior White House staffer.

title: Hillbilly Elegy: A Memoir of a Family and Culture in Crisis
author: J.D. Vance
description: A former marine and Yale Law School graduate gives an account of growing up in a poor Rust Belt town that offers a broader, probing look at the struggles of America’s white working class.

title: Rise of the Machines: A Cybernetic History
author: Thomas Rid
description: A history of our anxious embrace of technology and an examination of today’s clash of digital privacy and security.

title: Vinegar Girl
author: Anne Tyler
description: Pulitzer Prize winner Anne Tyler's contemporary take on Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew .

title: White Trash: The 400-Year Untold History of Class in America
author: Nancy Isenberg
description: A history of the class system in America, confronting our comforting myths about equality.

title: The Mandibles: A Family, 2029-2047
author: Lionel Shriver
description: In 2029, the United States is engaged in a bloodless world war that will wipe out the savings of millions of American families. An eccentric, former wealthy family must contend with the loss of their expected inheritance, but also—as the U.S. economy spirals into dysfunction—the challenge of sheer survival.

title: As Good as Gone
author: Larry Watson
description: Bill Sidey wants someone he knows well to watch his kids while his wife has surgery, and so he looks up a rank old cowboy, Calvin Sidey, who happens to be the father who virtually abandoned him when he was a boy.

title: Disappearance at Devil's Rock
author: Paul Tremblay
description: A family is shaken to its core after the mysterious disappearance of a teenage boy in this eerie tale, a blend of literary fiction, psychological suspense, and supernatural horror.

title: So Much For That Winter
author: Dorthe Nors, Trans. by Misha Hoekstra
description: A pair of novellas that playfully chart the aftermath of two very twenty-first-century romances.

title: Being a Beast: Adventures Across the Species Divide
author: Charles Foster
description: A passionate naturalist explores what it’s really like to be an animal?by living like them.

title: Bukowski in a Sundress
author: Kim Addonizio
description: A memoir in essays, Addonzizio opens up to chronicle the joys and indignities in the life of a writer wandering through middle age.

title: The After Party: Poems
author: Jana Prikryl
description: The After Party journeys across borders and eras, from cold war Central Europe to present-day New York City, from ancient Rome to New World suburbs, constantly testing the lingua francas we negotiate to know ourselves.

title: The Girls
author: Emma Cline
description: Northern California, during the violent end of the 1960s. At the start of summer, a lonely and thoughtful teenager, Evie Boyd, is drawn into a soon-to-be-infamous cult peopled by a group of free-spirited girls and their sinister but charismatic leader.

title: Barkskins
author: Annie Proulx
description: A multi-generational epic spanning three hundred years, telling the story of the descendants of two immigrant woodcutters in the Canadian wilderness.

title: In the Darkroom
author: Susan Faludi
description: A memoir from the Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist about an astonishing confrontation with the enigma of her now transgender father and the larger riddle of identity consuming our age.

title: The Course of Love
author: Alain De Botton
description: A novel that tracks the beautifully and complicated arc of a romantic partnership, from the author of On Love .

title: Sons and Daughters of Ease and Plenty
author: Ramona Ausubel
description: A novel about a wealthy New England family in the 1960s and '70s that suddenly loses its fortune—and its bearings.

title: William Tecumseh Sherman: In the Service of My Country: A Life
author: James Lee McDonough
description: A new biography of one of America’s most storied military figures.

title: Charcoal Joe: An Easy Rawlins Mystery
author: Walter Mosley
description: The latest detective Easy Rawlins mystery, set in Los Angeles in the late 1960's.

title: The Way to the Spring: Life and Death in Palestine
author: Ben Ehrenreich
description: Award-winning journalist Ben Ehrenreich brings us an immersion into the everyday struggles of Palestinian life.

title: The Strange Career of William Ellis: The Texas Slave Who Became a Mexican Millionaire
author: Karl Jacoby
description: A new story of the black experience in America through the life of a mysterious entrepreneur who adopted different racial identities.

title: I'm Thinking of Ending Things
author: Iain Reid
description: An intense literary thriller. A road trip in a snowstorm takes a sinister turn for a man and his girlfriend, the novel’s unnamed narrator.

title: Ratf**ked: The True Story Behind the Secret Plan to Steal America’s Democracy
author: David Daley
description: An account of how Republican legislators and political operatives fundamentally rigged our American democracy through redistricting.

title: I'm Just A Person
author: Tig Notaro
description: An emotionally raw account of the comedian's year of death, cancer, and epiphany.

title: Falling: A Daughter, a Father, and a Journey Back
author: Elisha Cooper
description: Elisha Cooper spends his morn­ings creating children’s books and his afternoons playing with his two daughters. But when he discovers a lump in five-year-old Zoë’s midsection as she sits on his lap at a Chicago Cubs game, everything changes.

title: Invisible Man, Got the Whole World Watching: A Young Black Man's Education
author: Mychal Denzel Smith
description: How do you learn to be a black man in America? Mychal Denzel Smith chronicles his own personal and political education during these tumultuous years, describing his efforts to come into his own in a world that denied his humanity.

title: The Crow Girl
author: Erik Axl Sund
description: Beginning in a Stockholm city park where the abused body of a young boy is discovered. Detective Superintendent Jeanette Kihlberg heads the investigation, battling an apathetic prosecutor and a bureaucratic police force unwilling to devote resources to solving the murder of an immigrant child. But with the discovery of the mutilated corpses of two more children, it becomes clear that a serial killer is at large.

title: Hot Dog Taste Test
author: Lisa Hanawalt
description: The James Beard Award-winning cartoonist and production designer/producer of Bojack Horseman muses on pop culture, relationships, and the animal in all of us.

title: A House Full of Daughters: A Memoir of Seven Generations
author: Juliet Nicholson
description: A family memoir that traces the myths, legends, and secrets of seven generations of remarkable women.

title: An Abbreviated Life
author: Ariel Leve
description: Having grown up with an eccentric mother, Leve seeks to understand the effects of chronic psychological maltreatment on a child’s developing brain, and to discover how to build a life for herself that she never dreamed possible: An unabbreviated life.

title: Under the Harrow
author: Flynn Berry
description: A psychological thriller and a haunting exploration of the fierce love between two sisters, the distortions of grief, and the terrifying power of the past.

title: Life Moves Pretty Fast: The Lessons We Learned from Eighties Movies
author: Hadley Freeman
description: From Vogue contributor and Guardian columnist Hadley Freeman, a personalized guide to eighties movies that describes why they changed movie-making forever—featuring exclusive interviews with the producers, directors, writers and stars of the best cult classics.

title: Spiral: Trapped in the Forever War
author: Mark Danner
description: A somber examination of why the war on terror has stretched over 15 years and appears to have no end in sight.

title: Stories of Your Life and Others
author: Ted Chiang
description: The first short story collection from multiple award-winning science fiction writer Ted Chiang.

title: End of Watch
author: Stephen King
description: A supernatural detective thriller, the final part of Stephen King's Bill Hodges trilogy.

title: Goodnight, Beautiful Women
author: Anna Noyes
description: Moving along the Maine Coast and beyond, the interconnected stories in Goodnight, Beautiful Women bring us into the sultry, mysterious inner lives of New England women and girls as they navigate the dangers and struggles of their outer worlds.

title: Grief Is the Thing with Feathers
author: Max Porter
description: Part novella, part polyphonic fable, part essay on grief, Grief is the Thing With Feathers focuses on a poetry scholar, adrift after his wife's sudden death, who, together with his two sons, is visited by a crow that acts as an aide to their emotional recovery.

title: Homegoing
author: Yaa Gyasi
description: Beginning with the story of two half-sisters, separated by forces beyond their control: one sold into slavery, the other married to a British slaver, Homegoing traces the generations of family who follow, as their destinies lead them through two continents and three hundred years of history.

title: Grunt: The Curious Science of Humans at War
author: Mary Roach
description: Grunt tackles the science behind some of a soldier's most challenging adversaries?panic, exhaustion, heat, noise?and introduces us to the scientists who seek to conquer them.

title: Never a Dull Moment: 1971 The Year That Rock Exploded
author: David Hepworth
description: A look at 1971, rock’s golden year, the year that saw the release of the indelible recordings of Led Zeppelin, David Bowie, the Who, Rod Stewart, Carole King, the Rolling Stones, and others and produced more classics than any other year in rock history.

title: Magic and Loss: The Internet as Art
author: Virginia Heffernan
description: Virginia Heffernan reveals the logic and aesthetics behind the Internet.

title: Diane Arbus: Portrait of a Photographer
author: Arthur Lubow
description: A biography of the controversial photographer Diane Arbus, linking her extraordinary life to her iconic photographs.

title: The Hatred of Poetry
author: Ben Lerner
description: An essay in which Lerner takes the hatred of poetry as the starting point of his defense of the art.

title: They May Not Mean To, But They Do
author: Cathleen Schine
description: A comic novel about how a close New York–based family copes with aging and death.

title: Kingdoms in the Air: Dispatches from the Far Away
author: Bob Shacochis
description: Brings together the very best of Shacochis’s culture and travel essays in one collection that spans his global adventures and his life passions.

title: Sex Object
author: Jessica Valenti
description: A new memoir from the Guardian columnist and 'professional feminist,' exploring the toll everyday sexism takes on women's lives.

title: Everybody Behaves Badly: The True Story Behind Hemingway’s Masterpiece The Sun Also Rises
author: Lesley M. M. Blume
description: The making of Ernest Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises , the outsize personalities who inspired it, and the vast changes it wrought on the literary world.

title: I Almost Forgot About You
author: Terry McMillan
description: From the author of How Stella Got Her Groove Back and Waiting to Exhale , the story of a woman who shakes things up in her life to find greater meaning.

title: Ordinarily Well: The Case for Antidepressants
author: Peter D. Kramer
description: The celebrated psychiatrist and author Peter D. Kramer examines the growing controversy about the popular medications.

title: Hogs Wild: Selected Reporting Pieces
author: Ian Frazier
description: The veteran humorist and reporter for the New Yorker presents a collection of pieces that record his pursuits of wild hogs, hermit crabs, Asian carp, a Styrofoam substitute, and more.

title: Everything Explained That Is Explainable: On the Creation of the Encyclopaedia Britannica's Celebrated Eleventh Edition, 1910-1911
author: Denis Boyles
description: The story of how grit and determination created an encyclopedia for the modern world.

title: The Burger Court and the Rise of the Judicial Right
author: Michael J. Graetz & Linda Greenhouse
description: A fresh look at the Warren Burger Supreme Court finds that it was not a 'moderate' or transitional court, as often portrayed, but a conservative one that still defines the constitutional landscape we live in today.

title: Melville in Love: The Secret Life of Herman Melville and the Muse of Moby-Dick
author: Michael Shelden
description: A books arguing that the anarchic spirit animating Melville’s canonical work was inspired by his great love affair with a shockingly unconventional married woman.

title: But What If We're Wrong?
author: Chuck Klosterman
description: An inquiry into why we’ll probably be wrong about almost everything, built on a series on interviews with a variety of creative thinkers.

title: The Invention of Russia: From Gorbachev's Freedom to Putin's War
author: Arkady Ostrovsky
description: A look at how the control of the media has helped plot the Russian political trajectory from dictatorship and back again.

title: Wintering
author: Peter Geye
description: "The two principal stories at play in Wintering are bound together when the elderly, demented Harry Eide escapes his sickbed and vanishes into the forbidding, northernmost wilderness that surrounds the town of Gunflint, Minnesota—instantly changing the Eide family, and many other lives, forever."

title: The Latter Days
author: Judith Freeman
description: A memoir about the path the author took—sometimes unwittingly—out of her Mormon upbringing and through a thicket of profound difficulties to become a writer.

title: Among Strange Victims
author: Daniel Saldaña París, Trans. by Christina MacSweeney
description: Rodrigo likes his vacant lot, its resident chicken, and being left alone. But when passivity finds him accidentally married to Cecilia, he trades Mexico City for the sun-bleached desolation of his hometown and domestic life with Cecilia for the debauched company of a poet, a philosopher, and Micaela, whose allure includes the promise of time travel.

title: Lily and the Octopus
author: Steven Rowley
description: A magical realist novel about a neurotic man and his devotion to his beloved, cancer-stricken dachshund.

title: Ink & Bone
author: Lisa Unger
description: A paranormal thriller in which a young woman's mysterious gift forces her into the middle of a dangerous investigation of a little girl's disappearance.

title: The Pivot: The Future of American Stagecraft in Asia
author: Kurt Campbell
description: An analysis and explanation of the new major shift in American foreign policy, its interests and assets, to Asia by one of it's principal architects.

title: Coyote America: A Natural and Supernatural History
author: Dan Flores
description: An environmental and deep natural history of the coyote.

title: Super Extra Grande
author: Yoss
description: A light-hearted space opera of intergalactic proportions from celebrated and controversial Cuban Sci-Fi author Yoss.

title: What We Become
author: Arturo Pérez-Reverte
description: Arturo Pérez-Reverte's novel of fate, love, and deception spans four decades as two beautiful misfits struggle to make a real human connection despite the violent politics of the Spanish Civil War and then the Cold War.

title: Before the Fall
author: Noah Hawley
description: On a foggy summer night, eleven people--ten privileged, one down-on-his-luck painter--depart Martha's Vineyard on a private jet headed for New York. Sixteen minutes later, the unthinkable happens: the plane plunges into the ocean. The only survivors are Scott Burroughs--the painter--and a four-year-old boy, who is now the last remaining member of an immensely wealthy and powerful media mogul's family.

title: Modern Lovers
author: Emma Straub
description: A novel set in modern day Brooklyn. Friends and former college bandmates Elizabeth and Andrew and Zoe have watched one another marry, buy real estate, and start businesses and families, all while trying to hold on to the identities of their youth. But nothing ages them like having to suddenly pass the torch to their own offspring.

title: The View from the Cheap Seats
author: Neil Gaiman
description: A collection of nonfiction essays by Neil Gaiman on a myriad of topics—from art and artists to dreams, myths, and memories.

title: A Hero of France
author: Alan Furst
description: A Resistance leader in Nazi-occupied France attempts to keep his lines of escape open in this lyrical spy novel.

title: The Hour of Land: A Personal Topography of America's National Parks
author: Terry Tempest Williams
description: A meditation and a manifesto on why wild lands matter to the soul of America, told through memoir, diaries, letters, poetry, and reporting.

title: Witness to the Revolution: Radicals, Resisters, Vets, Hippies, and the Year America Lost Its Mind and Found Its Soul
author: Clara Bingham
description: An account of the turbulent year when the sixties ended and America teetered on the edge of revolution.

title: Voyager: Travel Writings
author: Russell Banks
description: The award-winning novelist takes us on some of his most memorable journeys in this collection of travel essays that spans the globe, from the Caribbean to Scotland to the Himalayas.

title: The Reactive
author: Masande Ntshanga
description: "A novel about Lindanathi, a young HIV+ man grappling with the death of his brother, for which he feels unduly responsible. He and his friends—Cecelia and Ruan—work low-paying jobs and sell anti-retroviral drugs. In between, they huff glue, drift through parties, and traverse the streets of Cape Town where they observe the grave material disparities of their country."

title: Do Not Say We Have Nothing
author: Madeleine Thien
description: A novel about the lives of an extended family in China, before, during and after the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989.

title: The Last Samurai
author: Helen DeWitt
description: DeWitt assembles everything from letters of the Greek alphabet to Fourier analysis to tell the tale of a boy prodigy, stuffed with knowledge beyond his years but frustrated by his mother’s refusal to identify his father.

title: The City of Mirrors
author: Justin Cronin
description: The final book in Justin Cronin's epic, post-apocalyptic trilogy about the survivors of a virus that has created a race of deadly vampiric creatures.

title: Tribe: On Homecoming and Belonging
author: Sebastian Junger
description: Combining history, psychology, and anthropology, Tribe explores what we can learn from tribal societies about loyalty, belonging, and the eternal human quest for meaning."

title: Smoke
author: Dan Vyleta
description: A blend of historical fiction and fantasy, as three young friends scratch the surface of the grown-up world to discover startling wonders—and dangerous secrets.

title: Sweetbitter
author: Stephanie Danler
description: Twenty-two, and knowing no one, Tess leaves home to begin her adult life in New York City. Thus begins a year that is both enchanting and punishing, in a low-level job at 'the best restaurant in New York City.'

title: Jane Doe January
author: Emily Winslow
description: A real-life crime mystery and memoir of the cold case prosecution of a serial rapist, told by one of his victims.

title: Enchanted Islands
author: Allison Amend
description: The story of an independent American woman whose path takes her far from her native Minnesota when she and her husband, an undercover intelligence officer, are sent to the Galápagos Islands at the brink of World War II.

title: Free Speech: Ten Principles for a Connected World
author: Timothy Garton Ash
description: A manifesto for global free speech in the digital age.

title: The Mirror Test: America at War in Iraq and Afghanistan
author: J. Kael Weston
description: J. Kael Weston spent seven years on the ground in Iraq and Afghanistan working for the U.S. State Department in some of the most dangerous frontline locations. Upon his return home, while traveling the country to pay respect to the dead and wounded, he asked himself: When will these wars end? How will they be remembered and memorialized? What lessons can we learn from them?

title: The Fractured Republic: Renewing America’s Social Contract in the Age of Individualism
author: Yuval Levin
description: A book arguing that the politics of nostalgia is failing twenty-first-century Americans.

title: Secondhand Time: The Last of the Soviets
author: Svetlana Alexievich, Trans. by Bela Shayevich
description: In Secondhand Time , 2015 Nobel Prize winner, Svetlana Alexievich chronicles the demise of communism. Everyday Russian citizens recount the past thirty years, showing us what life was like during the fall of the Soviet Union and what it’s like to live in the new Russia left in its wake. Through interviews spanning 1991 to 2012, Alexievich takes us behind the propaganda and contrived media accounts, giving us a panoramic portrait of contemporary Russia and Russians who still carry memories of oppression, terror, famine, massacres—but also of pride in their country, hope for the future, and a belief that everyone was working and fighting together to bring about a utopia. Here is an account of life in the aftermath of an idea so powerful it once dominated a third of the world.

title: The Fireman
author: Joe Hill
description: A novel about worldwide pandemic of spontaneous combustion that threatens to reduce civilization to ashes and a band of improbable heroes who battle to save it, led by one powerful and enigmatic man known as the Fireman.

title: Joe Gould's Teeth
author: Jill Lepore
description: From New Yorker staff writer and Harvard historian Jill Lepore, the dark tale of her restless search for the long-lost, longest book ever written, a century-old manuscript called 'The Oral History of Our Time.'

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description: From the Pulitzer Prize-winning author of The Emperor of All Maladies —a history of the gene and a response to the defining question of the future: What becomes of being human when we learn to 'read' and 'write' our own genetic information?

title: Labor of Love: The Invention of Dating
author: Moira Weigel
description: Weigel examines the history and current practices of dating in hopes of making sense of her own feelings of discomfort and oppression.

title: The Politicians and the Egalitarians: The Hidden History of American Politics
author: Sean Wilentz
description: A book about the commanding role party politics has played in America’s enduring struggle against economic inequality.

title: The Second Life of Nick Mason
author: Steve Hamilton
description: Nick Mason has already spent five years inside a maximum security prison when an offer comes that will grant his release twenty years early. He accepts -- but the deal comes with a terrible price.

title: The Boys in the Bunkhouse: Servitude and Salvation in the Heartland
author: Dan Barry
description: The harrowing story of the exploitation and abuse of a resilient group of men with intellectual disability, and the heroic efforts of those who helped them to find justice and reclaim their lives.

title: A Country Road, A Tree
author: Jo Baker
description: The experiences of a struggling Irish writer in France during World War II—joining the Resistance, fleeing the Gestapo, risking everything again after escaping to the free zone—will help shape his groundbreaking literary future, suggests this novel based on the life of Samuel Beckett.

title: The After Party
author: Anton DiSclafani
description: A novel about the world of 1950s Texas socialites and the one irresistible, controversial woman at the bright, hot center of it all.

title: Porcelain: A Memoir
author: Moby
description: A memoir from the musician Moby focusing on his path from suburban poverty and alienation to a life of beauty, squalor and unlikely success out of the NYC club scene of the late '80s and '90s.

title: Collected Poems: 1974-2004
author: Rita Dove
description: The collected poems of Pulitzer Prize winner Rita Dove.

title: Nitro Mountain
author: Lee Clay Johnson
description: Set in a bitterly benighted, mine-polluted corner of Virginia, Nitro Mountain follows a group of people bound together by alcohol, small-time crime and music.

title: 32 Yolks: From My Mother's Table to Working the Line
author: Eric Ripert and Veronica Chambers
description: The acclaimed French chef and co-owner of Le Bernardin delivers an account of his life in France and Andorra before he moved to the United States in his early 20s.

title: Anatomy of a Soldier
author: Harry Parker
description: This debut novel by a British combat veteran chronicles a soldier’s maiming and recovery.

title: The Bitter Taste of Victory: Life, Love, and Art in the Ruins of the Reich
author: Lara Feigel
description: A cultural study exploring the ways artists forged a sense of redemption—both personal and societal—from the devastation of post–World War II Germany.

title: Girls on Fire
author: Robin Wasserman
description: A portrait of the intoxication of female friendship, set against the unsettled backdrop of a town gripped by moral panic.

title: Your Favorite Band Is Killing Me
author: Steven Hyden
description: Beatles vs. Stones. Biggie vs. Tupac. Kanye vs. Taylor. Who do you choose? And what does that say about you? Actually--what do these endlessly argued-about pop music rivalries say about us?

title: Swallowed by the Cold
author: Jensen Beach
description: A story collection are set in a Swedish village on the Baltic Sea as well as in Stockholm over the course of two eventful years.

title: Shrill: Notes from a Loud Woman
author: Lindy West
description: Coming of age in a culture that demands women be as small, quiet, and compliant as possible—like a porcelain dove that will also have sex with you—writer and humorist Lindy West quickly discovered that she was anything but.

title: Little Labors
author: Rivka Galchen
description: A compendium of observations, stories, lists, and brief essays about babies and literature.

title: Blood, Bone, and Marrow: A Biography of Harry Crews
author: Ted Geltner
description: The first full-length biography of one of the most unlikely figures in twentieth-century American literature.

title: The Noise of Time
author: Julian Barnes
description: A fictional treatment of the Russian composer Dmitri Shostakovich and his long history of humiliation and persecution under Soviet rule.

title: Valiant Ambition: George Washington, Benedict Arnold, and the Fate of the American Revolution
author: Nathaniel Philbrick
description: A surprising account of the middle years of the American Revolution, and the tragic relationship between George Washington and Benedict Arnold.

title: The Limousine Liberal: How an Incendiary Image United the Right and Fractured America
author: Steve Fraser
description: The story of one of the longest-lasting negative metaphors in America politics: the limousine liberal.

title: LaRose
author: Louise Erdrich
description: After accidentally shooting his friend and neighbor’s young son, a man on a Native American reservation subscribes to 'an old form of justice' by giving his own son, LaRose, to the parents of his victim.

title: The Fox Was Ever the Hunter
author: Herta Müller, Trans. by Peter Boehm
description: An atmospheric, lyrical novel from Nobel Prize–winning writer Müller of life in Romania during the closing days of the Ceausescu dictatorship.

title: The Loney
author: Andrew Michael Hurley
description: When the remains of a young child are discovered during a winter storm on a stretch of the bleak Lancashire coastline known as the Loney, a man named Smith is forced to confront the terrifying and mysterious events that occurred forty years earlier when he visited the place as a boy.

title: The Sun & The Moon & The Rolling Stones
author: Rich Cohen
description: A panoramic narrative history of the Rolling Stones, viewed through the lens of the Vanity Fair contributor who was along for the ride as a young reporter on the road with the band in the 1990s.

title: The Nazi Hunters
author: Andrew Nagorski
description: A detailed look at the grim work of tracking Nazis over the decades since World War II.

title: The Secret War: Spies, Ciphers, and Guerrillas, 1939-1945
author: Max Hastings
description: An examination of one of the most important yet underexplored aspects of World War II—intelligence—showing how espionage successes and failures by the United States, Britain, Russia, Germany, and Japan influenced the course of the war and its final outcome.

title: The Mirror Thief
author: Martin Seay
description: An epic, genre-bending debut set across three cities in three time different periods, reminiscent of David Mitchell's Cloud Atlas .

title: The Pier Falls
author: Mark Haddon
description: A collection of nine dark stories from the author of The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time .

title: First Dads: Parenting and Politics from George Washington to Barack Obama
author: Joshua Kendall
description: Parenting and politics from George Washington to Barack Obama.

title: Everything is Teeth
author: Evie Wyld & Joe Sumner
description: A graphic memoir about family, love, loss, and the irresistible forces that, like sharks, course through life unseen, ready to emerge at any moment.

title: Pit Bull: The Battle over an American Icon
author: Bronwen Dickey
description: The story of how a popular breed of dog became the most demonized and supposedly the most dangerous of dogs—and what role humans have played in the transformation.

title: String Theory: David Foster Wallace on Tennis
author: David Foster Wallace
