description: David Foster Wallace's collected writings on tennis.

title: You May Also Like: Taste in an Age of Endless Choice
author: Tom Vanderbilt
description: A book about what shapes our preferences and opinions. Vanderbilt stalks the elusive beast of taste, probing research in psychology, marketing, and neuroscience to answer myriad complex and fascinating questions.

title: Paper: Paging Through History
author: Mark Kurlansky
description: A definitive history of paper and the astonishing ways it has shaped today’s world.

title: Boy, Erased
author: Garrard Conley
description: When Garrard Conley was a nineteen-year-old college student, he was outed to his parents, and was forced to make a life-changing decision: either agree to attend a church-supported conversion therapy program that promised to 'cure' him of homosexuality; or risk losing family, friends, and the God he had prayed to every day of his life.

title: Everyone Brave is Forgiven
author: Chris Cleave
description: A wartime love story inspired by the real-life love letters between Chris Cleave’s grandparents during WWII.

title: Sweet Lamb of Heaven
author: Lydia Millet
description: Blending domestic thriller and psychological horror, this first-person novel follows a mother fleeing her estranged husband.

title: White Sands: Experiences From the Outside World
author: Geoff Dyer
description: The award-winning critic and novelist details his travels in such far-flung places as Tahiti and the Arctic Circle.

title: Pumpkinflowers: A Soldier's Story
author: Matti Friedman
description: A former soldier's account of youthful Israelis maturing, fighting, and dying at a forgotten Lebanon outpost.

title: Zero K
author: Don DeLillo
description: A cryogenic facility beyond the edges of civilization provokes a series of meditations on death and life in this new novel by Don DeLillo.

title: Imagine Me Gone
author: Adam Haslett
description: When Margaret's fiancé, John, is hospitalized for depression in 1960s London, she faces a choice: carry on with their plans despite what she now knows of his condition, or back away from the suffering it may bring her. She decides to marry him. Imagine Me Gone follows the fallout of this decision for Michael, their eldest son, as well as the family that must care for him.

title: Paul McCartney: The Life
author: Philip Norman
description: A biography of the former Beatle and music legend.

title: Grit: The Power and Passion of Perserverance
author: Angela Duckworth
description: Psychologist Angela Duckworth shows anyone striving to succeed—be it parents, students, educators, athletes, or business people—that the secret to outstanding achievement is not talent but a special blend of passion and persistence she calls 'grit.'

title: Heat & Light
author: Jennifer Haigh
description: A sprawling, thickly populated novel about fracking set in a small Pennsylvania town both blessed and cursed by its natural resources.

title: The Sport of Kings
author: C.E. Morgan
description: A novel about a Kentucky horse-breeding family that is both a meditation on race and a bitter inversion of the American dream.

title: The Bricks That Built the Houses
author: Kate Tempest
description: Becky, Harry, and Leon are leaving London in a fourth-hand Ford with a suitcase full of stolen money, in a mess of tangled loyalties and impulses. But can they truly leave the city that's in their bones?

title: Then Come Back: The Lost Neruda Poems
author: Pablo Neruda, Trans. Forrest Gander
description: A collection of lost poems, recently discovered in Neruda's archive.

title: We Were Feminists Once: From Riot Grrrl to CoverGirl®, the Buying and Selling of a Political Movement
author: Andi Zeisler
description: A biting history of how feminism has been co-opted, watered down, and turned into a gyratory media trend.

title: Eleven Hours
author: Pamela Erens
description: An intimate exploration of the physical and mental challenges of childbirth.

title: The Veins of the Ocean
author: Patricia Engel
description: After her older brother Carlito kills his girlfriend Isabela's baby girl because he thinks Isabela is cheating on him, 23-year-old Reina feels trapped trying to comfort him on death row—until his death frees her to start over in Crescent Key, a place where nobody knows her family history.

title: Everybody's Fool
author: Richard Russo
description: A sequel to Russo's Nobody’s Fool checks in on the residents of poor old North Bath, New York, 10 years later.

title: The Romanovs: 1613–1918
author: Simon Sebag Montefiore
description: The Romanovs were the most successful dynasty of modern times, ruling a sixth of the world’s surface for three centuries. How did one family turn a war-ruined principality into the world’s greatest empire? And how did they lose it all?

title: The Morning They Came For Us: Dispatches from Syria
author: Janine di Giovanni
description: Drawing from years of experience covering Syria for Vanity Fair , Newsweek , and the New York Times , award-winning journalist Janine di Giovanni gives us a collection of reports from the war-torn country, all told through the perspective of ordinary people?among them a doctor, a nun, a musician, and a student.

title: Missing Man: The American Spy Who Vanished in Iran
author: Barry Meier
description: The unsettling true story of Bob Levinson, a private investigator and former FBI agent gone missing in Iran.

title: Wilde Lake
author: Laura Lippman
description: A thriller tracing a family’s journey from raucous Baltimore to the meticulously planned community of Columbia, Maryland.

title: Amateurs
author: Dylan Hicks
description: A modern comedy of manners. Archer is a semi-celebrated novelist and sex-toy heir. His best friend, John, is as earnest as Archer is feckless. John’s girlfriend, Sara, envies Archer’s writing career. And Sara’s roommate, Lucas, wishes he’d never lost his girlfriend to the man.

title: The Cultural Revolution: A People's History, 1962-1976
author: Frank Dikotter
description: A people's history of the Cultural Revolution in China, drawing for the first time on hundreds of previously classified party documents, from secret police reports to unexpurgated versions of leadership speeches.

title: Inherited Disorders
author: Adam Ehrlich Sachs
description: A son receives an inheritance from his father and tries to dispose of it before it destroys him. Inherited Disorders tells this elemental story in over 100 variations.

title: The Winter Fortress: The Epic Mission to Sabotage Hitler's Atomic Bomb
author: Neal Bascomb
description: The true adventure and spy story about the greatest act of sabotage in all of World War II.

title: Beer Money: A Memoir of Privilege and Loss
author: Frances Stroh
description: A memoir of a city, an industry, and a dynasty in decline, and the story of a young artist’s struggle to find her way out of the ruins.

title: The Doll-Master and Other Tales of Terror
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: A collection of six haunting tales from Joyce Carol Oates.

title: Pinpoint: How GPS Is Changing Technology, Culture, and Our Minds
author: Greg Milner
description: The story of GPS, a scientific marvel that enables almost all modern technology?but is changing us in profound ways.

title: Track Changes: A Literary History of Word Processing
author: Matthew G. Kirschenbaum
description: A book examining how the interests and ideals of creative authorship came to coexist with the computer revolution. Who were the first adopters? What kind of anxieties did they share? Was word processing perceived as just a better typewriter or something more? How did it change our understanding of writing?

title: Old Age: A Beginner's Guide
author: Michael Kinsley
description: In this series of essays, Michael Kinsley uses his own battle with Parkinson’s disease to unearth answers to questions we are all at some time forced to confront.

title: City of Secrets
author: Stewart O'Nan
description: A moral thriller of the Jewish underground resistance in Jerusalem after the Second World War.

title: Ladivine
author: Marie NDiaye, Trans. by Jordan Stump
description: A psychological tale of a trauma that ensnares three generations of french women.

title: A Rage for Order: The Middle East in Turmoil, from Tahrir Square to ISIS
author: Robert F. Worth
description: A Rage for Order tracks the tormented legacy of what was once called the Arab Spring.

title: Her Again: Becoming Meryl Streep
author: Michael Schulman
description: A biography of Meryl Streep that explores her beginnings as a young woman of the 1970s grappling with love, feminism, and her astonishing talent.

title: Sex with Shakespeare
author: Jillian Keenan
description: A kinky, comic memoir about Shakespeare, love, obsession, and spanking.

title: Barbra Streisand: Redefining Beauty, Femininity, and Power
author: Neal Gabler
description: In the latest in the Jewish Lives series, an experienced biographer delves into Barbra Streisand's psyche.

title: Players: The Story of Sports and Money, and the Visionaries Who Fought to Create a Revolution
author: Matthew Futterman
description: The story of the people who transformed sports, in the span of a single generation, from a job that required top athletes to work in the off-season to make ends meet into a massive global business.

title: One of Us: The Story of Anders Breivik and the Massacre in Norway
author: Asne Seierstad
description: The story of Anders Breivik and the massacre on Utoya island in Norway.

title: In Gratitude
author: Jenny Diski
description: Upon being diagnosed with terminal cancer, Jenny Diski decided to write about being taken in at age fifteen by the author Doris Lessing, and the subsequent fifty years of their complex relationship.

title: The Excellent Lombards
author: Jane Hamilton
description: The tender story of a Wisconsin girl's reluctant coming of age amid the sprawling family that maintains their apple orchard.

title: The Gunning of America: Business and the Making of American Gun Culture
author: Pamela Haag
description: An examination of the controversial realm of American gun culture through the perspective of gun manufacturers, with an emphasis on the Winchester Repeating Arms Company.

title: Eligible: A modern retelling of Pride and Prejudice
author: Curtis Sittenfeld
description: A modern retelling of Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice set in New York City, focusing on Liz, a magazine writer in her late 30s.

title: Mothering Sunday
author: Graham Swift
description: In England of 1924, a maid who knows her affair with an estate owner’s son must end moves through that last day.

title: My Struggle: Book Five
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard
description: The fifth book of Knausgaard's My Struggle series. As a nineteen-year-old, Karl Ove moves to Bergen and invests all of himself in his writing. But his efforts get the opposite effect - he wants it so much that he gets writer's block.

title: Ghetto: The Invention of a Place, The History of an Idea
author: Mitchell Duneier
description: Duneier traces the idea of the ghetto from its beginnings in the sixteenth century and its revival by the Nazis to the present.

title: Maestra
author: L.S. Hilton
description: A thriller about a woman with exotic sexual appetites and a penchant for murdering those who cross her.

title: Hystopia
author: David Means
description: At the bitter end of the 1960s, after surviving multiple assassination attempts, President John F. Kennedy is entering his third term in office. The Vietnam War rages on, and the president has created a vast federal agency, the Psych Corps, dedicated to maintaining the nation’s mental hygiene by any means necessary. This destabilized version of American history is the vision of twenty-two-year old Eugene Allen, who has returned from Vietnam to write the book-within-a-book at the center of Hystopia .

title: Far and Away: Reporting from the Brink of Change
author: Andrew Solomon
description: Far and Away collects National Book Award winner Andrew Solomon’s writings about places undergoing seismic shifts—political, cultural, and spiritual.

title: Panic at the Pump: The Energy Crisis and the Transformation of American Politics in the 1970s
author: Meg Jacobs
description: A history of the energy crises of the 1970s and the world they wrought.

title: The Dig
author: John Preston
description: The strange story of a priceless treasure discovered in East Anglia on the eve of World War II.

title: Before the Wind
author: Jim Lynch
description: A cautionary tale of the costs of obsession, focusing three generations whose devotion to sailing holds them together and tears them apart.

title: Hard Light: A Cass Neary Crime Novel
author: Elizabeth Hand
description: Strobe-lit against an apocalyptic background of rock and roll, rave culture, fast drugs and transgressive photography, Hard Light continues the breathless saga of Cassandra Neary.

title: My Struggle: Book 4
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard, trans. by Don Bartlett
description: My Struggle: Book 4 finds an eighteen-year-old Karl Ove Knausgaard in a tiny fishing village in northern Norway, where he has been hired as a schoolteacher and is living on his own for the first time. When the ferocious winter takes hold, Karl Ove--in the company of the Håfjord locals--confronts private demons, reels from humiliations, and is elated by small victories.

title: "Most Blessed of the Patriarchs": Thomas Jefferson and the Empire of the Imagination
author: Annette Gordon Reed and Peter S. Onuf
description: A work of history that explicates Thomas Jefferson’s vision of himself, the American Revolution, Christianity, slavery, and race.

title: The Vanishing Velázquez: A 19th Century Bookseller's Obsession with a Lost Masterpiece
author: Laura Cumming
description: The true story—part art history and part mystery—of a Velázquez portrait that went missing and the obsessed nineteenth-century bookseller determined to prove he had found it.

title: The Other Slavery: The Uncovered Story of Indian Enslavement in America
author: Andrés Reséndez
description: The sweeping story of the enslavement of tens of thousands of Indians across America, from the time of the conquistadors up to the early 20th century.

title: The Bad-Ass Librarians of Timbuktu: And Their Race to Save the World's Most Precious Manuscripts
author: Joshua Hammer
description: To save precious centuries-old Arabic texts from Al Qaeda, a band of librarians in Timbuktu pulls off a brazen heist worthy of Ocean’s Eleven .

title: Raymie Nightingale
author: Kate DiCamillo
description: A YA novel about ten-year-old Raymie Clarke of Lister, Florida, who has a plan to get her father to come back home after he runs off with a dental hygienist.

title: The Lost Book of Moses: The Hunt for the World's Oldest Bible
author: Chanan Tigay
description: An account of one man's quest to find the oldest Bible in the world and solve the riddle of the brilliant, doomed antiquities dealer accused of forging it.

title: Daredevils
author: Shawn Vestal
description: A novel set in Arizona in the mid 1970s about Loretta, a teenager married off as a 'sister wife,' who makes a break for freedom.

title: The Regional Office is Under Attack!
author: Manuel Gonzalez
description: In a world beset by amassing forces of darkness, one organization—the Regional Office—and its coterie of super-powered female assassins protects the globe from annihilation. Then a prophecy suggests that someone from inside might bring about its downfall.

title: Mary Wept Over the Feet of Jesus
author: Chester Brown
description: The retelling in comics form of nine biblical stories that present Chester Brown's startling thesis about biblical representations of prostitution.

title: Alibaba: The House That Jack Ma Built
author: Duncan Clark
description: An insider’s account of how a teacher built one of the world’s most valuable companies—rivaling Walmart & Amazon—and reshaped the global economy.

title: Hamilton: The Revolution
author: Jeremy McCarter and Lin-Manuel Miranda
description: A behind the scenes look at the inspiration behind, and the making of, the musical Hamilton .

title: One in a Billion: The Story of Nic Volker and the Dawn of Genomic Medicine
author: Mark Johnson & Kathleen Gallagher
description: The story of a young boy with a never-before-seen disease, and the doctors who take a bold step into the future of medicine to save him—based on the authors’ Pulitzer Prize–winning reporting.

title: Stamped from the Beginning: The Definitive History of Racist Ideas in America
author: Ibram X. Kendi
description: The National Book Award-winning history of how racist ideas were created, spread, and deeply rooted in American society.

title: Orson Welles, Volume 3: One-Man Band
author: Simon Callow
description: The third volume of Simon Callow’s Orson Welles biography, covering the period of his exile from America (1947–1964), when he produced some of his greatest works, including Touch of Evil .

title: Disrupted: My Misadventure in the Start-Up Bubble
author: Dan Lyons
description: An inside-out look at the frenzied and at times surreal work environment of tech startup HubSpot.

title: Bucky F*cking Dent
author: David Duchovny
description: A frustrated young writer discovers a surprising redemption when he moves back in with his dying father, an obsessive Boston Red Sox fan.

title: All Tomorrow's Parties
author: Rob Spillman
description: A memoir by the Tin House magazine co-founding editor about growing up in West Berlin then returning as an adult to post–Soviet-era East Berlin to find artistic purpose.

title: Septimania
author: Jonathan Levi
description: A failed Ph.D. candidate, expelled from Cambridge’s Trinity College, learns he’s king of Septimania, the land given to the Jews of eighth-century France by Charlemagne.

title: Tuesday Nights in 1980
author: Molly Prentiss
description: A novel which follows a critic, an artist, and a desirous, determined young woman as they find their way—and ultimately collide—amid the ever-evolving New York City art scene of the 1980s.

title: Exposure
author: Helen Dunmore
description: A Cold War spy thriller and forbidden love story set in London in 1960.

title: The Red Parts: Autobiography of a Trial
author: Maggie Nelson
description: A memoir, an account of a murder trial, and an essay that interrogates the American obsession with violence and missing white women, exploring the nature of grief, justice, and empathy.

title: True Crimes: A Family Album
author: Kathryn Harrison
description: A collection of essays about the things we don’t always discuss, casting light on what lurks beneath the surface of everyday life, sifting through the artifacts of memory to find what haunts and endures.

title: Our Young Man
author: Edmund White
description: Our Young Man follows the life of a gorgeous Frenchman, Guy, as he goes from the industrial city of Clermont-Ferrand to the top of the modeling profession in New York City's fashion world, becoming the darling of Fire Island's gay community.

title: The Arm: Inside the Billion-Dollar Mystery of the Most Valuable Commodity in Sports
author: Jeff Passan
description: An exploration of baseball’s most valuable commodity and the redemption that can be found in one fragile and mysterious limb.

title: Now and Again
author: Charlotte Rogan
description: An Oklahoma-set tale about a number of characters impacted by America’s military-industrial juggernaut.

title: Prisoners of Hope: Lyndon B. Johnson, the Great Society, and the Limits of Liberalism
author: Randall B. Woods
description: A cautionary tale about the unintended consequences of even well-intentioned policy, Prisoners of Hope offers a portrait of LBJ and America’s most ambitious—and controversial—domestic policy agenda since the New Deal.

title: A Burglar's Guide to the City
author: Geoff Managh
description: Encompassing nearly 2,000 years of heists and tunnel jobs, break-ins and escapes, A Burglar's Guide to the City offers a blueprint to the criminal possibilities in the world all around us.

title: Pretentiousness: Why It Matters
author: Dan Fox
description: A short book that aims to put a positive spin on a term of almost universal disparagement.

title: Catastrophic Happiness: Finding Joy in Childhood's Messy Years
author: Catherine Newman
description: A comic memoir about childhood's second act from Real Simple journalist Catherine Newman.

title: Louisa: The Extraordinary Life of Mrs. Adams
author: Louisa Thomas
description: An intimate portrait of Louisa Catherine Adams, the wife of John Quincy Adams, who witnessed firsthand the greatest transformations of her time.

title: The Long Shadow of Small Ghosts: Murder and Memory in an American City
author: Laura Tillman
description: A harrowing investigation of the causes, effects, and communal toll of a deeply troubling crime—the brutal murder of three young children by their parents in the border city of Brownsville, Texas.

title: Kill 'Em and Leave: My Search for the Real James Brown
author: James McBride
description: National Book Award winner James McBride goes in search of the 'real' James Brown after receiving a tip that promises to uncover the man behind the myth.

title: Thomas Jefferson Dreams of Sally Hemings
author: Stephen O'Connor
description: A debut novel about Thomas Jefferson and Sally Hemings, in whose story the conflict between the American ideal of equality and the realities of slavery and racism played out in the most tragic of terms.

title: Consequence
author: Eric Fair
description: A candid and unsettling account of the author’s work as a government contractor in Iraq charged with interrogating detainees in Baghdad, Fallujah, and Abu Ghraib.

title: The Whole Harmonium
author: Paul Mariani
description: A biography of one the most important American poets of the twentieth century—Wallace Stevens—as seen through his lifelong quest to find and describe the sublime in the human experience.

title: Alice and Oliver
author: Charles Bock
description: An unflinching portrait of a young family’s journey through a medical crisis, laying bare a couple’s love and fears as they fight for everything that’s important to them.

title: America's War for the Greater Middle East
author: Andrew J. Bacevich
description: A reassessment of U.S. military policy in the Middle East over the past four decades from retired army colonel Andrew J. Bacevich.

title: The Last Painting of Sara De Vos
author: Dominic Smith
description: A detailed story that connects a 17th-century Dutch painting to its 20th-century American owner and the lonely but fervent art student who makes the life-changing decision to forge it.

title: Miller's Valley
author: Anna Quindlen
description: A coming-of-age story set in rural Pennsylvania, Quindlen focuses on a young woman buffeted by upheavals in her personal life and a threat to the farmland her family has owned for generations.

title: Lab Girl
author: Hope Jahren
description: Award-winning scientist Jahren delivers a personal memoir and a paean to the natural world.

title: The Midnight Assassin: Panic, Scandal, and the Hunt for America's First Serial Killer
author: Skip Hollandsworth
description: A sweeping narrative history of a terrifying serial killer--America's first--who stalked Austin, Texas in 1885.

title: The Lady With the Borzoi: Blanche Knopf, Literary Tastemaker Extraordinaire
author: Laura Claridge
description: The untold story of Blanche Knopf, the singular woman who helped define American literature.

title: I Will Find You
author: Joanna Connors
description: A reporter investigate the life of a man who raped her, considering race, class, education and the families that shape who we become.

title: Becoming Wise: An Inquiry into the Mystery and Art of Living
author: Krista Tippett
description: The host of NPR’s On Being draws on conversations with poets, scientists, theologians, and other seekers of truth, focusing on five concepts—words, flesh, love, faith, and hope.

title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
author: Ocean Vuong
description: A poetry collection which draws from individual, familial and historical traumas.

title: Till We Have Built Jerusalem
author: Adina Hoffman
description: A biographical excavation of one of the world’s great, troubled cities.

title: The Bed Moved
author: Rebecca Schiff
description: A collection of stories focusing on adolescence, death, sex; on being Jewish-ish; and on finding one’s way as a young woman in the world.

title: Empire of Things: How We Became a World of Consumers, from the Fifteenth Century to the Twenty-First
author: Frank Trentmann
description: An examination of how we became a world of consumers, from the fifteenth century to the twenty-first.

title: American Amnesia: How the War on Government Led Us to Forget What Made America Prosper
author: Jacob S. Hacker & Paul Pierson
description: A work examining what’s good for American business and what’s good for Americans—and why those interests are misaligned.

title: The Year of the Runaways
author: Sunjeev Sahota
description: Three young men, and one woman, come together in a journey from India to England, where they hope to begin something new—to support their families; to build their futures; to show their worth; to escape the past.

title: Black Hole Blues and Other Songs from Outer Space
author: Janna Levin
description: The story of the headline-making discovery of gravitational waves—by a theoretical astrophysicist and award-winning writer.

title: Girls & Sex: Navigating the Complicated New Landscape
author: Peggy Orenstein
description: An investigation into of the new sexual landscape girls face in their high school through college years, and how they are dealing with it.

title: Melancholy Accidents: Three Centuries of Stray Bullets and Bad Luck
author: Peter Manseau
description: A look at accidental shootings, known once as 'melancholy accidents,' throughout American history.

title: Violation: Collected Essays
author: Sallie Tisdale
description: An essay collection from Tisdale that spans 30 years of writing.

title: The Grand Tour: The Life and Music of George Jones
author: Rich Kienzie
description: A book which explores the wild life and extraordinary musical career of George Jones.

title: The Other Side of Silence (A Bernie Gunther Novel)
author: Philip Kerr
description: The latest in the Bernie Gunther crime series in which the sardonic former Berlin homicide detective and unwilling SS officer is now living on the French Riviera.

title: The Stopped Heart
author: Julie Myerson
description: A long-dead family haunts a ramshackle cottage, the new home of grieving Mary and Graham Coles.

title: Spain in Our Hearts: Americans in the Spanish Civil War, 1936-1939
author: Adam Hochschild
description: A sweeping history of the Spanish Civil War, told through a dozen characters, including Ernest Hemingway and George Orwell: a tale of idealism, heartbreaking suffering, and a noble cause that failed.

title: Lust & Wonder
author: Augusten Burroughs
description: A chronicle of Burroughs' exasperating love life in New York City following addiction and recovery.

title: The Little Red Chairs
author: Edna O'Brien
description: An Irish town is touched by the war crimes in Sarajevo when an outsider sleeps with a local woman and she's driven by shame and brutality into exile.

title: This House of Grief: The Story of a Murder Trial
author: Helen Garner
description: On Father’s Day in 2005, a car driven by Robert Farquharson, carrying his three young sons, veered off the highway outside of Winchelsea and plunged into a dam. Farquharson swam to shore, but his children drowned. In This House of Grief , Garner follows the subsequent murder trial, a case that stretched over eight years, and seeks to answer the incomprehensible: was Farquharson’s a deliberate act? Winner of a 2015 Windham Campbell Prize for Nonfiction.

title: Relief Map
author: Rosalie Knecht
description: A small Pennsylvania town swept up in a manhunt for a fugitive from foreign soil and a teenage girl struggling to make the right choices with little information and less time.

title: Rush Oh!
author: Shirley Barrett
description: A novel about a young woman's coming-of-age, during one of the harshest whaling seasons in the history of New South Wales.

title: John Quincy Adams: Militant Spirit
author: James Traub
description: Scholar and journalist James Traub draws on Adams’ diary, letters, and writings to evoke a diplomat and president whose ideas remain with us today.

title: Jane Steele
author: Lyndsay Faye
description: A reimagining of Jane Eyre as a gutsy, heroic serial killer.

title: The Caped Crusade: Batman and the Rise of Nerd Culture
author: Glen Weldon
description: A cultural history from NPR book critic Glen Weldon explains Batman’s rises and falls throughout the ages—and what his story tells us about ourselves.

title: The Summer Before the War
author: Helen Simonson
description: A romantic novel set in a small English town on the eve of World War I, from the author of Major Pettigrew's Last Stand .

title: The Nest
author: Cynthia D'Aprix Sweeney
description: A comic novel about four adult siblings and the fate of the shared inheritance that has shaped their choices and their lives.

title: The Association of Small Bombs
author: Karan Mahajan
description: When brothers Tushar and Nakul Khurana, two Delhi schoolboys, pick up their family’s television set at a repair shop with their friend Mansoor Ahmed one day in 1996, disaster strikes without warning. What follows is an exploration of radicalization, politics, and religion.

title: Hold Still
author: Lynn Steger Strong
description: A novel which traces a mother-daughter bond that must be rebuilt after a life-changing tragedy.

title: Patience
author: Daniel Clowes
description: A sci-fi love story from the author of Ghost World in which a man, whose wife has been murdered, travels back through time to try and save her.

title: Beijing Comrades
author: Bei Tong
description: The story of a tumultuous gay love affair set against the sociopolitical unrest of late-eighties China.

title: Something Will Happen, You'll See
author: Christos Ikonomou
description: Set in a working class neighborhood in Pireaus, Greece, Ikonomou's stories convey the plight of those worst affected by the Greek economic crisis.

title: The North Water
author: Ian McGuire
description: A dark, graphic tale of nineteenth-century whaling ship that sets sail for the Arctic with a killer aboard.

title: Boys Among Men
author: Jonathan Abrams
description: The story of the prep-to-pro generation, those basketball prodigies who from 1995 to 2005 made the jump directly from high school to the NBA.

title: Shelter
author: Jung Yun
description: Tensions quickly mount as Korean-American Kyung’s proximity to his parents forces old feelings of guilt and anger to the surface, along with a terrible and persistent question: how can he ever be a good husband, father, and son when he never knew affection as a child?

title: Knockout
author: John Jodzio
description: A unified collection of stories that create portraits of deeply flawed figures on the edge of the American Dream.

title: Alligator Candy
author: David Kushner
description: The story of how the author, now an award-winning journalist, and his family dealt with the senseless murder of his older brother when they were children.

title: Putin Country: A Journey into the Real Russia
author: Anne Garrels
description: Narrative snapshots over several decades of a Russia riven by contradictions, aspirations, and entrenched defenses.

title: Rightful Heritage: Franklin D. Roosevelt and the Land of America
author: Douglas Brinkley
description: An examination of the environmental legacy of FDR and the New Deal.

title: The Abundance: Narrative Essays Old and New
author: Annie Dillard
description: A collection of essays from the Pulitzer Prize winner's long career.

title: A Man Lies Dreaming
author: Lavie Tidhar
description: A down-on-his-luck Hitler, now working as a private detective in London, searches for a missing Jewish girl in this wild, noir-infused alternative history.

title: Burning Down the House
author: Jane Mendelsohn
description: Mendelsohn tracks the slow and gruesome fall of an elite New York family caught up in the darker side of capitalism.

title: Margaret the First
author: Danielle Dutton
description: A poetic meditation on the writing life as seen through the experiences of Margaret Cavendish, Duchess of Newcastle, a 17th-century woman of letters.

title: The Cosmopolitans
author: Sarah Schulman
description: Earl, a black, gay actor working in a meatpacking plant, and Bette, a white secretary, have lived next door to each other in the same Greenwich Village apartment building for thirty years. Shamed and disowned by their families, both found refuge in New York and in their domestic routine. Everything changes when Hortense, a wealthy young actress from Ohio, comes to the city to "make it."

title: So Sad Today
author: Melissa Broder
description: From poet and creator of the popular Twitter account @sosadtoday comes a darkly comic and brutally honest collection of essays.

title: Listen, Liberal: Or, What Ever Happened to the Party of the People?
author: Thomas Frank
description: A scathing look at the standard-bearers of liberal politics –– a book that asks: what's the matter with Democrats?

title: Stork Mountain
author: Miroslav Penkov
description: A young Bulgarian immigrant returns to the country of his birth in search of his grandfather, who suddenly and unexpectedly cut all contact with the family three years ago. High up in the Strandja Mountains he gets drawn by his grandfather into a maze of half-truths. And here, he falls in love with an unobtainable Muslim girl.

title: A Life Apart
author: Neel Mukherjee
description: Ritwik Ghosh, twenty-two and recently orphaned, finds the chance to start a new life when he arrives in England from Calcutta. But Oxford holds little of the salvation Ritwik is looking for. Instead, he moves to London, where he drops out of official existence into a shadowy hinterland of illegal immigrants.

title: The Throwback Special
author: Chris Bachelder
description: In this comic dissection of male bonding, a group of men gathers for their yearly celebration and re-enactment of a notorious play in professional football.

title: Smarter, Faster, Better: The Secrets of Productivity in Life and Business
author: Charles Duhigg
description: At the core of Smarter, Faster, Better are eight key productivity concepts—from motivation and goal setting to focus and decision making—that explain why some people and companies get so much done.

title: The Civil Wars of Julia Ward Howe
author: Elaine Showalter
description: The first biography to reveal Julia Ward Howe—the author of The Battle Hymn of the Republic —as a feminist pioneer who fought her own battle for creative freedom and independence.

title: Gone With the Mind
author: Mark Leyner
description: A joyride of autobiography, cultural critique, DIY philosophy, biopolitics, video games, demagoguery, and the most intimate confessions of the unconventional postmodernist author.

title: What Is Not Yours Is Not Yours
author: Helen Oyeyemi
description: Nine playful, casually interlocking stories, set in a familiar yet surreal contemporary world.

title: Scary Old Sex
author: Arlene Heyman
description: A debut story collection by a New York–based psychiatrist/psychoanalyst with long-standing literary connections delves into the complicated relationships and intimate sex lives of mature couples.

title: The Paper Menagerie
author: Ken Liu
description: A collection of Hugo and Nebula award winning stories.

title: The Violet Hour: Great Writers at the End
author: Katie Roiphe
description: A meditation on morality and an account of the last days of Susan Sontag, Sigmund Freud, John Updike, Dylan Thomas, Maurice Sendak, and James Salter.

title: All Things Cease to Appear
author: Elizabeth Brundage
description: A dark novel that combines noir and the gothic in a story about two families entwined in their own unhappiness, with, at its heart, a gruesome and unsolved murder.

title: A Woman of Property
author: Robyn Schiff
description: "A dark poetry collection located in a menacing, gothic landscape."

title: We Love You, Charlie Freeman
author: Kaitlyn Greenidge
description: An African-American family is hired by a private research institute to 'adopt' a chimpanzee and teach the animal sign language. A coming-of-age story that is also an exploration of family, race, and history.

title: Bullies: A Friendship
author: Alex Abramovich
description: An account of one writer's unlikely friendship with his childhood bully, now the president of a motorcycle club in one of America's most dangerous cities.

title: Innocents and Others
author: Dana Spiotta
description: The complex relationship among three women and the film world drives this tale of technology and its discontents.

title: High Dive
author: Jonathan Lee
description: Two narrative lines follow an imagined perpetrator and a father and daughter in the 1984 bombing that targeted Margaret Thatcher and other Conservative Party notables meeting at the Grand Hotel in Brighton, England.

title: The Fever of 1721: The Epidemic That Revolutionized Medicine and American Politics
author: Stephen Coss
description: More than fifty years before the American Revolution, Boston was in revolt against the tyrannies of the Crown, Puritan Authority, and Superstition. This is the story of a fateful year that prefigured the events of 1776.

title: The Selected Letters of Laura Ingalls Wilder
author: Laura Ingalls Wilder, ed. William Anderson
description: A portrait of the revered American author, illuminating her thoughts, travels, philosophies, writing career, and dealings with family, friends, and fans.

title: Noonday
author: Part Barker
description: The final part of a trilogy. London, the Blitz, Autumn 1940. As the bombs fall on the blacked-out city, ambulance driver Elinor Brooke races from bomb sites to hospitals trying to save the lives of injured survivors, working alongside former friend Kit Neville, while her husband Paul Tarrant works as an air-raid warden.

title: Peacekeeping
author: Mischa Berlinski
description: On the troubled half-island of Haiti, love, power, and poverty collide, as do a tough Florida cop, a beautiful singer, politicians, and the United Nations post-2004 peacekeeping mission.

title: Eruption: The Untold Story of Mount St. Helens
author: Steve Olson
description: Survival narrative meets scientific, natural, and social history in the story of a volcanic disaster.

title: Half-Earth: Our Planet's Fight for Life
author: Edward O. Wilson
description: Half-Earth proposes a plan to save our imperiled biosphere: devote half the surface of the Earth to nature.

title: Night at the Fiestas
author: Kirstin Valdez Quade
description: The debut collection of stories from Kirstin Valdez Quade tackles family ties and fissures across New Mexico, plunging us into the fierce, troubled hearts of characters defined by the desire to escape the past—or to plumb its depths. Winner of the 2015 National Book Critics Circle John Leonard Prize.

title: The Apache Wars: The Hunt for Geronimo, the Apache Kid, and the Captive Boy Who Started the Longest War in American History
author: Paul Andrew Hutton
description: A vivid historical account of the manhunt for Geronimo and the 25-year Apache struggle for their homeland.

title: Evicted: Poverty and Profit in the American City
author: Matthew Desmond
description: Based on two years the author spent embedded with eight poor families in Milwaukee, Evicted is a groundbreaking work on the central role of housing in the lives of the poor.

title: The Profiteers: Bechtel and the Men who Built the World
author: Sally Denton
description: The inside story of the Bechtel family and the empire they’ve controlled since the construction of the Hoover Dam.

title: The Ancient Minstrel
author: Jim Harrison
description: Three very different novellas with autobiographical elements in common.

title: Apostle: Travels Among the Tombs of the Twelve
author: Tom Bissell
description: A journey into the heart of Christianity that explores the mysterious and often paradoxical lives and legacies of the Twelve Apostles.

title: Imbeciles: The Supreme Court, American Eugenics, and the Sterilization of Carrie Buck
author: Adam Cohen
description: An examination an ugly chapter in American history: the 1920s mania for eugenics, focusing on the Supreme Court’s infamous 1927 Buck v. Bell ruling made government sterilization of 'undesirable' citizens the law of the land.

title: Don't Let My Baby Do Rodeo
author: Boris Fishman
description: A portrait of marriage and a family. The parents of an eccentric adopted child head west to explore his roots and learn a few things about their own.

title: Blackass
author: A. Igoni Barrett
description: A satire in which Furo Wariboko, a young Nigerian, awakes the morning before a job interview to find that he's been transformed completely into a white man, except for one particular body part.

title: The Lonely City: Adventures in the Art of Being Alone
author: Olivia Laing
description: A work of memoir, biography and cultural criticism on the subject of loneliness, told through the lives of six iconic artists.

title: Prodigals
author: Greg Jackson
description: Well-educated but rudderless people seek enlightenment in these stories—or at least an interesting trip and a good high.

title: Charlotte Brontë: A Fiery Heart
author: Claire Harman
description: On the two hundredth anniversary of her birth, a biography transforms Charlotte Brontë from a tragic figure into a modern heroine.

title: The Immortal Irishman: The Irish Revolutionary Who Became an American Hero
author: Timothy Egan
description: The story of Thomas Meagher (1823-1867), an Irishman radicalized by the famine who became a hero on three continents.

title: All the Single Ladies: Unmarried Women and the Rise of an Independent Nation
author: Rebecca Traister
description: An investigation into the sexual, economic, and emotional lives of modern women.

title: At the Existentialist Cafe: Freedom, Being and Apricot Cocktails
author: Sarah Bakewell
description: An account of one of the twentieth century’s major intellectual movements and the revolutionary thinkers who came to shape it.

title: I Met Someone
author: Bruce Wagner
description: The the story of Academy Award–winning actress Dusty Wilding, her wife Allegra, a long-lost daughter, and the unspeakable secret hidden beneath the glamour of their lavish, carefully calibrated celebrity life.

title: For a Little While
author: Rick Bass
description: A collection of tales from the iconic short story writer.

title: Trouble Boys: The True Story of the Replacements
author: Bob Mehr
description: A biography of The Replacements, written with the participation of the group's key members.

title: Scarpia
author: Piers Paul Read
description: A novel exploring the lives--part historical, part fictional--of figures from Puccini’s opera Tosca .

title: When We Are No More: How Digital Memory Is Shaping Our Future
author: Abby Smith Rumsey
description: Rumsey explores human memory from pre-history to the present to shed light on the grand challenge facing our world--the abundance of information and scarcity of human attention.

title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
author: Carlo Rovelli
description: This playful and mind-bending introduction to modern physics briskly explains Einstein's general relativity, quantum mechanics, elementary particles, gravity, black holes, the complex architecture of the universe, and the role humans play in this weird and wonderful world.

title: Dark Territory: The Secret History of Cyber War
author: Fred Kaplan
description: The never-before-told story of the officers, policymakers, scientists, and spies who devised this new form of warfare and who have been planning—and fighting—these wars for decades.

title: A Murder Over a Girl: Justice, Gender, Junior High
author: Ken Corbett
description: A psychologist's exploration of the brutal murder of a possibly transgender middle school student by an eighth grade classmate.

title: The Art of Charlie Chan Hock Chye
author: Sonny Liew
description: An imagined hybrid. Now in his early 70s, Chan has been making comics in his native Singapore since 1954, when he was a boy of 16. As he looks back on his career over five decades, we see his stories unfold before us in a dazzling array of art styles and forms, their development mirroring the evolution in the political and social landscape of his homeland and of the comic book medium itself.

title: Constance Fenimore Woolson: Portrait of a Lady Novelist
author: Anne Boyd Rioux
description: A biography reaffirming the literary stature of Constance Fenimore Woolson, who is perhaps best known for having contributed to Henry James’s conception of his heroine Isabelle Archer in The Portrait of a Lady , but who was herself one of the most accomplished American writers of the nineteenth century.

title: Carry Me
author: Peter Behrens
description: An historical novel which follows the fortunes of two intermingled families through one of the most turbulent times in modern history—England, Ireland and Germany in the first half of the 20th century.

title: I'm Glad About You
author: Theresa Rebeck
description: A tale of star-crossed Midwesterners: an actress making it big and the complicated relationship she has with the guy she met as a teenager.

title: The Slave's Cause: A History of Abolition
author: Manisha Sinha
description: A history of abolition that recovers the largely forgotten role of African Americans in the long march toward emancipation from the American Revolution through the Civil War.

title: Playing to the Edge: American Intelligence in the Age of Terror
author: Michael V. Hayden
description: The former director of the National Security Agency and the CIA defends espionage as vital to American safety in a violent world.

title: You Could Look It Up: The Reference Shelf From Ancient Babylon to Wikipedia
author: Jack Lynch
description: An exploration of the reference shelf from Ancient Babylon to Wikipedia.

title: A Gathering of Shadows
author: V.E. Schwab
description: The follow-up to V.E. Schwab's epic fantasy novel A Darker Shade of Magic .

title: 13 Ways of Looking at a Fat Girl
author: Mona Awad
description: A young woman navigates uneasy relationships with herself, her weight, and the world in Awad’s painfully raw—and bitingly funny—debut.

title: American Girls: Social Media and the Secret Lives of Teenagers
author: Nancy Jo Sales
description: An examination of social media and its effects on the lives of American teenagers.

title: The Green and the Black: The Complete Story of the Shale Revolution, the Fight over Fracking, and the Future of Energy
author: Gary Sernovitz
description: The story of the shale revolution, the fight over fracking, and the future of energy.

title: On the Move
author: Oliver Sacks
description: The story of a brilliantly unconventional physician and writer, a man who has illuminated the many ways that the brain makes us human. With unbridled honesty and humor, Sacks writes about the passions that have driven his life—from motorcycles and weight lifting to neurology and poetry. He writes about his love affairs, both romantic and intellectual; his guilt over leaving his family to come to America; his bond with his schizophrenic brother; and the writers and scientists who have influenced his work.

title: All The Poems
author: Stevie Smith
description: The essential edition of one of modern poetry’s most distinctive voices.

title: A Loaded Gun: Emily Dickinson for the 21st Century
author: Jerome Charyn
description: We think we know Emily Dickinson: the Belle of Amherst, virginal, reclusive, and possibly mad. But in A Loaded Gun , Jerome Charyn introduces us to a different Emily Dickinson: the fierce, brilliant, and sexually charged poet.

title: Pandemic: Tracking Contagions, from Cholera to Ebola and Beyond
author: Sonia Shah
description: Pandemic interweaves history, original reportage, and personal narrative to explore the origins of contagions, drawing parallels between cholera, one of history’s most deadly and disruptive pandemic-causing pathogens, and the new diseases that stalk humankind today.

title: The Widow
author: Fiona Barton
description: A psychological thriller about a meek woman whose husband is run over by a bus not long after being questioned in the disappearance of a young child.

title: Master of Ceremonies
author: Joel Grey
description: Joel Grey, the Tony and Academy Award-winning Master of Ceremonies in Cabaret tells his life story.

title: Strange Gods: A Secular History of Conversion
author: Susan Jacoby
description: An historical work that addresses religious conversion in the West from an uncompromisingly secular perspective.

title: Tender
author: Belinda McKeon
description: "An intimate novel in which two Dublin young people—poet and student Catherine and aspiring art photographer James—tumble into a friendship that, though its lines shift and blur, ultimately helps bring their identities into focus."

title: Forty Rooms
author: Olga Grushin
description: A novel of women's identity and women's choices. Forty rooms is a conceit: it proposes that a modern woman will inhabit forty rooms in her lifetime. They form her biography, from childhood to death.

title: Lovecraft Country
author: Matt Ruff
description: A kaleidoscopic portrait of racism in Jim Crow America. When his father Montrose goes missing, 22-year-old Army veteran Atticus Turner embarks on a road trip to New England to find him, encountering both mundane terrors of white America and malevolent spirits along the way.

title: The Road Taken: The History and Future of America's Infrastructure
author: Henry Petroski
description: The Road Taken explores our core infrastructure from historical and contemporary perspectives and explains how essential their maintenance is to America's economic health.

title: Seeing Red
author: Lina Meruane, Trans. by Megan McDowell
description: This intense autobiographical novel describes a young Chilean writer recently relocated to New York for doctoral work who suffers a stroke, leaving her blind and increasingly dependent on those closest to her.

title: Cities I've Never Lived In
author: Sara Majka
description: A collection of stories exploring distance in all its forms: the emotional spaces that open up between family members, friends, and lovers; the gaps that emerge between who we were and who we are; the gulf between our private and public selves.

title: Midnight Sun
author: Jo Nesbo
description: A tightly wound tale of a man running from retribution, a renegade hitman who goes to ground far above the Arctic circle, where the never-setting sun might slowly drive a man insane.

title: A Doubter's Almanac
author: Ethan Canin
description: A novel which explores the nature of genius, rivalry, ambition, and love among multiple generations of a gifted family.

title: Surveys
author: Natasha Stagg
description: Natasha Stagg's debut traces a few months in the life of Colleen, a twenty-three-year-old woman with almost no attachments or aspirations for her life, becoming fully alive only at night when she's online. Colleen attains ambiguous Internet stardom when she's discovered by Jim, a semi-famous icon of masculinity and reclusiveness.

title: A Mother's Reckoning: Living in the Aftermath of Tragedy
author: Sue Klebold
description: Sue Klebold, mother of Columbine shooter Dylan Klebold, chronicles her journey as a mother trying to come to terms with the incomprehensible.

title: In Europe's Shadow: Two Cold Wars and a Thirty-Year Journey Through Romania and Beyond
author: Robert D. Kaplan
description: A journey through one of Europe’s frontier countries—and an examination of the forces that will determine Europe’s fate in the postmodern age.

title: A Collapse of Horses
author: Brian Evenson
description: A stuffed bear’s heart beats with the rhythm of a dead baby, Reno keeps receding to the east no matter how far you drive, and in a mine on another planet, the dust won’t stop seeping in. In these stories, Evenson unsettles us with the everyday and the extraordinary—the terror of living with the knowledge of all we cannot know.

title: The First Congress: How James Madison, George Washington, and a Group of Extraordinary Men Invented the Government
author: Fergus M. Bordewich
description: The little known story of perhaps the most productive Congress in US history, the First Federal Congress of 1789–1791.

title: The Heart
author: Maylis de Kerangal, Trans. by Sam Taylor
description: The Heart takes place over the twenty-four hours surrounding a fatal accident and a resulting heart transplant as life is taken from a young man and given to a woman close to death.

title: Arcadia
author: Iain Pears
description: Three interlocking worlds. Four people looking for answers. But who controls the future—or the past?

title: The Fugitives
author: Christopher Sorrentino
description: To escape his turbulent private life and the scandal that’s maimed his public reputation, Sandy Mulligan has retreated from Brooklyn to the quiet Michigan town where he hopes to finish his long-overdue novel. There, he becomes fascinated by John Salteau, a native Ojibway storyteller who regularly appears at the local library. But Salteau is not what he appears to be—a fact suspected by Kat Danhoff, an ambitious Chicago reporter of elusive ethnic origins who arrives to investigate a theft from a nearby Indian-run casino.

title: Wreck and Order
author: Hannah Tennant-Moore
description: Purposefully aimless, self-destructive, and impulsively in and out of love, Elsie is a young woman who feels lost. She's in a tumultuous relationship, is stuck in a dead-end job, and has a relentless, sharp intelligence that’s at odds with her many bad decisions. When her initial attempts to improve her life go awry, Elsie decides that a dramatic change is the only solution.

title: Liar
author: Rob Roberge
description: When musician Rob Roberge learns that he's likely to have developed a progressive memory-eroding disease from years of hard living and frequent concussions, he is terrified by the prospect of becoming a walking shadow. In a desperate attempt to preserve his identity, he sets out to (somewhat faithfully) record the most formative moments of his life.

title: My Father, the Pornographer
author: Chris Offutt
description: When Andrew Offutt died, his son, Chris, inherited a desk, a rifle, and eighteen hundred pounds of pornographic fiction. Andrew, a volatile man, had been considered the 'king of twentieth-century smut.' Offutt takes us on the journey with him, reading his father’s prodigious literary output as both a critic and as a son seeking answers.

title: West of Eden: An American Place
author: Jean Stein
description: An oral history of Hollywood and Los Angeles from the author of the contemporary classic Edie .

title: Better Living Through Criticism: How to Think about Art, Pleasure, Beauty, and Truth
author: A. O. Scott
description: The New York Times film critic shows why we need criticism now more than ever.

title: Ways to Disappear
author: Idra Novey
description: A novel about the disappearance of a famous Brazilian novelist and the young translator who turns her life upside down to follow her author's trail.

title: Private Citizens
author: Tony Tulathimutte
description: A biting satire that tracks a group of recent Stanford grads anxiously navigating post-college life in mid-2000s San Francisco.

title: The Life of Elves
author: Muriel Barbery, Trans. by Alison Anderson
description: A fantasy story about two gifted girls who find themselves involved in an epic battle between forces that wish to reestablish harmony in the world and those that wish to shatter it definitively, being waged on earth and in the mysterious land of mist, where the elves dwell.

title: The Lost Time Accidents
author: Jon Wray
description: Haunted by a failed love affair and the darkest of family secrets, Waldemar 'Waldy' Tolliver wakes one morning to discover that he has been exiled from the flow of time. The world continues to turn, and Waldy is desperate to find his way back-a journey that forces him to reckon not only with the betrayal at the heart of his doomed romance but also the legacy of his great-grandfather's fatal pursuit of the hidden nature of time itself.

title: In Other Words
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
description: Translated from Italian, the non-fiction debut of Pulitzer Prize-winner Jhumpa Lahiri focuses on her decision to move to Italy and immerse herself fully in the Italian language.

title: Sudden Death
author: Alvaro Enrigue, Trans. by Natasha Wimmer
description: An experimental, kaleidoscopic novel about the clash of empires and ideas, told through a tennis match in the sixteenth century between the radical Italian artist Caravaggio and the Spanish poet Francisco de Quevedo.

title: Every Song Ever: Twenty Ways to Listen in an Age of Musical Plenty
author: Ben Ratliff
description: New York Times music critic Ben Ratliff reimagines the very idea of music appreciation for our times.

title: Incarceration Nations: A Journey to Justice in Prisons Around the World
author: Baz Dreisinger
description: A criminal justice professor travels behind bars in nine countries to rethink the state of justice in a global context.

title: The Yid
author: Paul Goldberg
description: Set in 1953, a pair of offbeat Jewish characters and an African American come to terms with life, death, and theater as Stalin's final pogrom gains steam.

title: Youngblood
author: Matt Gallagher
description: A novel about a young American soldier struggling to find meaning during the final, dark days of the War in Iraq.

title: Lit Up
author: David Denby
description: Author and critic Denby goes back to high school to find out whether books can shape lives.

title: The Firebrand and the First Lady: Portrait of a Friendship: Pauli Murray, Eleanor Roosevelt, and the Struggle for Social Justice
author: Patricia Bell-Scott
description: The story of how a brilliant writer-turned-activist, granddaughter of a mulatto slave, and the first lady of the United States, whose ancestry gave her membership in the Daughters of the American Revolution, forged an enduring friendship.

title: A Friend of Mr. Lincoln
author: Stephen Harrigan
description: A fictionalized portrait of Abraham Lincoln during a crucially revealing period of his life, the early Springfield years, when he risked both his sanity and his ethical bearings as he searched for the great destiny he believed to be his.

title: Exit Right: The People Who Left the Left and Reshaped the American Century
author: Daniel Oppenheimer
description: A look at the evolution of America’s political soul through the lives of six political figures—from Whittaker Chambers to Christopher Hitchens—who abandoned the left and joined the right.

title: The Queen of the Night
author: Alexander Chee
description: A lush novel that follows one woman’s rise from circus rider to courtesan to world-renowned diva.

title: The Vegetarian
author: Han Kang
description: Winner of the 2016 Man Booker International Prize, a darkly allegorical, Kafka-esque tale of power, obsession, and one woman’s struggle to break free from the violence both without and within her.

title: Blood Brothers: The Fatal Friendship Between Muhammad Ali and Malcolm X
author: Randy Roberts & Johnny Smith
description: Based on previously untapped sources, from Malcolm’s personal papers to FBI records, Blood Brothers offers a portrait of this complex bond.

title: Children of Paradise: The Struggle for the Soul of Iran
author: Laura Secor
description: The drama that shaped today’s Iran, from the Revolution to the present day.

title: While the City Slept: A Love Lost to Violence and a Young Man's Descent into Madness
author: Eli Sanders
description: A Pulitzer Prize–winning reporter’s account of one young man’s path to murder—and a wake-up call for mental health care in America.

title: The Secret Life of the American Musical
author: Jack Viertel
description: A lively examination of how Broadway shows are built.

title: The Black Presidency: Barack Obama and the Politics of Race in America
author: Michael Eric Dyson
description: A deep dive into the meaning of America's first black presidency.

title: Black Deutschland
author: Darryl Pinckney
description: Jed?young, gay, black, out of rehab and out of prospects in his hometown of Chicago?flees to the city of his fantasies, a museum of modernism and decadence: Berlin.

title: The High Mountains of Portugal
author: Yann Martel
description: Three grieving men’s odysseys interconnect in a meditation on loss, faith, and belonging from the author of Life of Pi .

title: Find Me
author: Laura van den Berg
description: A young woman trying to find her place in the world, Joy is alone. But when a sickness that begins with memory loss and ends with death sweeps the country, Joy, for the first time in her life, seems to have an advantage: she is immune. When Joy's immunity gains her admittance to a hospital in rural Kansas, she sees a chance to escape her bleak existence.

title: Why We Write About Ourselves
author: Ed. Meredith Maran
description: Twenty memoirists on why they expose themselves (and others) in the name of literature.

title: The Blue Line
author: Ingrid Betancourt
description: A novel set against the backdrop of Argentina’s Dirty War, and infused with magical realism, in which a girl is burdened with visions from the future.

title: Fine, Fine, Fine, Fine, Fine
author: Diane Williams
description: A collection of 40 very short, unsettling and comic stories from Diane Williams.

title: The Art of X-Ray Reading: How the Secrets of 25 Great Works of Literature Will Improve Your Writing
author: Roy Peter Clark
description: Writing teacher Roy Peter Clark offers writing lessons we can draw from 25 great texts.

title: Ostend: Stefan Zweig, Joseph Roth, and the Summer Before the Dark
author: Volker Weidermann
description: The true story of two of the twentieth century’s great writers and a coterie of artists, intellectuals, drunks, revolutionaries, and madmen who found themselves in limbo while Europe teetered on the edge of fascism and total war.

title: Good on Paper
author: Rachel Cantor
description: A translator struggling to redefine her work, her family, and her sense of self gets a call from a Nobel Prize-winning Italian poet who insists she’s the only one who can translate his newest book.

title: Where My Heart Used to Beat
author: Sebastian Faulks
description: From the author of Birdsong , a novel that mixes memory and desire as a World War II veteran accesses painful memories of a wartime romance.

title: The Life and the Adventures of a Haunted Convict
author: Austin Reed
description: The earliest known prison memoir by an African American writer—recently discovered and authenticated by a team of Yale scholars—sheds light on the longstanding connection between race and incarceration in America.

title: The Castle Cross the Magnet Carter
author: Kia Corthron
description: The Castle Cross the Magnet Carter sweeps American history from 1941 to the twenty-first century through the lives of four men--two white brothers from rural Alabama, and two black brothers from small-town Maryland--whose journey culminates in an explosive and devastating encounter between the two families.

title: All the Birds in the Sky
author: Charlie Jane Anders
description: As the battle between magic and science wages in San Francisco against the backdrop of international chaos, Laurence and Patricia are forced to choose sides. But their choices will determine the fate of the planet and all mankind.

title: On the Edge
author: Rafael Chirbes, Trans. by Margaret Jull Costa
description: One of Spain’s leading novelists, who died in August 2015, tackles the malaise that has swept his country in the wake of the Great Recession.

title: The Unfinished World
author: Amber Sparks
description: A collection of elliptical stories in which death throws a long shadow over an eclectic group of characters.

title: Dark Money: The Hidden History of the Rise of the Billionaire Businessmen Behind the Radical Right
author: Jane Mayer
description: The hidden history of the billionaires behind the rise of the radical right.

title: Cure: A Journey into the Science of Mind Over Body
author: Jo Marchant
description: A look at the new science behind the mind's surprising ability to heal the body.

title: Their Promised Land: My Grandparents in Love and War
author: Ian Buruma
description: Ian Buruma’s account of his grandparents’ enduring love through the terror and separation of two world wars.

title: The Stargazer's Sister
author: Carrie Brown
description: A nineteenth-century story of female empowerment before its time, based on the life of Caroline Herschel, sister of the great composer and astronomer William Herschel and an astronomer in her own right.

title: The Narrow Door
author: Paul Lisicky
description: In The Narrow Door , Paul Lisicky creates a collage of scenes and images drawn from two long-term relationships, one with a woman novelist and the other with his ex-husband, a poet.

title: The Road to Little Dribbling
author: Bill Bryson
description: The veteran comic travel writer takes us on another jaunt across Britain.

title: In a Different Key: The Story of Autism
author: John Donovan & Caren Zucker
description: A narrative history of autism: the story of parents fighting for their children ’s civil rights; of doctors struggling to define autism; of ingenuity, self-advocacy, and profound social change.

title: Thomas Murphy
author: Roger Rosenblatt
description: An elderly poet delivers a chatty, comic monologue on sex, death, life, and getting the girl.

title: Why the Right Went Wrong: Conservatism--From Goldwater to the Tea Party and Beyond
author: E. J. Dionne Jr.
description: The story of the GOP’s fracturing—from the 1964 Goldwater takeover to the Trump spectacle.

title: The Portable Veblen
author: Elizabeth McKenzie
description: On the brink of her marriage, a charmingly quirky, warmhearted young woman forges an unusually strong bond with a squirrel.

title: What Belongs to You
author: Garth Greenwell
description: The life of an American expat living in Bulgaria intersects repeatedly with that of a young gay hustler in this debut novel from Greenwell.

title: The Man Without a Shadow
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: Oates explores the lives of an amnesiac and the neuroscientist who studies and adores him.

title: Weathering
author: Lucy Wood
description: A novel about three generations of women and their search for home. Ada, who has never settled in one place for long, returns to the house of her childhood, accompanied by her 6-year-old daughter, to cast her mother Pearl’s ashes in the river.

title: The Confidence Game: Why We Fall for It . . . Every Time
author: Maria Konnikova
description: What makes a con artist, and why are we duped by them? New Yorker columnist Konnikova takes us into the art and psychology of the con game.

title: The Expatriates
author: Janice Y. K. Lee
description: Hong Kong sets the stage for stories of expatriation, cultural divide, and the varying ways in which grief causes isolation, as seen through three connected women.

title: The Idealist: Aaron Swartz and the Rise of Free Culture on the Internet
author: Justin Peters
description: A history of the Internet free culture movement and its larger effects on society—and the life and shocking suicide of Aaron Swartz, a founding developer of Reddit and Creative Commons—from Slate correspondent Justin Peters.

title: Dictator
author: Robert Harris
description: Set during the last gasp of the Roman Republic, the final volume of Harris’ Cicero trilogy chronicles the great Roman statesman’s fateful encounters with both Julius and Augustus Caesar.

title: Democracy in Black: How Race Still Enslaves the American Soul
author: Eddie S. Glaude Jr.
description: A powerful polemic on the state of black America that savages the idea of a post-racial society.

title: American Housewife
author: Helen Ellis
description: A collection of comic short stories about American housewives.

title: The Dogs of Littlefield
author: Suzanne Berne
description: Littlefield, Massachusetts, named one of the Ten Best Places to Live in America, full of psychologists and college professors, is proud of its fine schools, its girls’ soccer teams, its leafy streets, and charming village center. Yet no sooner has sociologist Dr. Clarice Watkins arrived to study the elements of 'good quality of life' than someone begins poisoning the town’s dogs.

title: The Defender: How the Legendary Black Newspaper Changed America
author: Ethan Michaeli
description: A chronicle of the influential black Chicago newspaper that simultaneously tracks the important issues pertaining to African-American history from the turn of the 19th century.

title: Rosalie Lightning: A Graphic Memoir
author: Tom Hart
description: Hart's graphic memoir about the untimely death of his young daughter, Rosalie.

title: Your Heart Is a Muscle the Size of a Fist
author: Sunil Yapa
description: A ground-level reimagining of the violent protests at the 1999 World Trade Organization meeting in Seattle, told from a host of perspectives.

title: Living on Paper: Letters from Iris Murdoch 1934-1995
author: Iris Murdoch (Edited by Avril Horner & Anne Rowe)
description: A selection of letters from the groundbreaking novelist Iris Murdoch.

title: Excellent Daughters: The Secret Lives of Young Women Who Are Transforming the Arab World
author: Katherine Zoepf
description: A book focusing on changing Arab societies—from 9/11 to Tahrir Square to the rise of ISIS—and giving voice to the remarkable women at the forefront of this change.

title: Hunters in the Dark
author: Lawrence Osborne
description: Adrift in Cambodia and eager to side-step a life of quiet desperation as a small-town teacher, 28-year-old Englishman Robert Grieve decides to go missing. As he crosses the border from Thailand, he tests the threshold of a new future.

title: When Breath Becomes Air
author: Paul Kalanithi
description: A meditation on life from a neurosurgeon with a passion for literature who tragically finds his perfect subject after his diagnosis of terminal lung cancer.

title: My Name is Lucy Barton
author: Elizabeth Strout
description: From the author of Olive Kitteridge , a simple hospital visit becomes a portal to the tender relationship between mother and daughter.

title: This Census-Taker
author: China Mieville
description: In a remote house on a hilltop, a lonely boy witnesses a profoundly traumatic event. He tries—and fails—to flee. Left alone with his increasingly deranged parent, he dreams of safety, of joining the other children in the town below, of escape.

title: Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship
author: Anjan Sundaram
description: "A journalist's insider look at a country caught still in political and social unrest, years after the genocide that shocked the world."

title: United States of Jihad: Investigating America's Homegrown Terrorists
author: Peter Bergen
description: A panoramic look at 'homegrown' Islamist terrorism from 9/11 to the present.

title: Hall of Small Mammals
author: Thomas Pierce
description: The stories in Thomas Pierce’s Hall of Small Mammals take place at the confluence of the commonplace and the cosmic, the intimate and the infinite. A fossil-hunter, a comedian, a hot-air balloon pilot, parents and children, believers and nonbelievers, the people in these stories are struggling to understand the absurdity and the magnitude of what it means to exist in a family, to exist in the world.

title: Let the People Rule: Theodore Roosevelt and the Birth of the Presidential Primary
author: Geoffrey Cowan
description: The story of the four-month campaign in 1912 that changed American politics forever.

title: The Cabaret of Plants: Forty Thousand Years of Plant Life and the Human Imagination
author: Richard Mabey
description: A globe-trotting exploration of the relationship between humans and the kingdom of plants by the renowned naturalist Richard Mabey.

title: Eternity Street: Violence and Justice in Frontier Los Angeles
author: John Mack Faragher
description: The story of a violent place in a violent time: the rise of Los Angeles from its origins as a small Mexican pueblo.

title: Anatomy of a Song
author: Marc Myers
description: In Anatomy of a Song , based on the ongoing Wall Street Journal column, writer and music historian Marc Myers brings to life five decades of music through oral histories of forty-five transformative songs woven from interviews with the artists who created them.

title: Countdown to Pearl Harbor: The Twelve Days to the Attack
author: Steve Twomey
description: A look at the twelve days leading up to the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor—the warnings, clues, and missteps—by a Pulitzer Prize–winning reporter.

title: The Kindness of Enemies
author: Leila Aboulela
description: Both a period piece and an examination of what it is to be Muslim in a post-9/11 world. It’s 2010 and Natasha, a half Russian, half Sudanese professor of history, is researching the life of Imam Shamil, the 19th century Muslim leader who led the anti-Russian resistance in the Caucasian War. When shy, single Natasha discovers that her star student, Oz, is not only descended from the warrior but also possesses Shamil’s priceless sword, the Imam’s story comes vividly to life.

title: Margaret Thatcher: At Her Zenith: In London, Washington and Moscow
author: Charles Moore
description: British historian/writer Moore delivers the second volume in his authorized biography of the pioneering—and divisive—prime minister.

title: One Child: The Story of China's Most Radical Experiment
author: Mei Fong
description: An investigation of the world’s largest experiment in social engineering, revealing how its effects will shape China for decades to come, and what that means for the rest of the world.

title: The Geography of Genius: A Search for the World's Most Creative Places from Ancient Athens to Silicon Valley
author: Eric Weiner
description: Eric Winer travels the world, from Athens to Silicon Valley—and back through history, too—to show how creative genius flourishes in specific places at specific times.

title: Stories I Tell Myself: Growing Up with Hunter S. Thompson
author: Juan F. Thompson
description: Juan Thompson tells the story of his father and of their getting to know each other during their forty-one fraught years together. He writes of the many dark times, of how far they ricocheted away from each other, and of how they found their way back before it was too late.

title: The Past
author: Tessa Hadley
description: A novel in which three sisters, a brother, and their children reunite at their country house in England, where they are forced to deal with their past and their hostilities toward one another.

title: Mr. Splitfoot
author: Samantha Hunt
description: Orphans, abandoned houses, and craters left by meteorites weave together a contemporary gothic tale set in New York state.

title: Sailor and Fiddler: Reflections of a 100-Year-Old Author
author: Herman Wouk
description: The author Herman Wouk reflects on his life and times from the remarkable vantage point of 100 years old.

title: City of Thorns: Nine Lives in the World's Largest Refugee Camp
author: Ben Rawlence
description: Former Human Rights Watch researcher Rawlence details the distressing story of Kenya’s gigantic Dadaab refugee camp, where nearly 500,000 people fleeing civil war in nearby Somalia live.

title: Shame and Wonder
author: David Searcy
description: A collection of essays searching for meaning in some intriguing places, from the sublime to the mundane.

title: The Gun
author: Fuminori Nakamura
description: A Tokyo college student’s discovery and eventual obsession with a stolen handgun awakens something dark inside him.

title: Sharon Tate: A Life
author: Ed Sanders
description: From the author of The Family , a book that traces Sharon's path from beauty queen to budding young actress: her early love affairs, her romance with and marriage to director Roman Polanski, and the excitement of the glamorous life she had always sought—all set against the background of the turbulent 1960s.

title: Alive, Alive Oh!: And Other Things That Matter
author: Diana Athill
description: A joyful insight into what really matters at the end of a long life, from the author of the award-winning Somewhere Towards the End .

title: Groucho Marx: The Comedy of Existence
author: Lee Siegel
description: Part of the Jewish Lives series, an examination of an iconic American figure that explores the cultural and psychological roots of his comic genius.

title: The Last Volcano: A Man, A Romance, and the Quest to Understand Nature's Most Magnificent Fury
author: John Dvorak
description: Ranging from Yellowstone in Wyoming to Mount Pelee in the Caribbean, from Bogoslof and Pavlov in Alaska, to Sakurajima in Japan, and, finally, to the massive volcanoes of Kilauea and Mauna Loa in Hawaii? The Last Volcano reveals the journey of a man on a mission to understand the awesome power of volcanic eruptions.

title: This Is Why I Came
author: Mary Rakow
description: A woman sits in prayerful meditation, waiting to offer her first confession in more than thirty years. She holds a small book on her lap, one that she’s made, and tells herself again the Bible stories it contains, the ones she has written anew, for herself, each story told aslant, from Jonah to Jesus, Moses to Mary Magdalene.

title: A General Theory of Oblivion
author: José Eduardo Agualusa, Trans. by Daniel Hahn
description: As the country goes through various political upheavals from colony to socialist republic to civil war to peace and capitalism, the world outside seeps into Ludo's life of sequestration through snippets on the radio, voices from next door, glimpses of someone peeing on a balcony, or a man fleeing his pursuers.

title: Feast of Excess: A Cultural History of the New Sensibility
author: George Cotkin
description: A portrait of 'The New Sensibility,' as it was named by Susan Sontag in 1965. The New Sensibility sought to push culture in extreme directions: either towards stark minimalism or gaudy maximalism.

title: The Invention of Science: A New History of the Scientific Revolution
author: David Wootton
description: An examination of the greatest event in history, the Scientific Revolution, and how it came to change the way we understand ourselves and our world.

title: Fools, Frauds, and Firebrands: Thinkers of the New Left
author: Roger Scruton
description: A critique of modern Left Wing thinking and a study of the thinkers who have most influenced the attitudes of the New Left.

title: Masters of Empire: Great Lakes Indians and the Making of America
author: Michael McDonnell
description: Masters of Empire reveals the pivotal role played by the native peoples of the Great Lakes in the history of North America.

title: The Relic Master
author: Christopher Buckley
description: An adventure novel featuring a sixteenth-century relic hunter and his best friend, Albrecht Dürer, who conspire to forge the Shroud of Turin.

title: Of Beards and Men: The Revealing History of Facial Hair
author: Christopher Oldstone-Moore
