description: A history of facial hair, Of Beards and Men makes the case that today’s bearded renaissance is part of a centuries-long cycle in which facial hairstyles have varied in response to changing ideals of masculinity."

title: The Blizzard
author: Vladimir Sorokin, Trans. by Jamey Gambrell
description: Garin, a district doctor, is desperately trying to reach the village of Dolgoye, where a mysterious epidemic is turning people into zombies. He carries with him a vaccine that will prevent the spread of this terrible disease, but is stymied in his travels by an impenetrable blizzard. A trip that should last no more than a few hours turns into a metaphysical journey.

title: Lingo: Around Europe in Sixty Languages
author: Gaston Dorren
description: Lingo spins the reader on a whirlwind tour of sixty European languages and dialects, sharing quirky moments from their histories and exploring their commonalities and differences.

title: Like Family
author: Paolo Giordano, Trans. by Anne Milano Appel
description: A portrait of marriage, adulthood, and the meaning of family.

title: Life and Death in the Andes: On the Trail of Bandits, Heroes, and Revolutionaries
author: Kim MacQuarrie
description: Unique portraits of legendary characters along South America’s mountain spine, from Charles Darwin to the present day.

title: Conquerors: How Portugal Forged the First Global Empire
author: Roger Crowley
description: The story of the emergence of Portugal, a small, poor nation that enjoyed a century of maritime supremacy thanks to the daring and navigational skill of its explorers—a tactical advantage no other country could match.

title: First Bite: How We Learn to Eat
author: Bee Wilson
description: Food writer Bee Wilson draws on the latest research from food psychologists and neuroscientists to reveal that our food habits are shaped by a host of factors: family and culture, memory and gender, hunger and love.

title: Drawing Blood
author: Molly Crabapple
description: An illustrated memoir of artistic exploration, political awakening, and personal transformation from artist and activist Molly Crabapple.

title: The American President: From Teddy Roosevelt to Bill Clinton
author: William E. Leuchtenberg
description: An account of American presidential actions from the assassination of William McKinley in 1901 to Bill Clinton's last night in office in January 2001.

title: The War on Alcohol: Prohibition and the Rise of the American State
author: Lisa McGirr
description: A dismantling of the glamorous myths associated with Prohibition and an examination of its effects on the American state.

title: And Yet...: Essays
author: Christopher Hitchens
description: Hitherto uncollected journalistic pieces in which the late author and social critic Hitchens takes stock of the world.

title: Boys in the Trees
author: Carly Simon
description: A memoir from iconic musician Carly Simon.

title: Gratitude
author: Oliver Sacks
description: A collection of essays from the late clinician and writer in which he explored his feelings about completing a life and coming to terms with his own death.

title: Lactivism: How Feminists and Fundamentalists, Hippies and Yuppies, and Physicians and Politicians Made Breastfeeding Big Business and Bad Policy
author: Courtney Jung
description: Political scientist Courtney Jung offers a critique of breastfeeding advocacy to date.

title: Portraits: John Berger on Artists
author: John Berger, Ed. Tom Overton
description: John Berger takes us through centuries of drawing and painting, revealing his lifelong fascination with a diverse cast of artists.

title: About Women: Conversations Between a Writer and a Painter
description: A provocative and wide-ranging conversation between two distinctive women—one American and one French—on the dilemmas, rewards, and demands of womanhood.

title: Hubris: The Tragedy of War in the Twentieth Century
author: Alistair Horne
description: After more than 50 years of writing about military matters, veteran historian Horne reflects on 'the common features of warfare that stood out over the ages.'

title: America Dancing: From the Cakewalk to the Moonwalk
author: Megan Pugh
description: An exuberant history of American dance, told through the lives of virtuoso performers who have defined the art.

title: Young Orson: The Years of Luck and Genius on the Path to Citizen Kane
author: Patrick McGiligan
description: On the centennial of his birth, the defining wunderkind of modern entertainment gets his due in a new biography of his early years—from his first forays in theater and radio to the inspiration and making of Citizen Kane .

title: This Old Man: All in Pieces
author: Roger Angell
description: A miscellany of prose from the acclaimed New Yorker writer and editor.

title: Emblems of the Passing World: Poems After Photographs of August Sander
author: Adam Kirsch
description: "August Sander’s photographic portraits of ordinary people in Weimar Germany inspire this new collection of poems by one of America’s most celebrated writers and critics."

title: Yours in Haste and Adoration: Selected Letters of Terry Southern
author: Ed. Nile Southern and Brooke Allen
description: The selected letters of satirist Terry Southern.

title: Dear Mr. You
author: Mary Louise Parker
description: An award-winning actress’s collection of never-sent literary missives to the men who have most influenced her personal development.

title: The Spectacle of Skill: Selected Writings of Robert Hughes
author: Robert Hughes
description: New and selected writings from Robert Hughes about art, architecture, culture, religion—and himself.

title: What the Eye Hears
author: Brian Seibert
description: The first authoritative history of tap dancing, one of the great art forms––along with jazz and musical comedy––created in America.

title: The Hidden Half of Nature: The Microbial Roots of Life and Health
description: An exploration of how microbes are transforming the way we see nature and ourselves?and could revolutionize agriculture and medicine.

title: Black Dragon River: A Journey Down the Amur River at the Borderlands of Empires
author: Dominic Zeigler
description: A personal journey down one of Asia’s great rivers that reveals the region’s essential history and culture.

title: The End of the Cold War: 1985-1991
author: Robert Service
description: A book which shows how a small but skillful group of statesmen grew determined to end the Cold War on their watch and transformed the global political landscape irreversibly.

title: The White Road: A Journey into Obsession
author: Edmund de Waal
description: An intimate narrative history of porcelain, structured around five journeys through landscapes where porcelain was dreamed about, fired, refined, collected, and coveted.

title: The Big Green Tent
author: Ludmila Ulitskaya
description: The story of three school friends who meet in Moscow in the 1950s and go on to embody the heroism, folly, compromise, and hope of the Soviet dissident experience.

title: A Wild Swan and Other Tales
author: Michael Cunningham
description: Fairy tales for our times from the Pulitzer Prize–winning author of The Hours .

title: Sam Phillips: The Man Who Invented Rock 'n' Roll
author: Peter Guralnick
description: A biography of Sam Phillips, the visionary genius who singlehandedly steered the revolutionary path of Sun Records.

title: Bird
author: Noy Holland
description: A brief, erotic novel. A woman who appears enveloped in conventional domesticity clings to memories of the dangerously bohemian life she shared with her former lover.

title: Hotels of North America
author: Rick Moody
description: A darkly comic portrait of a man who comes to life in the most unexpected of ways: through his online reviews.

title: Target in the Night
author: Ricardo Piglia, trans. Sergio Weisman
description: A political and psychological thriller set in a remote Argentinean Pampas town.

title: Nothing Is True and Everything Is Possible
author: Peter Pomerantsev
description: A journey into the glittering, surreal heart of 21st century Russia, where even dictatorship is a reality show. When British producer Peter Pomerantsev plunges into the booming Russian TV industry, he gains access to every nook and corrupt cranny of the country. It is a world erupting with new money and new power, changing so fast it breaks all sense of reality.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
description: A sweeping history of the Roman Empire from one of our foremost classicists.

title: No More Champagne: Churchill and His Money
author: David Lough
description: The story of Winston Churchill's lifetime of tangled personal finances.

title: Augustine: Conversions to Confessions
author: Robin Lane Fox
description: A biography of one of the most influential figures in all of Christianity.

title: John le Carre: The Biography
author: Adam Sisman
description: A biography of the internationally acclaimed author of The Spy Who Came in from the Cold , Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy , and A Perfect Spy .

title: Numero Zero
author: Umberto Eco, Trans. by Richard Dixon
description: From the author of The Name of the Rose , a novel about the murky world of media politics, conspiracy, and murder.

title: Letters to Vera
author: Vladimir Nabokov, Olga Voronina, Brian Boyd
description: The letters of Nabokov to his wife—gathered here for the first time—chronicle a decades-long love story and document anew the creative energies of an artist who was always at work.

title: The Improbability of Love
author: Hannah Rothschild
description: A satire set in the London art world in which an unlucky-in-love young woman finds herself pursued by parties who would do anything to possess her valuable painting: an exiled Russian oligarch, an avaricious sheikha, an unscrupulous art dealer.

title: The Crossing
author: Michael Connelly
description: Harry Bosch crosses the line to team up with Lincoln Lawyer Mickey Haller in the new thriller from #1 New York Times bestselling author Michael Connelly.

title: Twain and Stanley Enter Paradise
author: Oscar Hijuelos
description: A work of fiction inspired by the real-life, 37-year friendship between two towering figures of the late nineteenth century, famed writer and humorist Mark Twain and legendary explorer Sir Henry Morton Stanley.

title: A Just and Generous Nation: Abraham Lincoln and the Fight for American Opportunity
author: Harold Holzer
description: An account of the beliefs that inspired our sixteenth president to go to war when the Southern states seceded from the Union.

title: The Hunt for Vulcan
author: Thomas Levenson
description: The story of Isaac Newton, Albert Einstein, and the search for a planet that never existed.

title: The Muralist
author: B. A. Shapiro
description: Alizée Benoit, an American painter working for the Works Progress Administration (WPA), vanishes in New York City in 1940. 70 years later, her great-niece endeavors to find out.

title: The Japanese Lover
author: Isabel Allende
description: A love story and multigenerational epic that stretches from San Francisco in the present-day to Poland and the United States during World War II.

title: One Out of Two
author: Daniel Sada
description: A comic novella about two sinister sisters who run a tailoring business in Northern Mexico.

title: The Death of Cancer
author: Vincent T. DeVita Jr. and Elizabeth DeVita-Raeburn
description: After fifty years on the front lines of medicine, a pioneering oncologist reveals why the war on cancer Is winnable--and how we can get there.

title: Great is the Truth: Secrecy, Scandal, and the Quest for Justice at the Horace Mann School
author: Amos Kamil and Sean Elder
description: An exposé of sexual abuse and the struggle for justice at one of America's most prestigious schools.

title: The Mare
author: Mary Gaitskill
description: The story of a Dominican girl, the Anglo woman who introduces her to horse riding, and the horse who changes her life.

title: The Poetry of Yehuda Amichai
author: Yehuda Amichai, ed. Robert Alter
description: "The largest English-language collection to date from the Israeli poet."

title: The Bazaar of Bad Dreams
author: Stephen King
description: A collection of stories from the master of contemporary horror.

title: Ardennes 1944: The Battle of the Bulge
author: Antony Beevor
description: The prizewinning historian and author of D-Day and Stalingrad reconstructs the Battle of the Bulge.

title: All the Houses
author: Karen Olsson
description: A rich moment in political history is distilled through its long-term impact on a fractured Washington family.

title: Power Wars: Inside Obama's Post-9/11 Presidency
author: Charlie Savage
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Charlie Savage's penetrating investigation of the Obama presidency and the national security state.

title: This Gulf of Fire: The Destruction of Lisbon, or Apocalypse in the Age of Science and Reason
author: Mark Molesky
description: An account of one of the most consequential natural disasters of modern times.

title: The Art of the Publisher
author: Roberto Calasso
description: An interior look at Roberto Calasso's work as a publisher and his reflections on the art of book publishing.

title: Preparation for the Next Life
author: Atticus Lish
description: Zou Lei, orphan of the desert, migrates to work in America and finds herself slaving in New York's kitchens. She falls in love with a young man whose heart has been broken in another desert. A new life may be possible if together they can survive homelessness, lockup, and the young man's nightmares, which may be more prophecy than madness. Winner of the 2015 PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction.

title: Soul Machine: The Invention of the Modern Mind
author: George Makari
description: A comprehensive history of the creation of the modern Western mind.

title: London Fog: The Biography
author: Christine L. Corton
description: Corton combines historical and literary sensitivity with an eye for visual drama to reveal London fog as one of the great urban spectacles of the industrial age.

title: St. Marks is Dead: The Many Lives of America's Hippest Street
author: Ada Calhoun
description: A narrative history of three hallowed Manhattan blocks?the epicenter of American cool.

title: Avenue of Mysteries
author: John Irving
description: Juan Diego—a fourteen-year-old boy, who was born and grew up in Mexico—has a thirteen-year-old sister. Her name is Lupe, and she thinks she sees what's coming—specifically, her own future and her brother's. Lupe is a mind reader; she doesn't know what everyone is thinking, but she knows what most people are thinking. As an older man, Juan Diego will take a trip to the Philippines, but what travels with him are his dreams and memories; he is most alive in his childhood and early adolescence in Mexico.

title: The Only Street in Paris: Life on the Rue des Martyrs
author: Elaine Sciolino
description: Elaine Sciolino, the former Paris Bureau Chief of the New York Times , invites us on a tour of her favorite Parisian street, offering an homage to street life and the pleasures of Parisian living.

title: The Blue Touch Paper
author: David Hare
description: The British playwright's account of becoming a writer amid the enormous flux of postwar England and his breakthrough successes as a playwright amid the political ferment of the ’70s.

title: The Witches: Salem, 1962
author: Stacy Schiff
description: Pulitzer Prize winner Stacy Schiff provides a fresh view of the Salem witch trials.

title: The Other Paris
author: Luc Sante
description: A trip through Paris as it will never be again: dark and dank and poor and slapdash and truly bohemia.

title: Reporting Always: Writings From the New Yorker
author: Lillian Ross
description: A collection of Ross’s iconic New Yorker profiles and 'Talk of the Town' pieces that spans forty years.

title: The Givenness of Things
author: Marilynne Robinson
description: Robinson gives an impassioned critique of contemporary society?our addiction to technology, our materialism?while arguing that reverence must be given to who we are and what we are: creatures of singular interest and value, despite our errors and depredations.

title: The Evolution of Everything
author: Matt Ridley
description: Drawing on evidence from science, economics, history, politics, and philosophy, Matt Ridley demolishes conventional assumptions that the great events and trends of our day are dictated by those on high.

title: Slade House
author: David Mitchell
description: A genre- and reality-warping haunted house story spanning five decades, from the last days of the 1970s to the present, from the author of Cloud Atlas .

title: After Alice
author: Gregory Maguire
description: From the author of Wicked comes a magical new twist on Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland .

title: Sinatra: The Chairman
author: James Kaplan
description: The second and concluding volume in Kaplan's Frank Sinatra biography.

title: Notorious RBG: The Life and Times of Ruth Bader Ginsburg
author: Irin Carmon and Shana Knizhnik
description: Inspired by the Tumblr that amused the Justice herself and brought to you by its founder and an award-winning feminist journalist. It draws on intimate access to Ginsburg's family members, close friends, colleagues, and clerks, as well an interview with the Justice herself.

title: Hunger Makes Me a Modern Girl
author: Carrie Brownstein
description: An account of the life and times of an essential riot grrrl and the band she helped create.

title: Custer's Trials: A Life on the Frontier of a New America
author: T.J. Stiles
description: The 2016 Pulitzer Prize-winning biography of General Custer.

title: My Life on the Road
author: Gloria Steinem
description: Gloria Steinem—writer, activist, organizer, and inspiring leader—now tells a story she has never told before, an account of her life as a traveler, a listener, and a catalyst for change.

title: 2 A.M. at The Cat's Pajamas
author: Marie-Helene Bertino
description: An enchanting novel about one day in the lives of a smart-mouthed, rebellious nine-year-old, her fifth grade teacher, and a jazz club owner as they search for love, music, and hope on the snow-covered streets of Philadelphia.

title: The Arab of the Future
author: Riad Sattouf
description: A graphic memoir telling the story of Riad Sattouf's childhood, spent in the shadows of 3 dictators?Muammar Gaddafi, Hafez al-Assad, and his father.

title: No Such Thing as a Free Gift: The Gates Foundation and the Price of Philanthropy
author: Linsey McGoey
description: McGoey probes the business motivations of contemporary philanthropic organizations.

title: Mendocino Fire
author: Elizabeth Tallent
description: Tallent's first book in twenty years, a diverse suite of stories about men and women confronting their vulnerabilities in times of transition and challenge.

title: Rogue Lawyer
author: John Grisham
description: The latest legal thriller from John Grisham, focusing on a young street lawyer who defends the people that other lawyers won't go near.

title: Drinking in America
author: Susan Cheever
description: Cheever chronicles our national love affair with liquor, taking a long look at the way alcohol has changed our nation's history.

title: Doomed to Succeed: The U.S.-Israel Relationship from Truman to Obama
author: Dennis Ross
description: An account of America's changing relationship with Israel.

title: Unfaithful Music & Disappearing Ink
author: Elvis Costello
description: A memoir from Elvis Costello about his unlikely and sometimes comical rise to international success, with diversions through the previously undocumented emotional foundations of some of his best-known songs.

title: Thirteen Ways of Looking
author: Colum McCann
description: A novella and three stories from the Irish author of Let the Great World Spin .

title: Empire of Self: A Life of Gore Vidal
author: Jay Parini
description: A biography of Gore Vidal, one of the most accomplished, visible, and controversial American novelists and cultural figures of the past century.

title: Dissent and the Supreme Court: Its Role in the Court's History and the Nation's Constitutional Dialogue
author: Melvin I. Urofsky
description: A book which looks at the role of dissent in the Supreme Court and the meaning of the Constitution through the greatest and longest lasting public-policy debate in the country’s history, among members of the Supreme Court, between the Court and the other branches of government, and between the Court and the people of the United States.

title: A House of My Own: Stories From My Life
author: Sandra Cisneros
description: A memoir celebrating a life lived to the fullest from Mexican writer Sandra Cisneros.

title: The Tsar of Love and Techno
author: Anthony Marra
description: Interwoven stories about family, sacrifice, the legacy of war, and the redemptive power of art, from the author of A Constellation of Vital Phenomena .

title: Eve's Hollywood
author: Eve Babitz
description: A collection of reminiscences from the former journalist, party girl, bookworm, artist and muse.

title: Changing the Subject: Art and Attention in the Internet Age
author: Sven Birkets
description: Trenchant, expansive essays on the cultural consequences of ongoing, all-permeating technological innovation.

title: Keeping an Eye Open: Essays on Art
author: Julian Barnes
description: Essays on art from the Man Booker Prize–winning author of The Sense of an Ending .

title: The Secret Chord
author: Geraldine Brooks
description: A novel about the life of King David, from the Pulitzer Prize–winning author of People of the Book and March .

title: M Train
author: Patti Smith
description: From the musician and National Book Award–winning author of Just Kids : an odyssey of a legendary artist, told through the cafés and haunts she has worked in around the world.

title: The Witch of Lime Street: Séance, Seduction, and Houdini in the Spirit World
author: David Jaher
description: An account of the rivalry between Harry Houdini and the so-called Witch of Lime Street, whose iconic lives intersected at a time when science was on the verge of embracing the paranormal.

title: Rosemary: The Hidden Kennedy Daughter
author: Kate Clifford Lawson
description: Kate Clifford Larson uses newly uncovered sources to bring the story of Rosemary Kennedy—the beautifully but intellectually disabled sibling of John, Bobby and Ted—to light.

title: Death By Water
author: Kenzaburo Oe, Trans. by Deborah Boehm
description: Nobel Prize-winner Kenzaburo Oe's recurring protagonist and literary alter ego returns to his hometown village in search of a red suitcase fabled to hold documents revealing the details of his father’s death during World War II: details that will serve as the foundation for his new, and final, novel.

title: The Year of Lear
author: James Shapiro
description: Preeminent Shakespeare scholar James Shapiro shows how the tumultuous events in 1606 influenced three of Shakespeare’s greatest tragedies written that year— King Lear , Macbeth , and Antony and Cleopatra .

title: The Clasp
author: Sloane Crosley
description: This debut novel from essayist Crosley follows a circle of friends on a quest to find a priceless necklace, and regain the connection they once shared.

title: Ted Hughes: The Unauthorised Life
author: Jonathan Bate
description: A biography of the poet Ted Hughes, former Poet Laureate and widow of Sylvia Plath.

title: Katherine Carlyle
author: Rupert Thomson
description: Unmoored by her mother’s death and feeling her father to be an increasingly distant figure, Katherine Carlyle abandons the set course of her life and starts out on a mysterious journey to the ends of the world. Instead of going to college, she disappears, telling no one where she has gone.

title: Killing and Dying
author: Adrian Tomine
description: A collection of six previously published graphic stories of life's bittersweet struggles.

title: Man V. Nature
author: Diane Cook
description: These stories expose unsuspecting men and women to the realities of nature, the primal instincts of man, and the dark humor and heartbreak of our struggle to not only thrive, but survive.

title: Deep South
author: Paul Theroux
description: Setting out on a winding road trip, travel writer Paul Theroux discovers a region of architectural and artistic wonders, incomparable music, mouth-watering cuisine—and also some of the worst schools, medical care, housing, and unemployment rates in the nation.

title: Gold Fame Citrus
author: Claire Vaye Watkins
description: The story of a young couple trying to navigate a post-apocalyptic California, where severe drought has transformed the landscape into a wasteland.

title: Voyage of the Sable Venus
author: Robin Coste Lewis
description: "A triptych that begins and ends with lyric poems considering the roles desire and race play in the construction of the self."

title: Pretty Girls
author: Karin Slaughter
description: When Claire’s husband is killed, she and her estranged sister Lydia face their past and unearth the secrets that destroyed their family more than twenty years ago.

title: 1944: FDR and the Year That Changed History
author: Jay Winik
description: The author details the year 1944, which determined the outcome of World War II and put more pressure than any other on an ailing yet determined President Roosevelt.

title: The Dead Ladies Project
author: Jessa Crispin
description: When Jessa Crispin was thirty, she burned her settled Chicago life to the ground and took off for Berlin with a pair of suitcases and no plan beyond leaving. Half a decade later, she’s still on the road, in search not so much of a home as of understanding, a way of being in the world that demands neither constant struggle nor complete surrender. The Dead Ladies Project is an account of that journey.

title: The Point of Vanishing
author: Howard Axelrod
description: A lyrical memoir of two years spent in solitude after a life-changing injury.

title: Black Flags: The Rise of ISIS
author: Jody Warrick
description: Warrick traces how the strain of militant Islam behind ISIS first arose in a remote Jordanian prison and spread with the unwitting aid of two American presidents.

title: The Blue Guitar
author: John Banville
description: Oliver Otway Orme is a painter of some renown, and a petty thief who has never been caught...until now. Fearing the consequences, Olly flees and sets about trying to uncover the answer to how and why things have turned out as they did.

title: Gamelife
author: Michael W. Clune
description: Gamelife is the memoir of a childhood transformed by technology.

title: Only the Animals
author: Ceridwen Dovey
description: Ten tales are told by the souls of animals killed in human conflicts in the past century or so. Each narrator also pays homage to an author who has written imaginatively about animals during much the same time span.

title: Fates and Furies
author: Lauren Groff
description: At age twenty-two, Lotto and Mathilde are tall, glamorous, madly in love, and destined for greatness. A decade later, their marriage is still the envy of their friends, but we later understand that things are even more complicated and remarkable than they have seemed.

title: Notes on the Assemblage
author: Juan Felipe Herrera
description: "A collection of work from the nation's first Latino Poet Laureate, Juan Felipe Herrera."

title: The Art of Memoir
author: Mary Karr
description: Mary Karr synthesizes her experience as professor and therapy patient, writer and spiritual seeker, recovered alcoholic and “black belt sinner,” to examine the mechanics and art of writing a memoir.

title: The Story of My Teeth
author: Valeria Luiselli
description: Gustavo 'Turnpike' Sanchez is a man with a mission: he is planning to replace every last one of his unsightly teeth. Written in collaboration with the workers at a Jumex juice factory, Teeth is a romp through the industrial suburbs of Mexico City and Luiselli's own literary influences.

title: The Girl Who Wrote Loneliness
author: Kyung-Sook Shin
description: Homesick and alone, a teenaged girl has just arrived in Seoul to work in a factory. Her family, still in the countryside, is too impoverished to keep sending her to school, so she works long, sunless days on a stereo-assembly line, struggling through night school every evening in order to achieve her dream of becoming a writer.

title: The Invention of Nature
author: Andrea Wulf
description: Andrea Wulf reveals the forgotten life of Alexander von Humboldt, the visionary German naturalist whose ideas changed the way we see the natural world—and in the process created modern environmentalism.

title: Undermajordomo Minor
author: Patrick deWitt
description: Undermajordomo Minor is a black comedy of manners, an adventure, a mystery, and a portrayal of rural Alpine bad behavior, but above all it is a love story. And Lucy must be careful, for love is a violent thing.

title: Bright Dead Things
author: Ada Limón
description: A book of bravado and introspection, of 21st century feminist swagger and harrowing terror and loss, this fourth collection considers how we build our identities out of place and human contact—tracing in intimate detail the various ways the speaker’s sense of self both shifts and perseveres as she moves from New York City to rural Kentucky, loses a dear parent, ages past the capriciousness of youth, and falls in love.

title: So You Don't Get Lost in the Neighborhood
author: Patrick Modiano, trans. by Euan Cameron
description: From the winner of the 2014 Nobel Prize in Literature, a haunting novel of suspense in which a single, unexpected phone call to a man living quietly in Paris launches a chain of menacing encounters and events, unlocking a dark secret he had erased from memory.

title: Two Years Eight Months And Twenty-Eight Nights
author: Salman Rushdie
description: After a storm strikes New York City, the strangenesses begin. Unbeknownst to the characters, they are all descended from the whimsical, capricious, wanton creatures known as the jinn, who live in a world separated from ours by a veil.

title: Reckless: My Life as a Pretender
author: Chrissie Hynde
description: In her memoir, Chrissie Hynde tells exactly where she came from and what her crooked, winding path to stardom entailed.

title: Black Earth: The Holocaust as History and Warning
author: Timonthy Snyder
description: Based on new sources from eastern Europe and forgotten testimonies from Jewish survivors, Black Earth recounts the mass murder of the Jews as an event that is still close to us, more comprehensible than we would like to think, and thus all the more terrifying.

title: The Double Life of Liliane
author: Lily Tuck
description: Mixing family lore, historical events, and photographs, this autobiographical novel creates a portrait of the writer as a young woman.

title: This Is Your Life, Harriet Chance!
author: Jonathan Evison
description: Harriet Chance sets sail on an ill-conceived Alaskan cruise only to discover that she’s been living the past sixty years of her life under entirely false pretenses. Harriet is forced to confront the truth about pivotal events that changed the course of her life.

title: Beauty is a Wound
author: Eka Kurniawan, Trans. by Annie Tucker
description: The beautiful Indo prostitute Dewi Ayu and her four daughters are beset by incest, murder, bestiality, rape, insanity, monstrosity, and the often vengeful undead.

title: Cries For Help, Various
author: Padgett Powell
description: Padgett Powell's collection follows his mentor Donald Barthelme's advice that wacky mode must break their hearts.

title: Fear of Dying
author: Erica Jong
description: As the afternoon of life looms over Vanessa Wonderman, she watches her parents age, attends doctor appointments with her pregnant daughter, and sits by the hospital bed of her husband, Asher, fifteen years her senior. With her best years as an actress behind her, she's discovering that beginnings are easy, but endings can be hard.

title: Negroland
author: Margo Jefferson
description: Margo Jefferson's memoir on race, sex, and American culture through her upbringing and education among a black elite.

title: The Lost Landscape
author: Joyce Carol Oates
description: Joyce Carol Oates’ chronicle of her hardscrabble childhood in rural western New York State.

title: Black Man in a White Coat: A Doctor's Reflections on Race and Medicine
author: Damon Tweedy
description: Damon Tweedy's memoir of his experience grappling with race, bias, and the unique health problems of black Americans.

title: The Visiting Privilege
author: Joy Williams
description: A collection of stories by Joy Williams: thirty-three stories drawn from three collections, and another thirteen appearing here for the first time in book form.

title: A Brief History of Seven Killings
author: Marlon James
description: Winner of the 2015 Man Booker Prize Spanning decades and continents and peopled with a wide range of characters—assassins, drug dealers, journalists, and even ghosts—James brings to life the people who walked the streets of 1970s Kingston, who dominated the crack houses of 1980s New York, and who reemerged into a radically altered Jamaica of the 1990s.

title: Tram 83
author: Fiston Mwanza Mujila, trans. by Roland Glasser
description: Two friends, one a budding writer home from abroad, the other an ambitious racketeer, meet in the most notorious nightclub—Tram 83—in a war-torn city-state in secession, surrounded by profit-seekers of all languages and nationalities. Tram 83 plunges the reader into the modern African gold rush as cynical as it is comic and colorfully exotic, using jazz rhythms to weave a tale of human relationships in a world that has become a global village.

title: $2.00 a Day
author: Kathryn J. Edin and Luke Shaefer
description: An analysis of the growing portion of American poor who live on an average of $2 per day.

title: The Making of Asian America
author: Erika Lee
description: The definitive history of Asian Americans by one of the nation’s preeminent scholars on the subject.

title: The Story of the Lost Child
author: Elena Ferrante, Trans. by Ann Goldstein
description: Inexorable seismic changes—in society and in the lives of two female friends—mark the final volume of Ferrante's Neapolitan series.

title: Women Crime Writers: Eight Suspense Novels of the 1940s & 1950s
author: Sarah Weinman
description: Eight suspense novels by female writers of the 1940s & 50s.

title: The Girl in the Spider's Web
author: David Lagercrantz
description: She is the girl with the dragon tattoo—a genius hacker and uncompromising misfit. He is a crusading journalist whose championing of the truth often brings him to the brink of prosecution.

title: You Too Can Have a Body Like Mine
author: Alexandra Kleeman
description: A postmodernist novel reminiscent of The Crying of Lot 49 , White Noise , and City of Glass that is at once a missing-person mystery, an exorcism of modern culture, and a wholly singular vision of contemporary womanhood.

title: NeuroTribes: The Legacy of Autism and the Future of Neurodiversity
author: Steve Silberman
description: A popular science book which upends conventional thinking about autism and suggests a broader model for acceptance, understanding, and full participation in society for people who think differently.

title: The Things We Don't Do
author: Andrés Neuman, Trans. by Nick Caistor and Lorenza Garcia
description: Andrés Neuman's thirty-four short stories consider love, lechery, history, mortality, family secrets, therapy, Borges, mysterious underwear, translators, and storytelling itself.

title: The Complete Stories
author: Clarice Lispector, Trans. by Katrina Dodson
description: Now, for the first time in English, are all the stories that made Clarice Lispector a Brazilian legend: from teenagers coming into awareness of their sexual and artistic powers to humdrum housewives whose lives are shattered by unexpected epiphanies to old people who don’t know what to do with themselves. Clarice’s stories take us through their lives―and ours.

title: Eileen
author: Ottessa Moshfegh
description: A woman recalls her mysterious escape from home in this intense, creepy noir about broken families and their proximity to violence.

title: Fortune Smiles
author: Adam Johnson
description: The National Book Award winning short story collection from the author of The Orphan Master's Son .

title: A Manual for Cleaning Women
author: Lucia Berlin
description: A compilation of the best work of the recently rediscovered short story writer Lucia Berlin.

title: The Beautiful Bureaucrat
author: Sally Phillips
description: In a windowless building in a remote part of town, the newly employed Josephine inputs an endless string of numbers into something known only as The Database. As the days inch by, and the files stack up, Josephine feels increasingly anxious in her surroundings. When one evening her husband Joseph disappears and then returns, offering no explanation as to his whereabouts, her creeping unease shifts decidedly to dread.

title: Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki and His Years of Pilgrimage
author: Haruki Murakami
description: Haruki Murakami turns in a trademark story that blends the commonplace with the nightmarish in a Japan full of hollow men.

title: Katrina: After the Flood
author: Gary Rivlin
description: Ten years in the making, Katrina tells the stories of New Orleanians of all stripes as they confront the aftermath of one of the great tragedies of our age.

title: An Indigenous Peoples' History of the United States
author: Roxanne Dunbar-Ortiz
description: 2015 Winner of the American Book Award. Acclaimed historian and activist Roxanne Dunbar-Ortiz offers a history of the United States told from the perspective of Indigenous peoples and reveals how Native Americans, for centuries, actively resisted expansion of the US empire.

title: Panic in a Suitcase
author: Yelena Akhtiorskaya
description: Having left Odessa for Brighton Beach, Brooklyn, with a sense of finality, the Nasmertov family has discovered that the divide between the old world and the new is not nearly as clear-cut as they had imagined. With the collapse of the Soviet Union, returning is just a matter of a plane ticket, and the Russian-owned shops in their adopted neighborhood stock even the most obscure comforts of home. Pursuing the American Dream once meant giving up everything, but does the dream still work if the past refuses to grow distant and mythical, remaining alarmingly within reach?

title: The Fifth Season
author: N K Jemisin
description: In a post-apocalyptic world plagued by natural diasters, Essun lives in a small comunity barricaded against the outside world. When her husband relizes that she and her children are orogenes with the ability to manipulate seismic energy, he kills their son and kidnaps their daughter. Against the backdrop of the end of the world, Essun follows, beginning an odyssey which will not end until her daughter is safe.

title: All My Puny Sorrows
author: Miriam Toews
description: Winner of the Rogers Writers' Trust Fiction Prize in 2014. Elf and Yoli are sisters. While on the surface Elfrieda's is an enviable life and Yolandi's is a mess, they are fiercely close, raised in a Mennonite household and sharing the hardship of Elf's desire to end her own life. After Elf's latest attempt, Yoli must quickly determine how to keep her family from falling apart, how to keep her own heart from breaking, and what it means to love someone who wants to die.

title: Barbarian Days: A Surfing Life
author: William Finnegan
description: The Pulitzer Prize–winning autobiography about Finnegan's life-long love of surfing.

title: Land of Love and Drowning
author: Tiphanie Yanique
description: Chronicling three generations of the Bradshaw family and set against the emergence of Saint Thomas into the modern world, follows one island family from 1916 into the 1970s, through sixty years of fathers and daughters, mothers and sons, love affairs, curses, magical gifts, loyalties, births, deaths, and triumphs.

title: Between the World and Me
author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
description: Part memoir, part analysis of America's racial history, part investigation of the country's current crisis, all framed as a letter to Coates' son.

title: Go Set a Watchman
author: Harper Lee
description: Simultaneously the sequel and the original draft of the Pulitzer Prize winning classic To Kill a Mockingbird , this novel follows a 26 year old Jean Louise Finch ("Scout") as she returns home to Maycomb, Alabama to visit her aging father, Atticus. Set against the backdrop of the civil rights movement and the political turmoil that were transforming the South, Jean Louise’s homecoming turns bittersweet when she learns disturbing truths about her close-knit family, the town, and the people dearest to her.

title: Blackout: Remembering the Things I Drank to Forget
author: Sarah Hepola
description: A comic but poignant memoir about the author's history of heavy drinking and decision to get sober.

title: The Cartel
author: Don Winslow
description: The Cartel is a story of revenge, honor, and sacrifice, as one man tries to face down the devil without losing his soul. It is the story of the war on drugs and the men—and women—who wage it.

title: In the Country
author: Mia Alvar
description: Nine stories about exiles, emigrants, and wanderers uprooting their families from the Philippines to begin new lives in the Middle East, the United States, and elsewhere.

title: Heaven
author: Rowan Ricardo Phillips
description: Swerving from humor to heartbreak, from Colorado to Florida, from Dante's Paradise to Homer's Iliad , from knowledge to ignorance to awe, Phillips turns his gaze upward and outward, probing and upending notions of the beyond.

title: The Seven Good Years
author: Etgar Keret
description: A memoir, Etgar’s first nonfiction book published in America. The seven years between the birth of Etgar Keret’s son and the death of his father were good years, though still full of reasons to worry. Lev is born in the midst of a terrorist attack. Etgar’s father gets cancer. The threat of constant war looms over their home and permeates daily life.

title: Modern Romance
author: Aziz Ansari & Eric Klinenberg
description: An in-depth exploration of the pleasures and perils of modern romance from comedian Aziz Ansari.

title: The Hopeful
author: Tracy O'Neill
description: A figure skating prodigy, sixteen-year old Alivopro Doyle is one of a few "hopefuls" racing against nature's clock to try and jump and spin their way into the Olympics. But when a disastrous fall fractures two vertebrae, leaving Ali addicted to painkillers and ultimately institutionalized, it's not just her dreams of glory that get torn asunder, but the very fabric that holds her fragile family together.

title: The Sleepwalker's Guide to Dancing
author: Mira Jacob
description: Celebrated brain surgeon Thomas Eapen has been sitting on his porch, talking to dead relatives. At least that is the story his wife, Kamala, prone to exaggeration, tells their daughter, Amina, a photographer living in Seattle. Reluctantly Amina returns home and finds a situation that is far more complicated than her mother let on, with roots in a trip the family, including Amina’s rebellious brother Akhil, took to India twenty years earlier.

title: The Meursault Investigation
author: Kamel Daoud, trans. by John Cullen
description: He was the brother of “the Arab” killed by the infamous Meursault, the antihero of Camus’s classic novel. Seventy years after that event, Harun, who has lived since childhood in the shadow of his sibling’s memory, refuses to let him remain anonymous: he gives his brother a story and a name—Musa—and describes the events that led to Musa’s casual murder on a dazzlingly sunny beach.

title: Dietland
author: Sarai Walker
description: A novel about a reclusive young woman saving up for weight loss surgery when she gets drawn into a shadowy feminist guerilla group that doles out vigilante justice to misogynists.

title: Mislaid
author: Nell Fink
description: Freshman Peggy, falls under the spell of Lee, a blue-blooded poet and professor, and they begin an affair, leading to an unplanned pregnancy and marriage. The couple are mismatched from the start—she’s a lesbian, he’s gay—but it takes a decade of emotional erosion before Peggy runs off with their three-year-old daughter, leaving their nine-year-old son behind. Worried that Lee will have her committed for her erratic behavior, Peggy goes underground, adopting an African-American persona for her and her daughter. Eventually the long lost siblings will find each other, setting off a series of misunderstandings and culminating in a comedic finale worthy of Shakespeare

title: The Odd Woman and the City: A Memoir
author: Vivian Gornick
description: A memoir of self-discovery and the dilemma of connection in our time, The Odd Woman and the City explores the rhythms, chance encounters, and ever-changing friendships of urban life that forge the sensibility of a fiercely independent woman who has lived out her conflicts, not her fantasies, in a city that has done the same.

title: Girl at War
author: Sara Novic
description: A novel about a girl’s coming of age—and how her sense of family, friendship, love, and belonging is profoundly shaped by the war that broke out across Yugoslavia in the early 1990s.

title: Hold Still
author: Sally Mann
description: In this memoir, a unique interplay of narrative and image, renowned photographer Sally Mann explores the subjects of her life and art: family, race, mortality, and the storied landscape of the American South, as well as the family history that precedes her.

title: The Argonauts
author: Maggie Nelson
description: A genre-beniding memoir about the author's relationship with the artist Harry Dodge, and a voyage out to the frontiers of the latest thinking about love, language, and family.

title: A God in Ruins
author: Kate Atkinson
description: In the companion novel to Life After Life , Ursula’s beloved younger brother Teddy – would-be poet, heroic pilot, husband, father, and grandfather – navigates the perils and progress of a rapidly changing world.

title: My Struggle: Book 3
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard
description: A family of four―mother, father, and two boys―move to the south coast of Norway, to a new house. It is the early 1970s and the family's trajectory is upwardly mobile: the future seems limitless. In painstaking detail, Karl Ove Knausgaard paints a world familiar to anyone who can recall the intensity and novelty of childhood experience, one in which children and adults lead parallel lives that never meet.

title: Missoula: Rape and the Justice System in a College Town
author: Jon Krakauer
description: Journalist Jon Krakauer investigates a spate of campus rapes that occurred in Missoula over a four-year period. Taking the town as a case study for a crime that is sadly prevalent throughout the nation, Krakauer documents the experiences of five victims.

title: Spinster: Making a Life of One's Own
author: Kate Bolick
description: Journalist and cultural critic Kate Bolick examines the pleasures and possibilities of remaining single, and looks at the lives of five pioneering single women from the last century.

title: God Help the Child
author: Toni Morrison
description: A little girl is born with skin so black her mother will not touch her. Desperate for approval, to just once have her mother take her hand, she tells a lie that puts an innocent schoolteacher in jail for decades.

title: Sphinx
author: Anne Garréta, Trans. by Emma Ramadan
description: A beautiful and complex love story between two characters, the narrator, "I," and their lover, A***, written without using any gender markers to refer to the main characters.

title: Dreamland: The True Tale of America's Opiate Epidemic
author: Sam Quinones
description: From a small town in Mexico to the boardrooms of Big Pharma to main streets nationwide, comes an explosive and shocking account of addiction in the heartland of America. The 2015 National Book Critics Circle Award Winner for Nonfiction.

title: The Turner House
author: Angela Flournoy
description: When their powerful mother falls ill, the Turners are called home to decide the fate of their East Detroit house, and to reckon with how their past haunts—and shapes—their future.

title: Voices in the Night
author: Steven Millhauser
description: From the Pulitzer and Story Prize winner: 16 new stories that delve into the secret lives and desires of ordinary people, alongside retellings of myths and legends that highlight the aspirations of the human spirit.

title: Gutshot
author: Amelia Gray
description: A woman creeps through the ductwork of a quiet home. A medical procedure reveals an object of worship. A carnivorous reptile divides and cauterizes a town. Amelia Gray's curio cabinet expands in Gutshot , where isolation and coupling are pushed to their dark and outrageous edges.

title: The Sympathizer
author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
description: The Pulitzer Prize winning novel about a communist double agent who arranges to come to America after the Fall of Saigon, and while building a new life with other Vietnamese refugees in Los Angeles is secretly reporting back to his communist superiors in Vietnam.

title: The Folded Clock: A Diary
author: Heidi Julavits
description: In which the diary form becomes a meditation on time and self, youth and aging, betrayal and loyalty, friendship and romance, faith and fate, marriage and family, desire and death, gossip and secrets, art and ambition.

title: The Architect's Apprentice
author: Elif Shafak
description: Following the life of an invented apprentice to the actual Ottoman Empire architect Sinan, Turkish novelist Shafak offers a liberal interpretation of Islam.

title: A Little Life
author: Hanya Yanagihara
description: A Little Life follows four college classmates as they move to New York in search of fame and fortune. While their relationships, which are tinged by addiction, success, and pride, deepen over the decades, the men are held together by their devotion to the brilliant, enigmatic Jude, a man scarred by an unspeakable childhood trauma.

title: The Dream of My Return
author: Horacio Castellanos Moya
description: High-octane paranoia deranges a writer and fuels a dangerous plan to return home at the tail end of El Salvador's long civil war. Is the plan a dream or a nightmare? Is he courageous, foolhardy, or just plain dumb? Is the bubbling brew of horrors and threats actual or imagined?

title: The Buried Giant
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: In his tenth novel, Nobel Prize and Man Booker Prize–winner Kazoo Ishiguro wrote a lyrical, allusive (and elusive) voyage into the mists of British folklore.

title: H Is for Hawk
author: Helen Macdonald
description: Following the sudden death of her father, Macdonald tried to deal with her grief with a unique form of personal therapy: the purchase and training of an English goshawk.

title: The Sellout
author: Paul Beatty
description: Winner of the 2016 Man Book Prize. A biting, uproarious racial satire about a young man's isolated upbringing and the race trial that sends him to the Supreme Court.

title: Signs Preceding the End of the World
author: Yuri Herrera, trans. by Lisa Dillman
description: Yuri Herrera does not simply write about the border between Mexico and the United States and those who cross it. He explores the crossings and translations people make in their minds and language as they move from one country to another, especially when there’s no going back.

title: Call Me Home
author: Megan Kruse
description: Braiding the stories of a family in three distinct voices, 5 Under 35 Honoree Megan Kruse crafts a novel about family, our choices and how we come to live with them, what it means to be queer in the rural West, and the changing idea of home.

title: Young Skins
author: Colin Barrett
description: Winner of the Frank O'Connor International Short Story Award, the Guardian First Book Award, and the Rooney Prize for Irish Literature. Enter the small, rural town of Glanbeigh, a place whose fate took a downturn with the Celtic Tiger, a desolate spot where buffoonery and tension simmer and erupt, and booze-sodden boredom fills the corners of every pub and nightclub. Here, and in the towns beyond, the young live hard and wear the scars.

title: S O S: Poems 1961-2013
author: Amiri Baraka
description: Comprises the fullest spectrum of Baraka's rousing, revolutionary poems, from his first collection to previously unpublished pieces composed during his final years.

title: Breath, Eyes, Memory
author: Edwidge Danticat
description: At the age of twelve, Sophie Caco is sent from her impoverished Haitian village to New York to be reunited with a mother she barely remembers. There she discovers secrets that no child should ever know, and a legacy of shame that can be healed only when she returns to Haiti—to the women who first reared her. What ensues is a passionate journey through a landscape charged with the supernatural and scarred by political violence.

title: From the New World: Poems 1976-2014
author: Jorie Graham
description: "A volume of poems, selected from almost four decades of work, that tracks the evolution of Pulitzer Prize-winner Jorie Graham."

title: Jillian
author: Halle Butler
description: Megan, recently out of college and working a meaningless job as a gastroenterologist's secretary, openly hates all of her friends for being happy and successful. She makes herself feel better by obsessively critiquing the behavior of her coworker, Jillian, a rapid cycling, grotesque optimist, whose downfall is precipitated by the purchase of a dog.

title: Bird Box
author: Josh Malerman
description: In an apocalyptic near-future, a mother and her two small children must make their way down a river, blindfolded. One wrong choice and they will die. And something is following them -- but is it man, animal, or monster?

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: One hundred thousand years ago, at least six different species of humans inhabited Earth. Yet today there is only one—homo sapiens. What happened to the others? And what may happen to us? Most books about the history of humanity pursue either a historical or a biological approach, but Dr. Yuval Noah Harari breaks the mold with this book that begins about 70,000 years ago with the appearance of modern cognition. From examining the role evolving humans have played in the global ecosystem to charting the rise of empires, Sapiens integrates history and science to reconsider accepted narratives, connect past developments with contemporary concerns, and examine specific events within the context of larger ideas.

title: Do Everything in the Dark
author: Gary Indiana
description: Gary Indiana’s newest autopsy of America’s walking dead examines the tragicomic fate of la vie boheme when its cherished delusions and brightest hopes succumb to the harsh realities of the aging process.

title: Get in Trouble
author: Kelly Link
description: Kelly Link draws from myth, urban legend and genre fiction in this collection of short stories.

title: The Nightingale
author: Kristin Hannah
description: Hannah’s novel is an homage to the extraordinary courage and endurance of Frenchwomen during World War II.

title: Ghettoside: A True Story of Murder in America
author: Jill Leovy
description: A Los Angeles Times reporter looks at the thinly veiled racist origins of violence in South Central LA.

title: The Door
author: Magda Szabo, Trans. by Len Rix
description: An unsettling exploration of the relationship between two very different women living under Hungary's Communist regime.

title: The Girl on the Train
author: Paula Hawkins
description: Rachel sees something shocking through the window of the train. Soon she is deeply entangled not only in the police investigation but in the lives of everyone involved. Has she done more harm than good?

title: Outline
author: Rachel Cusk
description: A novel in ten conversations, Outline follows a novelist teaching a course in creative writing over an oppressively hot summer in Athens.

title: The First Bad Man
author: Miranda July
description: Cheryl is a tightly-wound, vulnerable woman who lives alone, with a perpetual lump in her throat. She is haunted by a baby boy she met when she was six, who sometimes recurs as other people’s babies. Cheryl is also obsessed with Phillip, a philandering board member at the women’s self-defense nonprofit where she works. When Cheryl’s bosses ask if their twenty-one-year-old daughter, Clee, can move into her house for a little while, Cheryl’s eccentrically ordered world explodes. And yet it is Clee—the selfish, cruel blond bombshell—who bullies Cheryl into reality and, unexpectedly, provides her the love of a lifetime.

title: Catalog of Unabashed Gratitude
author: Ross Gay
description: Catalog of Unabashed Gratitude is a sustained meditation on that which goes away - loved ones, the seasons, the earth as we know it - that tries to find solace in the processes of the garden and the orchard. That is, this is a book that studies the wisdom of the garden and orchard, those places where all - death, sorrow, loss - is converted into what might, with patience, nourish us. Winner of the 2015 National Book Critics Circle Award.

title: The Man Who Loved Dogs
author: Leonardo Padura, trans. by Anna Kushner
description: Leonardo Padura brings a noir sensibility to the assassination of Leon Trotsky by Ramón Mercader in this multilayered epic that weaves together three different plot threads ― Trotsky in exile, Ramón in pursuit, Iván in frustrated stasis ― to bring emotional truth to historical fact.

author: Ben Lerner
description: A self-referential and metafictional novel that explores sex, friendship, medicine, memory, art, and politics, and examines the role of fiction in everyday life.

title: How to Be Both
author: Ali Smith
description: Winner of the Bailey's Women's Prize for Fiction, the Costa Award, and the Goldsmiths Prize Borrowing from painting’s fresco technique to make an original literary double-take, is a fast-moving genre-bending conversation between forms, times, truths and fictions. Two tales of love and injustice twist into a singular yarn where time gets timeless, structural gets playful, knowing gets mysterious, fictional gets real—and all life’s givens get given a second chance.

title: Clothes, Clothes, Clothes. Music, Music, Music. Boys, Boys, Boys.
author: VIV Albertine
description: A feminist musician icon, Viv Albertine reveals the rocking, uncompromising story of her life on the front lines at the birth of the British punk movement and beyond.

title: Self-Portrait in Green
author: Marie Ndiaye, trans. by Jordan Stump
description: Asked to write her memoir, Marie Ndiaye published this paranoid fantasia of rising floodwaters, walking corpses, eerie depictions of her very own parents, and the incessant reappearance of women in green. This is an exploration of how we form our identities, how we discover those things we repress, and how our obsessions become us.

title: Loitering: New and Collected Essays
author: Charles D'Ambrosio
description: Charles D’Ambrosio’s essay collection Orphans spawned something of a cult following. Loitering gathers those eleven original essays with new and previously uncollected work, so that a broader audience might discover one of our great living essayists. A New York Times Notable Book and Winner of the Washington State Book Prize

title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Cixin Liu
description: This near-future trilogy is the first chance for English-speaking readers to experience this multiple-award-winning phenemonenon from China's most beloved science fiction author. When a secret military project sends signals into space, an alien civilization captures the signal and plans to invade Earth. Meanwhile, on Earth, different camps start forming, planning to either welcome the superior beings and help them take over a world seen as corrupt, or to fight against the invasion.

title: The Book of Strange New Things
author: Michel Faber
description: Michel Faber’s The Book of Strange New Things is a powerful examination of humanity that follows a Christian pastor sent to work with aliens in a neighbouring galaxy.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: Six days ago, astronaut Mark Watney became one of the first people to walk on Mars. Now, he's sure he'll be the first person to die there. After a dust storm nearly kills him and forces his crew to evacuate while thinking him dead, Mark finds himself stranded and completely alone with no way to even signal Earth that he’s alive—and even if he could get word out, his supplies would be gone long before a rescue could arrive.

title: Just Mercy: A Story of Justice and Redemption
author: Bryan Stevenson
description: In this Carnegie Award-winning book, the founder of the Equal Justice Initiative explores one of his first cases—that of Walter McMillian, a young black man sentenced to die for the murder of a white woman he didn't commit—and its web of conspiracy, political machination, and legal brinksmanship that transformed his understanding of mercy and justice forever.

title: Lila
author: Marilynne Robinson
description: Winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award for Fiction The third of the Gilead novels, Lila is the story of a girlhood lived on the fringes of society in fear, awe, and wonder.

title: Citizen: An American Lyric
author: Claudia Rankine
description: Winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award in Poetry, the NAACP Image Award, and the PEN Open Book Award, Rankine's poetry recounts mounting racial aggressions in ongoing encounters in twenty-first-century daily life and in the media.

title: You
author: Caroline Kepnes
description: When a beautiful, aspiring writer strides into the East Village bookstore where Joe Goldberg works, he decides that he must find a way to be with her. Joe moves from stalking her on the internet to stalking her in real life, staging a series of encounters until he becomes her very creepy boyfriend.

title: On Immunity: An Inoculation
author: Eula Biss
description: Upon becoming a new mother, Eula Biss addresses a chronic condition of fear: fear of the government, the medical establishment, and what is in children's food, mattresses, medicines, and vaccines. Biss investigates the metaphors and myths surrounding the conception of immunity and its implications for the individual and the social body. As she hears more and more fears about vaccines, Biss researches what they mean for her own child, her immediate community, America, and the world. A New York Times Best Seller, National Book Critics Circle Award Finalist and a New York Times Book Review Top 10 Book of the Year.

title: The Paying Guests
author: Sarah Waters
description: In 1922 London, impoverished widow Mrs. Wray and her spinster daughter, Frances, are obliged to take in lodgers. With the arrival of Lilian and Leonard Barber, a modern young couple of the “clerk class,” the routines of the house are shaken up in unexpected ways.

title: Broken Monsters
author: Lauren Beukes
description: A criminal mastermind creates violent tableaus in abandoned Detroit warehouses in Lauren Beukes's genre-bending novel of suspense.

title: The Noonday Demon: An Atlas of Depression
author: Andrew Solomon
description: Andrew Solomon's National Book Award-winning and bestselling treatise on depression.

title: Love Me Back
author: Merritt Tierce
description: Marie is a waitress at an upscale Dallas steakhouse, attuned to the appetites of her patrons and gifted at hiding her private struggle as a young single mother behind an easy smile and a crisp white apron. It’s a world of long hours and late nights, and Marie often gives in to self-destructive impulses, losing herself in a tangle of bodies and urgent highs as her desire for obliteration competes with a stubborn will to survive. A Chicago Tribune, Electric Literature, BookRiot Best Book of the Year, and Whiting Award Winner.

title: This Changes Everything: Capitalism vs. the Climate
author: Naomi Klein
description: From the author of the international bestseller The Shock Doctrine , an explanation of why the climate crisis challenges us to abandon the core “free market” ideology of our time, restructure the global economy, and remake our political systems.

title: A Girl is a Half-Formed Thing
author: Eimear McBride
description: Winner of the Baileys Women's Prize for Fiction and the Goldsmiths Prize The story of a young woman's relationship with her brother, and the long shadow cast by his childhood brain tumor, touching on everything from family violence to sexuality and the personal struggle to remain intact in times of intense trauma.

title: Those Who Leave and Those Who Stay
author: Elena Ferrante
description: In the third installment of the Neapolitan Quartet, Elena and Lila are independent women who struggle with all that their womanhood entails – motherhood, career, poverty, success, heartbreak – and continue to be inexorably bound to each other.

title: The Bone Clocks
author: David Mitchell
description: An unsolved mystery will echo through every decade of Holly’s life, affecting all the people Holly loves—even the ones who are not yet born.

title: The Secret Place
author: Tana French
description: Detective Stephen Moran has been waiting for his chance to join Dublin’s Murder Squad when 16-year-old Holly Mackey arrives in his office with a photo of a popular boy whose body was found at a girls’ boarding school a year earlier. Stephen joins with Detective Antoinette Conway to reopen the case—beneath the watchful eye of Holly’s father, fellow detective Frank Mackey—and discovers an underworld of teenage girls that turns out to be more dangerous than the detectives imagined.

title: Braiding Sweetgrass
author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
description: Drawing on her life as an indigenous scientist, and as a woman, Kimmerer shows how other living beings―asters and goldenrod, strawberries and squash, salamanders, algae, and sweetgrass―offer us gifts and lessons, even if we've forgotten how to hear their voices. In reflections that range from the creation of Turtle Island to the forces that threaten its flourishing today, she circles toward a central argument: that the awakening of ecological consciousness requires the acknowledgment and celebration of our reciprocal relationship with the rest of the living world.

title: Stone Mattress: Nine Tales
author: Margaret Atwood
description: A book of nine tales focused on the dark obsession of aging and lingering regrets of one's youth.

title: The Miniaturist
author: Jessie Burton
description: Set in Amsterdam in 1686, the illustrious merchant trader Johannes Brandt presents his young bride with a cabinet-sized replica of their home – a gift that helps Nella to pierce the closed world of the household and to uncover its unusual secrets.

title: The Narrow Road to the Deep North
author: Richard Flanagan
description: Winner of the Man Booker Prize Moving from a Japanese POW camp to present-day Australia, from the experiences of Dorrigo Evans and his fellow prisoners to that of the Japanese guards, The Narrow Road to the Deep North tells a story of the many forms of love and death, of war and truth, as one man comes of age, prospers, only to discover all that he has lost.

title: Bad Feminist
author: Roxane Gay
description: A collection of essays spanning politics, criticism, and feminism that looks at the ways in which the culture we consume becomes who we are, and a call-to-arms of all the ways we still need to do better.

title: White Girls
author: Hilton Als
description: In pieces that hairpin between critique and meditation, fiction and nonfiction, high culture and low, the theoretical and the deeply personal, Als presents a portrait of a writer by way of his subjects, and a guide to the culture of our time.

title: Big Little Lies
author: Liane Moriarty
description: In a story of three women at a crossroads in their lives, Big Little Lies takes on ex-husbands and second wives, mothers and daughters, schoolyard scandal, and the dangerous little lies we tell ourselves just to survive.

title: We Should All Be Feminists
author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
description: In this book-length essay, the Nigerian author of Americanah aims to give a nuanced definition of feminism for the 21st century.

title: A Man Called Ove
author: Fredrik Backman
description: Ove, a grumpy yet lovable man, finds his solitary world turned on its head when a boisterous young family moves in next door.

title: California
author: Edan Lepucki
description: In a frighteningly realistic near future, Cal and Frida leave behind a crumbling Los Angeles in search of a secure community to raise a child and must quickly decide whom they can trust.

title: Nobody Is Ever Missing
author: Catherine Lacey
description: Without telling her family, Elyria takes a one-way flight to New Zealand, abruptly leaving her stable but unfulfilling life in Manhattan. As her husband scrambles to figure out what happened to her, Elyria hurtles into the unknown, testing fate by hitchhiking, tacitly being swept into the lives of strangers, and sleeping in fields, forests, and public parks. Her risky and often surreal encounters with the people and wildlife of New Zealand propel Elyria deeper into her deteriorating mind.

title: A Brave Man Seven Storeys Tall
author: Will Chancellor
description: A literary debut that introduces Owen Burr an Olympian whose dreams of greatness are dashed and then transformed by an epic journey and his father, Professor Joseph Burr, who must travel the world to find his son.

title: The Silkworm
author: Robert Galbraith
description: In the second book of the Cormoran Strike series, novelist Owen Quine is found brutally murdered after completing a manuscript featuring poisonous pen-portraits of almost everyone he knows.

title: Everything I Never Told You
author: Celeste Ng
description: Celeste Ng's debut novel begins with the death of a teenage girl and then uses the mysterious circumstances of her drowning as a springboard to dive into the troubled waters beneath the calm surface of her Chinese-American family.

title: I Am Having So Much Fun Here Without You
author: Courtney Maum
description: Despite the success of his first solo show in Paris and the support of his brilliant French wife and young daughter, thirty-four-year-old British artist Richard Haddon is too busy mourning the loss of his American mistress to appreciate his fortune. But after Richard discovers that a painting he originally made for his wife, Anne—when they were first married and deeply in love—has sold, it shocks him back to reality and he resolves to reinvest wholeheartedly in his family life…just in time for his wife to learn the extent of his affair. Rudderless and remorseful, Richard embarks on a series of misguided attempts to win Anne back while focusing his creative energy on a provocative art piece to prove that he’s still the man she once loved.

title: My Struggle: Book 2
author: Karl Ove Knausgaard, trans. by Don Bartlett
description: In the second installment of Karl Ove Knausgaard's six-volume series, Karl Ove moves to Stockholm, where, having left his wife, he leads a solitary existence. He strikes up a deep friendship with another exiled Norwegian and tracks down Linda, whom he met at a writers' workshop a few years earlier.

title: A Replacement Life
author: Boris Fishman
description: Boris Fishman makes his literary debut with this provocative, soulful, and sometimes hilarious story of a failed journalist asked to do the unthinkable: Forge Holocaust-restitution claims for old Russian Jews in Brooklyn, New York. Winner of the VCU Cabell First Novelist Award, the American Library Association's Sophie Brody Medal and a finalist for the National Jewish Book Award. Finalist for the National Jewish Book Award

title: The Beast
author: Oscar Martinez, trans. by Daniela Maria Ugaz and John B. Washington
description: One day a few years ago, 300 migrants were kidnapped between the remote desert towns of Altar, Mexico, and Sasabe, Arizona. A local priest got 120 released, many with broken ankles and other marks of abuse, but the rest vanished. Óscar Martínez, a young writer from El Salvador, was in Altar soon after the abduction, and his account of the migrant disappearances is only one of the harrowing stories he garnered from two years spent traveling up and down the migrant trail from Central America and across the US border.

title: Motherland Fatherland Homelandsexuals
author: Patricia Lockwood
description: Colloquial and incantatory, the poems in Patricia Lockwood’s second collection address the most urgent questions of our time, like: Is America going down on Canada? What happens when Niagara Falls gets drunk at a wedding? Is it legal to marry a stuffed owl exhibit? Why isn’t anyone named Gary anymore? Did the Hatfield and McCoy babies ever fall in love? The steep tilt of Lockwood’s lines sends the reader snowballing downhill, accumulating pieces of the scenery with every turn.

title: Lost for Words
author: Edward St. Aubyn
description: From the author of the Patrick Melrose novels comes a send-up of a certain major literary award, satirizing both the literary establishment and the writers who crave its attention.

title: The Son
author: Jo Nesbø
description: When Sonny learns a stunning, long-hidden secret concerning his father, he makes a brilliantly executed escape from prison—and from the person he’d let himself become—and begins hunting down those responsible for the crimes against him.

title: Faces in the Crowd
author: Valeria Luiselli, Trans. by Christina MacSweeney
description: This winner of the Los Angeles Times Art Seidenbaum Award for First Fiction addresses the perils of literary translation in a novel of collapsing narratives and perspectives, moving readers around the last century in Mexico City, New York, and Philadelphia.

title: Age of Ambition: Chasing Fortune, Truth, and Faith in the New China
author: Evan Osnos
description: A Beijing correspondent for The New Yorker describes the clash in China between the rise of the individual and the Communist Party's struggle to retain control. He follows the stories of everyday people and reveals life in the new China to be a battleground between aspiration and authoritarianism, in which only one can prevail.

title: Remember Me Like This
author: Bret Anthony Johnston
description: Four years have passed since Justin Campbell’s disappearance, a tragedy that rocked the small town of Southport, Texas. Then, one afternoon, the impossible happens. The police call to report that Justin has been found only miles away, in the neighboring town. Though the reunion is a miracle, Justin’s homecoming exposes the deep rifts that have diminished his family, the wounds they all carry that may never fully heal. When a reversal of fortune lays bare the family’s greatest fears—and offers perhaps the only hope for recovery—each of them must fight to keep the ties that bind them from permanently tearing apart. Named one of the best books of the year by The New York Times Book Review, Esquire and BookPage.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
author: Anthony Doerr
description: Winner of the 2015 Pulitzer Prize A blind French girl and an albino German boy cross paths in occupied France as both try to survive the devastation of World War II.

title: An Untamed State
author: Roxane Gay
description: Roxane Gay’s debut novel is about a woman kidnapped for ransom, her captivity as her father refuses to pay and her husband fights for her release over thirteen days, and her struggle to come to terms with the ordeal in its aftermath.

title: Men Explain Things To Me
author: Rebecca Solnit
description: The writer, historian, and activist collects here seven feminist essays tackling subjects ranging from rape culture to "mansplaining," from French sex scandals to marriage and the nuclear family, from Virginia Woolf to colonialism.

title: The Infatuations
author: Javier Marias
description: Each day before work María Dolz stops at the same café. There she finds herself drawn to a couple who is also there every morning. Observing their seemingly perfect life helps her escape the listlessness of her own. But when the man is brutally murdered and María approaches the widow to offer her condolences, what began as mere observation turns into an increasingly complicated entanglement. Winner of Spain's National Literature Prize for Narrative.

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty, trans. by Arthur Goldhammer
description: In Capital in the Twenty-First Century , Thomas Piketty analyzes a unique collection of data from twenty countries, ranging as far back as the eighteenth century, to uncover key economic and social patterns. His findings will transform debate and set the agenda for the next generation of thought about wealth and inequality.

title: The Opposite of Loneliness
author: Marina Keegan
description: The Opposite of Loneliness is a collection of essays and short stories by a Yale graduate whose untimely death at age 22 cut short a promising journalistic and literary career.

title: Family Life
author: Akhil Sharma
description: Winner of the International Dublin Literary Award The Mishra family finds American life extraordinary until tragedy strikes, leaving one son severely brain-damaged and the other lost and virtually orphaned in a strange land.

title: The Empathy Exams: Essays
author: Leslie Jamison
description: Winner of the 2011 Graywolf Press Nonfiction Prize, this debut essay collection blends memoir, journalism, and philosophical meditation to address addiction, poverty tourism, strange physical ailments, mental health, and other subjects swirling around the subject of physical and psychic pain.

title: The Goblin Emperor
author: Katherine Addison
description: The youngest, half-goblin son of the Emperor has lived his entire life in exile, distant from the Imperial Court and the deadly intrigue that suffuses it. But when his father and three sons in line for the throne are killed in an 'accident,' he has no choice but to take his place as the only surviving rightful heir.

title: Encounters at the Heart of the World: A History of the Mandan People
author: Elizabeth A. Fenn
description: This Pulitzer Prize-winning history pieces together new discoveries in archaeology, anthropology, geology, climatology, epidemiology, and nutritional science to create a picture of the Plains Indian people, who—despite their busy towns along the upper Missouri River being for centuries central to the North American universe—have been largely forgotten.

title: Boy, Snow, Bird
author: Helen Oyeyemi
description: A reimagining of the Snow White story set in the United States during the 1950s and 1960s exploring family secrets, race, beauty, and vanity.

title: Redeployment
author: Phil Klay
description: Winner of the National Book Award for Fiction These twelve stories take readers to the frontlines of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, narrated by characters who struggle to make meaning out of chaos.

title: An Unnecessary Woman
author: Rabih Alameddine
