description: The intergenerational story of two North London families that are fundamentally intertwined, capturing an empire’s worth of cultural identity, history, and hope.

title: Being Dead
author: Jim Crace
description: Winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award In a narrative that moves backward from the moment of Joseph and Celine’s murders, Crace describes in minute detail the decisions that led up to it and their gradual return to the land.

title: In America
author: Susan Sontag
description: Winner of the National Book Award for Fiction In 1876 a group of Poles led by Maryna Zalezowska, Poland's greatest actress, emigrate to the United States and travel to California to found a “utopian commune.” When the commune fails, Maryna stays, learns English, and—as Marina Zalenska—forges a new, even more triumphant career on the American stage

title: House of Leaves
author: Mark Z. Danielewski
description: A young family discovers that their new house is bigger on the inside then it is on the outside and is forced to face the consequences of that impossibility.

title: A Heartbreaking Work of Staggering Genius
author: Dave Eggers
description: The memoir of a college senior who, in the space of five weeks, loses both of his parents to cancer and inherits his eight-year-old brother. A debut work that is a comical and experimental story of the love that holds a family together.

title: Amsterdam
author: Ian McEwan
description: From the acclaimed author of Atonement , the Booker Prize-winning contemporary morality tale (cleverly disguised as a comic novel) about two men and a plan to die.

title: King Leopold's Ghost: A Story of Greed, Terror, and Heroism in Colonial Africa
author: Adam Hochschild
description: In the 1880s, as the European powers were carving up Africa, King Leopold II of Belgium seized for himself the vast and mostly unexplored territory surrounding the Congo River. Carrying out a genocidal plundering of the Congo, he looted its rubber, brutalized its people, and ultimately slashed its population by ten million—all the while shrewdly cultivating his reputation as a great humanitarian. Heroic efforts to expose these crimes eventually led to the first great human rights movement of the twentieth century, in which everyone from Mark Twain to the Archbishop of Canterbury participated.

title: Motherless Brooklyn
author: Jonathan Lethem
description: When Lionel Essrogg's longtime mentor, Minna Frank is murdered, Lionel must turn detective, and find the killer—without letting his Tourette's get in the way. As Lionel untangles the complex, shadowy web of relationships, threats, and favors that make up the Brooklyn world he thought he knew so well, he finds that no one is who they seem.

title: Angela's Ashes
author: Frank McCourt
description: A Pulitzer Prize–winning memoir of Frank McCourt’s childhood, from Depression-era Brooklyn to the slums of Limerick, Ireland.

title: Freedom from Fear
author: David M Kennedy
description: The ninth volume in the Oxford History of the United States series and a Pulitzer Prize-winner, Kennedy's narrative spans the Great Depression, FDR's New Deal, and the Second World War.

title: Vera (Mrs. Vladimir Nabokov): Portrait of a Marriage
author: Stacy Schiff
description: This Pulitzer Prize-winning biography offers a portrait of Vera Nabokov, the woman who stood at the center of the life and work of the controversial author of Lolita , drawing on Vladimir's letters, Vera's diaries, and family correspondence.

title: Embracing Defeat: Japan in the Wake of World War II
author: John W Dower
description: Winner of the Pulitzer Prize, the 1999 National Book Award for Nonfiction, finalist for the Lionel Gelber Prize and the Kiriyama Pacific Rim Book Prize, Embracing Defeat is John W. Dower's examination of Japan in the immediate, shattering aftermath of World War II.

title: The Poisonwood Bible
author: Barbara Kingsolver
description: Barbara Kingsolver's novel, The Poisonwood Bible , is a large-scale saga of an American family’s enlightening and disillusioning African adventure.

title: Enduring Love
author: Ian McEwan
description: After attempting to rescue a child from a runaway hot-air balloon, Joe Rose finds himself part of a living nightmare of suspicion and obsession. From the bestselling author of The Innocent .

title: The Intuitionist
author: Colson Whitehead
description: It is a time of calamity in a major metropolitan city's Department of Elevator Inspectors, and Lila Mae Watson, the department's first black female inspector, is at the center of it. She has the highest accuracy rate in the entire department, but when an elevator in a new city building goes into total freefall on Lila Mae's watch, chaos ensues.

title: Gotham: A History of New York City to 1898
author: Edwin G. Burrows & Mike Wallace
description: The first volume in a two-volume history of New York City, this 1999 Pulitzer Prize-winning work begins with the earliest Indian tribes and ends with the consolidation of the five boroughs into Greater New York in 1898.

title: The Hours
author: Michael Cunningham
description: Interweaving three tales in the same manner as Virginia Woolf's Mrs. Dalloway , Michael Cunningham's The Hours tells the day-to-day happenings of an older Virginia Woolf, a 1950s housewife reading Woolf's book, and the present-day "Mrs. Dalloway."

title: Personal History
author: Katharine Graham
description: In this Pulitzer Prize-winning memoir, Katharine Graham, the woman who piloted the Washington Post through the crises of the Pentagon Papers, Watergate, and a pressmen's strike, tells her story.

title: Boyhood
author: J. M. Coetzee
description: A fictionalized autobiography of the renowned writer's early years, growing up in a new development north of Cape Town. With a father he despised, and a mother he both adored and resented, he led a double life—the brilliant and well-behaved student at school, the princely despot at home. His first encounters with literature, the awakenings of sexual desire, and a growing awareness of apartheid left him with baffling questions; and only in his love of the high veld could he find a sense of belonging.

title: Naked
author: David Sedaris
description: In Naked , David Sedaris's message, alternately rendered in Fakespeare, Italian, Spanish, and pidgin Greek, is the same: pay attention to me.

title: Cold Mountain
author: Charles Frazier
description: A National Book Award Winner for Fiction, Charles Frazier's debut novel, set in the Civil War-era rural South, considers both grand and intimate life themes as a wounded soldier makes his way home to the highlands of North Carolina and to his prewar sweetheart.

title: The Deep End of the Ocean
author: Jacquelyn Mitchard
description: The Deep End of the Ocean recounts every mother's most terrifying nightmare: the disappearance of her child. When three-year-old Ben vanishes while Beth Cappadora is checking in at her high school reunion, his disappearance will leave Beth frozen on a knife-edge of suppressed agony for nine years and will drive a shattering wedge through her marriage.

title: Infinite Jest
author: David Foster Wallace
description: A gargantuan, mind-altering comedy about the Pursuit of Happiness in America set in an addicts' halfway house and a tennis academy.

title: Palimpsest
author: Gore Vidal
description: Abounding in gossip, satire, historical apercus, and trenchant observations, Vidal's narrative weaves back and forth in time, providing a whole view of the author's celebrated life, and featuring a cast of memorable characters—including the Kennedy family, Marlon Brando, Anais Nin, and Eleanor Roosevelt.

title: The Liars' Club
author: Mary Karr
description: Karr’s darkly comic memoir about her childhood in an east Texas oil town tells of a hard-drinking father, a sister who can talk down the sheriff at age twelve, and an oft-married mother whose accumulated secrets threaten to destroy them all.

title: Barrel Fever
author: David Sedaris
description: This 1994 collection of short stories and essays by David Sedaris is divided into two sections. The first consists of short fiction and the second half contains autobiographical essays, and includes "The SantaLand Diaries."

title: Black Death at the Golden Gate: The Race to Save America from the Bubonic Plague.
author: David K. Randall
description: The bubonic plague claimed its first victim in Chinese immigrant Wong Chut King in 1900 and then established itself over the next several years, threatening the entire country. When Dr Rupert Blue was tasked with stopping the spread of the plague, he was pitted against the corrupt politics and racism of the city government, in a deadly race against time.

title: Magical Realism for Non-Believers
author: Anika Fajardo
description: Aged 21, Anika Fajardo boarded a plane and flew to Colombia to discover a birthplace that was foreign to her and a father who was a stranger. There she learned that sometimes, no matter how many pieces you find, fitting together a family history isn’t easy.

title: Freedom’s Laboratory
author: Audra J. Wolfe
description: Of psy-ops, seismic detection, and other emanations of the Cold War as it was conducted in petri dishes and cyclotrons.

title: A Key to Treehouse Living
author: Elliot Reed,
description: A Key to Treehouse Living is the adventure of William Tyce, a boy without parents, who grows up near a river in the rural Midwest. In a glossary-style list, he imparts his particular wisdom on subjects ranging from ASPHALT PATHS, BETTA FISH, and MULLET to MORTAL BETRAYAL, NIHILISM, and REVELATION.

title: Where Did You Get This Number?
author: Anthony Salvanto
description: The inside dope on how polls work—and don’t work—from CBS’s News Director of Elections and Surveys.

title: Know Thyself: Western Identity from Classical Greece to the Renaissance
author: Ingrid Rossellini
description: Polymath Rossellini shares the fruits of her broad knowledge of literature, philosophy, art, and history in this dense yet highly rewarding work in which readers 'return to the early times of our history with the intention of rediscovering the building blocks of our contemporary personality.'

title: The Pigeon Tunnel: Stories from My Life
author: John le Carre
description: A collection of reminiscences from John le Carré, the legendary bestselling author of Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy ; The Spy Who Came in from the Cold ; and The Night Manager .

title: Love from Boy: Roald Dahl's Letters to His Mother
author: Roald Dahl, Ed. by Donald Sturrock
description: A collection of the legendary children’s author and writer Roald Dahl's letters written to his mother, from early childhood through Dahl’s travels to Africa, his career in the Royal Air Force, his work in post-war Washington, D.C., and Hollywood, and the books that made him a literary star.

title: Freedom
author: Johnathan Franzen
description: Freedom is an epic of contemporary love and marriage that charts the mistakes and joys of the Berglund family as they struggle to learn how to live in an ever more confusing world.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
description: Twenty years after actor Arthur Leander had a heart attack onstage and a devastating flu pandemic brings civilization to its knees, Kirsten Raymonde moves between settlements of the altered world as part of the Traveling Symphony, dedicated to keeping the remnants of art and humanity alive.

title: The Sea Queen: A Novel
author: Linnea Hartsuyker
description: Now fighting opposite her brother, Svanhild must decide how to navigate an ever more treacherous Norway in Hartsuyker’s follow-up to The Half-Drowned King .

title: Maeve in America
author: Maeve Higgins
description: An Irish comic and writer gathers essays about her experiences living and working in the United States.

title: Click Here to Kill Everybody
author: Bruce Schneier
description: Big Brother is watching and scheming and up to no good—and, writes security technologist Schneier, it looks like he’s winning.

title: Hidden
author: Rebecca Zanetti
description: Hide. That's all Pippa can do to escape the terror chasing her. But now that she's off the grid in a safe house, she finds plenty of interesting things to watch through the window. Like her new neighbor, with his startling green eyes, killer smile, and sexy bad-boy tattoo.

title: What We Have Lost: The Dismantling of Great Britain
author: James Hamilton-Paterson
description: The esteemed British writer charts what he sees as a decline in Britain since World War II, touching on the decimation of the manufacturing industry, the rise of the banking sector, and other troubling developments.

title: Virtuoso
author: Yelena Moskovich
description: Just before Jana's seventh birthday, a new family moves in to their building: a bird-eyed mamka in a fox-fur coat, a stubble-faced papka—and a raven-haired girl named Zorka. As the first cracks begin to appear in the communist regime, Zorka teaches Jana to look beyond their building, beyond Prague, beyond Czechoslovakia ... and then, Zorka just disappears.

title: The Confession
author: Jessie Burton
description: One winter's afternoon on Hampstead Heath in 1980, Elise meets Constance and quickly falls under her spell. Connie is bold and alluring, a successful writer whose novel is being turned into a major Hollywood film. Elise follows Connie to LA, a city of strange dreams and swimming pools and late-night gatherings of glamorous people. But whilst Connie thrives on the heat and electricity of this new world, Elise finds herself floundering. When she overhears a conversation at a party that turns everything on its head, Elise makes an impulsive decision that will change her life forever. Three decades later, Rose Simmons is seeking answers about her mother, who disappeared when she was a baby, and learns that the last person to see her was a woman named Constance Holden...

title: Total: Stories
author: Rebecca Miller
description: Director Rebecca Miller returns to short fiction for the first time since her collection of stories since 2002's Personal Velocity .

title: All Down Darkness Wide: A Memoir
author: Seán Hewitt
description: A memoir debut, from one of Irish literature’s rising stars, that explores mental illness and queerness.
